% FILENAME: macros_attestation.tex  (Peer Attestation, Layer 0)  (v0.4.0)
%
% Root macro system for Peer Attestation (Layer 0) AND the base of the macro / skeleton /
% shared-presentation import chain for the whole stack.  Layer 0 is cited and does not
% cite: this file forward-references no consumer and names no realization.
%
% Downstream files EXTEND, never redefine.  Every name, environment, counter, reference type,
% and presentation primitive defined here is OWNED here.
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% VOCABULARY STANDARD (v0.3.0) — ONE TEST, STATED PLAINLY
%
%   Every notation choice in PART B obeys a single falsifiability test: prefer the name
%   that makes a claim MORE checkable; reject any name that makes a contested fact harder
%   to see — including when the harder-to-see version flatters us.  The test cuts both
%   ways, and the rows below keep the cases where it forced a BLUNT name and rejected a
%   PLEASANT one.  That two-sidedness is the point.
%
%   SYMMETRY ROWS (the renames that prove this is precision):
%     R -> phi        RENAMED.  R overclaims ("return"); the object is Omega/Y, monotone
%                     non-decreasing — a FLOOR.  phi underclaims and is therefore truer.
%     B -> A  (map)   RENAMED.  B reads "burn/balance"; the exported object is a
%                     non-financial ATTESTATION record.  A is mnemonic of the precise noun.
%     pi -> kappa     RENAMED.  pi collides with the constant and reads "market price";
%                     mandated APPLIED kappa(d) keeps it visibly a price-of-something.
%     Y               KEPT.  Y is accurate as supply.  We forbid GLOSSING it "yield";
%                     we do not rename it — renaming an accurate symbol would be optics.
%     burn            KEPT (operation).  Bluntest, most checkable name for "destroy own
%                     units irrecoverably".  Its connotations point TOWARD scrutiny, not
%                     away; the operation is never renamed after its output.
%     deposit         KEPT (operation).  The warehouse-deposit reading is the accurate
%                     one under the receipt model; we do not flee it to "contribute".
%     G -> SP         RENAMED on TWO sufficient grounds, each stated: (1) precision — the
%                     family labels PROVEN PROPERTIES of a constructed object, not
%                     assurances to a counterparty; "specified property" is the exact
%                     reading.  (2) collision-safety — two-letter no-hyphen SP is mutually
%                     unambiguous against P- (pins), D (residuals), T (rules), I (invariant).
%                     Either ground alone suffices.  Neither ground is a category avoided.
%     PEER TOKEN -> PEER ATTESTATION   RENAMED (title).  "Token" named the SCAFFOLDING
%                     (the burnable receipt, the consumed input); the layer exports exactly
%                     ONE object, the attestation map A, and "everything else is internal
%                     structure that makes the specified properties hold."  The title now
%                     agrees with the export A, not with the container Y that A outlives.
%                     This finishes the B->A rename at the document level.  The INSTRUMENT
%                     keeps its noun of record ("reserve receipt"): the system is named for
%                     what it PRODUCES, not for what it DESTROYS.
%     PT- -> PA-    RENAMED (xref namespace) on the same ground: the prefix names the
%                     DOCUMENT, and the document's name changed.  Pre-1.0 policy permits it.
%
%   The CLASS NOUN of record is the "reserve receipt" (a claim on an external reserve,
%   redeemable, transferable).  The two redemption states are the LIVE class (presently
%   redeemable) and the TIME-LOCKED class (not yet).  The proper name is "Peer Attestation";
%   the PA- cross-reference namespace names the DOCUMENT, not the instrument (the instrument
%   remains the "reserve receipt").
%
%   LOCALITY DISCIPLINE: facts true only at this layer ("non-redeemable", "never revalued
%   upward") must travel with the tag "at this layer".  This layer declines to price the
%   attestation and says so, rather than pricing it favorably.  See \atthislayer.
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% MAIN.TEX CONTRACT  (READ FIRST — this file does NOT toggle expl3)
%
%   The file is, in its entirety, expl3 source and contains NO \ExplSyntaxOn/Off.  Each
%   consumer's main.tex owns the toggle and wraps ALL macro inputs in one block, AFTER
%   amsthm + mathtools + hyperref + zref-clever + zref-titleref:
%
%       \ExplSyntaxOn
%         \input{macros_attestation.tex}  % Layer 0 — FIRST, every paper
%       \ExplSyntaxOff
%       \zcLanguageSetup{english}{ type = openproblem , ... }   % non-expl3 config OUTSIDE
%
%   The Peer Attestation document loads ONLY this file and stages NO xref bridge (it is the root).
%
%   expl3 catcodes obeyed throughout:  space/tab IGNORED -> use "~".  "_" is a LETTER ->
%   use \sb{...}, never "x_0".  ":" is a LETTER -> fine in label keys.  Multi-word
%   display text needs "~".
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% EXPORT STRATA — who may use what (one shared file; GREP/REVIEW-enforced)
%
%   [found]      shared maths, document skeleton, presentation.  Everywhere.
%   [interface]  the computational interface I0.  Everywhere.  The ONLY stratum a
%                consumer's PUBLISHED-QUANTITY formula may touch:
%                  \attest, \addrspace, \netliveshare, \attestcap.
%                (\attestunitcost is a DERIVED convenience over \netliveshare — the cost
%                projection 1/((1−f)ζ) — NOT a fifth interface object; the export count
%                stays four.)
%   [surface]    monetary surface: operations any economic agent may perform and the audit
%                quantities anyone may read.  Layer 0, the realization, Layer 2, and
%                CONSUMER PROSE — may be named and cited (via \attestationref) wherever a
%                consumer discusses it, but never used in the consumer's MACHINERY: not in
%                a published-quantity formula, not in a computation.
%   [core]       Layer~0-internal mechanism quantities.  Layer 0 (and the realization) only.
%
%   CONSUMPTION MATRIX        L0 doc  realization  consumer formula  consumer prose  L2
%     [found]                   y         y               y                y          y
%     [interface]               y         y               y                y          y
%     [surface]                 y         y               -            cited          y
%     [core]                    y         y               -                -          -
%
%   GREP LINT (consumer sources; review-blocking):
%     surface+core purity — a surface/core name in a consumer formula is a violation; a
%       surface name may appear in consumer PROSE only as a \attestationref citation:
%       grep -nE '\\(reservepool|escrow|holdings|supplyfrac|netcost|redeemratio|totsupply|livesupply|tlocksupply|ratefloor|ratefloorcap|livesplit|feerate|genesisreserve|cycleburnfrac|matcycle|matlead|matleadcap|feeflow|confprice|bootrange|normrange|burnop|depositop|redeemop|liveclass|tlockclass)\b'
%     core closure — core never appears in any consumer source:
%       grep -nE '\\(escrow|holdings|supplyfrac|netcost|redeemratio)\b'   -> nothing.
%     no-count rule — Layer~0 sources never mention the consumer count vocabulary:
%       grep -nE '\\(partthresh|actioncount|commitrate|remcap|leverage|effais|reffais|floorburn|excessburn)\b'  in attestation/sections/*.tex -> nothing.
%     two-clocks rule — attestation/sections/*.tex:  grep -niE 'epoch' -> nothing.
%     no-downward-reference — attestation/sections/*.tex carries no realization vocabulary
%       (covenant, on-chain, script, smart contract) and no realization pin/section name.
%       Scope: normative prose only (sections/*.tex); build-infrastructure comments in
%       this macro file may name tooling packages, including the anchor-set-hash
%       implementation.
%     upward silence — attestation/sections/*.tex carries no consumer noun
%       (actor, account, user, consumer, network, guild).  "operator" is allowed: the
%       Layer~0 administrator role (fee recipient, maturity announcer).
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% DESIGN PRINCIPLES
%   1. One macro = one semantic concept; none overloaded.
%   2. Empty braces -> bare symbol; non-empty -> applied/indexed:
%        \attest{} -> A      \attest{a} -> A_a
%   3. Modern expl3 internals (\cs_new_protected:Npn) + \NewDocumentCommand wrappers;
%      LaTeX2e interfaces (\newtheorem, \newcounter, ...) called as-is.
%   4. THE NO-COUNT RULE: no symbol here denominates per-action.  Two unit families —
%      reserve units and receipt units — with ONE conversion, the floor phi, applied at
%      exactly two points (burn, redemption).  The reserve->action conversion is the
%      CONSUMER's and is absent here.
%   5. ADDRESSES, NOT ACTORS: the index of \attest is an opaque address a in 𝔸; the
%      binding "address = actor key" is the consumer's import-time reading.  The glyph A
%      is unchanged across the boundary by design.
%   6. ROOT OF THE CHAIN: this file compiles standalone, references no sibling, and its
%      PART A apparatus is the FIRST \newtheorem/\newcounter the stack sees.
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% LABEL SCHEMA (Layer~0 document; consumers cite with prefix PA-)
%
%   <type> : <section> : <name>     — type vocabulary shared stack-wide:
%     sec subsec def thm prop cor lem rem ins post alg tbl eq app open invest ver
%     (two-segment by construction: sec:<section>, app:<name>, and the
%     front-matter singletons abs:abstract and motto:motto)
%   Section identifiers (the twelve, exactly — plus walkthrough, the birth
%   home of the ver:* register):
%     interface model operations invariants costliness containment discipline
%     seigniorage maturity limitations verification symbols walkthrough
%
%   CANONICAL HANDLES (stable keys + display titles; the consumer API — title the
%   environments EXACTLY, since \ztitleref reads the optional bracket):
%     def:interface:address-space             (Address Space)
%     def:interface:attestation               (Attestation)
%     post:interface:non-negativity           (Non-Negativity)
%     post:interface:monotonicity             (Monotonicity)
%     post:interface:auditability             (Public Auditability)
%     thm:interface:instantaneous-costliness  (Instantaneous Costliness)
%     prop:interface:bootstrap-capacity       (Bootstrap Capacity)
%     prop:interface:conservative-valuation   (Conservative Valuation)
%     def:interface:net-live-share            (Net Live Share)
%     def:operations:burn                     (Burn)
%     def:operations:deposit                  (Deposit)
%     def:operations:redemption               (Redemption)
%     def:model:ratefloor                     (Redemption-Rate Floor)
%     def:model:classes                       (Classes)
%     thm:invariants:floor-non-decrease       (Floor Non-Decrease)
%     post:maturity:announcement              (Maturity Announcement)
%
%   ANCHOR STABILITY (two tiers):
%     Canonical handles — key AND display title stable; consumers may \ztitleref.
%     Plain anchors     — key-stable only; titles may change. Existence is
%       guaranteed while the key is pinned by any released consumer's
%       anchor_set_hash: sha256( join("\n", sorted(distinct anchor names)) ),
%       names cited without the PA- prefix (recipe implemented and tested in
%       packages/peer-attestation-architecture, canonical::anchor_set_hash).
%     Pre-1.0 this file keeps rename freedom for UNPINNED labels; once a label
%     enters a released consumer's anchor set, renaming it is a breaking change
%     by definition — the hash says so. \OpenProblem labels are two-segment
%     (open:<name>) by macro construction and participate in the same contract.
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% SYMBOL COLLISION REGISTER
%
%   Internal:
%   \attest A_a        vs \attestcap A_max          subscript address vs "max".
%   \totsupply Y / \livesupply Y_L / \tlocksupply Y_T   one receipt, two classes.
%   \redeemratio d_liq vs \netcost D_net            case + subscript.
%   \matcycle k_m      vs bare k                     bare k is the local cycle index.
%   \addrspace 𝔸       vs the openproblem TYPE       the set is a glyph; the type is a name.
%   \addrspace 𝔸       vs algebraic numbers 𝔸        declared ONCE as an opaque set.
%   \genesisreserve E_0 vs \holdings h               distinct letters; both core/surface.
%   \ratefloor phi     vs golden-ratio / totient     the floor is ALWAYS applied, phi(t).
%   \confprice kappa   vs curvature                  the price is ALWAYS applied, kappa(d).
%
%   Cross-layer seam (the index reading flips downstream):
%   \ratefloor phi  vs a reward R_C / earnings R_i    subscript distinguishes.
%   \feerate f      vs an importing self-map f_i      subscript/argument.
%   \escrow Q       vs a diversity quantity q         case.
%   \supplyfrac s   vs a subsidy s (downstream sans)  family.
%   \livesplit zeta vs zeta(p) Riemann / a floor      NEVER the same.
%   \matlead Δk_min / \matleadcap Δk_max vs a downstream buffer δ
%                                                   letters/subscript/hat.
%   \attest A       vs a downstream proof-matrix A    blackboard vs calligraphic 𝓐.
%   \addrspace 𝔸    vs a downstream calligraphic 𝓐    blackboard vs calligraphic.
%   index a         L0: opaque address ∈ 𝔸.  Downstream: a bound actor.  Qualify at first use.
%   cycle k (L0)    vs a distinct downstream period word   TWO CLOCKS; never one word.
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% CHANGELOG
%   v0.4.0  Added \matleadcap (Δk_max), the maximum maturity lead.  Announced k_m is now
%           bounded within [Δk_min, Δk_max].  Rationale: set-once irrevocability makes an
%           over-far announcement unrevisable; Δk_max bounds its post-announcement cycle
%           distance.
%   v0.3.0  Vocabulary standard applied (precision + collision grounds only; no row is
%           justified by a category avoided).
%   v0.2.0  \ptbprice; \opidx; \bootrange/\normrange.  (Superseded names above.)
%   v0.1.0  Reserve vocabulary; surface operation set; \genesisreserve, \holdings, \Izero.
%   v0.1.0  expl3-pure + presentation promotion.
%   v0.1.0  Skeleton promotion.
%   v0.1.0  Initial extraction.
% ========================================================================================


% ========================================================================================
% PART A — SHARED DOCUMENT APPARATUS + PRESENTATION                   EXPORT: [found]
%   (Vocabulary-neutral; unchanged across the v0.3.0 rename except where noted.)
% ========================================================================================

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §A.1  Version management
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\tl_new:N \g_peerattest_version_tl
\NewDocumentCommand{\setversion}{m}{ \tl_gset:Nn \g_peerattest_version_tl {#1} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\docversion}{}{ \tl_use:N \g_peerattest_version_tl }

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §A.2  Theorem skeleton (one section-scoped counter) + equation numbering
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\theoremstyle{plain}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{corollary}[theorem]{Corollary}
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newtheorem{proposition}[theorem]{Proposition}
\newtheorem{conjecture}[theorem]{Conjecture}

\theoremstyle{definition}
\newtheorem{definition}[theorem]{Definition}
\newtheorem{axiom}[theorem]{Axiom}
\newtheorem{postulate}[theorem]{Postulate}
\newtheorem{protocol}[theorem]{Protocol}

\theoremstyle{remark}
\newtheorem{insight}[theorem]{Insight}
\newtheorem{remark}[theorem]{Remark}
\newtheorem{property}[theorem]{Property}

\numberwithin{equation}{section}

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §A.3  Open-problem counter family + environments
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\newcounter{openproblem}[subsection]
\newcounter{opensubproblem}[openproblem]
\newcounter{investigation}[subsection]

\cs_set:Npn \theopenproblem      { \thesubsection.\arabic{openproblem} }
\cs_set:Npn \theopensubproblem   { \theopenproblem.\arabic{opensubproblem} }
\cs_set:Npn \theinvestigation    { \thesubsection.\arabic{investigation} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHopenproblem
  { openproblem.\arabic{section}.\arabic{subsection}.\arabic{openproblem} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHopensubproblem
  { opensubproblem.\arabic{section}.\arabic{subsection}.\arabic{openproblem}.\arabic{opensubproblem} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHinvestigation
  { investigation.\arabic{section}.\arabic{subsection}.\arabic{investigation} }

\NewDocumentCommand{\OpenProblem}{m m}
  {
    \refstepcounter{openproblem}
    \paragraph{\theopenproblem\quad#1.}
    \label{open:#2}
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\OpenSubProblem}{O{} m}
  {
    \refstepcounter{opensubproblem}
    \emph{\theopensubproblem\quad#2.}
    \tl_if_blank:nF {#1} { \label{open:#1} }
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\ProposedInvestigation}{m m}
  {
    \refstepcounter{investigation}
    \paragraph{\theinvestigation\quad#1.}
    \label{invest:#2}
  }

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §A.4  Reference types for the theorem family
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% zref-clever derives a label's reference type from its COUNTER, and the whole
% scholarly family shares the `theorem' counter — so each environment forces its
% own counter-to-type mapping, scoped to the environment group, so its head
% label types by the environment while equation labels inside the body keep
% their own counter type. Display names are key-val configuration and live in
% main.tex, OUTSIDE the expl3 wrap.
\AddToHook{env/theorem/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=theorem}}}
\AddToHook{env/corollary/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=corollary}}}
\AddToHook{env/lemma/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=lemma}}}
\AddToHook{env/proposition/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=proposition}}}
\AddToHook{env/conjecture/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=conjecture}}}
\AddToHook{env/definition/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=definition}}}
\AddToHook{env/axiom/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=axiom}}}
\AddToHook{env/postulate/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=postulate}}}
\AddToHook{env/protocol/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=protocol}}}
\AddToHook{env/insight/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=insight}}}
\AddToHook{env/remark/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=remark}}}
\AddToHook{env/property/begin}{\zcsetup{countertype={theorem=property}}}

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §A.5  Shared scholarly environments
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\newenvironment{motto}{\begin{center}\itshape}{\end{center}}
\newenvironment{derivation}{\begin{proof}[Derivation]}{\end{proof}}

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §A.6  Formatting utilities
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_add_usc: { \addfontfeatures{Letters=SmallCaps} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\addUsc}{}{ \peerattest_add_usc: }

\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_insight_par:n #1 { \paragraph{Insight:}\emph{#1} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\insightpar}{m}{ \peerattest_insight_par:n {#1} }

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §A.7  Shared presentation toolkit
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\NewDocumentCommand{\KEY}{m}{ \boxed{#1} }

\NewDocumentCommand{\Izero}{}{ \ensuremath{I\sb{0}} }

\NewDocumentCommand{\stackmarginnote}{m m}
  {
    \marginpar
      {
        \footnotesize \linespread{0.85} \selectfont
        \textit{#1}~#2
      }
  }

\NewDocumentCommand{\proofsketch}{m}{ \stackmarginnote{Sketch:}{#1} }

\NewDocumentCommand{\networkref}{m}{ \stackmarginnote{Layer~1:}{\zcref{#1}} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\layertworef}{m}{ \stackmarginnote{Layer~2:}{\zcref{#1}} }

\NewDocumentCommand{\interfaceref}{m}
  { \stackmarginnote{Interface~\Izero{:}}{\zcref{#1}} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\surfaceref}{m}
  { \stackmarginnote{Surface:}{\zcref{#1}} }

% Locality tag (v0.3.0).  The presentation form of the locality discipline: a fact true
% only at this layer prints "at this layer", so the firewall reads as a fact, not a
% disclaimer.  Use INLINE in prose ("non-redeemable \atthislayer{}").
\NewDocumentCommand{\atthislayer}{}{ at~this~layer }

% "records, never bears" (v0.3.0).  The attestation RECORDS a magnitude; it never BEARS a
% value.  This primitive is the verb-level firewall: it renders "records" in the one place
% a careless "is worth"/"bears" would rebuild a balance.  #1 = the magnitude phrase.
\NewDocumentCommand{\attestrecords}{m}{ records~#1 }

% Cross-document references INTO the Layer~0 paper (consumer side, prefix PA-).  The prefix
% PA- names the DOCUMENT, not the instrument, so the receipt rename does not touch the noun.
\bool_new:N \g_peerattest_xref_bool
\NewDocumentCommand{\attestxreftrue} {}{ \bool_gset_true:N  \g_peerattest_xref_bool }
\NewDocumentCommand{\attestxreffalse}{}{ \bool_gset_false:N \g_peerattest_xref_bool }

\NewDocumentCommand{\attestationref}{m}
  {
    \stackmarginnote{Layer~0:}
      {
        \bool_if:NTF \g_peerattest_xref_bool
          { \zcref[cap]{PA-#1}~(\ztitleref{PA-#1}) }
          { \texttt{#1} }
      }
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\attestationcref}{s m}
  {
    Layer~0~
    \bool_if:NTF \g_peerattest_xref_bool
      { \zcref[cap]{PA-#2}\IfBooleanT{#1}{~(\ztitleref{PA-#2})} }
      { \texttt{#2} }
  }


% ========================================================================================
% PART B — NOTATION
% ========================================================================================

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §F0  FOUNDATIONS                                                    EXPORT: [found]
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\NewDocumentCommand{\Nat}    {}{ \ensuremath{\symbb{N}}            }
\NewDocumentCommand{\NatZero}{}{ \ensuremath{\symbb{N}\sb{0}}     }
\NewDocumentCommand{\IntPos} {}{ \ensuremath{\symbb{Z}\sb{+}}     }
\NewDocumentCommand{\R}      {}{ \ensuremath{\symbb{R}}            }

\DeclarePairedDelimiter{\set} {\lbrace}{\rbrace}
\DeclarePairedDelimiter{\abs} {\lvert} {\rvert}
\DeclarePairedDelimiter{\norm}{\lVert} {\rVert}

\NewDocumentCommand{\void}  {}{ \ensuremath{\varnothing} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\okmark}{}{ \ensuremath{\checkmark}  }

% Operator subscript token (the Layer~0 administrator role).  Use \attest{\opidx} for the
% operator attestation; keeps the subscript uniform across §8 / §A / §10.  Presentation
% only — "op" is not a consumer noun.
\NewDocumentCommand{\opidx}{}{ \ensuremath{\mathrm{op}} }

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §I0  THE COMPUTATIONAL INTERFACE I0                             EXPORT: [interface]
%
% The COMPLETE set of objects a consumer's published-quantity formula may reference.
% Four macros (\attest, \addrspace, \netliveshare, \attestcap).  \attestunitcost is a
% derived convenience over \netliveshare (the reciprocal cost projection), not a fifth
% object.  Everything else in PART B is surface or core.
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

% Opaque address space 𝔸.  A burn names an address a ∈ 𝔸; attestation accrues to the
% address, bounded by destruction.  No claim that an address is a person/holder/identity.
% COLLIDES: algebraic numbers 𝔸 (declared once here as an opaque set, not a number field);
%           a downstream calligraphic 𝓐 (blackboard vs calligraphic).
\NewDocumentCommand{\addrspace}{}{ \ensuremath{\symbb{A}} }

% Cumulative reserve-denominated ATTESTATION, per address.
%   \attest{}  -> A   (the map A : 𝔸 -> ℝ≥0)        \attest{a}  -> A_a
% THE export.  A RECORDS the reserve-value destroyed (it never BEARS value: non-transferable,
% non-redeemable AT THIS LAYER).  Six specified properties: 1 non-negative · 2 settlement-
% pinned monotone · 3 auditable as authenticated destruction · 4 instantaneously costly ·
% 5 bootstrap-capacity-bounded (\attestcap) · 6 conservatively valued (records ≤ redeemable
% value at the burn instant).  Index: OPAQUE ADDRESS here; a bound actor downstream (the
% consumer's import-time reading); glyph unchanged by design.
% COLLIDES: \attestcap A_max; a downstream proof-matrix 𝓐.  Subscript/blackboard.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_attest:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { A } { A\sb{#1} } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\attest}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_attest:n {#1} } }

% Net live share: the post-fee, immediately-redeemable share of a bootstrapping-phase mint,
% per reserve unit deposited = (1−f)·ζ.  A PURPOSE-NEUTRAL allocation ratio: it asserts no
% depositor intent.  A reader producing attestation reads its RECIPROCAL as the reserve cost
% of one attestation; a reader holding the position reads it as liquid retention.  This layer
% asserts neither projection (cf. the locality discipline: as the layer declines to PRICE the
% attestation, it declines to NAME the depositor's purpose).  FULL-FORM by design (renders the
% product, no new glyph) so the value cannot be misstated.  Phase scope is part of the export.
% First use in a consumer document must cite def:interface:net-live-share.
\NewDocumentCommand{\netliveshare}{}{ \ensuremath{ (1-\feerate)\,\livesplit } }

% [interface], derived companion for the cost projection (full-form, no new glyph).  The
% reserve cost of one attestation unit = 1/((1−f)ζ).  Provided so the cost PROJECTION renders
% honestly (direction-correct) wherever a consumer wants it, without re-deriving.  NOT a fifth
% interface object — a convenience over \netliveshare; the export count stays four.
\NewDocumentCommand{\attestunitcost}{}{ \ensuremath{ 1/\bigl((1-\feerate)\,\livesplit\bigr) } }

% Maximum aggregate attestation before external deposits:
%   A_max = E_0 ln(1/(1−ζ))   — property SP5's bound (E_0 = \genesisreserve).
% COLLIDES: \attest A_a — "max" vs address.
\NewDocumentCommand{\attestcap}{}{ \ensuremath{A\sb{\max}} }

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §S0  MONETARY SURFACE — OPERATIONS                                EXPORT: [surface]
%   Operations any economic agent may perform: deposit, transfer, burn, redeem.
%   Transfer needs no macro (class-internal; plain prose).  Maturity conversion is a model
%   event, not an agent operation (§S1 \matcycle).
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

% Destination-addressed burn: burn(x; a) — destroy x live-class units; record on address a
% an attestation of x·φ at the prevailing floor.  Funder unconstrained; consent-free (the
% record is monotone in the address's favor).  x is the ITALIC burn amount.
% KEPT "burn": the bluntest, most checkable name for irrecoverable destruction of one's own
% units; the operation is never renamed after its output.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_burnop:nn #1#2 { \operatorname{burn}(#1;#2) }
\NewDocumentCommand{\burnop}{m m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_burnop:nn {#1}{#2} } }

% Deposit: deposit(δ; a) — δ reserve units in; receipt minted at the next cycle boundary to
% holder address a, split ζ : (1−ζ) into LIVE : TIME-LOCKED during bootstrapping (all LIVE
% in the normal phase), less the mint fee f.
% KEPT "deposit": the warehouse-deposit reading is the accurate one under the receipt model.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_depositop:nn #1#2 { \operatorname{deposit}(#1;#2) }
\NewDocumentCommand{\depositop}{m m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_depositop:nn {#1}{#2} } }

% Redemption: redeem(x) — return x live-class units; receive x·φ reserve units.
% The time-locked class is not redeemable until maturity conversion relabels it.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_redeemop:n #1 { \operatorname{redeem}(#1) }
\NewDocumentCommand{\redeemop}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_redeemop:n {#1} } }

% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% §S1  MONETARY SURFACE — AUDIT QUANTITIES                          EXPORT: [surface]
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

% Reserve pool Ω.  \reservepool{t} -> Ω(t).  Held 1:1 against the receipt; the reserve
% asset is abstract (L-BTC, an external value token are named instantiations).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_reservepool:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \Omega } { \Omega(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\reservepool}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_reservepool:n {#1} } }

% Genesis reserve E_0 — the reserve deposited at genesis (Ω(0) = Y(0) = E_0, φ(0)=1).
% COLLIDES: \holdings h (different letters; both core/surface only).
\NewDocumentCommand{\genesisreserve}{}{ \ensuremath{E\sb{0}} }

% Total receipt supply Y = Y_L + Y_T.  ONE conserved receipt; LIVE/TIME-LOCKED are its two
% redemption CLASSES, not assets.  Y is SUPPLY — never glossed "yield".
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_totsupply:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { Y } { Y(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\totsupply}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_totsupply:n {#1} } }

% Live-class supply component Y_L (always redeemable).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_livesupply:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { Y\sb{\mathrm{L}} } { Y\sb{\mathrm{L}}(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\livesupply}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_livesupply:n {#1} } }

% Time-locked-class supply component Y_T (transferable; neither burnable nor redeemable; no
% redemption floor; converts into the live class in one relabel at k_m).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_tlocksupply:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { Y\sb{\mathrm{T}} } { Y\sb{\mathrm{T}}(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\tlocksupply}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_tlocksupply:n {#1} } }

% Redemption-rate floor φ = Ω/Y — reserve per receipt unit; the redemption price and THE
% unit conversion of Layer 0.  RATCHETS UP ONLY (monotone non-decreasing) — a floor, not a
% return; this is why the glyph is phi, not R.  One floor over the COMBINED supply.
% Property SP6 is an upper bound, so a lagged/last-settled valuation is valid, not a
% contradiction.
% COLLIDES: golden-ratio / totient (the floor is ALWAYS applied, phi(t); the constant does
%           not appear in this stack); a downstream reward R_C / earnings R_i.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_ratefloor:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \varphi } { \varphi(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\ratefloor}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_ratefloor:n {#1} } }

% Bootstrap floor ceiling φ_max = 1/(1−ζ); maturity conversion uncaps it.
\NewDocumentCommand{\ratefloorcap}{}{ \ensuremath{\varphi\sb{\max}} }

% LIVE/TIME-LOCKED split ζ ∈ (0,1): the live share at mint.  Published constant, fixed at
% genesis.
% COLLIDES: ζ(p) Riemann / a downstream floor — NEVER the same.
% magnitude is a calibration output, not a layer constant — see rem:model:calibration
\NewDocumentCommand{\livesplit}{}{ \ensuremath{\zeta} }

% Formula-fixed mint fee rate f ∈ (0,1).  Published constant, a deterministic function of
% public state.  ("formula-fixed", never "maintenance" — purpose words are not properties.)
% COLLIDES: a downstream self-map f_i.
% magnitude is a calibration output, not a layer constant — see rem:model:calibration
\NewDocumentCommand{\feerate}{}{ \ensuremath{f} }

% Cycle burn fraction χ^{(k)}.  "Cycle", not "epoch" — L0 periods are CYCLES; A flows
% continuously and a consumer samples it at ITS own boundary.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_cycleburnfrac:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \chi } { \chi\sp{(#1)} } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\cycleburnfrac}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_cycleburnfrac:n {#1} } }

% Maturity-conversion cycle k_m (one-time value-neutral TIME-LOCKED -> LIVE relabel in Y).
% COLLIDES: bare k (the local cycle index).
\NewDocumentCommand{\matcycle}{}{ \ensuremath{k\sb{\mathrm{m}}} }

% Minimum maturity lead Δk_min (cycles). Published constant.
% COLLIDES: a downstream buffer δ (letters/hat).
\NewDocumentCommand{\matlead}{}{ \ensuremath{\Delta k\sb{\min}} }

% Maximum maturity lead Δk_max (cycles). Published constant; Δk_min ≤ Δk_max.
% Bounds the post-announcement cycle distance to scheduled maturity under an irrevocable
% announcement. It neither compels announcement nor asserts wall-clock cycle liveness.
\NewDocumentCommand{\matleadcap}{}{ \ensuremath{\Delta k\sb{\max}} }

% Operator mint-fee flow per cycle during bootstrapping (immediately-destroyable live-class
% part): f·ζ·ΔY.  Renders the BOOTSTRAP form (the one the seigniorage bounds cite); the
% post-conversion form is f·ΔY.
\NewDocumentCommand{\feeflow}{}
  { \ensuremath{ \feerate\,\livesplit\,\Delta\totsupply{} } }

% [surface] alias retained for inheriting layers (the guild's fee-PT spigot \feespigot):
% the same bootstrap mint-fee flow f·ζ·ΔY as \feeflow.  Consumers cite it as the Layer~0
% mint-fee spigot; do not give it a divergent rendering.
\NewDocumentCommand{\feespigot}{}{ \feeflow }

% Time-locked-class secondary-market CONFIDENCE PRICE κ.  The signal an inheriting layer
% reads.  ALWAYS APPLIED: \confprice{d} -> κ(d) — keeps it visibly a price-of-something,
% never a static parameter.  bare \confprice{} -> κ.
% COLLIDES: curvature κ — the price is ALWAYS applied, κ(d).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_confprice:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \kappa } { \kappa(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\confprice}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_confprice:n {#1} } }

% Phase intervals (cycles), presentation helpers over \matcycle.  Use for "bootstrapping
% \bootrange" / "normal \normrange"; never bare "two-phase".
\NewDocumentCommand{\bootrange}{}{ \ensuremath{[0,\matcycle)}        }
\NewDocumentCommand{\normrange}{}{ \ensuremath{[\matcycle,\infty)}  }

% Standardized class names — keep the class/asset distinction grep-able in prose.
\NewDocumentCommand{\liveclass} {}{ \textnormal{live~class} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\tlockclass}{}{ \textnormal{time\nobreakdash-locked~class} }

% Deposit escrow Q — reserve received within a cycle, awaiting the boundary mint.
% COLLIDES: a downstream diversity quantity q (case).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_escrow:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { Q } { Q(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\escrow}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_escrow:n {#1} } }

% Holder receipt holdings h_i — receipt units held by holder address i; the numerator of
% the supply fraction.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_holdings:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { h } { h\sb{#1} } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\holdings}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_holdings:n {#1} } }

% Supply fraction s_i = h_i/Y — the pivot of the conservation identity and ζ-independence.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \peerattest_supplyfrac:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { s } { s\sb{#1} } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\supplyfrac}{m}{ \ensuremath{ \peerattest_supplyfrac:n {#1} } }

% Net economic cost Δ_net = Ω·x·(1−s)/(Y−x).
\NewDocumentCommand{\netcost}{}{ \ensuremath{\Delta\sb{\mathrm{net}}} }

% Redeemable cost ratio δ_liq (immediately-redeemable value-loss fraction).
\NewDocumentCommand{\redeemratio}{}{ \ensuremath{\delta\sb{\mathrm{liq}}} }

% THE FOUNDATION (read this first — it is the file's reason to exist)
%
%   Layer 1 IS a non-trivial inter-cluster comparator engine.  A network has
%   value only if it can compare clusters; cluster topology is relabeling-
%   invariant (gauge) and therefore fabricable, so topology ALONE cannot compare.
%   Comparison requires a scalar the topology cannot generate — EXOGENOUS in
%   origin, NEUTRAL, NON-TRANSFERABLE, MONOTONE, BOUND onto the graph.  Layer 0
%   prepares exactly such a scalar and, by DECLINING TO PRICE it, guarantees its
%   neutrality.  This macro system's job is to let an author CITE that object,
%   not merely its fibers.
%
%   The macro consequences (all applied below):
%     • \standing{i}  — THE COMPARATOR: the weighted MEDIANT of post-debit
%                       (balance, count) pairs; rate-DeGroot with action-mass
%                       weights; coincides with the uniform-activity DeGroot
%                       comparator (reduction theorem) — renders α.
%     • \commitrate   — the NEUTRAL SOURCE r_i = b_i/max(N_i,1), read from the
%                       θ-debit LEDGER (\burnbal), not the gross frame.
%     • \safethresh   — no longer a clamp nothing is charged at: THE per-action
%                       price, the ONLY debited object (V3 schedule).
%     • \numeraire    — the comparator's UNIT (structural numéraire).
%     • \partfloor    — the dimensionless participation FLOOR.
%     • \burnval    — the IMPORTED FRAME; its foundational content is the
%                       shared ordered codomain ℝ≥0 (the one line all addresses
%                       are forced onto), which has NO glyph (it is inhabited,
%                       never typeset).
%     • NO glyph is coined for ACCOUNTABILITY COST or UN-FLOORED INJECTION.  These
%       are BOUNDED-not-CLOSED and get CONCEPT LABELS, never symbols.  The gap
%       between a cited label and an absent glyph MEANS "open frontier".
%     • "floor" is reserved for the EXOGENOUS anchor (ν, ρ, ρν, φ) only; the
%       ENDOGENOUS primitive is "accountability cost", NEVER "floor".
%

% THE LAYER-0 SEAM  (the one load-bearing fact — comparator reading)
%
%   The network does NOT define the comparator.  Layer 0 PREPARES it and, by
%   DECLINING TO PRICE it, guarantees its neutrality.  \attest (A_a : 𝔸 → ℝ≥0) is
%   the ONE object Layer 0 exports; its foundational content is the SHARED ORDERED
%   CODOMAIN ℝ≥0 — the single line onto which all addresses are forced, the
%   comparator's neutral FRAME.  The network IMPORTS the frame under its own
%   burn-record symbol \burnval, names the codomain in prose (the comparator),
%   and BINDS the opaque address to an Actor at import:
%       B_i := A_{key(i)}        (the glyph flips A → B by design; §N7)
%   It then CONSTRUCTS the neutral SOURCE on its own side:
%       r_i = \burnbal{i}/max(\actcount{i},1)   (\commitrate, §N7;
%       \burnbal = imported frame minus the consummated θ-debits,
%       def:comparator:residual-balance)
%   and WELDS the source onto the topology to form the relative-standing field
%       \standing{i}             (the comparator realized on the graph; §5 α).
%
%   Roles, kept distinct on purpose:
%     \burnval  — the imported FRAME, fiber-wise (per-actor value).
%     codomain ℝ≥0 — the FRAME itself (the comparator's neutral reference); NO glyph.
%     \commitrate — the NEUTRAL SOURCE: the unique EXOGENOUS input to the standing
%                   recursion; the one quantity the topology cannot generate.
%     \standing   — the comparator: topology with its relabeling gauge FIXED by the
%                   neutral source.  EVERY value channel multiplies (1+\standing)
%                   by NECESSITY (only relative position is comparable) — the
%                   "universal amplifier".
%
%   ν (\numeraire) is the SOLE reserve→action join (Numéraire);
%   every reserve input is divided by it before meeting a count.  ρ (\partfloor)
%   is the dimensionless participation floor.  The two clocks
%   are decoupled: A flows continuously, L1 SAMPLES it at its epoch boundary; the
%   leverage-timing problem is cross-layer (jointly owned with L0).
%
%   The comparator stands on TWO COSTS, with opposite anchors:
%     SOURCE cost      — destroying scarce EXTERNAL value (L0).  EXOGENOUS, breaks
%                        the gauge, CLOSES.  Anchors WHO HAS MASS.
%     ACCOUNTABILITY cost — committing a public, immutable, attributed, self-defeating
%                        RECORD.  ENDOGENOUS, respects the gauge, DETERS but never
%                        ANCHORS — BOUNDED, never closes (every binding-axis open
%                        problem lives here).  Anchors the truth of an EDGE-CLAIM.
%   Source cost has glyphs (\burnval, \numeraire, \partfloor).  Accountability cost has a
%   CONCEPT LABEL (post:comparator:accountability-cost) and NO glyph, by design.
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% STANDING-TRANSPORT VOCABULARY  (Edition 5 conserved allocation)
%
%   The Action Graph remains the raw public record graph used by feed ranking,
%   raw bridge traversal, and structural folds.  Standing does not traverse it.
%
%   Standing is ONE CONSERVED OPERATOR.  Every Actor disposes of exactly one unit
%   of allocation over self and the recipients its own accepted acts name; the
%   ledger pair it disposes of is transported, not transferred; and the whole
%   system is solved as a single same-epoch equilibrium:
%
%     acts -> fold cells -> 𝖠_{uj} -> Λ^{(r)}(𝐱) -> 𝚷(𝐱) -> mediant -> 𝐱* -> 𝓚_k
%
%   FOLD CELL (\foldcell, \foldcells)
%     The order-free unit of standing input.  Every accepted Actor-authored act
%     enters exactly one, at the act level: a hyper-edge is one act, not two legs.
%     Nothing is filtered out — what is not allocated socially is retained by self.
%
%   RECIPIENT RESOLUTION (\resolve) and BASE SCORE (\basescore)
%     A published, deterministic, order-free rule sends each fold cell to a person
%     recipient or to the author's self-retention channel.  The base score 𝖠_{uj}
%     sums the resolved cells under published domain weights (\domweight,
%     \domprofile), over the self-retention base \selfretention.
%
%   TILT (\tiltshape, \tiltexp, \tiltstrength, \tiltcum)
%     Recipient standing modulates apportionment, hop by hop, through the
%     wall-clamped activation raised to υ_r(t).  It may only re-apportion a
%     source's conserved unit: it can create no relation the source did not
%     author, and it never modulates the self share.
%
%   TRANSPORT (\hopmatrix, \transport, \transportentry, \depthmass, \hopmax)
%     Row-stochastic per hop; a depth-mass-weighted sum of hop products to depth
%     L_hop, emission applied once to the mixture.  There is NO per-pair standing
%     flow.  "Transport" is not "transfer": the ledger moves nothing.
%
%   EMISSION (\emission, \emissionmat)
%     History travels on the back of balance: 𝔢_u = min(1, r̂_u/ρ_θ), applied to
%     the finished hop mixture as 𝚷 = 𝔈·(mixture) + (𝐈−𝔈).  Unexported mass stays
%     in the owner's own row — it is relocated, never deleted.  Pre-normalization
%     row scaling is a mathematical no-op and a prohibited pattern; so is a
%     per-recipient emission fraction 𝔢_{uj}, which would make emission a property
%     of a relation rather than of the source's pair (the tilt is the only
%     chartered modulator of relative allocation odds).
%
%   STANDING ATOMICITY:
%     A standing-bearing hyper-edge is consumed as one complete act.  Under
%     universal weighing this is now general, not a person-vouch privilege.
%
%   ARTIFACT NON-ALLOCATION:
%     Passive-node incidence cannot inherit, originate, or redirect allocation.
%     Any change to raw passive incidence that leaves the fold cells unchanged
%     leaves 𝖠, every Λ^{(r)}, 𝚷 and α unchanged.
%
%   SAFETY SCOPE:
%     Safety means one certified contraction enclosure over the conserved map
%     (\standingcert, \contractionfactor) inside the FREE invariant rate-hull box
%     (\hullbox) — forward invariance is not a separate obligation here.  The
%     profile screen ‖υ(t)‖₁ ≤ 2 is SUFFICIENT, not "iff contraction", and holds
%     whenever the contributing width does not exceed the published W_loc.  Safety
%     does NOT by itself mean bounded one-step movement or target consent; cross-
%     target rivalry is no longer an open question — conservation closes it.
%
%   MIGRATION STAGING:
%     This is Migration Guide 1 (macros only).  Body prose, theorem labels,
%     equations, and cross-references still carry Edition-4 meanings and will FAIL
%     to compile against the deleted names until later guides repoint them.  The
%     §N7d names reserve the Edition-5 meanings now; do not use them in normative
%     formulas until the corresponding body definitions land.
%
% ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
% PROHIBITED PATTERNS (Layer~1 prose and source)
%
%     numeraire uniqueness — grep -nE '\nu\b' sections/03_graph.tex sections/05_epoch.tex -> nothing.
%     genesis discipline   — grep -niE 'genesis' sections/*.tex | grep -i registration -> nothing.
%   leg vocabulary   — grep -nE '(Tag|Review|Bid|Write|Send|Invitation|De-invite)[~ ]L[12]\b' sections/*.tex -> nothing
%   write family     — grep -nE 'Write[~ ](hyper-edge|L[12]|edge)' sections/*.tex -> nothing (changelogs exempt)
%   write unit       — grep -nE 'admission[ -]cluster|cluster price|cluster key|priced out|lapsed clusters|lapsed from' sections/*.tex -> nothing (changelogs exempt)
%   unwritten L1     — grep -nE 'submission receipt|receipted|the book|published queue|consent-liveness' sections/*.tex -> nothing
%   theta discipline — grep -nE 'theta.?(pol|_\{?pol)' sections/*.tex macros_*.tex -> nothing
%   bar retirement   — grep -niE 'admission.bar|bar-blocked|p_\{?\\?mathrm\{policy' sections/*.tex -> nothing (changelogs exempt)
%   star order       — grep -nE 'prec\^?\\ast|prec\\sp\{\\ast' sections/*.tex -> nothing
%   endorser mass    — grep -nE '\bT_i\b' sections/D1_dynamics.tex -> nothing
%                      (App C bridge targets T_i are the sanctioned survivors)
%   stack strata     — grep -nE '\bL[012]\b' sections/*.tex -> review by hand
%                      (only taxonomy badges may carry bare L0/L1/L2)

%   θ_1,θ_2           §4 signed-SVD rotations (rem:graph:trace-determinant-recovery)
%   φ_1,φ_2           lem:graph:signed-svd-uniqueness proof angles
%   φ(s)              App D synchronized-sector map
%   σ                 App D/F perturbation floor (declared per-epoch noise floor)
%   σ, σ_C            App C realizing-forest path-count functions
%   σ*, σ'_C          §10 Nash-preservation strategy profiles
%   τ, τ_e, τ*, τ̄_c  GLOBAL: maturity family — single semantic, mint declined.
%                     REVISIT CLOSED at Edition 5: the tilt exponent was the second
%                     τ meaning, and it was given υ instead (\tiltexp), so τ keeps
%                     its monopoly.
%   ε, δ, γ, k        §10 approximation apparatus (shared analysis variables)
%   p_d, p_i, V, E, G, E_k, W_k, e   shared math (Tier 3, listed for closure)
% 
% ========================================================================================
% DESIGN PRINCIPLES (unchanged from the root)
%   1. One macro = one semantic concept; none overloaded.
%   2. Empty braces → bare symbol; non-empty → applied/indexed.
%   3. Internal \cs_new_protected:Npn (:n/:nn) + \NewDocumentCommand wrappers;
%      LaTeX2e interfaces as-is.
%   4. The CAN operates on raw (undamped) tensors; entropy damping applied once at
%      the thermodynamic boundary.  No symbol overloaded across unrelated concepts.
%   5. Standing flow uses the initiator-owned vouch projection: every hop is
%      one complete, positive, person-directed act authored by the hop's source
%      Actor; passive artifacts never carry standing.  The final source-target
%      flow \endflow{}{} is a certificate-clipped mixture of selected simple
%      projected paths through at most \vouchdepth complete acts.
%   6. (v0.15.0) A quantity that CLOSES gets a glyph; a quantity that only BOUNDS
%      gets a label and NO glyph.  The gap means "open frontier".
% ========================================================================================

% ========================================================================================
% §N7  THE COMPARATOR — NEUTRAL SOURCE AND RELATIVE STANDING   ★ THE LAYER-0 SEAM ★
%
%   This is the seam.  The network IMPORTS the neutral frame (\attest, read as
%   \burnval), names its shared ordered codomain (the comparator), CONSTRUCTS
%   the neutral source \commitrate on its side, and WELDS it onto the topology to
%   form the relative-standing field \standing.  \burnval may appear in a
%   network published-quantity formula (it is the imported interface object); the
%   [surface]/[core] surface macros may NOT.
%
%   ROLE MAP (do not collapse):
%     \burnval  fiber of the frame (per-actor)        — closes (source cost, L0)
%     codomain    the frame (NO glyph; inhabited)       — the comparator's reference
%     \commitrate neutral SOURCE (exogenous input)      — the one term topology lacks
%     \standing   THE COMPARATOR (gauge-fixed topology) — universal amplifier
% ========================================================================================

% THE COMPARATOR realized on the graph: the weighted MEDIANT
% α = [b_i + Σ W_end(j→i) b_j] / [max(N_i,1) + Σ W_end(j→i) N_j] —
% rate-DeGroot with action-mass weights (own weight N_i, endorser weight
% W·N_j).  Coincides EXACTLY with the uniform-activity DeGroot comparator
% (reduction theorem, def:epoch:standing); hull, anti-printer, anti-lurker
% invariants pinned in App F.  Canonical from v0.21.1.
% Glyph is α with the actor in the SUBSCRIPT (α_i).  App D's reduced
% α stays bare (the lint exempts App D + the signed-SVD internals).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_standing:n #1
{
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \alpha }
      { \alpha\sb{#1} }
}
% \standing{i} — CANONICAL comparator macro.
\NewDocumentCommand{\standing}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_standing:n{#1}}}

% The NEUTRAL SOURCE: r_i = \burnbal{i}/max(\actcount{i},1).  Reads the
% LEDGER, not the gross frame.  The UNIQUE
% EXOGENOUS input to the standing recursion — the one quantity the topology
% cannot generate (per-actor only as an IMPLEMENTATION of the imported frame;
% the object that matters is the shared codomain it inhabits).  Renders r / r_i.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_commitrate:n #1
{
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { r }
      { r\sb{#1} }
}
\NewDocumentCommand{\commitrate}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_commitrate:n{#1}}}

% The IMPORTED FRAME, fiber-wise: B_i := A_{key(i)}.  B_i when an argument is
% given; bare B otherwise.  Layer 0 WRITES this as attestation (\attest, A); the
% network READS it under B.  Glyph stays B (the A→B seam flip is load-bearing);
% only the cs NAME drops the false "count" — B is the continuous burn VALUE
% (continuous to 8 sig-figs per the index), never a tally.  Its FOUNDATIONAL
% content is the shared ordered codomain ℝ≥0 (the comparator's neutral frame —
% NO glyph; named in prose at def:comparator:imported-frame).  Non-decreasing at
% sampling depth; irrevocable.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_burnval:n #1
{
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { B }
      { B\sb{#1} }
}
\NewDocumentCommand{\burnval}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_burnval:n{#1}}}

% Bootstrap capacity bound B_max := A_max = E_0 ln(1/(1−ζ)): the bound that holds
% the comparator SOURCE-faithful against the costless Sybil through the pre-market
% interval.  The network's reading of \attestcap.
% COLLIDES: \burnval B_i — "max" subscript vs actor label.
\NewDocumentCommand{\burncap}{}{\ensuremath{B\sb{\max}}}

% Cumulative action count: N_i (per-actor).  Layer~1 quantity; the denominator of
% the neutral source r_i.  Non-decreasing.  Distinct from epoch length N_epoch.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_actcount:n #1
{
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { N }
      { N\sb{#1} }
}
\NewDocumentCommand{\actcount}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_actcount:n{#1}}}

% RETIRED v0.21.1: \excessburn — superseded by \burnbal; see changelog.
% Residual balance (THE ledger): b_i = B_i − Σ_a θ^{(k_a)} — the imported frame
% net of consummated θ-debits.  V2 at read (ν-current); the debit schedule is
% V3 (never re-calibrated).  Replaces the retired excess-burn macro (semantics
% changed: constant-ν diagnostic → θ-schedule ledger).  COLLIDES: App D
% circulant local b (post:dynamics:minimal-oscillator; qualify at first use).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_burnbal:n #1
{
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { b }
      { b\sb{#1} }
}
\NewDocumentCommand{\burnbal}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_burnbal:n{#1}}}

% ========================================================================================
% §N7d  EDITION-5 CONSERVED ALLOCATION STANDING
%
% k = epoch index.  i, u, j, v = Actor indices.  r = hop index, m = depth index.
%
% Published standing remains alpha / alpha-hat (\epochstanding, \epochrefstanding,
% retained below).  The internal reduced coordinate remains x exclusively — the
% Edition-4 reservation survives; its stage indices do not.
%
% This block REPLACES the Edition-4 staged-standing names (\finalstage,
% \stagestanding, \stagestandingvector, \standingstage, \standingstagevector,
% \stagebox, \finalstandingflow, \admittedmass, \stagerowcert, \stagerowcertrow)
% with the conserved-allocation spine:
%
%     acts -> fold cells -> 𝖠_{uj} -> Λ^{(r)}(𝐱) -> 𝚷(𝐱) -> mediant -> 𝐱* -> 𝓚_k
%
% The retired names are deliberately left undefined so every stale call site fails
% until a later migration guide repoints it.  A failed reference is the point.
%
% Chartered glyphs (sign-off checklist §A, G1–G5, B1/B2/B4, D4′):
%   𝖠_{uj}   sans A, base allocation score — the Layer-0 seam glyphs (A = \attest,
%            B = \burnval) are never reused at Layer 1, and face, not weight,
%            carries the distance.  Probe-confirmed against italic A at every size.
%   υ_r      tilt exponent.  NOT τ: the maturity family keeps that letter.
%   Υ_m(t)   cumulative tilt.  NOT S_m: the S-family is a chartered three-way.
%   F_{k,i}  conserved standing map.  NOT Φ: quadruple-loaded.
%   𝔪_m      depth mass.  NOT μ_m: μ is \redundancy, \fenceslack and App-D local.
%   𝚷        conserved transport, BOLD against the roman \actbundle Π(j,s,t,f) —
%            the \canval V / \matcanval 𝐕 precedent.
%   ~b, ~N   transported pair aggregates.  NOT β: β is \invtemp.
%   𝔢_u      source emission (D4 chartered).  Fraktur: roman e is the App-F
%            reference edges and Euler's constant.
%   𝔈, 𝐈     the emission diagonal and the identity it mixes against.  Fraktur E
%            because roman E is the epoch edge set; bold I because roman I_C is
%            the improvement index.
%
% \norm (used by \tiltnorm) is Layer-0 [found] stratum, declared in
% macros_attestation.tex.  Cross-seam consumption of [found] is the design, not a
% leak; do not re-flag it.
%
% TWO EXISTING MACROS THIS BLOCK LEANS ON, EASILY CONFUSED:
%   \refrate{u}      r̂_u   reduced RATE b_u/(ν N_u) — the mediant's coordinate and
%                          the emission input 𝔢_u = min(1, r̂_u/ρ_θ).
%   \refstanding{i}  α̂_i   reduced STANDING — the OUTPUT, and the gate input.
% Writing α̂ where r̂ belongs type-checks and renders; it is simply wrong.
% ========================================================================================


% Final full standing at epoch k: alpha_i^(k).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_epochstanding:nn #1#2
  {
    \alpha\sb{#2}\sp{(#1)}
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\epochstanding}{m m}
  {
    \ensuremath{\network_epochstanding:nn{#1}{#2}}
  }

% Final reduced standing at epoch k: alpha-hat_i^(k).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_epochrefstanding:nn #1#2
  {
    \hat{\alpha}\sb{#2}\sp{(#1)}
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\epochrefstanding}{m m}
  {
    \ensuremath{\network_epochrefstanding:nn{#1}{#2}}
  }

% ── Fold and score layer (P5, P6) ───────────────────────────────────────
% Standing fold cell ξ: the order-free unit of standing input.  Lowercase ξ
% against \campaignscalar Ξ_A — case distinguishes.
\NewDocumentCommand{\foldcell}{}{\ensuremath{\xi}}

  { \symcal{R}\sb{#1} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\foldcells}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_foldcells:n{#1}}}

% Total effective fold coefficient c(ξ) ∈ (0,1].  Reuses the c(·) glyph freed by
% \relationcoef; SEMANTICS CHANGED — total over all act classes, self included.

  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { c } { c(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\foldcoef}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_foldcoef:n{#1}}}

% Recipient resolution rcp(ξ) → Actor j or self.  Operator form, deliberately
% not the letter R (reward R_C, freed 𝓡).
\NewDocumentCommand{\resolve}{m}{\ensuremath{\operatorname{rcp}(#1)}}

% Published domain weight ω_D.  Against \depweight ω_{n→c}: domain subscript vs
% arrow subscript.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_domweight:n #1
  { \omega\sb{#1} }

% Act-level domain profile δ_D(ξ), summing to one over D.  Applied two-index
% form distinguishes it from δ_pos, δ_liq, δ_map.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_domprofile:nn #1#2
  { \delta\sb{#1}(#2) }
\NewDocumentCommand{\domprofile}{m m}{\ensuremath{\network_domprofile:nn{#1}{#2}}}

% Base allocation score 𝖠_{uj} = κ_self·1{u=j} + Σ_ξ c(ξ) Σ_D ω_D δ_D(ξ).
% SANS-SERIF: the Layer-0 seam glyphs (A = \attest, B = \burnval) are never
% reused at Layer 1, and face — not weight — carries the distance.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_basescore:nn #1#2
  { \symsf{A}\sb{#1#2} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\basescore}{m m}{\ensuremath{\network_basescore:nn{#1}{#2}}}

% Self-retention base κ_self.  NEVER bare κ: three κ already exist.

% ── Tilt layer (P7) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% Chartered tilt shape υ_r^∘ = (1, ½, ¼, ⅛) under profile B (D1).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_tiltshape:n #1
  { \upsilon\sb{#1}\sp{\circ} }
\NewDocumentCommand{\tiltshape}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_tiltshape:n{#1}}}

% Applied tilt exponent υ_r(t) = t·υ_r^∘.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_tiltexp:nn #1#2
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#2}
      { \upsilon\sb{#1} }
      { \upsilon\sb{#1}(#2) } }

% Profile vector and its L1 volume — the prior-screen coordinate.

% Accepted tilt strength t_k.  Reuses the t_k form freed by \stageadmission;

  { t\sb{#1} }

% Published tilt grid 𝓖_t and its chartered depth J_tilt.
\NewDocumentCommand{\tiltgrid}{}{\ensuremath{\symcal{G}\sb{t}}}

% Cumulative profile through hop m: Υ_m(t) = Σ_{r≤m} υ_r(t).  Capital upsilon,
% same family as υ_r; the S-family is a chartered three-way and stays closed.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_tiltcum:nn #1#2

% Migration Guide 15.  The atomic authored act q, its record projection, the

%   structural body    body(q)             — operator; NEVER the letter S (Schwarzian
%                                            / \settlement 𝓢 / centrality S_C).
%   proposal nonce     \mathsf{n}_q        — sans n; NOT a node identifier n.
%   commitments        C^{pre/con/dep}_q, salts s^{con/dep}_q, signatures
%                      σ^{pre/ver/app}_q   — roman C/s and σ with a role SUPERSCRIPT and
%                      the act in the subscript; NOT \creditset 𝓒 (calligraphic C).
%   ordered sequence   Q_k                 — capital Q, epoch subscript; NOT the
%                                            temporal-entropy kernel Q_η (η subscript).
%   dependency list    D_q                 — roman D, act subscript; NOT the interaction
%                                            domains 𝒟_I/𝒟_E (calligraphic D).

% ========================================================================================
% §N18  COUPLED DYNAMICS (App D) — ACTIVATION, GAIN, SCHWARZIAN, SPECTRAL, DRIFT
%
%   Layer~1-owned; consumed by §5 (the bond), §6 (the epoch convergence summary),
%   App F (verification), App G (the open cluster).  The Self-edge bond scalar
%   self-map is the SUBSET; these names cover the coupled extension.  No tier
%   macros: status is carried by the theorem/proposition/conjecture environment.
%
% ========================================================================================
% §N18a  EDITION-4 PROJECTED VOUCH ACTIVATION AND EFFECTIVE WALL GAIN
%
% g_vch      = smooth responsive base activation.
% bar-g_vch  = current safety-wall-clamped effective activation.
% tilde-g    = normalized deployed p-core.
%
% lambda_vch      = smooth responsive reduced-standing gain (retained \vouchgain).
% bar-lambda_vch  = effective generalized wall-clamped gain (new \wallvouchgain).
% lambda_Q        = clean full-depth screening envelope (retained \loggain).
%
% RETIRED at Edition 4: \bondact (rendered g_vch) and \redact (rendered
% tilde-g) — the responsive base is now \vouchactivation, the effective
% deployed activation is \wallactivation, and the normalized p-core is
% \vouchcore.  The retired names are deliberately left undefined.
% ========================================================================================

% Responsive smooth projected activation g_vch(x).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_vouchactivation:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      {
        g\sb{\mathrm{vch}}
      }
      {
        g\sb{\mathrm{vch}}(#1)
      }
  }
% EDITION-5 CONTRACT: this is the BASE of the recipient tilt.  The deployed form
% is the wall-clamped \wallactivation raised to \tiltexp{r}{t}, applied per
% recipient column at every hop.  It is no longer a per-edge activation.
\NewDocumentCommand{\vouchactivation}{m}
  {
    \ensuremath{\network_vouchactivation:n{#1}}
  }

% Effective current safety-wall-clamped activation bar-g_vch(x).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_wallactivation:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      {
        \bar{g}\sb{\mathrm{vch}}
      }
      {
        \bar{g}\sb{\mathrm{vch}}(#1)
      }
  }
% EDITION-5 CONTRACT: applied per RECIPIENT COLUMN at every hop, as
% \wallactivation{x_j}^{\tiltexp{r}{t}} inside \hopalloc.  Below the wall it is
% flat and dynamically inert; the self share is never modulated.
\NewDocumentCommand{\wallactivation}{m}
  {
    \ensuremath{\network_wallactivation:n{#1}}
  }

% Normalized deployed p-core tilde-g(p).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_vouchcore:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      {
        \tilde{g}
      }
      {
        \tilde{g}(#1)
      }
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\vouchcore}{m}
  {
    \ensuremath{\network_vouchcore:n{#1}}
  }

% Effective generalized wall-clamped reduced-standing gain bar-lambda_vch(x).
%
% Below wall: 0.
% At wall: [0, lambda_vch(rho_theta)].
% Above wall: lambda_vch(x).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_wallvouchgain:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      {
        \bar{\lambda}\sb{\mathrm{vch}}
      }
      {
        \bar{\lambda}\sb{\mathrm{vch}}(#1)
      }
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\wallvouchgain}{m}
  {
    \ensuremath{\network_wallvouchgain:n{#1}}
  }

%   ── gain ──
% Clean full-depth standing-gain envelope:
%   \loggain{}      -> lambda_Q
%   \loggain{x}     -> lambda_Q(x)
% This is the eta=0 conservative full-Q reduced-standing gain used by
% Fcert2, the safety-threshold screen, and the depth-four width fence.
% It is NOT the exact per-hop projected gain.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_loggain:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \lambda\sb{Q} }
      { \lambda\sb{Q}(#1) }
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\loggain}{m}
  { \ensuremath{\network_loggain:n{#1}} }

% Inverse of the clean full-depth screen, lambda_Q^{-1}(.).  Well defined
% because \loggain is strictly decreasing (lem:dynamics:monotone-gain), so
% the safety-threshold rule can be read either way round.
%
% Minted because the generated values registry was hand-typing
% "\lambda_Q^{-1}(...)" -- a BARE LAMBDA, which the register forbids
% everywhere else, in the one file no reviewer reads.  A macro is not
% decoration here: it is what makes the prohibition checkable.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_loggaininv:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \lambda\sb{Q}\sp{-1} }
      { \lambda\sb{Q}\sp{-1}(#1) }
  }
\NewDocumentCommand{\loggaininv}{m}
  { \ensuremath{\network_loggaininv:n{#1}} }

% Exact deployed per-hop projected-vouch gain:
%   \vouchgain{}    -> lambda_vch
%   \vouchgain{x}   -> lambda_vch(x)
% Satisfies L_vch * lambda_vch <= lambda_Q.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_vouchgain:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \lambda\sb{\mathrm{vch}} }
      { \lambda\sb{\mathrm{vch}}(#1) }
  }
% EDITION-5 CONTRACT: this IS Edition-5's ell(x).  No bare ell macro is minted
% (ell collides with ell_0, ell_1).  Its value at the wall is \wallgaincap,
% bar-ell, the constant in the hop-profile width fence.
\NewDocumentCommand{\vouchgain}{m}
  { \ensuremath{\network_vouchgain:n{#1}} }

% Exact projected p-coordinate gain:
%   \vouchpgain{}   -> kappa_vch
%   \vouchpgain{p}  -> kappa_vch(p)
% where kappa_vch = d/dp log g_vch.
% Distinct from the reduced-standing gain
% lambda_vch(x)=(1-p)^2 kappa_vch(p).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_vouchpgain:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \kappa\sb{\mathrm{vch}} }
      { \kappa\sb{\mathrm{vch}}(#1) }
  }
% EDITION-5 CONTRACT: the certified criticality partition covers the BASE curve
% only.  Each hop deploys a different power, \wallactivation^{\tiltexp{r}{t}}
% (1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 at t=1 under profile B — hop 1 is exactly the existing
% certified exponent).  Per-hop powered artifacts are separate, per-exponent, and
% non-load-bearing: safety is the certificate, not the partition.
\NewDocumentCommand{\vouchpgain}{m}
  { \ensuremath{\network_vouchpgain:n{#1}} }

% RETIRED at Edition 4: \maxgain (L_w).  Under the safety-wall clamp the relevant
% gain supremum is explicitly attained at the wall, sup bar-lambda_vch =
% lambda_vch(rho_theta); write \loggain{\safefloor} (lambda_Q(rho_theta)) for the
% clean full-depth screen instead of a separate L_w glyph.  Deliberately undefined.

% Floquet / critical-multiplier angle (App D).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_floqangle:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \theta } { \theta\sb{#1} } }

  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { S\,#2 } { S\sb{#1}\,#2 } }

%   ── reduced rate, dispersion, stability product ──

\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_refrate:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \hat{r} } { \hat{r}\sb{#1} } }

% write \refstanding (alpha-hat, the OUTPUT) in its place: both compile.
\NewDocumentCommand{\refrate}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_refrate:n{#1}}}

% Endorser weighted-mean rate: \endorsemean{i} -> r̄_i
% (eq:dynamics:endorsement-aggregates-r); \endorsemean{ik} -> r̄_{ik}
% (per-channel relay mean); \endorsemean{-k} -> r̄_{-k} (leave-k-out);
% \endorsemean{} -> r̄.  The DeGroot WEIGHT-mean of contributing rates — NOT
% \pooledrate (ρ̄, action-mass pooled); the two coincide only on uniform
% activity (the mediant reduction theorem).
% COLLIDES: \meanedgenorm w̄(n) (letter); §4 locals w̄_c, r̄_c (subscript c +
% local declaration); \refrate r̂ (hat vs bar); App F hatted forms stay
% declared-local.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_endorsemean:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \bar{r} } { \bar{r}\sb{#1} } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\endorsemean}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_endorsemean:n{#1}}}

% Fixed-point crossing gap Φ_× = ℓ − R: the strictly convex discriminant whose
% unique zero is the scalar fixed point (eq:dynamics:fixed-point-crossing).
% Minted v0.21.1 to de-overload Φ: \elast is the ELASTICITY α·λ(α) and never
% again denotes ℓ−R.  \crossgap{} -> Φ_× ; \crossgap{\alpha} -> Φ_×(α).
% COLLIDES: \elast Φ(·), \prosp Φ(v,d), \elastmax Φ_max — subscript ×
% distinguishes at source level.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_crossgap:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \Phi\sb{\times} }
      { \Phi\sb{\times}(#1) } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\crossgap}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_crossgap:n{#1}}}

% Reduced-rate dispersion Δ̂ = r̂_max − r̂_min (NEVER the hull ratio r_max/r_min).
\NewDocumentCommand{\ratespan}{}{\ensuremath{\hat{\Delta}}}

% RETIRED at Edition 4: \stabprod (the monolithic lambda_Q(x*) * Delta-hat
% screening product).  Edition 4 screens with the explicit width screen

% \stagerowcert{k}{h}; write the product explicitly rather than reviving a

%   ── spectral / coupling ──
% Exact per-channel cap for a stated projected motif:
%   kappa_max = 1/4 * lambda_vch(x*) * Delta-hat.
% It is NOT one quarter of the clean screening product \stabprod.
\NewDocumentCommand{\chancap}{}{\ensuremath{\kappa\sb{\max}}}

% Endorsement (coupling) graph 𝓔; directed cycles are the oscillation locus.
\NewDocumentCommand{\endorsegraph}{}{\ensuremath{\symcal{E}}}

%   ── drift / criticality data ──

\NewDocumentCommand{\lyapone}{}{\ensuremath{\ell\sb{1}}}

% EDITION-5 CONTRACT (this macro and \endorsemean, \endorsegraph, \crossgap):
% ANALYSIS-ONLY.  Their normative role died with the direct-vouch scalar self-map;
% they survive for the dynamics appendix's own reasoning and must not appear in a
% normative standing formula unless a scalar reduction theorem is re-proved over

% Endorser structural mass Σ_i (was bare T_i; renamed to free T_i for bridge
% targets).  ALWAYS applied/subscripted; never the summation operator.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_endorsermass:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1} { \symit{\Sigma} } { \symit{\Sigma}\sb{#1} } }
\NewDocumentCommand{\endorsermass}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_endorsermass:n{#1}}}

% RETIRED at Edition 4: \rowcert (K_row / K_row^(k)).  The row certificate is now

% Local contributing width: the width-fence input (def:dynamics:local-width).
% Additive width (max - min) of the contributing rate set, maximized over
% dynamically-live actors; published per epoch beside \rowcert.  CLOSES,
% hence the glyph.  Widths live in RATE space and are mass-blind; unchanged
% under the mediant.  \locwidth{} -> W_loc ; \locwidth{k} -> W_loc^{(k)}.
% COLLIDES: \endflow W_end, \posreg/\negreg W^± -- "loc" subscript distinguishes.
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_locwidth:n #1
  { \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { W\sb{\mathrm{loc}} }
      { W\sb{\mathrm{loc}}\sp{(#1)} } }
% EDITION-5 CONTRACT: the contributing set is redefined — sources with POSITIVE
% TRANSPORTED MASS (\transportentry{u}{i} > 0), not selected-path clip support.
% Because the support of \transport{} is fixed by the base scores and the ledger
% alone, this width is checkable BEFORE the solve; Edition 4 could not do that.
\NewDocumentCommand{\locwidth}{m}{\ensuremath{\network_locwidth:n{#1}}}

% Minimum safe SAFETY WALL at contributing width W:
%   \minsafewall{}  -> rho_{theta,min}
%   \minsafewall{W} -> rho_{theta,min}(W)
% This is the inverse clean full-depth gain screen used by the
% width fence (cor:dynamics:minimal-safe-wall); small-wall asymptote
% W/2.  It is a safety-wall quantity, not a policy/effective
% participation floor.  CLOSES, hence the glyph.

% distinguish); \specrad family (applied-to-matrix vs applied-to-width).
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_minsafewall:n #1
  {
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \rho\sb{\theta,\min} }
      { \rho\sb{\theta,\min}(#1) }
  }
% EDITION-5 CONTRACT: the function is unchanged; the fence that CONSUMES it is
% the hop-profile width fence, and the corollary stating it descends from
% lem:dynamics:monotone-gain, not from the retired depth-four budget.
\NewDocumentCommand{\minsafewall}{m}
  { \ensuremath{\network_minsafewall:n{#1}} }

% RETIRED at Edition 4: \massratio (rendered x_i).  The symbol x is now reserved

%   ── named activation conditions (prose-rendered; no glyph) ──
% (P4): the Möbius-covariant flip condition S_p\tilde g > 3/2 K² on [½,1).
\NewDocumentCommand{\condPfour}{}{\textnormal{(P4)}}

\NewDocumentCommand{\condPfourNS}{}{\textnormal{(P4\nobreakdash-NS)}}

% Conditional-result mark (App D; the honesty-parity device).  A superscript
% dagger, hyperlinked to the open item (conjecture or named residual) it hangs on, flagging a theorem or
% proposition whose statement carries a CONDITIONAL clause.  Placed FIRST in the
% environment's optional note so it reads as a mark on the head ("Theorem† …");
% its meaning is resolved in the App C head ("What is settled, and where").  This
% imports the STRONG honesty system's lesson — a label-without-glyph MEANS open
% frontier, legible ON THE PAGE — into the WEAK environment-as-status convention,
% so conjecture-dependence is LOCALLY visible, not legible only by reading which
% conjecture the body happens to cite.  Argument: the conjecture label.
\NewDocumentCommand{\condmark}{m}{\hyperref[#1]{\ensuremath{\sp{\dagger}}}\,}

% NOTE (deliberate non-coinage, mirroring App D's label-without-glyph convention):
%   • the report's saturation map ψ(W)=W/(1+W) is rendered with the EXISTING \sat (sat);
%     ψ is NOT coined (ψ is \fpm/\fpl).
%   • the circulant locals a,b,P,ω,σ get NO macros — declared at
%     post:dynamics:minimal-oscillator and scoped there.
%   • status is the ENVIRONMENT (theorem proved / proposition-under-conjecture /
%     conjecture open) — no [PROVED]/[NUMERICAL]/[EXTREMAL]/[OPEN] tier tags.  A
%     CONDITIONAL clause inside a theorem or proposition is ADDITIONALLY flagged
%     with \condmark (a † hyperlinked to the named conjecture): the environment
%     carries the default status, the † carries the local exception.

% ========================================================================================
% §N19  RESEARCH FRONTIERS (App G) — taxonomic frontier apparatus   [Layer 1 owned]
%
%   Green-field replacement for the [found] open-problem apparatus (\OpenProblem,
%   \OpenSubProblem, \ProposedInvestigation), which is RETIRED for Layer 1.  Pre-1.0
%   policy: backwards compatibility — including cross-reference labels — is an explicit
%   non-goal (main.tex header).  Layer 0 keeps its own apparatus in macros_attestation.tex;
%   every name below is NEW and disjoint, so nothing is redefined.
%
%   LABEL NAMESPACE (flat, species-independent):   frontier:<name>
%     The taxonomic SPECIES is carried by the reference TYPE (the stepped counter),
%     NEVER by the label string.  Reclassifying an entry changes its \zcref TEXT
%     ("Open Problem" -> "Guild Design Choice") but never its label, so no inbound
%     \zcref breaks.  This is the deliberate fix for taxonomy churn.
%
%   SIX numbered species  (counter / printed name):
%     core    frontiercore     Open Problem            — the narrow Layer-1 list (admission/faithfulness)
%     calib   frontiercalib    Calibration Obligation  — pre-lock, not unsolved
%     arch    frontierarch     Architectural Extension — expansion, not defect
%     guild   frontierguild    Guild Design Choice     — Layer-2 freedom (post:transport:guild-grant)
%     witness frontierwitness  Ceiling Witness         — bounded instance of a PROVED §2 limit
%     invest  frontierinvest   Proposed Investigation  — numerical exercise
%   plus  sub  frontiersub  — child of core (alphabetic: G.1a, G.1b)
%   plus  \frontierpointer  — UNNUMBERED Layer-0 courtesy pointer.
%
%   Each numbered entry self-adds to the ToC at subsubsection level (\numberline,
%   bookmark-safe); App G is fully navigable.  Titles containing math MUST pass a
%   plain bookmark string in the optional [..] slot (the on-page heading still uses the
%   math title).  Per-species numbering coexists like figures/tables ("Open Problem G.1",
%   "Calibration Obligation G.1") — disambiguated by the species name in every \zcref.
% ========================================================================================

% --- counters (per-species, section-reset; subs alphabetic under their core parent) ---
\newcounter{frontiercore}[section]
\newcounter{frontiercalib}[section]
\newcounter{frontierarch}[section]
\newcounter{frontierguild}[section]
\newcounter{frontierwitness}[section]
\newcounter{frontierinvest}[section]
\newcounter{frontiersub}[frontiercore]

\cs_set:Npn \thefrontiercore    { \thesection.\arabic{frontiercore} }
\cs_set:Npn \thefrontiercalib   { \thesection.\arabic{frontiercalib} }
\cs_set:Npn \thefrontierarch    { \thesection.\arabic{frontierarch} }
\cs_set:Npn \thefrontierguild   { \thesection.\arabic{frontierguild} }
\cs_set:Npn \thefrontierwitness { \thesection.\arabic{frontierwitness} }
\cs_set:Npn \thefrontierinvest  { \thesection.\arabic{frontierinvest} }
\cs_set:Npn \thefrontiersub     { \thefrontiercore \alph{frontiersub} }

\cs_set:Npn \theHfrontiercore    { frontier.core.\arabic{section}.\arabic{frontiercore} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHfrontiercalib   { frontier.calib.\arabic{section}.\arabic{frontiercalib} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHfrontierarch    { frontier.arch.\arabic{section}.\arabic{frontierarch} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHfrontierguild   { frontier.guild.\arabic{section}.\arabic{frontierguild} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHfrontierwitness { frontier.witness.\arabic{section}.\arabic{frontierwitness} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHfrontierinvest  { frontier.invest.\arabic{section}.\arabic{frontierinvest} }
\cs_set:Npn \theHfrontiersub
  { frontier.sub.\arabic{section}.\arabic{frontiercore}.\arabic{frontiersub} }

% --- frontier reference-type names are key-val configuration and live in
%     main.tex, OUTSIDE the expl3 wrap ---

% --- numbered entry:  \begin{frontier}[plain-toc]{species}{name}{Title} ---
%   [plain-toc] OPTIONAL: bookmark/ToC-safe string; REQUIRED if Title contains math.
\tl_new:N \l__network_frontier_num_tl

\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_frontier:nnnn #1#2#3#4
  {
    \str_case:nnF {#2}
      {
        {core}    { \refstepcounter{frontiercore}    \tl_set:Nx \l__network_frontier_num_tl { \thefrontiercore }    }
        {calib}   { \refstepcounter{frontiercalib}   \tl_set:Nx \l__network_frontier_num_tl { \thefrontiercalib }   }
        {arch}    { \refstepcounter{frontierarch}    \tl_set:Nx \l__network_frontier_num_tl { \thefrontierarch }    }
        {guild}   { \refstepcounter{frontierguild}   \tl_set:Nx \l__network_frontier_num_tl { \thefrontierguild }   }
        {witness} { \refstepcounter{frontierwitness} \tl_set:Nx \l__network_frontier_num_tl { \thefrontierwitness } }
        {invest}  { \refstepcounter{frontierinvest}  \tl_set:Nx \l__network_frontier_num_tl { \thefrontierinvest }  }
      }
      { \typeout{PEERNET~WARNING:~unknown~frontier~species~'#2'~(entry~'#3')} }
    \label{frontier:#3}
    \par \addvspace{\medskipamount}
    \noindent \textbf{\l__network_frontier_num_tl \quad #4.}\enspace \ignorespaces
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{\protect\numberline{\l__network_frontier_num_tl}#4} }
      { \addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{\protect\numberline{\l__network_frontier_num_tl}#1} }
  }
\NewDocumentEnvironment{frontier}{O{} m m m}
  { \network_frontier:nnnn {#1}{#2}{#3}{#4} }
  { \par }

% --- sub-problem (child of the enclosing core entry; not ToC-listed) ---
\cs_new_protected:Npn \network_frontiersub:nn #1#2
  {
    \refstepcounter{frontiersub}
    \label{frontier:#1}
    \par \addvspace{\smallskipamount}
    \noindent \emph{\thefrontiersub \quad #2.}\enspace \ignorespaces
  }
\NewDocumentEnvironment{frontiersub}{m m}
  { \network_frontiersub:nn {#1}{#2} }
  { \par }

% --- Layer-0 courtesy pointer (UNNUMBERED, not a Layer-1 item; ToC-listed) ---
\NewDocumentCommand{\frontierpointer}{O{} m}
  {
    \par \addvspace{\medskipamount}
    \noindent \textbf{#2.}\enspace \ignorespaces
    \tl_if_blank:nTF {#1}
      { \addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{#2} }
      { \addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{#1} }
  }

% --- uniform, greppable field helpers (optional, used inside an entry body) ---
\NewDocumentCommand{\frontierstatus}  {m}{ \emph{Status:}~#1 }
\NewDocumentCommand{\frontierpriority}{m}{ \emph{Priority:}~#1 }
\NewDocumentCommand{\frontieropen}    {m}{ \emph{Open~content:}~#1 }
\NewDocumentCommand{\frontierremedy}  {m}{ \emph{Remedy:}~#1 }
\NewDocumentCommand{\frontierxref}    {m}{ \emph{Cross-references:}~\zcref{#1} }
