% ============================================================================
% macros_values_runtime.tex — the \numval / \numrel accessors for the generated
% number registry.
%
% The generated values_macros.tex (from papers/network/math/derive.py via
% packages/values_codegen) declares data only: two prop-lists keyed by
% <id>.<form> — \g_num_value_prop (the rendered value/symbol) and
% \g_num_exact_prop (1 exact / 0 inexact). This hand-written file defines the
% accessors and their fail-closed error. Load the generated file first, then
% this file.
% ============================================================================
\ExplSyntaxOn

\msg_new:nnn { values } { unknown-id }
  { Unknown~number~id~'#1'~--~not~present~in~the~generated~values~registry. }

\cs_new:Npn \num_unknown_id:n #1
  { \msg_error:nnn { values } { unknown-id } {#1} }

% \numval{<id>.<form>} -> the BARE rendered value (.num rounded / .exact
% symbolic), no relation prefix. Use it inside tables and formulas. A hard error
% if the id/form is absent (renamed or not yet declared).
\NewDocumentCommand \numval { m }
  {
    \prop_if_in:NnTF \g_num_value_prop {#1}
      { \prop_item:Nn \g_num_value_prop {#1} }
      { \num_unknown_id:n {#1} }
  }

% \numrel{<id>.<form>} -> the value PREFIXED by its relation operator: `=` when
% the form is exact (a symbolic form, or a decimal that equals the true value),
% `\approx` when it is a rounding. The operator is generated from the exactness
% flag, never hand-typed, so it tracks the value. Use it where the paper writes
% `<symbol> = <value>` / `<symbol> \approx <value>`.
\NewDocumentCommand \numrel { m }
  {
    \prop_if_in:NnTF \g_num_exact_prop {#1}
      {
        \str_if_eq:eeTF { \prop_item:Nn \g_num_exact_prop {#1} } { 1 }
          { = }
          { \approx }
        \numval{#1}
      }
      { \num_unknown_id:n {#1} }
  }

\ExplSyntaxOff
% --- END included content from: macros_values_runtime.tex ---

%========================================================================================
% FILENAME: 00_title.tex (v0.24.2-dev)
%
% Front matter for Peer Network (Layer 1): title, abstract, motto.
% Owns \setversion{v0.24.2-dev}; \docversion is live from here onward.
%
% CHANGELOG:
%   v0.24.2-dev  Artifact update semantics.  Updating a node can only mean
%                authoring a new record about it, because records are
%                immutable; this line makes that legal where it was not.
%                The genesis role becomes a property of the RECORD rather
%                than of the family -- an act mints iff its terminal target
%                is its own mint -- so an ordinary act of the same family
%                may name an existing node.  Layer 1 gains the permission
%                and nothing else: which version is current stays a Layer-2
%                fold, because deciding that here is the failure the
%                architecture refuses.  Chat is the exception, revising by
%                succession rather than in place.  Minor-level surface in a
%                patch line because no existing act changes meaning: every
%                record legal before is legal now, with the same weight.

%   v0.24.1-dev  Edition 5 residue: the self-audit repair line.  Edition 5
%                deleted its retired objects at the macro layer and trusted
%                compile failure to find the call sites -- which it did, for
%                every site that named one.  Prose describing candidates,
%                selection, clips and stages without naming a deleted macro
%                compiled perfectly and survived, and eleven months on it has
%                stopped reading as stale and started reading as current.
%                This line clears that residue: the scalability chapter's
%                retired enumeration crisis, App I's retired replay sequence,
%                the screen-versus-certificate ruling, the coefficient of a

%                and the census rows still printing "standing: none".

%                Names that go, go with the machinery they described, so a
%                citation to one now fails loudly rather than resolving to

%                aliases -- 191 retired names, 0 live uses -- and replaced by
%                one conserved operator: acts fold into a base allocation
%                matrix, hop matrices tilt it, a published depth mass mixes

\setversion{v0.24.2-dev}

\title{Peer Network}
\author{PeerNetwork GmbH \\ \docversion}
\date{\today}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
    \label{abs:abstract}

    PeerNetwork is an engine for \textbf{non-trivially comparing
    clusters} of social interaction --- and it earns the word
    \emph{non-trivially} against a precise obstruction.  A network has
    value only insofar as it can weigh one community's standing against
    another's; but cluster topology is invariant under relabeling, so
    every purely structural quantity is gauge, and communities of the
    same internal shape are interchangeable.  That interchangeability
    is constructible: fabricating a plausible community is the act of
    building relabeling-equivalent structure.  No function of the graph
    alone can compare clusters.  Comparison requires a scalar the graph
    cannot generate --- \emph{exogenous in origin, neutral,
    non-transferable, monotone, and bound onto the topology}
    (\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}).  Such a scalar breaks
    the relabeling symmetry and converts absolute position into
    \emph{relative} position --- and only relative position is
    comparable.

    The Peer stack supplies this in two layers because the frame must be
    exogenous to the topology it measures.  \textbf{Layer~0 (Peer
    Attestation)} exports one object, the attestation map
    $\attest{}:\addrspace\to\R_{\geq0}$, and --- by declining to price
    it --- guarantees its neutrality
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:neutrality-from-silence}).  \textbf{This
    document (Layer~1)} binds that frame to a public directed graph and
    forms the neutral source
    \[
        \commitrate{i}
        =
        \frac{\burnbal{i}}{\max(\actcount{i},1)},
    \]
    where $\burnbal{i}$ is the residual balance of destroyed value net
    of consummated per-action debits
    (\zcref{def:comparator:rate,def:comparator:residual-balance}).

    Standing does not traverse arbitrary raw graph legs.  Layer~1 weighs
    \emph{every} accepted Actor-authored act of the epoch, at the act level,
    and resolves each by a published order-free rule to a person recipient or
    to the author's own retention channel
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection,%
    def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  A Reference or Invitation is
    consumed as one matched complete act; passive Chats, Content, Items,
    Types, Comments, Messages, Offers, and Profiles provide context without
    inheriting or redirecting allocation.  Every Actor then disposes of
    exactly one conserved unit of allocation over self and the recipients its
    own acts name: what one recipient gains, the siblings and the source's own
    retention lose.  Recipient standing tilts that division hop by hop, at
    full strength in the allocation of the Actor whose mass is flowing and
    fading with distance, and the whole system is solved as one same-epoch
    equilibrium admitted at the greatest tilt strength whose certificate
    passes.

    The conserved transport $\transportentry{u}{i}$ enters the
    \textbf{relative-standing field} as the exact post-debit
    balance/count mediant:
    \[
        \standing{i}
        =
        \frac{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\,\burnbal{u}
        }{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u}
        }.
    \]
    This is the comparator realized on the graph
    (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}): the frame welded to actor-authored
    delegation without allowing passive structure or unmatched
    hyper-edge legs to reroute it.  The comparator has one binding and
    two terminal readouts --- feed visibility and reward share
    (\zcref{ins:comparator:universal-amplifier}).  Sybil resistance is
    the security reading of the same measurement property
    (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}).

    The comparator stands on source cost and accountability cost
    (\zcref{tbl:comparator:two-costs}).  Source cost closes standing
    against fabricated source; accountability cost prices authored
    claims but remains endogenous, so it bounds the edge-semantic axis
    without closing it
    (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost,%
    rem:comparator:structural-ceiling}).  Every quantity affecting
    standing, ranking, or reward is fixed by published formula over the
    public record and independently reproducible from records,
    constants, folded acts, the base matrix, emission fractions, and certificates
    alone.  The resulting comparator is not merely defined but
    \textbf{auditable by the agents it measures}: no participant,
    including the operator, may own the neutral frame, splice another
    actor's source through an artifact, or silently redirect the
    standing field.
\end{abstract}

\begin{motto}
    \label{motto:motto}
    One graph, one neutral frame, one comparator --- standing no one can
    fake or reroute; what you are shown and what you are owed, yours to
    recompute.
\end{motto}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

This document specifies an engine for one thing: \textbf{comparing clusters} of
social interaction. A network has value only insofar as it can weigh one
community's standing against another's --- and every social platform already
does this, continuously, to decide what each person is shown and what each
contribution is worth. The question this document answers is not whether such a
comparison happens. It is who owns the instrument that performs it, whether
anyone can see it, and whether the people it measures can reproduce its verdict.

The chapter is foundational and human at once. It states why a comparator cannot
be drawn from the social graph alone and must rest on an external neutral frame;
it shows what that requirement looks like to a person --- as the difference
between a captured platform and a public good, recognizable in two precedents
the reader already trusts; and it derives the two-layer architecture, the public
substrate, and the verification model from that single foundation. The formal
comparator is built in \zcref{sec:comparator}; this chapter is what it means.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Captured Comparator}
\label{subsec:introduction:captured-comparator}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Every dominant platform runs on a single exchange: participation at zero
monetary cost, in return for data and attention sold to third parties. The
ranking algorithm is the platform's proprietary asset; the social graph is its
property; the rules that decide what each participant sees, what attribution
they receive, and what share of the revenue their contributions generate are not
published, not verifiable, and not theirs.

\begin{insight}[Every Platform Compares; the Wound Is Ownership]
    \label{ins:introduction:every-platform-compares}
    Ranking, attribution, and monetization are not three businesses --- they are
    three readings of one act: \emph{comparing communities to decide relative
    worth}. The harm in the incumbent model is not that this comparison occurs;
    a network that could not compare would have no feed, no economy, nothing to
    offer. The harm is that the comparator is \textbf{privately owned and
    unseen}: a measure applied to a person's standing that they cannot inspect,
    cannot reproduce, and cannot appeal. Privacy becomes the hidden price of
    being measured; the people who create the content receive none of the
    revenue; and no participant can determine whether the rules they were shown
    are the rules that were applied. This is not an engineering constraint. It
    is a choice made by systems that profit from opacity and would lose their
    primary asset if the comparator were public.
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[The Second Wound Is the Detector]
    \label{ins:introduction:the-detector}
    Ownership of the comparator is not the only wound. Before ranking anything,
    every platform faces the costless Sybil: automated account-creation and
    posting are effectively unbounded, so without a standing defense the
    fabricated floods the genuine (\zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster}).
    Incumbents meet this with an \textbf{admission apparatus} --- CAPTCHA,
    phone and email verification, device fingerprinting, behavioural
    bot-detection, per-account rate limits --- large, permanently staffed, and
    \emph{never finished}. It cannot finish: a humanity-proof is a
    \textbf{detector}, adversarial by construction, verifying an unfakeable
    property (you-are-human, you-are-unique) through fakeable proxies (puzzles,
    phone numbers, mouse paths), so every proxy invites a forgery and every
    forgery a deeper proxy, with no fixed point. This is Douceur's fork
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge}): absent a trusted identity
    authority, only a \emph{resource cost} bounds the Sybil. The incumbent took
    the identity-authority branch and inherited its endless arms race.

    The branch is doubly costly, and the dignity thesis
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:neutrality-is-dignity}) will reclaim both costs. A
    detector must be \textbf{privileged} --- a deciding thing must be
    authoritative, hence owned, hence tiltable, so the admission apparatus, not
    the ranker, is the deepest seat of capture --- and it works only by
    \textbf{learning who you are}, extracting the phone, the email, the
    biometric, the behavioural signature by which it judges you human. The
    proof-of-personhood gate and the data-extraction wound are one apparatus:
    the flood defense \emph{is} the surveillance.
\end{insight}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Only Question}
\label{subsec:introduction:the-only-question}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Strip the comparison engine to its foundation and a single fact organizes
everything that follows.

A comparator cannot be built from the graph alone
(\zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster,rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge}). A
non-trivial comparator therefore requires the external frame of
\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}; its binding onto the graph converts
absolute position into relative position.

\begin{insight}[Who Owns the Frame]
    \label{ins:introduction:who-owns-the-frame}
    Because the comparator must rest on an external frame, a comparison engine
    raises exactly one ethical question, and it is structural: \textbf{who owns
    the frame?} A frame owned and priced by the operator is a platform --- the
    captured comparator of \zcref{ins:introduction:every-platform-compares}, with
    the operator free to tilt the measure toward its own interest. A frame that
    is neutral, public, and owned by no one is a public good. This is the hinge
    of the entire design, and it is simultaneously a mathematical requirement
    (the frame must be exogenous and neutral) and a moral one (no one may own the
    measure of another's standing). The remainder of this document is the
    construction of a comparator whose frame no participant --- including the
    operator --- can own or price.
\end{insight}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Two Precedents}
\label{subsec:introduction:two-precedents}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The two properties the frame must have --- unpriced neutrality and public
auditability --- are not novel aspirations. Each is the defining virtue of an
existing system the reader already relies on.

\begin{insight}[TCP/IP Is Unpriced Neutrality]
    \label{ins:introduction:tcp-is-unpriced-neutrality}
    The Internet's transport layer forwards every packet by the same rules,
    owned by no participant, pricing nothing it carries. It does not decide which
    traffic is worthy; it provides a neutral substrate on which worth is decided
    elsewhere. This is exactly the posture of the comparator's frame source
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:neutrality-from-silence}): the human face of ``the
    frame is owned by no one.''
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[Wikipedia Is Public Auditability]
    \label{ins:introduction:wikipedia-is-public-auditability}
    Wikipedia's every judgment of relative significance --- what is included,
    what is foregrounded, what is corrected --- is reproducible from a public
    record by the very people it ranks. The verdict is not handed down; it is
    recomputable, contestable, and owned in common. This is the second property
    the comparator requires: not merely that the frame be neutral, but that the
    \emph{measurement} be reproducible by the agents it measures
    (\zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model}). Wikipedia is the human face
    of ``the comparator is auditable by those it ranks.''
\end{insight}

PeerNetwork is the union of these two virtues: TCP's \emph{unpriced neutrality}
in the layer that supplies the frame (\zcref{sec:comparator}), under Wikipedia's
\emph{public auditability} in the layer that binds it (this document). The core
behaves like TCP --- a substrate that does not bias --- and presents like
Wikipedia --- a public, reproducible record of social significance, managed in
the open.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Dignity}
\label{subsec:introduction:dignity}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PeerNetwork is built on the premise that a social network should do good, and
that network neutrality is the grounding principle that enables dignity --- the
foundation of the German idea of fairness. The two precedents make this concrete,
and the foundation makes it precise.

\begin{insight}[Neutrality Is Dignity]
    \label{ins:introduction:neutrality-is-dignity}
    Dignity, in a comparison engine, has an exact statement: \textbf{no
    participant's standing is fixed by a measure they cannot see, cannot
    reproduce, or that is welded to a frame chosen to pick them}. The neutral,
    public, non-ownable frame is not a feature added for fairness --- it
    \emph{is} the fairness, stated in the same terms as the mathematics. A
    private comparator denies dignity not by malice but by structure: a measure
    you cannot inspect is a measure that can be turned against you without your
    knowledge. ``Neutral frame'' and ``network neutrality'' are the same words
    doing the same work; the math and the ethics are one claim, not two.
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[One Price Replaces the Admission Apparatus]
    \label{ins:introduction:price-not-detector}
    The frame answers the first wound; the gate answers the second. The
    apparatus of \zcref{ins:introduction:the-detector} --- existence-control and
    rate-control alike --- decomposes into a structural price and published
    floors, $\numeraire$, $\safefloor$, and $\partfloor$: existence-control is
    the door $\actstamp{}\ge\partfloor$ (W2b, epoch-averaged), rate-control
    the solvency debit $\burnbal{i}\ge\safethresh$ (W1) with its individual
    safety stamp $\actstamp{}\ge\safefloor$ (W2a, never averaged) --- a rate
    limit denominated in burned value per action, not in requests-per-account
    (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}). A price is not a verdict, so it needs no owner:
    there is \textbf{nothing to fool} --- destroyed external value is destroyed
    whoever destroyed it --- and the defense \emph{terminates} exactly where a
    detector escalates
    (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}). And the price does
    not \emph{verify}: it relocates the question of who is genuine out of band,
    and rations, by burn alone, the attention that question costs
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:vouch-not-check}). One price and two floors run the
    whole height
    (\zcref{post:epoch:act-debit,def:epoch:safety-floor,def:epoch:participation-floor}) --- a crude
    resource-filter at the floor, a graduated trust-attractor above it --- owned
    at no height, and at no height asking who you are
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:identity-is-layer-2}). The privileged gatekeeper and
    the door-tax of PII close by one stroke, because they were always one
    apparatus.
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[Equal Among Peers]
    \label{ins:introduction:equal-among-peers}
    Dignity has a second face the frame alone does not show: inside a
    community in which one is genuinely embedded, standing becomes a
    pooled commitment rate rather than a comparison of isolated
    balances.

    Let
    \[
        n_i\coloneqq\max(\actcount{i},1).
    \]
    In the exact balance/count mediant
    (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}), actor~$i$'s own pair carries the
    action mass it retains, $\transportentry{i}{i}\actcount{i}$, while
    source~$u$'s pair carries the mass it allocates to~$i$,
    $\transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}$.  The own-pair share is therefore
    \[
        \frac{\transportentry{i}{i}\actcount{i}}{
            \transportentry{i}{i}\actcount{i}+
            \displaystyle\sum_{u\neq i}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}
        }
        =
        \frac{1}{1+M_i},
        \qquad
        M_i
        \coloneqq
        \frac{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u\neq i}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}
        }{\transportentry{i}{i}\actcount{i}}.
    \]
    The quantity that controls peer convergence is incoming transported
    \emph{action mass}, not headcount alone --- and the denominator is now
    the actor's own \emph{retained} mass, which its own allocations spend:
    an actor who allocates outward keeps less of itself in its own mediant.

    As $M_i\to\infty$, actor~$i$'s own pair vanishes from the mediant
    and standing approaches the action-mass-weighted pooled rate of the
    sources whose allocation reaches it:
    \[
        \standing{i}
        \longrightarrow
        \frac{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u\neq i}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\burnbal{u}
        }{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u\neq i}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}
        }.
    \]
    \textbf{Individual standing dissolves into the costly commitment
    rate of the actors whose accepted acts allocate to the target.}  The comparator remains between communities because
    no raw artifact, unmatched leg, or unviewed third party may create
    that support relation
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection,%
    def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).

    The uniform-activity DeGroot expression survives as a reduction
    theorem, not as the general formula: when contributing action
    counts are equal, the action-mass factors cancel and the familiar
    weight-average form is recovered.  The normative comparator is the
    mediant.
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[No Escape Velocity Within a Community]
    \label{ins:introduction:no-escape-velocity}
    The peer convergence is not a passive arithmetic average.  Every
    projected person-vouch terminating at actor~$i$ receives the same
    standing-dependent target activation.  At a fixed accepted rung, that
    activation is strictly increasing in~$\standing{i}$: as an embedded actor
    rises, the authored relations through which peers weigh that actor
    strengthen as well.

    \textbf{The averaging pressure of an established support base
    therefore tightens with the target's standing, subject to the
    the published emission fractions.}  Raw burning can raise the actor's own
    source rate, but it does not detach the actor from the complete
    vouches already admitted into the same mediant.  Nor can the actor
    manufacture a substitute support base through a popular Chat,
    Content item, or other artifact: passive context carries no
    standing authority
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
    post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}).

    This is a local statement about a fixed certified epoch, not a claim that
    every next-epoch tilt rung remains unchanged.  The safety compiler may
    lower the accepted tilt strength at a later boundary; it may never raise
    it by treating an uncertified rung as safe.
    What persists is the structural principle: standing above one's own
    source is relational and actor-authored, never an artifact-routed
    escape from peer judgment.
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[The Scope of the Peer Claim]
    \label{ins:introduction:peer-claim-scope}
    The claim is exact but conditional on relational mass.  ``Equal
    among peers'' is not a headcount threshold, and the specification
    assigns no universal group size to it.  Its exact coordinate is
    \[
        M_i
        =
        \frac{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u\neq i}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}
        }{
            \transportentry{i}{i}\actcount{i}
        }.
    \]
    Actor~$i$ retains own-pair share $1/(1+M_i)$; own and incoming
    mass are equal at $M_i=1$; the own share falls below ten per cent
    only when $M_i>9$.  Density, the tilt the recipients earn, the
    domain weights their acts carry, and source action mass all matter.  A
    small but strongly committed support base may outweigh a larger weak
    one; artifact-directed acts contribute nothing to anyone else, because
    they resolve home.

    The unembedded actor receives no allocation but its own:
    \[
        \transportentry{u}{i}=0
        \quad\text{for every }u\neq i,
    \]
    and therefore
    \[
        \standing{i}
        =
        \commitrate{i}.
    \]
    That actor is measured by their own costly source alone.  This is
    dignity \emph{through} embeddedness: standing is conferred
    relationally by actors whose complete vouches reach one through
    the relation multigraph, not by strangers, passive
    artifacts, or the operator.

    Both boundaries are explicit.  Weakly embedded actors retain
    substantial individual differentiation; strongly embedded actors
    converge toward the pooled source rate of their support base.  The
    paper claims neither a universal community-size threshold nor
    interpersonal equality independent of actual relational mass; the
    stranger-against-stranger ranking the plutocracy worry requires
    remains reserved for clusters and settled by aggregate commitment,
    never run between persons
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:only-faithful-coordinate}).
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[The Only Faithful Coordinate]
    \label{ins:introduction:only-faithful-coordinate}
    What survives the peer convergence
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:equal-among-peers}) is not a residual dignity
    problem but a claim of a different kind: communities are ranked by their
    aggregate costly commitment, and the reach and reward gradients track it.
    This is \emph{distributional}, not interpersonal --- and the same gauge
    argument that founds the comparator shows it to be the only faithful
    coordinate
    (\zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster,rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge}). For
    two communities that share no edge, the distinguishing coordinate is the one
    the topology cannot generate: their exogenous, unauthored mass
    (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}). To protest that
    communities are ranked by commitment is to protest that strangers can be
    compared at all; the only alternative the mathematics leaves is the captured
    comparator's, which separates strangers by whatever the operator privately
    decides (\zcref{ins:introduction:every-platform-compares}). Ranking by
    demonstrated costly commitment is simply what remains once no one may own
    the measure.

    And it is costly commitment borne \emph{per action}, not a hoard.
    Standing is a balance/count mediant, so every source contributes its
    residual balance together with the action mass over which that
    balance was accumulated.  In a strongly embedded community the
    resulting coordinate is the pooled, action-mass-weighted commitment
    rate
    \[
        \frac{
            \sum_u \transportentry{u}{i}\burnbal{u}
        }{
            \sum_u \transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}
        },
    \]
    not an arithmetic average of account rates and not a total-reserve
    measure.  The comparator is intensive: a small, dedicated community
    may outrank a large, weakly committed one, while accumulated balance
    buys no standing that its per-action rate and actor-authored support
    do not justify.  What survives between otherwise disconnected
    communities is the one coordinate the topology cannot fabricate:
    costly source, carried only through accountable initiator-owned
    delegation.
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[The Floor We Name]
    \label{ins:introduction:the-floor-we-name}
    Honesty about a comparator includes honesty about its limit. The frame
    anchors \emph{who has genuine standing} against an external cost no effort
    can fake. It cannot, by the same gauge argument that requires it, fully
    anchor \emph{the truth of every claim made within the graph}: a public,
    immutable, attributed record raises the price of a lie its author can be
    held to but cannot
    make the lie impossible (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}). This is the
    one floor the architecture cannot pour --- and the document states it as a
    structural limit rather than phasing it away
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:structural-ceiling}). Where mathematics ends, the
    system asks its participants, not its formulas, to hold the line: it makes
    the lie costly, public, and self-defeating, and trusts the community to read
    it. A system honest enough to name the floor it cannot pour is the dignity
    thesis completed --- it does not pretend to a guarantee it cannot give.
\end{insight}

\begin{insight}[The Cut No Mechanism Can Make]
    \label{ins:introduction:the-cut-no-mechanism-can-make}
    The floor of \zcref{ins:introduction:the-floor-we-name} can be named
    exactly. The source cost does its whole job, and does it correctly: burn
    thins the unbounded population of cheap fakes to a \emph{finite, funded
    arena}, because a cluster with no source takes standing zero and the unit
    amplifier $\ampfactor{}=1$ and cannot buy comparability it did not earn
    (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}). What it leaves is
    the one cut no mechanism can make: \textbf{inside the funded arena,
    splitting funded-real from funded-fake}. This is a theorem, not a gap to
    engineer away. Any internal test of authenticity --- an ``independent
    witness'' asserted inside the graph --- is a node the adversary writes;
    under the relabeling that carries a fabricated cluster, its corroborating
    evidence co-moves with it, because one hand authored both
    (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}). Measuring whether a witness is
    independent is itself an edge in the field being measured, so any mechanism
    that could make the cut is one the fake would have authored. The cut is
    therefore made \textbf{from outside the rent structure}, or not at all ---
    by a human looking: the will to go check, against the gradient, where no
    internal proof can be had. That look is the single exogenous, un-buildable
    input the system rests on and cannot contain
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:structural-ceiling}).
\end{insight}
\begin{insight}[The Network Carries the Vouch, Not the Check]
    \label{ins:introduction:vouch-not-check}
    The participation gate is the floor of dignity --- a neutral price
    no one owns
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:neutrality-is-dignity,%
    ins:introduction:price-not-detector}); what rises above it is the
    fairness.  Standing grades reach through the universal amplifier,
    and reach is not itself a verdict on a person --- it is an
    occasion on which people may recognize one another.

    That recognition happens out of band.  No mechanism on the network
    proves a person human or genuine; a community member decides to
    vouch on whatever real-world knowledge they hold.  What returns to
    the graph is not the private check but a \emph{complete authored
    act}: an Opinion on a Profile, an Invitation, a Reference, or any other
    accepted Actor-authored act, each resolved to a person or to its author
    by the published rule
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection,%
    def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  The record is public,
    accountable, and priced.

    The conserved rule then says exactly how regard travels.  Source~$u$
    apportions its one unit of allocation across the recipients its own acts
    name; each of those recipients apportions its own unit in turn, and the
    transport composes those hops to bounded depth:
    \[
        \transportm{m}{\standingvector}
        = \hopmatrix{1}{\standingvector}\cdots\hopmatrix{m}{\standingvector} .
    \]
    A Reference matters because someone to whom~$u$ allocated authored it.
    It does not matter merely because its anchoring artifact is popular, or
    because another actor placed an incoming edge on that artifact: an
    artifact-directed act resolves to its own author and moves nobody else
    (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}).

    Two fairnesses follow.  First, scrutiny is source-relative and
    costly: an actor's act can carry only the view already attributable
    to that actor, and every revision remains a priced action.  Second,
    the check belongs to the community, not to a privileged detector:
    Layer~1 records the accountable act without learning or certifying
    the private evidence behind it.  That is the dignity thesis in
    operational form --- recognition by people who choose to know one
    another, not classification by an apparatus that must.
\end{insight}
\begin{insight}[The Right to Leave, and the Dignity It Owes Others]
    \label{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}
    The append-only graph completes the dignity thesis of
    \zcref{ins:introduction:neutrality-is-dignity} by turning it toward others.
    There, dignity was the neutrality of the frame --- no one may own the measure
    of your standing. Here it is the inviolability of what others have justly
    chosen \emph{on the basis of you}. An actor is its Layer~0 address
    permanently, and the husk it leaves --- its standing, its title, the trust
    others built on it --- persists by construction
    (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}). This is not a failure to forget; it is
    a duty, and in the German tradition the document is built on it is the central
    one: human dignity is inviolable, and no person may be reduced to a mere
    object of another's purposes. The trust an actor earned \emph{justifies} other
    people's standing, their settlements, their public economic choices ---
    exercises of \emph{their} agency --- and to let a departing actor reach back
    and dissolve that basis would make those others mere instruments of its exit,
    unmaking self-determination they had already, justly, exercised. The one thing
    the network will not return is therefore the only thing that was never the
    leaver's alone to take: it is owed to the unbounded, unpredictable set of
    people who stood on it.

    What \emph{can} be returned, it returns completely, and without cost to that
    duty. Layer~1 holds no notion of \emph{who} an actor is --- the person behind
    an actor is a Layer~2 fact the network never represents
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:identity-is-layer-2}) --- so there is no identity to
    surrender; leaving, on that axis, is Layer~2 forgetting an association Layer~1
    never knew. And an actor may erase the \emph{content} of any or all of its
    actions --- every authored act carries a removable payload projection
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-projection}) --- with no effect on any standing, title, or reward
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-projection,rem:graph:act-payload-removal-neutrality}): the
    measure never read those words, so erasing them cannot move it. The network
    keeps the edge-ontology boundary as a field boundary in one record format:
    all supplied content is payload, removable including genesis payloads; all
    relied-upon structure is structural, the immutable husk
    (\zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology}). It keeps exactly what belongs to the
    community and lets go of exactly what
    belongs to the person --- the same neutrality, read as care for the departing
    and the remaining at once.

    Honesty about the seam (\zcref{ins:introduction:the-floor-we-name}) requires
    naming its one limit, and the limit is self-aligning. What cannot be erased is
    \emph{structural position}: the trust edges others authored toward you persist
    because they are what others stand on. The network itself stays blind to whose
    husk it is --- its structural rules are gauge
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge}) --- but a party who already knows
    some of your former neighbours can walk those preserved edges inward and
    recognize the husk from outside, names and words gone. The exposure
    and the duty-to-retain are \emph{one quantity}. A deeply connected actor is
    easily recognized --- a rich, distinctive trust-fingerprint defeats anonymity
    --- but that same connectivity \emph{is} the economic weight others depend on,
    so its husk is exactly the one that cannot be removed while keeping faith with
    them. A sparsely connected actor carries little weight and creates little
    dependency, so its husk is near-inert to remove --- and it also offers little
    to recognize, hiding among its relabeling-equivalent peers, the one place the
    gauge protects rather than exposes. You are therefore re-identifiable in exact
    proportion to how much you were owed to others
    (\zcref{frontier:structural-residue-reidentification}). Privacy of departure is
    bounded, not absolute --- and the boundary falls in the only place it honestly
    can: the part of you the network cannot return is the part that was, in truth,
    always someone else's.
\end{insight}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Two Layers, Derived}
\label{subsec:introduction:two-layers-derived}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The architecture is not a design preference; it falls out of the foundation. The
frame must be \emph{exogenous to the topology}
(\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}(i)). It therefore cannot live in the
layer that draws the graph --- a frame computed alongside the graph would inherit
the graph's gauge and break nothing. The frame must come from below, from a layer
that produces value-bearing scarcity without reference to the social structure
above it. Hence two layers:

\begin{description}[nosep]
    \item[\textbf{Layer 0 (Peer Attestation) --- the frame source.}] Exports
        exactly one object, the neutral attestation map
        (\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame,rem:comparator:neutrality-from-silence}).
        It knows nothing of clusters, feeds, or rewards.
    \item[\textbf{Layer 1 (this document) --- the binding.}]
        Reads the imported frame as residual per-actor source, compiles
        complete person-vouch acts into the initiator-owned Actor graph,
        resolves every accepted act to a recipient or to its author, solves
        one conserved same-epoch equilibrium, and forms the relative-standing
        field $\standing{i}$ as the exact balance/count mediant
        (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing,%
        def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).
        Passive artifacts remain in the public Action Graph for feed,
        attribution, title, and content context but carry no standing
        authority.  Layer~1 publishes the standing field and the
        certificates required to reproduce it.  It is the
        public-auditability layer.
\end{description}

\textbf{Guilds (Layer 2)} operate independently on the shared graph, each
publishing its own attribution recursion and reward pool
(\zcref{sec:transport,app:can}); no guild owns the graph or the frame. The two
properties the incumbent model lacks --- that the operator cannot tilt the
measure, and that no party can fabricate standing --- are \emph{consequences},
not promises: neither layer can simulate the other (the operator cannot dictate
rewards; a guild cannot fabricate frame values) precisely because the frame is
exogenous to both.

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{The two layers, by the role each plays in the comparator. The
    operator's only economic inflow is the Layer~0 minting fee.}
    \label{tbl:introduction:layer-roles}
    \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l X X@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Layer} & \textbf{Comparator role} & \textbf{Owns / prices} \\
        \midrule
        Layer 0 (Attestation)
                        & frame source --- supplies the neutral exogenous scalar
                        & owns nothing of the graph
                            (\zcref{rem:comparator:neutrality-from-silence}) \\
        \addlinespace
        Layer 1 (Network)
            & the binding --- compiles complete actor-authored vouches,
              derives source-relative safe standing flow, forms the
              balance/count mediant, and publishes the standing field,
              hop matrices, emission fractions, and certificates
            & owns the public infrastructure; earns only the Layer~0 fee \\
        \addlinespace
        Layer 2 (Guilds)
            & readouts --- consume $\standing{i}$ to attribute and reward;
              identity association and payload carriage are likewise Layer~2
              (consumers, of which guilds are the economic kind)
            & each owns its own pool and recursion; none owns frame or graph \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabularx}
\end{table}

Where exactly the boundary between the layers falls --- which published
values bind and which are free --- is not a list to be maintained but a
predicate any participant can compute. \zcref{sec:network} draws it once, as
the \emph{admission closure}, and everything downstream cites it.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Graph}
\label{subsec:introduction:the-graph}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The substrate onto which the frame is bound is a public directed graph
$G = (V,E)$ with node partition $V = V_u \sqcup V_c$: \textbf{active} nodes
$V_u$ (Actors) author edges; \textbf{passive} nodes $V_c$ (artifacts) never
autonomously originate or redirect one (\zcref{def:graph:partition},
\zcref{ax:graph:passivity}). The graph is append-only --- new interactions create
new edges and nodes without altering existing ones --- and each edge stores a
$3\times3$ sentiment slice from which the network's geometric quantities are
extracted (\zcref{sec:graph}).

The Action Graph is not itself the standing graph.  Its passive nodes,
raw hyper-edge legs, tensor geometry, title records, and content
relationships remain essential to feed, attribution, settlement, and
public context; but standing reads it only through the fold cells of the
epoch and the recipients they resolve to
(\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection,%
def:epoch:standing-fold-cell}).  This distinction prevents a passive
artifact from acting as a switchboard through which one actor redirects
another actor's source.

The graph is exactly the gauge substrate of
\zcref{subsec:introduction:the-only-question}: every quantity computed from $G$
alone is relabeling-invariant, hence fabricable, hence insufficient to compare
clusters. It is the space the frame's intersection makes \emph{relative}.
\zcref{sec:graph,sec:nodes} develop its geometry; the only thing the
Introduction asks of it is that it be public, immutable, and causally ordered ---
the requirements stated next, which are also exactly what makes a record legible
enough to bear the cost of a lie (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{What the Substrate Must Guarantee}
\label{subsec:introduction:infrastructure}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The binding and its two costs impose five abstract requirements on the
infrastructure that carries the graph and the ledger. They are stated
independently of any mechanism that achieves them. Each is also a foundational
requirement read plainly: a frame must be \emph{public} to be a common reference,
\emph{immutable} and \emph{irrevocable} to be a stable monotone reference, and
\emph{causally ordered} so the weld samples a settled value --- and a record must
be all of these to be \emph{legible} enough that lying in it carries a cost.

\begin{postulate}[Public Accessibility]
    \label{post:introduction:public-accessibility}
    The graph record and the ledger are continuously readable by any participant
    at any time, without access control or authentication. (The frame is a
    \emph{common} reference only if everyone can read it; a record is legible
    only if it is public.)
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Record Integrity]
    \label{post:introduction:record-integrity}
    Once an edge record or ledger entry is published, it cannot be silently
    altered. A participant who retrieves a record may treat it as matching what
    was published. (Immutability is what makes a record bear the accountability cost
    of \zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}: an unalterable claim names its
    author for as long as the graph exists.)
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Irrevocability]
    \label{post:introduction:irrevocability}
    A ledger entry, once published, cannot be reversed, removed, or reduced. The
    monotone non-decrease of the committed quantity $\burnval{i}$ is a Layer~0
    property the network reads, not a network primitive
    (\attestationcref{thm:interface:instantaneous-costliness},
    \attestationcref{lem:costliness:attestation-append-only}); the network's frame
    stability at its own sampling depth follows from it
    (\zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability}). (A reference that can move backward
    is not a frame, \zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}(iv).) Immutability
    also protects others' justified past: the trust an actor's record carries is
    owed to those who stood on it (\zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}).
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Authoritative Ordering]
    \label{post:introduction:authoritative-act-order}
    The host chooses a total \emph{authoritative order} over the accepted
    authored acts of each epoch and assigns each act a logical time by its
    position (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}). The order is
    semantically authoritative: it is not forced by incidence, but it must place
    every declared dependency earlier, and it is published so that any two
    participants holding the same ordered sequence $Q_k$ reproduce the same
    result. \emph{Agreement on $Q_k$ --- not merely on the edge set --- is
    required.} (The authoritative order is what lets the weld sample a settled
    value --- the temporal precondition of clause~(S) of
    \zcref{post:comparator:faithfulness}.)
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Epoch Edge-Set Provision]
    \label{post:introduction:epoch-edge-set}
    At each epoch boundary $k$ the operator provides a finite edge set
    $E_k \subseteq E$ that is \emph{causally closed}
    ($e' \in E_k \wedge e \prec e' \Rightarrow e \in E_k$) and \emph{monotone}
    ($E_{k-1} \subseteq E_k$). $E_k$ is the sole topological input to the
    epoch-$k$ computation; the mechanism by which the operator forms it is out of
    scope. (The settled sampling depth that makes
    \zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability} hold is a property of $E_k$, not of any
    global clock.)
\end{postulate}

\begin{remark}
    \label{rem:introduction:mechanism-agnostic}
    These are stated independently of any mechanism for achieving them. Any
    mechanism --- a strict append log, an ordered cluster-closure write,
    a frontier-finality gadget --- delivering a monotone $E_k$ together with an
    authoritative order $Q_k$ on which honest participants agree is compliant.
    Agreement on the ordered sequence $Q_k$, not merely on the set $E_k$, is
    what the downstream computation consumes
    (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism,prop:epoch:epoch-replay-determinism}).
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Comparator, Previewed}
\label{subsec:introduction:comparator-previewed}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The relative-standing field is the comparator realized on the graph.
Its construction is \zcref{sec:comparator,sec:epoch}; the Introduction
names only its shape and the two faces it turns toward a person.

The network reads the imported frame as burn value $\burnval{i}$,
subtracts consummated per-action debits to obtain residual balance
$\burnbal{i}$, and forms the neutral source
\[
    \commitrate{i}
    =
    \frac{\burnbal{i}}{\max(\actcount{i},1)}
\]
(\zcref{def:comparator:rate,def:comparator:residual-balance}).
This source is derivable from the public ledger without graph traversal.

The network then weighs every accepted Actor-authored act of the epoch and
resolves each to a person recipient or to its author
(\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  A Reference or
Invitation is one complete act, not an independently reachable T-leg; the
passive middle node supplies context and allocates nothing.  Each Actor
apportions one conserved unit over self and those recipients, weighted by
published domain weights and tilted by recipient standing, and the
allocation composes across at most $\hopmax$ hops into the conserved
transport $\transportentry{u}{i}$.

The standing field is the exact post-debit mediant:
\[
    \standing{i}
    =
    \frac{
        \displaystyle\sum_{u}
            \transportentry{u}{i}\burnbal{u}
    }{
        \displaystyle\sum_{u}
            \transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}
    }.
\]
It is bounded in the contributing rate hull and independently
replayable from the frame snapshot, accepted records, fold-cell outcomes,
the base allocation scores, the accepted tilt rung, and published constants
(\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).

One scope note, because this chapter's argument is easy to read one size too
large.  Everything claimed here about commitment and standing is
\emph{distributional}: a community's mass-weighted standing is exactly what
its ledger backs (\zcref{thm:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity}), and that
is what \zcref{ins:introduction:only-faithful-coordinate} rests on.  The
individual reading --- that one Actor's further commitment raises that
Actor's own standing --- is proved only at the anchor rung, where transport
does not depend on the state it computes.  At the operating rung it is
\textbf{open}: a burn that raises one Actor also re-apportions every row that
Actor's mass passes through, and whether the net effect is monotone is a
question this edition asks rather than answers
(\zcref{prop:epoch:no-tilt-commitment-monotonicity,%
frontier:tilted-monotonicity}).  The distributional claim does not depend on
the individual one, so nothing above is weakened; but the two should not be
read as the same sentence.

\begin{insight}[The Comparator Made Human]
    \label{ins:introduction:comparator-made-human}
    The comparator turns two terminal faces toward a person:
    \textbf{the feed --- what you are shown}
    (\zcref{sec:sorting}), and \textbf{the reward --- what you are
    owed} (\zcref{sec:transport}).  Both read the same standing field
    (\zcref{ins:comparator:universal-amplifier}), but neither owns its
    frame or may redirect another actor's source through passive
    structure.  The measure is public, actor-authored in its relational
    inputs, and reproducible by the people it compares.
\end{insight}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Verification Model and Deployment Phases}
\label{subsec:introduction:verification-model}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The comparator is auditable by the agents it measures
(\zcref{ins:introduction:wikipedia-is-public-auditability}): every computation
affecting standing, ranking, attribution, or reward is specified by published
formula over the public record and independently reproducible from records and
constants alone (\zcref{prop:scalability:raw-path-verifiability,prop:scalability:conserved-standing-verifiability}). What changes
across deployment phases is not \emph{whether} verification is possible but
\emph{what role it plays when it runs}.

\begin{description}[nosep]
    \item[Centralized phase: verification as audit.]
        Computations are submitted by the operator and take effect before
        independent verification completes. Verification detects errors, exposes
        them, and supports challenges --- but a result is already applied when an
        error is found. This phase exists to observe real-scale graph statistics
        against the network scoring constants and validate them empirically
        before they are locked; the Layer~0 surface constants are calibrated
        separately against reserve-economy sustainability
        (\attestationcref{subsec:model:constants}).
    \item[Decentralized phase: verification as gate.]
        Once parameters are validated and locked, the append layer
        decentralizes. A computation is not accepted unless it passes
        verification; nothing failing verification against the public record
        takes effect. Whether this requires trust in the operator is determined
        by the mechanism satisfying
        \zcref{post:introduction:record-integrity,post:introduction:irrevocability},
        not by this specification.
\end{description}

For standing, verification has three explicit layers.  First, the
epoch certificate commits the complete person-vouch projection and its
selected simple Actor paths.  Second, the admission schedule and exact
balance/count mediant are replayed from public action masses and residual
balances.  Third, the graph-dependent path-incidence certificate checks
the declared standing box and the chartered row-contraction margin
(\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}).  An uncertifiable path fraction
has safe polarity: it contributes zero.  If all relational flow into an
actor is zero-clipped, that actor's standing is exactly their own neutral
source.

This dynamic certificate proves contraction on
the declared box.  It does not, by itself, claim that one-boundary
standing movement is small, that source-relative envelope is conserved
across different recipients, or that the target consented to the
incoming vouch.  Those properties are stated separately rather than
hidden inside the word ``safe.''

The mathematical specification is identical across both phases. The system's
eventual trustlessness is not a different system --- it is the same comparator
with verification moved from after acceptance to before it. \zcref{app:deployment}
documents the structural properties the deployment must maintain in both phases.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Reading Guide}
\label{subsec:introduction:reading-guide}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The body is the \emph{decomposition of this foundation} in dependency order ---
not a mechanism that never names its purpose. \zcref{sec:comparator} builds the
comparator: the gauge axiom, the imported frame, the two costs it stands on, and
the binding discipline that keeps it faithful. \zcref{sec:network} names the
machine that runs it --- the write, the admission closure, the object taxonomy,
and the host contract. \zcref{sec:graph,sec:nodes} develop the gauge substrate ---
the sentiment geometry and the node and edge types it is drawn from.
\zcref{sec:epoch} compiles complete person-vouch acts into the
initiator-owned Actor graph, derives source-relative paths through at
most four projected acts, applies certificate-derived standing safety
emission fractions, and publishes the conserved transport and balance/count standing
field; the two readouts follow --- \zcref{sec:sorting}
the feed, \zcref{sec:transport} the reward --- together with content governance
(\zcref{sec:content}) and the approximation, Nash-preservation, and resistance
guarantees (\zcref{sec:scalability}). The
appendices carry the gate geometry and sustaining strategy
(\zcref{app:gates}), the two calculi (CAN, \zcref{app:can}; bridge transport,
\zcref{app:bridge}), the standing dynamics --- the direct-vouch scalar
limit, the depth-four path-incidence Jacobian, the clipped local
certificate, and the residual criticality structure outside the
certified contraction region (\zcref{app:dynamics}) ---
and the symbol index, verification suite, research frontiers, and
structural-necessity arguments. The foundation of everything that follows is
\zcref{sec:comparator}, which begins on the next page.
