\section{The Comparator}
\label{sec:comparator}

A network has value only insofar as it can compare clusters --- weigh one
community's standing against another's. Ranking, attribution, and reward are
each a reading of such a comparison; without it there is no relative value, no
economy, only geometry. This chapter establishes the comparison engine that is
the network's reason to exist. It does so in three movements: it states why a
comparator cannot be built from the graph alone and must import an external
neutral frame (\zcref{subsec:comparator:the-axis}); it imports that frame from
\emph{Peer Attestation} (Layer~0) and welds the network's only count-economy
primitive onto it (\zcref[range]{subsec:comparator:imported-frame,subsec:comparator:the-source});
and it identifies the two costs the comparator stands on --- one inherited and
closed, one owned and only bounded --- and the binding discipline that keeps
the measurement faithful (\zcref[range]{subsec:comparator:two-costs,subsec:comparator:faithfulness}).
No reserve pool, redemption rate, phase, or seigniorage bound is defined here;
each is cited through \texttt{\textbackslash attestationcref}.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Comparator Axis}
\label{subsec:comparator:the-axis}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{axiom}[Inter-Cluster Comparator]
    \label{ax:comparator:inter-cluster}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:participation-floor}%
    A network's value is the value of its comparator: a map assigning to each
    cluster a \emph{relative standing} that can be weighed against any other
    cluster's. Cluster topology cannot supply this map. Every purely structural
    quantity of the graph $G=(V,E)$ is invariant under relabeling --- under any
    automorphism, two clusters with the same internal structure are
    interchangeable --- so topology alone is \emph{gauge}, and a comparator
    built from topology alone assigns interchangeable clusters interchangeable
    standing. Comparison therefore requires a scalar the topology cannot
    generate, satisfying \zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}. Its
    intersection with the topology breaks the relabeling symmetry and converts
    absolute graph position into \emph{relative} position --- and only relative
    position is comparable.
\end{axiom}

\begin{remark}[Topology Is Gauge]
    \label{rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge}
    The obstruction is exact, not rhetorical. Let $\phi$ be an automorphism of
    $G$. Any quantity computed from $G$ by a structural rule satisfies
    $f(\phi\cdot x) = f(x)$; it cannot distinguish $x$ from $\phi\cdot x$. A
    fabricated cluster is, by construction, a subgraph chosen to be
    near-automorphic to a genuine one: identity multiplication is the
    construction of relabeling-equivalent
    structure.\footcite{douceur2002sybil} Hence no function of the graph alone
    separates a genuine high-standing cluster from a cheap, plausible
    lookalike. The path-view determinant
    (\zcref{def:graph:determinant-sign}) measures whether an interaction is
    \emph{coherent}; it cannot measure whether it is \emph{costly}. Coherence,
    maturity, and every tensor-geometric quantity of \zcref{sec:graph} are
    \emph{shape}, and shape is fabricable by effort. The comparator needs
    \emph{mass}, and mass cannot be authored.
\end{remark}

\begin{postulate}[Frame Requirements]
    \label{post:comparator:frame-requirements}
    The scalar that founds the comparator must be:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\roman*)]
        \item \textbf{Exogenous in origin.} It must originate outside the
              topology; a quantity derived from $G$ inherits $G$'s gauge
              symmetry and breaks nothing.
        \item \textbf{Neutral.} It must measure, not select --- the same
              magnitude everywhere, picking no winner --- so that it can serve
              as a common reference.
        \item \textbf{Non-transferable.} It must be welded to the identity it
              measures, so that standing cannot be relocated, pooled, or
              donated across clusters.
        \item \textbf{Monotone.} Its reference must not move backward, or it is
              not a frame.
        \item \textbf{Bound onto the graph.} It must attach to topological
              position, so that an exogenous magnitude becomes a position in
              the field.
    \end{enumerate}
    Origin outside; attachment inside. Layer~0 prepares exactly such a neutral
    scalar (\zcref{rem:comparator:neutrality-from-silence}).
\end{postulate}

\begin{remark}[Actor Field and Cluster Comparison]
    \label{rem:comparator:actor-field-cluster-comparison}
    Layer~1 does not define, enumerate, or partition social clusters. Cluster
    identity, overlap, membership, aggregation, and comparison are terminal
    Layer~2 concerns.

    Layer~1 publishes the gauge-fixed Actor standing field
    \[
        \boldsymbol\alpha^{(k)}
        =
        \bigl(
            \epochstanding{k}{i}
        \bigr)_{i\in V_u^{(k)}}.
    \]
    This field is the common comparison coordinate from which a Layer~2
    consumer constructs an inter-cluster comparator under its own published
    cluster definition and aggregation rule.

    In this document, ``the comparator field'' means the Layer~1 Actor
    standing field. It does not mean that Layer~1 has chosen a canonical
    cluster partition or cluster-level aggregation formula.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Imported Frame}
\label{subsec:comparator:imported-frame}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Imported Frame]
    \label{def:comparator:imported-frame}
    \attestationref{def:interface:attestation}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}%
    Peer Attestation exports exactly one computational object: the attestation
    map $\attest{} : \addrspace \to \R_{\geq 0}$
    (\attestationcref*{def:interface:attestation}). Its foundational content is
    not the per-address values but the \emph{shared ordered codomain} --- the
    single line $\R_{\geq 0}$ onto which every address in $\addrspace$ is
    forced. That one common ordered line, into which all clusters are
    projected, \emph{is} the comparator's frame; the per-address value is its
    fiber. The network reads the map under its own \emph{burn-value} symbol:
    for each actor~$i$ with Layer~0 address
    $\operatorname{key}(i) \in \addrspace$,
    \begin{equation}
        \burnval{i} \;\coloneqq\; \attest{\operatorname{key}(i)}.
        \label{eq:comparator:seam}
    \end{equation}
    The glyph flips $A \to B$ and the index reading flips from opaque address
    to bound actor; both are reading conventions fixed at import
    (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}), not new structure. The frame is
    exogenous in origin (it originates in Layer~0's external reserve, not in
    $G$) and satisfies the remaining requirements of
    \zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements} as established below:
    non-negativity (\attestationcref{post:interface:non-negativity}),
    non-transferability (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}), monotonicity at
    the network's sampling depth (\zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability}), and
    binding onto the graph (the weld, \zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Neutrality from Silence]
    \label{rem:comparator:neutrality-from-silence}
    The property that silences Layer~0 is the same property that qualifies its
    export to be a frame. The attestation \attestrecords{a destroyed magnitude};
    it never bears a value, and Layer~0 \emph{declines to price it}, conferring
    no claim at its own layer
    (\attestationcref*{def:interface:attestation},
    \attestationcref{ins:interface:two-relations}). A \emph{priced} attestation
    would carry bias and could not serve as a neutral reference. So Layer~0's
    refusal to name a use is not merely a firewall discipline --- it is
    constitutive of neutrality (\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}(ii)).
    The layer that may not say what its export is \emph{for} is, for that exact
    reason, fit to supply the common frame. Naming the export's purpose is left
    to the layer that prices it (\zcref{rem:comparator:network-prices-the-frame}).
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Frame Binding]
    \label{def:comparator:frame-binding}
    The index of $\attest{}$ is an opaque address $a \in \addrspace$; Layer~0
    makes no claim that an address is a person, holder, or identity
    (\attestationcref*{def:interface:address-space}). The network supplies the
    binding $\operatorname{key} : V_u \to \addrspace$ sending each actor to its
    address: origin exogenous, attachment endogenous
    (\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}(i),(v)); the binding is permanent
    (an actor is its address for the life of the graph), so the husk an actor
    leaves carries its full standing and title by construction. The attestation is
    non-transferable across addresses, so $\burnval{i}$ on one actor cannot
    be aggregated with another's --- the frame is faithful on cluster structure
    (\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}(iii)), and this faithfulness,
    not net cost, is the structural basis of the network's Sybil resistance
    (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Destination Funding and Non-Transferability]
    \label{rem:comparator:destination-funding-non-transferability}
    Layer~1 represents the Actor-bound destination of the imported
    attestation and does not represent the funder of the underlying
    Layer~0 operation.

    A third party may cause new attestation to accrue at the address
    permanently bound to Actor~$i$.  Once recorded there, no Layer~1
    operation may move, merge, reassign, rebind, or transfer that recorded
    source to Actor~$j\ne i$.  Destination-funded accrual therefore does
    not constitute transfer between Actors.

    The frame requirement is Actor-level non-transferability, not a claim
    that every Actor-bound attestation was self-funded.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Identity Is Layer 2]
    \label{rem:comparator:identity-is-layer-2}
    The map from an actor to the \emph{person} behind it is never represented at
    Layer~1: it has no feedback read-site
    (\zcref{def:network:admission-closure}), so by the boundary predicate it
    is terminal, hence Layer~2 (\zcref{tbl:symbols:boundary}). Severing it changes
    no $\standing{}$, $\transportentry{}{}$, title, or reward --- leaving, on the
    identity axis, is Layer~2 forgetting an association Layer~1 never knew
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}).
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Frame Stability at Epoch Sampling Depth]
    \label{lem:comparator:frame-stability}
    Sampled at epoch boundaries, the imported frame is non-decreasing:
    $\burnval{i}^{(k-1)} \leq \burnval{i}^{(k)}$ for every actor~$i$ and
    every epoch~$k$. The reference does not move backward
    (\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}(iv)).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    Layer~0 guarantees that the raw burn value is irrevocable and that its
    reserve-denominated valuation is \emph{settlement-pinned}: fixed at
    Layer~0 settlement events, conservative between settlements, and revisable
    only ever downward to the last-settled value, and only when an
    event-ordering at a settlement boundary is itself revised
    (\attestationcref*{post:interface:monotonicity}). Layer~0 discharges flat
    monotonicity to a reader against the reader's own sampling depth.

    The network samples $\burnval{i}^{(k)}$ from the boundary burn state
    provided with the causally closed, monotone epoch edge set~$E_k$, sampled
    at the settlement-stability depth $\snapbuf$
    (\zcref{post:epoch:final-edge-set}). Choosing $\snapbuf$ to exceed Layer~0
    settlement-ordering uncertainty makes each sampled value last-settled at
    the instant of sampling; the boundary state is then order-free
    (\attestationcref{prop:invariants:burn-order-residual}) and equals the
    settled valuation. Between two network samples the settled valuation only
    rises and is never revised downward, because no settlement below sampling
    depth is reopened. Hence $\burnval{i}^{(k)}$ is non-decreasing in~$k$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Auditability Is Provenance, Not Total]
    \label{rem:comparator:auditability}
    The frame is verified by \emph{recompute-and-verify-provenance}, never
    scan-and-total: every unit of $\burnval{i}$ is provenance-anchored to a
    genuine, irrecoverable Layer~0 destruction and capped, per recording event,
    by the destruction it rides on; a recording not backed by destruction
    contributes \emph{zero}
    (\attestationcref*{post:interface:auditability}). Because the network
    \emph{reads} the frame rather than maintaining its own counter, this
    property is inherited at the seam, not re-established here
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}). Auditability in this sense ---
    reproducibility of a \emph{computation} --- is distinct from the
    \emph{accountability} of a \emph{record} introduced in
    \zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}: a computation is auditable if
    anyone can re-run it; a record holds its author accountable when it can be
    read against them.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Neutral Source}
\label{subsec:comparator:the-source}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The frame is imported; the comparator is the frame welded onto the topology
(\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}). The weld consumes one network-owned scalar
joining the reserve-denominated frame to the per-action history of the graph.
Layer~0 carries no per-action quantity by its no-count rule; the join is the
network's, and it is the \emph{neutral source} of the entire standing
recursion.

\begin{definition}[Commitment Rate --- the Neutral Source]
    \label{def:comparator:rate}
    \networkref{subsec:introduction:comparator-previewed}%
    For actor~$i$, with residual balance $\burnbal{i}$
    (\zcref{def:comparator:residual-balance}) and cumulative action count
    $\actcount{i} \in \NatZero$ (network-owned, non-decreasing):
    $\actcount{i}$ counts \emph{user-authored accepted acts} only;
    derived Self-edge bond components never increment it.
    \begin{equation}
        \commitrate{i}
        = \frac{\burnbal{i}}{\max(\actcount{i},\;1)}.
        \label{eq:comparator:rate}
    \end{equation}
    This is the \emph{neutral source}: the unique exogenous input to the
    standing recursion (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}), the one quantity the
    topology cannot generate
    (\zcref{post:comparator:frame-requirements}(i),(ii)). It is per-actor only
    as an \emph{implementation} of the frame; the object that matters is the
    shared codomain it inhabits (\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame}). Its
    properties:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
          \item $\commitrate{i} \geq 0$; $\commitrate{i} = 0$ iff
              $\burnbal{i} = 0$.
          \item \emph{Decreasing under action}: each action debits $\safethresh$
              from the numerator and adds one to the denominator --- dilution
              is now priced, not merely counted.
        \item \emph{Non-decreasing} in $\burnval{i}$ at fixed
              $\actcount{i}$: burns irrevocably raise it
              (\zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability}).
          \item Independently derivable from the public attestation record, the
              committed action count, and the published debit schedule by any
              participant, without querying any server and without graph traversal
              (\zcref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}).
    \end{enumerate}
    The relative-standing field $\standing{i}$
    (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}) consumes $\commitrate{i}$ at each epoch
    boundary as the source that fixes its gauge.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Residual Balance --- the \safethresh{}-Schedule Ledger]
    \label{def:comparator:residual-balance}
    \begin{equation}
        \burnbal{i} \;=\; \burnval{i} \;-\; \sum_{a}\safethresh^{(k_a)},
        \label{eq:comparator:residual-balance}
    \end{equation}
    the imported frame net of the consummated per-action debits, summed over
    actor~$i$'s accepted acts $a$ at the writing epoch's price.  The debit
    schedule is the system's sole vintage object (V3): a debit is never
    re-calibrated.  The balance is read at the current numéraire (V2).  $\burnbal{i}$ is the
    numerator of the neutral source and the object of the solvency gate
    (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}, W1).  Generalizes the retired
    constant-$\numeraire$ excess-burn diagnostic.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Vintage Trichotomy]
    \label{rem:comparator:vintage-trichotomy}
    (V1)~accepted records retain their recorded parameters; (V2)~current
    reserve-denominated carried state is evaluated under the constants in
    force at read ($\burnbal{}$); (V3)~consummated per-act debits retain
    the $\safethresh$ value charged by their accepted epoch and are never
    recalculated.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Type Asymmetry and the Sole Join]
    \label{rem:comparator:type-asymmetry}
    $\burnval{i} \in \R_{\geq 0}$ is a continuous, reserve-denominated
    quantity read from Layer~0; $\actcount{i} \in \NatZero$ is a discrete
    network count. The source is therefore a real-over-integer quotient, not a
    ratio of like quantities. The num\'eraire $\numeraire$
    (\zcref{def:comparator:numeraire}) is the \emph{sole} join between the
    reserve economy (Layer~0) and the action economy (Layer~1) --- the
    comparator's unit: every reserve
    input is converted by $\div\numeraire$ before it meets a count
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire}). The \safethresh{}-debit
    (\zcref{post:epoch:act-debit}) performs this conversion at each write:
    one act consumes exactly $\safethresh$ reserve units --- the join applied
    per action, never as a frozen factor.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Numéraire]
    \label{def:comparator:numeraire}
    The \emph{numéraire} $\numeraire \in \R_{>0}$ (units: reserve per
    action-credit) is the sole join of
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire}: every reserve-denominated
    input is divided by $\numeraire$ before meeting a count.  All reduced
    quantities are $\numeraire$-reductions ($\refstanding{}$,
    $\floorburn{}$, $\refrate{}$).
    $\numeraire$ is a structural-tier constant.
\end{definition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Two Costs}
\label{subsec:comparator:two-costs}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The comparator is faithful only if standing reflects cost no actor can fake.
The cost has two parts, with opposite anchors. One is inherited from Layer~0,
exogenous, and closed; the other is the network's own, endogenous, and ---
provably --- only bounded.

\begin{insight}[Inherited Costliness]
    \label{ins:comparator:inherited-costliness}
    The network needs one fact about burning: that it is costly,
    instantaneously and per unit, from the first cycle. Layer~0 establishes it.
    Reaching $\burnval{i} = M$ required destroying live-class receipt
    redeemable for exactly $M$ reserve units at the floor at which the burn
    settled (\attestationcref*{thm:interface:instantaneous-costliness}, the
    specified property SP4), with no operation mapping the record back to
    receipt or reserve. Irrevocability is \zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability};
    the increment is conservatively valued
    (\attestationcref{prop:interface:conservative-valuation}, SP6); aggregate
    pre-deposit capacity is bounded by \zcref{def:comparator:bootstrap-capacity} (SP5).
    These are everything \zcref{sec:epoch,sec:transport} consume of the source
    cost.
\end{insight}

\begin{definition}[Source Faithfulness]
    \label{def:comparator:source-faithful}
    A contribution to the standing $\standing{i}$ is \emph{source-faithful} iff
    the mass behind it is real and irrecoverable at the point of contribution.
    This factors at two levels, with different anchors:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{(S-actor)}] the contributing actor's mass
            $\burnval{j}$ is genuinely destroyed reserve-value --- floored at
            genesis by instantaneous costliness, post-market by net cost --- and
            non-transferable across addresses
            (\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame,def:comparator:frame-binding}).
            \emph{Status: closed} (it is Layer~0's specified property,
            inherited).
        \item[\textnormal{(S-edge)}] the contributing \emph{edge} represents a
            consummated event, not a bare claim --- a settlement edge that
            asserts a commercial tie corresponds to a \emph{recognized}
            settlement (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}), not merely to
            an authored Accept. \emph{Status: open}; its only anchor is the
            accountability cost of \zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}, and only
            partially (\zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}).
    \end{description}
    The two levels are not the same reality: (S-actor) asks whether there is
    mass behind the actor; (S-edge) asks whether there is an event behind the
    edge. Source faithfulness is their conjunction, and the comparator is
    source-faithful only to the depth its weakest level is anchored.
\end{definition}

\begin{postulate}[Accountability Cost]
    \label{post:comparator:accountability-cost}
    Where source cost cannot reach --- the truth of the \emph{claim an edge
    makes}, as opposed to the \emph{mass behind the actor} --- the comparator
    is defended by a second, weaker primitive. To author an edge that asserts
    an event (a settlement, an endorsement, a consent) is to commit a record
    that is \textbf{public, immutable, attributed, and self-defeating when false
    and checked}: it enters the append-only graph, cannot be retracted, names
    its author, and --- if the asserted event is not corroborated and a reader
    performs the corroboration check --- feeds the reputation conjunction and
    dilutes the author's own source (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation},
    \zcref{def:comparator:rate}). This is the \emph{accountability cost}: the
    price of being held to a claim one cannot retract or disown.

    Accountability cost shares three properties with source cost --- it is
    irrecoverable, non-transferable, and monotone --- and differs in the one
    that decides everything: it is \textbf{endogenous}. The record lives in the
    graph; the corroboration predicate is a function of graph edges
    (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}). A fabricated cluster authors its
    corroborating records as freely as a genuine one.

    \medskip
    \noindent\textbf{Ceiling (structural, not provisional).}
    Because it is endogenous, accountability cost respects the relabeling symmetry
    it is meant to break (\zcref{rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge}): both the
    record and its corroboration are gauge-covariant, so a relabeling carries a
    cluster's self-authored evidence along with it. Accountability cost therefore
    \textbf{deters but never anchors}: it raises the price of a false claim; it
    cannot make the claim impossible. A cohort willing to absorb the reputation
    loss and the diluted sources in bulk can drive an un-corroborated event
    through. Consequently the edge-semantic half of source faithfulness
    (\zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful}, S-edge) is \textbf{bounded, not
    closed}, and no calibration of Layer~1 constants closes it: closure would
    require an \emph{exogenous} floor on edge-claims, which the architecture
    does not provide and this postulate does not promise. This ceiling witness
    (\zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}) is not unfinished work --- it is
    the frontier of a primitive that does not terminate. The temporal gap in
    the weld beneath clause~(S)
    (\zcref{frontier:leverage-timing}) is, by contrast, a genuinely open
    admission problem, not an instance of this ceiling. This is the same gauge obstruction that founded the chapter
    (\zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster}), reappearing one level up, where the
    edge-claim has no Layer~0 beneath it to resolve it.
\end{postulate}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{The two costs the comparator stands on. They share three of four
    properties; they differ on exogeneity, and that single difference is the
    difference between closed and open.}
    \label{tbl:comparator:two-costs}
    \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l X X@{}}
        \toprule
        & \textbf{Source cost} & \textbf{Accountability cost} \\
        \midrule
        What it costs
            & destroying scarce \emph{external} value
            & authoring a public, immutable, attributed, self-defeating
              \emph{record} \\
        \addlinespace
        Origin
            & \textbf{exogenous}
            & \textbf{endogenous} (the record is in the graph) \\
        Shared properties
            & irrecoverable, non-transferable, monotone
            & irrecoverable, non-transferable, monotone \\
        Role
            & \textbf{breaks the gauge} --- anchors \emph{who has mass}
            & \textbf{respects the gauge} --- deters \emph{lying within the
              topology} \\
        Anchors
            & \zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful} (S-actor)
            & \zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful} (S-edge) \\
        Status
            & \textbf{closed}
            & \textbf{bounded, never closes} \\
        Owner
            & Layer~0 (axiomatized)
            & Layer~1 (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}) \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{remark}[Net Economic Cost Is Layer~0's, and Unneeded Here]
    \label{rem:comparator:net-cost-is-layer-zero}
    The conservation identity, the supply-fraction form, the
    $\livesplit$-independence of net cost, and the position decomposition are
    Layer~0-internal mechanism (the \emph{core} stratum): they explain
    \emph{why} the source cost's specified properties hold and are not
    exported, not even for citation. The network does not need them. Its Sybil
    resistance runs on the frame's faithfulness
    (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}), not on net
    economic cost. The closed-pool
    facts the net-cost analysis yields --- zero net cost at full supply
    ownership, net discipline activating only once an external market exists ---
    are inherited limitations (\zcref{rem:comparator:inherited-limitations}),
    not network results; they are exactly the genesis$\to$market sharpening of
    (S-actor) in \zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful}.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Binding Faithfulness}
\label{subsec:comparator:faithfulness}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{postulate}[Comparator Faithfulness]
    \label{post:comparator:faithfulness}
    The comparator $\standing{i}$ is \emph{faithful} iff source mass
    reaches standing only through all of:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{(S) source}]
            the contributing mass is real, irrecoverable, and bound to
            the contributing Actor
            (\zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful});

        \item[\textnormal{(N) num\'eraire}]
            every reserve-denominated input is divided by
            $\numeraire$ before it meets a count
            (\zcref{rem:comparator:type-asymmetry,%
            subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire});

        \item[\textnormal{(M) measurement}]
            standing is computed over the record and possessed within it
            by no one: the ledger after the measurement is the ledger
            before it
            (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-is-measurement});

        \item[\textnormal{(P1) conservation}]
            transport is row-stochastic on intact pairs: pair mass is
            neither created nor destroyed in transit, and allocation is
            rival, including against self
            (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation});

        \item[\textnormal{(P2) epoch set}]
            no standing quantity reads host-assigned order, relation
            frontiers, or any intra-epoch ``latest''
            (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism});

        \item[\textnormal{(P3) title}]
            settlement acts allocate toward a counterparty only through
            the epoch title fold
            (\zcref{post:epoch:settlement-standing-title-coupling});

        \item[\textnormal{(P4) memory}]
            no previous epoch's standing is a semantic input
            (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-memorylessness});

        \item[\textnormal{(P5) universality}]
            every accepted Actor-authored act is weighed exactly once,
            resolving to a person recipient or to self-retention, and a
            standing-bearing hyper-edge is consumed atomically, so no
            unmatched leg, unrelated incoming edge, or passive artifact
            can carry or redirect standing
            (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing,%
            def:graph:act-edge-projection,%
            cor:graph:standing-act-atomicity,%
            def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution});

        \item[\textnormal{(P6) domains}]
            folded coefficients are summed under the published domain
            weights (\zcref{post:epoch:domain-weighted-act-sum});

        \item[\textnormal{(P7) tilt}]
            recipient standing modulates only the relative apportionment
            of authored allocation, hop-faded, at the greatest certified
            rung (\zcref{post:epoch:hop-faded-responsive-tilt});

        \item[\textnormal{(P8) cluster rate}]
            transport within a closed community is purely distributive,
            so no internal arrangement of regard raises what that
            community's ledger backs
            (\zcref{post:epoch:cluster-rate-invariance});

        \item[\textnormal{(Q) epoch quantization}]
            final-set admission reads only the completed post-debit
            standing result.
    \end{description}

    A contribution reaching $\standing{i}$ by any route that does not
    factor through (S)--(Q) is an \emph{un-floored injection}.  In
    particular: creation or deletion of pair mass in transit;
    order-derived standing; previous-standing reads; a tilt-created
    relation unsupported by authored acts; pre-normalization
    ``emission'' scalings, which are a mathematical no-op; per-hop
    emission damping, which charges a relay for its source's obligation;
    passive-node splicing; unmatched hyper-edge legs; unviewed
    third-party redirection; source-count totalization; and any positive
    tilt above the accepted rung.  Faithfulness is their absence.

    The hull bound of \zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull} is a
    consequence and audit witness of this construction, not a
    substitute for source or fold provenance.

    \medskip
    \noindent\textbf{Discharge status.}
    Every clause is accounted for here, and two are accounted for by saying
    they are not closed.

    (S) is closed at the Actor level by Layer~0 and remains bounded at
    the edge-semantic level
    (\zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful}); (N) is the dimensional
    discipline of \zcref{subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire}.
    (P1)--(P2) and (P5)--(P8) are discharged by construction and
    certificate: conservation is an identity of the operator rather
    than a property of its fixed point
    (\zcref{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport}), and the
    accepted rung carries a certified invariant box, unique fixed point,
    and gate-decisive certificate
    (\zcref{def:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium,%
    def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid}).  (P3) consumes the title fold as
    published.  (P4) is discharged by
    \zcref{cor:dynamics:standing-initialization-independence}: the accepted
    rung's equilibrium is unique in its invariant box, so the solve reaches
    it from any admissible starting point and the previous epoch's standing
    cannot survive as a semantic input even when it is used as one
    numerically.  Source emission caps what a history carries without
    deleting any of it (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}), which is
    what keeps (P1) and (P8) compatible with a source-root rule at all.

    (M) is discharged by construction \emph{and} by fixture.  No step of the
    solve writes the ledger --- allocation, transport, tilt and the mediant
    are functions of it --- and the suite checks it rather than trusting the
    reading: every ledger entry is snapshotted, the solve runs, and the
    entries are compared
    (\zcref{ver:standing:ledger-invariance}).  Construction is the argument;
    the fixture is what an independent implementation can fail.

    (Q) is \textbf{not discharged}.  It is an obligation on the boundary
    operator, not a property of the standing construction: this paper defines
    what the completed post-debit result is, and the admission rules read it,
    but no result here establishes that final-set admission reads \emph{only}
    that.  It is the one clause with no supporting reference in its own
    statement, and it is stated as a requirement on deployment.

    The temporal frame-sampling seam remains
    \zcref{frontier:leverage-timing}.  The edge-semantic precondition of
    (S) remains bounded rather than closed for settlement ties
    (\zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}).  Conservation closes
    cross-target cloning; it is \emph{not} an Actor-splitting
    invariance, which remains a nonclaim pending split fixtures and an
    explicit theorem.  This postulate names the property those residuals
    limit; it does not phase the limits away.
\end{postulate}

\begin{insight}[The Comparator Is the Universal Amplifier]
    \label{ins:comparator:universal-amplifier}
    Because only relative position is comparable
    (\zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster}), every channel that reads value must
    grade its output by standing. The comparator is therefore the single factor
    every value channel multiplies: the dimensionless factor $\ampfactor{C}$ appears in the
    relevance score (\zcref{eq:sorting:relevance-score}, what a reader is shown)
    and in the reward formula (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}, what a
    contributor is owed) by \emph{necessity}, not coincidence. The comparator
    has one binding and two readouts: the weld that reattaches it to the graph
    each epoch (\zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}), and the two
    projections --- feed visibility and reward share --- through which it is
    observed. Each channel supplies its own structure (path relevance, content
    norm, centrality, attribution); the comparator supplies the common
    relativity.

    Your standing is the action-mass-weighted commitment consensus
    carried by the complete initiator-owned vouches that safely reach
    you.  A vouch is not every positive-parity edge and not every record
    targeting a Profile: it is one complete act designated by the closed
    standing census
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection,def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).
    For an act authored by~$a$, source~$u$ reaches it only by allocating
    to~$a$ first, and what travels onward is a share of \emph{$u$'s}
    conserved unit; a passive artifact supplies context and no inherited
    standing authority
    (\zcref{rem:nodes:reference-author-allocation}).

    The two terminal readouts remain \emph{what you are shown} and
    \emph{what you are owed}.  Scrutiny reads the same field through the
    target activation and the actor-authored support mass, while the
    certificate admits only the relational fractions that the coupled
    dynamics cannot safely admit; reach remains the occasion for an
    out-of-band check whose only on-network trace is the vouch
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:vouch-not-check}).  The appearance of
    $\ampfactor{C}$ in both terminal channels is therefore still the
    expected signature of one comparator seen twice, not a double count
    (\zcref{rem:transport:cross-channel-commitment-amplification}).

    The hat is load-bearing: the raw
    form adds a pure number to a reserve-denominated quantity, the units error
    of \zcref{subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire}; the recursion's own
    self-weight $1$ is a count and exempt. In reduced coordinates, the adapted
    comparator readout is a function of dimensionless state only: a
    $\numeraire$ migration no longer silently rescales feed scores or reward
    shares after re-adaptation, restoring readout compatibility and matching the
    hat-family siblings already frozen at epoch boundaries.
\end{insight}

\begin{remark}[Amplifier Rendering Is Terminal]
    \label{rem:comparator:amplifier-rendering}
    Zero standing is unchanged by the reduced readout:
    $\refstanding{}=0 \Leftrightarrow \standing{}=0$, so every unit-amplifier
    corollary keeps its value. The gate-relative alternative
    $(1+\refstanding{}/\partfloor)$ is rejected: it couples the terminal
    readout to an admission-policy dial and would make display contrast a
    host-steerable surface. A guild that owns a terminal rendering may instead
    publish $\ampfactor{}^\gamma$ under \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}, with
    disclosed exponent $\gamma$ and canonical default $\gamma=1$.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the Conserved-Allocation Guarantee]
    \label{rem:comparator:conserved-allocation-scope}
    Conserved allocation proves provenance and rivalry, not every property one
    might attach to social consent.

    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{No passive or unowned redirection.}
              An Actor's source cannot be spliced through a passive
              artifact, an unmatched hyper-edge leg, or an act authored
              by an Actor outside the source-relative delegation path.

        \item \textbf{No target veto at Layer~1.}
              A complete positive person-vouch is unilateral.  It may
              lift or dilute its target within the contributing rate
              hull.  The target has no Layer~1 acceptance predicate;
              adding one would be a separate mechanism.

        \item \textbf{Cross-target rivalry is closed.}
              A source disposes of one conserved unit over self and all
              recipients (\zcref{thm:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}),
              so allocating more to one beneficiary allocates less to the
              others or to self.  Beneficiaries \emph{do} split rather than
              clone --- which Edition~4 could not say, and which is the
              substantive change conserved allocation buys.

        \item \textbf{Splitting invariance is not.}
              Conservation constrains each row, not the number of rows.
              Whether an Actor fragmenting its ledger and acts across
              addresses can change any standing outcome remains a nonclaim
              pending split fixtures and an explicit theorem
              (\zcref{frontier:allocation-split-invariance}).  Citing
              conservation as splitting invariance is a defect.

        \item \textbf{Dynamic safety is not a movement cap.}
              The certificate proves contraction on the rate hull box.  It
              does not by itself prove that one-boundary standing movement is
              small.  Standing movement and transported mass are published
              verification quantities and remain calibration obligations.
    \end{enumerate}

    These distinctions are part of comparator faithfulness: the paper
    states exactly which property is proved rather than allowing the
    word ``safe'' or ``consent'' to promise more than the mechanism
    supplies.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Sybil Resistance Is Faithfulness]
    \label{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}
    Sybil resistance is the security reading of comparator
    faithfulness: multiplying raw accounts or passive structure cannot
    manufacture source, target activation, or delegated standing flow.

    A never-ignited fabricated Actor has residual source
    $\commitrate{}=0$; with no genuine source reaching it, its final standing
    mediant is zero
    (\zcref{rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support}).  The below-wall
    activation clamp is a fixed path factor, not a source, so it cannot
    manufacture standing.  Incoming
    raw edges, popular Chats, Content, Items, Types, Comments, Messages,
    Offers, unmatched Reference/T or Invitation/T legs, and
    self-vouches cannot ignite or reroute standing
    (\zcref{rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support,%
    def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
    cor:graph:standing-act-atomicity}).  Non-transferability prevents
    pooling source across addresses
    (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}).

    A fabricated actor can enter the relational standing field only
    after acquiring genuine costly source and a valid target activation,
    and thereafter only through complete person-vouches authored along
    the source-relative delegation path.  Thus account multiplication
    remains gauge-equivalent zero-source structure; neither artifact
    density nor third-party leg splicing converts it into standing.

    The network-layer resistance statement of
    \zcref{cor:scalability:sybil-resistance} is this corollary read for
    security rather than measurement.
    \proofsketch{No source gives no valid activation; complete-act
    ownership and passive non-interference block structural
    redirection; non-transferability blocks source aggregation.}
\end{corollary}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Capacity and Admission Benchmarks}
\label{subsec:comparator:capacity-and-admission-benchmarks}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Bootstrap Capacity Bound]
    \label{def:comparator:bootstrap-capacity}
    \attestationref{prop:interface:bootstrap-capacity}%
    The network reads the Layer~0 bootstrap capacity bound under its own
    symbol:
    \begin{equation}
        \burncap \;\coloneqq\; \attestcap .
        \label{eq:comparator:capacity}
    \end{equation}
    During the bootstrapping phase, aggregate $\burnval{}$ before external
    deposits cannot exceed $\burncap$
    (\attestationcref*{prop:interface:bootstrap-capacity}, SP5). This is the
    capacity bound that holds the comparator source-faithful against the
    costless Sybil through the pre-market interval, before net cost extends
    (S-actor) faithfulness to the resourced reserve-holder
    (\zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful},
    \zcref{rem:comparator:inherited-limitations}). The bound's closed form is
    Layer~0's; the network uses only the interface object $\attestcap$.
\end{definition}

For $m$ unsupported proposed acts, the burn-value admission benchmarks
are the W1, safety-wall, and door-neutral thresholds
(\zcref{cor:epoch:universal-burn-benchmarks}):
\[
    B_{\mathrm{W1}}(m)=m\safethresh,
    \qquad
    B_{\mathrm{safety}}(m)=2m\safethresh,
    \qquad
    B_{\mathrm{door}}(m)=m(\safethresh+\numeraire\partfloor).
\]
Projected through the Layer~0 cost interface, the corresponding reserve
deposits are
\begin{equation}
    \delta_{\mathrm{W1}}(m)=m\safethresh\,\attestunitcost,
    \quad
    \delta_{\mathrm{safety}}(m)=2m\safethresh\,\attestunitcost,
    \quad
    \delta_{\mathrm{door}}(m)=m(\safethresh+\numeraire\partfloor)\attestunitcost,
    \label{eq:comparator:admission-benchmark-deposits}
\end{equation}
with $\attestunitcost=1/\netliveshare$ the Layer~0 unit-cost projection
(\attestationcref*{def:interface:net-live-share}).  The expressions are
interface-pure and unsupported: relational standing, final W2b, the
finite epoch record budget, and boundary selection all still apply.

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Burn-value admission benchmarks for $m$ unsupported acts.}
    \label{tbl:comparator:admission-benchmarks}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l c l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Benchmark} & \textbf{Burn value} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
        \midrule
        W1           & $m\safethresh$
            & pays the proposed debits \\
        safety       & $2m\safethresh$
            & unsupported final source at $\safefloor$ \\
        door-neutral & $m(\safethresh+\numeraire\partfloor)$
            & unsupported final source at the effective door \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Monetary Surface (Cited)}
\label{subsec:comparator:the-surface}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{remark}[The Network Prices the Frame]
    \label{rem:comparator:network-prices-the-frame}
    By \zcref{rem:comparator:neutrality-from-silence}, \textbf{the
    network is the layer that prices the frame --- and it prices it as the
    comparator.}  It imports $\burnval{i}$, derives residual source
    $\commitrate{i}$, compiles complete actor-authored person-vouches,
    admits certificate-safe source-relative flow, and forms
    $\standing{i}$ as the exact balance/count mediant
    (\zcref{def:comparator:rate,def:epoch:final-standing}).
    Reading the result through the two terminal value channels
    (\zcref{ins:comparator:universal-amplifier}) is precisely the meaning
    Layer~0 holds open for a consumer to confer.

    This is the layer boundary working as designed: destruction is real
    and irrevocable at Layer~0; the Actor-only relational projection and
    standing assigned to that record are Layer~1's own public act.  Passive
    context remains available to feed, attribution, title, and content
    without acquiring the authority to redirect the imported frame.
    Everything in
    this subsection below the comparator is read from Layer~0 in prose only ---
    cited, never used in a network published-quantity formula.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The Monetary Surface, in Layer~0 Nouns]
    \label{rem:comparator:surface-readings}
    The instrument deployed under \emph{Peer Attestation} is the Layer~0
    \emph{reserve receipt}, held in two redemption classes --- the \liveclass{}
    and the \tlockclass{} (\attestationcref*{def:model:classes}). The system is
    named for what it \emph{produces} --- the attestation --- not for what it
    \emph{destroys}. The network therefore
    carries no monetary brand of its own. It names the surface in Layer~0's own
    nouns and glyphs of record, and only in prose: every quantity below is cited,
    never used in a network published-quantity formula.

    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Layer~0 surface noun (cited, not in machinery)}
            & \textbf{Where defined} \\
        \midrule
        reserve pool $\reservepool{}$, genesis reserve $\genesisreserve$
            & \attestationcref*{def:model:reserve-pool},
              \attestationcref{post:model:genesis} \\
        receipt supply $\totsupply{}$; \liveclass{} $\livesupply{}$,
        \tlockclass{} $\tlocksupply{}$
            & \attestationcref*{def:model:supply},
              \attestationcref{def:model:classes} \\
        redemption-rate floor $\ratefloor{}$, bootstrap ceiling $\ratefloorcap$
            & \attestationcref*{def:model:ratefloor},
              \attestationcref{prop:containment:floor-ceiling} \\
        fee rate $\feerate$, split $\livesplit$
            & \attestationcref{def:model:fee-and-split} \\
        bootstrapping / normal phase
            & \attestationcref{def:model:bootstrapping-phase},
              \attestationcref{def:model:normal-phase} \\
        maturity conversion $\matcycle$, lead $\matlead$
            & \attestationcref*{def:maturity:conversion},
              \attestationcref{post:maturity:announcement} \\
        \tlockclass{} confidence price $\confprice{}$
            & \attestationcref{rem:maturity:confidence-signal} \\
        market discipline, anti-correlation
            & \attestationcref{sec:discipline},
              \attestationcref{prop:discipline:anti-correlation} \\
        deposit / burn / redeem
            & \attestationcref{def:operations:deposit},
              \attestationcref{def:operations:burn},
              \attestationcref{def:operations:redemption} \\
        cycle burn fraction $\cycleburnfrac{}$
            & \attestationcref{def:operations:cycle-burn-fraction} \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{center}

    The redemption-rate floor is $\ratefloor{}$ (Layer~0's glyph); the one-time
    class relabel is \emph{maturity conversion}; the secondary-market signal is
    the confidence price $\confprice{}$. Here ``floor'' is the
    Layer~0 redemption floor $\ratefloor{}$ ($\varphi$), a distinct object from the
    Layer~1 num\'eraire $\numeraire$ and the participation floor $\partfloor$;
    neither is ever attached to an
    edge-claim, which is deterred by accountability cost
    (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Operator Identity]
    \label{rem:comparator:operator-identity}
    The Layer~0 operator --- fee recipient and maturity announcer, attested
    under the operator subscript $\attest{\opidx}$ --- \emph{is} the network
    operator of \zcref{subsec:introduction:two-layers-derived}, who additionally
    maintains the graph and the epoch machinery. The network reads the
    operator's attestation as $\burnval{\opidx}$; the bounds on it are
    Layer~0's specified seigniorage results
    (\attestationcref*{thm:seigniorage:bootstrapping-bound},
    \attestationcref{thm:seigniorage:lifetime-envelope}), cited rather than
    re-proved. The minting fee is the operator's sole protocol-level inflow.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Limitations}
\label{subsec:comparator:limitations}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{remark}[Inherited Limitations]
    \label{rem:comparator:inherited-limitations}
    The limitations of the source cost are properties of a closed, full-reserve
    pool, and are Layer~0's (\attestationcref*{sec:limitations}): net
    economic cost is zero when one party holds the entire supply; maximum
    irrecoverable exposure during bootstrapping is the time-locked-class
    portion; the non-decreasing floor imposes a cross-cohort deflationary
    asymmetry; external deposit incentives are exogenous to the receipt
    mechanism; and maturity timing is operator-discretionary, disciplined by
    the confidence price rather than by mechanism constraint. The network
    inherits each as stated. In comparator terms these are the genesis$\to$market
    sharpening of (S-actor): at genesis the frame is source-faithful against
    the \emph{costless} Sybil unconditionally; net economic cost is what extends
    (S-actor) faithfulness to the \emph{resourced} reserve-holder once an
    external market exists (\zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful}). The
    portfolio-level bound --- zero net cost across colluding addresses --- is
    real but is neutralised at the network layer by frame non-transferability,
    not by net cost (\zcref{rem:comparator:net-cost-is-layer-zero}).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[A Structural Ceiling, Not a Provisional One]
    \label{rem:comparator:structural-ceiling}
    Every other limitation in this specification is provisional --- a constant
    to be calibrated, a phase to be entered. This one is not. The edge-semantic
    half of faithfulness (\zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful}, S-edge) rests
    on endogenous accountability cost (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}).
    No choice of Layer~1
    constant closes it; closure would require an exogenous floor on edge-claims
    that the architecture does not provide. This is the document's one
    \emph{structural} limitation: the binding axis is bounded by construction,
    because the relabeling obstruction that founded the chapter
    (\zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster}) reappears at the edge level with no
    Layer~0 beneath it. The network states this rather than phasing it away
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:the-floor-we-name}).
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Deferred binding-axis frontier.}
Three frontier items touch the comparator, all on the binding axis; all are
stated with full numbering in \zcref{app:frontiers}.

\emph{Cross-layer burn-timing} (\zcref{frontier:leverage-timing}) is the temporal
gap in the weld beneath clause~(S): the weld samples once per epoch
(\zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability}) and can be front-run within a Layer~0
cycle. The count-free half --- the within-cycle bound, the only ratio involved
--- is owned and bounded by Layer~0 (\attestationcref*{open:leverage-timing}); the
frozen-factor half is the network's. The two halves share the slug
\texttt{leverage-timing} by design.

\emph{Settlement injection under non-recognition}
(\zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}) is the open edge-semantic precondition of
clause~(S): a settlement edge passes (N) and (P1)--(P8) cleanly, and its
Layer~0 value welds like any other, yet may stamp
a commercial tie for an event that never consummated. It is the canonical
instance of accountability cost failing to close
(\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}).

\emph{Operator deposit disambiguation} is \emph{not} a network problem: it asks
whether operator deposits are distinguishable from non-operator deposits under
the public-auditability guarantee, a pure reserve-economy question with no
count content. It is owned entirely by Layer~0
(\attestationcref*{open:operator-disambiguation}); the network defers without
restating.
