\section{The Network}
\label{sec:network}

The introduction said what the network is for; the comparator chapter built its
foundational object. This chapter defines the machine that admits one completed
epoch state and publishes the shared objects derived from it, and it is
deliberately short, because its work is to draw boundaries.

Four boundaries are load-bearing. First, graph state changes only through a
\emph{write}: admission of a valid final set of dependent records at epoch
closure. Second, the binding surface is the feedback closure of final-set
admission. Third, every published object carries one of the five permission
tags of \zcref{def:network:object-taxonomy}. Fourth, the host owes the complete
public material required to reproduce the accepted final state and its conserved
standing result.

Edition~5 makes one further boundary explicit. Standing is not updated record by
record and is not advanced one step from previous standing. For each proposed
final write set, the network forms the completed tentative edge set and final
post-debit ledger, weighs every accepted act into one conserved unit of
allocation per Actor, and solves a single same-epoch equilibrium at the greatest
certified tilt rung, publishing one final standing vector. There are no stages:
depth enters through the published depth mass, not through a ladder of
separately certified admissions. Trial candidate sets and intermediate solver
iterates are not Layer-1 objects.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Write}
\label{subsec:network:the-write}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Write]
    \label{def:network:write}
    A \emph{write} is the admission, at an epoch boundary, of the accepted
    authoritative ordered authored-act sequence $\actsequence{k}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}) into the public edge set, via its
    record projection:
    \[
        \edgeincrement{k}=\bigcup_{q\in \actsequence{k}}\actedges{q},\qquad E_k=E_{k-1}\cup \edgeincrement{k}.
    \]
    Every act in $\actsequence{k}$ is Actor-approved (\zcref{def:graph:approval-witness}),
    formation-valid, and dependency-valid at its position
    ($\depok{k}{}$); $\actsequence{k}$ is a finite union of dependent sets
    (\zcref{def:graph:dependent-act-set}), each whole or not at all
    (\zcref{cor:graph:act-projection-atomicity}).  It is written only after the
    completed tentative state indexed by~$\actsequence{k}$ passes
    \zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}, including formation, dependency
    closure, aggregate solvency, the conserved standing certificate, individual
    final safety, epoch backpressure, and the epoch record budget.

    A write is the sole mutation of graph state, and it occurs only at epoch
    closure (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-closure}).  The dependent set remains
    the atomic dependency unit \emph{inside}~$\actsequence{k}$; the accepted epoch unit is
    the ordered authored-act sequence, and participants must agree on $\actsequence{k}$, not
    merely on the record set $\actsequence{k}$.  No record in a failed proposed final set
    becomes part of~$E$, and no standing value computed while testing that set
    becomes a Layer-1 object.  What was not written was not refused --- it was
    nothing.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[What Is Not a Write]
    \label{rem:network:not-a-write}
    Several near-misses, kept deliberately outside the definition. Derived
    edges are recomputation from the certificate, never writes
    (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}): Layer~1 authors nothing, and raw
    Self-edge derivation (\zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}) remains a
    reading, not a write. Payload reduction is not a write
    (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}). A non-written candidate is
    not a failed write: it leaves no Layer-1 trace and mutates nothing.

    A provisional standing solve performed while testing a candidate final set
    is not a graph event. Nor are the internal depth-two, depth-three, or
    depth-four equilibria separate writes: they are values inside one boundary
    computation, as are cache updates and fixed-point solver iterations. Only
    the accepted final set and its final standing package speak.
    ``Append-only'' remains the right name for the \emph{store}; the \emph{act}
    is the write.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Admission Closure}
\label{subsec:network:admission-closure}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The boundary between what binds and what is free is usually drawn as a list.
A list is fragile --- it must be maintained, and it cannot tell a guild
whether a \emph{new} quantity it wishes to own is binding. The boundary is
not a list; it is a closure, and any participant can decide membership.

\begin{definition}[Admission Closure and the Binding Boundary]
    \label{def:network:admission-closure}
    Work on the \emph{consumption graph}, whose nodes are the network's
    published values and rules and whose directed edge $V \to r$ records that
    read-site~$r$ consumes value~$V$. The \emph{admission set} $\mathcal{A}$
    is the set of rules that decide whether a proposed final epoch write
    set becomes the next public edge set:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{(formation)}] the act-identifier, endpoint-typing,
            asserted-parent, dependent-set, approval-witness, and
            authoritative-order rules
            (\zcref{def:graph:act-identifier,def:graph:act-causal-parents,%
            def:graph:dependent-act-set,def:graph:approval-witness,%
            def:graph:authoritative-act-order}); formation is class-syntactic
            and stateless except act-identifier freshness
            (\zcref{lem:graph:act-edge-identifier-uniqueness}); only an approved verified act may
            be ordered, and only a Registration may carry fresh grounded
            endpoints (\zcref{def:graph:registration});
        \item[\textnormal{(final state)}] the proposed completed edge set and
            final post-debit balance/count pairs
            (\zcref{def:epoch:proposed-final-act-state});
        \item[\textnormal{(conserved standing)}] the complete conserved
            standing package --- the base allocation matrix, wall-clamped
            activation, the accepted tilt rung, the depth mass, source
            emission, and the certified equilibrium
            (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package}) --- which feeds
            W2a/W2b through the published final standing and stamps;
        \item[\textnormal{(final gates)}] aggregate solvency W1, individual
            final standing safety W2a, the epoch door W2b, and the epoch
            record budget (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule});
        \item[\textnormal{(recognition)}] settlement recognition and the prior
            title input its clause~(iii) consumes
            (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}); recognition gates
            \emph{binding effect}, not the write --- an unauthorized Accept is
            written but never binds --- and reads no selection position
            (\zcref{rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance});
        \item[\textnormal{(write)}] admission of the valid final write set and
            publication of the final edge set
            (\zcref{def:network:write,post:epoch:final-edge-set}); the host
            writes a valid sequence of dependent sets within the target
            budget, and selection among valid final sets is discretionary and
            touches membership only.
    \end{description}
    The \emph{feedback closure} $\overline{\mathcal{A}}$ is the transitive
    set of values read --- directly, through other values, or through a
    binding validity predicate --- into any rule in~$\mathcal{A}$.

    A value belongs to the closure not only when it appears
    arithmetically in W1/W2 or recognition, but also when its validity
    decides which value may appear there.  Consequently the fold, the base
    allocation matrix, the emission fractions, the hop matrices, the hull box,
    and the certificate verdict at each rung all lie in
    $\overline{\mathcal{A}}$: they determine which rung is accepted, and
    therefore which final standing, reaches W2.

    A proof transcript is different.  It is \emph{evidence about} a
    binding value and has no alternative arithmetic read-site.
    Replacing a valid proof transcript with another proof of the same
    committed statement does not change standing.  Such transcripts are
    verification objects, not closure inputs.

    A read-site is \emph{terminal} when its output is
    consumed only by an agent (a user, a guild, an advertiser) and never
    re-enters the forward evolution of~$E$. An object is then
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textbf{binding}] iff it lies in $\overline{\mathcal{A}}$ ---
            it influences admission;
        \item[\textbf{free}] iff every one of its read-sites is terminal.
    \end{description}
\end{definition}

Two laws make the predicate usable. \emph{Authority is per read-site, not per
object.} A value with one feedback read-site and one terminal read-site is
closure-authored yet freely readable. A \emph{straddler} is such a value
whose terminal read-sites moreover consume the published value as an
authoritative semantic object rather than recompute it for audit; exactly two
first-class objects straddle this way --- the standing field $\standing{i}$
(read by the gate, and read again as the reward multiplier $\ampfactor{i}$)
and the title certificate $\titlecert{k}$ (read by recognition clause~(iii),
and read again by guild routing). \emph{Recomputability is irrelevant to
authority.} The standing field, the title certificate, and the whole conserved
standing package are all recomputable from $E_k$ yet binding: recomputability
sets \emph{audit cost}, never \emph{permission}. The package contains many
binding intermediate values --- the base matrix, the hop matrices, the
emission fractions --- but only the final standing field is a straddler; those
intermediates carry no independent terminal semantics and exist only to
compose the one operator. The permission axis is feedback;
the publication axis is recomputability; they are orthogonal.

\paragraph{The decision a guild runs.}
For any quantity~$V$ a guild wishes to own, the verdict is mechanical:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item list every read-site~$r$ that consumes~$V$;
    \item for each~$r$, ask whether $r$'s output re-enters the forward
        evolution of~$E$ --- whether it feeds the write rule
        (W1/W2a/W2b), the formation rule, or settlement recognition. If
        so, $r$ is a \emph{feedback} read-site; otherwise (read by a human,
        guild, or advertiser) it is \emph{terminal};
    \item if \emph{every} read-site is terminal, $V$ is free: the guild may
        reimplement it;
    \item if \emph{any} read-site is feedback, $V$ is binding: the guild
        must consume the published value and may not override it --- though
        it may still recompute~$V$ to audit it.
\end{enumerate}
The two straddlers are the entire subtlety. Title has read-sites
(a)~recognition clause~(iii), \emph{feedback}, and (b)~guild routing through
the owner's Self-edge, \emph{terminal}; the one feedback site makes it
binding, and the reason is not that title is hard to compute --- it is a
deterministic fold of~$E_k$ --- but that two guilds disagreeing on the owner
would recognize different next settlements, forking~$E$. Standing is the
same: binding as gate input, free as a number a guild reads downstream.
Everything above the straddlers in the ledger (\zcref{tbl:symbols:boundary})
is consume-only because it \emph{is} the kernel or feeds it; everything below
is free because it is terminal.

\begin{remark}[The Boundary in One Sentence]
    \label{rem:network:boundary-one-sentence}
    The binding surface is the feedback closure of final-set admission:
    the accepted record set, final post-debit ledger, constants,
    formation and recognition rules, the complete conserved standing
    package, final standing and stamps, and the W1/W2 validity verdicts.

    The base allocation matrix, the accepted tilt rung, the depth mass, the
    emission fractions, and the certificate verdict are binding because
    changing any of them may change final standing and therefore final-set
    admission.

    Raw feed scores, raw damped weights, raw determinant parity, raw
    bridge composition, CAN values, payload rendering, identity
    association, and reward formulas remain terminal.  They may be
    recomputed or replaced by guilds under
    \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}; the one residual tie leak
    (\zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}) is consumed terminally,
    so its remedy is on the guild's side of the line.

    Recomputability grants an audit right, never an override right.
    Previous standing and solver caches grant neither: they may change
    work but not the certified result.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Object Taxonomy}
\label{subsec:network:object-taxonomy}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The closure sorts objects into binding and free. Five finer tags are needed
in practice, because ``binding'' conflates three different reasons a value is
published, and because one class of values crosses the seam from below.

\begin{definition}[Object Taxonomy]
    \label{def:network:object-taxonomy}
    Every value this document names carries exactly one tag, decided by its
    read-sites against \zcref{def:network:admission-closure}:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\tagLzero{}] the value originates below the comparator seam
            and is read at import (\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame}).
            The network cites it and can never author it.
        \item[\tagclosure{}] at least one read-site re-enters the admission
            set, directly or through other values. Consume at the published
            value; recomputation is an audit right, never an override right.
        \item[\tagverify{}] the value is evidence required to reproduce
            or check a closure output, and neither the value nor its
            verdict selects among alternative closure outputs.  A proof
            transcript is \tagverify{}; a certificate scalar or
            pass/fail result that decides whether a positive standing
            schedule takes effect is \tagclosure{}.  Withholding
            evidence breaks auditability, falsifying it is publicly
            demonstrable, and no formula consumes it.
        \item[\tagbyproduct{}] the epoch computation produces the value
            anyway, and the host \textsc{may} publish it as a present ---
            non-normative, never load-bearing, clearly labeled as such. A
            participant who distrusts it recomputes from the certificate.
        \item[\tagLtwo{}] every read-site is terminal. The guild's to
            reimplement, under the grant of
            \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}.
    \end{description}
    Shared mathematics (norms, delimiters, number sets) is tag-exempt.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Conserved Standing Package]
    \label{def:network:conserved-standing-package}
    For a proposed final write set~$\actsequence{k}$, the \emph{conserved
    standing package} is the complete deterministic object from which any
    participant reproduces the final standing result and its admission
    consequences.  It contains or publishes:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep,label=(\roman*)]
        \item the proposed final epoch state of
              \zcref{def:epoch:proposed-final-act-state} --- final edge set, final
              residual balances and action counts, settled burn snapshot, and
              the constants in force;

        \item the fold cells, their coefficients $\foldcoef{\foldcell}$, the
              recipient resolution of each, the published domain weights, and
              the base allocation matrix $\basescore{u}{j}$ they determine
              (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-fold-cell,%
              def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
              eq:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation});

        \item the responsive and safety-wall-clamped activation formulas
              (\zcref{def:epoch:responsive-vouch-activation,%
              def:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation}) and the safety wall
              $\safefloor$;

        \item the tilt profile shape, the published backoff grid, the accepted
              rung $\tiltstrength{k}$, and the certificate verdict of every
              rung attempted above it
              (\zcref{post:epoch:hop-faded-responsive-tilt,%
              def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid});

        \item the depth mass $\depthmass{m}$, the hop allocation matrices, and
              the conserved transport $\transport{\standingeq}$ they compose
              (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-depth-mass,%
              def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport});

        \item the emission fractions $\emission{u}$
              (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}).  These are derivable from
              item~(i) by any participant, and are published anyway: a reader
              auditing why a source's history carried as far as it did should
              not have to re-derive the reason;

        \item the rate hull box $\hullbox{k}$, the standing certificate
              $\standingcert{k}$ with its verdict, the fixed-point enclosure,
              final standing, final stamps, door headroom, and the W1/W2
              verdicts (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull,%
              def:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium,%
              def:epoch:final-standing,def:epoch:final-act-stamps});

        \item the public interval boxes, residual bounds, and other
              reproducibility evidence needed to check the mathematical claims
              independently.
    \end{enumerate}

    Items~(i)--(vii), their deterministic rules, and their certificate verdicts
    are \tagclosure{}: changing any of them may change final standing and
    therefore final-set admission.  The interval boxes and residual reports of
    item~(viii) are \tagverify{} evidence: they prove the binding package was
    computed correctly but supply no independent standing input.

    The package contains no previous-standing input and no prior standing
    memory.  A previous epoch solution may initialize a solver or cache, but
    changing that initialization cannot change the certified fixed point.  No
    hashes, roots, or source digests are normative: the package states the
    formula editions and constants used, and any participant reruns those
    public formulas against the declared input data.

    Only the package attached to the accepted final write set becomes the
    epoch-$k$ standing package.  Packages computed while testing unsuccessful
    candidate sets are not Layer-1 objects.
\end{definition}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{The five tags, by representative objects.  The
    normative per-object assignment is the ledger of
    \zcref{tbl:symbols:boundary}.}
    \label{tbl:network:object-taxonomy}
    \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l X@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Tag} & \textbf{Representative objects} \\
        \midrule
        \tagLzero{}
            & $\burnval{i}$, $\burncap$, the boundary burn state, and
              the frame's ordered codomain \\
        \addlinespace
        \tagclosure{}
            & $E_k$ and accepted $\actsequence{k}$; binding constants
              $\invtemp,\bleedparam,\numeraire,\polfloor,\safethresh,
              \marginfactor,\epochlen,\snapbuf,\hopmax,\maxpayload$;
              standing formula editions; final residual balances and action
              counts; fold cells, coefficients $\foldcoef{\foldcell}$, and
              recipient resolutions; the base allocation matrix
              $\basescore{}{}$; wall-clamped activation constants; the tilt
              profile and accepted rung $\tiltstrength{k}$; the depth mass
              $\depthmass{m}$; the emission fractions $\emission{u}$; the
              conserved transport $\transport{\standingeq}$; the hull box, the
              certificate $\standingcert{k}$, and its verdict; final standing,
              stamps, and W1/W2;
              the straddlers $\standing{i}$ and $\titlecert{k}$ \\
        \addlinespace
        \tagverify{}
            & complete-act and candidate-path replay reports; accepted
              interval boxes; generalized max-tie enclosures; fixed-point
              residual reports; point-Jacobian comparisons; dependent-set
              partition; door headroom $\doorheadroom{k}$; backoff and
              transport diagnostics; attested boundary timestamp \\
        \addlinespace
        \tagbyproduct{}
            & host-cached canonical raw defaults and derived values:
              $\divpref$, raw depth~$L$, $\wspam$,
              $\wmax$, $\wmaxop$, raw $\dampedweight{e}$, raw
              $\detsign{e}$, canonical-default feed/bridge-consent
              values, membership, content norms, and post-ranking
              diagnostics, each clearly labeled non-normative \\
        \addlinespace
        \tagLtwo{}
            & raw feed $S(u,c)$; raw depth and diversity preference;
              raw damped-weight, parity, and path-composition formulas;
              reward $R_C$; CAN and its aggregation function; bridge
              composition; identity association; license enforcement \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{remark}[Four Cells Worth a Sentence Each]
    \label{rem:network:taxonomy-subtleties}
    \emph{Final standing and title} remain the two straddlers: each has
    one feedback read-site and one terminal readership.

    \emph{Intermediate standing objects} are binding but not straddlers:
    the base matrix and the hop matrices are consumed only by the transport
    they compose.

    \emph{Certificate values and certificate evidence} remain distinct: the
    certificate scalar and its pass/fail verdict select the accepted rung or
    the fallback and are therefore \tagclosure{}; interval boxes, residual
    reports, and pointwise comparisons are \tagverify{} evidence.

    \emph{Raw edge weights and parity} are terminal.
    Standing consumes complete projected acts, not raw
    $\dampedweight{e}$ or $\detsign{e}$.  A host-cached raw value is a
    by-product; a guild may independently recompute or replace the raw
    terminal traversal.

    \emph{By-products} remain the one tag defined by permission rather
    than obligation: nothing binding may depend on them.  If a guild
    elects to treat a by-product as authoritative inside its own
    terminal service, it owns that choice and must publish it.

    The word ``constant'' does not itself imply binding authority.  A
    constant used by the projected standing activation, W1/W2,
    formation, or recognition belongs to the closure.  A canonical
    raw-feed or raw-bridge default whose every read-site is terminal
    belongs to Layer~2; a host-published cached value of that default
    is a by-product.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[What Is Frozen During the Solve]
    \label{rem:network:within-epoch-solve-freeze}
    Two things are frozen while the equilibrium is solved, and they are frozen
    for different reasons.  The base allocation matrix is frozen because it is
    a reading of the completed epoch set and nothing in the solve may change
    it.  The emission diagonal is frozen because it reads only the epoch-final
    ledger, which is what lets the certificate transfer
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:emission-certificate-transfer}).

    Nothing else is.  There is no path schedule to freeze, because there are no
    selected paths: the transport apportions over the whole support at every
    hop, and the state moves continuously.  ``Frozen'' therefore never means
    inherited from the preceding epoch --- that would be a memory read
    (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-memorylessness}) --- and it never describes a
    choice the solver made.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Host Contract}
\label{subsec:network:host-contract}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The host operates the boundary and publishes the results. Its entire
authority is the contract below; everything else it computes is either owed
(closure, verification) or gifted (by-products).

\begin{postulate}[Host Contract]
    \label{post:network:host-contract}
    At each accepted epoch boundary~$k$, the host publishes one
    self-contained final-state package.

    \begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\roman*)]
        \item \textbf{accepted records:}
              the final write set~$\actsequence{k}$, final edge set~$E_k$, dependent-set
              partition, realized size, closure cause, and attested boundary
              timestamp;

        \item \textbf{final ledger:}
              the settled boundary burn state, final residual balances, final
              action counts, accepted-act increments
              $\actcountincrement{k}{i}$, and debit vintages;

        \item \textbf{semantic projection:}
              every accepted Actor-authored act, its fold cell and coefficient
              $\foldcoef{\foldcell}$, its recipient resolution, inviter
              revocation, and the base allocation matrix $\basescore{}{}$ the
              published domain weights determine from them;

        \item \textbf{allocation and transport:}
              the tilt profile shape, the accepted rung $\tiltstrength{k}$ with
              the certificate verdict of every rung attempted above it, the
              depth mass $\depthmass{m}$, the emission fractions
              $\emission{u}$, and the conserved transport
              $\transport{\standingeq}$;

        \item \textbf{final standing and admission:}
              the rate hull box $\hullbox{k}$, the standing certificate
              $\standingcert{k}$, the fixed-point enclosure, final standing,
              final action and epoch stamps, door headroom, and the W1/W2
              verdicts;

        \item \textbf{shared closure outputs and policy:}
              the title certificate $\titlecert{k}$, the settlement-recognition
              result, the epoch target size, the published minimum and maximum
              durations, and the policy-floor schedule ($\polfloor$ announced
              at boundary~$k$, effective at~$k{+}1$, valid iff
              $\polfloor \ge \safefloor$; \zcref{def:epoch:policy-floor}),
              safety-threshold schedule, and margin factor $\marginfactor\numrel{const.epoch.margin.exact}$,
              all under the no-silent-change discipline of
              \zcref{subsec:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas};

        \item \textbf{reproducibility evidence:}
              the public formula editions, declared constants, interval boxes,
              residual bounds, and reports sufficient for any participant to
              rerun the calculation.
    \end{enumerate}

    Every binding value is reproducible from the accepted records, final
    ledger, public formulas, and constants.  Reproducibility is an audit right,
    never an override right.  Previous standing, warm starts, cached path
    products, and local solver state are not package inputs: the host may use
    them to reduce work but may not use them to select a different result.  No
    hashes, roots, or source digests are normative.

    A finite implementation must publish a standing enclosure narrow enough to
    decide every binding threshold comparison.  If an enclosure straddles
    $\safefloor$ for an author or straddles $\partfloor$ for the epoch stamp,
    the proposed set is not yet certified: the calculation must be refined or
    the set rejected.  Rounding may not decide a gate whose exact value remains
    enclosed on both sides.

    A write set takes effect only when the completed final package satisfies
    \zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}; otherwise no member of that
    proposed set becomes a Layer-1 record.  Misbehavior at the boundary is
    evidence, not prevention (\zcref{post:graph:boundary-accountability}).
\end{postulate}

\begin{definition}[Door Headroom]
    \label{def:network:door-headroom}
    For the accepted nonempty authored-act sequence~$\actsequence{k}$,
    \[
        \doorheadroom{k}
        =
        \sum_i \actcountincrement{k}{i}
            \bigl(\epochrefstanding{k}{i}-\partfloor\bigr)
        =
        \sum_{q\in\actsequence{k}}\bigl(\actstamp{q}-\partfloor\bigr).
    \]
    Summing over acts, not edge projections, so a hyper-edge act counts its one
    stamp once. It is certificate-derived and \tagverify{}: the congestion
    diagnostic (band admission is headroom-limited), consumed by no admission
    formula. The final-set door itself is $\epochstamp{k}\ge\partfloor$; headroom
    merely reports the resulting surplus, and since an accepted $\actsequence{k}$
    satisfies W2b the published accepted-set headroom is nonnegative.  The tilt backoff has no
    read-site in $\doorheadroom{k}$, and headroom is never an actuator.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Durations Are Policy, Not Objects]
    \label{rem:network:durations-no-glyph}
    The epoch minimum and maximum durations are host wall-clock policy: not
    derivable from records, and absent from every formula. By the
    document's own discipline --- a quantity that closes gets a glyph; one
    that only governs gets a name --- they are prose-named and glyph-free.
    Their sole formal shadows are the certificate's closure-cause field and
    the attested timestamp, both \tagverify{}.
\end{remark}

\begin{insight}[Back-Pressure Is the Minimum Duration]
    \label{ins:network:back-pressure}
    The write rate of the network is capped at $\epochlen$ records per
    epoch minimum duration, and this single published bound is where the
    congestion economics comes from. While demand stays under it, every
    valid dependent set can be written and the door headroom remains visibly
    positive: the boundary is invisible. When demand exceeds the
    budget, the epoch fills before the clock permits closure and the host must
    choose among valid dependent sets --- the door and the averages decide
    what \emph{can} be written, discretion decides what \emph{is}, and the
    headroom records how much room the band had. Demand itself is invisible to
    Layer~1: only its shadow --- a binding regime and depleted headroom --- is
    written. The maximum
    duration is the opposite guarantee: an epoch that never fills still
    closes, so liveness is never hostage to demand. One systemic
    back-pressure (W1 remains the \emph{per-actor} throttle), two liveness
    bounds, one target --- the whole boundary in
    three published quantities.

    The conserved standing certificate is separate from this boundary packing
    problem.  Back-pressure acts before the write but is measured only on the
    accepted final set: the host may search among candidate dependent-set
    unions, but each proposed final set pays its own standing computation and
    clears its own W1/W2 verdict, and a rejected trial set leaves no Layer-1
    record and no published standing state.  The tilt backoff solves a
    different problem --- finding the loudest rung at which one proposed final
    set certifies --- and the host may not use a lowered rung as an unpriced
    substitute for record-selection policy.
\end{insight}

The normative machinery this chapter points at --- the final-set closure and
write rule, the safety threshold and its requirements, and the policy floor ---
lives with the epoch architecture
(\zcref{sec:epoch}) and the graph foundations (\zcref{sec:graph}), where its
proofs are. This chapter is the map; those are the territory.

\section{Graph Foundations}
\label{sec:graph}

Every edge in the graph stores two continuous parameters and a discrete
domain label.  From these, the master formula produces a $3 \times 3$
matrix.  From this matrix, three interfaces are extracted: a scalar norm,
a $2 \times 2$ bilinear block, and a full $3 \times 3$ norm.  The
$2 \times 2$ block admits a signed SVD decomposition that yields --- in
a single pass on any nonsingular $2 \times 2$ matrix --- the strength of
directional coherence, the orientation of the sentiment map, the
diversity of the interaction, and the dominant mode of engagement.  These
quantities are the complete information content of the path-view
interface.  Every formula in \zcref{sec:sorting,sec:transport} and
\zcref{app:can} consumes a named subset of them and nothing else; the
consumer map (\zcref{subsec:graph:consumer-map}) is the contract.

The section proceeds from partition and temporal structure to the
sentiment slice, rank-2 property and dual-view split, path-view
extraction and the signed SVD tool, per-edge determinant sign and tier
structure, temporal augmentation, path composition and scoring,
structural properties, diagnostics and archetypes, aggregation,
hyper-edges, interaction domains, and the consumer map.  Unless noted,
definitions describe the \ActionGraph{} reading; the \CompGraph{}
reading is defined in \zcref{app:can}.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Edge Ontology}
\label{subsec:graph:edge-ontology}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{axiom}[Authored Acts Are Records; Edges Are Projections]
    \label{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology}
    The graph's primitive append-only public history is the set of accepted
    \emph{authored acts}.  An accepted act~$q$ owns exactly:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[act fields] its act identifier~$\actid{q}$, author, family,
            semantic body~$\actbody{q}$ (carrying the type-fixed or authored
            parameters $(p_d,p_i)$, domain/mask, and family-specific
            structural metadata), public protocol references
            $\actprotocolrefs{q}$ (including any \texttt{settles} reference
            and license qualifiers) and asserted causal parents
            $\actparents{q}$, the removable payload projection~$\actpayload{q}$
            and dependency projection~$\actdeps{q}$, the commitments and
            signatures of its admission handshake, and its approval
            witness~$\approvewitness{q}$;
        \item[finalization metadata] the host-attached epoch and
            authoritative logical time~$\acttime{q}$, assigned when the
            approved act is placed into the authoritative order
            (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}); this is not an
            authored field.
    \end{description}
    Its \emph{graph projection}~$\actedges{q}$ contains exactly one binary
    edge or exactly two role-labelled hyper-edge projections
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection}).  The edge set is derived from the
    accepted act history,
    \[
        E_k \;=\; \bigcup_{j\le k}\ \bigcup_{q\in\actsequence{j}} \actedges{q},
    \]
    and an edge projection~$e\in\actedges{q}$ contains only its parent act
    reference~$\actof{e}$, projection role~$\edgerole{e}$, source identifier,
    target identifier, and the role-specific rendering of the act's semantic
    coordinates $(p_d,p_i)$.  No edge projection owns an independent payload,
    dependency list, causal-parent set, signature, action-count increment,
    safety-threshold debit, or logical time: the familiar edge accessors ---
    author, family, and logical time~$\acttime{\actof{e}}$ --- are read from
    the parent act.  Consequently:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[implicit existence] A node is an identifier occurring in
            the endpoint fields of projected edges.  $V$ is derived:
            $v \in V$ iff some projected edge references~$v$
            (\emph{referenced}; the anchoring refinement is
            \zcref{def:graph:anchoring}).  There is
            no node-creation operation, no node table, and no node
            attribute store.
        \item[folds only] Every ``node property'' in this specification
            --- sentiment, norm, maturity, affordances, connectivity,
            license, creator, ownership, membership --- is a declared
            fold over the projected edges referencing that identifier.  A
            property without a declared fold is undefined, and stating
            the fold is stating the property.
        \item[derived edges] Layer~1 appends no authored act.  Edges previous
            editions described as Layer-1-issued are \emph{derived
            edges}: deterministic recomputations from the epoch
            certificate (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}).  The accepted
            authored-act history is Actor-authored in its entirety; the edge
            set is its deterministic structural projection.
    \end{description}
\end{axiom}

\begin{remark}[Act-Ownership Invariant]
    \label{rem:graph:act-ownership-invariant}
    An accepted authored act~$q$ is the atomic public record.  It owns or
    carries the act identifier, author, family, semantic body, public protocol
    references, causal parents, payload projection~$\actpayload{q}$, dependency
    projection~$\actdeps{q}$, commitments, signatures, and approval
    witness~$\approvewitness{q}$; the host attaches the finalization epoch and
    authoritative logical time~$\acttime{q}$.  Its graph
    projection~$\actedges{q}$ contains one binary edge or two role-labelled
    hyper-edge projections.  An edge projection owns only its parent-act
    reference~$\actof{e}$, role~$\edgerole{e}$, source, target, and
    role-specific semantic rendering.  No edge projection may possess, omit,
    revise, or contradict an act-owned payload, dependency, causal reference,
    approval, debit, count increment, stamp, or logical time; materialized
    copies of inherited fields are caches and carry no independent authority.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Hyper-Act Indivisibility]
    \label{cor:graph:hyper-act-indivisibility}
    Under \zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology}, the A- and T-edge projections
    of a hyper-edge are not two records later joined into one act: they are two
    graph projections of one already-formed authored act.  They therefore share
    by construction --- not by an equality constraint imposed after the fact ---
    one act identifier, one author, one payload lifecycle, one dependency
    projection, one causal-parent set, one approval witness, one
    $\safethresh$-debit, one action-count increment, one final stamp, and one
    authoritative logical time~$\acttime{q}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Ontology Promotion]
    \label{rem:graph:ontology-promotion}
    \zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology} is the load-bearing generalization of
    three facts already held locally: Item identity is declarative
    (\zcref{def:graph:item-genesis-act}), payload state is invariant for all
    Layer~1 quantities (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}), and
    every derived quantity is a replay of records plus constants.  The
    axiom promotes the pattern to the ontology: the accepted authored act is
    the only thing that is authored; the edge set, and everything else, is a
    published way of reading it.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Identifier Algebra]
        \label{def:graph:identifier-algebra}
        Node identifiers form the inductive term algebra
        \[
                I \;::=\;
                \mathsf{addr}(a)
                \;\mid\; \mathsf{prof}(a)
                \;\mid\; \mathsf{name}(s)
                \;\mid\; \mathsf{mint}(\alpha),
        \]
        with $a \in \addrspace$
        (\attestationcref{def:interface:address-space}), $s \in \strset$,
        and $\alpha$ an authored-act identifier
        (\zcref{def:graph:act-identifier}).
        The \emph{class} of an identifier is its outermost constructor:
        \textbf{grounded} ($\mathsf{addr}$, $\mathsf{prof}$),
        \textbf{named} ($\mathsf{name}$), \textbf{minted} ($\mathsf{mint}$).
        Exactly two constructors take their atoms from outside the record
        set --- $\mathsf{addr}$ from the reserve economy, $\mathsf{name}$
        from the public string commons --- and each breaks one relabeling
        symmetry: $\mathsf{addr}$ anchors \emph{mass}
        (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}), $\mathsf{name}$ anchors
        \emph{reference} (tags from disjoint communities meet on one node).
        $\mathsf{prof}$ is the unique non-atomic grounded constructor: one
        atom, two identifiers --- an Actor and its Profile are one
        anchoring, not two (\zcref{def:graph:registration}).  A minted
        identifier names the genesis authored act that created the node
        (\zcref{def:graph:act-identifier}), never the node itself and never a
        host-assigned time; the author-local sequence inside the act
        identifier makes each term finite and non-self-referential, so
        ``a node cannot be re-minted'' is a property of term formation, not a
        rule.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Authored Act]
    \label{def:graph:authored-act}
    An \emph{authored act} $q$ is the atomic unit of formation, admission,
    ordering, dependency declaration, action counting, safety-threshold debit,
    and final-set authorship.  Its record projection is
    \[
        \actedges{q}=
        \begin{cases}
            \{e\}, & q\text{ binary},\\
            \{e_A,e_T\}, & q\text{ a hyper-edge act},
        \end{cases}
    \]
    a binary act carrying exactly one edge record and a hyper-edge act exactly
    two matched records (one A-leg, one T-leg); no other cardinality is valid.
    Every accepted authored act increments its author's action count by one and
    incurs exactly one debit $\theta^{(k)}$ --- a hyper-edge does not debit per
    leg --- and carries exactly one dependency projection belonging to the act
    as a whole, not to either leg.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Act Identifier and Minted-Node Identity]
    \label{def:graph:act-identifier}
    The Actor chooses a unique author-local sequence value $s_q$ fixed before
    submission.  The authored act's identifier is
    \[
        \actid{q}=
        \mathsf{act}\bigl(\operatorname{author}(q),\,s_q,\,
        \operatorname{family}(q)\bigr),
    \]
    which contains no host-assigned logical time and no minted target, so it
    exists before host salting, verification, ordering, and time assignment.
    Record identifiers project it by role,
    \[
        \edgeid{e}=\mathsf{record}\bigl(\actid{q},
        \mathrm{binary}\bigr),
        \qquad
        \edgeid{e_A}=\mathsf{record}\bigl(\actid{q},A\bigr),
        \quad
        \edgeid{e_T}=\mathsf{record}\bigl(\actid{q},T\bigr),
    \]
    and a node minted by a genesis authored act takes identity
    \[
        \operatorname{id}\bigl(\operatorname{mintedTarget}(q)\bigr)
        =\mathsf{mint}\bigl(\actid{q}\bigr).
    \]
    The minted node names its genesis \emph{act}, never itself: this removes the
    prior self-reference in which a genesis record's identity key contained the
    very target it minted.  A monotone author-local sequence makes accidental
    reuse directly detectable; a random nonce is valid if collision probability
    is negligible.  Registration is distinct --- it anchors an existing grounded
    Actor/Profile pair and mints no node --- yet still carries an act identifier
    because it is an admitted action.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Class Disjointness and Decidability]
        \label{lem:graph:identifier-disjointness}
        The four constructor images are pairwise disjoint, and the class of
        any identifier is decidable from its outermost constructor alone;
        no record content, fold, or census lookup is consulted.
        \proofsketch{Free term algebra: distinct constructors have disjoint
        images; classhood is syntactic.}
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Reference, Anchoring, Dangling]
        \label{def:graph:anchoring}
        Relative to an epoch edge set $E_k$: an identifier $v$ is
        \emph{referenced} ($v \in V_k$) per
        \zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology}; it is \emph{anchored} iff its
        class-specific anchor is present in $E_k$ ---
        $\mathsf{addr}(a)$/$\mathsf{prof}(a)$: the accepted Registration
        record of~$a$; $\mathsf{name}(s)$: vacuously (names are commons);
        $\mathsf{mint}(\cdot)$: the accepted genesis authored act bearing that
        act identifier.  A referenced, unanchored identifier is \emph{dangling}.
        Danglingness is representable by construction --- a record may cite
        any well-formed term --- and inert by the fold discipline:
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Dangling Identifiers Are Fold-Neutral]
        \label{lem:graph:dangling-neutral-fold}
        Every canonical fold (\zcref{def:graph:canonical-folds}) returns its
        neutral element on a dangling identifier:
        $\operatorname{creator} = \bot$ (unit amplifier),
        $\titlecert{k} = \void$, membership false, sentiment/norm the
        empty-record folds, Reputation bond inert.  No admission rule reads
        a dangling identifier's fold, so danglingness never binds.
        \proofsketch{Each fold is total over the possibly-empty record set
        referencing $v$; the anchor records are exactly what the
        non-neutral branches read.}
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Node Taxonomy and Identity]
    \label{def:graph:node-taxonomy}
    Every node identifier belongs to exactly one class:
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l l X X@{}}
        \toprule
                \textbf{Class} & \textbf{Types} & \textbf{Constructor}
                        & \textbf{Anchored when} \\
        \midrule
        Grounded
            & Actor, Profile
                        & $\mathsf{addr}(a)$ with $a = \operatorname{key}(i)$,
                            exogenous; $\mathsf{prof}(a)$ over the same atom
            & its Registration record is accepted
                            (\zcref{def:graph:registration}); identity pre-exists
                            anchoring \\
        \addlinespace
        Named
            & Type
                        & $\mathsf{name}(s)$, $s \in \strset$: an intrinsic public
                            name, never minted, owned by no one
                            (\zcref{rem:graph:name-equality})
                        & vacuously (commons) \\
        \addlinespace
        Minted
            & Content, Item, Chat, Offer, Comment, Message
                        & $\mintid{q}$ of its
                            genesis authored act~$q$
                            (\zcref{def:graph:act-identifier})
                        & its genesis act is accepted; identity and anchor
                            coincide \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabularx}
    \end{center}
    Minted identity generalizes Item's declarative identity to every
        created node: the node is minted from its genesis \emph{act} --- identity
        and anchor are one act, which is why re-minting is impossible and
        updating means authoring \emph{about} the node.  Grounded identity is
        the deliberate opposite: identity comes from the atom, anchoring from
        the Registration record, and the two never re-bind --- which is
        exactly what lets parallel Registrations update a Profile's payload
        chronicle without forking the node
        (\zcref{rem:graph:profile-update}).  Genesis is
    therefore structurally unique; a collision is author-equivocation,
    rejected by record integrity, never adjudicated.  Two actors
    registering ``the same'' chat, artwork, or item create two nodes;
    which referent is real is out-of-band by the gauge argument, exactly
    as already stated for Items.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Name Equality Is Byte Equality]
    \label{rem:graph:name-equality}
    Layer~1 compares $\mathsf{name}(s)$ identifiers by exact byte
    equality on~$s$: no case folding, Unicode normalization, or
    similarity metric.  Two spellings are two Type nodes, exactly as two
    listings are two Items (\zcref{def:graph:item-genesis-act}); whether they
    denote one concept is out-of-band by the gauge argument, and any
    display-level normalization is a terminal Layer-2 rendering choice
    (\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}).  $\strset$ is the same universe
    as the registry $\symbf{\Lambda}$'s domain
    (\zcref{def:can:compositional-attribution-network}); the two uses
    share the alphabet and nothing else.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Genesis Act and Creator]
    \label{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}
    The \emph{genesis act} of a minted node is the authored act whose act
    identifier it mints (\zcref{def:graph:act-identifier}); the node's genesis
    record is that act's edge projection.

    \textbf{Minting is a role a record plays, not a property of its family.}
    Write $\terminaltarget{q}$ for an act's \emph{terminal target}: the target
    of a binary act, and the T-leg's terminus for a hyper-edge act.  Then for
    every act~$q$ of a genesis family,
    \[
        \operatorname{role}(q) =
        \begin{cases}
            \text{genesis}, & \terminaltarget{q}=\mathsf{mint}(\actid{q}),\\
            \text{ordinary}, & \text{otherwise},
        \end{cases}
    \]
    decidable from two fields of the one act, by syntactic term equality and
    no lookup.  A genesis act mints; an ordinary act of the same family mints
    nothing and names a node that already exists.

    The identifier algebra already said this: $\mathsf{mint}$ takes an
    \emph{act} identifier, so a family-level reading would require
    $\mathsf{mint}(\actid{q})$ to be derivable from the family alone.  Chat
    demonstrates it --- the founding Participant mints and every later one
    does not, one family and two roles --- and nothing distinguishes Chat here
    but that its second case was already needed.

    That a node cannot be re-minted needs no rule: $\mathsf{mint}$ is
    injective, distinct acts carry distinct identifiers
    (\zcref{lem:graph:act-edge-identifier-uniqueness}), and an ordinary act's
    terminal target is not derived from its own identifier.

    The genesis families are:
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Node} & \textbf{Genesis family} & \textbf{Status} \\
        \midrule
        Item & Owner (Actor$\to$Item) & existing \\
        Offer & Bid/T (Item$\to$Offer) & existing \\
        Comment & Review/T (Passive$\to$Comment) & existing \\
        Message & Send/T (Chat$\to$Message) & existing \\
        Chat & Participant (Actor$\to$Chat), the founding member's & existing family, newly designated genesis \\
        Content & Publish (Actor$\to$Content) & new census row \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{center}
    Publish is an Economic-style single-parameter edge with attachment
    $a \in [-1,1]$, $p_d=a$, $p_i=1$, promoted full mask, and the \tierfull{} tier,
    mirroring Owner.  The creator map is uniform:
    \[
        \operatorname{creator}(n) :=
        \begin{cases}
            \operatorname{author}(\operatorname{genesis}(n)),
                & n = \mathsf{mint}(\cdot),\\
            n, & n = \mathsf{addr}(a),\\
            \mathsf{addr}(a), & n = \mathsf{prof}(a),\\
            \bot, & n = \mathsf{name}(s),
        \end{cases}
    \]
    with the convention $\standing{\bot}:=0$, so a Type reached as a
    feed terminus takes the neutral amplifier $\ampfactor{\bot}=1$.
    No one owns a concept; named nodes are commons by construction.
    \textbf{[Closes N-01:} $\operatorname{creator}(c)$ is defined for
    every node type; the feed is reproducible.\textbf{]}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Registration]
    \label{def:graph:registration}
    The \emph{Registration record} is an actor-authored edge
    Actor$\to$Profile and the \emph{anchoring record} of the grounded
    pair $(\mathsf{addr}(a), \mathsf{prof}(a))$
    (\zcref{def:graph:anchoring}).  It is the sole record family whose
    endpoints may be fresh grounded identifiers --- fresh because
    grounded identity pre-exists the graph
    (\zcref{def:graph:identifier-algebra}); nothing is minted and no
    identity key is formed.  It anchors; it does not create.
    Under final-set admission, Registration is one ordinary act: it
    contributes one accepted-act increment, incurs one
    $\safethresh$-debit, consumes epoch write capacity, and is evaluated
    by the same completed-state W1, W2a, and W2b conditions as every other
    proposed act
    (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule,%
    rem:epoch:registration-final-set-admission}).  The canonical payload
    is profile data; the Profile husk is structural.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Derived Raw Edges]
    \label{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}
    A \emph{derived raw edge} is a deterministic terminal graph reading
    computed from an accepted epoch package and never appended to~$E$.

    The raw Self-edge is the sole derived raw-edge family.  For Actor~$i$
    at accepted epoch~$k$, its Declaration and Reputation components share
    the final standing coordinate
    \[
        p_i^{(k)}
        =
        \frac{\epochrefstanding{k}{i}}{1+\epochrefstanding{k}{i}}.
    \]
    Their tensors, determinant scores, parity, and raw damped weights are
    derived under the ordinary raw graph formulas.  The raw Self-edge is not an
    authored act and carries no authored-act time; the epoch package places its
    derived reading at the boundary slot $\boundaryslot{k}$ --- boundary-relative
    ordering metadata that follows every act accepted into~$E_k$ and precedes
    acts accepted at later boundaries, not an authored-act logical time --- and
    its maturity follows the published tenure schedule
    $\tau_i^{(k)} = 1 - 1/(k-k_i^{\mathrm{reg}}+1)$.

    The raw Self-edge is computed after final standing.  It is available
    to feed, raw bridge, and declared CAN consumers and is not an input to
    any standing stage.  Every record in~$E$ is Actor-authored, and the
    admission set governs all records while derived raw edges are
    recomputation.  Derived raw edges carry no payload projection, consume
    no action count, incur no $\safethresh$-debit, and are absent from the
    append-only record set.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Raw Traversal Snapshot]
    \label{def:graph:raw-traversal-snapshot}
    The accepted projected edge set at boundary~$k$ is~$E_k$.  Let
    $\derivedrawset{k}$ be the deterministic set containing the current
    derived Declaration and Reputation readings of every anchored Actor.
    The epoch-$k$ raw traversal graph is
    \[
        \rawgraph{k}
        \coloneqq
        \bigl(
            V_k,
            E_k\cup\derivedrawset{k}
        \bigr).
    \]

    The derived readings in $\derivedrawset{k}$:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item are not authored acts;
        \item are not members of~$E_k$;
        \item carry no payload, dependency, approval, debit, count
              increment, or act time;
        \item are recomputed from the current accepted epoch package;
        \item replace earlier derived readings in the current raw snapshot
              rather than accumulating as historical edges.
    \end{enumerate}

    Feed ranking, raw signed traversal, and canonical bridge traversal
    consume $\rawgraph{k}$.  Standing consumes the base allocation matrix
    $\basescore{}{}$ and never traverses $\derivedrawset{k}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Derived Self-Edge Reading]
    \label{def:graph:derived-self-reading}
    For anchored Actor~$i$ at accepted boundary~$k$, define the raw
    Self-edge coordinate
    \[
        p_i^{(k)}
        =
        \frac{
            \epochrefstanding{k}{i}
        }{
            1+\epochrefstanding{k}{i}
        }.
    \]
    The current derived Declaration and Reputation readings use this
    shared coordinate and the shared tenure maturity
    \[
        \tau_{i,\mathrm{Self}}^{(k)}
        =
        1-
        \frac{
            1
        }{
            k-k_i^{\mathrm{reg}}+1
        }.
    \]
    Thus
    \[
        \tau_{i,\mathrm{Dec}}^{(k)}
        =
        \tau_{i,\mathrm{Rep}}^{(k)}
        =
        \tau_{i,\mathrm{Self}}^{(k)}.
    \]

    Neither component matures the other.  Both are current raw traversal
    readings, not accepted acts and not standing relations.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Raw Snapshot Path]
    \label{def:graph:raw-snapshot-path}
    A raw snapshot path is a directed simple path in $\rawgraph{k}$.  Its
    depth is the number of raw edge projections or current derived raw
    readings it traverses.

    The canonical raw services admit paths of length at most~$L$.  Raw
    path viability does not require edge times to increase: raw feed and
    bridge services measure connectivity in the current public snapshot,
    not a chronological event chain.

    The host-published act order remains binding for act acceptance,
    edge-projection maturity, bundle folds, title, standing, and current
    derived Self-edge parameters.  It is not a path constraint on terminal
    snapshot traversal.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Raw Edge-Weight Ceiling]
    \label{thm:graph:raw-weight-ceiling}
    For every raw edge projection or current derived raw reading admitted
    by the canonical family census, every legal semantic parameter tuple,
    every routing tier, and every raw graph maturity $\tau\in[0,1)$:
    \[
        0
        \le
        \dampedweight{e}
        \le
        \wmax
        <1.
    \]
    Equality at zero holds exactly for routing-inert zero-determinant
    edges.  The strict upper bound implies positive additive log costs,
    bounded max-product registers, and the existence of a simple
    representative for every optimal bounded raw walk.
    \proofsketch{The raw damped weight is the product of a bounded
    determinant score and bounded maturity/entropy factors and vanishes
    exactly when the edge determinant vanishes
    (\zcref{prop:nodes:raw-self-edge-properties}).  Its supremum across
    every admitted family, tier, and maturity is the verified raw
    Reputation ceiling $\wmax \numrel{bound.raw.wmax.num} < 1$
    (\zcref{tbl:verification:bounds-summary}).  Because $\wmax<1$, the
    additive log cost $-\log\dampedweight{e}$ is strictly positive on every
    routing-live edge, so a repeated-node cycle strictly increases total
    log cost and cannot improve a bounded max-product; an optimal bounded
    raw walk therefore has a simple representative.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Canonical Node Folds]
    \label{def:graph:canonical-folds}
    The folds defining node-level quantities are:
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l X X@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Property} & \textbf{Fold} & \textbf{Consumer} \\
        \midrule
        Sentiment slice $\symbf{\Psi}_c$
            & arithmetic means $\bar p_d,\bar p_i$ of role parameters
              over user-authored incoming stance records; control
              families and structural genesis metadata excluded; full
              mask rendering
            & content norm \\
        Node maturity $\bar\tau_c$
            & mean $\tau_e$ over the same record set
            & content norm \\
        Content norm
            & $\|\symbf{\Psi}(\bar p_d,\bar p_i)\|_F\cdot
              \sqrt{1+\bar\tau_c^2}$
            & relevance terminus; terminal, canonical default \\
        Creator
            & \zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}
            & feed amplifier, reward \\
        Ownership
            & title fold, epoch-quantized per D1/D2
            & recognition; binding \\
        Membership
            & canonical membership fold
              (\zcref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold})
            & terminal \\
        Affordances / connectivity
            & properties of the node's class, taxonomy, and genesis
              family; \zcref{sec:nodes}'s connectivity blocks
              document the fold
            & --- \\
        License
            & structural metadata of the genesis record; immutable,
              survives payload removal, read only by Layer~2 policy
            & terminal \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabularx}
    \end{center}
    \textbf{[Closes N-04:} the undefined $w_{uc},r_{uc}$ become the
    declared parameter means; cross-domain mixing is resolved by the
    stance-record restriction and full-mask rendering; the missing
    temporal factor is $\bar\tau_c$; and because the content norm is
    terminal, the fold is a canonical default rather than a binding
    commitment.\textbf{]}  \textbf{[Closes D3 licensing relocation:}
    license was always edge-shaped --- set at creation, immutable, and
    Layer-1-blind; it now lives where its behavior said it lived.\textbf{]}

    \emph{Structural genesis metadata means genesis} \textbf{fields}\emph{,
    not genesis records.}  The exclusion removes the minting act's structural
    body --- the fields that fix identity, creator and license --- from the
    stance means.  It does not remove the record.  A genesis Publish folds
    into $\bar p_d,\bar p_i$ like any other Publish, because its author's
    stance toward the thing they published is a stance like any other; what
    is excluded is the part of that record which is machinery rather than
    opinion.

    Reading it the other way is available and wrong, and now costs
    something: with the genesis role a property of the record
    (\zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}), a record-level exclusion
    would make the first act about a node invisible to the fold while every
    later act about it counts --- the same gesture weighed or not by whether
    the author happened to be first.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Act and Edge-Projection Identifier Uniqueness]
    \label{lem:graph:act-edge-identifier-uniqueness}
    Distinct accepted acts never share an act identifier, and distinct
    edge projections never share an edge-projection identifier.
    \proofsketch{An author's records chain through the author endpoint,
    so each strictly increments the author's local clock and equal
    $(\acttime{},\operatorname{author})$ pairs cannot occur across
    distinct honest records; the chain is grounded at the author's
    Registration record (\zcref{def:graph:registration}).  A forged
    equal-key pair is author-equivocation, rejected by record integrity
    independently of this lemma.  The chain property holds for any
    same-author record set, not merely per-family bundles.}
    \textbf{[Closes F-01.]}
\end{lemma}

\begin{axiom}[Universal Authored-Act Parallelism]
    \label{ax:graph:parallel-authored-acts}
    For every edge family, an author may append an authored act parallel to
    their own prior act --- same author, same source, same target,
    same family --- without restriction beyond the universal gates.  The
    append layer:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\roman*)]
        \item never rejects an act for being parallel to an existing
              one;
        \item never merges, supersedes, or tombstones; every parallel
              act is a first-class member of the accepted history, and its
              edge projections are permanent members of~$E$;
        \item assigns no Layer~1 semantics to the parallel relationship
              itself.  What a later parallel act means for an earlier
              one is a property of a declared fold over the authored-act
              bundle, with exactly the two Layer~1 consumers named in
              \zcref{rem:graph:authored-act-bundle-consumers}.
    \end{enumerate}
    Equivalently: Layer~1 stores chronicles, never state.  ``Current
    profile,'' ``current stance,'' and ``current membership'' are all
    readings; the accepted history contains only the acts.
\end{axiom}

\begin{definition}[Authored-Act Bundle]
    \label{def:graph:authored-act-bundle}
    The \emph{authored-act bundle} $\actbundle{j,s,t,f}$ is the set of
    accepted acts with author~$j$, source~$s$, target~$t$, and family~$f$.
    Its edge projections $\bigcup_{q\in\actbundle{j,s,t,f}}\actedges{q}$
    populate~$E$; for a hyper-edge act each projection carries its own role
    (A or T) and full incidence, including the terminal target.  A bundle
    groups acts by their public act identities
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection}); it never regroups bare edge
    projections into acts.

    A raw consumer may fold the projected edges of a bundle where its own
    specification permits.  An act consumer may not construct an act by
    pairing independently folded projections, by substituting an unrelated
    incoming edge for an A-projection, or by selecting a T-projection whose
    parent act it cannot resolve.  Acts are regrouped only through their
    public act identities.

    Since an author's acts chain through the author endpoint, every
    authored-act bundle is a strict $\prec$-chain
    (\zcref{lem:graph:act-edge-identifier-uniqueness}), so the $\prec$-latest member is
    well-defined without any linearization.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Authored-Act Edge Projection]
    \label{def:graph:act-edge-projection}
    The \emph{edge projection} $\actedges{q}$ of an accepted authored
    act~$q$ is deterministic and fixed at formation.  It is not an appended
    record of its own: the act is the primitive record, and its projection
    is a way of reading it into the graph~$G$.

    A binary act projects to exactly one binary edge; a hyper-edge act
    projects to exactly one A-role edge and one T-role edge of the same
    family and initiating author:
    \[
        \abs{\actedges{q}}
        =
        \begin{cases}
            1, & q\text{ binary},\\
            2, & q\text{ hyper-edge},
        \end{cases}
        \qquad
        \actedges{q}=\set{e_A(q),e_T(q)}\ \text{when hyper-edge},
    \]
    with edge-projection identifiers derived from the act identifier and
    role,
    \[
        \edgeid{e_A(q)}=\mathsf{edge}(\actid{q},A),
        \qquad
        \edgeid{e_T(q)}=\mathsf{edge}(\actid{q},T).
    \]
    A hyper-edge projection is \emph{formation-valid} iff it contains
    exactly one A-role and one T-role edge, with agreeing author and family
    and with full incidence and family parameter tuple consistent under the
    family specification.  The two projections are siblings because they
    share one parent act, $\actof{e_A}=\actof{e_T}=q$ --- not because they
    carry reciprocal co-leg fields.  A valid accepted hyper-edge therefore
    can never have an accepted unmatched leg: a missing projection is a
    malformed or incompletely retrieved act, not a partially accepted graph
    state.

    The \emph{semantic target} of a binary act is the binary edge's
    target.  The semantic target of a hyper-edge act is its T-projection
    target; the middle passive artifact supplies context and is not the
    semantic target.  The family's parameter tuple belongs to the act:
    leg-role swaps are renderings of that tuple, not independent
    standing coordinates.

    Each projection inherits the act's authoritative logical time,
    $\acttime{\actof{e}}=\acttime{q}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}); in particular both
    projections of a hyper-edge share the one act
    time~$\acttime{e_A(q)}=\acttime{e_T(q)}=\acttime{q}$, not two equal
    edge-owned clocks.  A consumer requiring an ordered sequence of acts
    uses strictly increasing act times.

    Payload bytes, payload state, and the co-removed private value enter
    none of the act identity, author, semantic target, parameter tuple,
    or act-time fields.  Edge-projection identity is therefore
    invariant under payload reduction
    (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Binding Consumers of Authored-Act Bundles]
    \label{rem:graph:authored-act-bundle-consumers}
    Layer~1 reads authored-act bundles in exactly two places, and nowhere else:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{(standing)}] the \emph{standing projection}
            consumes each eligible bundle through sum-then-clip netting
            (\zcref{def:epoch:net-stance}), the Vouch Predicate
            (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}), and inviter-revocation
            suppression (\zcref{def:epoch:inviter-revocation}) --- one
            composite reading, feeding $\standing{}$ and hence the gate;
        \item[\textnormal{(title)}] settlement recognition consumes the
            settlement families through the epoch-quantized ordering of
            \zcref{post:graph:title-act-bundle-reservation}.
    \end{description}
    Both are binding for the standard reason: two readers disagreeing on
    either fork the gate or the title thread.  \textbf{Every other reading
    of a parallel bundle is Layer-2-free}: current-profile (latest),
    membership (\zcref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold}), chronicles,
    display amendment vs.\ accumulation, decay --- all terminal, all
    guild-replaceable under \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}.  The
    v0.18.x netting exclusion list becomes a corollary: settlement
    families are consumed by the title reading, control families by the
    projection's suppression rules and by no stance sum, derived edges
    are not records and have no bundle.
\end{remark}

\begin{postulate}[Title Reservation over Authored-Act Bundles]
    \label{post:graph:title-act-bundle-reservation}
    Title is the sole binding consumer of parallel semantics outside the
    standing projection, because it is the sole quantity where two
    readers disagreeing on the fold fork the shared graph: recognition
    reads title back into validity.  Within the settlement families
    (Bid/Accept/Ratify/Withdraw/Rescind on one Offer thread), the
    epoch-quantized latest fold governs: a cancel co-epochal-or-earlier
    defeats a commit (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}, clauses
    (iv)--(v)); conflicting co-epochal commits mutually consume
    (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold,def:graph:settlement-consumption}).

    Genesis is parallelism-exempt by construction, not by rule.  A
    parallel genesis is a record with the same identity key, which is
    author-equivocation (\zcref{lem:graph:act-edge-identifier-uniqueness}); it is rejected
    by record integrity, never folded.  A node cannot be re-minted; one
    can only author new records about it.
\end{postulate}

\begin{remark}[Profile Update]
    \label{rem:graph:profile-update}
    An actor updating their profile is a parallel Registration record:
    same author, source, target, and family.  The new record carries the
    new payload; the Layer~2 latest fold reads the current profile; the
    chronicle retains the history; payload removal applies per-record as
    always; and each update is a priced act.  Parallel Registrations
    re-bind nothing: Actor/Profile identifiers are grounded
    (\zcref{def:graph:node-taxonomy}), so the bundle updates the payload,
    never the identity or the key-binding.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[What Stays Deliberately Undefined]
    \label{rem:graph:parallel-undefined}
    For every bundle reading other than the two consumers of
    \zcref{rem:graph:authored-act-bundle-consumers}, Layer~1 takes no position,
    including whether parallel Opinions display as amended or
    accumulated, whether a chronicle's shape is itself a signal, and
    whether old parallel records decay.  These are exactly the readings
    assigned to guilds at terminal read-sites.  Any future binding
    consumer of parallel semantics would require amending the named
    two-consumer rule.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[A Grounded Target Does Not Imply a Vouch]
    \label{rem:graph:grounded-target-does-not-imply-allocation}
    Grounded target class is syntactic information, not standing
    authority.  A record targeting an Actor or Profile does not become a
    person-vouch merely because its target's outermost constructor is
    $\mathsf{addr}$ or $\mathsf{prof}$
    (\zcref{lem:graph:identifier-disjointness}).

    Standing authority is conferred only by the closed person-vouch
    census and complete-act rules of \zcref{sec:nodes,sec:epoch}.  A
    structural anchoring record, a control record, a non-designated
    commentary family, or any future grounded-target family contributes
    no standing unless that census explicitly designates the complete
    act.

    The class test remains useful: once a designated complete act has
    been admitted by the census, grounded target syntax identifies its
    person-directed semantic target without a node-table lookup.  Target
    class is therefore a necessary typing input where the census says so,
    never a sufficient vouch predicate.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Right-to-Leave, Completed]
    \label{rem:graph:right-to-leave-completed}
    Under \zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology}, erasure is uniform: all content
    anyone supplied lives in payload projections, removable including
    genesis payloads such as profile data, content bytes, and item
    descriptions; all structure anyone relied on lives in structural
    fields, the immutable husk.  The boundary between what the network
    returns and what it keeps is now a field boundary in one record
    format, not a case analysis over node types.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Partition and Passivity}
\label{subsec:graph:partition-and-passivity}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Graph Partition]
    \label{def:graph:partition}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:directed-edges}%
    The network is a directed graph $G = (V, E)$ over the primitive
    record set $E$ (\zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology}); $V$ is the derived
    identifier set, partitioned $V = V_u \sqcup V_c$, where $V_u$ are
    \textbf{active} nodes
    (Actors) and $V_c$ are \textbf{passive} nodes (artifacts).
    Every record is authored by an active node.  Passive-sourced
    user-authored edges occur only as terminal legs of hyper-edges whose
    initiating actor is recorded; the Profile-to-Actor Reputation
    component of the Self-edge bond is a derived traversal edge, not a
    record.
\end{definition}

\begin{axiom}[Passive Authorship Control]
    \label{ax:graph:passivity}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:passivity}%
    In the \ActionGraph{}:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\roman*)]
        \item \textbf{Authorship.} Every edge $e = (u,v) \in E$ is
              authored by an active node.  Exactly one of the following holds:
              (a)~$u \in V_u$, authored by its source actor; (b)~$e$ is sourced
              from a passive node $c \in V_c$ and is the terminal leg
              of a hyper-edge authored by some $a \in V_u$
              (the T-legs: Tag/T, Review/T, Bid/T, Send/T,
              Invitation/T, De-invite/T, Reference/T, Participant/T).
              There is no case~(c): the Reputation
              component is a \emph{derived edge}
              (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}), not a record; every
              record is actor-authored.
        \item \textbf{Non-autonomy.} No passive node initiates,
              redirects, or modifies any edge.  Every outgoing edge
              from a node $c \in V_c$ is determined at creation by the
              authoring actor and is thereafter immutable
              (\zcref{subsec:deployment:immutability}).
    \end{enumerate}
\end{axiom}

Passive nodes do emit edges --- every Taggable, Reviewable, Ownable, or
Conversational node sources the terminal leg of each hyper-edge in which
it serves as the middle node --- but never autonomously: each such edge
is authored by an active node and fixed at creation.  The Reputation
component is the sole derived passive-sourced edge; its target is fixed
by derivation and independently verifiable by comparing the edge
target against the registered Actor ownership record
(\zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}).  The feed-ranking BFS
and the raw signed double-cover service process raw edges uniformly;
their output filters select content nodes (feed ranking) or
actor-valued targets (raw signed queries), not an edge-type restriction
at the passive layer.  Standing does not rely on such output filtering:
it consumes only complete person-vouch acts, so passive incidence never
enters a projected standing path
(\zcref{cor:graph:standing-act-atomicity}).  The directed 2-cycle
$\mathrm{Actor}_j \to \mathrm{Profile}_j \to \mathrm{Actor}_j$ is
computationally neutral (\zcref{prop:nodes:self-loop-neutral}).

\begin{lemma}[Passive Out-Degree Structure]
    \label{lem:graph:passive-out-degree}
    For each passive node $c \in V_c$,
    $\deg^{\mathrm{out}}(c) = R(c) + H(c)$, where $R(c) \in \set{0,1}$
    equals $1$ iff $c$ is a Profile node (the derived Reputation
    component, counted here as a traversal edge though it is not a
    record; \zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}) and
    $H(c)$ counts the hyper-edge terminal legs sourced at $c$.  By node
    type:
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Type} & $\deg^{\mathrm{out}}$ \\
        \midrule
        Offer   & $|\text{Review}| + |\text{Reference}|$ \\
        Profile & $1 + |\text{Tag}| + |\text{Review}| + |\text{Reference}|$ \\
        Content & $|\text{Tag}| + |\text{Review}| + |\text{Reference}|$ \\
        Item    & $|\text{Tag}| + |\text{Review}| + |\text{Bid}| + |\text{Reference}|$ \\
        Type    & $|\text{Tag}| + |\text{Review}| + |\text{Reference}|$ \\
        Chat    & $|\text{Tag}| + |\text{Review}| + |\text{Send}| + |\text{Invitation}| + |\text{De-invite}| + |\text{Reference}| + |\text{Participant}|$ \\
        Comment & $|\text{Tag}| + |\text{Review}| + |\text{Reference}|$ \\
        Message & $|\text{Tag}| + |\text{Review}| + |\text{Reference}|$ \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{center}
    where $|\cdot|$ counts the hyper-edge instances in which $c$ is the
    middle node.  These terminal (T-)legs satisfy the authorship invariant
    (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity}, clause~(i)).  Every passive out-edge is a
    hyper-edge terminal leg or the Profile Reputation component; none is
    autonomously originated.
    \proofsketch{Each affordance trait
    (\zcref{tbl:nodes:affordance-traits}) that $c$ implements admits one
    hyper-edge family in which $c$ is the middle node and sources the
    terminal leg; summing over instances gives $H(c)$.  Offer implements
    Reviewable only.  Reference/A may source from any passive node (universal
    citing artifact), contributing $|\text{Reference}|$ author-fixed
    Reference/T terminal legs to every type; each satisfies clause~(i).}
\end{lemma}

\begin{remark}[Asymmetry]
    \label{rem:graph:asymmetry}
    Edges between actors may be asymmetric: $e_{uv}$ does not imply
    $e_{vu}$, and each edge carries independent sentiment parameters
    set unilaterally by its originating actor.
\end{remark}
