% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Temporal Structure}
\label{subsec:graph:temporal-structure}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{axiom}[Authored-Act Causality]
    \label{ax:graph:act-causality}
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:immutability}%
    Authoritative logical time is finalization metadata attached to the
    accepted authored act, not an edge-owned attribute.  Each accepted act is
    one Lamport event whose causal incidence is determined by the complete graph
    projection of the act (\zcref{def:graph:act-incidence-causality}), and the
    host publishes one authoritative sequence that totalizes acts of equal
    Lamport height (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}), subject to every
    causal parent and declared dependency being placed earlier.  Each edge
    projection inherits its parent act's time, $\acttime{\actof{e}}$.
\end{axiom}

\begin{definition}[Two-Way and Three-Way Act Causality]
    \label{def:graph:act-incidence-causality}
    Every accepted authored act is one Lamport event.  Its causal incidence is
    determined by the complete graph projection of the act, not by either edge
    projection in isolation.

    For a binary act~$q$, the incidence set is
    $\operatorname{Inc}(q)=\set{\operatorname{src}(q),\operatorname{tgt}(q)}$; the
    act is a two-way Lamport event over its source and target endpoints.  For a
    hyper-edge act~$q$, the incidence set is
    \[
        \operatorname{Inc}(q)
        =
        \set{
            \operatorname{author}(q),
            \operatorname{middle}(q),
            \operatorname{semanticTarget}(q)
        };
    \]
    the act is a three-way Lamport event over its initiating Actor, contextual
    middle node, and semantic target.  The middle passive node participates in
    causal incidence only; the update confers neither authorship, autonomy,
    standing authority, nor a right to originate another edge.

    Let $\actsequence{k}=(q_{k,1},\ldots,q_{k,m_k})$ be the host-published
    authoritative act sequence, let $L_{j-1}(v)$ be endpoint~$v$'s Lamport
    frontier immediately before act~$q_{k,j}$, and let $\operatorname{Pred}(q)$
    be the union of $q$'s public causal parents
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-causal-parents}) and Actor-declared dependencies
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection}).  The act's Lamport time is
    \[
        \acttime{q_{k,j}}
        =
        1+
        \max\!\left(
            \max_{v\in\operatorname{Inc}(q_{k,j})}L_{j-1}(v),
            \max_{p\in\operatorname{Pred}(q_{k,j})}\acttime{p}
        \right),
    \]
    and every incident endpoint then advances to the act frontier:
    \[
        L_j(v)
        =
        \begin{cases}
            \acttime{q_{k,j}}, & v\in\operatorname{Inc}(q_{k,j}),\\
            L_{j-1}(v),        & v\notin\operatorname{Inc}(q_{k,j}).
        \end{cases}
    \]
    The two edge projections of a hyper-edge inherit the one event frontier of
    their parent act,
    $\acttime{\actof{e_A}}=\acttime{\actof{e_T}}=\acttime{q}$: they are two graph
    projections of one three-way event, never two independently timed records.

    The host's authoritative position totalizes acts whose Lamport frontiers are
    equal.  The authoritative causal key is the lexicographic pair
    \[
        \actfrontier{k}{q}
        \coloneqq
        \bigl(
            \acttime{q},
            \actposition{k}{q}
        \bigr),
    \]
    which preserves ordinary Lamport causality while retaining the host's
    semantically authoritative ordering of concurrent acts.  An implementation
    may fold the host position into a strictly increasing scalar clock; the
    normative object is the pair.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[A Frontier Is Not an Ancestry Proof]
    \label{rem:graph:causal-frontier-not-ancestry}
    A lower Lamport time is necessary but not sufficient for causal ancestry.
    Public causal parents, Actor-declared dependencies, shared endpoint
    incidence, and the host-published authoritative sequence remain the sources
    of the ordering relation.  The scalar frontier summarizes replay; it does not
    create a causal parent that no accepted act declared or inherited by
    incidence.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Edge-Projection Maturity]
    \label{def:graph:edge-projection-maturity}
    Let $e\in\actedges{q}$ be one edge projection of accepted act~$q$.  Its raw
    graph maturity is
    \[
        \tau_e
        =
        1-
        \frac{1}{
            1+
            \max\!\left(
                \deg^{\mathrm{pre}}_q(\operatorname{src}(e)),
                \deg^{\mathrm{pre}}_q(\operatorname{tgt}(e))
            \right)
        },
    \]
    where $\deg^{\mathrm{pre}}_q(v)$ is the endpoint-incidence degree of~$v$ in
    the accepted projected graph immediately before the parent act~$q$ in the
    authoritative replay (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}).

    The two projections of one hyper-edge see the same pre-act graph state and do
    not mature one another.  Public causal parents and Actor-declared
    dependencies constrain the act order but add no endpoint incidence and
    therefore do not increase~$\tau_e$.  Maturity is edge-projection-owned; the
    act time $\acttime{\actof{e}}$ it inherits is not, and the optional audit
    position $\logpos{e}$ (\zcref{def:epoch:log-position}) enters no Layer~0 graph
    quantity.  This label covers accepted authored-act projections only; derived
    Self-edge maturity is defined separately with the derived raw snapshot.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Authoritative Act Order]
    \label{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}
    For epoch $k$ the host chooses a finite total order
    $\actsequence{k}=(q_{k,1},\ldots,q_{k,m_k})$ of the accepted authored acts and
    publishes each act's authoritative position
    $\actposition{k}{q_{k,j}}=j$.  Together with the Lamport time of
    \zcref{def:graph:act-incidence-causality}, this fixes the authoritative causal
    key $\actfrontier{k}{q}=(\acttime{q},\actposition{k}{q})$, ordered
    lexicographically.  The order is \emph{total} and \emph{semantically
    authoritative}: it is not forced by endpoint incidence, but it must linearize
    the causal-parent relation $\causalparent$ and every declared dependency
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-causal-parents,def:graph:act-dependency-projection}) ---
    each such prior act at strictly lower authoritative key --- while placing
    the two edge projections of one hyper-edge act ($\actof{e_A}=\actof{e_T}$,
    \zcref{def:graph:dependent-act-set}) at the same key.  Write $e \prec e'$ for
    precedence in this order
    ($\actfrontier{k}{\actof{e}}<\actfrontier{k}{\actof{e'}}$); where
    this document writes $\prec$ or $\prec_{\mathrm{inc}}$ in scoring, maturity, or
    path viability it means authoritative-order precedence, with the internal
    $A\to T$ transition of one act permitted at equal key.  Acts the host may
    place in either order (no dependency between them) are its residual
    discretion; the resulting quantities depend on the chosen order, so
    participants must agree on $\actsequence{k}$, not merely on the edge set $E_k$
    (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}).  The order's compliance with
    the declared dependencies is $\depok{k}{q}$: every dependency of $q$ lies in
    the finalized history at strictly lower authoritative key.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Host Ordering Discretion]
    \label{rem:graph:host-ordering-discretion}
    For acts not ordered by a public causal-parent relation or an
    Actor-declared dependency, Layer~1 imposes no arrival-order, fairness,
    neutrality, or canonical-identifier preference. The host may select any
    dependency-compliant authoritative order according to its own incentives.

    Different valid host choices may produce different authoritative causal
    keys, edge-projection maturities, folded relation frontiers, causal
    standing paths, standing fields, and final-set admission outcomes. This
    is authorized boundary discretion, not a change to the imported frame or
    a deviation from the standing formula.

    The guarantee is public visibility and deterministic replay: once the
    host publishes $\actsequence{k}$, every participant holding the same
    accepted acts, final ledger, constants, and formula editions derives the
    same consequences. This specification therefore claims order transparency
    and replay determinism, not incentive-neutral ordering.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Act Clock and Projected-Path Order]
    \label{prop:graph:act-clock-path-order}
    The authoritative causal key of \zcref{def:graph:act-incidence-causality} is
    strictly increasing along the order, and a sequence of edge projections is
    a viable standing path (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}) only if
    consecutive
    projections either belong to one authored act via its internal $A\to T$
    transition (equal authoritative key) or have strictly increasing
    authoritative key; formally, for consecutive projections $e,e'$ with
    $\actof{e}\ne\actof{e'}$,
    $\actfrontier{k}{\actof{e}}<\actfrontier{k}{\actof{e'}}$.
    \proofsketch{The host position $\actposition{k}{q_{k,j}}=j$ is strictly
    increasing, so the lexicographic key
    $\actfrontier{k}{q}=(\acttime{q},\actposition{k}{q})$ is strictly
    increasing along the sequence; viability requires each step to respect that
    order, with the one-act $A\to T$ transition the sole equal-key exception.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Authored-Act Time Is Not Wall Time]
    \label{rem:graph:act-time-not-wall-clock}
    The order is host-chosen but bounded: it must respect every declared
    dependency and group each act's legs, and it is published so that replay is
    reproducible (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}).  The maturity
    scalar $\tau_e$ (\zcref{def:graph:edge-projection-maturity}) counts endpoint-%
    incidence pre-degree from the graph state \emph{immediately before} the act
    in the authoritative order, so the two legs of one hyper-edge never mature
    each other and later acts never contribute to an earlier act's maturity.
    Asserted parents are admission metadata and add no pre-degree
    (\zcref{rem:graph:act-ordering-relations}); no wall-clock is presupposed.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Public Causality and Removable Dependencies]
    \label{rem:graph:act-ordering-relations}
    Two act-level relations constrain the authoritative order. Public asserted
    parents define the non-removable \emph{causal-parent} relation
    $p\causalparent q \Leftrightarrow \actid{p}\in\actparents{q}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-causal-parents}); the Actor-authored dependency
    projection defines the removable \emph{declared-dependency} relation
    $p\declareddep q \Leftrightarrow \actid{p}\in\actdeps{q}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection}). Both require the parent at
    strictly lower authoritative time,
    $p\causalparent q \lor p\declareddep q \;\Rightarrow\; \acttime{p}<\acttime{q}$,
    but only the second may later become unavailable through
    dependency-projection tombstoning (the retained commitment still permits a
    later opening and fraud proof). Both belong to the authored act; neither
    belongs to any edge projection. Maturity $\tau$, pre-degree, path viability,
    and every quantity covered by \zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}
    read endpoint incidence under the authoritative order
    (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}), never either ordering field. The
    reason is incentive-facing: asserted parents and declared dependencies are
    user-authored metadata, and admitting them into $\tau$ would create a
    $\tau$-farming channel by letting authors inflate apparent pre-degree. Lint
    rule: an asserted parent or declared dependency in a scoring formula is
    prohibited; the ordering relations are admission and ordering metadata only.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Choice of $\max$ in the Maturity Scalar]
    \label{rem:graph:maturity-max-rationale}
    The maturity scalar uses the \emph{maximum} of the two endpoint
    pre-degrees, not the minimum or a symmetric function.  This
    design choice captures the \emph{bridging potential} of the
    connection: a new actor ($\deg^{\mathrm{pre}} = 0$) connecting to
    an established hub ($\deg^{\mathrm{pre}} \gg 1$) creates
    precisely the kind of sparse-to-dense link that the serendipity
    mechanism rewards (\zcref{cor:sorting:serendipity-conditions});
    $\max$ gives this link high $\tau$, while $\min$ would force
    $\tau = 0$ regardless of the hub's history, destroying the
    bridging signal.  Conversely, a connection between two
    established hubs has high $\tau$ under all three options ($\max$,
    $\min$, or mean) and the distinction is moot.  The quantity is
    therefore a measure of \emph{connection-context maturity}, not
    maturity in the colloquial sense; edges with high $\tau$ are those
    whose endpoints have collectively deep interaction histories.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Maturity Bounds]
    \label{prop:graph:maturity-bounds}
    $\tau_e = 0$ for the first edge at both endpoints; $\tau_e$ is
    monotonically non-decreasing in prior degree; $\tau_e < 1$ for
    finite graphs; $\tau_e \to 1$ as degree grows.
    \proofsketch{$f(d) = 1 - 1/(1+d)$ is monotone
    $\NatZero \to [0,1)$.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Temporal Entropy]
    \label{def:graph:temporal-entropy}
    $\tentropy{e}
    = -\tau_e \ln \tau_e - (1-\tau_e)\ln(1-\tau_e)$,
    with $\tentropy{} = 0$ when $\tau_e = 0$.  Applied at the thermodynamic
    boundary (\zcref{ax:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary}).
\end{definition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Separable Act Commitment}
\label{subsec:graph:separable-commitment}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Act Payload Projection and Its Bound]
    \label{def:graph:act-payload-projection}
    Every authored act carries a \emph{payload projection}~$\actpayload{q}$: a
    byte string the network never reads, bounded \emph{per act} by a single
    Layer~1 constant,
    \[
        \operatorname{len}\bigl(\operatorname{encode}(\actpayload{q})\bigr)
        \;\leq\; \maxpayload,
    \]
    together with the private value of
    \zcref{post:graph:separable-act-projections}. For a hyper-edge act the
    payload may be a structured, role-addressed object
    $\actpayload{q}=(Y_q^{\mathrm{act}},Y_q^{A},Y_q^{T})$ when the application
    needs separate semantic fields, but this is \emph{one} act payload under one
    commitment and one lifecycle; the role labels are schema fields, not
    payloads attached independently to edge projections. The $\maxpayload$ bound
    is therefore aggregate over the act, so a two-projection hyper-edge carries
    no more payload than a binary act while paying one action and one debit.
    The canonical empty payload is the zero-length byte string; the commitment
    component is present on every act without exception, so only the byte string
    may be empty. The payload is \textbf{removable at the request of its
    controller (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-controller}), or of any legitimate
    entity}, under the phase-custody split of
    \zcref{rem:graph:act-payload-custody-phases}. The act's structural record ---
    author binding (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}), endpoints,
    authoritative time $\acttime{q}$, parameters, and the parity $\detsign{e}$ of
    each edge projection $e\in\actedges{q}$ --- is not, and neither the act
    identifier nor an edge-projection identity key admits any payload datum, so
    \texttt{settles}-reference resolution and title recognition are invariant
    under every payload state. $\maxpayload$ is an infrastructure constant,
    sized so the depth-$L$ ego-network stays device-local-cacheable under
    worst-case payload use on every act
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:device-local}) and epoch edge sets stay bounded
    (\zcref{post:introduction:epoch-edge-set}); it enters no scoring,
    attribution, transport, or capacity formula, and is locked in the
    centralized phase (\zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model}).
\end{definition}

\begin{postulate}[Separable, Concealing Act Commitment]
    \label{post:graph:separable-act-projections}
    The append mechanism's commitment to every authored act
    (\zcref{rem:introduction:mechanism-agnostic} leaves the mechanism open) must
    \emph{factor} into a \textbf{structural} part, over the act's
    irrevocable record, and a \textbf{content} part, over the payload --- the act
    commitment reproducible from the two together. The structural part must verify
    whether or not the payload is held. The content part must be:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{binding}] no second payload is consistent with it ---
            removal erases, never rewrites;
        \item[\textnormal{concealing}] alone, it reveals nothing recoverable about
            the payload --- formed over the payload together with a private value
            held \emph{beside the payload in carriage}, never in the structural
            record, and removed \textbf{atomically with it}.
    \end{description}
    An act thus presents in two projections reproducing the same commitment:
    \textbf{full} (payload and private value present; carriage verified against the
    act) and \textbf{reduced} (both removed; the structural record verified against
    an \emph{inert} content residue that binds yet conceals). Content state moves
    full~$\to$~reduced only; the structural record is invariant across the
    transition. The canonical empty payload is committed identically --- the
    private value is present --- so both projections exist for every act.
\end{postulate}

\begin{definition}[Act Payload State]
    \label{def:graph:act-payload-state}
    The payload projection of an authored act is in one of three states:
    \emph{full-empty} (canonical zero-length bytes, private value present),
    \emph{full} (bytes and private value present), or \emph{reduced} (both
    removed, the inert residue remaining). State moves toward reduced only.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Removable-Projection Invariance]
    \label{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}
    Tombstoning or removing either act-owned removable projection --- the
    payload $\actpayload{q}$ or the dependency opening $\actdeps{q}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-tombstone}) --- changes neither
    $\actedges{q}$ nor any edge-projection identifier, incidence, role, parameter
    rendering, act time $\acttime{q}$, standing quantity, title quantity, or raw
    graph quantity. Concretely, every Layer~1 quantity --- $\symbf{\Psi}_e$,
    $\pathview{e}$, $\detsign{e}$, $\dampedweight{e}$, $\baseval{e}$,
    $\transportentry{}{}$, $\standing{}$, settlement recognition,
    $\titlecert{k}$, and every gate --- is identical across all payload states of
    every act.
    \proofsketch{No Layer~1 formula has a payload or removable-dependency
    argument (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-projection}); an act's record
    projection and structural record are invariant across removable-projection
    states (\zcref{post:graph:separable-act-projections}), so changing an
    act-owned removable projection cannot alter its edge projection.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Act Payload Controller]
    \label{def:graph:act-payload-controller}
    The payload controller of an authored act is simply its author,
    $\operatorname{controller}(q)=\operatorname{author}(q)$: the entity entitled
    to request removal of the act's payload projection. There is no separate
    A-leg or T-leg controller --- the initiating author owns the one act payload.
    Derived edges carry no payload projection
    (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}); there is nothing to control.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Payload Size Is Not Act Cost]
    \label{rem:graph:payload-size-not-act-cost}
    One authored \emph{act} consumes one action credit --- a hyper-edge, both
    projections, is one act --- regardless of payload
    length: payload bytes, length, schema, and state enter neither
    $\actcount{}$ nor W1/W2 nor any gate. $\maxpayload$ is a
    carriage bound, never an action-denomination rule.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Removal Is Scoring-Neutral]
    \label{rem:graph:act-payload-removal-neutrality}
    The payload and its private value sit outside the structural part, so the
    reduced projection carries the entire scoring surface: every Layer~1 quantity
    --- $\standing{i}$, $\transportentry{j}{i}$, the relevance score (whose content norm
    reads incoming edge sentiment, not the payload), settlement recognition, the
    reputation conjunction --- reads only the structural record. Epoch replay
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:epoch-replay-determinism}) is bit-identical across full and
    reduced; erasing every payload changes no standing, title, or reward. This is
    why actor-or-operator removal is \emph{not} the moderation the architecture
    forbids
    (\zcref{tbl:introduction:layer-roles}): the measure never reads the payload, so
    erasing it cannot tilt the measure.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Payload Custody Across Phases]
    \label{rem:graph:act-payload-custody-phases}
    The content commitment (the \emph{witness}: binding-and-concealing residue of
    \zcref{post:graph:separable-act-projections}) is invariant across phases; only
    \emph{carriage} migrates. Centralized: Layer~1 tracks payload and salt,
    removable on request. Decentralized: Layer~1 tracks only the witness; payload
    and salt are out of scope, a Layer~2 carriage obligation. The structural record
    is identical in both.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[A Named Limit on Erasure]
    \label{rem:graph:erasure-floor}
    In the register of \zcref{ins:introduction:the-floor-we-name}: an edge that
    committed to content keeps, after removal, an inert content residue --- it
    reveals nothing yet does not vanish, being what lets the edge still
    authenticate. Binding the content and leaving no trace of it are incompatible;
    the architecture commits to the former and names the latter as the price (a
    deployment needing zero residue must leave the payload wholly outside the
    commitment, making the two projections vacuous). And concealment rests on the
    entropy of a value the network cannot audit: private by construction, so its
    quality is the committer's charge --- the operator's in the centralized phase, a
    constrained-generation obligation once the append layer decentralizes. Finally,
    \emph{payload} authorship --- that an actor wrote those bytes --- is in neither
    projection: the edge's authorship is always provable; the payload's only above
    Layer~1, exactly as the transport layer carries bytes it does not authenticate
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:tcp-is-unpriced-neutrality}). And commentary outlives
    its subject: a Comment quoting a payload persists, in its reviewer's controlled
    record, through the quoted payload's removal --- the surviving record is the
    reviewer's own authored act, exactly the class
    \zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave} protects.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Extended Sentiment Slice}
\label{subsec:graph:sentiment-slice}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Rows correspond to modes of the intensity parameter $p_{\mathrm{int}}$;
columns to modes of the directional parameter $p_{\mathrm{dir}}$.  Mode~0
is signed, mode~1 is absolute, mode~2 is unit (independent of the other
parameter).  Two clamping functions are used:
the primitive subscripted sigmoid is
$\sigmoid{x} = 1/(1 + e^{-x})$, the standard logistic function, so
$\sigmoid{0} = \tfrac{1}{2}$.
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item $\fpm{x} = \clamptanh{x}$: for signed arguments, bounded in
          $(-1,1)$.
    \item $\fpl{x} = \clampsigmoid{x}$: for non-negative arguments,
          bounded in $(0.5,1)$.
\end{itemize}

\begin{definition}[Extended Sentiment Slice]
    \label{def:graph:sentiment-slice}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:tensor-format}%
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:clamped-entry-bounds}%
    For an edge with parameters $p_d \coloneqq p_{\mathrm{dir}}$,
    $p_i \coloneqq p_{\mathrm{int}}$, domain $D$, and binary mask
    $\symbf{a}_D = (a_{00}, a_{01}, a_{10}, a_{11}) \in \set{0,1}^4$:
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:graph:sentiment-slice}
        \symbf{\Psi}_e
        =
        \begin{pmatrix}
            a_{00}\, \fpm{p_i p_d}
            & a_{01}\, \fpm{p_i |p_d|}
            & \fpm{p_i} \\[6pt]
            a_{10}\, \fpm{|p_i| p_d}
            & a_{11}\, \fpl{|p_i| |p_d|}
            & \fpl{|p_i|} \\[6pt]
            \fpm{p_d}
            & \fpl{|p_d|}
            & \fpl{1}
        \end{pmatrix}
    \end{equation}
    The mask applies only to the upper-left $2 \times 2$ bilinear
    block.  Marginals and baseline are always active.
\end{definition}

\paragraph{Entry semantics.}
Rows are indexed by the intensity mode $g \in \set{0,1,2}$
($0$~=~signed, $1$~=~absolute, $2$~=~unit); columns by the
directional mode $h \in \set{0,1,2}$.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}c c c l@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Position $(g,h)$} & \textbf{Product} & \textbf{Clamp}
        & \textbf{Name} \\
    \midrule
    $(0,0)$ & $p_i p_d$     & $\psi_{\pm}$ & Tribal alignment \\
    $(0,1)$ & $p_i |p_d|$   & $\psi_{\pm}$ & Popularity \\
    $(1,0)$ & $|p_i| p_d$   & $\psi_{\pm}$ & Engagement buzz \\
    $(1,1)$ & $|p_i| |p_d|$ & $\psi_{+}$   & Polarization \\
    $(0,2)$ & $p_i$         & $\psi_{\pm}$ & Net intensity \\
    $(1,2)$ & $|p_i|$       & $\psi_{+}$   & Gross intensity \\
    $(2,0)$ & $p_d$         & $\psi_{\pm}$ & Net direction \\
    $(2,1)$ & $|p_d|$       & $\psi_{+}$   & Gross direction \\
    $(2,2)$ & $1$           & $\psi_{+}$   & Baseline ($\numrel{const.graph.fpl_baseline.num}$) \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{remark}[Marginal Archetypes]
    \label{rem:graph:marginal-archetypes}
    The marginal terms resolve the weak-parameter problem: an edge
    with strong direction ($p_d = 0.9$) but weak intensity
    ($p_i = 0.05$) produces bilinear entries $\approx 0.045$ but
    marginal entries $\fpm{0.9} \approx 0.556$.  The directional
    signal survives independently.
\end{remark}

The slice $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ is the stored object.  It is never
transmitted, composed, or scored directly.  All computation operates
on projections extracted from it.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Rank-2 Structure of the Slice}
\label{subsec:graph:rank-two-structure}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The stored $3 \times 3$ slice is intrinsically near-rank-2.  Its
$3 \times 3$ determinant degenerates, but the $2 \times 2$ bilinear
block is well conditioned.  This structural fact forces the dual-view
architecture defined in the next subsection.

\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic Rank-2 Constraint]
    \label{prop:graph:rank-two-constraint}
    For any $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ from \zcref{def:graph:sentiment-slice},
    writing $\svdone{} \geq \svdtwo{} \geq \svdthree{} \geq 0$ for the
    singular values of the stored $3 \times 3$ slice:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item The unclamped, \emph{unmasked} matrix is exactly rank~1
              (outer product of $(p_i, |p_i|, 1)^T$ and
              $(p_d, |p_d|, 1)$).
          \item With clamping and domain mask applied,
              $\svdthree{}/\svdone{}$
              is bounded by the effective mask (full-mask bound
              numerically verified on a $21 \times 21$ grid;
              Identity and Minimal restricted-mask bounds attained at
              the extremal corner $|p_d| = |p_i| = 1$; Epistemic and
              Economic bounds are interior maxima, since $|p_d| = 1$
              forces columns~1 and~2 of $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ to coincide
              and $|p_i| = 1$ forces rows~1 and~2 to coincide, giving
              $\svdthree{} = 0$ at the corner):
              \begin{center}
              \begin{tabular}{@{}l l c@{}}
                  \toprule
                  \textbf{Effective mask} & \textbf{Domain(s)}
                      & \textbf{Bound on}
                        $\svdthree{}/\svdone{}$ \\
                  \midrule
                  $(1,1,1,1)$ (full)
                      & Tribal + all promoted & $< 0.05$ \\
                  $(1,0,0,1)$
                      & Identity              & $\leq 0.14$ \\
                  $(0,1,0,1)$
                      & Epistemic             & $\leq 0.10$ \\
                  $(0,0,1,1)$
                      & Economic              & $\leq 0.10$ \\
                  $(0,0,0,1)$
                      & Minimal               & $\leq 0.22$ \\
                  \bottomrule
              \end{tabular}
              \end{center}
        \item \label{prop:graph:rank-two-constraint:energy-share}
              For full-mask edges,
              $\svdone{}^2 + \svdtwo{}^2$ accounts for ${>}99.5\%$
              of $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F^2$.  For restricted-mask edges
              the two-singular-value share is $\geq 95.5\%$ (Minimal)
              to $\geq 99\%$ (Epistemic/Economic).
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    (1)~Without clamping or masking, every entry is
    $g(p_i) \cdot h(p_d)$ for $g \in \set{p_i, |p_i|, 1}$,
    $h \in \set{p_d, |p_d|, 1}$: an outer product of rank~1.

    (2)~\emph{Full mask.}  The clamping functions $\fpm{\cdot}$ and
    $\fpl{\cdot}$ differ by a multiplicative $\tanh$ factor, breaking
    exact row proportionality.  The third singular value captures only
    the residual of fitting row~2 as a linear combination of rows~0
    and~1.  Numerically: for a Tribal edge ($p_d = \numval{fixture.e2.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.e2.indirect.exact}$),
    singular values of the stored $3 \times 3$ slice are
    $\approx (\numval{result.e2.psi_svd1.num}, \numval{result.e2.psi_svd2.num}, \numval{result.e2.psi_svd3.num})$, giving
    $\svdthree{}/\svdone{} \numrel{result.e2.psi_svd_ratio.num}$.  A $21 \times 21$ grid over
    $(p_d, p_i) \in [-1,1]^2$ with step $0.1$ \emph{numerically}
    confirms $\svdthree{}/\svdone{} \leq \numval{bound.graph.svd_ratio_grid.num}$ at every sampled
    full-mask point.  The full-mask bound is stated as numerically
    verified at this resolution; the interpolation gap between grid
    points is not analytically estimated here, and a closed-form
    bound is deferred.

    \emph{Restricted masks.}  When the domain mask zeroes one or more
    bilinear entries, the always-active marginal row
    $(\fpm{p_d},\; \fpl{|p_d|},\; \fpl{1})$ and marginal column
    $(\fpm{p_i},\; \fpl{|p_i|},\; \fpl{1})^T$ contribute structure
    linearly independent of the surviving bilinear entries, injecting
    genuine rank-3 content.  The Identity and Minimal masks retain
    rank~3 at the extremal corner $|p_d| = |p_i| = 1$ and attain their
    bounds there.  The Epistemic and Economic masks degenerate at the
    corner: $|p_d| = 1$ makes the absolute-directional and unit columns
    of $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ coincide (Epistemic), and $|p_i| = 1$ makes the
    absolute-intensity and unit rows coincide (Economic), so
    $\svdthree{} = 0$ there and their $\svdthree{}/\svdone{}$ maxima are
    interior, confirmed on the $21 \times 21$ grid.  Concretely for the
    Minimal mask $(0,0,0,1)$ at $p_d = \numval{fixture.minimal.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.minimal.indirect.exact}$:
    \[
        \symbf{\Psi}_e
        = \begin{pmatrix}
            0 & 0 & \fpm{1} \\
            0 & \fpl{1} & \fpl{1} \\
            \fpm{-1} & \fpl{1} & \fpl{1}
        \end{pmatrix},
    \]
    yielding $\svdthree{}/\svdone{} \numrel{result.minimal.psi_svd_ratio.num}$.

    (3)~For full-mask edges, the verified
    $\svdthree{}/\svdone{} \leq \numval{bound.graph.svd_ratio_grid.num}$ bound gives
    $\svdthree{}^2/\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F^2 \leq \numval{bound.graph.svd_energy_grid.num}$, so the top two
    singular values account for ${>}99.5\%$ of the Frobenius energy.
    For the Minimal worst case above, the singular values are
    $(\svdone{},\svdtwo{},\svdthree{}) \approx (\numval{result.minimal.psi_svd1.num},\; \numval{result.minimal.psi_svd2.num},\; \numval{result.minimal.psi_svd3.num})$ (check:
    $\svdone{}^2+\svdtwo{}^2+\svdthree{}^2 = \numval{result.minimal.frobenius_sq.num} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F^2$), giving a
    two-singular-value share of
    $(\numval{result.minimal.psi_svd1_sq.num} + \numval{result.minimal.psi_svd2_sq.num})/\numval{result.minimal.frobenius_sq.num} = 96.0\%$, confirming $\geq 95.5\%$.
    For the Epistemic mask at $|p_d| = |p_i| = 1$, the identity
    $|p_d| = 1$ collapses columns~1 and~2 of $\symbf{\Psi}_e$
    (signed and absolute directional modes coincide), giving
    $\svdthree{} = 0$ and energy share $100\%$.  The Economic mask
    exhibits the analogous row collapse at $|p_i| = 1$ (signed
    and absolute intensity modes coincide).  The supremum of
    $\svdthree{}^2/\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F^2$ for both masks occurs
    at interior parameter values; evaluated on the same
    $21 \times 21$ grid, the maximum is $\leq \numval{bound.graph.svd_energy_grid_restricted.num}$ for both
    masks, confirming $\geq 99\%$.
\end{proof}

\begin{insight}[Rank-2 Structural Consequence]
    \label{ins:graph:rank-two-structural-consequence}
    Composition in $3 \times 3$ loses directional information to rank
    degeneracy, forcing the system to extract a well-conditioned
    $2 \times 2$ bilinear block for path composition (whose determinant
    measures directional coherence) and to retain the full $3 \times 3$
    Frobenius norm for attribution (which captures total information
    equitably across edge types).  The rank-2 approximation quality is
    itself domain-dependent ($\svdthree{}/\svdone{} < 0.05$ for full-mask
    edges; $\leq 0.22$ for the Minimal mask), which \emph{reinforces}
    the split: restricted-mask edges carry higher effective rank in the
    $3 \times 3$ slice, making the $2 \times 2$ path-view extraction
    even more necessary for clean composition, while the Frobenius norm
    captures more independent information per edge for these domains.
    This ratio characterizes approximation quality; downstream
    computations use the \PathView{} block directly and do not consume
    the $3 \times 3$ SVD.
\end{insight}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Three Computational Interfaces}
\label{subsec:graph:three-interfaces}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Dual-View Architecture]
    \label{def:graph:dual-view-architecture}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture}%
    Every edge stores $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ and exposes three interfaces:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[Scalar.]
            $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_e}_F
            = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F \cdot \sqrt{1+\tau_e^2}$.
        \item[\PathView{}.]
            $\pathview{e} \in \R^{2 \times 2}$
            (\zcref{subsec:graph:path-view-and-signed-svd}).
            The $\bleedparam$-softened bilinear block, scored via the
            $2 \times 2$ signed SVD and determinant sign.
            Used by sorting (\zcref{sec:sorting}) and advertiser
            transport (\zcref{sec:transport}).
        \item[\AttrView{}.]
            $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F$ (full $3 \times 3$,
            no~$\tau$).  CAN base value (\zcref{app:can}).
    \end{description}
\end{definition}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Computational interfaces extracted from the stored
    $3 \times 3 \times 2$ tensor. The \PathView{} determinant produces the
    shared raw-edge primitive of \zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive} for
    raw graph consumers.  Standing separately compiles complete acts into
    the actor-only vouch projection.}
    \label{tbl:graph:computational-interfaces}
    \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l l X X@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Interface} & \textbf{Source}
            & \textbf{Layer~1 Role}
            & \textbf{Layer~2 (Guild) Role} \\
        \midrule
        Scalar
            & $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F \cdot \sqrt{1+\tau_e^2}$
                        & Content quality factor at path terminus
            & Content quality signal in the relevance score \\
        \addlinespace
        \PathView{}
            & $\pathview{e}$ ($2 \times 2$,
              $\bleedparam$-softened)
            & Feed-ranking BFS edge weight ($\dampedweight{e}$); raw
              signed double-cover edge weight ($\dampedweight{e}$); raw
              shortest-path costs.  Standing is not a raw \PathView{}
              traversal; it consumes complete projected acts.
            & Bridge campaign circuit~$\campaignscalar{A}$;
              betweenness centrality~$S_C$ \\
        \addlinespace
        \AttrView{}
            & $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F$
              (full $3 \times 3$, no~$\tau$)
            & CAN base value inputs (no temporal factor)
            & CAN recursion;
              enrichment factor $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\tierfull{} and \tiermarginal{} edges differ by $\sim\!5\times$ in
$\detscore{}$ but only $\sim\!16\%$ in $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F$
(\zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}:
$\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \in [\numval{result.e7.frobenius.num}, \numval{result.e8.frobenius.num}]$, ratio $\numval{result.tier.frob_ratio.num}$).
Discrimination lives in sorting (\PathView{}); equity lives in
attribution (\AttrView{}).  See
\zcref{ins:graph:rank-two-structural-consequence}.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Path-View Extraction and the Signed SVD}
\label{subsec:graph:path-view-and-signed-svd}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

% ─── bleed-softening ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

\paragraph{Path-view sentiment matrix.}

\begin{definition}[Path-View Sentiment Matrix and Routing Tier]
    \label{def:graph:path-view-extraction}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:eta-softening}%
    Each edge carries a routing tier
    $T(e) \in \set{\tierfull{}, \tierhalf{}, \tiermarginal{}}$.  The
    path-view matrix $\pathview{e} \in \R^{2 \times 2}$ is
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:graph:path-view-extraction}
        \pathview{e}
        =
        \begin{pmatrix}
            \softmask{00}\, \fpm{p_i p_d}
            & \softmask{01}\, \fpm{p_i |p_d|}  \\[6pt]
            \softmask{10}\, \fpm{|p_i| p_d}
            & \softmask{11}\, \fpl{|p_i| |p_d|}
        \end{pmatrix},
    \end{equation}
    with softened coefficients set by the binary domain mask
    $a_{gh} \in \set{0,1}$ and the tier floor:
    \begin{equation}
        \softmask{gh}
        =
        \begin{cases}
            a_{gh} + (1 - a_{gh})\,\bleedparam,
                & T \in \set{\tierfull{}, \tiermarginal{}}, \\[4pt]
            1, & T = \tierhalf{},\ (g,h) = (1,1), \\[4pt]
            \halffloor, & T = \tierhalf{},\ (g,h) \neq (1,1),
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    $\bleedparam \numrel{const.graph.bleed.num}$, $\halffloor \numrel{const.graph.halffloor.num}$.  The polarization
    corner $\softmask{11} = 1$ always.  Equivalently, the tier is the
    $\bleedparam$-power of $\softmask{00}$:
    \tierfull{} $\Leftrightarrow \softmask{00} = 1$ (full or Identity
    mask); \tierhalf{} $\Leftrightarrow \softmask{00} = \halffloor$;
    \tiermarginal{} $\Leftrightarrow \softmask{00} = \bleedparam$
    (restricted mask).  The \tierhalf{} floor is a path-view-only
    attenuation: it scales the three signed off-corner entries of a
    \emph{full stored block} to $\halffloor$, leaving the polarization
    corner, the entire $3 \times 3$ stored slice, the \AttrView{}
    Frobenius norm, and every CAN base value unchanged.
\end{definition}

\paragraph{Softened masks per domain.}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l c c@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Domain} & \textbf{Binary mask} & \textbf{Softened} \\
    \midrule
    Tribal $(\symcal{D}_T)$
        & $(1,1,1,1)$ & $(1, 1, 1, 1)$ \\
    Identity $(\symcal{D}_I)$
        & $(1,0,0,1)$ & $(1, .05, .05, 1)$ \\
    Epistemic $(\symcal{D}_E)$
        & $(0,1,0,1)$ & $(.05, 1, .05, 1)$ \\
    Economic $(\symcal{D}_X)$
        & $(0,0,1,1)$ & $(.05, .05, 1, 1)$ \\
    Relational $(\symcal{D}_R)$
        & $(0,0,1,1)$ & $(.05, .05, 1, 1)$ \\
    Minimal $(\symcal{D}_M)$
        & $(0,0,0,1)$ & $(.05, .05, .05, 1)$ \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\emph{Tier override.}  The settlement-handshake edges (Bid, Accept,
Ratify; \zcref{subsec:graph:settlement-lifecycle}) and the
conversational proposal edges (Join Request, Invitation/A;
\zcref{def:graph:proposal-half-tier}) carry a full stored block but
route at the \tierhalf{} tier: their path-view
off-corner entries are scaled to $\halffloor$ regardless of the domain
softening above.

% ─── Signed SVD: the complete tool ───────────────────────────────────

\paragraph{The signed SVD over $SO(2)$: complete decomposition tool.}

The following decomposition applies to any nonsingular
$M \in \R^{2 \times 2}$.  It is stated here as a matrix-agnostic
tool; the system applies it to individual path-view matrices
$\pathview{e}$ (per-edge) and to composed path matrices $\pathmatrix{p}$
(post-ranking).

\begin{definition}[Signed SVD over $SO(2)$]
    \label{def:graph:signed-svd}
    For any $M \in \R^{2 \times 2}$ with $\det(M) \neq 0$, the
    following sign-resolved variant of the standard
    SVD\footcite[\S2.4]{golub2013matrix}, called the
    \emph{signed SVD over $SO(2)$}, is the decomposition:
    \begin{equation}
        M = R_1
        \begin{pmatrix}
            \svdone{} & 0 \\
            0 & \epsilon\,\svdtwo{}
        \end{pmatrix}
        R_2^T,
        \label{eq:graph:signed-svd}
    \end{equation}
    where $R_1, R_2 \in SO(2)$, $\svdone{} \geq \svdtwo{} > 0$, and:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item By convention $\svdone{}$ is the unsigned $(1,1)$-entry
              of the diagonal (the dominant stretch).  The determinant
              identity $\det M = \epsilon\,\svdone{}\svdtwo{}$ then
              forces the $(2,2)$-entry to be $\epsilon\,\svdtwo{}$.
        \item $\epsilon(M) \coloneqq \operatorname{sgn}(\det(M))
              \in \set{+1,-1}$ is the \emph{determinant sign} of $M$:
              $+1$ if $M$ preserves orientation; $-1$ if it reverses
              it.  The sign is determined by $M$; it is not a
              convention degree of freedom.
    \end{itemize}
\end{definition}

At the graph level, the determinant sign turns continuous sentiment
parameters into a signed-edge observable. This places the construction
near empirical work on positive and negative links in online social
networks\footcite{leskovec2010predicting}, while differing in source:
the sign is derived from the determinant of a continuous path-view
matrix, not supplied as a discrete relation label.

\begin{lemma}[Uniqueness of the Signed SVD]
    \label{lem:graph:signed-svd-uniqueness}
    Under $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$, the decomposition of
    \zcref{def:graph:signed-svd} is unique up to the simultaneous
    replacement $(R_1, R_2) \to (-R_1, -R_2)$.  The dominant axis
    (the line spanned by the first column of $R_1$) is invariant
    under this residual.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    Let $M = R_1 S R_2^T = R_1' S R_2^{\prime T}$ with
    $S = \operatorname{diag}(\svdone{}, \epsilon\svdtwo{})$ fixed.
    Write $A = R_1^{\prime T} R_1 = R(\varphi_1)$ and
    $B = R_2^{\prime T} R_2 = R(\varphi_2)$, both in $SO(2)$; these
    angles are local to this proof.  Then
    $AS = SB$.  Matching the $(1,2)$-entry:
    $\epsilon\svdtwo{} \sin\varphi_1 = \svdone{} \sin\varphi_2$.  Matching
    the $(2,1)$-entry:
    $\svdone{} \sin\varphi_1 = \epsilon\svdtwo{} \sin\varphi_2$.
    Multiplying these two equations:
    $\epsilon\svdone{}\svdtwo{} \sin^2\varphi_1
    = \epsilon\svdone{}\svdtwo{} \sin^2\varphi_2$, hence
    $\sin^2\varphi_1 = \sin^2\varphi_2$.  Substituting back:
    $(\svdone{}^2 - \svdtwo{}^2)\sin\varphi_1 = 0$.  Since
    $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$, we conclude $\sin\varphi_1 = 0$, so
    $(A, B) \in \set{(I, I),\, (-I, -I)}$.

    Under $A = B = -I$: $R_1' = -R_1$, $R_2' = -R_2$.  The first
    column of $R_1$ maps to its negative, spanning the same line.

    At $\svdone{} = \svdtwo{}$ (isotropic case), the
    $(\svdone{}^2 - \svdtwo{}^2)$ factor vanishes and the residual
    expands to a continuous family.  The dominant axis is undefined;
    $\vartheta$ is not assigned.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Five named quantities.}
The signed SVD of any nonsingular $M \in \R^{2 \times 2}$ yields:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l l p{5.5cm}@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Quantity} & \textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Range}
        & \textbf{Meaning} \\
    \midrule
    Determinant sign
        & $\detsign{M}$
        & $\set{+1,-1}$
        & Orientation: coherent or inverted \\
    Determinant score
        & $|\det M|^{1/2}$
        & $\R_{>0}$
        & Directional coherence magnitude ($= \sqrt{\svdone{}\svdtwo{}}$) \\
    Condition number
        & $\condnum{M} = \svdone{}/\svdtwo{}$
        & $[1,\infty)$
        & Focus of the interaction \\
    Coherence ratio
        & $\cohratio{M} = \svdtwo{}/\svdone{}$
        & $(0,1]$
        & Diversity survival ($= 1/\condnum{M}$) \\
    Dominant mode angle
        & $\modeangle{M}$
        & $[0,\pi/2]$
        & Net intensity vs.\ gross intensity balance \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{definition}[Coherence Ratio]
    \label{def:graph:coherence-ratio}
    For any nonsingular $M$ with $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$:
    $\cohratio{M} = \svdtwo{} / \svdone{} \in (0,1)$.
    At $\svdone{} = \svdtwo{}$: $\cohratio{M} = 1$ (isotropic), and the
    dominant axis is undefined, so the mode angle $\modeangle{M}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:dominant-mode-angle}) is not assigned at this
    point.
    Measures sentiment diversity survival: $\cohratio{} \approx 1$
    means both modes survive (diverse); $\cohratio{} \approx 0$
    means one mode dominates (echo chamber).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Dominant Mode Angle]
    \label{def:graph:dominant-mode-angle}
    For any nonsingular $M$ with $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$, let
    $U = R_1$ be the left rotation in the signed SVD:
    \begin{equation}
        \modeangle{M}
        = \arctan\!\left|\frac{U_{10}}{U_{00}}\right|
        \in [0, \tfrac{\pi}{2}],
        \label{eq:graph:dominant-mode-angle}
    \end{equation}
    with $\modeangle{} = \pi/2$ when $U_{00} = 0$ (by continuity).
    This is the acute angle between the dominant axis and the first
    coordinate axis.  The ratio $U_{10}/U_{00}$ is automatically
    invariant under the residual sign of $R_1$
    (\zcref{lem:graph:signed-svd-uniqueness}); the absolute value
    folds the dominant axis (a line, not a vector) into its acute
    angle with the first coordinate axis, giving range
    $[0, \pi/2]$ as a theorem.

    The left singular vectors live in the \emph{intensity-mode}
    space (row indices of the path-view matrix: row~0 = signed
    $\psi_\pm$ mode, row~1 = absolute $\psi_+$ mode).
    $\modeangle{} \approx 0$: the dominant output mode is primarily
    net/signed intensity.
    $\modeangle{} \approx \pi/2$: the dominant output mode is
    primarily gross/unsigned intensity.
    Not defined at $\svdone{} = \svdtwo{}$ (isotropic; dominant axis
    undefined).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Geometric Mean at $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$]
    \label{rem:graph:signed-svd-geometric-mean}
    At $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$, the SVD path score uses
    $\sqrt{\svdone{} \svdtwo{}} = |\det(M)|^{1/2}$ --- real and
    positive regardless of $\epsilon$.  The feed-ranking BFS computes
    this magnitude and discards the sign.  The raw signed double-cover
    service (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}) retains the sign to
    distinguish positive-parity raw paths from negative-parity raw
    paths, using the identical raw per-edge weight formula
    $\dampedweight{e}$ for both purposes.  Standing is not such a
    raw-path consumer: it first compiles complete person-vouch acts.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The Score Exponent Is Dynamics-Locked]
    \label{rem:graph:score-exponent-uniqueness}
    The square root in $\detscore{e} = |\det(\pathview{e})|^{1/2}$ is not a
    free aesthetic.  For a hypothetical exponent $q$ ($|\det|^{q}$) the bond
    activation inherits
    $\tfrac{d}{dp}\log\tanh^{q}p = 2q\operatorname{csch}2p$, and the
    small-$p$ Schwarzian of the reduced activation then carries the singular
    residue $(\tfrac12 - 2q^{2})\,p^{-2}$, which vanishes \emph{iff}
    $q = \tfrac12$ (\zcref{thm:dynamics:core-margin-limit}).  The convention chosen
    here for Dijkstra factorization
    (\zcref{rem:graph:diversity-preference-default}) is thereby also the
    unique exponent taming the flip margin at small standing: changing it is
    a bifurcation event, not a scoring preference (prohibited-patterns
    register).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Trace and Determinant Channels]
    \label{rem:graph:trace-determinant-recovery}
    Writing the signed SVD as
    $M = R_1\,\operatorname{diag}(\svdone{},\,\epsilon\svdtwo{})\,R_2^T$
    with $R_1 = R(\theta_1)$, $R_2 = R(\theta_2) \in SO(2)$ and relative
    angle $\varphi = \theta_1 - \theta_2$, the classical trace and
    determinant channels are:
    \begin{align}
        \operatorname{tr}(M)
        &= (\svdone{} + \detsign{M}\,\svdtwo{})\cos\varphi,
        \label{eq:graph:trace-recovery} \\
        \det(M)
        &= \detsign{M} \cdot \svdone{}\,\svdtwo{}.
        \label{eq:graph:det-recovery}
    \end{align}
    The determinant channel depends only on the two singular values
    and the orientation bit, and is therefore recovered exactly by the
    per-edge extractions $\detsign{M}$ and
    $\sqrt{\svdone{}\,\svdtwo{}}$; the trace additionally requires the
    relative rotation angle $\varphi$, which the per-edge tier does not
    compute.  The coherence ratio $\cohratio{}$ is a continuous
    generalisation of the determinant channel, and the mode angle
    $\modeangle{}$ supplies directional information that neither trace
    nor determinant alone captures.
\end{remark}

Of these five quantities, only $\detsign{}$ and $|\det|^{1/2}$ are
computed per edge in either traversal.  The condition number,
coherence ratio, and dominant mode angle require a composed path
matrix; their computational tiering is tabulated in
\zcref{subsec:graph:path-composition} after the path score that
justifies the collapse.

\paragraph{Worked example: Opinion edge.}
For the reference Opinion edge ($p_d = \numval{fixture.e2.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.e2.indirect.exact}$; Tribal,
full mask), the path-view matrix is:
\[
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{\numval{result.e2.inner.num}} & \fpm{\numval{result.e2.inner.num}} \\[4pt]
        \fpm{\numval{result.e2.inner.num}} & \fpl{\numval{result.e2.inner.num}}
    \end{pmatrix}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \numval{result.e2.core_pm.num} & \numval{result.e2.core_pm.num} \\
        \numval{result.e2.core_pm.num} & \numval{result.e2.core_pl.num}
    \end{pmatrix}.
\]
$\det(\pathview{e}) = \numval{result.e2.core_pm.num} \times \numval{result.e2.core_pl.num} - \numval{result.e2.core_pm.num}^2 = \numval{result.e2.pv_ad.num} - \numval{result.e2.pv_bc.num}
\numrel{result.e2.pv_det.num}$.  Therefore $\detsign{e} = +1$ and
$\detscore{e} = \sqrt{0.123} \numrel{result.e2.detscore.num}$.  Since $\pathview{e}$ is
symmetric positive-definite here, its singular values equal its
eigenvalues: $\svdone{} \numrel{result.e2.pv_svd1.num}$, $\svdtwo{} \numrel{result.e2.pv_svd2.num}$
(check: $\svdone{}\svdtwo{} = \numval{result.e2.pv_det.num} = \det$;
$\svdone{}^2 + \svdtwo{}^2 = \numval{result.e2.pv_frob_sq.num} = \norm{\pathview{e}}_F^2$), giving
$\cohratio{} \numrel{result.e2.pv_cohratio.num}$, $\condnum{} \numrel{result.e2.pv_condnum.num}$, and $\modeangle{}
\numrel{result.e2.pv_modeangle.num}$ rad (both intensity modes contribute substantially).
Full verification: \zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Per-Edge Determinant Sign and Tier Structure}
\label{subsec:graph:determinant-sign-and-tiers}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

% ─── Per-edge determinant sign ───────────────────────────────────────

\begin{definition}[Per-Edge Determinant Sign]
    \label{def:graph:determinant-sign}
    For each edge $e$:
    \begin{equation}
        \detsign{e}
        \coloneqq \operatorname{sgn}(\det(\pathview{e}))
        \in \set{+1,\,-1}.
        \label{eq:graph:determinant-sign}
    \end{equation}
    Well-defined for all edges with nonzero parameters:
    $\bleedparam$-softening guarantees
    $\det(\pathview{e}) \neq 0$
    (\zcref{prop:graph:path-view-determinant-bound}).  A
    \emph{positive edge} has $\detsign{e} = +1$; a \emph{negative
    edge} has $\detsign{e} = -1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Extraction Cost]
    \label{rem:graph:one-bit-extraction-cost}
    The per-edge sign $\detsign{e}$ requires one sign-test beyond
    what the feed-ranking BFS already computes: evaluate
    $\det(\pathview{e})$ (already required for $\detscore{e}$), then
    test its sign.  No matrix accumulation, no SVD, and no additional
    floating-point arithmetic is required beyond the sign detection.
    The raw signed double-cover service
    (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs})
    adds $\sim 1$ floating-point operation per edge relative to the
    feed-ranking BFS
    (\zcref{lem:epoch:double-cover-bfs-correctness}).
    The cheapness is a performance property; the necessity of
    retaining the sign is a correctness property --- routing
    influence through an inverted path treats an inverted signal as
    an endorsement
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}).
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Anisotropy of Pipeline Path-View Matrices]
    \label{prop:graph:pipeline-anisotropy}
    For every path-view matrix $\pathview{e}$ produced by the
    canonical pipeline (\zcref{post:nodes:canonical-tensor-pipeline})
    with both parameters nonzero: $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$.  The
    isotropic point $\svdone{} = \svdtwo{}$ is not attained, so the
    uniqueness guarantee of \zcref{lem:graph:signed-svd-uniqueness}
    and the definitions of $\cohratio{}$ and $\modeangle{}$ apply to
    all such matrices.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    A real $2 \times 2$ matrix $M$ has $\svdone{} = \svdtwo{}$ iff
    $M^T M$ is a scalar multiple of $I$, equivalently $(M^TM)_{01} = 0$.  Writing
    $M = \pathview{e} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} a & b \\ c & d
    \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ with
    $a = \softmask{00}\fpm{p_ip_d}$,
    $b = \softmask{01}\fpm{p_i|p_d|}$,
    $c = \softmask{10}\fpm{|p_i|p_d}$,
    $d = \softmask{11}\fpl{|p_i||p_d|}$, the off-diagonal of $M^TM$ is
    $(M^TM)_{01} = ab + cd$.  All mask coefficients $\softmask{gh}$
    are positive ($1$, $\halffloor$, or $\bleedparam$).  The signs of the two terms
    are $\operatorname{sgn}(ab) = \operatorname{sgn}(p_ip_d)
    \operatorname{sgn}(p_i) = \operatorname{sgn}(p_d)$ and
    $\operatorname{sgn}(cd) = \operatorname{sgn}(p_d) \cdot (+)
    = \operatorname{sgn}(p_d)$, since $d = \fpl{\cdot} > 0$.  With
    both parameters nonzero, $a, b, c$ are nonzero, so both terms are
    nonzero and carry the same sign $\operatorname{sgn}(p_d)$; their
    positively weighted sum is therefore nonzero:
    $(M^TM)_{01} \neq 0$.  Hence $M^TM$ is not a scalar multiple of $I$, and
    $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$.  (For the full-mask case with $p_d > 0$,
    $a = b = c$ and $(M^TM)_{01} = a(a + d) > 0$ transparently.)
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Graceful Degeneracy at Zero Parameters]
    \label{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy}
    When either parameter vanishes, $\det(\pathview{e}) = 0$,
    $\detsign{e}$ is undefined, and $\dampedweight{e} = 0$; the
    edge is routing-inert and does not participate in any BFS
    relaxation.  The anisotropy guarantee of
    \zcref{prop:graph:pipeline-anisotropy} and the uniqueness
    guarantee of \zcref{lem:graph:signed-svd-uniqueness} are
    vacuously satisfied.  The Self-edge bond at
    $\standing{j} = 0$ ($p_i = 0$) is the principal instance:
    \zcref{prop:nodes:raw-self-edge-properties} Property~1
    confirms $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} = 0$, and
    \zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity} gives
    strict recovery as $\standing{j}$ becomes positive.
    The second instance users will actually meet is the neutral-attachment
    Owner ($a = 0$): it anchors the title thread of its Item
    (\zcref{def:graph:item-genesis-act}) while contributing nothing to routing
    --- title is sentiment-blind
    (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}), reach is not.
\end{remark}

% ─── Tier structure ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

\paragraph{Path-view determinant bound and tier structure.}

\begin{proposition}[Path-View Determinant Bound and Tier Structure]
    \label{prop:graph:path-view-determinant-bound}
    For every $\pathview{e}$: $|\det(\pathview{e})| > 0$ whenever
    both parameters are nonzero ($\bleedparam$-softening ensures
    generic rank-2).
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l c l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Tier} & $\sqrt{|\det(\pathview{})|}$
            & \textbf{Edge types} \\
        \midrule
        \tierfull{}
            & $\approx 0.27\text{--}0.36$
            & Opinion, Review/A, Self, Owner, Participant, Send/A \\
        \tierhalf{}
            & $\approx 0.20\text{--}0.22$
            & Bid, Accept, Ratify, Join~Request, Invitation/A \\
        \tiermarginal{}
            & $\approx 0.07\text{--}0.08$
            & Tag, Affinity, Review/T, Send/T, Invitation/T \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{center}
    The displayed \tierfull{} band is the reference band for non-Self
    full-mask edges and the calibrated Self/Reputation fixed point.
    The Self/Reputation component remains \tierfull{} but is standing-dependent;
    as $\standing{}$ grows, its determinant score can rise above this
    band, with the corresponding damped-weight supremum tracked
    separately by $\wmax$.  For typical above-threshold actors the
    Self/Reputation $\detscore{}$ lies \emph{above} the non-Self Full
    band; its supremum is tracked by $\wmax$.
    \emph{Self:} \tierfull{} (standing-dependent; $\detscore{} \to 0$ as
    $\standing{} \to 0$; effective \tierfull{} membership requires
    reduced standing $\refstanding{} \gtrsim 1$, i.e.\ at or above the
    participation gate).
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    We verify $\det(\pathview{e}) \neq 0$ for each mask family when
    both $p_d, p_i \neq 0$, and bound the resulting $|\det|^{1/2}$.

    \emph{Full mask $(1,1,1,1)$.}
    All four entries are active at full strength.  Write
    $\pathview{e} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
    a & b \\ c & d \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ with
    $a = \fpm{p_i p_d}$, $b = \fpm{p_i|p_d|}$,
    $c = \fpm{|p_i|p_d}$, $d = \fpl{|p_i||p_d|}$.
    Since $d = \psi_+(\cdot) \geq 0.5$ and $|a|, |b|, |c| < 1$
    (range of $\psi_\pm$):
    $|ad| \geq 0.5|a|$ while $|bc| < 1$.  At reference parameters
    ($p_d = \numval{fixture.e2.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.e2.indirect.exact}$): $\det \numrel{result.e2.pv_det.num}$,
    $|\det|^{1/2} \numrel{result.e2.detscore.num}$.

    \emph{Epistemic mask $(\bleedparam, 1, \bleedparam, 1)$.}
    $\pathview{e} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
    \bleedparam a & b \\ \bleedparam c & d \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.
    $\det = \bleedparam(ad - bc)$.  The bracket $(ad - bc)$ is nonzero
    for generic nonzero parameters because $d = \psi_+(\cdot) > 0.5$
    exceeds the off-diagonal $\psi_\pm$ products.  At reference
    Epistemic parameters ($p_d = \numval{fixture.e5.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.e5.indirect.exact}$), all four
    bilinear arguments equal $\numval{result.e5.inner.num}$ in magnitude, so
    $a = b = c = \fpm{\numval{result.e5.inner.num}} \numrel{result.e5.core_pm.num}$, $d = \fpl{\numval{result.e5.inner.num}} \numrel{result.e5.core_pl.num}$, and
    $ad - bc = \numval{result.e5.core_pm.num}(\numval{result.e5.core_pl.num} - \numval{result.e5.core_pm.num}) \numrel{result.e5.core_bracket.num}$:
    $\det = \numval{const.graph.bleed.num} \times \numval{result.e5.core_bracket.num} \numrel{result.e5.pv_det.num}$,
    $|\det|^{1/2} \numrel{result.e5.detscore.num}$.

    \emph{Economic mask $(\bleedparam, \bleedparam, 1, 1)$.}
    $\pathview{e} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
    \bleedparam a & \bleedparam b \\ c & d \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.
    $\det = \bleedparam(ad - bc)$.  Same structure; the scaling factor
    is again $\bleedparam$, giving $|\det|^{1/2} = O(\sqrt{\bleedparam})$.

    \emph{Identity mask $(1, \bleedparam, \bleedparam, 1)$.}
    $\pathview{e} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
    a & \bleedparam b \\ \bleedparam c & d \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.
    $\det = ad - \bleedparam^2 bc$.  Since $a = \fpm{\cdot}
    = d\tanh(\cdot) < d$ and $b, c$ share the same magnitude as $a$,
    so $bc < ad$, the leading term dominates the $O(\bleedparam^2)$
    correction: $|\det| \geq ad(1 - \bleedparam^2) > 0$.  At reference Self
    parameters ($p_d = \numval{fixture.e1.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.e1.indirect.exact}$): $a \numrel{result.e1.core_pm.num}$, $d \numrel{result.e1.core_pl.num}$,
    so $\det \numrel{result.e1.pv_det.num}$, $|\det|^{1/2} \numrel{result.e1.detscore.num}$, above the non-Self
    full-mask band and consistent with the \tierfull{} assignment.

    \emph{Minimal mask $(\bleedparam, \bleedparam, \bleedparam, 1)$.}
    $\pathview{e} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
    \bleedparam a & \bleedparam b \\ \bleedparam c & d \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.
    $\det = \bleedparam(ad - \bleedparam bc)$.
    Since $d = \psi_+(\cdot) \geq 0.5$ and $|b|, |c| < 1$, the bracket
    satisfies $|ad - \bleedparam bc| \geq 0.5|a| - \bleedparam$, which is strictly
    positive whenever $|a| > 2\bleedparam = 0.1$.  At small parameters the
    bracket approaches zero; the smallest
    \tiermarginal{} determinant scores observed in the verification suite are
    $\detscore{} \in [\numval{result.e7.detscore.num}, \numval{result.e5.detscore.num}]$
    (\zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}).

    \emph{Half tier (full block, $\softmask{} = \halffloor$
    off-corner).}  $\pathview{e} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
    \halffloor\,a & \halffloor\,b \\ \halffloor\,c & d
    \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ with $|a| = |b| = |c|$ and $d > |a|$
    (full block).  $\det = \halffloor\,ad - \bleedparam\,bc
    = \halffloor(ad - \halffloor\,bc) = O(\halffloor)$.  At reference
    Accept parameters ($p_d = \numval{fixture.accept.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.accept.indirect.exact}$): $\det \numrel{result.accept.pv_det.num}$,
    $|\det|^{1/2} \numrel{result.accept.detscore.num}$; at reference Bid parameters
    ($p_d = \numval{fixture.bid.direct.exact}$, $p_i = \numval{fixture.bid.indirect.exact}$): $\det \numrel{result.bid.pv_det.num}$, $|\det|^{1/2} \numrel{result.bid.detscore.num}$.

    The tier gap arises because the leading-order determinant scales
    as $O(1)$ for full and Identity masks, $O(\halffloor)$ for
    \tierhalf{} edges, and $O(\bleedparam)$ for Epistemic, Economic,
    and Minimal masks
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:eta-softening}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Tier-Floor Sign Invariance]
    \label{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}
    Let $e$ have a full stored bilinear block and let
    $f \in \set{1, \halffloor}$ be the path-view floor on its three
    signed off-corner entries ($f = 1$ for \tierfull{},
    $f = \halffloor$ for \tierhalf{}).  Then
    $\det(\pathview{e}) = f\,AD - f^2 BC$ with
    $A = \fpm{p_ip_d}$, $B = \fpm{p_i|p_d|}$, $C = \fpm{|p_i|p_d}$,
    $D = \fpl{|p_i||p_d|}$, and
    \[
        \detsign{e}
        = \operatorname{sgn}(AD)
        = \operatorname{sgn}(p_i p_d)
        \qquad\text{independent of } f.
    \]
    Demoting a full-block edge from \tierfull{} to \tierhalf{}
    therefore preserves its determinant sign exactly.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    For a full block $|A| = |B| = |C| = |\fpm{|p_ip_d|}| =: m$ and
    $D = \fpl{|p_ip_d|} > m$ (since $\fpl{} > \fpl{}\tanh = |\fpm{}|$),
    while $\operatorname{sgn}(A) = \operatorname{sgn}(BC)
    = \operatorname{sgn}(p_ip_d)$.  Hence
    $f\,AD - f^2 BC
    = \operatorname{sgn}(p_ip_d)\,f\,m\,(D - f\,m)$,
    and $D - f m \geq D - m > 0$ for $f \leq 1$.  The sign equals
    $\operatorname{sgn}(p_ip_d)$ at both floors.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Quadrant Law]
    \label{lem:graph:quadrant-law}
    For every edge produced by the canonical pipeline, in every mask and at
    every tier floor,
    \[
        \detsign{e} \;=\; \operatorname{sgn}(p_d\,p_i),
    \]
    and under the joint sign flip $(p_d, p_i) \to (-p_d, -p_i)$ the
    path-view matrix transforms by orthogonal conjugation,
    \[
        \pathview{}(-p_d,\,-p_i) \;=\; D\,\pathview{}(p_d,\,p_i)\,D,
        \qquad D = \operatorname{diag}(1,-1),
    \]
    so $\det$, both singular values, $\condnum{}$, $\cohratio{}$,
    $\modeangle{}$, and $\dampedweight{e}$ are invariant under the flip.
    The flip is detected only by the stored slice's marginal row and column
    ($\fpm{p_d}$, $\fpm{p_i}$), which the path view drops and the Frobenius
    norm squares away.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    Every off-corner path-view entry is a positive floor times
    $\fpm{\cdot}$ of a product carrying $\operatorname{sgn}(p_ip_d)$,
    $\operatorname{sgn}(p_i)\operatorname{sgn}(p_d)$, or their swap; the
    corner is $\fpl{\cdot} > 0$. The diagonal product $ad$ carries
    $\operatorname{sgn}(p_ip_d)$ and dominates $f^2bc$ at every floor
    $f \in \set{1, \halffloor, \bleedparam}$ exactly as in
    \zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}, giving the sign identity.
    For the conjugation: $\fpm{}$ is odd and $\fpl{}$ even in its
    argument, so the flip negates exactly the off-diagonal entries of
    $\pathview{}$ --- entrywise $D M D$. Orthogonal conjugation preserves
    singular values and determinant; the mode-angle ratio
    $|U_{10}/U_{00}|$ is $D$-invariant.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Sign Semantics: Coherence Bit, Not Favor Bit]
    \label{rem:graph:sign-semantics}
    The Quadrant Law is Heider's product rule at parameter scale, and it
    is one $\mathbb{Z}_2$ law at three scales: parameter product within an
    edge, leg product within a hyper-edge
    (\zcref{thm:graph:hyper-edge-reduction}), parity product along a path
    (\zcref{cor:graph:path-parity-sign}). Consequently $(-1,-1)$ is
    \emph{gauge-equivalent} to $(+1,+1)$ for coherence consumers:
    shared aversion is tribal bonding, and both quadrants route and
    rank identically where the consumer is attention, surfacing, or
    object-mediated resonance.  They do \emph{not} carry the same
    endorsement meaning.
    Endorsement is a stance consumer, so an actor-directed record enters
    the standing projection only when it satisfies the Vouch
    Predicate (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}).  Coherent condemnation
    $(-1,-1)$ is therefore a strong coherent signal, but not a vouch.
    Three consequences are normative. \emph{First},
    $\detsign{}$ is a coherence bit, never a favor bit: what it records is
    whether the sentiment map preserves orientation, not whether the
    author approves. For the edge-type-level listing of which types are
    structurally forced to $\detsign{} = +1$ and which admit $\pm 1$,
    see \zcref{tbl:nodes:archetype-fingerprints}. \emph{Second},
    indifference is magnitude, not sign:
    ``I do not care'' is $p_i = 0$, which is routing-inert
    (\zcref{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy}) --- the graph forgets
    what its authors do not care about, structurally. A Layer-2 client
    that encodes ``dislike and dismiss'' as $(-1,-1)$ instead of
    $(-1, 0)$ makes its user \emph{maximally endorse} along that edge;
    the mapping rule for any interface is: valence is the sign, caring is
    the magnitude, indifference is zero. \emph{Third}, the stance itself
    is never lost: it survives in the marginal row of the stored slice,
    in cross-author aggregation (\zcref{def:graph:aggregated-sentiment},
    where opposed crowds cancel), in per-author netting
    (\zcref{def:epoch:net-stance}), in the Vouch Predicate that gates
    actor-directed endorsement (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}), and
    in the stance conjunction of commercial reputation
    (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation}), all of which read the
    $D$-odd component the routing gauge cannot see.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Augmented Relevance Tensor}
\label{subsec:graph:augmented-tensor}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Augmented Relevance Tensor]
    \label{def:graph:augmented-tensor}
    The Frobenius norm factorizes:
    $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_e}_F
    = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F \cdot \sqrt{1 + \tau_e^2}$.
    \begin{equation}
        \symbf{\symcal{T}}_e
        = \symbf{\Psi}_e \boxtimes
          \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ \tau_e \end{pmatrix}
        \in \R^{3 \times 3 \times 2}.
        \label{eq:graph:augmented-tensor}
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Maturity Amplification]
    \label{thm:graph:maturity-amplification}
    The factor $\sqrt{1 + \tau_e^2}$ ranges from $1$ (no maturity)
    to $\sqrt{2}$ (maximal), amplifying the scalar edge weight
    monotonically in $\tau_e$.
    \proofsketch{$\partial/\partial\tau > 0$ for $\tau > 0$.}
\end{theorem}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Path Composition and Scoring}
\label{subsec:graph:path-composition}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

% ─── Path matrix ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

All singular values in this subsection refer to the $2 \times 2$
path-view matrices $\pathview{e}$ and their products, not to the
stored $3 \times 3$ slice.

\paragraph{Path matrix.}

\begin{definition}[Path Matrix]
    \label{def:graph:path-matrix}
    For a directed raw snapshot path $p = (e_1, \ldots, e_d)$
    (\zcref{def:graph:raw-snapshot-path}):
    \begin{equation}
        \pathmatrix{p}
        = \pathview{e_1} \cdot \pathview{e_2}
          \cdots \pathview{e_d}
        \in \R^{2 \times 2}.
        \label{eq:graph:path-matrix}
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}

\paragraph{Composition semantics.}
Write
$A = \pathview{e_1}
= \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} A_{00} & A_{01} \\
  A_{10} & A_{11} \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and
$B = \pathview{e_2}
= \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} B_{00} & B_{01} \\
  B_{10} & B_{11} \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.
Each entry of the two-edge product $AB$ combines self-reinforcement
and cross-coupling:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}c l l@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Entry} & \textbf{Terms} & \textbf{Question} \\
    \midrule
    $(AB)_{00}$ & $A_{00}B_{00} + A_{01}B_{10}$
        & Does consensus persist? \\
    $(AB)_{01}$ & $A_{00}B_{01} + A_{01}B_{11}$
        & Does approval broaden? \\
    $(AB)_{10}$ & $A_{10}B_{00} + A_{11}B_{10}$
        & Does energy organize? \\
    $(AB)_{11}$ & $A_{10}B_{01} + A_{11}B_{11}$
        & Does intensity sustain? \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

% ─── Composition laws ────────────────────────────────────────────────

\paragraph{Composition laws.}

\begin{proposition}[Polarization Self-Reinforcement]
    \label{prop:graph:polarization-self-reinforcement}
    Write $m_\ell = (\pathview{e_\ell})_{11}$ (the polarization entry,
    satisfying $m_\ell \geq 0.5$ by the Polarization Floor),
    $k_1 = (\pathview{e_1})_{10}$ (engagement buzz of the first edge),
    and $j_2 = (\pathview{e_2})_{01}$ (popularity of the second edge),
    so that $(\pathmatrix{})_{11} = m_1 m_2 + k_1 j_2$.  When
    $k_1 j_2 \geq 0$, $(\pathmatrix{})_{11} \geq m_1 m_2 \geq 0.25$.
    The condition $k_1 j_2 \geq 0$ holds whenever the first edge's
    directional parameter $p_d^{(1)}$ and the second edge's intensity
    parameter $p_i^{(2)}$ share a sign, since
    $\operatorname{sgn}(k_1) = \operatorname{sgn}(p_d^{(1)})$ and
    $\operatorname{sgn}(j_2) = \operatorname{sgn}(p_i^{(2)})$.
    The cross term is negative only when the two edges carry
    opposite-signed engagement and popularity, in which case the
    $0.25$ floor need not hold.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[SVD Composition Bounds]
    \label{thm:graph:svd-composition-bounds}
    For $\pathmatrix{} = AB$, writing singular values of the
    $2 \times 2$ path-view matrices:
    $\svdone{AB} \leq \svdone{A}\svdone{B}$
    (submultiplicative)
    and
    $\svdtwo{AB} \geq \svdtwo{A}\svdtwo{B}$
    (supermultiplicative).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    \emph{Submultiplicativity.}
    Standard\footcite[\S2.3]{golub2013matrix}: $\svdone{AB}
    = \max_{\norm{x}=1}\norm{ABx}
    \leq \svdone{A}\max_{\norm{x}=1}\norm{Bx}
    = \svdone{A}\svdone{B}$.

    \emph{Supermultiplicativity.}
    $|\det(AB)| = |\det A|\,|\det B|
    = \svdone{A}\svdtwo{A}\svdone{B}\svdtwo{B}$.
    Since $\svdone{AB}\svdtwo{AB} = |\det(AB)|$ and
    $\svdone{AB} \leq \svdone{A}\svdone{B}$:
    \[
        \svdtwo{AB}
        = \frac{|\det(AB)|}{\svdone{AB}}
        \geq \frac{\svdone{A}\svdtwo{A}\svdone{B}\svdtwo{B}}
                  {\svdone{A}\svdone{B}}
        = \svdtwo{A}\svdtwo{B}. \qedhere
    \]
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Determinant Product]
    \label{thm:graph:determinant-product}
    $\det(\pathmatrix{p}) = \prod_{e \in p} \det(\pathview{e})$.
    This identity is the foundation of two independent mechanisms:
    Dijkstra-compatible scoring\footcite{dijkstra1959note} at
    $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:svd-path-score}), and the raw path parity product
    $\detsign{p} = \prod_{e \in p} \detsign{e}$
    (\zcref{cor:graph:path-parity-sign}) used by the raw signed
    double-cover service (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}) and by any
    complete-act validation that consumes raw leg parity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Condition Number Submultiplicativity]
    \label{cor:graph:condition-number-submultiplicativity}
    $\condnum{\pathmatrix{p}}
    \leq \prod_e \condnum{\pathview{e}}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Order Sensitivity]
    \label{rem:graph:order-sensitivity}
    Path matrix composition $\pathmatrix{p} = \prod_e \pathview{e}$
    is order-sensitive.  By \zcref{thm:graph:determinant-product},
    $\det(\pathmatrix{p}) = \prod_e \det(\pathview{e})$ is
    order-\emph{in}dependent (and so is any function of $|\det|$).
    Therefore: path scoring at $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$ and the
    parity sign $\detsign{p}$ depend only on the edge set (with
    causal validity, \zcref{ax:graph:act-causality}), while
    $\cohratio{}$, $\modeangle{}$
    (\zcref{subsec:graph:path-diagnostics-and-archetypes}), and
    scoring at $\divpref \neq \tfrac{1}{2}$ are order-sensitive.
    The causal ordering axiom (\zcref{ax:graph:act-causality})
    uniquely determines composition order among viable paths.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Ordered-Replay Determinism]
    \label{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}
    Fix the finalized authoritative order $\actsequence{k}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}) and the published constants.
    Then $\acttime{\actof{e}}$, $\tau_e$, $\dampedweight{e}$, $\detsign{e}$, every path
    parity $\detsign{p}$, the SVD score $\svdscore{p}$ at
    $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$, the path distance $d(\cdot,\cdot)$, the relevance
    score $S(u,c)$, and every CAN value $\canval{n}$ are functions of $\actsequence{k}$ and
    the constants alone: every participant holding the same ordered history
    reproduces them identically. None references $\logpos{e}$, and no quantity
    reads any host discretion beyond the order $\actsequence{k}$ itself.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    $\acttime{q}$ is the act's position in $\actsequence{k}$; $\tau_e$ reads endpoint-incidence
    pre-degree from the graph state immediately before the act in that order
    (\zcref{rem:graph:act-time-not-wall-clock}); hence $\dampedweight{e}$, a
    function of edge parameters and $\tau_e$
    (\zcref{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight}), is determined by $\actsequence{k}$.
    By \zcref{thm:graph:determinant-product} and
    \zcref{rem:graph:order-sensitivity}, $|\det \pathmatrix{p}|$ and
    $\detsign{p} = \prod_{e\in p}\detsign{e}$ depend only on the edges
    of $p$ with causal validity, not on composition order; at
    $\divpref=\tfrac12$ the score factorizes per edge
    (\zcref{eq:graph:half-score}), so $\svdscore{p}$, $d$, and $S$ are
    products, sums, minima, or maxima over authoritative-order chains. A
    Dijkstra/BFS traversal yields the same optimal values regardless of
    the order in which equally ranked nodes are visited. The CAN
    operates atemporally on the CompGraph induced by $E_k$
    (\zcref{def:can:base-value}), with no temporal or positional input.
    No quantity references $\logpos{e}$.
\end{proof}

% ─── Path parity sign ────────────────────────────────────────────────

\paragraph{Path parity sign.}

\begin{corollary}[Path Parity Sign]
    \label{cor:graph:path-parity-sign}
    For any viable path $p = (e_1, \ldots, e_d)$:
    \begin{equation}
        \detsign{p}
        \coloneqq \prod_{e \in p} \detsign{e}
        = \operatorname{sgn}(\det(\pathmatrix{p})).
        \label{eq:graph:path-parity-sign}
    \end{equation}
    This follows directly from
    \zcref{thm:graph:determinant-product} and requires no new proof.
    $\detsign{p}$ is a parity bit, computable as a running product
    at $O(1)$ per edge with no path-matrix accumulation.  A path is
    \textbf{positive} if $\detsign{p} = +1$; \textbf{negative} if
    $\detsign{p} = -1$.
\end{corollary}

A path with $\detsign{p} = -1$ carries a net orientation inversion:%
\necessityref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}
the sentiment signal arriving at the target is structurally inverted
relative to the source.  The magnitude $|\det \pathmatrix{p}|^{1/2}$
may be large --- measuring strong directional coherence --- while the
sign records that the coherence has been inverted an odd number of
times.  The raw parity register prevents a raw signed consumer from
treating an orientation-inverted path as positive evidence.  Standing
adds stronger requirements: complete-act ownership and the closed
person-vouch census.

% ─── SVD path score ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

\paragraph{SVD path score and the $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$ collapse.}

\begin{definition}[SVD Path Score]
    \label{def:graph:svd-path-score}
    At diversity preference $\divpref \in [0,1]$, writing singular
    values of the $2 \times 2$ path-view path matrix:
    \begin{equation}
        \svdscore{p}
        = \svdone{\pathmatrix{p}}^{1-\divpref}
          \cdot \svdtwo{\pathmatrix{p}}^{\divpref}
          \cdot \prod_{e \in p} \sqrt{1+\tau_e^2}
          \cdot \prod_{e \in p} \boltzfactor{\tentropy{e}}.
        \label{eq:graph:svd-path-score}
