Bid/T naming an existing Offer would give that Offer inbound incidence from a
second Item --- inert in the settlement fold, which resolves by Bid act
identifier, but perfectly live in raw traversal, in CAN, and in any sentiment
fold admitting Bid.  Inertness in one fold is not inertness.  Revising an
offer means authoring a new one.

Formation cannot check more than this.  It is class-syntactic and stateless
apart from act-identifier freshness, so it can decide \emph{fresh mint or
existing} and cannot decide \emph{existing and consistent with that node's
genesis} --- the latter needs a lookup against other records.  A Review/T
update whose A-leg names a different context is therefore well-formed, and
the discrepancy is left to the fold that reads it.

Offer is the sole non-Taggable passive type, by decision rather than
residue: a settlement artifact does not belong in the semantic taxonomy,
and its incidence structure is deliberately special
(\zcref{subsec:graph:settlement-lifecycle}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Active Node}
\label{subsec:nodes:active-node}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Actor}{actor}
The sole active node type ($n_a \in V_u$). Originates all edges,
injects all temporality primitives, and is the exclusive reward
recipient within any guild. Each Actor's standing $\standing{i}$ is the
Layer~1 comparator value published at each epoch boundary
(\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}).
\networkref{subsec:introduction:comparator-previewed}%
Raw records do not carry standing directly.  The epoch compiler first
derives the actor-only, initiator-owned person-vouch projection from
the closed census of \zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}; standing
then reads the final safe source-target flow produced by that
projection.

The Actor's derived Self-edge bond remains available to raw graph
consumers: $\standing{i}$ enters the bond tensor (shared by both
components) via $\bondkernel{i} = \standing{i}/(\numeraire+\standing{i})$
and does not determine which computational interface (\PathView{} or
\AttrView{}) is used.  For standing, the bond's analytic core supplies
the target activation attached to every projected person-vouch edge;
neither Declaration nor Reputation is independently a projected vouch.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_a) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Profile}_a
                   \xrightarrow{\text{Self (Rep., derived)}} n_a,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Accept}} n_a,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Ratify}} n_a} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_a \to \text{Passive (all leaf types)},\;
                n_a \xrightarrow{\text{Registration, Publish}}
                \text{Profile}, \text{Content},\; \\
                     & \phantom{\set{}}\;
                n_a \xrightarrow{\text{Join Request, Invitation/A}}
                \text{Chat},\; \\
                     & \phantom{\set{}}\;
                        n_a \xrightarrow{\text{Leave, De-invite/A}}
                        \text{Chat},\;
                        n_a \xrightarrow{\text{Accept}} \text{Actor},\;
                        n_a \xrightarrow{\text{Ratify}} \text{Actor},\;
                        n_a \xrightarrow{\text{Withdraw, Rescind}}
                        \text{Offer}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:actor}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} Outgoing edges contribute to path
          scoring. Six edge types originating from Actors are
          promoted to \tierfull{} under the mask rationalization
          (\zcref{def:graph:mask-promotion-criterion}).
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} Outgoing edges contribute to CAN
          base values via $3 \times 3$ Frobenius norms.
        \item \textbf{Self-edge bond:} Binds the Actor to their Profile
            through derived Declaration (Actor~$i \to$ Profile$_i$) and
            Reputation (Profile$_i \to$ Actor~$i$) components with shared
            intensity $\bondkernel{i} = \standing{i}/(\numeraire+\standing{i})$,
            derived from the epoch certificate at each boundary
            (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}); never appended.  Both
            remain \tierfull{} Identity edges for raw graph consumers.
            In standing, neither component is a projected vouch; the
            bond's analytic core supplies the target activation of
            projected person-vouch edges
            (\zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).
                \item \textbf{Participation:} An actor's record is writable under the
                    two-gate rule: solvency $\burnbal{i}\ge\safethresh$ (W1,
                    continuous), individual stamp $\actstamp{}\ge\safefloor$ (W2a,
                    boundary-frozen), and epoch door $\epochstamp{}\ge\partfloor$ (W2b)
                    (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}). All are independently derivable from
                    public Layer~1 data.
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{remark}[Anchoring and Relational Support]
    \label{rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support}
    An Actor receives a standing coordinate only when its Registration
    anchor is present in the completed accepted or tentative epoch set.

    The wall-clamped activation does not create source.  If every source
    rate reaching an anchored Actor is zero, the final standing mediant
    remains zero.  A positive-rate external source may support the Actor
    through a complete person-vouch under the ordinary source-rate hull
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).

    Registration, source burn, incoming vouches, and the resulting
    standing may all belong to one completed epoch state.  The standing
    calculation interprets that final state once at closure.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Leaf Passive Nodes}
\label{subsec:nodes:leaf-passive-nodes}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Profile}{profile}
Passive identity anchor ($n_p \in V_c$), uniquely bound to one
Actor via Registration and the derived Self-edge bond. Implements \textbf{Taggable} and
\textbf{Reviewable}. Its passive-sourced \ActionGraph{} edges are the
derived Reputation component directed to its owning Actor and
author-fixed Tag/T and Review/T terminal legs.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_p) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Registration}} n_p,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Self (Dec., derived)}} n_p,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}} n_p,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/A, Review/A}} n_p,\;
                       \text{Chat}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Invitation/T, De-invite/T}} n_p,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_p,\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_p} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_p
                        \xrightarrow{\text{Self (Rep., derived)}}
                        \text{Actor},\;
                        n_p \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} \text{Type},\;
                        n_p \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment},\;
                        n_p \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:profile}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} Self-edge bond components are \tierfull{}
            (Identity mask). Incoming Opinions (Tribal, \tierfull{})
            strengthen the Profile as a routing element.
        \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} The Declaration component's
            $3 \times 3$ norm captures standing-derived intensity
            and marginal directional signal; the Reputation component
            is excluded from the \CompGraph{}.
        \item \textbf{Raw routing and standing target:} Positive incoming
            sentiment affects raw feed and raw signed traversal through
            the existing path-view determinants.  The derived Reputation
            component continues to enable the profile-bridged \emph{feed}
            discovery path
            (\zcref{def:nodes:profile-bridged-discovery-path}); a Profile
            used as a Tag, Review, or Reference middle node additionally
            sources the corresponding terminal leg
            (\zcref{lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).

            Standing does not traverse the raw Profile$\to$Actor
            Reputation edge.  A standing-designated complete act whose
            semantic target is Profile$_i$ compiles directly to
            Actor~$i$ and receives Actor~$i$'s projected target
            activation.  The Profile therefore identifies the
            person-directed target without becoming an intermediate
            standing vertex.
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Content}{content}
Primary digital artifact ($n_c \in V_c$). Implements
\textbf{Taggable} and \textbf{Reviewable}.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_c) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Publish}} n_c,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}} n_c,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/A, Review/A}} n_c,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_c,\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_c} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_c \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} \text{Type},\;
                        n_c \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment},\;
                        n_c \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:content}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} Incoming Opinions are Tribal,
          \tierfull{}. Polarization Floor
          (\zcref{prop:graph:polarization-floor}) guarantees
          $\Psi^{11} \geq 0.5$. High-$m$ content shortens paths
          terminating at it.
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} Baseline entry $\Psi^{22}
          \numrel{const.graph.fpl_baseline.num}$ provides the non-vanishing floor.
        \item \textbf{Scalar:} Aggregate $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F$
            enters the relevance score as the content quality factor,
            standing-amplified by $\ampfactor{\mathrm{creator}(c)}$
          (\zcref{def:sorting:relevance-score}).
                \item \textbf{Genesis:} the Publish record mints the node and
                        fixes $\operatorname{creator}(n_c)$
                        (\zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}).
        \item \textbf{Outgoing legs:} As a Taggable and Reviewable middle
            node, Content sources author-fixed Tag/T (to Type), Review/T (to
            Comment), and Reference/T (to any passive target) legs
            (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Item}{item}
Ownable entity ($n_i \in V_c$). Implements \textbf{Taggable},
\textbf{Reviewable}, and \textbf{Ownable}.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_i) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Owner}} n_i,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}} n_i,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/A, Review/A, Bid/A}}
                       n_i,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_i,\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_i} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_i \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} \text{Type},\;
                        n_i \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment},\;
                        n_i \xrightarrow{\text{Bid/T}} \text{Offer},\;
                        n_i \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:item}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{} ($\uparrow$):} Owner edge promoted to
          full mask, moving from \tiermarginal{} to \tierfull{} ($\sqrt{|\det|}$:
          $\numval{result.owner_econ.detscore.num} \to \numval{result.e8.detscore.num}$, a $\numval{result.promotion.ratio.num}\times$ gain). Items are
          first-class path-routing elements.
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} Owner edge's $3 \times 3$ norm
          enhanced by marginal row capturing $p_d = a$.
    \item \textbf{Ownership lifecycle:} Items in sparse graph regions
          are natural advertising targets; their path-routing weight
          scales with the owner's standing via the Self-edge bond.
        \item \textbf{Outgoing legs:} As a Taggable, Reviewable, and Ownable
            middle node, Item sources author-fixed Tag/T, Review/T, Bid/T (to
            Offer), and Reference/T legs
            (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Type}{type}
Semantic anchor representing a concept ($n_t \in V_c$). Implements
\textbf{Taggable} and \textbf{Reviewable}.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_t) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Affinity}} n_t,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}} n_t,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/A, Review/A}} n_t,\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} n_t,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_t,\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_t} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_t \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} \text{Type},\;
                        n_t \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment},\;
                        n_t \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:type}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{} (\tiermarginal{}):} Reached primarily through
          Epistemic edges. The $\sim\!5\times$ tier gap makes Type
          nodes weak routing elements.
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{} (equalized):} $3 \times 3$ norms are
          comparable to \tierfull{} edges. CAN treats Tag-to-Type
          compositions equitably across edge-type tiers.
        \item \textbf{Outgoing legs:} As a Taggable and Reviewable middle
            node, Type sources author-fixed Tag/T (to Type), Review/T (to
            Comment), and Reference/T (to any passive target) legs
            (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
        \item \textbf{Contestable taxonomy:} Reviews of a Type give
            definitional disputes an authored, attributed, immutable
            anchor; a Review binds no tag and alters no Type semantics
            (\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Chat}{chat}
Structural container for conversations ($n_{\mathrm{chat}} \in V_c$).
Implements \textbf{Conversational}, \textbf{Taggable}, and
\textbf{Reviewable}.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_{\mathrm{chat}}) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Participant/A}}
                       n_{\mathrm{chat}},\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}}
                       n_{\mathrm{chat}},\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Join Request, Leave, Send/A, Tag/A, Review/A}}
                       n_{\mathrm{chat}},\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Invitation/A, De-invite/A}}
                       n_{\mathrm{chat}},\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_{\mathrm{chat}},\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_{\mathrm{chat}}} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_{\mathrm{chat}}
                        \xrightarrow{\text{Invitation/T}} \text{Profile},\;
                        n_{\mathrm{chat}}
                        \xrightarrow{\text{De-invite/T}} \text{Profile},\;
                        n_{\mathrm{chat}}
                        \xrightarrow{\text{Send/T}} \text{Message},\;
                        n_{\mathrm{chat}}
                        \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} \text{Type},\;
                        n_{\mathrm{chat}}
                        \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment},\;
                        n_{\mathrm{chat}}
                        \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target},\;
                        n_{\mathrm{chat}}
                        \xrightarrow{\text{Participant/T}} \text{Chat}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:chat}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{} ($\uparrow$):} Participant edge promoted
          to full mask (\tiermarginal{} $\to$ \tierfull{}). Chat participation
          carries the same path-view richness as an Opinion.
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} Participant norms comparable to
          Opinion norms. CAN values conversational participation
          equitably.
        \item \textbf{Genesis:} the founding actor's Participant record
            mints the Chat (\zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}).
                \item \textbf{Outgoing legs:} As a Conversational, Taggable, and
                    Reviewable middle node, Chat sources author-fixed
                    Invitation/T, De-invite/T, Tag/T, Review/T, and
                    Send/T (to Message), and Reference/T legs
            (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
        \item \textbf{Review vs.\ Send:} a Send speaks \emph{inside} the channel;
            a Review annotates it from \emph{outside} --- at the conversation
            (Chat) or, Messages being Reviewable, at the specific utterance
            (\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Hyper-Leaf Passive Nodes}
\label{subsec:nodes:hyper-leaf-passive-nodes}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Hyper-leaf nodes are created by hyper-edge decomposition
(\zcref{thm:graph:hyper-edge-reduction}). Both legs contribute to
path scoring (determinants and parity signs multiply) and CAN
attribution (independent base values, $\redundancy{} = 1$).

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Comment}{comment}
Contextual annotation created via a Review hyper-edge
($n_{co} \in V_c$). Implements \textbf{Taggable} and \textbf{Reviewable}.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_{co}) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} n_{co},\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}} n_{co},\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/A, Review/A}} n_{co},\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_{co},\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_{co}} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_{co} \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} \text{Type},\;
                        n_{co} \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment}',\;
                        n_{co} \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:comment}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{} (cross-tier):} Review/A
          (Actor $\to$ Passive) is Tribal, \tierfull{}. Review/T
          (Passive $\to$ Comment) is Epistemic, \tiermarginal{}. The weak T-leg
          creates a path bottleneck.
    \item \textbf{Independent growth:} Subsequent Opinions (\tierfull{})
          build the Comment's own routing weight.
        \item \textbf{Outgoing legs:} As a Taggable and Reviewable middle node,
            Comment sources author-fixed Tag/T (to Type), Review/T (to
            Comment), and Reference/T (to any passive target) legs
            (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{remark}[Nested Comment Review]
    \label{rem:nodes:nested-comment-review}
    Because Comment is Reviewable, a Review may target an existing Comment
    and create a fresh Comment as its contextual response: the reviewed
    Comment sources the author-fixed Review/T leg to the new node.
    Under universal Reviewable the same chains may originate at any passive
    middle node, including Type and Message; depth remains bounded in
    traversal by $L$ and damped identically. This is
    a causal chain of new records, not a passive self-loop; chain depth is
    bounded in traversal by $L$ and damped by \tiermarginal{} compounding
    and CAN transmission decay.
\end{remark}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Message}{message}
Discrete communicative act within a Chat, created via a Send
hyper-edge ($n_m \in V_c$). Implements \textbf{Taggable} and \textbf{Reviewable}.

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_m) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Chat}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Send/T}} n_m,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}} n_m,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/A, Review/A}} n_m,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_m,\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_m} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_m \xrightarrow{\text{Tag/T}} \text{Type},\;
                        n_m \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment},\;
                        n_m \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:message}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{} (cross-tier, A-leg promoted):} Send/A
          (Actor $\to$ Chat) promoted to \tierfull{}. Send/T
          (Chat $\to$ Message) is Minimal, \tiermarginal{}. The Message is
          reached via the sparsest path-view profile; richer semantics
          emerge from subsequent engagement.
        \item \textbf{Outgoing legs:} As a Taggable and Reviewable middle
            node, Message sources author-fixed Tag/T (to Type), Review/T (to
            Comment), and Reference/T (to any passive target) legs
            (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
        \item \textbf{Review vs.\ Send:} a Send speaks \emph{inside} the channel;
            a Review annotates it from \emph{outside} --- at the conversation
            (Chat) or, Messages being Reviewable, at the specific utterance
            (\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{node}{Offer}{offer}
Monetarily significant proposal created via a Bid hyper-edge
($n_o \in V_c$).

\begin{equation}
    \text{Connectivity}(n_o) =
    \begin{cases}
        \text{In: }  & \set{\text{Item}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Bid/T}} n_o,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Opinion}} n_o,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Review/A}} n_o,\; \\
                     & \phantom{\set{}}\;
                       \text{Actor}_{\mathrm{buyer}}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Withdraw}} n_o,\;
                       \text{Actor}_{\mathrm{seller}}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Rescind}} n_o,\;
                       \text{Actor}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/A}} n_o,\;
                       \text{Passive}
                       \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} n_o} \\
        \text{Out: } & \set{n_o \xrightarrow{\text{Review/T}} \text{Comment},\;
                        n_o \xrightarrow{\text{Reference/T}} \text{Target}}
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:nodes:connectivity:offer}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{} (lifecycle):} The Bid/T creation leg is a
          full-block leg routed at the \tierhalf{} tier under signed
          generosity (\zcref{def:graph:proposal-half-tier}). The Offer's path weight evolves
          across the settlement lifecycle
          (\zcref{subsec:graph:settlement-lifecycle}): created at the Bid,
          settled at a title-transferring certificate, cancellable by Withdraw
          or Rescind before boundary finality.
\end{itemize}
Offer implements \textbf{Reviewable}: it sources author-fixed
Review/T legs to Comments, which are commentary and never
settlement state (\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}).  The settlement Accept and
Ratify edges \emph{reference} the Offer via their
\texttt{settles}-pointers but are not incident to it
(\zcref{subsec:graph:settlement-lifecycle}); only the Bid/T creation leg
and the Withdraw/Rescind cancels are graph-incident to the Offer.
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Outgoing legs:} Offer additionally sources author-fixed
          Reference/T legs (\zcref{lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Binary Edges}
\label{subsec:nodes:binary-edges}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Each edge specification shows domain, mask, promotion status, tier,
parameter roles, the stored $3 \times 3$ matrix, and the path-view
$2 \times 2$ extraction. For promoted edges with full mask, the
path-view is the unmodified upper-left $2 \times 2$.

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Let $p = \standing{j}/(\numeraire+\standing{j}) \in (0,1)$ be the shared
intensity parameter (equivalently $p=\refstanding{j}/(1+\refstanding{j})$),
derived from Actor~$j$'s standing published
by Layer~1 at the current epoch boundary
(\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}), and let $p_d = 1$. Domain:
Identity $(\symcal{D}_I)$. Mask: $(1,0,0,1)$. Tier: 1.

\paragraph{Stored $3 \times 3$ for both components.}
\begin{equation}
    \symbf{\Psi}
    =
    \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{p} & 0 & \fpm{p} \\[6pt]
        0       & \fpl{p} & \fpl{p} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{1} & \fpl{1} & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-stored}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Path-view $2 \times 2$ for both components.}
Applying $\bleedparam$-softening to mask $(1,0,0,1)$ gives softened
mask $(1,\bleedparam,\bleedparam,1)$:
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{}
    =
    \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{p}
            & \bleedparam\cdot\fpm{p} \\[6pt]
        \bleedparam\cdot\fpm{p}
            & \fpl{p}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-pathview}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Determinant and detscore.}
For $p > 0$, $\fpm{p} = \clampsigmoid{p}\tanh(p)$ and
$\fpl{p} = \clampsigmoid{p}$:
\begin{align}
    \det(\pathview{})
    &= \fpm{p}\bigl(\fpl{p} - \bleedparam^2\fpm{p}\bigr)
    \notag \\
    &= \clampsigmoid{p}^2
       \tanh(p)
       \bigl(1 - \bleedparam^2\tanh(p)\bigr)
    \label{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-det} \\[4pt]
    \detscore{e}
    &= \clampsigmoid{p}\,
       \sqrt{\tanh(p)\bigl(1-\bleedparam^2\tanh(p)\bigr)}
    \label{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-detscore}
\end{align}

\paragraph{Determinant sign.}
For all $p > 0$: $\tanh(p) > 0$ and
$1 - \bleedparam^2\tanh(p) > 0$ (since
$\bleedparam^2 = 0.0025 \ll 1$), so:
\begin{equation}
    \detsign{e_{\mathrm{Dec}}}
    = \detsign{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}
    = +1
    \qquad \forall\; \standing{j} > 0.
    \label{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-parities}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Damped weight.}
\begin{equation}
    \dampedweight{e}
    = \clampsigmoid{p}\,
      \sqrt{\tanh(p)\bigl(1-\bleedparam^2\tanh(p)\bigr)}
      \cdot \sqrt{1+\tau_e^2}
      \cdot \boltzfactor{\tentropy{e}}
    \label{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-dampedweight}
\end{equation}
At $\standing{j} = 0$: $p = 0$, $\tanh(0) = 0$,
$\dampedweight{e} = 0$. The bond is inert.

\paragraph{Attribution View.}
$\baseval{e_{\mathrm{Dec}}} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F$. At reference
parameters ($\standing{} = \numval{fixture.seed.alice_rate.num}$, $p = \numval{fixture.e1.indirect.exact}$):
$\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \numrel{result.e1.frobenius.num}$, consistent with
\zcref{tbl:verification:reference-edges} row~$e_1$.

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}%
    {Self-Edge Bond --- Declaration Component}%
    {self-declaration}
The Declaration component is the Actor-to-Profile leg of the
Self-edge bond, carrying the shared intensity parameter
$p_i = \standing{j}/(\numeraire+\standing{j})$ and directional parameter
$p_d = 1$.  It is derived from the epoch certificate at each boundary
(\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}); never appended.

\textbf{Domain:} Identity ($\symcal{D}_I$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{CG:} \okmark\ (CAN leaf, Rule~1). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = 1$,\;
$p_i = \standing{j}/(\numeraire+\standing{j})$.
\networkref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}%

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} \tierfull{};
          $\detscore{} \numrel{result.e1.detscore.num}$ at reference parameters;
          $\detsign{} = +1$ for all $\standing{j} > 0$
          (\zcref{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-parities}).
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} CAN leaf;
          $\baseval{e_{\mathrm{Dec}}} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F$.
    \item \textbf{Tensor:}
          \zcref{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-stored,%
          eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-pathview}.
    \item \textbf{Standing:} none, and for the one reason that still
          licenses that answer: Declaration is a \emph{derived} raw
          traversal edge, not an authored act, so there is no act to weigh
          (\zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  It is the
          authored Self-edge components that are weighed, each in its own
          right.
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}%
    {Self-Edge Bond --- Reputation Component}%
    {self-reputation}
The Reputation component shares the stored tensor,
path-view extraction, $\detscore{}$, and damped weight formula with the
Declaration component
(\zcref{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-stored,%
eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-pathview,%
eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-detscore,%
eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-dampedweight}) and is distinguished entirely by
direction and graph participation.

\textbf{Domain:} Identity ($\symcal{D}_I$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{CG:} \texttimes\ (excluded, Rule~3 of
\zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = 1$,\;
$p_i = \standing{j}/(\numeraire+\standing{j})$.
\networkref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}%

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\ActionGraph{}:}
            derived passive-sourced edge, distinct from any
            author-fixed hyper-edge terminal legs sourced at
            $\mathrm{Profile}_j$ and permitted by
            \zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}.
    \item \textbf{Feed-Ranking BFS:}
          Traversed by \zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs} from
          $\mathrm{Profile}_j$ to $\mathrm{Actor}_j$. Enables the
          profile-bridged discovery path
          (\zcref{def:nodes:profile-bridged-discovery-path}).
        \item \textbf{\CompGraph{}:}
            Excluded by Rule~3 of \zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}.
            The Reputation component contributes no node to the \CompGraph{};
            Profile-sourced hyper-edge legs enter only as Rule~2 leg-leaves.
            No CAN base value is associated with the Reputation component.
    \item \textbf{Standing target activation:}
          Reputation is not independently traversed by standing and is
          not a projected vouch edge.  Its standing-dependent analytic
          core is transformed into the projected target activation
          attached once to every projected person-vouch terminating at
          the owning Actor (\zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  The
          raw Profile$\to$Actor edge remains available to feed and raw
          signed consumers, with $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}$
          determined by the \emph{target} actor's $\standing{}$.
        \item \textbf{Raw maturity channel:}
            repeated derivation ratchets $\tau_{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} \to 1^-$
            and continues to change the raw
            $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}$ used by feed and other raw
            graph consumers: at equal standing a mature bond outweighs a
            first-epoch bond by at most $\sqrt{2}/\numval{const.activation.g_half.num} \numrel{result.activation.maturity_ratio.num}\,\times$,
            capped by $\wmax$ and unable to restore a failed gate.
            Maturity and temporal entropy do not enter the projected
            standing activation; no $\tau$-ratchet is carried through
            standing (\zcref{rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support}).
    \item \textbf{Raw parity:}
          $\detsign{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} = +1$ for all
          $\standing{j} > 0$ (\zcref{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-parities}).
          This is a raw traversal property and grants no independent
          allocation.

\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Registration}{registration}
Actor's self-introduction; the \emph{anchoring record} of the grounded
pair (Actor, Profile) --- no node is minted
(\zcref{def:graph:registration}) --- and the root of the author's
act-identifier sequence (\zcref{def:graph:act-identifier}).  Parallel
Registrations update the
payload only; identifiers and key-binding never re-bind
(\zcref{rem:graph:profile-update}).
\textbf{Domain:} Identity ($\symcal{D}_I$). \quad \textbf{Mask:} $(1,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad \textbf{Params:} $p_d = 1$, $p_i = 1$ (fixed). \quad
$\detsign{} = +1$ (forced). \quad \textbf{CG:} \okmark\ (leaf).

\textbf{Standing:} resolves to self.  Registration anchors the grounded
Actor/Profile pair, and anchoring is not vouching
(\zcref{rem:graph:grounded-target-does-not-imply-allocation}) --- but it is an
accepted authored act, so it is weighed, and it is weighed home.  Registering
costs its author allocation like anything else they do.
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Publish}{publish}
Actor publishes to a Content node.  A Publish whose target is its own mint is
the genesis record, fixing $\operatorname{creator}$; a Publish naming an
existing Content mints nothing and leaves creator, comments, reactions and
references untouched (\zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}).
\textbf{Domain:} Economic ($\symcal{D}_X$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$ $\uparrow$ promoted. \quad \textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $a \in [-1,1]$ (attachment), $p_d = a$, $p_i = 1$ ---
mirroring Owner (\zcref{edge:nodes:owner}), including the row-collapse
note (\zcref{rem:nodes:row-collapse}). \quad
$\detsign{} = \pm 1$. \quad \textbf{CG:} \okmark\ (leaf).
License qualifiers are structural metadata of this record
(\zcref{def:graph:canonical-folds}).
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{definition}[Profile-Bridged Discovery Path]
    \label{def:nodes:profile-bridged-discovery-path}
    For actors $i \neq j$ where Actor~$i$ holds an Opinion edge to
    $\mathrm{Profile}_j$ and Actor~$j$ holds an Opinion edge to
    content~$c$, the \emph{profile-bridged discovery path} from
    Actor~$i$ to $c$ is:
    \[
        \mathrm{Actor}_i
        \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Opinion}}
        \mathrm{Profile}_j
        \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Reputation}}
        \mathrm{Actor}_j
        \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Opinion}}
        c
    \]
    with path weight:
    \begin{equation}
        W_{\mathrm{bridge}}
        =
        \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Op}_{i\to\mathrm{Prof}_j}}}
        \cdot
        \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}
        \cdot
        \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Op}_{j\to c}}}
        \label{eq:nodes:profile-bridged-weight}
    \end{equation}
    Since $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} < 1$ for all finite
    $\standing{j}$ and all $\tau \in [0,1)$
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-bound}), the
    profile-bridged path is always strictly weaker than a direct
    Opinion path at equal sentiment parameters.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Raw Profile-Bridge Amplification]
    \label{def:nodes:raw-profile-bridge-amplification}
    For content $c$ authored by Actor~$j$ reached via the
    profile-bridged path:
    \begin{equation}
                A(\refstanding{j})
                = \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}(\standing{j})
                    \cdot \ampfactor{j}
        \label{eq:nodes:commitment-amplification-product}
    \end{equation}
        $A$ is strictly increasing in $\refstanding{j}$: both factors are
        strictly increasing in $\refstanding{j}$
        (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity} and trivially for
        $\ampfactor{j}$). At $\standing{j} = 0$: $A = 0$.
\end{definition}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Opinion}{opinion}
Actor's sentiment toward a passive node. The archetypal edge.

\textbf{Domain:} Tribal ($\symcal{D}_T$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $p \in [-1,1]$ (polarity),
$r \in [-1,1]$ (reaction). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = p$, $p_i = r$.

\emph{Stored $3 \times 3$:}
\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_e
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{rp}   & \fpm{r|p|}  & \fpm{r}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|r|p} & \fpl{|r||p|} & \fpl{|r|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{p}    & \fpl{|p|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\emph{Path-view $2 \times 2$} (full mask, no softening):
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{rp}    & \fpm{r|p|}  \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|r|p}  & \fpl{|r||p|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:opinion}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Standing role.}
An Opinion allocates towards a person only when its semantic target is
Profile$_i$.  After the per-author bundle fold, an effective Opinion
whose mandatory coordinates are both strictly positive may compile into
one binary person-vouch authored by the Opinion author toward Actor~$i$
(\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  Every Opinion targeting
Content, Item, Type, Chat, Comment, Message, or Offer instead resolves to its
author, regardless of determinant sign or raw routing weight --- weighed,
priced, and dilutive of that author's outward shares
(\zcref{rem:epoch:artifact-activity-crowds-out-export}).  An opinion about a
thing is not free; it is simply not about a person.

The raw Opinion record remains unchanged for feed ranking, raw signed
traversal, payload carriage, and CAN.
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Affinity}{affinity}
Actor's affinity for a Type node. Relevance, not verdict.

\textbf{Domain:} Epistemic ($\symcal{D}_E$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,1,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Not promoted.} \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $a \in [-1,1]$ (association),
$t \in [-1,1]$ (attraction). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = a$, $p_i = t$.

\emph{Stored $3 \times 3$:}
\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_e
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        0          & \fpm{t|a|}   & \fpm{t}   \\[6pt]
        0          & \fpl{|t||a|} & \fpl{|t|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{a}    & \fpl{|a|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\emph{Path-view $2 \times 2$} (softened Epistemic:
$(.05, 1, .05, 1)$):
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        .05 \cdot \fpm{ta}   & \fpm{t|a|}   \\[6pt]
        .05 \cdot \fpm{|t|a} & \fpl{|t||a|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:affinity}
\end{equation}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Participant (hyper-edge)}{participant}
Actor's movement into a Chat: \textbf{A-leg whence, T-leg whither}.  One
meaning, four instantiations --- \emph{I move from $A$ to $T$}:
\[
\begin{array}{l|l|l}
    \text{case} & \text{A-leg (whence)} & \text{T-leg (whither)}\\
    \hline
    \text{found}           & \mathsf{mint}(\actid{q}) & \mathsf{mint}(\actid{q})\\
    \text{join}            & C_1                      & C_1\\
    \text{found successor} & C_0                      & \mathsf{mint}(\actid{q})\\
    \text{move}            & C_0                      & C_1
\end{array}
\]
Joining is moving from the chat one is joining; founding is moving from a chat
one simultaneously creates.  There is no shape branch to test and no field a
reader must consult to know what they are looking at, and the terminal target
alone decides whether the act mints
(\zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}).  $C_0=C_1$ with distinct legs is
malformed; origin is otherwise unchecked at formation, so a move from a chat
one was never in is a decorated join and the fold reads leg roles rather than
the origin claim.

This makes explicit something the binary form could not represent:
participation always had a provenance.  A binary edge could record only
arrival, so movement had to be reconstructed by a fold noticing two acts side
by side and guessing they were one gesture.  Uniformity makes provenance a
field with a value --- sometimes the trivial one.

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Chat).}
\textbf{Domain:} Relational ($\symcal{D}_R$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{$\uparrow$ Promoted} from $(0,0,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $i \in [-1,1]$ (interactivity),
$r \in [-1,1]$ (responsibility). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = i$, $p_i = r$.  These are the act's mandatory
coordinates (\zcref{rem:epoch:compiled-acts-fold-into-cells}).

\paragraph{T-leg (Chat $\to$ Chat).}
\textbf{Domain:} Epistemic ($\symcal{D}_E$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,1,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $c \in [0,1]$ (continuity), $p_d = c$, $p_i = 1$ type-fixed,
so $\detsign{}=+1$ is forced --- following Invitation/T, and required by
\zcref{lem:nodes:self-loop-neutral}.  The coordinate is authored and, in the
join and found cases, semantically vacuous; it is \emph{not} mandatory, so a
choice on a meaningless field never moves its author's coefficient.

\emph{Rationale:} Both parameters are signed directional quantities
--- interactivity can be enthusiastic or reluctant, responsibility
embraced or resisted.

\emph{Stored $3 \times 3$:}
\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_e
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{ri}   & \fpm{r|i|}   & \fpm{r}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|r|i} & \fpl{|r||i|} & \fpl{|r|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{i}    & \fpl{|i|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\emph{Path-view $2 \times 2$} (full promoted mask):
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{ri}   & \fpm{r|i|}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|r|i} & \fpl{|r||i|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:participant}
\end{equation}

\emph{Standing role:} resolves to self.  Participation is an enacted relation
to a Chat, not a person-vouch toward every Actor connected to it --- so the
act allocates to nobody but its author, and is weighed there at its A-leg
coefficient, in all four cases alike
(\zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  One act, one debit, one
action-count increment, one stamp, one authoritative time
(\zcref{cor:graph:hyper-act-indivisibility}), and one unit of the epoch act
budget however many projections it has
(\zcref{def:epoch:epoch-act-budget}).
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{lemma}[Self-Loop Traversal Neutrality]
    \label{lem:nodes:self-loop-neutral}
    Let $e_\circ$ be an edge projection with
    $\operatorname{src}(e_\circ)=\operatorname{tgt}(e_\circ)=v$ and
    $\detsign{e_\circ}=+1$.  Then no max-product register in any canonical raw
    traversal, and no additive log-cost shortest path, attains through a walk
    traversing $e_\circ$ a value it does not attain without it: every optimal
    bounded raw walk has an $e_\circ$-free representative of the same parity.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    If $\det(\pathview{e_\circ})=0$ the edge is routing-inert and every
    canonical traversal skips it.  Otherwise
    $0<\dampedweight{e_\circ}\le\wmax<1$
    (\zcref{thm:graph:raw-weight-ceiling}).  For a walk $p\ni e_\circ$,
    deleting that occurrence leaves a walk --- contiguity holds because
    $\operatorname{tgt}(e_{i-1})=\operatorname{src}(e_\circ)
    =\operatorname{tgt}(e_\circ)=\operatorname{src}(e_{i+1})=v$ --- with
    $\prod_{e\in p}\dampedweight{e}
    =\dampedweight{e_\circ}\prod_{e\in p'}\dampedweight{e}
    <\prod_{e\in p'}\dampedweight{e}$,
    and equal parity by hypothesis.  Strictly greater and strictly shorter;
    induct on occurrences.  The feed relaxation shows it directly:
    $R(v)\gets\max(R(v),R(v)\dampedweight{e_\circ})=R(v)$.
\end{proof}

The argument uses only $\dampedweight{}<1$ --- not the node's class, family,
or tier --- so \zcref{prop:nodes:self-loop-neutral} is the Actor$\leftrightarrow$Profile
\emph{instance} of this fact rather than a precedent being stretched to cover
a new case.

\begin{remark}[The Parity Hypothesis Is Load-Bearing]
    \label{rem:nodes:self-loop-parity}
    Drop $\detsign{e_\circ}=+1$ and the lemma is false, in the direction that
    matters.  At $\detsign{e_\circ}=-1$, deleting the occurrence yields a walk
    with strictly greater product \emph{and opposite parity}, so the
    original's contribution is dominated in the other register rather than its
    own: where every other walk to a target carries parity $-\sigma$, the
    self-loop populates $W^{\sigma}$ where it would otherwise be zero.  A
    negative-parity self-loop is a parity-flipping device, and the cheapest
    one available.

    Two things make that live rather than curious.  It is
    \textbf{promiscuous}: a negative Participant/A edge flips parity only for
    walks from its author, whereas a self-loop at a Chat is available to every
    traversal through that Chat --- and Chat has out-edges to Profile through
    Invitation/T.  And it \textbf{points the wrong way}: bridge consent
    subtracts the negative register from the positive
    (\zcref{def:bridge:consent}), so converting negative-parity paths to
    positive \emph{raises} consent, and a third party could author the
    conversion against someone else's consent calculation.

    Hence the type-fixed $p_i=1$ on Participant/T.  Forced parity constrains
    the parameters, which softens the mask, which bounds the tier: the
    movement edge routes at \tiermarginal{} and is therefore weak.  That is a
    consequence of the safety requirement rather than a free choice, and it is
    arguably the right one --- a lineage marker should be weak.
\end{remark}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Owner}{owner}
Actor's ownership of an Item.

\textbf{Domain:} Economic ($\symcal{D}_X$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{$\uparrow$ Promoted} from $(0,0,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $a \in [-1,1]$ (attachment). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = a$, $p_i = 1$.

\emph{Rationale:} Attachment is signed --- holding ($a > 0$)
vs.\ motivated selling ($a < 0$). Claiming ownership is a
directional act.

\emph{Stored $3 \times 3$:}
\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_e
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{a} & \fpm{|a|} & \fpm{1} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{a} & \fpl{|a|} & \fpl{1} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{a} & \fpl{|a|} & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

Since $|p_i| = p_i = 1$, rows~1 and~2 are identical.

\emph{Path-view $2 \times 2$} (full promoted mask):
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{a} & \fpm{|a|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{a} & \fpl{|a|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:owner}
\end{equation}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Join Request}{join-request}
Actor's request to join a Conversational Chat: a proposal, not
participation (\zcref{rem:nodes:chat-proposals-do-not-participate}).

\textbf{Domain:} Relational ($\symcal{D}_R$). \quad
\textbf{Stored mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$ $\uparrow$ promoted. \quad
\textbf{Routing tier:} \tierhalf{} (\zcref{def:graph:proposal-half-tier}). \quad
\textbf{Params:} $u \in [-1,1]$ (urgency), $f \in [-1,1]$ (formality). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = u$, $p_i = f$.

\emph{Path-view $2 \times 2$} (full stored block, \tierhalf{} floor):
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \halffloor\,\fpm{fu}   & \halffloor\,\fpm{f|u|}   \\[6pt]
        \halffloor\,\fpm{|f|u} & \fpl{|f||u|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:join-request}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} \tierhalf{}; $\detscore{e} \numrel{result.join.detscore.num}$ at
          reference parameters; $\detsign{e} = \pm 1$, preserved by
          \zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}.
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} CAN leaf (Rule~1).
    \item \textbf{Effect:} records a proposal; creates no membership and
          alters no Chat state.
    \item \textbf{Payload:} the request message, or the canonical empty
          payload.
    \item \textbf{Standing:} resolves to self.  A proposal to join a Chat is
          not a person-vouch toward the Chat's participants, invitees, or
          later references --- it allocates to nobody but its author, and it
          is weighed there.
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Accept (settlement consent)}{accept}
Seller's consent and counterterms for a pending Bid.  Carries the seller's
signed commercial sentiment and a \texttt{settles}-pointer to the Bid under
negotiation.  \textbf{Not binding}: title transfers only at the epoch boundary
(\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition,thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}).

\textbf{Domain:} Relational ($\symcal{D}_R$). \quad
\textbf{Stored mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$ $\uparrow$ promoted. \quad
\textbf{Routing tier:} \tierhalf{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $c \in [-1,1]$ (comfort), $e \in [-1,1]$ (equity). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = c$, $p_i = e$. \quad
\textbf{Settles:} Bid identity key.
\networkref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}%

\emph{Rationale:} comfort and equity are signed; the seller's sentiment
sits on a record the seller authored, so seller comfort is never
attributed to buyer authorship.

\emph{Path-view $2 \times 2$} (full stored block, \tierhalf{} floor):
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \halffloor\,\fpm{ec}   & \halffloor\,\fpm{e|c|}   \\[6pt]
        \halffloor\,\fpm{|e|c} & \fpl{|e||c|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:accept}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} \tierhalf{} (path-view floor $\halffloor$;
            $\detscore{e} \numrel{result.accept.detscore.num}$ at reference parameters);
            $\detsign{e} = \pm 1$, preserved under the floor by
            \zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}. Settlement reputation
            reads stance marginal, not route parity
            (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation}).
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} CAN leaf (Rule~1);
          $\baseval{e} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F$.
    \item \textbf{Authorship:} author $=$ source $=$ seller; a plain binary
          Actor$\to$Actor edge, identical in authorship to Opinion.
    \item \textbf{Standing role:}
          When the authored comfort and equity coordinates are both
          strictly positive, Accept is a binary person-vouch from the
          seller to the buyer
          (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  The projected edge
          receives the buyer's projected target activation; the raw direct
          Actor$\to$Actor record is not traversed as a separate standing
          path edge.

          This allocation expresses the seller's positive authored
          stance and is independent of title recognition.  Title remains
          sentiment-independent
          (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}); fabricated or unrecognized
          positive settlement ties remain the bounded ceiling witness
          \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}.
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Ratify (settlement commit)}{ratify}
Buyer's final confirmation and the \textbf{commit record}.  Carries the
buyer's signed final sentiment and a \texttt{settles}-pointer matching the
Accept's.  The commit \emph{finalizes at the first boundary unchallenged};
Layer-2 escrow observes the certificate as the release trigger
(\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-cross-layer}).

\textbf{Domain:} Relational ($\symcal{D}_R$). \quad
\textbf{Stored mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$ $\uparrow$ promoted. \quad
\textbf{Routing tier:} \tierhalf{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $c \in [-1,1]$ (final comfort), $e \in [-1,1]$ (final
equity). \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = c$, $p_i = e$. \quad
\textbf{Settles:} Bid identity key (must match the Accept's).
\networkref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}%

\emph{Path-view $2 \times 2$} (full stored block, \tierhalf{} floor):
\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \halffloor\,\fpm{ec}   & \halffloor\,\fpm{e|c|}   \\[6pt]
        \halffloor\,\fpm{|e|c} & \fpl{|e||c|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:ratify}
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} \tierhalf{}; $\detsign{e} = \pm 1$
          (preserved by \zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}); enters the
          reputation conjunction (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation}).
    \item \textbf{\AttrView{}:} CAN leaf (Rule~1).
    \item \textbf{Authorship:} author $=$ source $=$ buyer.  The commit is
          the buyer's own act, coupling funding and commitment
          (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-cross-layer}).
    \item \textbf{Standing role:}
          When the authored final-comfort and final-equity coordinates are
          both strictly positive, Ratify is a binary person-vouch from the
          buyer to the seller
          (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  The projected edge
          receives the seller's projected target activation; the raw direct
          Actor$\to$Actor record is not traversed as a separate standing
          path edge.

          This allocation is independent of title recognition and does
          not make title sentiment-dependent.  The residual fabricated-tie
          exposure remains \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}.
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Withdraw (settlement cancel)}{withdraw}
Buyer's cancellation, available in both the Open and Accepted states.  A
structural control signal, not a sentiment edge.

\textbf{Domain:} Minimal ($\symcal{D}_M$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $p_d = 1$, $p_i = 1$ (fixed). \quad
\textbf{$\detsign{}$:} $+1$ (forced). \quad
\textbf{CG:} \texttimes\ (Rule~4 control-edge exclusion,
\zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}).
\networkref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}%

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Geometry:} Actor$_{\mathrm{buyer}} \to$ Offer
          (graph-incident).  Author $=$ source $=$ buyer.
    \item \textbf{\PathView{}:} Minimal \tiermarginal{}; negligible
          $\dampedweight{}$.  The Offer is terminal (zero out-degree), so
          the edge is a routing dead-end and pollutes no path.
        \item \textbf{Effect:} from Open, kills the Bid; from Accepted, abandons
            the settlement; co-epochal with a Ratify, defeats it
            (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}, clause~(iv)). No value
            is locked at either state.
    \item \textbf{Accountability:} a public, authored, immutable retraction
          record; Withdraw rate is an auditable reliability signal
          (Layer~2).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Rescind (settlement cancel)}{rescind}
Seller's withdrawal of a not-yet-ratified Accept, available in the Accepted
state.  A structural control signal.

\textbf{Domain:} Minimal ($\symcal{D}_M$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $p_d = 1$, $p_i = 1$ (fixed). \quad
\textbf{$\detsign{}$:} $+1$ (forced). \quad
\textbf{CG:} \texttimes\ (Rule~4 control-edge exclusion).
\networkref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}%

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Geometry:} Actor$_{\mathrm{seller}} \to$ Offer.
          Author $=$ source $=$ seller.
        \item \textbf{Role:} the seller's sole escape from a non-binding
            Accept before commit; load-bearing, since Ratify would otherwise
            bind a regretful seller.  A Rescind co-epochal with, or earlier
            than, the Ratify defeats the sale
            (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}, clause~(v)); a
            later-epoch Rescind is inert (\zcref{rem:graph:regret-window}).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Leave (conversational control)}{leave}
Actor's unilateral declaration of departure from --- or dissociation
with --- a Chat.  A structural control signal, not a sentiment edge.

\textbf{Domain:} Minimal ($\symcal{D}_M$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Params:} $p_d = 1$, $p_i = 1$ (fixed). \quad
\textbf{$\detsign{}$:} $+1$ (forced). \quad
\textbf{CG:} \texttimes\ (Rule 4 control-edge exclusion,
\zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}).

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Geometry:} Actor $\to$ Chat.  Author $=$ source $=$ the
        departing actor.
    \item \textbf{Validity:} unconditional.  Layer~1 imposes no membership
        precondition: a Leave from an actor who was never a Participant,
        or who has already left, is a valid record --- a public act of
        dissociation, priced per action and deterred only by
        accountability cost
        (\zcref{subsec:necessity:unrestricted-departure}).
    \item \textbf{Effect at Layer~1:} none.  No standing, endorsement,
        title, or gate quantity reads it
        (\zcref{rem:epoch:control-acts-resolve-to-self}).
    \item \textbf{Layer~2:} the exit record of the canonical membership
        fold (\zcref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold}): membership is
        the $\prec$-maximal record of the actor's own
        $\set{\text{Participant}, \text{Leave}}$ chain toward the Chat.
    \item \textbf{Payload:} parting reason, or canonical empty.
    \item \textbf{Accountability:} an auditable departure record;
        leave-rate and leave-without-membership rate are terminal
        reliability signals (Layer~2).
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Hyper-Edges}
\label{subsec:nodes:hyper-edges}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Every hyper-edge is one authored act (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order,%
def:graph:authored-act}) whose edge projection is two edges, an A-projection
and a T-projection. Each projection is independently assigned a domain and mask; they may
occupy different tiers. By \zcref{thm:graph:hyper-edge-reduction}, the parity
sign of the composed hyper-edge is the product of the two projection signs:
$\detsign{\symcal{H}} = \detsign{e_1} \cdot \detsign{e_2}$.
The two projections share one parent act ($\actof{e_A}=\actof{e_T}$,
\zcref{cor:graph:act-projection-atomicity}): admitted together, they carry one act
identifier and one authoritative time
(\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}), with the internal $A\to T$ transition
taken at equal act time. The act carries one action count, one $\safethresh$-debit,
and one dependency projection --- never one per leg.

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Tag (hyper-edge)}{hyper-tag}
Actor applies a Type to a Taggable node.

\textbf{Params:} $r \in [-1,1]$ (relevance),
$c \in [0,1]$ (confidence).

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Passive).}
\textbf{Domain:} Epistemic. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,1,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Not promoted.} \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = r$, $p_i = c$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        0        & \fpm{c|r|}  & \fpm{c}   \\[6pt]
        0        & \fpl{c|r|}  & \fpl{c}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{r}  & \fpl{|r|}   & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        .05 \cdot \fpm{cr} & \fpm{c|r|} \\[6pt]
        .05 \cdot \fpm{cr} & \fpl{c|r|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:tag-l1}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{T-leg (Passive $\to$ Type).}
\textbf{Domain:} Epistemic. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,1,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = c$, $p_i = r$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        0        & \fpm{rc}    & \fpm{r}   \\[6pt]
        0        & \fpl{|r|c}  & \fpl{|r|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{c}  & \fpl{c}     & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        .05 \cdot \fpm{rc}   & \fpm{rc}   \\[6pt]
        .05 \cdot \fpm{|r|c} & \fpl{|r|c}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:tag-l2}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Standing role.}
None.  Tag remains a semantic-classification act for raw graph and CAN
consumers.  Positive parity, a Profile middle node, or a Type target does
not make Tag a person-vouch
(\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Review (hyper-edge)}{hyper-review}
Actor creates a contextual Comment on a Reviewable node.

\textbf{Params:} $e \in [-1,1]$ (enthusiasm),
$f \in [-1,1]$ (effort).

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Passive).}
\textbf{Domain:} Tribal. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = e$, $p_i = f$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{fe}   & \fpm{f|e|}   & \fpm{f}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|f|e} & \fpl{|f||e|} & \fpl{|f|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{e}    & \fpl{|e|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{fe}   & \fpm{f|e|}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|f|e} & \fpl{|f||e|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:review-l1}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{T-leg (Passive $\to$ Comment).}
\textbf{Domain:} Epistemic. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,1,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Not promoted.} \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = f$, $p_i = e$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        0        & \fpm{e|f|}   & \fpm{e}   \\[6pt]
        0        & \fpl{|e||f|} & \fpl{|e|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{f}  & \fpl{|f|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        .05 \cdot \fpm{ef}   & \fpm{e|f|}   \\[6pt]
        .05 \cdot \fpm{|e|f} & \fpl{|e||f|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:review-l2}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Standing role.}
None.  Review remains attributed commentary.  A reviewed Profile, a
positive Review/A leg, or a later Reference from the created Comment
does not convert the Review into a person-vouch
(\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
rem:graph:reviews-commentary}).
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Bid (hyper-edge)}{hyper-bid}
Actor places a bid on an Ownable Item, creating an Offer.

\textbf{Params:} $g \in [-1,1]$ (signed generosity),
$u \in [0,1]$ (urgency). Generosity is signed (generous $g>0$ vs.\
predatory $g<0$); both legs carry a full stored block and route at the
\tierhalf{} tier under \zcref{def:graph:proposal-half-tier}.
The buyer's stance $\operatorname{sgn}(g)$ enters the settlement stance
conjunction (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation});
\zcref{cor:nodes:bid-leg-parity} makes the reading leg-unambiguous.

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Item).}
\textbf{Domain:} Economic. \quad
\textbf{Stored mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$ $\uparrow$ promoted. \quad
\textbf{Routing tier:} \tierhalf{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = g$, $p_i = u$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{ug}   & \fpm{u|g|}   & \fpm{u}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|u|g} & \fpl{|u||g|} & \fpl{|u|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{g}    & \fpl{|g|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \halffloor\,\fpm{ug}   & \halffloor\,\fpm{u|g|}   \\[6pt]
        \halffloor\,\fpm{|u|g} & \fpl{|u||g|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:bid-l1}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{T-leg (Item $\to$ Offer).}
\textbf{Domain:} Economic. \quad
\textbf{Stored mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$ $\uparrow$ promoted. \quad
\textbf{Routing tier:} \tierhalf{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = u$, $p_i = g$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{gu}   & \fpm{g|u|}   & \fpm{g}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|g|u} & \fpl{|g||u|} & \fpl{|g|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{u}    & \fpl{|u|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \halffloor\,\fpm{gu}   & \halffloor\,\fpm{g|u|}   \\[6pt]
        \halffloor\,\fpm{|g|u} & \fpl{|g||u|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:bid-l2}
\end{equation}
\begin{corollary}[Bid Leg Parity]
    \label{cor:nodes:bid-leg-parity}
    The legs swap roles --- $(p_d, p_i) = (g, u)$ and $(u, g)$ --- and
    $\operatorname{sgn}(p_ip_d)$ is swap-symmetric
    (\zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law}), so with $u \geq 0$ both legs carry
    $\detsign{} = \operatorname{sgn}(g)$: any reference to ``the Bid's
    sign'' is well-defined without naming a leg, and it coincides with
    the stance marginal. The \emph{composed} hyper-edge parity is forced
    positive, $\detsign{\symcal{H}} = \operatorname{sgn}(g)^2 = +1$ for
    all $g \neq 0$: a predatory Bid is parity-visible per leg but
    parity-neutral as a composition --- buyer stance is read by the
    stance conjunction, never by traversal parity of the pair. At
    $g = 0$ or $u = 0$ both legs are routing-inert ($\det = 0$,
    \zcref{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy}) while Offer creation and
    recognition proceed unaffected (structural predicates are
    sentiment-blind).
\end{corollary}

\paragraph{Standing role.}
None.  Bid remains an Offer-creation and settlement-proposal act.
Its signed generosity may be consumed by raw parity and terminal
commercial-reputation policy, but neither leg compiles into standing.
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Invitation (hyper-edge)}{hyper-invitation}
Actor invites another actor to a Conversational Chat: a public, priced,
authored vouch that the invitee fits the community
(\zcref{ins:introduction:vouch-not-check}); a proposal, not participation
(\zcref{rem:nodes:chat-proposals-do-not-participate}).

\textbf{Params:} $u \in [-1,1]$ (urgency), $f \in [-1,1]$ (formality),
$r \in [0,1]$ (relevance of invitee to Chat).

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Chat).}
\textbf{Domain:} Relational. \quad
\textbf{Stored mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$ $\uparrow$ promoted. \quad
\textbf{Routing tier:} \tierhalf{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = u$, $p_i = f$.

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \halffloor\,\fpm{fu}   & \halffloor\,\fpm{f|u|}   \\[6pt]
        \halffloor\,\fpm{|f|u} & \fpl{|f||u|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:invitation-l1}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{T-leg (Chat $\to$ Profile$_{\mathrm{invitee}}$).}
\textbf{Domain:} Epistemic. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,1,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = r$, $p_i = 1$. \quad
$\detsign{} = +1$ (forced: $r \in [0,1]$, $p_i = 1$).

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        .05 \cdot \fpm{r} & \fpm{r}   \\[6pt]
        .05 \cdot \fpm{r} & \fpl{r}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:invitation-l2}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Standing role.}
Only the complete matched Invitation act may carry standing.  If the
act survives the inviter-revocation fold and every mandatory semantic
coordinate is strictly positive, the inviter may compile one complete
hyper-vouch toward the invitee's bound Actor
(\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
cor:graph:standing-act-atomicity}).

For source Actor~$u$, the inviter's act can matter only after $u$ has
allocated to the inviter~$a$: what reaches the invitee~$i$ is the share of
\emph{$u$'s} conserved unit that $a$ apportions onward, a composite of
consecutive hops and never a weight of its own
(\zcref{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport}).  Another Actor's
Participant, Opinion, Join Request, Send, or other relation to the Chat
cannot substitute for the Invitation/A leg and cannot inherit the
Invitation/T leg.  The Chat supplies conversational context and no
transferable standing.

The T-leg terminates at Profile$_i$, never directly at Actor~$i$, so the
complete act receives the invitee's projected target activation under
the uniform standing compiler.  Canonical payload remains the invitation
message on the A-leg and canonical empty on the T-leg.
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{De-invite (hyper-edge)}{hyper-deinvite}
Actor's declaration that another actor should not be --- or should no
longer be --- part of a Conversational Chat.  A structural control
signal: the revocation counterpart of Invitation, with force conferred
entirely by Layer-2 policy
(\zcref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold}).

\textbf{Params:} none (both legs type-fixed at $p_d = p_i = 1$).

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Chat).}
\textbf{Domain:} Minimal ($\symcal{D}_M$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
$\detsign{} = +1$ (forced). \quad
\textbf{CG:} \texttimes\ (Rule 4).

\paragraph{T-leg (Chat $\to$ Profile$_{\mathrm{de\text{-}invitee}}$).}
\textbf{Domain:} Minimal ($\symcal{D}_M$). \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
$\detsign{} = +1$ (forced). \quad
\textbf{CG:} \texttimes\ (Rule 4).

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Validity:} unconditional.  The author need not be a
        member, an inviter, or connected to the target; the target need
        not be a member.  Authority is a Layer-2 policy fact, never a
        Layer-1 precondition
        (\zcref{subsec:necessity:unrestricted-departure}).
    \item \textbf{Profile terminus:} the terminal leg targets the
        de-invitee's \emph{Profile}, never the Actor: the sole
        passive-sourced in-edge of any Actor remains its own Reputation
        component (\zcref{subsec:necessity:deinvite-profile-terminus}),
        so even the attention conduit is damped through the target's
        standing-dependent bond, zero at zero standing.
    \item \textbf{Standing inertness:}
        both legs are control records and resolve to their author
        (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
        rem:epoch:control-acts-resolve-to-self}).  They are absent from
        complete person-vouch compilation, so a De-invite never carries
        a source rate toward its target.  Raw feed traversal may still
        observe the Minimal-weight records as attention, never standing:
        expulsion may make its target weakly \emph{discoverable}, never
        \emph{endorsed}.
    \item \textbf{Inviter revocation:} the one projection-visible effect.
        A De-invite suppresses \emph{its own author's} Invitation bundle
        toward the same (Chat, Profile) incidence
        (\zcref{def:epoch:inviter-revocation}); it never affects another
        author's invitation.
    \item \textbf{Payload:} reason on the A-leg; canonical empty on the T-leg.
\end{itemize}
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Reference (hyper-edge)}{hyper-reference}
Actor cites an existing node from an anchoring artifact: the Review hyper-edge
with its legs transposed. Where a Review \emph{mints} a Comment as the sink of
its terminal leg, a Reference \emph{mints nothing} --- it uses an existing
passive node as the source of its terminal leg and points that leg at a
pre-existing target. Like Review it is commentary, never state
(\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}): it transitions no settlement, moves no
title, binds no tag, creates no membership. The census sibling is Tag (both
mint nothing); the strength profile is Review's, transposed so the strong
Tribal leg carries the citation itself (artifact $\to$ target) and the weak
Epistemic leg carries authorship (actor $\to$ artifact).

\textbf{Params:} $e \in [-1,1]$ (enthusiasm), $f \in [-1,1]$ (effort).

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Artifact).}
\textbf{Domain:} Epistemic. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,1,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Not promoted.} \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = f$, $p_i = e$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        0        & \fpm{e|f|}   & \fpm{e}   \\[6pt]
        0        & \fpl{|e||f|} & \fpl{|e|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{f}  & \fpl{|f|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        .05 \cdot \fpm{ef}   & \fpm{e|f|}   \\[6pt]
        .05 \cdot \fpm{|e|f} & \fpl{|e||f|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:reference-l1}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{T-leg (Artifact $\to$ Target).}
\textbf{Domain:} Tribal. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = e$, $p_i = f$. \quad
\textbf{Target:} any existing passive node ($V_c$) --- any node except an
Actor, including a Profile.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{fe}   & \fpm{f|e|}   & \fpm{f}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|f|e} & \fpl{|f||e|} & \fpl{|f|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{e}    & \fpl{|e|}    & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{fe}   & \fpm{f|e|}   \\[6pt]
        \fpm{|f|e} & \fpl{|f||e|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:reference-l2}
\end{equation}

\begin{remark}[A Reference Is Weighted Through Its Author]
    \label{rem:nodes:reference-author-allocation}
    A Reference whose semantic target is not a Profile resolves to its
    author and is weighed there.  It remains available to feed ranking, raw
    signed traversal, CAN, provenance display, and terminal guild policy.

    A complete Reference whose matched T-leg targets Profile$_i$ may
    become one complete hyper-vouch authored by the Reference author
    toward Actor~$i$, provided its mandatory semantic coordinates are
    strictly positive
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
    cor:graph:standing-act-atomicity}).  For source Actor~$u$, the
    Reference matters only after $u$ has allocated to its author, and what
    travels onward is a share of \emph{$u$'s} conserved unit apportioned by
    that author (\zcref{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport}).
    The anchoring artifact supplies context and no transferable
    standing.  Incoming Opinion, Participant, Owner, Tag, Review, Bid,
    Send, or other weight on that artifact cannot enter the Reference/T
    leg; no unrelated edge may substitute for the matched Reference/A
    leg.

    Self-Reference is excluded by the projected standing compiler, not
    by the old $j\neq i$ summation argument.  The raw Reference records
    remain public and fully usable by non-standing consumers.
\end{remark}
\end{NetworkStructure}

\begin{remark}[Departure Composes with Opinion]
    \label{rem:nodes:departure-composes-with-opinion}
    Leave and De-invite carry no stance parameters by design: the census
    already provides the sentiment channel (Opinion on the Chat, Tribal,
    \tierfull{}; Opinion on the Profile, person-vouch eligible under
    \zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  A rage-quit is
    Leave $+$ negative Opinion; a regretful, amicable de-invite is
    De-invite $+$ payload reason.  Duplicating stance into the control
    family would re-open exactly the vacuous-vouch surface that
    \zcref{rem:epoch:control-acts-resolve-to-self} closes.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Proposals Do Not Create Participation]
    \label{rem:nodes:chat-proposals-do-not-participate}
    Join Request and Invitation edges are proposals. They establish no
    membership and do not substitute for the Participant edge: a Chat
    membership signal exists only when the joining actor authors a
    Participant edge. Ignoring a proposal requires no graph action.

    Invitation is nevertheless eligible for one distinct allocation:
    the inviter's own complete, positive, unsuppressed act may compile into
    a person-vouch toward the invitee
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  No other Actor's relation to
    the Chat is inherited by that act.  A Join Request allocates to nobody
    but its author.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Canonical Membership Fold (Layer-2 Default)]
    \label{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold}
    For actor~$a$ and Chat~$C$, let $M(a,C)$ be $a$'s own \textbf{acts}
    bearing on membership of~$C$ --- not edges incident on~$C$, which is a
    different and wrong set.  Three shapes bear:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item a Participant act with $T=C$ --- participation in~$C$;
        \item a Participant act with $A=C$ and $T\neq C$ --- departure
              from~$C$;
        \item a \texttt{Leave} toward~$C$ --- departure from~$C$.
    \end{itemize}
    The \emph{canonical membership fold} is
    \[
        \operatorname{member}^{(k)}(a, C) = \text{true}
        \iff
        M(a,C) \neq \void
