        \ \text{and its latest element is a participation shape.}
    \]
    One move act is simultaneously $C_0$-departing and $C_1$-joining, and is
    read once in each fold from the leg roles of the same act.

    \emph{The fold keys on leg role, never on family incidence}, and getting
    that wrong is the likeliest bug this design admits.  A fold reading ``any
    Participant act incident on~$C$'' as participation treats a move's A-leg
    as a rejoin of the chat being left: the family is Participant and the
    A-leg genuinely is incident on~$C_0$, so \emph{moving away would read as
    staying}.  The predicate was edge-level while \texttt{Leave} was act-level
    everywhere else, which is why this repair is owed independently of
    uniform Participant --- the reshape only makes it bite.

    \texttt{Leave} survives, and uniformity does not subsume it: departing
    without arriving is not expressible as a Participant act, because there is
    no ``nowhere'' node and a self-referential T-leg is a join.  Dissociation
    without destination remains its own gesture, and the two forms do not
    overlap.
    Under the canonical default, De-invite records are \emph{advisory}:
    they enter the fold only through a published chat or guild policy
    $\mathcal{P}$ naming an authority set.  Where $\mathcal{P}$
    recognizes them, the \emph{conservative rule} governs: a recognized
    De-invite (author in $\mathcal{P}$'s authority set, middle~$C$,
    terminus $\mathrm{Profile}_a$) defeats membership iff it strictly
    $\prec$-follows the $\prec$-maximal element of $M(a,C)$; a concurrent
    or $\prec$-earlier De-invite has no effect (incumbent membership
    persists, mirroring \zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}); and a
    Participant strictly $\prec$-following the De-invite re-establishes
    membership unless $\mathcal{P}$ specifies ban semantics.
    $\mathcal{P}$ is published per
    \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Membership Is Terminal]
    \label{rem:nodes:membership-is-terminal}
    No admission rule reads $\operatorname{member}^{(k)}$: it feeds
    neither the gate, nor capacity, nor settlement recognition
    (\zcref{def:network:admission-closure}).  It is therefore
    Layer~2 in the strict boundary sense --- two guilds may derive
    different membership from the same $E_k$ without forking anything.
    Contrast title, which is binding \emph{because} recognition
    clause~(iii) reads it back.  This is why Leave and De-invite append
    unconditionally: a Layer-1 validity precondition would drag a
    membership predicate into the admission closure
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:unrestricted-departure}).
\end{remark}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{NetworkStructure}{edge}{Send (hyper-edge)}{hyper-send}
Actor sends a Message into a Conversational Chat. The family named
\emph{Write} in earlier drafts is renamed: \emph{write} is the protocol act
--- the admission of a cluster at epoch closure
(\zcref{def:network:write}) --- and no edge family may shadow it. A Send is,
like every record, carried into the graph by a write; it is not one.

\textbf{Params:} $i \in [-1,1]$ (importance).

\paragraph{A-leg (Actor $\to$ Chat).}
\textbf{Domain:} Relational. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(1,1,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{$\uparrow$ Promoted} from $(0,0,1,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tierfull{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = i$, $p_i = 1$.

\emph{Rationale:} Importance is signed --- a message can be
positively or negatively important.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{i} & \fpm{|i|} & \fpm{1} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{i} & \fpl{|i|} & \fpl{1} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{i} & \fpl{|i|} & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

Since $p_i = 1$, rows~1 and~2 are identical.

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_1}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        \fpm{i} & \fpm{|i|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{i} & \fpl{|i|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:send-a}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{T-leg (Chat $\to$ Message).}
\textbf{Domain:} Minimal. \quad
\textbf{Mask:} $(0,0,0,1)$. \quad
\textbf{Not promoted.} \quad
\textbf{Tier:} \tiermarginal{}. \quad
\textbf{Roles:} $p_d = 1$, $p_i = i$.

\begin{tensorblock}
    \symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        0        & 0           & \fpm{i}   \\[6pt]
        0        & \fpl{|i|}   & \fpl{|i|} \\[6pt]
        \fpm{1}  & \fpl{1}     & \fpl{1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{tensorblock}

\begin{equation}
    \pathview{e_2}
    = \begin{pmatrix}
        .05 \cdot \fpm{i} & .05 \cdot \fpm{i} \\[6pt]
        .05 \cdot \fpm{|i|} & \fpl{|i|}
    \end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:nodes:path-view:send-t}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Standing role.}
None.  Sending into a Chat does not endorse the Chat's participants,
invitees, referenced Profiles, or Message reviewers.
\end{NetworkStructure}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{proposition}[Self-Loop Neutrality]
    \label{prop:nodes:self-loop-neutral}
    The self-loop path
    $\mathrm{Actor}_j \to \mathrm{Profile}_j \to
    \mathrm{Actor}_j$
    (traversing Declaration then Reputation) produces no register
    update at node~$j$ in the raw signed double-cover service
    (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}) and no weight update in
    the feed-ranking BFS (\zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs}).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
    The raw signed double-cover service and feed-ranking BFS operate on
    the snapshot raw graph
    $E_k$ (\zcref{post:epoch:final-edge-set}); the current
    certificate's derived bond components (published in Step~3 of
    \zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}) are therefore excluded.  The
    standing projection does not traverse the Declaration/Reputation
    loop at all (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}); the argument
    below is retained for raw graph consumers, and all of it applies to
    the snapshot subgraph.

    \emph{(1) Max-product update (primary).} The loop candidate at any
    node with register value $W$ is
    $W \cdot \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Dec}}}\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} < W$
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-bound}); the max-product relaxation
    is a no-op at the source ($W=1$) and at every mid-path node alike.

    \emph{(2) Parity (corroborating).}
    Both edges satisfy $\detsign{} = +1$
    (\zcref{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-parities}). The candidate maps
    $(\posreg{j}, \negreg{j}) = (1, 0)$ to $(\tilde{w}^2, 0)$ with
    $\tilde{w}^2 < 1$: no register state exceeds its initialised
    value.

    Argument~(1) holds at every traversal depth and independently of the
    passive out-degree structure (\zcref{lem:graph:passive-out-degree}).
    (Causal ordering does \emph{not} block the loop: user edges authored
    after derivation share the snapshot and satisfy
    $\acttime{} > \boundaryslot{k}$.)
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Raw Self-Edge Properties]
    \label{prop:nodes:raw-self-edge-properties}
    The following are properties of the raw derived Self-edge bond used
    by raw graph and CAN consumers.  They do not define the projected
    standing activation, whose formula and certificate are owned by
    \zcref{sec:epoch,app:dynamics}; in particular, raw maturity
    amplification and raw profile-bridged ceilings are feed properties
    only, and raw maturity amplification cannot create a valid projected
    standing activation (\zcref{rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support}).
    For all $\standing{j} \geq 0$ and $\tau \in [0,1)$:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
      \item \textbf{Zero at zero.}
          $\standing{j} = 0 \Rightarrow p = 0 \Rightarrow
          \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} = 0$.
          The bond is inert.
      \item \textbf{Strict monotonicity.}
          $\partial\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}/
          \partial\standing{j} > 0$ for all $\standing{j}>0$
          (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}).
      \item \textbf{Upper bound.}
          $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} < 1$ for all
          $\standing{j}$, all $\tau$
          (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-bound}).
      \item \textbf{Concavity.}
          $\partial^2\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}/
          \partial\standing{j}^2 < 0$ for all $\standing{j}>0$
          (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-concavity}).
      \item \textbf{Positive parity.}
          $\detsign{e_{\mathrm{Dec}}} =
          \detsign{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} = +1$ for all
          $\standing{j} > 0$
          (\zcref{eq:nodes:self-edge-bond-parities}).
      \item \textbf{Synchronisation.}
          Both components share identical stored tensor,
          $\detscore{}$, and damped weight formula at every epoch
          boundary
          (\zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}).
      \item \textbf{CAN independence.}
          $\partial(\canval{n_j}/V_{\max})/
          \partial\standing{j} = 0$ for actors whose Declaration
          component does not lie within their own composition
          dependency closure
          (\zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}).
          The Reputation component contributes nothing to CAN
          (Rule~3 of \zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}).
      \item \textbf{Feed-ranking hierarchy.}
          Profile-bridged ceiling:
          $(\wmaxop)^2 \cdot \wmax \approx
          (\numval{bound.raw.wmaxop.num})^2 \times \numval{bound.raw.wmax.num} \numrel{bound.raw.bridge_ceiling.num}$.
          Direct Opinion ceiling: $\wmaxop \numrel{bound.raw.wmaxop.num}$.
          The bridge is always at least $2\times$ weaker than a
          direct Opinion path.
      \item \textbf{Raw $\tau$-channel ceiling at frozen $p$.}
          $\sup_\tau \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}(p_0;\tau)
          = \detscore{}(p_0)\cdot\sqrt{2} < 1$
          (\zcref{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds}); a raw feed
          property only.
    \end{enumerate}
    \proofsketch{
    (1)~$\tanh(0) = 0$.
    (2,3,4)~\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity,%
    prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-bound,%
    prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-concavity}.
    (5)~$\clampsigmoid{p} > 0$, $\tanh(p) > 0$,
    $\bleedparam^2\tanh(p) \ll 1$.
    (6)~Shared derivation with identical $p_j^{(k)}$.
    (7)~Reputation excluded from \CompGraph{}; Declaration generically
    not in its own source's dependency closure.
    (8)~$\wmaxop$ bounds both Opinion factors; $\wmax$ bounds the
    Reputation factor.
    (9)~$\sqrt{1+\tau^2} \leq \sqrt{2}$,
    $e^{-\invtemp \tentropy{}} \leq 1$.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[The Edge Census Is Normative]
    \label{rem:nodes:edge-census-normative}
    \zcref{tbl:nodes:archetype-fingerprints,%
    tbl:nodes:act-payload-schema,%
    tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}
    are the normative edge and act censuses.

    \zcref{tbl:nodes:archetype-fingerprints} governs raw family
    membership, tier, promotion, CG inclusion, and raw
    determinant-sign forcing.
    \zcref{tbl:nodes:act-payload-schema} governs the act payload controller and
    canonical act-payload placement.
    \zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution} alone governs whether a binary
    record or complete hyper-edge act is eligible to compile into
    projected standing.

    Where prose disagrees with the relevant table, the table governs.
    The mask promotion criterion
    (\zcref{def:graph:mask-promotion-criterion}) motivates raw routing
    geometry and directs no allocation.
    Registration and Publish are census rows: grounded anchoring and minted
    genesis are append records, while the Self-edge components are annotated as
    derived traversal edges rather than records.
    A trait expansion that adds no edge family changes no census row:
    Review/A·T are listed once
    regardless of which middle-node types implement the trait.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Coherence column, not vouch column.}
The $\detsign{}$ column in
\zcref{tbl:nodes:archetype-fingerprints} is the raw
routing/coherence parity column.  It never directs allocation.
Standing eligibility is fixed exclusively by
\zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}; the epoch compiler then applies
the complete-act positive-coordinate and bundle rules.

Thus:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item a $(-,-)$ Opinion on Profile$_i$ remains coherent but does
          not vouch;
    \item a positive Tag, Review, Bid, Send, or control record still
          resolves home, and is weighed there;
    \item a positive Reference/T or Invitation/T leg is not itself an act
          and contributes nothing unless its matched complete act survives
          compilation;
    \item raw parity continues to serve feed, raw bridge, and diagnostic
          consumers independently of standing.
\end{itemize}

    $\operatorname{controller}(q)=\operatorname{author}(q)$. Rendering

\paragraph{Forced $+1$ entries.}
Self~Dec/Rep (derived): $p_d = 1$, $p_i > 0$ by derivation.
Registration: $p_d = p_i = 1$ fixed.
Withdraw/Rescind, Leave, De-invite/A·T: $p_d = p_i = 1$ fixed (control
signals).
Invitation/T: $r \in [0,1]$, $p_i = 1$. Bid/A·T admits $\pm 1$ under
signed generosity. All other types contain at least one signed
user-controlled parameter and thus admit $\pm 1$.

\paragraph{Tier structure.}
Full-block edges route at \tierfull{} ($\sqrt{|\det|} \approx
0.27$--$0.36$ at reference non-Self parameters).  The settlement edges
(Bid, Accept, Ratify) carry a full stored block but route at \tierhalf{}
($\sqrt{|\det|} \approx 0.20$--$0.22$): a path-view-only $\halffloor$
attenuation that preserves their determinant signs
(\zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}) and leaves their
\AttrView{} norms and CAN base values intact.  Restricted-mask edges
route at \tiermarginal{} ($\sqrt{|\det|} \approx 0.07$--$0.08$).  The
per-edge gaps compound multiplicatively along paths.  The promotions
(Owner, Participant, Send/A, and the proposal and settlement families)
keep economic and relational interactions informationally on par with social
judgments while reserving \tierfull{} routing force for enacted relations
(\zcref{def:graph:proposal-half-tier}).  Betweenness centrality in the guild reward formula is
dominated by \tierfull{} engagement; the CAN enrichment factor uses
\AttrView{} norms equalized across all tiers ($\sim\!21\%$ full-range
variation; \zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}).  The
standing-dependent Self/Reputation component remains \tierfull{} with its
separate upper bound $\wmax$.

\begin{proposition}[Structural Edge Properties]
    \label{prop:nodes:structural-edge-properties}
    For all edges produced by the canonical pipeline:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \label{prop:nodes:structural-edge-properties:floor}
              $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F \geq \numval{const.graph.fpl_baseline.num}$
              (from baseline $\Psi^{22}$).
        \item \label{prop:nodes:structural-edge-properties:upper}
              $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F \leq 3$
              (9 entries, each $\leq 1$).
        \item \label{prop:nodes:structural-edge-properties:rank2}
              $\svdthree{}/\svdone{} < 0.05$ for full-mask edges;
              $\leq 0.22$ for restricted-mask edges
              (domain-stratified;
              \zcref{prop:graph:rank-two-constraint};
              worst case: $\svdthree{}/\svdone{} \numrel{result.minimal.psi_svd_ratio.num}$
              for the Minimal mask at $|p_d| = |p_i| = 1$;
              \zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}).
        \item \label{prop:nodes:structural-edge-properties:monotone}
              $|\Psi^{gh}|$ is monotonically non-decreasing in
              $|p_d|$ and $|p_i|$ for every active entry.
        \item \label{prop:nodes:structural-edge-properties:pol-floor}
              $\Psi^{11} \geq 0.5$ for all edges (Polarization
              Floor compatibility).
        \item \label{prop:nodes:structural-edge-properties:tier-gap}
              The tier gap
              $\sqrt{|\det_{\mathrm{T1}}|}/
              \sqrt{|\det_{\mathrm{T2}}|}
              \geq 2.5$ for moderate parameter values.
    \end{enumerate}
    \proofsketch{(1) baseline always active. (2) clamping bounds.
    (3) \zcref{prop:graph:rank-two-constraint}. (4) composition of
    monotone functions. (5) $\fpl{0} = 0.5$ and $a_{11} = 1$ for
    all domains. (6) \zcref{prop:graph:path-view-determinant-bound}.}
\end{proposition}

\zcref{sec:sorting} shows how path-view scoring drives content
sorting, and \zcref{sec:transport} extends the same path machinery
to advertiser transport.

% §6: Epoch Architecture — Layer 1 Published Quantities

% CHANGELOG:
%   v0.22.0-dev  Invitation-conduit remark extended to Reference-to-Profile (net-stance withdrawal noted).

\section{Epoch Architecture}
\label{sec:epoch}

The network operator publishes, at each epoch boundary, the complete
set of Layer~1 quantities on which the binding comparator depends.
Every quantity defined here is independently reproducible from the
accepted records, the public residual-balance ledger, the published
constants, and the epoch certificate.

The architecture separates two graph readings.

\begin{description}[nosep]
    \item[\textbf{Raw graph services.}]
        Feed ranking, raw bridge traversal, signed diagnostics, and CAN
        continue to consume the public Action Graph and its raw per-edge
        quantities, including $\dampedweight{e}$ and $\detsign{e}$.

    \item[\textbf{Standing.}]
        Standing never traverses arbitrary raw graph legs.  The epoch
        compiler first folds per-author records, reconstructs complete
        person-vouch acts, and derives an initiator-owned Actor-to-Actor
        projection from the closed standing census
        (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection,%
        def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  A source-relative standing
        path is then a simple causal sequence of at most
        $\hopmax=4$ hops of transport.  Allocated mass receives
        the accepted tilt rung, and only the conserved transport
        $\transportentry{u}{i}$ enters the balance/count standing
        mediant.
\end{description}

The chapter proceeds from raw edge primitives
(\zcref[range]{subsec:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary,%
  subsec:epoch:damped-edge-weight})
to the commitment rate (\zcref{subsec:epoch:commitment-rate}), complete
person-vouch compilation
(\zcref{subsec:epoch:act-folding}), the projected target
activation and Actor-only standing graph, source-relative paths and safe
standing flow (\zcref{subsec:epoch:conserved-standing-transport}), the retained raw
signed double-cover service
(\zcref{subsec:epoch:raw-signed-service}), the exact standing mediant
(\zcref{subsec:epoch:final-standing}), the coupled-dynamics summary
(\zcref{subsec:epoch:within-epoch-standing-solver}), the epoch boundary and
derivation sequence (\zcref{subsec:epoch:epoch-boundary}), the
\safethresh{}-debit ledger (\zcref{subsec:epoch:act-debit}), the
two-gate write rule (\zcref{subsec:epoch:participation-gates}), and
threshold and margin governance
(\zcref{subsec:epoch:floor-governance}).

No guild reward rule appears in this chapter.  The standing projection,
path schedule, admission schedule, and final standing field are binding
Layer~1 outputs; feed and reward remain terminal readouts.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Thermodynamic Boundary}
\label{subsec:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{axiom}[Thermodynamic Boundary]
    \label{ax:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:inverse-temperature}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas}%
    Internal quantities flow undamped.  The Boltzmann factor
    $\boltzfactor{\tentropy{}}$ is applied once at \emph{observation
    boundaries}, which differ across subsystems:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Per-edge raw observation} for content sorting
              (\zcref{sec:sorting}), raw signed double-cover traversal
              (\zcref{subsec:epoch:raw-signed-service}), and the canonical
              raw bridge-affinity channel (\zcref{def:bridge:affinity}),
              using the raw damped weight $\dampedweight{e}$
              (\zcref{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight}).
        \item \textbf{Per-creator-epoch observation} for reward
              distribution (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}), via
              $\boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}$.
    \end{itemize}
    Both granularities share $\invtemp \numrel{const.activation.beta_2ln2.exact} \numrel{const.activation.beta_2ln2.num}$.
    The exponential weighting of the temporal entropy $\tentropy{}$ is
    the maximum-entropy form.\footcite{jaynes1957information}
    The shared raw traversal primitive is
    \zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}.

    Standing is not a thermodynamic raw-edge consumer.  Its
    relation coefficient and projected target activation are defined
    separately in
    \zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,%
    def:epoch:responsive-vouch-activation}.  Raw maturity and raw
    temporal entropy therefore remain available to feed and bridge
    traversal without creating a maturity ratchet inside standing.  See
    \zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model} for the
    deployment-phase interpretation of verification failures against
    these constants.
\end{axiom}


The inverse temperature $\invtemp = 2\ln 2 \numrel{const.activation.beta_2ln2.num}$ damps
maximum-entropy edges to $\approx 38\%$ of their raw weight.
\proofsketch{$\invtemp$ calibration:
$\exp(-2(\ln 2)^2) \numrel{const.activation.maxent_damping.num}$.}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Damped Edge Weight}
\label{subsec:epoch:damped-edge-weight}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Damped Edge Weight]
    \label{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight}
    At $\divpref \numrel{const.graph.divergence_preference.exact}$:
    \begin{equation}
        \dampedweight{e}
        = \underbrace{\detscore{e}}_{\text{coherence}}
        \;\cdot\;
        \underbrace{\sqrt{1 + \tau_e^2}}_{\text{maturity}}
        \;\cdot\;
        \underbrace{\boltzfactor{\tentropy{e}}}_{\text{boundary}}.
        \label{eq:epoch:damped-edge-weight}
    \end{equation}
    This is the raw per-edge primitive for raw Action-Graph consumers
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}).  It enters feed ranking,
    the raw signed double-cover service, and raw bridge-affinity
    traversal.  It does not enter any standing formula directly: a
    complete person-vouch act instead receives one complete-act
    coefficient and one projected target activation
    (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,%
    def:epoch:responsive-vouch-activation}).  (Placement: a per-edge
    quantity housed in the epoch chapter because damping is applied at
    the observation boundary,
    \zcref{ax:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary}.)
\end{definition}


\begin{remark}[Shared Raw-Edge Primitive]
    \label{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}
    \zcref{eq:epoch:damped-edge-weight} remains the identical raw
    per-edge primitive for every \emph{raw graph} consumer that uses
    it: the feed-ranking BFS (\zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs}), the
    raw signed double-cover service
    (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}), and Channel~1 of the bridge
    transport (\zcref{def:bridge:affinity}).  No raw consumer applies a
    variant, a rescaling, or a per-system correction --- the coherence
    ($\detscore{e}$), maturity ($\sqrt{1+\tau_e^2}$), and boundary
    ($\boltzfactor{\tentropy{e}}$) factors are evaluated the same way,
    so an edge amplified or suppressed in one raw traversal is amplified
    or suppressed by the same factor in the others.

    Standing is not a raw graph consumer.  It compiles complete
    semantic acts into projected Actor edges and uses the
    standing-specific coefficient, target activation, source envelopes,
    and emission fractions of
    \zcref{subsec:epoch:act-folding,%
    subsec:epoch:conserved-standing-transport}.  Sharing public edge parameters
    does not make the raw and standing traversals interchangeable:
    the invariant is ``one raw formula for raw graph consumers,'' not
    ``one traversal for feed and standing.''
\end{remark}


\begin{proposition}[Damped Weight Bounds]
    \label{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds}
    For every edge:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \label{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds:positive}
              $\dampedweight{e} \geq 0$, strictly positive for every
              routing-active edge (nonzero mandatory parameters):
              $\bleedparam$-softening prevents mask-induced determinant
              collapse, but a vanishing mandatory parameter still gives
              $\det = 0$ and $\dampedweight{e} = 0$
              (\zcref{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy}).
        \item \label{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds:upper}
              $\dampedweight{e} \leq \detscore{e} \cdot \sqrt{2}$,
              approached as $\tau \to 1$, $\tentropy{} \to 0$.
        \item \label{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds:floor}
              Parameter-band floors: at reference-band parameters
              ($\detscore{} \geq 0.27$), \tierfull{}-tier
              $\dampedweight{e} \gtrsim 0.10$; no parameter-free full-mask
              floor exists (weights vanish as parameters $\to 0$; the
              full-mask spam edge sits at $\numrel{result.spam.weight.num}$).
              \tiermarginal{}-tier extreme weak-parameter floor:
              $\dampedweight{e} \gtrsim 0.006$ (empirical \tiermarginal{}
              minimum $\numrel{result.e5.weight.num}$;
              \zcref{subsec:verification:spam-resistance}).
        \item \label{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds:non-monotone}
              As a function of $\tau$, $\dampedweight{}$ is
              non-monotone: minimum near $\tau \approx 0.5$ (maximum
              entropy), recovery above $\tau^*$.
    \end{enumerate}
    \proofsketch{(1) all factors positive.  (2) $\sqrt{1+\tau^2}
    \leq \sqrt{2}$, $\boltzfactor{H} \leq 1$.  (3) worst-case temporal
    at $\tau=0.5$: factor $\numrel{const.activation.g_half.num}$; multiply by tier-minimum
    $\detscore{}$.  (4) $g(\tau) = \sqrt{1+\tau^2} \cdot \boltzfactor{\tentropy{}}$
    has $g(0)=1$, $g(0.5) \numrel{const.activation.g_half.num}$, $g(1^-) \to
    \sqrt{2}$.}
\end{proposition}


\begin{definition}[Maturity Crossover]
    \label{def:epoch:maturity-crossover}
    $\tau^*$ is the unique value in $(0.5, 1)$ satisfying
    $\sqrt{1+(\tau^*)^2} \cdot e^{-\invtemp \tentropy{\tau^*}} = 1$.
\end{definition}


\begin{proposition}[Crossover Location]
    \label{prop:epoch:crossover-location}
    $\tau^* \in (0.93, 0.94)$ for $\invtemp \numrel{const.activation.beta_2ln2.num}$.  Independent
    of the sentiment factor $\detscore{e}$. Because $\dampedweight{e}$
    is the shared raw per-edge primitive
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}),
    every edge passing $\tau^*$ receives net amplification in every raw
    consuming system simultaneously.  Standing is unaffected: raw
    maturity does not enter the projected standing activation.
    \proofsketch{Evaluate $g(0.93) \numrel{result.activation.g_093.num} < 1$,
    $g(0.94) \numrel{result.activation.g_094.num} > 1$.  IVT.}
\end{proposition}


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Commitment Rate}
\label{subsec:epoch:commitment-rate}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The commitment rate $\commitrate{i}=\burnbal{i}/\max(\actcount{i},1)$,
its ledger $\burnbal{i}$, and the type asymmetry of the real-over-integer
quotient are defined in \zcref{sec:comparator}
(\zcref{def:comparator:rate,def:comparator:residual-balance,rem:comparator:vintage-trichotomy}).
The epoch sequence consumes $\commitrate{i}$ as a published per-actor scalar:
the standing (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}) reads it at each epoch boundary, and
each accepted act debits $\safethresh$ from $\burnbal{i}$ at the writing
epoch's price (\zcref{post:epoch:act-debit}) --- the reserve-to-action
conversion performed per act, with no frozen factor.


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Proposed Final Epoch State}
\label{subsec:epoch:final-state}

\begin{definition}[Proposed Final Epoch State]
    \label{def:epoch:proposed-final-act-state}
    Fix epoch boundary~$k$ and a proposed write set~$\actsequence{k}$.  For Actor~$i$,
    let $\actcountincrement{k}{i}$ be the number of proposed epoch-$k$ acts
    authored by~$i$: one binary record is one act, one complete hyper-edge
    is one act, and Registration is one ordinary act.  It counts acts, not
    records.

    Let $\burnval{i}^{(k)}$ be the settled boundary burn snapshot and write
    $\Delta\burnval{i}^{(k)}\coloneqq\burnval{i}^{(k)}-\burnval{i}^{(k-1)}$;
    this increment may be positive even for an Actor who authored no act.
    The proposed final residual balance and action count are
    \begin{equation}
        \burnbal{i}^{(k)}(\actsequence{k})
        =
        \burnbal{i}^{(k-1)}
        +
        \Delta\burnval{i}^{(k)}
        -
        \actcountincrement{k}{i}\,\safethresh^{(k)},
        \label{eq:epoch:final-residual-balance}
    \end{equation}
    \begin{equation}
        \actcount{i}^{(k)}(\actsequence{k})
        =
        \actcount{i}^{(k-1)}
        +
        \actcountincrement{k}{i}.
        \label{eq:epoch:final-action-count}
    \end{equation}
    Prior debit vintages remain consummated and are not repriced; a
    candidate Actor has prior count zero but takes no special formula.

    The tentative final edge set is $E_k(\edgeincrement{k})\coloneqq E_{k-1}\cup \edgeincrement{k}$.
    Every standing, path, admission-fraction, stamp, and gate quantity associated
    with~$\actsequence{k}$ is computed from this completed tentative state.  A
    contributing source transports its current pair
    $(\burnbal{u}^{(k)},\actcount{u}^{(k)})$, and the same completed ledger fixes
    its emission fraction (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}): the export
    capacity is read once, from the epoch-final balance, so a late burn moves the
    rate and the emission together and neither is repriced afterwards.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Epoch-Quantized Standing}
\label{subsec:epoch:standing-quantization}

\begin{postulate}[Epoch-Quantized Standing]
    \label{post:epoch:standing-quantization}
    Standing is defined only for a completed epoch edge set.  For a
    proposed write set~$\actsequence{k}$, the network computes one simultaneous
    standing result from $E_k(\edgeincrement{k})$ and the proposed final pairs of
    \zcref{def:epoch:proposed-final-act-state}.

    No normative standing value exists after Registration but before a
    vouch, after a burn but before an action, or after one same-epoch act
    but before another.  Registration, newly settled burn, same-epoch
    accepted acts, all $\safethresh$-debits, and all action-count
    increments are interpreted together at closure.  The solver's iterates
    toward the current-epoch equilibrium are internal calculations; only the
    final certified result is published as epoch standing.

    The preceding epoch's standing is not an argument of any epoch-$k$
    standing map.  An implementation may use it as a warm start or cache,
    but uniqueness of the certified fixed point makes the result
    independent of initialization.
\end{postulate}

\begin{remark}[Causality without Intra-Epoch Standing]
    \label{rem:epoch:causality-without-intra-epoch-standing}
    Causal order continues to govern record formation, act identity, and
    dependency validity.  It does not induce a sequence of standing snapshots
    within an epoch, and standing reads no position within it: the solver's
    iterates are a numerical path, not a timeline.
\end{remark}


\subsection{The Standing Principles}
\label{subsec:epoch:standing-principles}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Standing is one conserved operator.  The principles below fix what that
operator may and may not do; the model of
\zcref{subsec:epoch:standing-allocation-inputs} and
\zcref{subsec:epoch:conserved-standing-transport} is their realization, and
every later theorem is answerable to them.

Each states a constraint on the class of admissible designs, not a member of
it.  A principle survives every recalibration: if every constant in this
document moved, each would read unchanged.  Formulas, coordinates, exchange
rates and grids belong to the definitions that follow, and the certificate
verifies the instance.  Where a principle names a mechanism, it names it as an
example of what it forbids, never as what it requires.

\begin{postulate}[Standing Measures; It Does Not Hold]
    \label{post:epoch:standing-is-measurement}
    Standing is a comparison coordinate computed over the record, never a
    quantity possessed within it.  Nothing the measurement does --- no
    allocation, transport, tilt, or equilibrium --- moves, encumbers, or spends
    anything an Actor owns: the ledger after the measurement is the ledger
    before it, and the transport neither mints nor burns what the ledger
    supplies (\zcref{rem:epoch:transport-is-not-ledger-transfer}).  Standing
    confers relative position, and relative position only.

    Conservation, in the principle that follows, is therefore a property of one
    epoch's measurement.  The ledger itself does change across epochs, through
    burns and debits; that is the ledger's business and not the operator's.

    This is checked, not merely argued.  The suite snapshots every ledger entry
    the solve reads, solves, and compares
    (\zcref{ver:standing:ledger-invariance}); the largest change is
    $\numval{result.standing.ledger_defect.num}$.  The postulate is the one
    place where holding \emph{by inspection of the operator} would be least
    adequate, since inspection is exactly what an implementation is free to
    diverge from.
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Standing Pair-Mass Conservation]
    \label{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}
    During standing transport, each Actor disposes of exactly one unit of
    allocation over all recipients \emph{including itself}.  The transported
    quantity is the residual pair $(\burnbal{u},\actcount{u})$.  Allocating more
    to one recipient necessarily allocates less to the others or to self: no
    transport operation creates, destroys, or exports pair mass beyond the
    source's one conserved unit.

    Conservation holds within the transport of one completed epoch state
    (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-is-measurement}).
\end{postulate}

\begin{theorem}[Standing Pair-Mass Conservation]
    \label{thm:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}
    $\sum_i\transportentry{u}{i}=1$ for every source~$u$, at every state
    $\standingvector$ and every rung $\tiltstrength{k}$.  Hence
    \[
        \sum_i\transbal{i}=\sum_u\burnbal{u},
        \qquad
        \sum_i\transcount{i}=\sum_u\actcount{u} .
    \]
    \zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation} is therefore an
    \emph{identity of the operator}, not a property of its fixed point or a
    constraint the solver must be trusted to respect.
    \proofsketch{Each hop matrix is row-stochastic by normalization; products
    and convex combinations of row-stochastic matrices are row-stochastic; and
    the emission mixture is a convex combination of a row-stochastic matrix
    with the identity (\zcref{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport}).}
\end{theorem}


\begin{postulate}[Standing Is Determined by Epoch Inclusion, Not Act Order]
    \label{post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism}
    Standing at boundary~$k$ is a function of the accepted epoch set, the final
    ledger, the title fold of \zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}, and published
    constants.  It is invariant under every dependency-compliant permutation of
    the authoritative act sequence.  No standing quantity reads host-assigned
    sub-epoch position, or intra-epoch ``latest'' by order.

    Every fold consumed by standing is therefore epoch-quantized.  Revocation is
    decided by epoch indices with ties favouring the revocation, mirroring
    settlement consent.  Formation, dependency validity, and admission may still
    read the order; standing may not.
\end{postulate}

\begin{definition}[Tentative Title Fold]
    \label{def:epoch:tentative-title-fold}
    Settlement standing reads the title fold computed on the \emph{candidate}
    final set: the same epoch-quantized fold as
    \zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}, evaluated against
    $E_k(\edgeincrement{k})$ before the write is accepted.  It is tentative in
    the only sense that matters --- the set it reads may be rejected, in which
    case nothing computed from it becomes a Layer-1 object.

    It is not tentative in order.  The fold is decided by epoch indices, and a
    settlement's standing meaning does not depend on where in the sequence its
    act sits (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism}).  Naming this
    object separately keeps that distinction visible: ``tentative'' qualifies
    the \emph{set}, never the \emph{ordering}, and a fold that resolved ties by
    position would fail the epoch-set principle no matter what it was called.
\end{definition}

\begin{postulate}[Acts Are Weighed at Their Settled Public Meaning]
    \label{post:epoch:settlement-standing-title-coupling}
    An act is weighed as what it publicly, finally means, never as what it
    merely asserts.  Same-author revision nets rather than accumulates,
    revocation suppresses, a hostile or empty gesture is not a gift, and an act
    whose meaning depends on an outcome is weighed by the outcome.

    Settlement is the sharpest instance, and the one that names this
    principle's mechanism.  Accept and Ratify produce counterparty-directed
    allocation only when their settlement candidate is recognized,
    unchallenged, and title-transferring under the epoch title fold.  A
    canceled, consumed, unauthorized, or losing settlement act is still
    weighed, and resolves to the author's self-retention channel rather than to
    the counterparty.  The title fold is consulted for this reason rather than
    by stipulation: it is where the public meaning of a settlement is settled.

    A successful transfer is \emph{event-persistent}: a later resale does not
    retroactively revoke it.  Settled meaning is settled once; what a later
    epoch may change is what is true from then on, never what an earlier epoch
    correctly weighed.
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Standing Is Memoryless]
    \label{post:epoch:standing-memorylessness}
    $\partial\epochstanding{k}{i}/\partial\epochstanding{k-1}{j}\equiv 0$ as a
    semantic dependency.  Standing is a memoryless functional of stateful
    inputs: the ledger and the title chain carry history, the standing map does
    not.

    More generally, standing reads no clock the record does not contain.
    Previous standing, a warm start, a cache, an iteration count, and every
    other state of the solver that produced the answer are alike invisible to
    it: they may change how long the measurement takes and may never change
    what it returns
    (\zcref{cor:dynamics:standing-initialization-independence}).  Two holders
    of the same completed record compute the same standing, always.
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Every Actor-Authored Act Is Weighed]
    \label{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}
    Every accepted Actor-authored act enters the allocation exactly once, at the
    act level --- a hyper-edge is one act, not two legs
    (\zcref{cor:graph:hyper-act-indivisibility}).  Every act is resolved by a
    published, deterministic, order-free rule to either a person recipient or the
    author's self-retention channel.  There is no ``role: none'' category: what is
    not allocated socially is retained by self, and is still priced, counted, and
    rate-dilutive.
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Acts Are Summed Under Published Domain Weights]
    \label{post:epoch:domain-weighted-act-sum}
    Effective folded act coefficients are summed with published nonnegative
    domain weights $\domweight{D}$.  Same-author, same-incidence bundles are
    folded before summation, so revision nets rather than accumulates.  A
    hyper-edge act carries a published act-level domain profile
    $\domprofile{D}{\foldcell}\ge 0$ with $\sum_D\domprofile{D}{\foldcell}=1$, so
    no act is double-counted across the raw domains of its projections.
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Equilibrium Standing Weighs Directed Acts, Fading with Distance]
    \label{post:epoch:hop-faded-responsive-tilt}
    At each epoch boundary --- after final-set inclusion, title folding,
    order-independent act folding, recipient resolution, and domain weighting ---
    standing and act allocation are solved simultaneously as one current-epoch
    equilibrium.

    A published tilt profile governs how recipient standing modulates allocation,
    hop by hop.  At the accepted strength $\tiltstrength{k}$ the profile is
    $\tiltprofile{\tiltstrength{k}}$ with chartered shape
    $\tiltshape{r}$.  For hop~$r$, every non-self recipient-directed score
    authored by Actor~$u$ is multiplied by the wall-clamped activation of the
    recipient's current-epoch reduced standing, raised to
    $\tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}$.  The source's self-retention score is never
    standing-modulated.  The resulting scores are normalized over self and all
    recipients: one row-stochastic allocation matrix per hop.

    Recipient standing may alter only the relative apportionment of a source's
    conserved pair mass.  It may not create a relation unsupported by the
    source's accepted acts, create or destroy source mass, read previous-epoch
    standing, or introduce act-order dependence.  Because the profile decays with
    hop index, standing speaks at full strength in the allocation of the Actor
    whose mass is flowing, and progressively less as that mass passes through
    intermediaries.

    Standing's voice is relative, and it is the \emph{only} voice: no other
    quantity may modulate the division of a source's regard among the
    recipients that source authored
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:relative-allocation-odds}).  This is a constraint on the
    design and not merely on the tilt.  Any second modulator --- a
    per-recipient export fraction, a popularity factor, a recency bonus --- is
    a violation of this principle rather than an unchartered parameter, however
    it is packaged.

    The accepted strength $\tiltstrength{k}$ is the greatest value in the
    published grid $\tiltgrid$ for which the current-epoch map has a certified
    invariant box, a unique fixed point, and a gate-decisive residual enclosure.
    The safe anchor $\tiltstrength{k}=0$ is the exact no-tilt allocation rule.
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[The Average Standing of a Closed Cluster Is Its Ledger]
    \label{post:epoch:cluster-rate-invariance}
    For any set of Actors whose base allocation has no boundary-crossing
    support, the transported-mass-weighted mean of standing equals the cluster's
    aggregate residual balance over its aggregate action mass, at every state of
    the solve.  Standing transport within a closed community is purely
    distributive: no internal arrangement of regard, tilt, or transport may raise
    or lower what the community's ledger can back.

    Any rule that \emph{deletes} pair mass in transit is therefore inadmissible,
    because deletion detaches a cluster's mean from its ledger.  A rule that
    \emph{relocates} unexported mass into its owner's own row is admissible; this
    is what source emission does
    (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}).
\end{postulate}


\subsection{Standing Allocation Inputs}
\label{subsec:epoch:standing-allocation-inputs}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Standing Fold Cell]
    \label{def:epoch:standing-fold-cell}
    A \emph{standing fold cell} $\foldcell$ is the order-free unit of standing
    input: one accepted Actor-authored act of the completed epoch set, folded
    with its same-author, same-incidence bundle
    (\zcref{def:graph:authored-act-bundle}) before any standing quantity reads
    it.  A hyper-edge act is one cell, never two
    (\zcref{cor:graph:hyper-act-indivisibility}).  The eligible set of epoch~$k$
    is $\foldcells{k}$; by \zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing} every
    accepted Actor-authored act lies in exactly one cell of it, and by
    \zcref{post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism} the fold reads epoch
    inclusion only.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Effective Act Contribution]
    \label{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}
    Each cell carries a \emph{total effective coefficient}
    $\foldcoef{\foldcell}\in[0,1]$: the geometric mean of the
    \emph{magnitudes} of the cell's mandatory folded coordinates.  A cell whose
    folded mandatory coordinates are not all positive contributes no social
    allocation and resolves to self
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}), but it still carries
    this coefficient, and carries it home.  The coefficient is total, not
    positive-quadrant: hostile and zero-stance acts are weighed, and are
    weighed home.

    Taking magnitudes is what makes the coefficient total.  On a cell whose
    coordinates are all positive it changes nothing, so no outward allocation
    moves; off that quadrant it is the difference between a defined weight and
    none, since the geometric mean of a hostile cell's signed coordinates need
    not be real at all.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Hostility Costs What Support Costs]
    \label{rem:epoch:hostility-is-priced}
    A consequence of taking magnitudes, and the reason to prefer it over any
    rule that discounts the non-positive quadrant: a maximally hostile act
    consumes exactly as much of its author's conserved unit as a maximally
    supportive one.  Attacking is not cheaper than endorsing.  A rule that
    weighed hostility below support would price attention by its direction and
    make hostility the efficient way to spend an epoch's allocation.

    The direction is still fully respected --- a hostile cell resolves home
    and gives its target nothing
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  What magnitude decides
    is the \emph{price}, not the destination.

    The endpoint is reachable and means what it says.  A cell whose stance
    folds to exactly zero has coefficient zero and contributes nothing to any
    entry, which is not an exemption restored by the back door: the act was
    admitted, debited and counted like any other
    (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}), and nothing about it is
    unweighed.  Its weight is what a stance that netted to nothing is worth.
    Note that $\basescore{u}{u}\ge\selfretention>0$ regardless
    (\zcref{def:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}), so no row can be
    emptied this way.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Standing Recipient Resolution]
    \label{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}
    The published, deterministic, order-free operator $\resolve{\foldcell}$ sends
    each cell to a person recipient or to the author's self-retention channel,
    by act class, as in \zcref{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}.  Its
    settlement rows read the epoch title fold and nothing else
    (\zcref{post:epoch:settlement-standing-title-coupling}); its revocation rows
    read epoch indices with ties favouring the revocation
    (\zcref{def:epoch:inviter-revocation}).  Coherence does not select a
    recipient, and grounded target syntax does not by itself select a non-self
    one.

    The recipient index is the epoch's \textbf{anchored} Actors: those whose
    Registration anchor is present in the completed set
    (\zcref{rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support}).  A cell whose
    syntactic target is not one of them --- a dangling identifier, which the
    record may perfectly well carry (\zcref{def:graph:anchoring}) --- has no
    person recipient available, and therefore resolves to self by the clause
    above.  This is the same rule, not an exception to it: syntax alone never
    selects a non-self recipient, and an unanchored target is exactly the case
    where syntax is all there is.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[One Index Set, and Why It Must Be Closed]
    \label{rem:epoch:allocation-index-set}
    Resolution and allocation therefore range over the same finite set, so
    $\basescore{}{}$ and $\transport{\standingvector}$ are square over the
    anchored Actors and every row of the transport is a full unit.

    The alternative --- letting a cell resolve to an unanchored identifier ---
    is not merely untidy.  Such a target would own a column and no row: it
    could receive allocation and never make any.  Row-stochasticity would be
    vacuous on the missing rows, the summation exchange of
    \zcref{thm:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity} would need a caveat about
    them, and, worst, the mediant would evaluate perfectly well at that
    column and \emph{publish a standing for an Actor that has none} ---
    contradicting \zcref{rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support} through
    arithmetic rather than through any rule anyone wrote.

    \zcref{lem:graph:dangling-neutral-fold} settles the canonical folds and
    does not reach $\basescore{}{}$ or $\transport{\standingvector}$, which
    are newer.  This is the corresponding statement for them.
\end{remark}

    \centering
    \caption{Standing recipient resolution.  Every accepted Actor-authored act
    appears exactly once.  ``Self'' is the author's own retention channel: still
    priced, still counted, still rate-dilutive.}
    \label{tbl:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}
    \begin{tabular}{ll}
        \toprule

\begin{definition}[Standing Domain Profile]
    \label{def:epoch:standing-domain-profile}
    Each cell carries a published act-level domain profile
    $\domprofile{D}{\foldcell}\ge 0$ with
    $\sum_D\domprofile{D}{\foldcell}=1$.  A single-domain act family carries a
    point mass; a hyper-edge act spreads its unit across the domains of its
    projections, so that no act is counted twice through them
    (\zcref{post:epoch:domain-weighted-act-sum}).
\end{definition}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Published domain weights.  Reference values pending the calibration
    lock; the scaling law is a calibration obligation.}
    \label{tbl:epoch:standing-domain-weights}
    \begin{tabular}{ll}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Weight} & \textbf{Reference value} \\
        \midrule
        $\domweight{D}$, every published domain $D$ & unity (uniform) \\
        $\selfretention$, the self-retention base   & unity \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{definition}[Self-Retention Base]
    \label{def:epoch:self-retention-base}
    Every Actor's own row carries the published base $\selfretention>0$ before
    any act is weighed.  It guarantees $\basescore{u}{u}>0$, hence a well-defined
    row for every anchored Actor, including one who has authored nothing.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Domain-Weighted Base Allocation]
    \label{def:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}
    For the completed epoch-$k$ state, the \emph{base allocation score} of the
    ordered Actor pair $(u,j)$ is
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}
        \basescore{u}{j}
        =
        \selfretention\,\mathbf 1_{u=j}
        +
        \sum_{\substack{\foldcell\in\foldcells{k}\\ \operatorname{src}(\foldcell)=u,\ \resolve{\foldcell}=j}}
        \foldcoef{\foldcell}\sum_D \domweight{D}\,\domprofile{D}{\foldcell}
        \;\ge\;0 ,
    \end{equation}
    with $\basescore{u}{u}\ge\selfretention>0$.  The matrix
    $\basescore{}{}$ is the sole standing-relevant reading of the epoch's acts:
    no standing quantity reads the Action Graph beyond it.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Artifact Activity Crowds Out Export]
    \label{rem:epoch:artifact-activity-crowds-out-export}
    Universal weighing has a consequence worth stating plainly, because it
    inverts an Edition-4 intuition.  Every accepted act is weighed, and acts
    that resolve to no person resolve to self
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}), so they land on
    $\basescore{u}{u}$.  Since the row is normalized, a prolific author of
    self-resolved artifacts \emph{shrinks every one of their authored
    shares}: allocation is conserved, and there is no unallocated remainder to
    draw from.  Publishing more does not spread more regard --- it concentrates
    the same unit on oneself.

    The magnitude is not marginal.  In the two-Actor fixture of
    \zcref{ver:standing:artifact-crowding}, three units of self-resolved
    coefficient take an author's outward share from
    $\numval{result.crowding.bare.num}$ to
    $\numval{result.crowding.loaded.num}$ --- a
    $\numval{result.crowding.drop.num}$ fraction of what it could otherwise
    send.  An Actor who reads the census as saying artifact activity is free
    is mispricing their whole act mix by about that much.

    This is neither a penalty nor an accident.  Under Edition~4's per-pair
    flows a source could regard many people without diluting any of them,
    which is precisely the property conservation exists to remove.  An Actor
    who wishes to carry others must \emph{spend} on them, and the currency is
    the same single unit their own activity consumes.  Note the direction:
    self-resolution reduces what a source exports; it does not raise the
    source's own standing, which reads the source's own rate through
    $\transportentry{u}{u}$ either way.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Conserved Standing Transport}
\label{subsec:epoch:conserved-standing-transport}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Standing Tilt Profile]
    \label{def:epoch:standing-tilt-profile}
    The chartered shape $\tiltshape{r}$ assigns a nonnegative exponent to each
    hop $r\in\{1,\dots,\hopmax\}$, decreasing in $r$.  At accepted strength
    $\tiltstrength{k}$ the applied profile is
    $\tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}=\tiltstrength{k}\,\tiltshape{r}$, written
    $\tiltprofile{\tiltstrength{k}}$ as a vector, and its cumulative sum through
    hop~$m$ is $\tiltcum{m}{\tiltstrength{k}}$.  Shape is preserved under
    backoff: only volume shrinks.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hop Allocation Score and Matrix]
    \label{def:epoch:hop-allocation-score}
    In reduced standing state $\standingvector$, for hop~$r$ and $j\ne u$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:hop-allocation-score}
        s^{(r)}_{uj}(\standingvector)
        = \basescore{u}{j}\;
          \wallactivation{\standingstate{j}}^{\tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}},
        \qquad
        s^{(r)}_{uu} = \basescore{u}{u} ,
    \end{equation}
    the self score being unmodulated.  Normalizing each row over self and all
    recipients gives the \emph{hop allocation matrix}
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:hop-allocation-matrix}
        \hopalloc{r}{u}{j}{\standingvector}
        = \frac{s^{(r)}_{uj}(\standingvector)}{\sum_v s^{(r)}_{uv}(\standingvector)},
        \qquad
        \hopmatrix{r}{\standingvector}
        = \bigl[\hopalloc{r}{u}{j}{\standingvector}\bigr]_{u,j},
    \end{equation}
    row-stochastic at every state by construction.
    \label{def:epoch:hop-allocation-matrix}
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[The Exponent Belongs to the Transported Mass]
    \label{rem:epoch:mass-owner-relative-hop-order}
    Hop~$1$ is always the source-adjacent factor.  The mass apportioned at
    hop~$r$ of a product $\hopmatrix{1}{}\cdots\hopmatrix{m}{}$ originated
    $r-1$ hops upstream, so the fading is read \emph{mass-owner-relative}: one
    author's row renders at hop-$1$ strength when it apportions that author's
    own pair, and at hop-$r$ strength when it relays the pair of a source
    $r-1$ hops away.  The exponent belongs to the transported mass, never to
    the row.  Reading it the other way --- as though an Actor's regard had a
    single strength fixed by who authored it --- makes the whole fence
    unprovable, because the same row would then have to carry two exponents at
    once.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Relative Allocation Odds]
    \label{prop:epoch:relative-allocation-odds}
    For any two non-self recipients $j,j'$ of the same source~$u$ at hop~$r$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:relative-allocation-odds}
        \frac{\hopalloc{r}{u}{j}{\standingvector}}
             {\hopalloc{r}{u}{j'}{\standingvector}}
        = \frac{\basescore{u}{j}}{\basescore{u}{j'}}
          \left(
            \frac{\wallactivation{\standingstate{j}}}
                 {\wallactivation{\standingstate{j'}}}
          \right)^{\tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}} ,
    \end{equation}
    independent of every other entry of the row and of the normalization.  The
    tilt is therefore the \emph{sole} modulator of a source's relative
    allocation odds: nothing else in the construction can reorder whom a source
    favours, and any proposed rule that varies across a source's recipients ---
    a per-recipient emission fraction, for instance --- is a second
    odds-modulator and is prohibited
    (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Rival Allocation Response]
    \label{prop:epoch:rival-allocation-response}
    Fix hop~$r$ and row~$u$.  For every recipient coordinate $j\ne u$ and every
    entry~$v$, including $v=u$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:rival-allocation-response}
        \frac{\partial\hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{\standingvector}}{\partial \standingstate{j}}
        =
        \tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}\,
        \wallvouchgain{\standingstate{j}}\,
        \hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{\standingvector}
        \bigl(\mathbf 1_{\set{v=j}}-\hopalloc{r}{u}{j}{\standingvector}\bigr),
    \end{equation}
    with the Clarke interval $[0,\wallgaincap]$ replacing
    $\wallvouchgain{\standingstate{j}}$ at the wall kink.  Consequently:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Rivalry is conservative per row:}
              $\sum_v\partial_j\hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{\standingvector}=0$ --- a
              rising recipient gains exactly what every sibling \emph{and the
              self-share} lose.  The case $v=u$ is pure denominator loss, not a
              separate rule.
        \item \textbf{Wall flatness:} below the safety wall every derivative
              vanishes.  A below-wall recipient is level-discounted but
              dynamically inert, at every hop.
        \item \textbf{Row independence of own standing:} row~$u$ does not
              depend on $\standingstate{u}$, because the self score is
              unmodulated, so standing never directly defends its own
              retention.  This removes only the \emph{direct} self-channel;
              diagonal Jacobian terms arising through other Actors' rows remain
              and are priced by the certificate.
    \end{enumerate}
    This is the only normative statement of the allocation derivative.  Every
    certificate, fence, and screen in this document consumes
    \zcref{eq:epoch:rival-allocation-response} and no other form.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Standing Support Preservation]
    \label{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}
    The wall-clamped activation is strictly positive, so raising it to any
    exponent cannot zero a score, and normalization preserves which entries
    vanish.  Hence for every hop~$r$, every state $\standingvector$, and every
    rung $\tiltstrength{k}$,
    \[
        \hopalloc{r}{u}{j}{\standingvector}>0
        \iff
        \basescore{u}{j}>0 ,
    \]
    and the support of $\transport{\standingvector}$ is fixed by the base
    matrix together with the ledger: a source with zero balance emits nothing
    to others (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}) and retains an identity row,
    and every other support question is answered by reachability in
    $\basescore{}{}$ at the supported depths.

    The consequence is procedural and load-bearing: \textbf{who contributes to
    whom is checkable before the solve}, independently of $\standingvector$ and
    of the accepted rung.  Contributing sets, cluster closure, and the widths
    that the safety threshold consumes are therefore properties of published
    data, not of a fixed point that has not yet been computed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Standing Depth Mass]
    \label{def:epoch:standing-depth-mass}
    The published depth mass $\depthmass{m}\ge 0$, $m\in\{1,\dots,\hopmax\}$,
    satisfies $\sum_m\depthmass{m}=1$.  Its deepest supported index is
    $\suppdepth=\max\{m:\depthmass{m}>0\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Source Emission]
    \label{def:epoch:source-emission}
    History travels on the back of balance.  The \emph{emission fraction} of
    source~$u$ is
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:source-emission}
        \emission{u}
        = \min\Bigl(1,\ \frac{\burnbal{u}}{\safethresh\,\actcount{u}}\Bigr)
        = \min\Bigl(1,\ \frac{\refrate{u}}{\safefloor}\Bigr)\in[0,1] ,
    \end{equation}
    the source's own reduced rate measured against the safety wall and capped at
    one; no constant beyond the chartered pair $(\safethresh,\numeraire)$ enters.
    The middle form is numéraire-free outright --- $\numeraire$ does not occur in
    it --- so the reduced form's invariance is inherited rather than assumed, and
    the exported capacity $\burnbal{u}/\safethresh$ \emph{is} the ledger's
    remaining-action capacity up to integrality.  The emission diagonal is
    $\emissionmat=\operatorname{diag}(\emission{u})$.

    Emission is a property of the source's pair, never of one of its relations:
    a per-recipient fraction $\emission{uj}$ is prohibited, because the tilt is
    the sole chartered modulator of a source's relative allocation odds
    (\zcref{post:epoch:hop-faded-responsive-tilt}).  With that premise the
    scaling is uniform across the row, and the emitted operator of
    \zcref{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport} is the only rule
    satisfying conservation, cluster rate invariance, the export cap, and
    self-as-sink.  Scaling base scores before normalization is a mathematical
    no-op and is prohibited; damping inside a hop matrix would charge a relay for
    its source's obligation and is equally prohibited.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite-Depth Conserved Transport]
    \label{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport}
    The \emph{conserved transport} of epoch~$k$ applies source emission to the
    depth-mass mixture of hop products:
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport}
        \transport{\standingvector}
        = \emissionmat\sum_{m=1}^{\hopmax}\depthmass{m}\,\transportm{m}{\standingvector}
          + \bigl(\idmat-\emissionmat\bigr),
        \qquad
        \transportm{m}{\standingvector}
        = \hopmatrix{1}{\standingvector}\cdots\hopmatrix{m}{\standingvector} .
    \end{equation}
    Hop~$1$ is always the source-adjacent factor: the mass being apportioned is
    the source's own, and the profile is read mass-owner-relative.  Emission is
    applied once, to the finished mixture: inside a hop it would compound as
    $\emission{u}^{m}$ and silently reprice the depth mass, and a depleted relay
    must pass a solvent source's history on at full strength.  The un-emitted
    mixture is written $\transportraw{}(\standingvector)$ where the emission step
    itself is under discussion; it is solver-internal, and
    $\transport{\standingvector}$ --- emitted --- is the published operator that
    the mediant, the certificate, and every boundary artifact consume.

    Products and convex combinations of row-stochastic matrices are
    row-stochastic, and the emission mixture is itself a convex combination of a
    row-stochastic matrix with the identity, so $\sum_i\transportentry{u}{i}=1$
    identically --- \zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation} is an
    identity of the operator, not a property of its fixed point.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Transport Is Not Ledger Transfer]
    \label{rem:epoch:transport-is-not-ledger-transfer}
    $\transport{}$ transports pairs \emph{for comparison}; the ledger
    transfers nothing.  No balance moves between addresses, no count is
    reassigned, and the imported frame's non-transferability
    (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}) is untouched: after the solve,
    every $\burnbal{u}$ and $\actcount{u}$ is exactly where the ledger put
    it.  Transport is a virtual, conserved re-weighting of whose pairs are
    consulted in whose mediant --- a reading of the ledger, never an
    operation on it.  The word ``transfer'' in standing prose is a defect.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Emission Self-Inertia]
    \label{rem:epoch:emission-self-inertia}
    Unexported mass returns home:
    \begin{equation*}
        \transportentry{u}{u}
        = \emission{u}\,\transportraw{uu} + (1-\emission{u})
        \;\ge\; \transportraw{uu} .
    \end{equation*}
    A depleted Actor's own row therefore weights its own near-zero rate
    \emph{more} heavily than under full-pair transport, and the inbound-regard
    lift channel (\zcref{rem:gates:propped}) weakens in proportion to the
    retained mass $(1-\emission{u})\bigl(1-\transportraw{uu}\bigr)\actcount{u}$.
    Rehabilitation by burning is unaffected --- strengthened, in fact: one burn
    raises $\burnbal{u}$, $\refrate{u}$ and $\emission{u}$ together, so recovery
    remains a price, never a ban.  The asymmetry is intended --- history that
    cannot be backed should not be laundered away by admiration --- but it is a
    behavioural change from full-pair transport, stated here rather than
    inherited silently: \emph{whom a depleted Actor can be rehabilitated by}
    shifts from the community toward the Actor's own ledger.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Emission Conserves and Complies]
    \label{cor:epoch:conserving-emission}
    The emitted transport is row-stochastic, and a closed cluster's identity
    survives it verbatim.  Row sums are $\emission{u}\cdot1+(1-\emission{u})=1$;
    and because emission relocates a source's unexported mass onto that
    source's own diagonal, which lies inside any cluster containing the source,
    no term of \zcref{eq:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity} moves
    (\zcref{post:epoch:cluster-rate-invariance}).  Emission is a member of the
    admissible class rather than an exception to it
    (\zcref{cor:epoch:conserving-source-root-criterion}).
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Emission Export Bound]
    \label{thm:epoch:emission-export-bound}
    No Actor exports more history than its present balance could pay for at
    today's action price:
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:emission-export-bound}
        \sum_{j\ne u}\transportentry{u}{j}\,\actcount{u}
        \;=\;
        \emission{u}\,\actcount{u}\sum_{j\ne u}\transportraw{uj}
        \;\le\;
        \min\Bigl(\actcount{u},\ \frac{\burnbal{u}}{\safethresh}\Bigr) .
    \end{equation}
    The first bound is the full-pair ceiling, which emission cannot exceed; the
    second is the capacity reading, and it is the sharper one exactly when the
    source is faded.

    The exported ceiling $\burnbal{u}/\safethresh$ is the ledger's
    remaining-action capacity up to integrality: the number of acts the balance
    could still pay for is the number of acts of history it can still carry.
    That coincidence is the whole content of the chartered rule, and it is why
    no new constant was minted to state it.
    \proofsketch{Substitute
    $\transportentry{u}{j}=\emission{u}\transportraw{uj}$ for $j\ne u$, bound
    the row sum by one, and apply the two branches of the minimum in
    \zcref{eq:epoch:source-emission}.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Emission Wall Symmetry]
    \label{rem:epoch:emission-wall-symmetry}
    One chartered coordinate governs both faces of the wall.  Below
    $\safefloor$ an Actor's standing does not respond
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:safety-wall-clamp}) and its history does not fully
    carry (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}); at $\safefloor$ emission
    saturates exactly.  The kink of $\emission{}$ lives in \emph{ledger} space,
    not state space, so it contributes nothing to the standing Jacobian --- which
    is why the certificate never has to enclose it.

    One coupling across boundaries is recorded here so it is not rediscovered
    as a circularity.  Emission shrinks contributing widths; a smaller
    $\locwidth{}$ lowers the next epoch's $\safethresh$ under the interim rule;
    and a lower wall raises marginal emission.  That is feedback \emph{across}
    epochs, not within one --- both reads consume the prior certificate --- and
    it is already governed by the threshold's step bound and hysteresis
    (\zcref{def:epoch:safety-threshold}, R3 and R4).
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Artifacts Allocate Nothing]
    \label{prop:epoch:artifact-non-allocation}
    Changing raw incidence on a passive artifact --- a Chat, Content item,
    Item, Type, Comment, Message, Offer, or Profile --- leaves every entry of
    $\basescore{}{}$ unchanged, and therefore leaves every transported share
    and every standing value unchanged.

    The reason is structural rather than a guard: only accepted Actor-authored
    acts fold into cells, and only cells contribute
    (\zcref{eq:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}).  An artifact has no row
    to allocate from and no authorship to inherit, so there is no channel to
    close.  Popularity is visible to feed and bridge, and invisible here.
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Conserved Standing Map]
    \label{def:epoch:conserved-standing-map}
    For an epoch whose every anchored source carries $\actcount{u}\ge 1$
    (Registration is an accepted act), the current-epoch standing map is the
    transported pair mediant
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:conserved-standing-map}
        \standingmap{k}{i}{\standingvector}
        = \frac{\sum_u \transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u}\,\refrate{u}}
               {\sum_u \transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u}},
        \qquad
        \transbal{i} = \sum_u \transportentry{u}{i}\,\burnbal{u},
        \quad
        \transcount{i} = \sum_u \transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u} .
    \end{equation}
    The count guard matters: the pair form equals the mediant only while every
    transporting source has a positive action count.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Conserved Standing Equilibrium]
    \label{def:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium}
    The epoch's standing state is the fixed point
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium}
        \standingeq = \standingmapvector{k}{\standingeq},
        \qquad
        \standingeq\in\hullbox{k},
    \end{equation}
    solved once, in the current epoch, from the completed final state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tilt Backoff Grid]
    \label{def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid}
    The published grid $\tiltgrid$ is finite with chartered depth
    $\tiltgriddepth$ and terminates at zero.  The accepted strength
    $\tiltstrength{k}$ is its greatest element whose certificate passes; the
    anchor $\tiltstrength{k}=0$ is the exact no-tilt allocation rule and always
    certifies.

    Backoff preserves the shape exactly:
    $\frac{d}{dx}\log\wallactivation{x}^{\tiltexp{r}{t}}
    = t\,\tiltshape{r}\,\wallvouchgain{x}$, so a lower rung is the \emph{same
    signal at lower volume}, never a signal substitution.  What is monotone
    in~$t$ is the certified \emph{bound}, which is linear in it; the exact
    supremum $\sup_{\hullbox{k}}\norm{D\standingmapvector{k}{}}_\infty$ is
    \textbf{not} asserted monotone, and soundness requires that each rung be
    independently certified rather than inferred from a higher one.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Tilt Backoff Is Not Export Backoff]
    \label{rem:epoch:tilt-backoff-is-not-export-backoff}
    Lowering $\tiltstrength{k}$ reduces \emph{discrimination among
    recipients}; it does not, in general, reduce a source's total non-self
    allocation, which is set by the base scores and self-retention.  A backoff
    says how sharply standing tilts the division, never that less standing was
    exported --- that quantity is emission's
    (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}), on a different axis.  Conversely, a
    ledger-rate tilt is not a rung of $\tiltgrid$: switching the tilt's input
    from the standing verdict to the ledger rate mid-protocol would be a
    silent semantics change, and remains a separately charterable policy only.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[A Rung Can Fail Two Ways, and They Are Not the Same Failure]
    \label{rem:epoch:certificate-failure-versus-indecisive-enclosure}
    A rung is accepted only on a passing certificate, so both failure modes
    below are safe --- but they must not be confused, and the certificate must
    say which occurred.

    A \emph{certificate failure} is a proof: the verified enclosure establishes
    that the margined fence does not hold at that rung, on that epoch's graph.
    The correct response is the next rung down, and the signal is real ---
    the graph moved.

    An \emph{indecisive enclosure} proves nothing: the interval arithmetic is
    too wide to separate $\marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}$ from one.  Backing
    off is sound but not indicated; the answer is a tighter enclosure, and
    tightening it may certify the same rung unchanged.  Reporting
    indecisiveness as instability would make the tilt strength a function of
    the verifier's numerical hygiene rather than of the network, and would
    corrupt exactly the calibration series that the backoff depth
    $\tiltgriddepth$ is meant to be chosen from.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Act Folding and Net Stance}
\label{subsec:epoch:act-folding}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Net Stance]
    \label{def:epoch:net-stance}
    For every eligible same-author parallel bundle
    $\actbundle{a,s,t,f}$ of
    \zcref{def:graph:authored-act-bundle}, the epoch compiler forms the
    effective authored coordinates
    \[
        \netpd{a\to t}
        =
        \operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
        \left(
            \sum_{e\in\actbundle{a,s,t,f}}p_d(e)
        \right),
        \qquad
        \netpi{a\to t}
        =
        \operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
        \left(
            \sum_{e\in\actbundle{a,s,t,f}}p_i(e)
        \right).
    \]

    The fold is per author, family, source, target, and full incidence;
    it never nets across authors.  For a complete hyper-edge family,
    each accepted act retains its public complete-act identity
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection}); the compiler may fold revisions of
    the same authored semantic incidence but may not pair independently
    folded A- and T-legs, replace an A-leg with unrelated incoming
    weight, or create a complete act from unmatched records.

    Excluded from stance aggregation:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item derived Self-edge components, which are not authored
              records;
        \item settlement records whose individual authored coordinates
              are consumed directly (Accept and Ratify;
              recognition likewise reads individual records,
              \zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition});
        \item control records (Withdraw, Rescind, Leave, and
              De-invite/A$\cdot$T);
        \item every family that resolves to its author where the
              fold would otherwise be used only to create standing.
    \end{itemize}

    Feed ranking, raw signed traversal, CAN, title, payload display, and
    settlement recognition continue to read their declared raw-record
    or raw-bundle inputs.  Net stance is one input to complete
    act folding, not a mutation or deletion of the public
    record; it never merges, hides, or removes payload projections,
    which remain individually visible and individually removable
    (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Compiled Acts Fold Into Standing Cells]
    \label{rem:epoch:compiled-acts-fold-into-cells}
    After the per-author net-stance fold and inviter revocation, the
    compiler groups the accepted acts of one full incidence into folded
    cells (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-fold-cell}).  \textbf{Every} cell bears
    standing (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}); there is no
    eligibility predicate deciding which do.  What the mandatory coordinates
    decide is the \emph{destination}: a cell with strictly positive mandatory
    coordinates, live authored consent, author ownership and an anchored
    person target may resolve outward, and every other cell resolves home
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).  Both are weighed, and
    both are priced by the same coefficient
    (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}).

    The mandatory coordinates are family-specific, and every accepted family
    has them, because under universal weighing every cell carries a
    coefficient.  For the initial census:
    \[
    \begin{array}{c|c|c}
        \text{family} & \text{mandatory coordinates} & \text{may resolve outward}\\
        \hline
        \text{Opinion}      & p_d,\ p_i & \text{yes}\\
        \text{Reference}    & e,\ f     & \text{yes}\\
        \text{Invitation}   & u,\ f,\ r & \text{yes}\\
        \text{Accept}       & c,\ e     & \text{yes}\\
        \text{Ratify}       & c,\ e     & \text{yes}\\
        \hline
        \text{Publish}      & a         & \text{no}\\
        \text{Owner}        & a         & \text{no}\\
        \text{Affinity}     & a,\ t     & \text{no}\\
        \text{Tag}          & r,\ c     & \text{no}\\
        \text{Review}       & e,\ f     & \text{no}\\
        \text{Send}         & i         & \text{no}\\
        \text{Bid}          & g,\ u     & \text{no}\\
        \text{Join Request} & u,\ f     & \text{no}\\
        \text{Participant}  & i,\ r     & \text{no}\\
        \hline
        \text{Registration, Withdraw, Rescind,} & \text{---} & \text{no}\\
        \text{Leave, De-invite} & &
    \end{array}
    \]
    The two blocks answer two different questions and should not be run
    together.  For an outward-capable family, the coordinates must be
    \emph{strictly positive} for the cell to resolve to a person, and their
    magnitudes then price it.  For the rest, the coordinates only ever price:
    the cell resolves home whatever they are, so there is no positivity gate
    to fail and a negative coordinate costs its author exactly what the
    positive one would (\zcref{rem:epoch:hostility-is-priced}).  The last row
    carries no authored coordinate at all, so the geometric mean is empty and
    the coefficient is~$1$: a Registration or a control record is weighed at
    full magnitude, and its author pays for it accordingly.

    Where a family's legs carry separate coordinates, the mandatory set is the
