    \textbf{A-leg}'s.  A T-leg records where the act points, not what its
    author felt about pointing there, and a coordinate that is semantically
    vacuous in some instantiations of its family must not move that author's
    coefficient in those instantiations.

    An Invitation coordinate is absent while suppressed by
    \zcref{def:epoch:inviter-revocation}, and no control record itself
    resolves outward.

    The resolution rule is local and order-free once the epoch record set
    and bundle folds are fixed, and it has no glyph: it picks a destination
    for a public, complete, Actor-authored relation, not a score.  Raw
    determinant parity remains a terminal coherence observable, neither
    necessary nor sufficient to direct allocation outward; a coherent-hostile
    $(-,-)$ person-directed relation fails the positive-coordinate clause and
    is weighed home at its own magnitude
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:hostility-is-priced}).
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Person-Vouch Compilation Properties]
    \label{prop:epoch:act-folding-properties}
    Fold-cell compilation is:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Author-owned.}
              Every cell is sourced by the author of the
              complete act that creates it.

        \item \textbf{Passive-independent.}
              Passive context may identify the act and its semantic
              target but contributes no upstream standing weight.

        \item \textbf{Standing-atomic.}
              A complete hyper-edge contributes once or not at all
              (\zcref{cor:graph:standing-act-atomicity}).

        \item \textbf{Record-preserving.}
              Incomplete, hostile, suppressed, and self-resolving records
              remain public and available to every non-standing consumer
              that declares them.

        \item \textbf{Range-safe.}
              The cell coefficient of
              \zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution} lies in $[0,1]$,
              the endpoints included and both reachable.

        \item \textbf{Self-inclusive.}
              A cell that resolves to its author lands on the diagonal of
              the base matrix, where it is priced and counted like any
              other (\zcref{def:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}).
              There is no projected edge for it to be excluded from: the
              diagonal is a destination, not a defect.

        \item \textbf{Deterministic.}
              Two participants holding the same $E_k$, bundle folds,
              census, and constants compile the same cells with the same
              coefficients and the same recipients.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Folding Precedes Allocation]
    \label{rem:epoch:folding-precedes-allocation}
    Folding is a compiler, not a condition evaluated during transport.  It
    reconstructs complete acts, applies bundle folds and revocations, resolves
    each cell to a recipient or to self, and emits the base allocation matrix.
    Only then does anything allocate.

    This order is load-bearing.  A passive artifact cannot enter the base
    matrix, so it cannot enter any hop of the transport either --- the
    exclusion happens once, in the compiler, rather than being re-checked at
    every depth.  Raw feed and signed services continue to traverse the Action
    Graph independently, and read nothing from this matrix.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Control Acts Resolve to Self]
    \label{rem:epoch:control-acts-resolve-to-self}
    Withdraw, Rescind, Leave, and De-invite/A$\cdot$T are accepted acts, so
    universal weighing does weigh them
    (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}).  What they do not do is
    resolve towards a counterparty: recipient resolution sends them to self
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}), so they consume their
    author's allocation without directing any of it outward.

    This is a stronger statement than Edition~4's exclusion, and a more honest
    one.  Under a census these acts were invisible to standing; under
    conservation they are visible and cost their author exactly what any other
    act costs, which is the correct price for using the graph.

    The De-invite/T leg illustrates why this semantic exclusion is
    necessary: its fixed raw parameters are positive, but the act
    expresses revocation, not praise.  Treating raw positivity as
    vouching would turn expulsion into standing support
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:control-self-retention}).  The
    control family never enters the standing projection; its only
    standing-visible effect is the per-author suppression of the
    corresponding Invitation act under
    \zcref{def:epoch:inviter-revocation}.

    Raw feed traversal may still observe Minimal-weight control records
    as attention.  Attention is not standing.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Aggregation Properties]
    \label{prop:epoch:net-stance-properties}
    (1)~\emph{Order-stable}: the sum is commutative and the $\prec$-maximum is
    determined by the authoritative order, so the compilation is a function of
    the ordered history $\actsequence{k}$
    (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism} extends). (2)~\emph{Range-safe}: the
    clip returns parameters to the master formula's domain, so every existing
    ceiling ($\wmax$, $\wmaxop$, the coupling cap) is untouched.
    (3)~\emph{Person-vouch gate}: a net-hostile mixed-sign stance and a
    coherent-hostile stance $(-,-)$ alike fail the strictly-positive
    coordinate clause of \zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution} and compile no
    person-vouch, whatever their raw parity
    (\zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law}).  Net near zero is
    routing-inert (\zcref{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy}); withdrawal is
    continuous, not a cliff. (4)~\emph{Priced}: every revision edge
    increments $\actcount{a}$, irrevocably diluting $\commitrate{a}$.
    (5)~\emph{Append-only untouched}: records are immutable; only the ongoing
    effect is steerable --- revocation as a derived quantity.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Conviction Has Inertia]
    \label{rem:epoch:conviction-inertia}
    Sum-then-clip is chosen over the order-free alternative (latest-edge-wins on the
    $\prec$-chain) deliberately: walking back accumulated conviction costs
    counter-edges in proportion to it, so flip-flopping is expensive and stance is
    sticky --- the same ethos as irrevocability, relaxed to
    steerable-but-priced. \zcref{subsec:necessity:average-based-aggregation}'s
    anti-summation argument does not apply: that argument concerns cross-author
    node aggregation saturating the clamp; this sum is per-author, parameter-level,
    and the clip \emph{is} the range guard. Note one corner closed by the
    typed sign architecture: a bundle netted negative in \emph{both} parameters
    carries $\detsign{}=+1$ (the Quadrant Law,
    \zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law}) and therefore remains coherent for routing,
    but it fails the person-vouch predicate
    (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}) and compiles no vouch.  Full
    withdrawal still targets net zero; overshoot into coherent hostility
    produces no person-vouch because one or more mandatory semantic
    coordinates are non-positive.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Severance Is Not Represented]
    \label{rem:epoch:severance-blindness}
    Whether a net-zeroing is a change of opinion or a pre-departure scrub is a fact
    about a person, and persons are Layer~2
    (\zcref{rem:comparator:identity-is-layer-2}); the network cannot and does not
    distinguish them. Outgoing authored stance remains epoch-live through
    the declared per-author folds and complete-act compiler: a
    source-relative path uses the current certified projected edge of
    each author, and no Actor may erase inbound acts authored by others.
    What \zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave} protects is the \emph{inbound}
    structure others authored --- which no one but its authors can net.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Inviter Revocation]
    \label{def:epoch:inviter-revocation}
    For author~$a$, Chat~$C$, and Profile~$P$, let $R(a,C,P) \subseteq E_k$
    be $a$'s Invitation and De-invite records with middle~$C$ and
    terminus~$P$.  In complete person-vouch compilation, actor~$a$'s
    Invitation act toward $(C,P)$ is \emph{absent} iff the latest
    \textbf{epoch index} represented in $R(a,C,P)$ contains a De-invite ---
    ties within an epoch favouring the revocation, and a later complete
    Invitation at a subsequent epoch re-establishing the act.

    The rule is \emph{epoch-quantized, not order-read}, and that is
    obligatory rather than stylistic: this fold feeds person-vouch
    compilation, and no standing quantity may read host-assigned order or any
    intra-epoch ``latest''
    (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism}).  Selecting the
    $\prec$-maximal element of $R(a,C,P)$ would do exactly that --- the
    authoritative order is free among acts with no declared dependency
    between them, so a host could decide suppression by placement.  The tie
    rule replaces that choice with a published constant, mirroring settlement
    consent.  Suppression is
    strictly per author: a De-invite never affects another author's
    Invitation (netting across authors
    remains prohibited, \zcref{def:epoch:net-stance}), and it is a
    suppression predicate, not a parameter contribution --- no control
    edge enters any stance sum.

    This is the sole compilation-visible effect of the conversational
    control family, and it closes a genuine gap: Invitation relevance is
    non-negative ($r \in [0,1]$), so sum-then-clip netting is monotone
    non-decreasing and the invitation-vouch would otherwise be the one
    authored vouch its author cannot withdraw.  \textbf{Conviction sums;
    consent toggles}: stance bundles aggregate with inertia
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:conviction-inertia}), but a vouch-of-fitness is live
    consent, and live consent is latest-record-wins --- the same
    cancel-over-commit shape as settlement's epoch-quantized consent rule
    (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}, clauses~(iv),(v)).  Each
    toggle is a priced action; oscillation dilutes
    $\commitrate{a}$ irrevocably.
    Suppression is a compilation rule of the standing consumer
    (\zcref{rem:graph:authored-act-bundle-consumers}), not a third bundle semantics.
\end{definition}


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Projected Vouch Activation}
\label{subsec:epoch:vouch-activation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Responsive Projected Vouch Activation]
    \label{def:epoch:responsive-vouch-activation}
    Work in reduced standing
    \[
        x=\refstanding{i}=\standing{i}/\numeraire,
        \qquad
        p(x)=\frac{x}{1+x}.
    \]
    The non-temporal normalized deployed core is
    \[
        \vouchcore{p}
        =
        \frac{Q(p)}{Q(1)},
        \qquad
        Q(p)
        =
        \sigmoid{\invtemp p}
        \sqrt{
            \tanh p\,
            \bigl(1-\bleedparam^2\tanh p\bigr)
        },
    \]
    and the responsive projected per-hop standing activation is
    \begin{equation}
        \vouchactivation{x}
        \coloneqq
        \vouchcore{p(x)}^{\actexponent},
        \qquad
        \hopmax=4.
        \label{eq:epoch:responsive-vouch-activation}
    \end{equation}

    The responsive activation is:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item zero at zero standing;
        \item strictly increasing in standing;
        \item less than one at every finite standing;
        \item independent of raw edge maturity and temporal entropy.
    \end{enumerate}

    Its reduced-standing log-gain is one quarter of the full deployed
    core gain:
    \[
        \vouchgain{x}
        =
        \frac{d}{dx}\log\vouchactivation{x}
        =
        \actexponent
        \frac{d}{dx}\log\vouchcore{p(x)}.
    \]
    Every transported chain through at most $\hopmax$ live Actor
    targets therefore consumes at most one full-$Q$ log-gain budget; the
    graph-dependent use of that budget is certified in
    \zcref{app:dynamics}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Safety-Wall-Clamped Vouch Activation]
    \label{def:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation}
    Every standing stage evaluates the \emph{effective} activation
    \begin{equation}
        \wallactivation{x}
        \coloneqq
        \vouchactivation{\max(x,\safefloor)}.
        \label{eq:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation}
    \end{equation}
    It reads only the current standing state~$x$: there is no
    previous-standing input and no externally supplied activation mode.
    Below the safety wall
    $\safefloor$ the activation is constant with zero derivative; above it
    the activation is responsive; at the wall it is continuous with a
    generalized gain interval.  The clamp is a within-epoch analytic
    device: activation does not pay $\safethresh$, create source, or grant
    admission.  Its properties are proved in
    \zcref{prop:dynamics:safety-wall-clamp}.
\end{definition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Raw Signed Double-Cover Service}
\label{subsec:epoch:raw-signed-service}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The double-cover traversal remains a public Layer~1 raw graph service
for consumers that require signed raw-path evidence, including the
canonical bridge-consent calculation.  It does not compute standing.

\paragraph{Determinant sign and raw signed paths.}
Every edge carries a \emph{determinant sign}
$\detsign{e} = \operatorname{sgn}(\det(\pathview{e})) \in \set{+1,-1}$
(\zcref{def:graph:determinant-sign}), extracted as a one-bit
observation of the \PathView{} determinant already computed for
feed-ranking.  No additional per-edge computation is introduced beyond
sign detection.  Along a viable path $p = (e_1, \ldots, e_d)$, signs
multiply:
\begin{equation}
    \detsign{p}
    = \prod_{e \in p} \detsign{e}
    = \operatorname{sgn}(\det(\pathmatrix{p})),
    \label{eq:epoch:path-sign}
\end{equation}
which follows from \zcref{thm:graph:determinant-product} and requires
no new proof.

\begin{remark}[Parity Product, Not Classical Structural Balance]
    \label{rem:epoch:parity-not-balance}
    The rule that the raw signed service separates positive- from
    negative-parity paths has a motivational analogy in structural
    balance theory\footcite{heider1946attitudes,cartwright1956structural}:
    balanced cycles have an even number of negative links.  This analogy
    is purely motivational.  The operational rule derives from the
    double cover parity construction\footcite{zaslavsky1982signed}
    below, not from a structural balance hypothesis.  The closest
    modern empirical comparison is signed-link prediction in online
    social networks\footcite{leskovec2010predicting}.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Double cover BFS state.}

\begin{definition}[Double Cover BFS State]
    \label{def:epoch:double-cover-bfs-state}
    For source actor~$j$, each node $v \in V$ carries:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item $\posreg{v}$: maximum product weight over positive-parity
              paths from~$j$ to~$v$.
        \item $\negreg{v}$: maximum product weight over negative-parity
              paths from~$j$ to~$v$.
    \end{itemize}
    \textit{Initialization:}
    $\posreg{j} = 1$, $\negreg{j} = 0$;
    $\posreg{v} = \negreg{v} = 0$ for all $v \neq j$.
\end{definition}


\begin{algorithm}
    \caption{Exact Signed Raw Traversal.
    Returns the raw positive- and negative-parity registers
    $\posreg{v},\negreg{v}$ for every reached node~$v$, exactly and
    without any pruning threshold.}
    \label{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}%
    \phantomsection\label{alg:epoch:exact-signed-raw-traversal}
    \begin{algorithmic}[1]
        \State \textbf{Input:} Source actor~$j$, raw snapshot
               $\rawgraph{k}$
               (\zcref{def:graph:raw-traversal-snapshot}),
               depth bound~$L$
        \State $W_0^{+}(j) \gets 1$;\; $W_0^{-}(j) \gets 0$;\;
               all other depth-zero registers $\gets 0$
        \State $\posreg{j} \gets 1$;\; $\negreg{j} \gets 0$;\;
               $\posreg{v} \gets 0$,\; $\negreg{v} \gets 0$
               \quad for all $v \neq j$
        \For{$d = 1$ \textbf{to} $L$}
            \State $W_d^{+}(v), W_d^{-}(v) \gets 0$ for every node~$v$
            \ForAll{directed raw snapshot edges $e: v \to w$}
                \State $\dampedweight{e}
                       \gets \detscore{e}
                       \cdot \sqrt{1 + \tau_e^2}
                       \cdot \boltzfactor{\tentropy{e}}$
                \State $\detsign{e}
                       \gets \operatorname{sgn}(\det(\pathview{e}))$
                \If{$\detsign{e} = +1$}
                    \State $W_d^{+}(w) \gets
                           \max\!\bigl(W_d^{+}(w),\;
                           W_{d-1}^{+}(v) \cdot \dampedweight{e}\bigr)$
                    \State $W_d^{-}(w) \gets
                           \max\!\bigl(W_d^{-}(w),\;
                           W_{d-1}^{-}(v) \cdot \dampedweight{e}\bigr)$
                \ElsIf{$\detsign{e} = -1$}
                    \State $W_d^{+}(w) \gets
                           \max\!\bigl(W_d^{+}(w),\;
                           W_{d-1}^{-}(v) \cdot \dampedweight{e}\bigr)$
                    \State $W_d^{-}(w) \gets
                           \max\!\bigl(W_d^{-}(w),\;
                           W_{d-1}^{+}(v) \cdot \dampedweight{e}\bigr)$
                \Else
                    \State skip $e$
                           \Comment{routing-inert zero-determinant edge}
                \EndIf
            \EndFor
            \State $\posreg{v} \gets \max(\posreg{v}, W_d^{+}(v))$,\;
                   $\negreg{v} \gets \max(\negreg{v}, W_d^{-}(v))$
                   for every node~$v$
        \EndFor
        \State \Return $\posreg{v},\negreg{v}$
               for all reached nodes~$v$
    \end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}


\begin{lemma}[Exact Signed Raw Traversal: Correctness and Complexity]
    \label{lem:epoch:double-cover-bfs-correctness}
    \zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs} correctly and exactly computes the
    maximum raw positive- and negative-parity path products through
    depth~$L$ for the raw snapshot supplied by its caller, with no pruning
    threshold.  Per-edge cost: $\sim 9$ floating-point operations --- one
    sign detection added to the feed-ranking BFS's $\sim 8$ operations
    (\zcref{lem:sorting:bfs-correctness}).  Memory: $2\times$ the
    feed-ranking BFS state, depth-buffered over the fixed horizon~$L$.
    \proofsketch{Induction on depth via the depth-buffered relaxation
    rule, which extends the standard bounded-depth max-product argument to
    two parity registers with a zero-determinant skip; the raw edge-weight
    ceiling (\zcref{thm:graph:raw-weight-ceiling}) gives each optimal
    bounded walk a simple representative, so the depth-$L$ registers are
    exact.}
\end{lemma}


\begin{proposition}[Reduction to Feed-Ranking BFS]
    \label{prop:epoch:bfs-reduction-to-feed-ranking}
    When all traversed edges of the supplied raw projection satisfy
    $\detsign{e} = +1$, the
    $\posreg{}$ register of \zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}
    is identical to the feed-ranking BFS state
    (\zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs}).
    \proofsketch{All-positive edges: $\negreg{v}$ stays at $0$;
    the relaxation simplifies to
    $\posreg{w} \gets \max(\posreg{w},\, \posreg{v} \cdot
    \dampedweight{e})$.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Computational overhead: feed-ranking vs.\ raw signed
    double-cover traversal.}
    \label{tbl:epoch:overhead-comparison}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Component}
            & \textbf{Feed-Ranking BFS}
            & \textbf{Raw Signed Double-Cover BFS} \\
        \midrule
        Edge weight formula
            & $\dampedweight{e}$
            & $\dampedweight{e}$ (identical) \\
        State per node
            & $W(v)$ --- 1 scalar
            & $\posreg{v}, \negreg{v}$ --- 2 scalars \\
        Per-edge operations
            & ${\sim}\,8$
            & ${\sim}\,9$ \\
        Output
            & $W(c)$ for $c \in V_c$
            & $\posreg{i}$ for $i \in V_u$ \\
        Dijkstra-compatible
            & yes
            & yes (bipartite double cover) \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Final Standing}
\label{subsec:epoch:final-standing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Final Epoch Standing]
    \label{def:epoch:final-standing}
    \networkref{subsec:introduction:comparator-previewed}%
    Let $n_i^{(k)}=\max(\actcount{i}^{(k)},1)$.  The final reduced and full
    standing of Actor~$i$ are the current-epoch equilibrium coordinate of
    \zcref{def:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium} and its num\'eraire
    scaling:
    \begin{equation}
        \epochrefstanding{k}{i}
        =
        \standingstate{i}^{\star},
        \qquad
        \epochstanding{k}{i}
        =
        \numeraire\,\epochrefstanding{k}{i}.
        \label{eq:epoch:final-standing}
    \end{equation}
    Because the conserved map is a mediant of the transported pairs, this
    equals the exact post-debit balance/count mediant driven by the conserved
    transport:
    \begin{equation}
        \boxed{
        \epochstanding{k}{i}
        =
        \frac{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\,\burnbal{u}^{(k)}
        }{
            \displaystyle\sum_{u}
                \transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u}^{(k)}
        }
        \;=\;
        \frac{\transbal{i}}{\transcount{i}} .
        }
        \label{eq:epoch:final-standing-mediant}
    \end{equation}

    The sums run over \emph{all} sources, Actor~$i$ included: every row of
    the transport carries a self column
    (\zcref{def:epoch:self-retention-base}), so Actor~$i$'s own pair enters
    its own mediant through $\transportentry{i}{i}>0$ rather than as a
    separate leading term.  Every contributing source satisfies
    $\actcount{u}^{(k)}\ge1$, Registration being an accepted act; the
    $\max(\cdot,1)$ guard belongs only to the published reduced rate and is
    never silently applied to a transporting source.  Because each row of
    $\transport{\standingvector}$ sums to unity
    (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}), source~$u$'s pair
    is apportioned across targets and self, never replicated: what one
    recipient gains, the siblings and the source's own retention lose.

    Under uniform contributing action counts the mediant reduces exactly to
    the familiar rate-weighted DeGroot expression: the mediant is the
    normative formula, DeGroot is the reduction theorem.  This field is the
    comparator of \zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster} realized on the
    graph; its value-channel role is
    \zcref{ins:comparator:universal-amplifier}.  As a sparse-graph trust
    propagation mechanism it is closest in application to reputation
    systems such as EigenTrust\footcite{kamvar2003eigentrust}.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Full-Pair Source Transport Is a Current Nonclaim]
    \label{rem:epoch:full-pair-source-transport}
    The mediant (\zcref{eq:epoch:final-standing-mediant}) transports the
    \emph{full} current source pair
    $(\burnbal{u}^{(k)},\actcount{u}^{(k)})$ of every contributing source with
    $\actcount{u}^{(k)}\ge1$, and applies no source-root attenuation.  A
    depleted source with $\burnbal{u}^{(k)}=0$ therefore contributes zero to the
    numerator but positive count to the denominator: it dilutes the target as
    pure denominator ballast through an otherwise valid standing path.  This is
    priced, visible, and bounded by the source-rate hull
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}), and it violates no contraction or
    admission invariant --- but the specification makes \emph{no} claim that
    every unit of relational standing pressure is continuously backed by positive
    current residual balance.  Whether to replace full-pair transport with a
    source-root eligibility rule is an open economic question, scoped as
    \zcref{frontier:source-root-eligibility,frontier:depleted-source-ballast}
    rather than silently assumed away.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Final Standing Hull]
    \label{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}
    Write, for a source $u$ with $\transportentry{u}{i}>0$,
    \[
        r_u = \frac{\burnbal{u}^{(k)}}{\actcount{u}^{(k)}} .
    \]
    Then \label{prop:epoch:standing-bounded}%
    final standing lies in the transported-rate hull,
    \[
        \epochstanding{k}{i}
        \in
        \left[
            \min\set{r_u:\transportentry{u}{i}>0},
            \max\set{r_u:\transportentry{u}{i}>0}
        \right],
    \]
    at every state of the solve and not merely at the fixed point, and if
    every transporting source shares one action count, that count cancels and
    \zcref{eq:epoch:final-standing-mediant} reduces to the rate-DeGroot
    average.

    The contributing set is the support of the transport, which by
    \zcref{def:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation} is fixed by the base
    scores and the ledger alone: it does not move with the state or with the
    accepted tilt strength, so the hull --- and the box it bounds --- is known
    before the solve begins.
    \proofsketch{$\standingmap{k}{i}{\standingvector}$ is a
    $\{\transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}\}$-weighted average of the rates
    $r_u$; a weighted average of a finite set lies in its hull.  Common-count
    cancellation gives the DeGroot reduction.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Equal-Rate Standing Invariance]
    \label{prop:epoch:equal-rate-standing-invariance}
    If every source contributing to row~$i$ carries the same reduced rate~$c$,
    then $\epochstanding{k}{i}=\numeraire c$ exactly, at every state, at every
    tilt strength, under every profile and depth mass.  A community of equal
    rate cannot lift itself, and no arrangement of regard inside it changes any
    member's standing.

    This is the degenerate case of the closed-cluster identity
    (\zcref{thm:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity}), where the cluster's
    ledger ratio and each member's rate coincide, and it is the sharpest
    single test of the whole construction: it fails immediately for any rule
    that lets structure substitute for cost.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[No-Tilt Anchor]
    \label{prop:epoch:no-tilt-anchor}
    At $\tiltstrength{k}=0$ every applied exponent vanishes, so each hop
    allocation matrix reduces to the row-normalized base matrix and the
    transport is a constant, state-independent, row-stochastic matrix.  The map
    is then affine with zero derivative, the certificate is exact and trivially
    valid, and the equilibrium is the closed-form transported mediant.  The
    anchor rung therefore always certifies, which is what makes the backoff
    grid safely degradable: there is a rung that cannot fail
    (\zcref{def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid}).
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Closed-Cluster Rate Identity]
    \label{thm:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity}
    Call a set $S$ of Actors \emph{closed} when
    $\basescore{u}{j}=0$ whenever exactly one of $u,j$ lies in~$S$ --- a
    property of the base matrix alone, checkable before the solve and
    independent of $\standingvector$ and $\tiltstrength{k}$
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}).  Then at every state of
    the solve, not merely at equilibrium,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity}
        \sum_{i\in S}\transbal{i}=\sum_{u\in S}\burnbal{u},
        \qquad
        \sum_{i\in S}\transcount{i}=\sum_{u\in S}\actcount{u},
    \end{equation}
    and hence the \textbf{transported-mass-weighted} mean standing of the
    cluster equals its ledger ratio:
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:epoch:closed-cluster-mean}
        \frac{\sum_{i\in S}\transcount{i}\,\epochstanding{k}{i}}
             {\sum_{i\in S}\transcount{i}}
        =
        \numeraire\,
        \frac{\sum_{u\in S}\burnbal{u}}{\sum_{u\in S}\actcount{u}} .
    \end{equation}

    The weighting is \emph{mandatory}.  The identity holds for the
    $\transcount{i}$-weighted mean only; the unweighted mean drifts under
    asymmetric transport.  Any restatement of this result
    must carry the weight or it is false.

    Closure is two-sided by definition, and one-sided closure does not suffice:
    a target's denominator sums over all sources, so inbound crossing mass
    breaks the count identity even when no mass leaves.
    \proofsketch{Each row of $\transport{\standingvector}$ sums to one, and for
    $u\in S$ closure puts all of that row's support inside~$S$.  Exchanging the
    order of summation in $\sum_{i\in S}\sum_u\transportentry{u}{i}\burnbal{u}$
    therefore collects each $\burnbal{u}$ with total weight one; identically
    for the counts.  Emission relocates unexported mass onto the owner's own
    diagonal, which lies inside~$S$, so it changes no term of either sum.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Conserving Source-Root Criterion]
    \label{cor:epoch:conserving-source-root-criterion}
    A source-root rule is admissible under
    \zcref{post:epoch:cluster-rate-invariance} if and only if it acts as
    row-stochastic mixing on intact pairs after transport.  Any rule that
    \emph{deletes} pair mass detaches a closed cluster's mean from its ledger
    and is inadmissible; any rule that \emph{relocates} unexported mass into
    its owner's own row preserves
    \zcref{eq:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity} verbatim.  Source emission is
    the chartered member of the admissible class
    (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}), and the argument for its admissibility
    is this identity rather than its particular formula.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Cluster Rate Leakage]
    \label{cor:epoch:cluster-rate-leakage}
    Exact closure is a limit, not a field condition.  If a cluster's boundary
    carries base-allocation weight at most~$\varepsilon$ in each direction,
    the two sides of \zcref{eq:epoch:closed-cluster-mean} differ by
    $O(\varepsilon\locwidth{})$: the leak is bounded by how much weight crosses
    the boundary times how far apart the rates on either side are.  A dense
    community with thin external ties therefore satisfies the identity nearly
    exactly, and a community whose members allocate mostly outward was never
    a cluster in the sense the postulate means.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}[Bidirectional Final-Standing Response]
    \label{prop:epoch:final-standing-response}
    For fixed other flows, a source lifts or dilutes its target according
    to whether its rate exceeds final standing:
    \[
        \operatorname{sgn}
        \frac{\partial\epochstanding{k}{i}}
             {\partial\transportentry{u}{i}}
        =
        \operatorname{sgn}\bigl(r_u-\epochstanding{k}{i}\bigr).
    \]
    A higher-rate source lifts; a lower-rate source dilutes; Layer~1
    provides no target veto (\zcref{rem:comparator:conserved-allocation-scope}).
    \proofsketch{Quotient rule on \zcref{eq:epoch:final-standing-mediant}.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Strong-Embedding Limit]
    \label{prop:epoch:final-standing-embedding}
    If incoming transported action mass dominates the own pair,
    $\sum_{u\neq i}\transportentry{u}{i}\actcount{u}^{(k)}
    /(\transportentry{i}{i}\actcount{i}^{(k)})\to\infty$, then final standing
    approaches the transported-mass-weighted source average
    \[
        \epochstanding{k}{i}
        \longrightarrow
        \frac{
            \sum_{u\neq i}\transportentry{u}{i}\,\burnbal{u}^{(k)}
        }{
            \sum_{u\neq i}\transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u}^{(k)}
        };
    \]
    and if every relational flow is zero, $\epochstanding{k}{i}$ reduces to
    the own source rate (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).
    \proofsketch{The own pair's share vanishes; direct substitution.}
\end{proposition}


\begin{remark}[Initiator-Directed Delegation]
    \label{rem:epoch:author-directed-allocation}
    Each allocation $a\to i$ is authored by~$a$.  A source~$u$ therefore
    reaches $i$ through $a$ only in the composite sense the transport already
    expresses: the product $\hopalloc{1}{u}{a}{\standingvector}\,
    \hopalloc{2}{a}{i}{\standingvector}$ is a share of \emph{$u$'s} conserved
    unit that $a$ apportions onward, never a share of $a$'s.  The act does not
    pull standing backward to its author and cannot inherit weight from a
    passive artifact.

    Directionality does not provide a target veto.  A valid incoming
    person-vouch may lift or dilute its target according to the source
    rate, within the hull of
    \zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}.  That unilateral,
    accountable, priced posture is stated explicitly in
    \zcref{rem:comparator:conserved-allocation-scope}; dilution pressure is bounded
    by \zcref{prop:epoch:dilution-cost} and dispositioned --- priced,
    visible, mitigable, out of scope --- in
    \zcref{rem:epoch:rate-parking}.
\end{remark}


\begin{proposition}[Dilution Cost]
    \label{prop:epoch:dilution-cost}
    Coordinated low-rate endorsement is \safethresh{}-priced exactly: each ballast action
    debits $\safethresh$, so sustained dilution pressure of $n$ endorsers costs
    $n\safethresh$ per epoch-action and total grip is bounded by spent balance
    $/\safethresh$ --- capacity per reserve unit is $1/\safethresh$
    ($\numval{const.epoch.capacity_per_reserve.num}$ at the chartered value):
    grip is rented, not owned.
    \proofsketch{Every authored act is priced by W1 and increments the
    author's action count.  Amplification by multiplicity is closed by
    conservation rather than by any per-path rule: a source apportions one
    unit however many acts it authors
    (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}), so additional acts
    redistribute that unit instead of adding to it, and no relation exists in
    transport that its source did not author
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}).  Cross-target rivalry
    is not claimed; repeated acts remain separately priced, and the rate-hull
    bound still confines the result
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).  The safety-wall clamp holds
    wall-failed ballast at a fixed, non-amplifying activation
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:rate-parking}), and source emission bounds what a
    depleted history can export at all
    (\zcref{thm:epoch:emission-export-bound}).}
\end{proposition}


\begin{remark}[Griefing Resistance]
    \label{rem:epoch:griefing-resistance}%
    Standing griefing is bounded by four independent constraints:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item only acts their author authored enter that author's row, and
              no artifact or third party can create or redirect one
              (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation});
        \item every act is authored, priced, and action-count dilutive;
        \item a source's total outward allocation is one unit no matter how
              many acts it authors, so griefing volume redistributes rather
              than accumulates
              (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation});
        \item what a depleted history can export is bounded by what its
              author presently stakes
              (\zcref{thm:epoch:emission-export-bound}).
    \end{enumerate}
    A low-rate source may still dilute a target within the contributing
    rate hull; Layer~1 provides no target veto.  The mechanism makes
    that action attributable, priced, source-relative, and dynamically
    certified rather than impossible.  Raw spam weights near
    $\wspam \numrel{result.spam.weight.num}$ remain relevant to feed ranking and the raw
    signed service, not to standing.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Rate Parking Is Priced, Visible, and Out of Scope]
    \label{rem:epoch:rate-parking}
    A parked actor whose reduced standing falls below $\safefloor$ is
    wall-clamped: its projected activation is fixed at the wall value with zero
    standing derivative (\zcref{def:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation}).
    Below-wall incoming source may still change its standing, but the target's
    standing does not recursively strengthen its own activation while it remains
    below the wall; each parked endorsement action still pays $\safethresh$.  Parking
    is priced, visible, and wall-clamped --- and no longer a certificate hazard.
    Whether to play or answer such games is the community's business, not the
    mechanism's (\zcref{ins:introduction:price-not-detector}).
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[No-Tilt Commitment Monotonicity]
    \label{prop:epoch:no-tilt-commitment-monotonicity}
    At the anchor rung $\tiltstrength{k}=0$ the transport is
    state-independent (\zcref{prop:epoch:no-tilt-anchor}), so for every
    Actor~$i$ and every source~$u$ with $\transportentry{u}{i}>0$,
    \[
        \frac{\partial\epochstanding{k}{i}}{\partial\burnbal{u}}
        =
        \frac{\transportentry{u}{i}}{\transcount{i}}
        \;>\;0 :
    \]
    a burn raises the standing of everyone the burner's allocation reaches,
    including the burner.

    At $\tiltstrength{k}>0$ \textbf{no such claim is made}.  The transport
    then depends on the state it is used to compute, and under global rival
    feedback a burn that raises one Actor also re-apportions every row that
    Actor's mass passes through; whether final standing is monotone in an
    underlying burn is genuinely open
    (\zcref{frontier:tilted-monotonicity}).  This is a narrower claim than
    Edition~4 made, and deliberately so: the earlier statement was never
    examined under coupled feedback.

    Terminal reward monotonicity in the \emph{published} standing input is a
    separate, retained property
    (\zcref{pty:transport:final-standing-input-monotonicity}) and must not be
    cited as if it discharged this one.  It says rewards rise with standing;
    it says nothing about whether standing rises with burn.
\end{proposition}


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Within-Epoch Standing Solver}
\label{subsec:epoch:within-epoch-standing-solver}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The within-epoch standing solve is a fixed-point problem: the wall-clamped
activation that tilts each allocation depends on the standing the allocation
determines.  Under conserved allocation the resolution is uniform rather than
regional.  The rate hull is invariant with no certificate at all
(\zcref{thm:dynamics:conserved-standing-existence}); a valid certificate makes
the fixed point unique on it and every orbit converge geometrically to it
(\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}); and the
solution does not depend on where the solver started
(\zcref{cor:dynamics:standing-initialization-independence}).

Edition~4 needed two sufficient regions here --- a decoupled scalar regime and
an acyclic coupling graph --- because its map had no single certificate
covering both.  The conserved map does, so the regions are gone rather than
merely satisfied.  The bifurcation thresholds locating instability remain
quarantined pending rederivation on the fixed-standing base
(\zcref{subsec:dynamics:quarantined-residuals}); the \emph{contraction}
certificate depends on none of it.

\begin{remark}[Static Existence and Open Extensions]
    
    Static fixed-point existence follows from Brouwer's
    theorem\footcite{brouwer1911abbildung} applied to the bounded
    convex domain
    $[\min_j \commitrate{j},\, \max_j \commitrate{j}]^n$.
    The residual coupled cases --- the dynamic Neimark--Sacker corner and
    non-normal transfer --- are open; see \zcref{subsec:dynamics:quarantined-residuals}.
\end{remark}


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Final-Set Closure and Epoch Boundary}
\label{subsec:epoch:epoch-boundary}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Log Position]
    \label{def:epoch:log-position}
    The log position $\logpos{e} \in \NatZero$ is the zero-based rank of $e$
    within the written record set under the identity-key order $\idorder$ ---
    the total order induced by the lexicographic key
    $(\acttime{\actof{e}}, \operatorname{author}(e), \operatorname{src}(e),
    \operatorname{tgt}(e))$, which refines the authoritative order $\prec$. It is
    a deterministic audit coordinate and nothing more: epoch membership is
    decided by the closure rule below, and no scoring, recognition, or
    boundary quantity consumes $\logpos{e}$
    (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}). $\idorder$ retains exactly
    one consumer: an optional audit tie-break within the authoritative order
    (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Epoch Act Budget]
    \label{def:epoch:epoch-act-budget}
    The epoch target $\epochlen$ is denominated in accepted authored acts:
    \[
        |\actsequence{k}| \le \epochlen.
    \]
    A binary act, a complete hyper-edge act, and a Registration each
    consume one unit of this budget.  A hyper-edge's A- and T-projections
    are two graph projections of one budgeted act and consume no
    independent epoch units.

    The projected edge increment is
    \[
        \edgeincrement{k}
        =
        \bigcup_{q\in\actsequence{k}}
        \actedges{q},
    \]
    a derived storage and traversal quantity whose size satisfies
    \[
        |\actsequence{k}|
        \le
        |\edgeincrement{k}|
        \le
        2\,|\actsequence{k}|.
    \]
    It is not the epoch admission budget.
\end{definition}


\begin{postulate}[Final-Set Closure]
    \label{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-closure}
    An epoch closes at the earliest moment at which either the host
    determines the write set below fills the epoch target size $\epochlen$
    and the published epoch minimum duration has elapsed, or the published
    epoch maximum duration has elapsed.

    At close, the host fixes the authoritative ordered authored-act sequence
    $\actsequence{k}$ (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}) and writes its record
    projection $\edgeincrement{k}=\bigcup_{q\in \actsequence{k}}\actedges{q}$, a union of dependent sets
    (\zcref{def:graph:dependent-act-set}).  The order is used only for dependency
    formation and authoritative placement; W1, W2a, W2b, standing, and the ledger
    are evaluated \emph{once} on the completed final union --- no prefix of $\actsequence{k}$
    carries a normative standing value ---
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\roman*)]
        \item formation-valid, with every member's author clearing W1 and W2a
            individually (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule});
        \item every member clearing the safety stamp individually,
            $\actstamp{} \ge \safefloor$;
        \item the epoch door clearing W2b, $\epochstamp{k}\ge\partfloor$
            (\zcref{def:epoch:final-act-stamps}), computed once over the
            complete final union $\actsequence{k}$;
    \end{enumerate}
    with $|\actsequence{k}| \le \epochlen$
    (\zcref{def:epoch:epoch-act-budget}). \textbf{Selection among valid ordered sequences
    is host discretion}: optimal packing under dependencies and averages is
    expensive, and this document fixes the constraints, not the algorithm.
    The certificate publishes the ordered partition of $\actsequence{k}$ into its dependent
    sets, so validity --- every clause above --- is replayable by any
    participant; the chosen sequence is host discretion but, once published, is
    the agreed $\actsequence{k}$ (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}).  Conflict
    recognition still reads only membership and epoch, never the residual
    sub-epoch order (\zcref{rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance}).

    The epoch's \emph{regime} is certificate-derived: \textbf{binding} iff
    $|\actsequence{k}| = \epochlen$, \textbf{slack} otherwise.
\end{postulate}

\begin{postulate}[Final Epoch Edge Set]
    \label{post:epoch:final-edge-set}
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement}%
    The epoch-$k$ \emph{snapshot edge set} is
    $E_k = E_{k-1} \cup \edgeincrement{k}$, where $\edgeincrement{k}$ is the union of the dependent sets' edge projections
    written at boundary~$k$. $E_k$ is monotone by construction and causally
    closed by the dependency closure of \zcref{def:graph:dependent-act-set}:
    every asserted parent and hyper-edge co-leg of a written record is written
    with it or already present. $E_k$ therefore
    satisfies \zcref{post:introduction:epoch-edge-set} with no appeal to any
    global position coordinate.

    Commitment rates $\commitrate{i}^{(k)}$ used in the epoch-$k$ derivation
    are computed from $\burnbal{i}$ and $\actcount{i}$ accumulated within
    $E_k$; the boundary burn state $\set{\burnval{i}^{(k)}}$ and debit schedule are provided
    alongside $E_k$, sampled at the settlement-stability depth $\snapbuf$:
    a Layer-0 depth chosen to exceed settlement-ordering uncertainty, so
    every sampled value is last-settled at the instant of sampling
    (\zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability};
    \attestationcref{prop:invariants:burn-order-residual}). $\snapbuf$
    buffers the \emph{burn snapshot}, not edge membership --- membership is
    the closure rule's alone. Any participant accepting the same $E_k$
    reproduces every epoch-$k$ quantity from the published constants alone
    (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism,%
    prop:epoch:epoch-replay-determinism}).
\end{postulate}


\begin{definition}[Raw Self-Edge Reading]
    \label{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}
    After final standing is published
    (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}), Layer~1 exposes a raw Self-edge
    reading for feed and raw bridge services only.  The shared raw bond
    parameter of Actor~$i$ is the M\"obius image of final reduced
    standing,
    \begin{equation}
        p_i^{(k)}
        =
        \frac{\epochrefstanding{k}{i}}{1+\epochrefstanding{k}{i}}
        =
        \frac{\epochstanding{k}{i}}{\numeraire+\epochstanding{k}{i}},
        \label{eq:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}
    \end{equation}
    from which the derived Declaration
    ($\mathrm{Actor}_i\to\mathrm{Profile}_i$) and Reputation
    ($\mathrm{Profile}_i\to\mathrm{Actor}_i$) edges take their raw tensor
    parameter (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}): recomputable by any
    participant, never appended, placed causally after every record in
    $E_k$ and before every record accepted after boundary~$k$.  Their
    maturity follows the published raw tenure schedule
    $\tau_i^{(k)}=1-1/(k-k_i^{\mathrm{reg}}+1)$, and they remain available
    to feed, raw signed, and CAN consumers through their existing
    interfaces.

    The reading is a deterministic function of the current final standing:
    there is no freeze, no previous-standing memory, and no below-wall
    branch.  It has no effect on standing --- standing does not traverse
    these raw edges but uses the wall-clamped projected activation
    $\wallactivation{x_i}$ of
    \zcref{def:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation} --- and raw maturity
    remains terminal: it may change raw feed traversal but never the
    projected standing activation.  Derived Declaration and Reputation are
    raw graph readings only.
\end{definition}


\begin{algorithm}
    \caption{Conserved Standing Computation.}
    \label{alg:epoch:conserved-standing-computation}
    \begin{algorithmic}[1]
        \State \textbf{Input:} proposed $\actsequence{k}$, settled boundary burn
               state, $E_{k-1}$, published constants
        \State Validate formation and dependent-set closure
        \State Form the tentative $E_k(\edgeincrement{k})=E_{k-1}\cup \edgeincrement{k}$
               \Comment{\zcref{def:epoch:proposed-final-act-state}}
        \State Apply all $\actcountincrement{k}{i}$ count increments and
               $\safethresh$ debits
        \State \textbf{reject} at once if any final residual balance
               $\burnbal{i}^{(k)}$ is negative
        \State Fold every accepted act into cells, resolve each recipient,
               and form the base allocation matrix $\basescore{}{}$
               \Comment{\zcref{def:epoch:standing-fold-cell,%
               def:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}}
        \State Read the emission fractions $\emission{u}$ and the
               contributing widths from the base matrix and the ledger
               \Comment{\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission,%
               prop:dynamics:support-state-independence}}
        \For{each rung $\tiltstrength{k}$ of $\tiltgrid$, greatest first}
            \State Evaluate the certificate $\standingcert{k}$ over
                   $\hullbox{k}$
                   \Comment{\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}}
            \State \textbf{break} if $\marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}\le1$
        \EndFor
        \State Solve the unique equilibrium $\standingeq$ at the accepted
               rung; the anchor $\tiltstrength{k}=0$ always certifies
               \Comment{\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness,%
               prop:epoch:no-tilt-anchor}}
        \State Compute the transport entries $\transportentry{u}{i}$ and
               final standing $\epochstanding{k}{i}$
               \Comment{\zcref{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport,%
               def:epoch:final-standing}}
        \State Compute final action stamps, the epoch stamp, and headroom
               \Comment{\zcref{def:epoch:final-act-stamps}}
        \State Check W1, W2a, and W2b
               \Comment{\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}}
        \State Derive the raw Self-edge reading for raw consumers
               \Comment{\zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}}
        \If{all final-set conditions pass}
            \State \textbf{accept} $\actsequence{k}$ and publish $E_k=E_{k-1}\cup \edgeincrement{k}$
                   with the accepted rung and the certificate
                   $\standingcert{k}$
        \Else
            \State \textbf{reject} the proposed set; publish no standing
                   for it
        \EndIf
    \end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}


\begin{algorithm}
    \caption{Tilt Backoff.}
    \label{alg:epoch:tilt-backoff}
    \begin{algorithmic}[1]
        \State \textbf{Input:} the base matrix, the emission fractions, the
               hull box, the published grid $\tiltgrid$
        \For{each rung $t$ of $\tiltgrid$ in decreasing order}
            \State Evaluate $\standingcert{k}$ over $\hullbox{k}$ at $t$
                   \Comment{\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}}
            \If{$\marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}\le1$}
                \State \textbf{return} $\tiltstrength{k}\gets t$ and the verdict
                       of every rung attempted above it
            \EndIf
            \State Record whether this rung FAILED or was INDECISIVE
                   \Comment{\zcref{rem:epoch:certificate-failure-versus-indecisive-enclosure}}
        \EndFor
        \State \textbf{return} the anchor $\tiltstrength{k}\gets0$
               \Comment{always certifies, \zcref{prop:epoch:no-tilt-anchor}}
    \end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}

The loop terminates because the grid is finite and its last rung is the anchor,
which certifies without evaluating anything.  Each rung is judged on its own
certificate: a rung is never accepted because a higher one passed, and never
rejected because a higher one failed
(\zcref{def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid}).  Recording the two failure modes
separately is what lets calibration tell a graph that got harder from a
verifier that got sloppier.

\begin{proposition}[Epoch Replay Determinism]
    \label{prop:epoch:epoch-replay-determinism}
    Given $E_k$, the boundary burn state, the debit schedule, the
    published constants, the projection-compiler version, and the
    declared certificate procedure, the entire epoch-$k$ derivation is
    deterministic:
    \[
        \begin{gathered}
        \commitrate{i}^{(k)},\quad
        \text{fold cells},\quad
        \foldcoef{\foldcell},\quad
        \basescore{}{},\quad
        \emission{u},\quad
        \tiltstrength{k},\\
        \transportentry{u}{i},\quad
        \epochstanding{k}{i},\quad
        \titlecert{k},\quad
        \text{raw Self-edge reading},\quad
        \text{effective activation},\\
        \actstamp{},\quad
        \epochstamp{k},\quad
        \doorheadroom{k},\quad
        \standingcert{k}.
        \end{gathered}
    \]
    Every object is a function of the authoritative order $\actsequence{k}$
    (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}) and is invariant under every
    payload state (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}).
    \proofsketch{Complete-act compilation and the person-vouch
    predicate are determined by the ordered history
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:act-folding-properties}); path enumeration,
    allocation order, and bisection are canonical; every remaining step
    is algebraic.}
\end{proposition}


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The \texorpdfstring{\safethresh{}-Debit}{Safety-Threshold Debit} Ledger}
\label{subsec:epoch:act-debit}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{postulate}[\safethresh{}-Debit]
    \label{post:epoch:act-debit}
    Each accepted act by actor~$i$ in epoch~$k$ debits
    $\burnbal{i}\mathrel{-}=\safethresh^{(k)}$ and increments
    $\actcount{i}\mathrel{+}=1$ (a hyper-edge is one act: one $\safethresh$, one
    stamp). The debit is consummated at the writing epoch's price and never
    re-calculated (V3, \zcref{rem:comparator:vintage-trichotomy}). $\safethresh$ is the
    \emph{only} debited object: no gate, door, or stamp moves a balance.
    Capacity \emph{is} the balance: remaining actions
    $=\lfloor\burnbal{i}/\safethresh\rfloor$, restored immediately by burning.
\end{postulate}

\begin{proposition}[Translation Law]
    \label{prop:epoch:translation-law}
    At fixed endorsement weights and uniform \safethresh{}-history, the debit enters every
    numerator in exact proportion to the denominator's weights: post-debit
    standing $=$ pre-debit standing $-\;\safefloor\numeraire$ (reduced: the
    field translates rigidly by $\safefloor$).  Exact (dps-floor residuals,
    \zcref{subsec:verification:two-gate}); corollary
    $\epochstamp{k}=\overline{\refstanding{}}_{\mathrm{pre}}-\safefloor$.  At
    fixed \emph{points} the weights move and the translation is only
    approximate, up to a small kernel residual.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Dense Cluster Fairness]
    \label{rem:epoch:dense-cluster-fairness}
    In a dense cluster, $\standing{i}$ converges to the pooled leave-one-out
    burn-per-action of the support base.  No hub identification, celebrity
    block decomposition, or topology-dependent branching is required.  The
    fairness rationale for this convergence --- effective standing as the
    consensus of one's consensual support base --- is given in
    \zcref{rem:epoch:author-directed-allocation} and surfaced as the dignity claim it
    discharges, standing dissolving into peer consensus with comparison
    reserved for between communities, in
    \zcref{ins:introduction:equal-among-peers,ins:introduction:no-escape-velocity,ins:introduction:peer-claim-scope}.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Two Samplings of the Action Count]
    \label{rem:epoch:two-action-counts}
    Two readings coexist by design: boundary pairs $(\burnbal{},\actcount{})^{(k)}$
    feed stamps and standing; live pairs $(\burnbal{}(t),\actcount{}(t))$
    feed W1.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Two-Gate Write Rule}
\label{subsec:epoch:participation-gates}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{postulate}[Final-Set Write Rule]
    \label{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}
    A record $e$ by actor~$i$ is \emph{writable} in epoch~$k$ iff all three hold:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{(W1, solvency, debited)}]
            $\burnbal{i}\ge\safethresh^{(k)}$; on write the debit of
            \zcref{post:epoch:act-debit} executes. Evaluated continuously;
            only your own balance pays your $\safethresh$.
        \item[\textnormal{(W2a, safety, individual)}]
            $\actstamp{q}\ge\safefloor^{(k)}$, the boundary-frozen
            post-mediant, post-debit stamp.  \textbf{Never averaged}: no
            member's deficit is paid by another's surplus.
        \item[\textnormal{(W2b, policy, averaged)}]
            the closed set satisfies $\epochstamp{k}\ge\partfloor^{(k)}$,
            $|\actsequence{k}|\le\epochlen$.  \textbf{Never debited}; vacuous on empty
            epochs.  Band actors ($\safefloor\le\actstamp{}<\partfloor$)
            are writable exactly when the door has headroom --- the membrane,
            not a wall (\zcref{rem:epoch:band-dwell}).
    \end{description}
    W2a reads the single certified equilibrium of the epoch
    (\zcref{def:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium}) at the accepted tilt
    rung: there is one standing solution per epoch, and no gate reads a
    partial or intermediate one.
\end{postulate}

\begin{remark}[Relational Gate versus Own Export]
    \label{rem:epoch:relational-gate-vs-own-export}
    Three thresholds share the coordinate pair $(\safethresh,\safefloor)$ and
    must never be merged.
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{W1 solvency}] $\burnbal{u}\ge\safethresh$:
            \emph{may you act}.
        \item[\textnormal{Full emission}] $\refrate{u}\ge\safefloor$,
            equivalently $\burnbal{u}\ge\safethresh\,\actcount{u}$:
            \emph{does your whole history carry}
            (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}).
        \item[\textnormal{W2a safety}] $\actstamp{}\ge\safefloor$: \emph{does
            your standing clear the wall} --- a post-transport quantity, and
            the only one of the three that others' regard can lift.
    \end{description}
    An Actor can be W1-solvent and emission-faded at once: one act is cheap,
    a thousand acts of history are not.  Relational support can carry your
    acts through the gate, but \textbf{only your own backing carries your
    history outward}.  The word rule follows: emission caps what a history
    \emph{carries}, W1 gates whether you may \emph{act} --- different verbs,
    different axes.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Admission-Statistics Quarantine]
    \label{rem:epoch:admission-statistics-quarantine}
    Binding-regime statistics --- the regime bit and the door headroom under
    congestion --- are boundary-side data. They carry external-demand basis and
    gauge-coordinate pricing; no unit-level $\numeraire$-side formula may consume
    them. Shape statistics are measurement-valid only for what was written;
    Layer~1 has no demand set behind the certificate. The failure polarity is
    one-way: a manipulated boundary may silence downstream consumers, never
    point them.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Consent Under Boundary Discretion]
    \label{rem:epoch:consent-exposure}
    Layer~1 does not represent the unwritten, so a cancel the host declines to
    write leaves no Layer-1 trace --- no pre-write artifact, no demand ledger,
    and no detector, and this document does not pretend otherwise. What binds is
    written-side: a cancel written in any epoch up to the commit's defeats it
    (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}, clauses~(iv)--(v)), the maximum
    duration guarantees boundaries keep arriving, and early regret is reliable
    regret (\zcref{rem:graph:cancellation-best-effort}). The residual --- a host
    suppressing a last-epoch cancel while writing the commit --- is a
    boundary-censorship exposure of exactly the kind
    \zcref{frontier:boundary-mechanism} exists to close by mechanism rather than
    by audit; it is witnessed at \zcref{frontier:boundary-censorship}, and the
    policy-floor discipline it once vetoed is carried instead by the safety
    clamp and the announcement lead (\zcref{def:epoch:policy-floor}).
\end{remark}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Actor participation states.}
    \label{tbl:epoch:actor-states}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l c c l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{State}
            & $\actstamp{} \geq \safefloor$
            & $\burnbal{} \geq \safethresh$
            & \textbf{May act}
            & \textbf{Remedy} \\
        \midrule
        Active
            & \okmark & \okmark
            & yes & --- \\
        Band
            & \okmark & \okmark
            & headroom & Door headroom \\
        Insolvent
            & \okmark & $\times$
            & no & Burn immediately \\
        Frozen
            & $\times$ & (irrel.)
            & no & Burn lump to re-cross wall \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{remark}[Band Dwell]
    \label{rem:epoch:band-dwell}
    An unendorsed no-burn actor at $(\hat r_0,N_0)$ reaches the door membrane
    in exactly
    $m_1=N_0(\hat r_0-\partfloor)/(\partfloor+\safefloor)$ actions and the
    freeze wall in
    $m_2=N_0(\hat r_0-\safefloor)/(2\safefloor)$ --- linear, exact, no
    continuum limit. Reference: $654.4$ / $1393.7$; band dwell $739.3$ actions,
    headroom-permitting. Re-entry from below either boundary is a burn lump ---
    a price, not a duration.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Non-Written Actors Remain Dynamically Live]
    \label{rem:epoch:non-written-dynamic-live}
    Not being written is neither write failure nor solvency failure. It
    does not trigger any below-wall clamp of
    \zcref{def:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation}, which keys on the
    current safety wall only. Non-written actors remain dynamically live:
    their rates contribute, their rows remain in the mediant field, and
    $\locwidth{}$ and $\standingcert{k}$ are functions of
    the written state only.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Registration under Final-Set Admission]
    \label{rem:epoch:registration-final-set-admission}
    Registration is one act in the proposed final write set: it
    contributes one accepted-act increment, incurs one
    $\safethresh$-debit, competes under W1, W2a, and W2b, consumes epoch
    write capacity, and receives the same final standing stamp as every
    other same-author act in the set
    (\zcref{def:epoch:final-act-stamps}).  Its structural permission
    to anchor fresh grounded Actor/Profile identifiers does not alter its
    admission arithmetic.  A candidate Actor has prior count zero; with no
    relational flow its stamp is its own source rate
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}), and a current high-rate
    external vouch may lift it under the ordinary hull
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Same-Epoch Source-Hull Bound]
    \label{cor:epoch:same-epoch-source-hull}
    Final standing remains within the hull of the current post-debit
    contributing source rates reaching an Actor
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).  Consequently a same-epoch
    cohort whose source rates all lie below $\safefloor$ cannot mutually
    vouch itself above $\safefloor$, and a zero-rate cohort stays at zero
    absent an external positive-rate source; only a current external
    positive-rate vouch lifts a newly registered Actor.  Same-epoch
    topology creates no source.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Universal Per-Act Burn Benchmarks]
    \label{cor:epoch:universal-burn-benchmarks}
    For an unsupported Actor proposing $m\ge1$ epoch acts, the per-act burn
    benchmarks are
    \[
        B_{\mathrm{W1}}(m)=m\safethresh,
        \qquad
        B_{\mathrm{safety}}(m)=2m\safethresh,
        \qquad
        B_{\mathrm{door}}(m)=m\bigl(\safethresh+\numeraire\partfloor\bigr).
    \]
    These are final-state gate benchmarks, not prices that guarantee
    selection into the finite write set
    (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}); there is no universal
    admission price.
\end{corollary}

\paragraph{Rehabilitation.}
Restoring a failed safety wall requires some combination of:
new burns raising $\commitrate{i}$ directly, and new positive-parity
connections from actors with $\commitrate{j} > \standing{i}$, lifting
the weighted average
(\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).

The joint geometry of the two gates --- W1 debit and W2 stamp/door --- and the
minimum-burn schedule that sustains action on them is developed in
\zcref{app:gates}.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Threshold Pair and the Effective Floor}
\label{subsec:epoch:floor-governance}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The participation floor of \zcref{subsec:epoch:participation-gates} is not one
number but a pair with an inequality between them: a \emph{safety threshold}
the network computes, and a \emph{policy floor} the host publishes above it.
They live on different axes on purpose --- one is a price, one is a position
--- and they meet in exactly one comparison, through an explicit
$\numeraire$.

\begin{definition}[Safety Threshold]
    \label{def:epoch:safety-threshold}
    The \emph{safety threshold} $\safethresh \in \R_{>0}$ (units: reserve per
    action) is the minimum attestation price behind a write that the coupled
    dynamics certifiably tolerate. It is an algorithmic output of the epoch
    computation --- never a host input --- published in each certificate with
    one-boundary lead: certificate~$k$ carries $\safethresh^{(k+1)}$, the
    value in force at boundary~$k{+}1$. This document fixes the algorithm's
    \emph{requirements}; the algorithm itself is a calibration deliverable
    (\zcref{frontier:floor-calibration}).
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{(R1) Derivability.}] $\safethresh^{(k+1)}$ is a
            function of the epoch-$k$ certificate and the published constants
            alone, replayable by any participant.
        \item[\textnormal{(R2) Sufficiency.}] The width fence holds at the
            threshold with a declared margin. Under conserved allocation the
            fence is \emph{two-sided}, because a recipient's gain is every
            sibling's and the source's own loss:
            \begin{equation*}
                2\,\wallgaincap\,\tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\,
                \locwidth{} \;\le\; \contractionfactor{k} \;<\; 1 ,
            \end{equation*}
            evaluated at the accepted rung. Because $\loggain{}$ is decreasing
            (\zcref{lem:dynamics:monotone-gain}), the fence then holds at every
            valid effective floor above the threshold: safety is monotone in
            the dial.
        \item[\textnormal{(R2b) Width dominance.}] The published
            $\locwidth{}$ must be an upper bound on the width actually realized
            in the epoch it governs: the contributing set of every row is
            $\set{u:\transportentry{u}{i}>0}$
            (\zcref{def:dynamics:local-width}), and if a realized row exceeds
            the published bound, R2 certifies nothing. This premise is where
            the threshold rule's cancellation happens --- $\safethresh$ is
            \emph{defined} by inverting the gain at $1/(\marginfactor
            \locwidth{})$, so a stale or understated $\locwidth{}$ silently
            weakens every downstream margin. It is a publication obligation on
            the host, checkable against the certificate, not an assumption.
        \item[\textnormal{(R3) Step-boundedness.}] The per-epoch change of
            $\safethresh$ is bounded, and any downward step is cleared
            against the projected post-move live set
            (\zcref{frontier:incremental-equilibrium-solver}).
        \item[\textnormal{(R4) Hysteresis.}] The response to $\locwidth{}$
            is Schmitt-stepped; the threshold does not chatter.
        \item[\textnormal{(R5) Lead.}] One-boundary lead, so policy-floor
            compliance is checkable ex ante.
        \item[\textnormal{(R6) Publication.}] Published beside
            $\standingcert{k}$, the accepted rung $\tiltstrength{k}$, and
            $\locwidth{}$ in the certificate
            (\zcref{post:network:host-contract}).
        \item[\textnormal{(R7) Declared covariance.}] The algorithm states
            how $\safethresh$ transforms under a numéraire migration,
            compensated and uncompensated, so validity margins are
            predictable across the move
            (\zcref{prop:epoch:compensation}).
    \end{description}
    \emph{Canonical interim rule (chartered):}
    $\safethresh^{(k+1)}=\numeraire\cdot\loggaininv{1/(\marginfactor\,\locwidth{}^{(k)})}$
    with \textbf{declared margin factor $\marginfactor\numrel{const.epoch.margin.num}$}
    (fence slack $\fenceslack = 1-1/\marginfactor \numrel{const.epoch.fenceslack.num}$), a published
    constant under the no-silent-change discipline
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas}). R3:
    per-boundary $|\Delta\safefloor|\le\min(0.10,25\%)$. R4: recompute only
    when the implied $\safefloor$ change exceeds $5\%$; hysteresis released
    before re-raising. R7 carries $\marginfactor$ explicitly.
    \emph{Escalation clause:} $\marginfactor\to1.5$ if p95 one-boundary
    $\locwidth{}$ growth exceeds $\sqrt{\marginfactor} \numrel{const.epoch.margin_sqrt.num}$ over the
    calibration window.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Policy Floor]
    \label{def:epoch:policy-floor}
    The \emph{policy floor} $\polfloor \in \R_{>0}$ is dimensionless: the
    host's standing dial against spam and Sybil pressure, expressed on the
    gate axis. It is announced at boundary~$k$, effective at~$k{+}1$, and
    persists until re-announced. A certificate is \emph{valid} only if
    \begin{equation}
        \polfloor \;\ge\; \safefloor
        \label{eq:epoch:floor-validity}
    \end{equation}
    at the values in force (equivalently $\polfloor\numeraire\ge\safethresh$)
    --- the one sanctioned meeting of the two axes, with the numéraire
    explicit. An announcement violating \zcref{eq:epoch:floor-validity} against
    the led $\safethresh^{(k+1)}$ is
    invalid at publication: a formula constraint on the dial, not a
    discretion. Canonical default $\polfloor \numrel{const.comparator.policy_floor.num}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Effective Participation Floor]
    \label{def:epoch:participation-floor}
    The \emph{effective participation floor} is derived, not dialed:
    \begin{equation}
        \partfloor \;\coloneqq\;
        \max\!\bigl(\polfloor,\ \safethresh/\numeraire\bigr).
        \label{eq:epoch:effective-floor}
    \end{equation}
    On every valid certificate $\partfloor = \polfloor$; the $\max$ is fault
    totalization with safe polarity --- a pipeline that mispublishes can only
    ever \emph{over}-floor, never under-floor. Read-sites: the door (W2b) and
    the per-act door benchmark $\partfloor\numeraire$
    (\zcref{cor:epoch:universal-burn-benchmarks}); the safety wall
    $\safefloor$ keys the below-wall activation clamp.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Safety Floor]
    \label{def:epoch:safety-floor}
    $\safefloor\coloneqq\safethresh/\numeraire$ is the gate image of the
    per-action price: W2a's comparator, the below-wall activation-clamp key, and
    the fence pin $\loggain{\safefloor}\locwidth{}\marginfactor=1$. The glyph is intentional:
    the old no-hat-glyph lint was correct at one read-site and wrong at three.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Final Standing Stamps]
    \label{def:epoch:final-act-stamps}
    Every epoch-$k$ act authored by Actor~$i$ receives the same final
    action stamp, the reduced final standing:
    \begin{equation}
        \actstamp{q}
        =
        \epochrefstanding{k}{i}
        =
        \standingstate{i},
        \qquad
        q\in\actsequence{k},\ \operatorname{author}(q)=i.
        \label{eq:epoch:final-action-stamp}
    \end{equation}
    The stamp is act-owned: a hyper-edge act carries one $\actstamp{q}$, and if an
    implementation serializes it beside both edge projections those are cached
    copies counted once in W2b. There is no special Registration branch.  For
    nonempty $\actsequence{k}$, the action-weighted epoch stamp is
    \begin{equation}
        \epochstamp{k}
        =
        \frac{
            \sum_i \actcountincrement{k}{i}\,\epochrefstanding{k}{i}
        }{
            \sum_i \actcountincrement{k}{i}
        },
        \label{eq:epoch:final-epoch-stamp}
    \end{equation}
    action-weighted by construction since stamps are boundary-frozen; for
    an empty act sequence W2b is vacuous.  With the effective floor
    $\partfloor$, the epoch headroom is
    \begin{equation}
        \doorheadroom{k}
        =
        \sum_i \actcountincrement{k}{i}
        \bigl(\epochrefstanding{k}{i}-\partfloor\bigr).
        \label{eq:epoch:final-epoch-headroom}
    \end{equation}
    These are measurements, not floors; stamps are never debited.
\end{definition}

\begin{postulate}[Reduction Convention]
    \label{post:epoch:reduction-convention}
    Every dynamical and routing quantity --- the bond kernel
    $p_i = \standing{i}/(\numeraire + \standing{i})$, the activation, the
    gain, stamps --- is $\numeraire$-reduced.  $\partfloor$ appears in the
    door (W2b) and the per-act door benchmark; $\safefloor$ appears in the
    below-wall activation clamp and W2a. Derived analysis
    (\zcref{app:dynamics}) reads each floor only through
    the corresponding door/wall condition, never as a reduction scale.
\end{postulate}

\begin{proposition}[Compensation Structure]
    \label{prop:epoch:compensation}
    Under $(\numeraire, \polfloor) \to (c\numeraire, \polfloor/c)$: the
    admission set and per-act door benchmark --- functions of the door product
    $\polfloor\numeraire$ alone on a valid certificate --- are invariant;
    reduced quantities scale by $1/c$; per-action cost is \safethresh{}-mediated. The gate
    axis $\set{\polfloor,\actstamp{},\epochstamp{}}$ is \emph{exactly}
    invariant (stamps and floors co-scale); W1/W2a are \safethresh{}-mediated per the R7
    declaration, so a compensated announcement publishes
    $(\safethresh',\safefloor')$. Local widths scale as
    $\locwidth{}\to\locwidth{}/c$, and the fence certificate degrades by the
    declared family law (\zcref{subsec:dynamics:quarantined-residuals}).
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Historical Capacity Crush]
    \label{rem:epoch:capacity-crush}
    Historical (v0.20 machinery): the retroactive repricing branch was deleted
    by the \safethresh{}-debit ledger --- a consummated debit is never
    re-calculated (\zcref{post:epoch:act-debit}) --- so the current mechanism
    has no frozen stock to crush.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Two Axes, One Meeting Point]
    \label{rem:epoch:two-axes}
    The split is load-bearing, not notational. $\polfloor$ is a statement
    about \emph{position} --- who participates, relative to the numéraire ---
    and is rightly dimensionless: it survives a recoinage untouched, because
    ``stand at $\polfloor$ times the unit'' is not a price. $\safethresh$ is
    a statement about \emph{real cost} --- what minimum attestation the
    dynamics tolerate behind a write --- and is rightly
    reserve-denominated: the danger it fences is anchored in the rate
    ledger, which lives on the price axis. Collapsing them onto one axis
    would make one of the two claims silently covariant with the wrong
    transformation; keeping them apart makes the recoinage question
    explicit, which is exactly what R7 exists to answer. Under
    $(\numeraire,\polfloor) \to (c\numeraire,\polfloor/c)$ the door price
    $\polfloor\numeraire$ is invariant (\zcref{prop:epoch:compensation}) ---
    but the validity margin of \zcref{eq:epoch:floor-validity} moves however
    $\safethresh$ moves, and only the algorithm's declared covariance says
    how. What was a latent assumption is now a published obligation.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the Dials]
    \label{rem:epoch:dial-scope}
    The decomposition of \zcref{def:comparator:numeraire} sharpens.
    $\numeraire$ governs the price image $\safefloor=\safethresh/\numeraire$
    and the stability operating point; it is structural, and moving
    it is a migration event. $\polfloor$ governs admission --- purely
    extensive: it excludes, and cannot reprice a survivor's actions.
    $\marginfactor$ governs the margin --- one dial read four ways: the
    contraction certificate (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), the
    Lipschitz constant (\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}), the width
    fence (\zcref{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}), and the margined safety wall
    (\zcref{cor:dynamics:minimal-safe-wall}). Door headroom
    $\doorheadroom{k}$ is deliberately absent from this list: it is an outcome
    of demand against the write budget, not a dial.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Host Authority over the Floor]
    \label{rem:epoch:operator-authority-floor}
    The host's entire floor authority is the $\polfloor$ schedule of
    \zcref{post:network:host-contract}: announced with one-boundary lead,
    valid only above the led safety threshold, auditable ex ante by any
    participant. Everything that was previously stage-scoped discretion is
    now split cleanly: the fence clearance lives inside $\safethresh$ (R2),
    the step discipline inside R3, and the region below the certified ridge
    bracket is unreachable through a valid dial by construction ---
    $\safethresh/\numeraire$ cannot be published below it (R2), and
    $\polfloor$ cannot be published below $\safethresh/\numeraire$
    (\zcref{eq:epoch:floor-validity}). The safeguard is visibility plus the
    clamp, not trust.
\end{remark}
