\section{Content Sorting}
\label{sec:sorting}

Content sorting is a terminal Layer~2 reading of the raw Action Graph
(\zcref{subsec:introduction:the-graph}).
It uses the raw \PathView{} interface
(\zcref{def:graph:dual-view-architecture}) and the canonical raw damped
edge weight of \zcref{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight}.  It does not
consume the relation multigraph, causal standing
paths, or tilt rungs.

The standing field $\standing{}$ is nevertheless a binding Layer~1
input to the terminal creator amplifier.  Thus sorting combines:
\begin{description}[nosep]
    \item[\textnormal{raw discovery}]
        max-product traversal over raw Action-Graph legs through feed
        depth~$L=4$, using raw determinant, maturity, and temporal
        damping;
    \item[\textnormal{binding creator comparison}]
        the already-certified standing factor
        $\ampfactor{\operatorname{creator}(c)}$, published at each epoch
        boundary (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}) and consumed here as a
        fixed external scalar at $O(1)$ per content node
        (the creator $\operatorname{creator}(c)$ is the genesis-record
        author, \zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator};
        $\standing{\bot}:=0$ for named nodes, so a Type terminus takes
        the unit amplifier);
    \item[\textnormal{terminal content quality}]
        the content scalar
        $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F$.
\end{description}

The raw depth~$L$ counts Action-Graph legs and is distinct from
$\hopmax$, which bounds how far a source's allocation is transported.
A guild may reimplement raw sorting under
\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}; it may not override the standing
field consumed by the amplifier.

The CAN (\zcref{app:can}) remains a separate terminal \AttrView{}
attribution reading, entering only through the enrichment factor in the
reward formula at a single passive-node terminus.  Content sorting
itself consumes no CAN recursion.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Relevance Score}
\label{subsec:sorting:relevance-score}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Relevance Score]
    \label{def:sorting:relevance-score}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:max-product-path-scoring}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:feed-reproducibility}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:device-local}%
    For user $u \in V_u$ and content $c \in V_c$, at
    $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$:
    \begin{equation}
        S(u, c)
        = \underbrace{
            \max_{p \in \operatorname{Paths}_L(u \to c)}
            \prod_{e \in p} \dampedweight{e}
          }_{\text{max-product path relevance}}
        \;\times\;
        \underbrace{
            \ampfactor{\operatorname{creator}(c)}
            \cdot \norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F
          }_{\text{standing-amplified content norm}},
        \label{eq:sorting:relevance-score}
    \end{equation}
    where $\operatorname{Paths}_L$ denotes
    viable \emph{raw Action-Graph} paths containing at most $L=4$ raw legs
    --- feed
    depth, not standing transport depth $\hopmax$.  Path edges enter through
    $\detscore{e}$ (\PathView{} --- discrimination by directional
    coherence); the content terminus enters through
    $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F$ (scalar interface --- equity
    across edge types).  This is the per-edge instance of the
    dual-view split stated in \zcref{ins:graph:rank-two-structural-consequence}.
    Every factor is payload-free: the path product, the content norm, and the
    standing amplifier read structural records only
    (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}).
    $\operatorname{creator}(c)$ is the genesis-record author
    (\zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator}; $\standing{\bot}:=0$ for named
    nodes, so a Type terminus takes $\ampfactor{\bot}=1$), and
    $\standing{}$ is a Layer~1 input (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}), independently
    derivable from the public burn ledger and committed epoch edge
    set (\zcref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}).
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Final Standing Input]
    \label{rem:sorting:final-standing-input}
    Fix accepted epoch~$k$.  Every relevance calculation consumes the
    final reduced standing
    $\epochrefstanding{k}{\operatorname{creator}(c)}$.  The base allocation
    matrix, hop matrices, emission fractions, the accepted rung, the
    certificates, fixed-point enclosures, and solver iterates have no feed
    read-site; their only terminal consequence is the final standing value
    they jointly determine.
\end{remark}

The content norm uses the \emph{scalar interface}
($\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_c}_F \cdot \sqrt{1+\bar{\tau}^2}$) because the
content node is a terminus, not a path step: it does not participate in
matrix composition.  The standing factor is imported as one binding
scalar and is independent of the feed's raw path traversal: its own
Actor-only projection and certificate have already been evaluated at
the epoch boundary.  The factor $\ampfactor{\operatorname{creator}(c)}$
also appears in the reward formula
(\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}); this cross-channel
co-appearance is deliberate and not double-counting
(\zcref{rem:transport:cross-channel-commitment-amplification}).

\begin{remark}[Terminal vs.\ Routing Contribution]
    \label{rem:sorting:terminal-routing-asymmetry}
    A content node's \emph{routing} contribution depends on the
    directional structure of incoming edges (path-view determinant).
    Its \emph{terminal} contribution uses total energy (scalar
    $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F$) because the content node is a
    path terminus, not a path step.  A path reaching content with high
    total engagement but directionally incoherent incoming edges has
    strong terminal weight but pays routing costs at each intermediate
    step.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Score Positivity]
    \label{prop:sorting:score-positivity}
    $S(u,c) > 0$ whenever a viable path of length $\leq L$ exists;
    $S(u,c) = 0$ otherwise.
    \proofsketch{All damped weights positive
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds}); content norm positive
    (\zcref{lem:graph:non-vanishing-norm});
    $\ampfactor{} \geq 1$.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Weak-Link Suppression]
    \label{prop:sorting:weak-link-suppression}
    If any edge $e^*$ on the optimal path has
    $\detscore{e^*} = \sqrt{\epsilon}$ with $\epsilon \ll 1$:
    \[
        S(u,c)
        \leq \sqrt{\epsilon}
        \cdot \textstyle\prod_{e \neq e^*} \dampedweight{e}
        \cdot \ampfactor{\operatorname{creator}(c)}
          \norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F.
    \]
    A single low-determinant edge suppresses the entire path score.
\end{proposition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Log-Transform Equivalence}
\label{subsec:sorting:log-transform-equivalence}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Log-Relevance Distance]
    \label{def:sorting:log-relevance-distance}
    \begin{equation}
        d_{\log}(u, c)
        = \min_{p \in \operatorname{Paths}_L(u \to c)}
          \sum_{e \in p} (-\ln \dampedweight{e}).
        \label{eq:sorting:log-relevance-distance}
    \end{equation}
    Per-edge log-cost decomposition:
    \begin{equation}
        -\ln \dampedweight{e}
        = \underbrace{
            -\tfrac{1}{2}\ln|\det(\pathview{e})|
          }_{\text{coherence cost}}
        \;\underbrace{
            -\tfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+\tau_e^2)
          }_{\text{maturity discount}}
        \;+\;
        \underbrace{
            \invtemp \tentropy{e}
          }_{\text{boundary penalty}}.
        \label{eq:sorting:log-cost-decomposition}%
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Log-Transform Equivalence]
    \label{thm:sorting:log-transform-equivalence}
    At $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$, the max-product path and the
    min-sum log-distance path are identical:
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{p}
        \textstyle\prod_{e \in p} \dampedweight{e}
        \;=\;
        \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{p}
        \textstyle\sum_{e \in p} (-\ln \dampedweight{e}).
        \label{eq:sorting:log-equivalence}
    \end{equation}
    On the positive-weight subgraph all path computations reduce to
    shortest-path problems with positive additive costs:
    \textbf{Dijkstra-compatible}.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    Routing-active edges have $\dampedweight{e} > 0$
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:damped-weight-bounds}), so $\ln$ is well-defined on
    every positive-weight path.  A routing-inert edge
    ($\dampedweight{e} = 0$, \zcref{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy})
    gives product zero, is never the maximizer, and is excluded from the
    shortest-path reduction with cost $-\ln\dampedweight{e} = +\infty$.  Then:
    \[
        \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{p}
        \textstyle\prod_{e} \dampedweight{e}
        \;=\;
        \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{p}
        \textstyle\sum_{e} \ln \dampedweight{e}
        \;=\;
        \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{p}
        \textstyle\sum_{e} (-\ln \dampedweight{e}).
    \]
    First equality: $\ln$ is strictly increasing.  Second: negation
    reverses the ordering.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Raw sorting--transport comparison.}
Content sorting and the canonical bridge-affinity channel both consume
the raw damped edge formula $\dampedweight{e}$
(\zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}).  Sorting operates on the
raw Action Graph; bridge affinity operates on the raw positive subgraph
$\posgraph$ (\zcref{def:bridge:positive-subgraph}).  Both inherit raw
maturity and temporal damping, including the maturity crossover
$\tau^*$ (\zcref{prop:epoch:crossover-location}).

Standing is excluded from this comparison.  It consumes complete
projected person-vouch acts and the projected standing activation,
not raw $\dampedweight{e}$.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Anisotropy Penalty}
\label{subsec:sorting:anisotropy}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{proposition}[Anisotropy Penalty]
    \label{prop:sorting:anisotropy-penalty}
    The per-edge log-cost under determinant scoring exceeds the
    Frobenius log-cost by:
    \begin{equation}
        c_{\mathrm{det}}(e) - c_{\mathrm{Frob}}(e)
        = \tfrac{1}{2}
          \ln\!\bigl(
          \condnum{\pathview{e}} + 1/\condnum{\pathview{e}}
          \bigr).
        \label{eq:sorting:anisotropy-penalty}
    \end{equation}
    Isotropic ($\condnum{}=1$): $\approx 0.35$.
    Focused ($\condnum{}=10$): $\approx 1.16$.
    Rank-1 ($\condnum{} \to \infty$): $\to \infty$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    $-\ln\norm{\pathview{}}_F
    = -\tfrac{1}{2}\ln(\svdone{}^2 + \svdtwo{}^2)$.
    Determinant cost:
    $-\tfrac{1}{2}\ln(\svdone{}\svdtwo{})$.
    Difference:
    $\tfrac{1}{2}\ln[(\svdone{}^2+\svdtwo{}^2)/(\svdone{}\svdtwo{})]
    = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(\condnum{}+1/\condnum{})$.
\end{proof}

Balanced engagement (low $\condnum{}$) is cheaper per edge than focused
engagement (high $\condnum{}$) with the same total energy.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Algorithms}
\label{subsec:sorting:algorithms}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

By \zcref{thm:sorting:log-transform-equivalence}, computing $S(u,c)$
reduces to shortest paths with costs $-\ln\dampedweight{e}$.

\deploymentref{subsec:deployment:feed-reproducibility}%
\deploymentref{subsec:deployment:device-local}%
\begin{algorithm}
    \caption{Exact Bounded-Depth Feed Traversal
    (paths $\leq L$).  Returns the exact max-product
    $R(c) = \max_p \prod_e \dampedweight{e}$ for all content
    $c \in V_c$.  The per-edge value $\dampedweight{e}$ is the
    canonical raw terminal default of
    \zcref{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight}; it is shared with raw
    bridge and signed services, not with standing
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}).}
    \label{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs}%
    \phantomsection\label{alg:sorting:exact-feed-traversal}
    \begin{algorithmic}[1]
        \State \textbf{Input:} User $u$, raw snapshot $\rawgraph{k}$
               (\zcref{def:graph:raw-traversal-snapshot}), depth $L$
        \State $R_0(u) \gets 1$;\; $R_0(v) \gets 0$ for $v \neq u$;\;
               $R_{\le 0} \gets R_0$
        \For{$d = 1$ \textbf{to} $L$}
            \State $R_d(v) \gets 0$ for every node~$v$
            \ForAll{directed raw snapshot edges $v \to w$}
                  \State $R_d(w) \gets \max\!\bigl(R_d(w),\;
                      R_{d-1}(v) \cdot \dampedweight{v \to w}\bigr)$
            \EndFor
            \State $R_{\le d}(v) \gets \max(R_{\le d-1}(v), R_d(v))$
                   for every node~$v$
        \EndFor
        \ForAll{content $c \in V_c$ with $R_{\le L}(c) > 0$}
            \State $S(u,c) \gets R_{\le L}(c) \cdot
                   \ampfactor{\operatorname{creator}(c)}
                   \cdot \norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F$
        \EndFor
        \State \Return sort descending by $S(u,c)$
    \end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}

\begin{lemma}[BFS Correctness and Complexity]
    \label{lem:sorting:bfs-correctness}
    \zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs} computes max-product path
    relevance in $O(\bar{d}^L)$ time.  Per-edge: $\sim\!8$
    floating-point operations (one $2 \times 2$ determinant, one
    square root, two lookups, two multiplications).
    \proofsketch{Induction on depth.  Damped weight is $O(1)$ per
    edge.}
\end{lemma}

\begin{remark}[Matrix BFS]
    \label{rem:sorting:matrix-bfs}
    For $\divpref \neq \tfrac{1}{2}$, the score does not factorize
    per edge: $2 \times 2$ matrix accumulators must be propagated,
    at $\sim\!25$ ops/edge.  The system default
    $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$ avoids this overhead.
    The raw signed double-cover service
    (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}) uses the same raw
    $\dampedweight{e}$ formula (at $\divpref = \tfrac{1}{2}$ by design)
    and adds one parity-sign operation per raw edge
    ($\sim\!9$ ops/edge total), with two registers per node and no
    matrix accumulation.  It does not compute standing.
    A guild may expose $\divpref\neq\tfrac12$ for its own terminal
    sorting, at matrix-BFS cost, without changing binding standing
    (\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Raw Pruning Is an Implementation Detail]
    \label{rem:sorting:raw-pruning-is-implementation}
    The canonical raw feed, signed, and bridge services are exact
    bounded-depth max-product computations on $\rawgraph{k}$.  Layer~1
    publishes no raw pruning tolerance, precision clip, semantic weak-path
    cutoff, or permanent pruned-node state.

    An implementation may use caching, best-first evaluation,
    branch-and-bound, or state pruning only when the optimization
    preserves the exact declared output.  Approximate or thresholded raw
    traversal is a terminal Layer~2 choice and must publish its own error,
    cutoff, and tie semantics.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Estimator Semantics]
    \label{rem:sorting:mc-estimator-semantics}
    A biased random walk with transition probabilities
    $\propto \dampedweight{e}$ estimates the sum-of-paths quantity
    $R_\Sigma(c) = \sum_{p:\,u\to c} \prod_{e\in p}\dampedweight{e}$,
    not the max-product $R(c) = \max_p \prod_{e\in p}\dampedweight{e}$
    used by the relevance score
    (\zcref{def:sorting:relevance-score}).  The two coincide up to a
    multiplicative factor only when path mass concentrates on the
    dominant path.
\end{remark}

\begin{algorithm}
    \caption{Monte Carlo Sum-of-Paths Mass Estimation
    (paths $> L$).  Estimates sum-of-paths
    $\hat{R}_\Sigma(c)$; distinct from $R(c)$, see
    \zcref{rem:sorting:mc-estimator-semantics}.}
    \label{alg:sorting:monte-carlo-sum-of-paths}
    \begin{algorithmic}[1]
        \State \textbf{Input:} User $u$, \ActionGraph{} $G$,
               samples $k$
        \For{$j = 1$ \textbf{to} $k$}
            \State Random walk from $u$, transition
                   $\propto \dampedweight{e}$
            \ForAll{content $c$ visited}
                \State $\hat{R}_\Sigma(c) \mathrel{+}=
                       \prod_{e \in \text{subpath}(u \to c)}
                       \dampedweight{e}$
            \EndFor
        \EndFor
        \State \Return $\hat{R}_\Sigma(c)/k$ for all visited $c$
    \end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}

\begin{theorem}[Monte Carlo Concentration]
    \label{thm:sorting:monte-carlo-concentration}
    Let $M = \max_j X_j$ be the maximum single-sample contribution.
    By Hoeffding's inequality\footcite{hoeffding1963probability}, for
    any $\epsilon, \delta > 0$:
    \[
        \Pr[|\hat{R}_\Sigma(c) - R_\Sigma(c)| > \epsilon]
        \leq 2\exp\!\bigl(-2k\epsilon^2/M^2\bigr).
    \]
    Sample complexity:
    $k \geq (M^2/2\epsilon^2)\ln(2/\delta)$.
    \proofsketch{Hoeffding's inequality on bounded, independent
    $X_j \in [0, M]$ with mean $R_\Sigma(c)$.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Boundary Tightening]
    \label{cor:sorting:boundary-tightening}
    The Boltzmann factor reduces $M$, tightening concentration.
    Required sample count decreases with average path entropy.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Post-Ranking Diagnostic Cost]
    \label{rem:sorting:diagnostic-cost}
    The path diagnostics of
    \zcref{subsec:graph:path-diagnostics-and-archetypes}
    are computed \emph{after} sorting, not during the BFS.  For each
    content node in the ranked feed: propagate the $2 \times 2$
    path-view accumulator along the optimal path ($4d$
    multiplications), compute one closed-form $2 \times 2$ SVD
    (12 ops), and extract $\cohratio{}$, $\detsign{}$, $\modeangle{}$
    ($\sim\!5$ ops).  Total: $\sim\!4L + 17$ operations per displayed
    card; at $L = 4$, $\sim\!33$ operations.  BFS complexity
    (\zcref{lem:sorting:bfs-correctness}) is unchanged.  There is no
    interaction with the binding standing package: diagnostics are
    computed on the raw feed-ranking path.  The raw signed double-cover
    service (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}) is a separate terminal
    computation.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Cross-Cluster Amplification}
\label{subsec:sorting:cross-cluster-amplification}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{theorem}[Cross-Cluster Amplification]
    \label{thm:sorting:cross-cluster-amplification}
    Along a path of length $d$ with uniform maturity $\tau$, the
    ratio of the damped path product to the zero-maturity baseline is:
    \begin{equation}
        \frac{\prod_e \dampedweight{e}}
             {\prod_e \detscore{e}}
        = g(\tau)^d,
        \qquad
        g(\tau) = \sqrt{1+\tau^2} \cdot e^{-\invtemp \tentropy{}}.
        \label{eq:sorting:cross-cluster-amplification}
    \end{equation}
    Independent of the sentiment factor.  Net amplification iff
    $\tau > \tau^*$ (\zcref{def:epoch:maturity-crossover}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}c c c c@{}}
    \toprule
    $\tau$ & $g(\tau)$ & $g(\tau)^4$ & Net effect \\
    \midrule
    $0.00$ & $1.000$ & $1.000$ & baseline \\
    $0.50$ & $\numval{const.activation.g_half.num}$ & $\numval{result.activation.g4_half.num}$ & $29\times$ suppression \\
    $0.80$ & $\numval{result.activation.g_08.num}$ & $\numval{result.activation.g4_08.num}$ & $6\times$ suppression \\
    $0.94$ & $\numval{result.activation.g_094.num}$ & $\numval{result.activation.g4_094.num}$ & breakeven \\
    $0.95$ & $\numval{result.activation.g_095.num}$ & $\numval{result.activation.g4_095.num}$ & $1.2\times$ amplification \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{corollary}[Serendipity Conditions]
    \label{cor:sorting:serendipity-conditions}
    Cross-tribal content discovery requires two simultaneous
    conditions:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Decisive maturity:}
              $\tau > \tau^* \approx 0.94$.
        \item \textbf{Sentiment coherence:} connecting edges must
              be \tierfull{} (directional judgments with substantial
              $\detscore{}$).  Cross-cluster paths through \tiermarginal{}
              edges are dramatically suppressed.
    \end{enumerate}
    Since $\tau = k/(k+1)$ for integer prior-degree maximum~$k$,
    the threshold $\tau > \tau^* \approx 0.94$ is a discrete
    prior-degree condition: $k \geq 16$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Polarized Cluster Amplification]
    \label{cor:sorting:polarized-cluster-amplification}
    High-engagement content maintains a well-conditioned path-view matrix via
    the Polarization Floor (\zcref{prop:graph:polarization-floor}), creating
    gravitational pull that shortens paths terminating at it.
\end{corollary}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Score Monotonicity}
\label{subsec:sorting:score-monotonicity}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{theorem}[Score Monotonicity]
    \label{thm:sorting:score-monotonicity}
    $S(u,c)$ is:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{standing-monotone:}
              $\partial S / \partial \refstanding{\operatorname{creator}}
              \geq 0$.
        \item \textbf{Content-quality-monotone:}
              $\partial S / \partial
              \norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F \geq 0$.
        \item \textbf{Coherence-monotone:}
              $\partial S / \partial |\det(\pathview{e})| \geq 0$
              for any path edge.
        \item \textbf{Maturity-non-monotone:} minimum near
              $\tau \approx 0.5$; net amplification only above
              $\tau^*$.
        \item \textbf{Entropy-monotone:}
              $\partial S / \partial \tentropy{} \leq 0$.
        \item \textbf{Diversity-monotone} (for $\divpref > 0$):
              $\partial S / \partial \svdtwo{} \geq 0$.
        \item \textbf{Focus-penalizing} (for $\divpref > 0$):
              $\partial S / \partial \condnum{} \leq 0$
              when $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$ (generically satisfied:
              $\bleedparam$-softening guarantees $\det \neq 0$ and
              hence $\svdtwo{} > 0$, with $\svdone{} > \svdtwo{}$
              unless the path matrix is isotropic).
        \item \textbf{Raw profile-bridge-monotone:}
              For a fixed raw profile-bridged feed path from an
              actor~$i$ to content~$c$ authored by Actor~$j$, the raw
              derived Reputation edge remains monotone in the published
              standing input under its raw bond rule:
              \[
                  \frac{\partial S(i,c)}{\partial\refstanding{j}}
                  \geq 0
              \]
              through both the raw bridge factor
              $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}(\standing{j})$ and
              the terminal amplification $\ampfactor{j}$.  This is a
              feed property only; the projected standing activation
              uses a different formula and graph.
    \end{enumerate}
    \proofsketch{(1--2) non-negative multiplicative factors outside
    the path product.  (3) $\dampedweight{}$ monotone in $\detscore{}$.
    (4--5) maturity--boundary interaction.  (6--7) $\svdtwo{}$ enters
    with positive exponent at $\divpref > 0$.  (8) The commitment
    amplification product $A(\refstanding{j})$
    (\zcref{def:nodes:raw-profile-bridge-amplification}) is a product
    of two strictly increasing non-negative functions of $\refstanding{j}$;
    all other path weight factors are non-negative. Since
    $\partial S/\partial\standing{} =
    (1/\numeraire)\,\partial S/\partial\refstanding{}$ and
    $\numeraire>0$, the full-coordinate monotonicity claims follow by the
    chain rule.}
\end{theorem}

Property~(3) is the formal mechanism by which the system rewards
directionally coherent engagement over one-dimensional volume.

\zcref{sec:transport} uses the bridge campaign scalar
$\campaignscalar{A}$ (\zcref{app:bridge}) as the advertiser-value gate,
the realizing-forest $S_C$ for attribution, and the \AttrView{} CAN
enrichment factor as the Layer~2 reward signal, receiving the
standing $\standing{C}$ from Layer~1 at each epoch boundary
(\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}).

\section{Advertiser Transport}
\label{sec:transport}

Advertising is a Layer~2 operation on Layer~1 inputs.  The advertiser
purchases \emph{endorsed connection} to actor targets ---
proximity to a target's community through an intermediary the community
trusts, who vouches for the advertiser, and whom the advertiser regards
positively --- not structural proximity.  Under structural proximity
alone, an advertiser may be one hop from a target while every
intermediary is oriented against it, connecting with no one; the
bilateral bridge circuit prices exactly the conditions under which
genuine connection exists.

This chapter describes a canonical guild design that any guild may
adopt, adapt, or replace entirely, subject to the structural invariants
of \zcref{app:can} and the verifiability requirements of
\zcref{app:deployment}.  The network operator does not constrain guild
economic design beyond those invariants.

All channel definitions, the campaign scalar $\campaignscalar{A}$, the
Cancellation Lemma, the full distributional surface (realizing-forest $S_C$,
$I_C$, $V_{\max}$), and the re-scoped monotonicity live in
\zcref{app:bridge}; this chapter carries the reward-formula slot, the
guild model, and the properties that hold verbatim.  Nothing in this
chapter is load-bearing without \zcref{app:bridge}.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Commitment via Burn}
\label{subsec:transport:commitment-via-burn}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Commitment via Burn]
    \label{def:transport:commitment-via-burn}
    $\burnval{i} \in \R_{\geq 0}$ is the burn value of
    \zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame}: the cumulative reserve-denominated
    value committed by actor~$i$, read from Layer~0. Costliness and
    irrevocability are inherited at the network's sampling depth
    (\zcref{ins:comparator:inherited-costliness}); the underlying Layer~0
    properties are
    \attestationcref{thm:interface:instantaneous-costliness} and
    \attestationcref{lem:costliness:attestation-append-only}. During the
    bootstrapping phase aggregate $\burnval{i}$ is capacity-bounded by
    $\burncap$ (\zcref{def:comparator:bootstrap-capacity}). All formulas in this
    section consume $\burnval{i}$ as a non-negative, non-decreasing,
    publicly auditable scalar; no surface quantity appears.
\end{definition}


\begin{remark}[Burn Granularity]
    \label{rem:transport:burn-granularity}
    The minimum burn increment and the representational precision
    of $\burnval{i}$ are implementation-defined.  This document
    specifies $\burnval{i} \in \R_{\geq 0}$; any compliant
    implementation must support sufficient precision that
    the \emph{reduced} rate $\hat r_i=\commitrate{i}/\numeraire$ is
    representable to at least $8$ significant figures (a \emph{relative}
    requirement, independent of $\numeraire$). IEEE-754 double precision
    supplies this for any $\numeraire$ in $[10^{-39},10^{5}]$ and far
    beyond.  The precision requirement is a network implementation
    constraint on the read value $\burnval{i}$; the granularity and
    class structure of the underlying surface unit are Layer~0's
    (\attestationcref{def:operations:burn}, \attestationcref{def:model:classes}).
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Guild Model}
\label{subsec:transport:guild-model}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\paragraph{Layer~1 obligations.}
\networkref{subsec:introduction:two-layers-derived}%
The network operator provides the binding infrastructure on which all
guilds operate:

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item the accepted public record graph and boundary source state,
          satisfying
          \zcref{post:introduction:public-accessibility,%
post:introduction:record-integrity,%
post:introduction:authoritative-act-order,%
post:introduction:epoch-edge-set};
    \item the exact conserved standing package, including the base
          allocation matrix, the accepted tilt rung, the depth mass,
          source emission, the conserved transport, the standing field,
          and the certificate verdict
          (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package});
    \item title and every other binding closure output;
    \item the constants and formula/hash versions used by binding
          computation.
\end{itemize}

The binding network constants include
$\invtemp$, $\bleedparam$, $\numeraire$, the floor family,
$\marginfactor$, $\epochlen$, $\snapbuf$, $\hopmax$, and
$\maxpayload$, together with the standing compiler and certificate
versions.  The canonical raw-feed and raw-bridge defaults
$\divpref$, raw depth~$L$, $\wspam$, $\wmax$, and
$\wmaxop$ are terminal defaults: the host may publish cached values,
but a guild may independently recompute or replace them under
\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}.  The Layer~0 surface
constants $\feerate$, $\livesplit$, and $\matlead$ (with their derived
$R_{\mathrm{ceil}}$) are Layer~0's, surfaced for reproducibility
(\attestationcref{subsec:model:constants}).

The operator's economic inflow remains the Layer~0 minting fee
(\attestationcref{def:model:fee-and-split}, surfaced at
\zcref{sec:comparator}): the sole protocol-level value flow to the
operator.  No protocol-level fee is extracted from content
transactions, advertising spend, or guild reward pools.

\paragraph{Layer~2: Guilds.}
\layertworef{subsec:introduction:two-layers-derived}%
Multiple guilds operate simultaneously and independently on the shared
Layer~1 graph.  Each guild:

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item Publishes its complete CAN recursion, all guild-specific
          economic parameters, and its reward formula in full, so any
          participant can independently reproduce every reward
          computation (\zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}).
    \item Maintains a self-contained reward pool funded by guild-level
          advertising spend, from which the guild may retain a published
          fee or operating margin
          (\zcref{rem:transport:guild-economic-autonomy}).
    \item Selects its own CAN aggregation function, attribution
          threshold parameters, reward distribution schedule, and
          bridge composition rule (\zcref{app:bridge}).
    \item Has no claim over Layer~1 infrastructure: edge records,
          commitment scores, and standing values are public.
\end{itemize}

Three structural CAN invariants are mandatory for all guilds
(\zcref{def:can:mandatory-guild-invariants}): depth decay, transmission
strictly less than one, and context independence.

\begin{postulate}[Guild Reimplementation Grant]
    \label{post:transport:guild-grant}
    A guild MAY redefine, replace, or independently recompute any published
    value every read-site of which is \emph{terminal} --- consumed only by an
    agent and never read back into the decision of what may append to~$G$ (the
    write rule W1/W2a/W2b, the formation rule, or settlement recognition,
    \zcref{def:network:admission-closure,def:graph:settlement-recognition}). Equivalently: a guild owns the
    entire \emph{terminal complement} of the admission closure
    (\zcref{def:network:admission-closure}) --- the feed $S(u,c)$, the
    reward $R_C$, the CAN and its aggregation function, and the bridge transport
    and its composition rule (\zcref{tbl:symbols:boundary}).

    The terminal complement also includes raw graph scoring formulas:
    a guild may replace the canonical raw feed depth, diversity preference,
    raw damped-edge weighting, raw positive-subgraph composition, and raw
    bridge-consent policy, provided it publishes the replacement completely.
    The host's cached raw $\dampedweight{e}$, $\detsign{e}$, and derived
    raw constants are non-authoritative by-products.

    The grant does not include any component of the conserved standing package
    (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package}): the fold compiler and its
    recipient resolution, the base allocation matrix, the tilt profile and the
    accepted rung, the depth mass, source emission, the conserved transport
    $\transport{}$, the rate hull box, the certificate verdict, and the final
    $\standing{}$ are binding and must be consumed as published, though every
    participant may recompute them to audit.

    Conservation is what makes that list closed rather than arbitrary.  Every
    item above feeds a single row-stochastic operator, so a guild that replaced
    any one of them would not merely publish a different number --- it would
    publish a different \emph{total}, and one guild's regard would no longer be
    rival against another's (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}).
    The terminal complement is safe to fork precisely because nothing in it is
    conserved.

    A guild MAY NOT override any value with a feedback read-site: the kernel
    inputs (accepted edge set, binding constants, burn snapshot), the admission
    rules, and the derived straddlers --- the conserved standing package with
    its relative-standing field
    $\standing{i}$ \emph{as gate input} and the title certificate
    $\titlecert{k}$ --- which it must consume as published. A guild MAY still
    \emph{recompute} any such value to audit it
    (\zcref{prop:scalability:conserved-standing-verifiability}); recomputation is an audit
    right, never an override right.

    Deviating from a terminal default forks only the deviating guild (loss of
    composability); attempting to deviate from a binding value forks the shared
    graph and is rejected. The binding surface is the accepted-state kernel,
    admission rules, conserved standing package, standing as gate input, and
    title --- and no larger.
\end{postulate}

\begin{remark}[Why the Grant Is Safe: Three Preconditions]
    \label{rem:transport:guild-grant-preconditions}
    The grant is sound when three conditions hold; they are its
    preconditions, not its corollaries.
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{The binding surface is minimal and fixed.} It was
            minimized in the mechanism design --- one shared registry (title),
            guild-local reward pools, no global reward state. Guilds cannot
            enlarge or shrink it; the grant explicitly closes it at
            $\set{
            \text{accepted-state kernel},
            \text{admission rules},
            \text{conserved standing package},
            \standing{}\text{-as-gate},
            \titlecert{}
            }$.
        \item \textbf{Straddlers are consumed at their kernel value, audited
            not authored.} A guild reads $\standing{i}$ and $\titlecert{k}$
            from the epoch certificate; it may recompute both from the published
            authoritative order $Q_k$ to verify ---
            \zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism} guarantees the
            recomputation reproduces the certificate --- but a guild's
            \emph{own} standing or
            \emph{own} owner has no standing in the shared graph.
        \item \textbf{The feedback-but-terminally-consumed cell is flagged, not
            hidden.} The grant frees terminal values, yet
            \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication} exhibits a binding-authored
            value --- the commercial tie feeding standing parity --- whose
            \emph{consumers} are terminal. The honest disposition, and the
            reason the grant is safe to give, is that its surviving exposure
            lands in the terminal complement, so the fix (a cancel-heavy
            discount) is \emph{itself} a guild choice the grant already permits.
            The boundary does not merely classify the open problem; it hands its
            remedy to Layer~2.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Computed Share versus Realized Reward]
    \label{rem:transport:guild-economic-autonomy}
    The canonical reward formula
    (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}) produces a
    \emph{calculable, normalized share}~$R_C$: a deterministic,
    independently reproducible fraction of the pool $\guildpool$
    assigned to creator~$C$.  What that share transpires to --- the
    unit of account, the payout schedule, any guild fee or operating
    margin, eligibility windows, and the funding relationship between
    advertising spend and $\guildpool$ --- is a Layer~2 policy
    decision reserved entirely to the guild.  The sole cross-cutting
    constraint is \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}: any fee,
    margin, or denomination policy must be published.  No
    protocol-level fee is extracted from $\guildpool$.
\end{remark}


\paragraph{Self-targeting.}
Any actor may act as an advertiser targeting any actor other than
itself.  The domain restriction $T_i \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$,
$B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$ in the campaign scalar
(\zcref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar}) empties the target set when
$A$ targets itself, giving $\campaignscalar{A} = 0$ and hence
$R_C = 0$ for all creators (\zcref{rem:bridge:self-target}).
The structural machinery handles this without a categorical
prohibition.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Advertiser Objective}
\label{subsec:transport:advertiser-objective}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Any actor~$A$ may specify weighted actor targets
$T = \set{(T_i, w_i)}$, $T_i \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$,
$\sum_i w_i = 1$.  The canonical bridge design is a terminal guild
computation over public raw records and the binding standing field.
It purchases three distinct terminal signals:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item raw positive-path affinity from target to bridge
          (\zcref{def:bridge:affinity});
    \item the bridge's raw authored stance toward the advertiser,
          carried through the advertiser's raw Reputation edge
          (\zcref{def:bridge:endorsement});
    \item the advertiser's raw signed consent view of the bridge
          (\zcref{def:bridge:consent}).
\end{enumerate}
These channels do not enter standing, do not alter the standing
projection, and do not reuse hop matrices.  They may read the
published standing field where their raw Reputation or terminal
amplifier formula specifies it.  The \emph{bridge campaign scalar}
\begin{equation}
    \campaignscalar{A}
    = \sum_{i:\, T_i \neq A} w_i
      \max_{B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}}
      \circqual{T_i, B, A}
    \label{eq:transport:campaign-scalar}
\end{equation}
prices the quality of the best such circuit per target; the full
calculus is in \zcref{app:bridge}.  Guild reward pools distribute for
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A} > 0$.
\bridgeref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar}%

\begin{remark}[Targets Are Actors]
    \label{rem:transport:actor-targets}
    The economic object an advertiser purchases is proximity to an
    audience, and audiences are actor-shaped.  To reach a topic or a
    piece of content, an advertiser targets the actor hubs influential
    in that community.  The bridge circuit prices exactly this.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Reward Formula}
\label{subsec:transport:reward-formula}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{equation}
    \boxed{
    R_C
    = \guildpool \cdot \frac{
        \Delta\campaignscalar{A}
        \cdot S_C
        \cdot \dfrac{\canval{n_C}}{V_{\max}}
        \cdot I_C
        \cdot \ampfactor{C}
        \cdot \boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}
    }{
        \displaystyle\sum_{\text{creators}} (\text{same terms})
    }
    }
    \label{eq:transport:reward-formula}
\end{equation}
\deploymentref{subsec:deployment:completeness}%


\paragraph{Campaign scalar gate.}
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A} = \campaignscalar{A}^{(k)} -
\campaignscalar{A}^{(k-1)}$.  The pool distributes when
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A} > 0$; $R_C = 0$ for all creators otherwise.
By the Cancellation Lemma (\zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation}), the
magnitude of $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ cancels in the normalized
ratio: it survives only as the binary gate and as a market signal to
the advertiser for pool-funding decisions.  The creator-varying weights
that survive normalization are $S_C$, $\canval{n_C}$, $I_C$,
$\standing{C}$, and $\epochentropy{C}$
(\zcref{cor:bridge:global-factors-inert}).

\paragraph{Realizing-structure creator-varying weights.}
Three of the surviving weights are defined over the structure that
realizes $\campaignscalar{A}$, so campaign value and per-creator
attribution are computed on the same paths:

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Realizing-forest betweenness $S_C$}
          (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-centrality}): betweenness on
          the extended realizing forest $\set{\realizingpath{i}}$,
          computed exactly in $O(kL)$ from Channel~1's predecessor
          structure.  Credits the bridge plus the affinity-segment
          relays; excludes the target source, the advertiser, and
          passive nodes.
    \item \textbf{Circuit-improvement influence $I_C$}
          (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-active-influence}): authored
          fraction of the circuit-improvement edge set
          $\improveset{A}$ (newly-accepted authored edges on the
          epoch-$k$ realizing forest).  When the creditable
          change-set is empty --- the gate was opened solely by the
          advertiser's own consent edge --- $I_C$ falls back to
          the winning-path support.
    \item \textbf{Realizing-path normalization $V_{\max}$}
          (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-vmax}): maximum CAN value over
          realizing-path nodes.  Distributionally moot (cancels as a
          campaign-global factor); normalized over realizing paths for
          interpretive consistency.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Recipient-population shift.}
Content-creation labor is compensated through the CAN enrichment factor
$\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$, which uses the \AttrView{} ($3 \times 3$
Frobenius norms, ${\sim}\,16\%$ cross-type variation;
\zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}).  Endorsement
intermediation --- affinity relay and bridge vouching --- is
compensated through the realizing-forest $S_C$, which uses the \PathView{}
(determinant scoring, ${\sim}\,4.5\times$ tier gap).  This separation
is a consequence of the dual-view architecture: the \AttrView{} prices
creation equitably; the \PathView{} prices endorsement discriminately.
A creator who also bridges earns from both.  A pure bridge earns from
$S_C$ alone.  A pure creator earns from CAN alone.

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Dual-layer origin of each reward factor.}
    \label{tbl:transport:layer-origins}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Factor} & \textbf{Origin} & \textbf{View} \\
        \midrule
        $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$
            & Layer~2 guild; from Layer~1 channels (\zcref{app:bridge})
            & \PathView{} \\
        $S_C$ (realizing forest)
            & Layer~2 guild; on realizing forest (\zcref{app:bridge})
            & \PathView{} \\
        $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$
            & Layer~2 guild CAN; on Layer~1 Frobenius norms
            & \AttrView{} \\
        $I_C$ (circuit improvement)
            & Layer~2 guild; from Layer~1 edge records (\zcref{app:bridge})
            & view-independent \\
        $\ampfactor{C}$
            & Layer~1; published at epoch boundary (\zcref{sec:epoch})
            & view-independent \\
        $\boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}$
            & Layer~2 guild; from Layer~1 edge records
            & view-independent \\
        $\guildpool$
            & Layer~2 guild advertising pool
            & --- \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

The per-creator-epoch entropy is:
\begin{equation}
    \epochentropy{C}
    = \frac{1}{|E_C|} \sum_{e \in E_C} \tentropy{e}.
    \label{eq:transport:epoch-entropy}
\end{equation}


\paragraph{Dual-view roles.}
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$, $S_C$: \PathView{} routing on
          the realizing forest.  Discrimination by directional
          coherence; \tierfull{} engagement dominates betweenness.
    \item $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$: \AttrView{} ($3 \times 3$ norms,
          no~$\tau$).  Attribution equity across interaction domains
          ($\sim\!16\%$ full-range variation in Frobenius norms;
          \zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}).
    \item $I_C$, $\ampfactor{C}$,
          $\boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}$: independent of both views.
\end{itemize}

Binding standing inputs and their compiler/certificate constants are
identical for all guilds operating on the same epoch package.  A guild
must consume the published $\standing{C}$.

Canonical raw terminal defaults need not be identical across guilds:
a guild may publish another diversity preference, raw path depth,
raw edge-weight formula, bridge composition rule, or CAN aggregation
function under \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}.  Guild-specific
choices affect only that guild's terminal feed, attribution, transport,
or reward output ($\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$, $S_C$,
$\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$, $I_C$, $\guildpool$) and never feed back
into~$E$.

\begin{remark}[Cross-Channel Commitment Amplification]
    \label{rem:transport:cross-channel-commitment-amplification}
    The factor $\ampfactor{C}$ appears in both the relevance score
    (\zcref{eq:sorting:relevance-score}) and the reward formula
    (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}) --- the universal-amplifier signature
    (\zcref{ins:comparator:universal-amplifier}), not a double count: the two
    formulas ration different resources (feed attention; pool funds). The
    insulation principle (\zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation})
    forbids only $\standing{}$ entering the same allocation twice, as it would
    through the enrichment factor. Cross-channel compounding --- visibility,
    reward share, and bridge reachability rising together --- is the commitment
    thesis working as intended; removing the factor from either channel would
    decouple visibility from revenue.

    This cross-channel reuse is of the already-certified standing scalar,
    not of its internal hop matrices, emission fractions, or recipient activations.
    Terminal guild formulas may read $\standing{C}$; they may not rerun or
    override the binding standing package under another raw graph rule.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Properties}
\label{subsec:transport:properties}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The properties below depend on the reward formula's structure as a
ratio of non-negative multiplicative terms.

\begin{property}[Final Standing Input Monotonicity]
    \label{pty:transport:final-standing-input-monotonicity}
    Fix every creator-varying reward factor other than final standing.
    Then the canonical reward share is non-decreasing in the published
    input $\epochrefstanding{k}{C}$ through the multiplier
    $1+\epochrefstanding{k}{C}$.

    This is a property of the terminal reward formula.  It does not assert
    that a local change to burn, an act, a vouch, a path coefficient, or a
    lowered tilt rung monotonically changes the recomputed final standing
    field.
\end{property}


\begin{corollary}[Zero-Reward]
    \label{cor:transport:zero-reward}
    If $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} \leq 0$, then $R_C = 0$ for all
    creators.  If $A$ targets itself, the domain restriction empties
    the target set, $\campaignscalar{A} = 0$, and the gate fails.
    \proofsketch{$\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ is a multiplicative
    factor in every numerator term; when $\leq 0$, the gate sets
    all shares to zero.}
\end{corollary}


\begin{theorem}[Epoch Entropy Damping]
    \label{thm:transport:epoch-entropy-damping}
    $\partial R_C / \partial\,\mathrm{Chaos}(\tau) < 0$, where
    $\mathrm{Chaos}(\tau)$ measures the concentration of an actor's
    edge timings near the maximum-entropy point $\tau \approx 0.5$.
    Actors whose interaction patterns cluster at the maximum-entropy
    maturity value receive lower rewards, independently of their
    commitment rate or centrality.
    \proofsketch{Chain rule: $\mathrm{Chaos}(\tau) \uparrow\;
    \Rightarrow\; \epochentropy{C} \uparrow\;
    \Rightarrow\; \boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}} \downarrow\;
    \Rightarrow\; R_C \downarrow$.  Each step is monotone and
    independent of all Layer~1 constants except~$\invtemp$.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reward Proportionality]
    \label{thm:transport:reward-proportionality}
    The reward $R_C$ to creator $C$ within a canonical guild is proportional to
    their composite utility --- campaign-value improvement
    ($\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$), centrality, CAN enrichment, influence,
    standing, and boundary damping --- normalised across all contributing
    creators.\footcite{shapley1953value}
    \proofsketch{Ratio of non-negative multiplicative terms; the efficiency,
    dummy, and proportionality axioms are immediate.}
\end{theorem}


\paragraph{Campaign-value monotonicity and incentive alignment.}
The bridge campaign scalar $\campaignscalar{A}$ is monotone in each
channel factor (affinity, endorsement magnitude, consent,
standing) as a gate-opening and signal property, not as a per-creator weight
--- the magnitude cancels in the normalized ratio
(\zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation}).  Creator shares move at discrete
restructuring events (argmax flips, optimal-path promotions,
tie-splits), not as smooth gradients of $\campaignscalar{A}$.  A relay
maximizes its share by being selected onto the optimal realizing path,
which is the aligned behavior.  The full re-scoped monotonicity theorem,
the discrete structure sensitivity proposition, and the
selection-tournament incentive corollary are in
\zcref{thm:bridge:monotonicity,%
prop:bridge:discrete-structure-sensitivity,%
cor:bridge:selection-tournament}.

\paragraph{Fee monotonicity (guild-level).}
Increasing guild fee reduces $\guildpool$, hence $R_C$ for all
creators proportionally.  The fee is a guild policy choice
(\zcref{rem:transport:guild-economic-autonomy}), transparent by
\zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}.

\zcref{sec:content} specifies content-level governance (licensing,
provenance) that affects adoption and hence $S_C$.
\zcref{sec:scalability} uses the same \PathView{} distances for the
approximation guarantee, Nash preservation, Sybil resistance, and the
four-layer spam resistance argument, with the bridge model's exact
$O(kL)$ betweenness
(\zcref{prop:bridge:sc-inheritance}) eliminating the approximation
requirement for advertising centrality.

% §9: Content Governance
%
% CHANGELOG:
%   v0.22.0-dev  Version normalization and changelog squash; no content change.

\section{Content Governance}
\label{sec:content}

Every authored act carries a payload projection
(\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-projection}) and
every content node carries metadata beyond the sentiment
slice: licensing terms that constrain downstream use, provenance markers
that record origin and AI involvement, and format-level attributes that
the current specification does not formalize.  None of these enter any
scoring, attribution, or transport formula in
\zcref{sec:epoch,sec:sorting,sec:transport} or
\zcref{app:can,app:bridge}.  They are governance-layer attributes:
they affect what actors \emph{choose} to do with content (adopt it,
share it, build on it), and those choices in turn affect the graph
topology that the scoring and transport machinery reads.  The
interaction is indirect and one-directional.

Payload state also leaves complete-act standing identity unchanged.
For a binary person-vouch act, author, semantic target, parameter tuple,
and projected time are structural.  For a hyper-edge person-vouch,
the A-leg/T-leg roles, reciprocal co-leg keys, author, semantic target,
and parameter tuple remain structural
(\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection}).  Removing payload bytes therefore
changes neither
\[
    \operatorname{actkey}(q),
    \qquad
    \foldcoef{\foldcell},
    \qquad
    \basescore{u}{j},
\]
provided the same accepted structural records remain: for any completed
epoch state the base allocation entry is unchanged,
because payload state enters no standing formula.

Thus content erasure cannot create, destroy, redirect, or retarget a
standing vouch.  It removes the controlled payload while preserving the
public structural act on which other Actors may already rely.

This chapter is the structural home for these rules.  At present it
contains the licensing framework inherited from the protocol's initial
design and two stubs marking the growth directions.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Licensing}
\label{subsec:content:licensing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[License Qualifiers]
    \label{def:content:license-qualifiers}
    Two qualifiers apply to content:
    \textbf{Attribution} $a \in \set{0,1}$ (credit requirement) and
    \textbf{Oversight} $o \in \set{0, 0.5, 1}$ (AI provenance).
    License severity $l_{ij} = a_i + o_j \in [0,2]$ spans a
    $2 \times 3$ space:
    \begin{equation}
        \tensor{\symbf{L}}{_{ij}}
        = \begin{pmatrix}
            \text{Public Domain}
                & \text{Conditional Disclosure}
                & \text{Full Provenance} \\
            \text{Attribution}
                & \text{Conditional Attribution}
                & \text{Full Provenance + Attribution}
        \end{pmatrix}
        \label{eq:content:license-matrix}
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}


\begin{remark}[License--Guild Interaction]
    \label{rem:content:license-guild-interaction}
    High $l_{ij}$ reduces adoption, lowering betweenness centrality
    $S_C$ (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-centrality}) and therefore
    reward $R_C$ within any guild's canonical formula.  The commitment
    rate~$\commitrate{C}$ and standing~$\standing{C}$ provide a
    partially offsetting amplification via $\ampfactor{C}$ in the
    reward formula (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}).  Guilds
    with different target communities may tolerate different license
    profiles; the economic consequence of any license choice is
    guild-specific.  Licensing constrains adoption, not tensor
    geometry; it is orthogonal to the dual-view architecture and does
    not affect any Layer~1 computation.
\end{remark}


Licensing metadata is structural metadata of the content's genesis
record (\zcref{def:graph:genesis-act-and-creator,def:graph:canonical-folds}) ---
set at minting, immutable, surviving payload removal
(\zcref{subsec:deployment:immutability}).  It is published as part of
the self-sufficient edge record
(\zcref{subsec:deployment:sufficiency}) and independently verifiable:
any participant can read the license qualifier pair $(a, o)$ from the
published content record and confirm compliance with a guild's
published licensing policy.  No Layer~1 formula consumes $l_{ij}$;
enforcement of licensing terms is a Layer~2 guild responsibility,
published per \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}.

\begin{remark}[Payload Governance Across Phases]
    \label{rem:content:payload-governance-phases}
    In the centralized phase the host may impose schemas, media
    restrictions, or rendering rules on full payload carriage as a custody
    policy; failing a host schema may affect carriage or display but changes
    no Layer~1 computation (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}). In
    the decentralized phase Layer~1 carries only structural records and
    payload residues: payload bytes are not seen and therefore not governed
    by Layer~1. Payload governance is then entirely a Layer~2 carriage and
    rendering concern, of which the licensing qualifiers of
    \zcref{def:content:license-qualifiers} are the content-node special case.

    In both phases the structural complete-act linkage required by the
    standing projection remains public and immutable.  Decentralized
    payload custody therefore changes neither projection completeness nor
    Vcert replay.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Provenance and AI Oversight}
\label{subsec:content:provenance}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The oversight qualifier $o \in \set{0, 0.5, 1}$ from the licensing
matrix (\zcref{def:content:license-qualifiers}) is the seed of a
provenance framework.  Three levels are defined by the qualifier:
$o = 0$ (no AI disclosure required), $o = 0.5$ (conditional
disclosure --- AI involvement must be declared when queried), and
$o = 1$ (full provenance --- the complete generation chain is
published alongside the content record).

At present the specification records the qualifier but does not
formalize the provenance chain itself: what constitutes a valid
provenance record, how provenance claims are verified, and whether
provenance affects any Layer~1 or Layer~2 formula are open design
questions deferred to a future version.  The structural commitment
is that provenance is a content-governance concern, housed here
rather than in the graph mechanics (\zcref{sec:graph}), epoch
infrastructure (\zcref{sec:epoch}), or transport machinery
(\zcref{sec:transport}), and that its eventual formalization
will not require changes to any scoring, attribution, or transport
definition.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Content-Level Metadata}
\label{subsec:content:metadata}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Content nodes carry attributes beyond the sentiment slice and the
licensing qualifiers: media type (text, image, video, audio), format
identifiers, language tags, and display metadata.  The current
specification does not formalize these.  They do not enter any formula
in \zcref{sec:epoch,sec:sorting,sec:transport} or
\zcref{app:can,app:bridge}; they are deployment-layer attributes
satisfying the self-sufficient record requirement of
\zcref{subsec:deployment:sufficiency} (the published record contains
whatever is needed for rendering and policy enforcement) but not
consumed by scoring or attribution.

A future version may introduce content-type-specific rules at this
location --- for example, media-type-dependent CAN weighting (a
Layer~2 guild choice), language-aware feed diversification (a Layer~2
sorting refinement), or format-specific provenance requirements (an
extension of \zcref{subsec:content:provenance}).  Each such rule would
be a content-governance addition housed in this chapter, consuming the
content-node metadata record and producing a modifier consumed
downstream, without altering the graph-level, epoch-level, or
transport-level definitions on which the rest of the specification
rests.

% FILENAME: 10_scalability.tex (v0.22.0-dev)

% CHANGELOG:
