\section{Scalability}
\label{sec:scalability}

Standing is recomputed at every accepted epoch as the unique certified
equilibrium of the completed final epoch state
(\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}).  This does not require discarding
every prior computation.

The mathematical result has no previous-standing input.  A deployment
may nevertheless reuse a cached act fold, base-matrix support, strongly
connected component, interval subdivision, or fixed-point value whenever the
current inputs to that subcomputation are unchanged.  If the inputs changed, a cached standing
value may initialize the new solve but cannot determine its result:
certified contraction makes the fixed point unique
(\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}).

The standing workload has two qualitatively different parts, and conserved
allocation makes the larger one disappear.  One map pass is linear in the
support of the base matrix, and contraction gives a finite geometric iteration
bound (\zcref{prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost}).  Edition~4's
potentially large part --- constructing the exact source-target candidate
relation, the depth-two max envelope and the depth-three and depth-four
candidates selected from the intermediate equilibria --- has no successor at
all.  There is nothing to select: the transport apportions over the support the
base matrix already fixes.

This section separates allocation-input maintenance, fixed-point evaluation,
interval certification, and boundary search.  Optional global guild centrality
remains a separate terminal workload.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Bottleneck Separation}
\label{subsec:scalability:bottleneck}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{proposition}[Bottleneck Separation]
    \label{prop:scalability:bottleneck}
    The network has five distinct computational surfaces
    (\zcref{subsec:transport:reward-formula};
    standing, \zcref{subsec:epoch:final-standing}):
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Raw terminal traversal} (\ActionGraph{},
              \PathView{}): bounded raw depth~$L$ gives local
              $O(\bar d_{\mathrm{raw}}^{\,L})$ traversal per source
              under the canonical default
              (\zcref{lem:sorting:bfs-correctness}).  Terminal.
        \item \textbf{CAN attribution} (\CompGraph{}, \AttrView{}):
              $O(|N| + |E_{\mathrm{CAN}}|)$ via topological-order
              traversal, with registered subtrees cached
              (redundancy $\redundancy{n}$: reachable leaf sets, finite
              and cached).  Per-leaf cost $O(9)$ for the $3 \times 3$
              Frobenius norm.  DAG-terminal.
        \item \textbf{Conserved standing:} binding per epoch --- the base
              allocation matrix, the accepted rung's map passes, and the
              final W1/W2 gates
              (\zcref{prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost}).  Each pass
              is sparse in $\nnz_k$ and their number is a published
              constant; there is no candidate relation and nothing is
              selected.  It runs once per epoch package, not per feed or
              reward query; a guild reward consumes the published
              $\standing{i}$ as a fixed external scalar at $O(1)$ per Actor.
        \item \textbf{Standing certification:} the certificate and its
              verdict
              (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), one
              closed-form sweep of the base matrix's support
              (\zcref{prop:scalability:standing-certificate-cost}).  It is
              cheaper than a single map pass and does not depend on the
              solve, so it does not compete with the surface above for the
              epoch's budget.
        \item \textbf{Optional global guild centrality} $S_C$:
              $O(|V| \cdot |E| + |V|^2 \log |V|)$ via the weighted
              variant of Brandes's algorithm\footcite{brandes2001faster}
              (the $|V|^2 \log |V|$ term is the Dijkstra overhead),
              the largest potentially unbounded \emph{terminal} guild
              workload when a guild requests global centrality; canonical
              advertising centrality remains exact at $O(kL)$
              (\zcref{rem:scalability:advertising-centrality-exact}).
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Advertising Centrality Is Exact Under the Bridge Model]
    \label{rem:scalability:advertising-centrality-exact}
    The general $O(|V|\cdot|E| + |V|^2\log|V|)$ Brandes bound above is
    the worst case for global betweenness.  For advertiser transport it
      does not bind: the realizing-forest $S_C$
    (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-centrality}) is betweenness on the
    extended realizing forest of at most $k$ targets, each of depth
    $\leq 5$, and is computed \emph{exactly} in $O(kL)$ from Channel~1's
    predecessor structure with approximation error $\epsilon = 0$
    (\zcref{prop:bridge:sc-inheritance}).  The $(\epsilon,\delta)$
    machinery of \zcref{subsec:scalability:approximation-guarantee} is
    therefore general infrastructure, not the advertising path; advertising
    centrality clears the bottleneck by construction.

    The realizing forest is a raw terminal bridge object and is unrelated
    to the causal standing-path set, even when both contain the same
    Actor identifiers.
\end{remark}

The graph readings scale independently:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item raw feed traversal runs on local raw ego networks;
    \item CAN runs on the composition DAG;
    \item standing compiles an Actor-only complete-act projection and
          certifies certified depth-four stages once per epoch;
    \item optional global centrality remains a separate terminal guild
          cost.
\end{itemize}
The raw signed double-cover service is invoked only by terminal callers
that require signed raw-path evidence, such as canonical bridge consent.
It is not on the standing or per-reward critical path.

After exact standing candidate work is accounted for, global betweenness
is not the only potentially dense graph computation.  It remains the
principal unbounded \emph{terminal} guild computation; exact standing
closure is the principal binding \emph{candidate-generation}
computation.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Standing Work Model}
\label{subsec:scalability:conserved-standing-work-model}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Conserved Standing Work Measures]
    \label{def:scalability:conserved-standing-work-measures}
    For accepted epoch~$k$ let $n_k$ be the number of anchored Actors and
    $\nnz_k$ the number of nonzero entries of the base allocation matrix
    $\basescore{}{}$ after folding and recipient resolution
    (\zcref{eq:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}).  Every standing cost
    below is expressed in $\nnz_k$, and $\nnz_k\ge n_k$ because the diagonal is
    strictly positive.

    There is no path count, no candidate family, and no admitted-mass measure:
    the base matrix is the only standing-relevant reading of the epoch, so it
    is the only thing whose size can drive standing work.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Allocation Input Maintenance Cost]
    \label{prop:scalability:allocation-input-maintenance-cost}
    Building $\basescore{}{}$ from the accepted epoch set costs one pass over
    the accepted acts: each act folds into exactly one cell, each cell resolves
    to exactly one recipient or to self, and each contributes to exactly one
    entry (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}).  The cost is therefore
    $O(\lvert\actsequence{k}\rvert)$ and is independent of graph density,
    diameter, and every previous epoch's state.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Conserved Map Pass Cost]
    \label{prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost}
    One evaluation of $\standingmapvector{k}{\standingvector}$ costs
    $O(\hopmax\cdot\nnz_k)$.

    The transport is \textbf{applied, never materialized}.  The mediant needs
    only the two transported aggregates $\transbal{i}$ and $\transcount{i}$,
    each of which is $\transport{\standingvector}$ applied to a vector; and
    $\transport{\standingvector}$ applied to a vector is $\hopmax$ sparse
    products against the hop matrices, whose support is that of
    $\basescore{}{}$ (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}).  The
    dense $n_k\times n_k$ object $\transport{\standingvector}$ never exists in
    memory, and forming it would be a defect rather than an optimization.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Standing Certificate Cost]
    \label{prop:scalability:standing-certificate-cost}
    The certificate costs one pass, $O(\nnz_k)$, and is closed form.

    This is the sharpest cost consequence of the fence.  Entrywise
    proportionality (\zcref{lem:dynamics:transport-derivative-propagation})
    collapses the supremum over the box to
    $2\wallgaincap\tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\locwidth{}$
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}), in which the only
    graph-dependent quantity is the contributing width.  Width is a range over
    each row's contributing rates, and support is state-independent
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:support-state-independence}), so the whole
    certificate reduces to one sweep of the base matrix's support.  No
    interval evaluation over the box is required, and no fixed point need be
    known before the certificate is decided --- which is why a rung can be
    screened before it is solved rather than after.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Conserved Equilibrium Cost]
    \label{thm:scalability:conserved-equilibrium-cost}
    Solving one epoch's standing costs
    $O\bigl(\lvert\actsequence{k}\rvert + \tiltgriddepth\cdot\nnz_k
    + \hopmax\cdot\nnz_k\cdot\lceil\log(1/\epsilon)/\log\marginfactor\rceil\bigr)$
    to residual~$\epsilon$: one pass to build the base matrix, one certificate
    sweep per rung attempted, and a geometric number of map passes at the
    accepted rung.

    Every factor is a published constant except $\nnz_k$ and the accepted
    rung's depth in the grid.  There is no term in the number of paths, of
    candidates, or of admitted flows, because none of those objects exists;
    and there is no term that grows with graph diameter, because depth is
    bounded by the published depth mass rather than by reachability.

    The certificate term is the one worth noticing.  It is \emph{additive}, not
    multiplicative, and it does not contain the iteration count --- a rung is
    screened before it is solved
    (\zcref{prop:scalability:standing-certificate-cost}), so a failing rung
    costs one sweep rather than a wasted solve.  Edition~4 could not order the
    work this way: its certificate was per stage and read the stage's own box,
    so a stage had to be constructed before it could be judged.
    \proofsketch{Sum the three preceding propositions, with the iteration count
    from the contraction factor $1/\marginfactor$ of
    \zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Conserved standing work, by surface.  $\nnz_k$ is the support size
    of the base allocation matrix
    (\zcref{def:scalability:conserved-standing-work-measures}); every other
    factor is a published constant.}
    \label{tbl:scalability:conserved-standing-work}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Surface} & \textbf{Cost} & \textbf{Grows with} \\
        \midrule
        Allocation input
            & $O(\lvert\actsequence{k}\rvert)$
            & accepted acts \\
        One map pass
            & $O(\hopmax\,\nnz_k)$
            & support, published depth \\
        Certificate, per rung
            & $O(\nnz_k)$
            & support only \\
        Iterations
            & $O(\log(1/\epsilon)/\log\marginfactor)$
            & margin, not graph \\
        Verification
            & same as production
            & --- \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{proposition}[Conserved Standing Verifiability]
    \label{prop:scalability:conserved-standing-verifiability}
    Any participant reproduces the epoch's standing from the conserved standing
    package (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package}) at the same
    asymptotic cost as the host paid: one pass to rebuild $\basescore{}{}$,
    $O(\hopmax\nnz_k)$ per map evaluation, one pass for the certificate, and
    the published rung to avoid rediscovering the backoff.  Verification is
    never asymptotically harder than production, and it needs no previous
    epoch's solution (\zcref{cor:dynamics:standing-initialization-independence}).
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Fixed-Point Iteration Cost}
\label{subsec:scalability:fixed-point-cost}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{lemma}[Contraction Stopping Rule]
    \label{lem:scalability:contraction-stopping-rule}
    Let a stage map have contraction factor $c<1$ on a box of
    $\infty$-diameter~$D$.  After $t$ Picard passes
    $\norm{x_t-x^\star}_\infty\le c^tD$, so an a-priori error $\le\varepsilon$
    is guaranteed after
    \[
        \boxed{\,T(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil\frac{\log(D/\varepsilon)}{-\log c}\right\rceil.\,}
    \]
    The a-posteriori residual bound
    (\zcref{lem:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure})
    $\norm{x_t-x^\star}_\infty\le\norm{F(x_t)-x_t}_\infty/(1-c)$ permits the
    weaker stopping test $\norm{F(x_t)-x_t}_\infty\le(1-c)\varepsilon$.
\end{lemma}

A fixed universal $\varepsilon$ does not decide admission.  The enclosure
must be narrow enough that, for every proposed-set author,
$\underline x_i\ge\safefloor$ (W2a) and, for the epoch stamp,
$\underline\rho_{\mathrm{ep}}\ge\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (W2b); an enclosure
straddling a threshold is refined, or the proposed set is changed or
rejected.  Rounding may not choose a side
(\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule}).

There is one solve, so there is one worst case.  A rung is valid exactly when
$\marginfactor\standingcert{k}\le1$
(\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), so the contraction
factor of an accepted map is at most
$\numval{const.standing.worst_contraction.num}$ --- the reciprocal of the
published margin, and the only screen there is.  Substituting it into the
stopping rule bounds the passes; the theorem carries the resulting term
(\zcref{thm:scalability:conserved-equilibrium-cost}).

That bound is worst-case, not expected runtime: warm starts reduce initial
error, and a certificate on a benign graph is usually far below its cap.  A
single fixture reporting a small factor does not generalize into a protocol
bound, and stopping must use a certified residual either way.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Solver Decomposition and Exact Reuse}
\label{subsec:scalability:solver-decomposition}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{proposition}[Stage SCC Decomposition]
    \label{prop:scalability:transport-scc-decomposition}
    Use the dependency graph induced by the support of the conserved
    transport, which is fixed by the base matrix and the ledger and so is
    known before the solve
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:support-state-independence}).  Its strongly connected components are computed in
    $O(n_k+L_{k,h})$, where $L_{k,h}$ is the number of derivative-bearing
    dependency edges; the condensation is acyclic and is solved in
    topological order, source-dependent components first, independent
    components at one level in parallel.  A singleton component may still
    carry terminal self-dependence and require a scalar solve; an isolated
    zero-relational row satisfies $x_i=\hat r_i$ directly with no
    iteration.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Exact Component Reuse]
    \label{prop:scalability:exact-component-reuse}
    If a component's current source rates, relation coefficients, activation
    constants, emission fractions, and upstream solved inputs are identical to
    a preceding accepted epoch or trial-set evaluation, then its map is the
    same function with the same unique fixed point: its cached certified
    equilibrium is the exact current equilibrium and may be reused without
    iteration.  This is exact memoization of an unchanged mathematical object,
    not a historical standing input.  If any relevant input changes,
    invalidate that component and every downstream component in the
    condensation DAG, retaining the rest.  Invalidation is by support, not by
    winner: a changed relation coefficient perturbs every row whose transport
    reaches it, so the invalidated set is the reachable set at the supported
    depth.  No optimal minimal invalidation set is claimed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Warm Starts Change Work, Not Standing]
    \label{rem:scalability:warm-start-neutrality}
    When a stage map changes, the preceding accepted equilibrium or a
    nearby trial-set equilibrium may initialize the new solve; certified
    contraction guarantees convergence to the same unique fixed point from
    every point in the invariant box
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:within-epoch-fixed-point-convergence}).  A warm
    start is therefore not a standing input --- it changes iteration count
    only.  Cached path products, previous interval subdivisions, and prior
    SCC decompositions are the same: reusable only after their current
    inputs are checked.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Checking a Claimed Equilibrium}
\label{subsec:scalability:checking-a-claim}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{proposition}[Fixed-Point Check Cost]
    \label{prop:scalability:fixed-point-check-cost}
    Given a claimed approximate fixed point $\tilde x$ and the epoch's
    certificate, one map pass computes
    $r=\norm{F(\tilde x)-\tilde x}_\infty$ and hence
    $\norm{\tilde x-x^\star}_\infty\le r/(1-\standingcert{k})$
    (\zcref{lem:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure}).  Checking a
    claimed equilibrium therefore costs one map evaluation, one residual
    reduction, and the threshold enclosure checks:
    $O(\hopmax\cdot\nnz_k)$ by
    \zcref{prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost}.  A verifier need not
    reproduce the solver's iteration history.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Certification Does Not Parallelize, Because It Does Not Need To]
    \label{rem:scalability:certification-is-one-sweep}
    A reader arriving from a design whose certificate was an interval
    enclosure will expect a decomposition here: rows certified independently
    over projected sub-boxes, distributed across workers, recombined by
    maximum.  There is none, and its absence is not an omission.  The
    certificate is closed form and costs a single $O(\nnz_k)$ sweep
    (\zcref{prop:scalability:standing-certificate-cost}), which is already
    the cost of reading the input; there is no tree to distribute and nothing
    for a second worker to do.

    The decomposition would return with the tighter object of
    \zcref{frontier:certificate-enclosure}, and would be part of its price
    rather than a feature of the design as chartered.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Boundary Search}
\label{subsec:scalability:boundary-search}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{remark}[Boundary Search Is Separate from Validation]
    \label{rem:scalability:boundary-search-cost}
    The final-set predicate answers whether a proposed~$\actsequence{k}$ is valid, not
    which valid~$\actsequence{k}$ to select from every candidate union.  Selection may
    involve dependency-constrained packing, final source-rate and staged
    standing changes, W2a constraints, W2b headroom, epoch target size,
    title conflicts, and censorship concerns; no polynomial
    optimal-selection theorem is claimed.  If the mechanism evaluates
    $S_k$ trial sets with validation costs $V_{k,s}$, worst-case search
    cost is $\sum_{s=1}^{S_k}V_{k,s}$, naively $O(S_kV_k^{\max})$ --- a
    search cost, not the validation complexity of one accepted set.
    Nearby trials differing by few dependent sets may reuse ledger deltas,
    changed bundles, adjacency, D2 wedges, candidate indices, SCC
    decompositions, warm starts, and interval subdivisions, each checked
    against the new trial's current inputs.  Trial sets and their
    provisional standings remain local search state; only the accepted
    final set and its package are Layer-1 objects.  Until the boundary
    mechanism is decentralized the host may choose among valid final sets:
    validity is reproducible, but optimality and non-censorship are not
    inferred from it (\zcref{frontier:boundary-mechanism}).
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Dense Projections}
\label{subsec:scalability:dense-projection}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{remark}[A Dense Projection Costs Its Own Density and Nothing More]
    \label{rem:scalability:dense-projection-cost}
    On a complete directed Actor projection $\nnz_k=\Theta(n_k^2)$, and every
    cost in \zcref{tbl:scalability:conserved-standing-work} is linear
    in~$\nnz_k$, so the whole solve is quadratic --- the cost of reading a
    quadratic input once per pass, at a published constant number of passes.
    There is no superlinear term in $\nnz_k$ anywhere, because conserved
    allocation \emph{apportions} rather than selects: no path is enumerated,
    no candidate is scored, no co-maximizer class is represented, and the
    transport is applied rather than materialized
    (\zcref{prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost}).

    This is the point on which Edition~5 differs most sharply from what it
    replaced.  The retired design selected among candidate paths, and
    candidate counts grow polynomially in $n_k$ faster than the projection
    itself does, so density was a threat to be bounded before parameter lock.
    Apportionment removes the object those bounds were bounding.  What
    remains is the ordinary cost of a dense input, and it is bounded by the
    input.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Approximation Guarantee}
\label{subsec:scalability:approximation-guarantee}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The approximation machinery in this subsection applies to terminal guild
quantities such as optional global centrality.  It does not approximate
binding standing, the exact depth-two max envelope, staged path
emission fractions, or final W1/W2.  A deployment may terminate a standing
solver at finite precision only with the certified residual enclosure of
\zcref{lem:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure}; that is verified
numerical evaluation of the same standing object, not a different
statistical approximation.  Monte Carlo standing is not a permissible
scaling method.

\begin{definition}[$(\epsilon, \delta)$-Approximation]
    \label{def:scalability:approximation}
    A collection of estimators $\hat{S}_C$ for all creators such that
    $\Pr[|\hat{S}_C - S_C| > \epsilon] < \delta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Efficient Approximation]
    \label{thm:scalability:efficient-approximation}
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates}%
    For any $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$, there exists a
    randomized estimator computable in
    $O(k \cdot (|E| + |V|\log|V|))$ time, with
    $k = O(\epsilon^{-2}\log\delta^{-1})$, achieving
    $(\epsilon,\delta)$-approximation of $S_C$ for all creators.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
            Draw $k$ independent shortest-path trees from $A$ via
            Dijkstra\footcite{dijkstra1959note} with edge costs
    $1/(\detscore{e} \cdot \sqrt{1+\tau_e^2})$. Costs are positive on the
    routing-active subgraph ($\bleedparam$-softening prevents mask-induced
    collapse; routing-inert zero-parameter edges are excluded,
    \zcref{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy}) and bounded
    (\zcref{lem:graph:frobenius-bound,%
    prop:graph:path-view-determinant-bound}).

    For each sample $j$ and target $(n_i, w_i)$, define
    $X_C^{(j,i)} = 1$ if $C$ lies on the shortest path from $A$
    to $n_i$. The estimator is
    $\hat{S}_C = k^{-1}\sum_j \sum_i w_i X_C^{(j,i)}$.
      Each summand is in $[0,1]$. By Hoeffding's
      inequality\footcite{hoeffding1963probability}:
    \[
        \Pr[|\hat{S}_C - S_C| > \epsilon]
        \leq 2\exp(-2k\epsilon^2).
    \]
    Solving for $\delta$:
    $k \geq (2\epsilon^2)^{-1}\ln(2/\delta)$.
\end{proof}

Under the bridge model the advertising $S_C$ is itself exact
(\zcref{rem:scalability:advertising-centrality-exact}), so the
CAN-enriched centrality
$S_C^{\mathrm{CAN}} = S_C \cdot \canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ is exact as well:
the CAN factor is a deterministic constant computed at registration
time (\AttrView{}), and $\epsilon = 0$ for the centrality factor it
multiplies.  Where a guild instead requires global (non-campaign)
betweenness, the $(\epsilon,\delta)$ bound above applies verbatim.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Nash Preservation}
\label{subsec:scalability:nash-preservation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Incentive Slack]
    \label{def:scalability:incentive-slack}
    The exact reward system has slack $\gamma > 0$ at Nash
    equilibrium $\sigma^*$ if, for every actor $C$ and every
    unilateral deviation $\sigma'_C$:
    $R_C(\sigma^*_C) - R_C(\sigma'_C) \geq \gamma$.
      Here $\sigma^*$ and $\sigma'_C$ are local strategy profiles for this
      subsection.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nash Preservation]
    \label{thm:scalability:nash-preservation}
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:completeness}%
    If the exact system has Nash equilibrium $\sigma^*$ with
    slack $\gamma > 0$, and
    $|\hat{R}_C - R_C| \leq \epsilon R_{\max}$ for all creators
    (where $R_{\max}$ is the maximum reward within the guild's
    pool in epoch $k$), then the equilibrium persists whenever
    $2\epsilon R_{\max} < \gamma$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    Under approximation:
            \begin{align*}
        \hat{R}_C(\sigma'_C) - \hat{R}_C(\sigma^*_C)
        &\leq [R_C(\sigma'_C) + \epsilon R_{\max}]
              - [R_C(\sigma^*_C) - \epsilon R_{\max}] \\
        &= \underbrace{R_C(\sigma'_C)
           - R_C(\sigma^*_C)}_{\leq -\gamma}
           + 2\epsilon R_{\max}
        < 0.
            \end{align*}
    No deviation appears profitable.
\end{proof}

The slack $\gamma$ arises from the zero-reward floor
(\zcref{cor:transport:zero-reward}) and standing-input
monotonicity (\zcref{pty:transport:final-standing-input-monotonicity}),
both of which depend on the reward formula's algebraic structure, not
the scoring primitive.

The approximation theorem concerns terminal reward factors.  It does
not approximate binding standing, hop matrices, emission fractions, or
the standing certificate.  Guild approximations may not alter the
published standing input.

The standing field itself is not replaced by an estimator.  A finite
solver publishes an enclosure for the unique exact standing fixed point
(\zcref{lem:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure}).  Any reward
computation using an approximate representative must include the
resulting deterministic standing-input interval in its own error
accounting; the enclosure can be made below any required threshold, so
no standing-approximation error may be folded silently into~$\gamma$.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Sybil and Spam Resistance}
\label{subsec:scalability:sybil-and-spam-resistance}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{corollary}[Sybil Resistance]
    \label{cor:scalability:sybil-resistance}
    In Douceur's resource-constraint
    sense,\footcite{douceur2002sybil} account multiplication and
    passive-structure multiplication do not manufacture standing.

    Registration is an ordinary final-set act: every proposed act debits
    $\safethresh$ and increments the action count, with no newcomer
    exception (\zcref{rem:epoch:registration-final-set-admission}).  Same-epoch
    standing stays inside the current post-debit source hull
    (\zcref{cor:epoch:same-epoch-source-hull}), so a zero-rate cohort
    cannot mutually vouch itself above zero and a below-wall cohort cannot
    mutually vouch itself above the maximum current source rate reaching
    it.  Raw incoming edges, passive-node degree, unmatched Reference/T or
    Invitation/T legs, self-vouches, and artifact-rich lookalike clusters
    cannot create a projected person-vouch path
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation,%
    rem:nodes:anchoring-and-relational-support}).  A fabricated Actor enters standing
    only after acquiring genuine costly source and complete actor-authored
    vouches along the projected relation.

    For one source-target pair, active maximizing paths cannot stack above the
    raw source envelope
    (\zcref{thm:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}), and uncertifiable relational
    flow clips toward zero.  Non-transferability continues to prevent
    source pooling across addresses
    (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}).

    On the terminal surfaces, a fabricated cluster additionally has
    $S_C \approx 0$ (not on genuine shortest paths), $I_C = 0$, and the
    unit amplifier $\ampfactor{C}=1$; under
    $(\epsilon,\delta)$-approximation it extracts at most
    $\epsilon P$ from any guild pool.
    This is the security reading of the comparator's faithfulness
    (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}) and of
    price-not-detector admission
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:price-not-detector}).

    The corollary bounds structural fabrication and path multiplication.
    It does not yet impose a cross-target rivalry budget, nor attenuate a
    source pair solely because its current residual balance is small ---
    a depleted source pair may remain denominator ballast through an old
    vouch, which is the open source-root eligibility question.  Separate
    recipient-facing acts remain separately priced and action-count
    dilutive (\zcref{rem:comparator:conserved-allocation-scope}).
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Spam Resistance]
    \label{cor:scalability:spam-resistance}
    Spam is suppressed on two distinct surfaces.

    \paragraph{Raw attention and terminal reward.}
    Raw weak-parameter, chaotic-timing edges remain penalized by:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{near-rank-1 determinant suppression in the raw
              \PathView{}:} weak parameters produce near-zero bilinear
              entries except $\Psi^{11} \geq 0.5$, yielding
              $\detscore{} \approx 0.025$; the anisotropy penalty
              (\zcref{def:graph:anisotropy-penalty}) compounds this,
              $\condnum{} \gg 100$;
        \item \textbf{raw temporal-entropy damping:} chaotic timing
              ($\tau \approx 0.5$) maximises $\tentropy{}$,
              producing boundary damping of $\numval{const.activation.maxent_damping.num}$;
        \item \textbf{per-creator-epoch entropy damping} in the
              canonical reward formula via
              $\boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}$
              (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}).
    \end{enumerate}
    Spam damped weight: $\numrel{result.spam.weight.num}$
    (\zcref{subsec:verification:spam-resistance}); weakest legitimate
    \tiermarginal{} edge: $\numrel{result.e5.weight.num}$; per-edge gap $\numval{result.spam.gap.num}\times$,
    with a $k$-hop spam chain at $\sim \numval{result.spam.weight.num}^k$ dominated by any single
    \tierfull{} edge for all $k \geq 1$.
    These mechanisms affect feed and raw bridge traversal, not standing.
    Raw traversal is exact and bounded-depth: Layer~1 publishes no raw
    pruning tolerance or precision clip
    (\zcref{rem:sorting:raw-pruning-is-implementation}), and an
    implementation may prune only when the optimization preserves the exact
    declared output.

    \paragraph{Standing.}
    Standing spam is constrained by:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item the closed person-vouch census;
        \item complete-act and author continuity;
        \item passive non-interference and unmatched-leg exclusion;
        \item the exact depth-two max envelope and depth-three/four
              source-target simplices, preventing path stacking;
        \item the safety-wall clamp, limiting dynamic gain below the wall
              (\zcref{prop:dynamics:safety-wall-clamp});
        \item the conserved standing certificate, limiting row feedback
              (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate});
        \item final W2a and W2b on every proposed-set author, and the
              finite epoch record budget;
        \item the per-action $\safethresh$ debit and irrevocable
              action-count dilution
              (\zcref{post:epoch:act-debit}): since
              $\commitrate{i} = \burnbal{i}/\actcount{i}$, spam is
              doubly self-defeating --- the numerator falls as the
              denominator rises, and a stamp below $\safefloor$ places the
              author below the safety wall, its residual balance/count
              dilution not reversed merely by stopping.
    \end{enumerate}

    The wall clamp is a dynamics control, not a source filter: it prevents
    below-wall standing from producing unbounded local gain; it does not
    erase an Actor's authored source pair or solve cross-target rivalry.

    Thus raw content spam and standing manipulation are not defended by
    one overloaded score.  Each consumer has a formula matched to what
    it transports: raw attention reads raw edge geometry; standing reads
    costly complete actor-authored delegation.
\end{corollary}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Verifiability}
\label{subsec:scalability:verifiability}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{proposition}[Raw-Path Verifiability]
    \label{prop:scalability:raw-path-verifiability}
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:public-availability}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:immutability}%
    Given the public graph state
    (\zcref{post:introduction:public-accessibility,%
    post:introduction:record-integrity,%
    post:introduction:authoritative-act-order,%
    post:introduction:epoch-edge-set}) and a retrieved record for each
    traversed edge, a raw feed or bridge path of length~$d$ is verified in
    $O(d)$ arithmetic: reconstruct each raw tensor/path view, determinant,
    maturity, temporal factor, damped weight, and authoritative order.  This
    result is terminal and unchanged in substance.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    The record satisfies \zcref{post:introduction:record-integrity}; the
    required ordering is causal, and no check below consumes $\logpos{e}$.
    Given a retrieved edge record, the verifier independently:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item reconstructs $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ from parameters via the master
              formula (\zcref{def:graph:sentiment-slice}): $O(1)$;
        \item extracts $\pathview{e}$ with $\bleedparam$-softening: $O(1)$;
        \item computes the $2 \times 2$ determinant and its sign
              $\detsign{e}$: $O(1)$;
        \item computes the per-edge damped weight
              $\dampedweight{e}=\detscore{e}\cdot\sqrt{1+\tau_e^2}\cdot\boltzfactor{\tentropy{e}}$:
              $O(1)$;
        \item checks causal ordering and confirms the path weight as the
              product of per-edge damped weights: $O(1)$ per edge;
        \item for a raw signed claim, checks path parity
              $\detsign{p}=\prod_{e\in p}\detsign{e}$: $O(1)$ per edge;
        \item for a reward claim, confirms $\boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}$
              from the published epoch-snapshot edge records: $O(|E_C|)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    No access to the full graph is required.
\end{proof}

The \PathView{} and \AttrView{} components are verifiable
independently: raw path claims against the committed edge set (via
determinant recomputation and sign detection) and CAN claims against
the registered subtree in $\symbf{\Lambda}$ (via Frobenius norm
recomputation and scalar recursion).

The raw signed double-cover service may still be verified independently,
but it supplies no standing input.  Standing verification is the
reproducible-package procedure of
\zcref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}: the commitment
rate $\commitrate{i}$ and standing $\standing{i}$ are published at epoch
boundaries, and any participant recomputes them from the public burn
ledger and the committed epoch edge set using the published binding
constants and formula editions.  Roots and hashes form an optional commitment
layer --- locators and integrity aids that detect a silent change but never
substitute for replay --- and are not themselves normative; the sole exception is
a projection commitment (\zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection}), the retained
binding representation of tombstonable data.

\section{Gate Geometry and the Sustaining Strategy}
\label{app:gates}

\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-write-rule} imposes three admission conditions:
W1 is own residual-balance solvency, W2a is the individual safety wall,
and W2b is the action-weighted epoch door.  The conserved standing package
adds a separate relational-safety condition:
\[
    \marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}\le1.
\]
That certificate governs whether the epoch's standing solution may take
effect at the accepted tilt rung; it neither pays W1 nor changes the
per-action debit.

This appendix records the Actor-facing geometry of the two admission
floors and the exact burn-value needed to sustain action at either one.
It also states where relational regard can help: others' allocation may
carry an Actor's standing stamp across W2a or the epoch door, but
only the Actor's own residual balance can satisfy W1
--- and only the Actor's own balance carries its history outward
(\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}).

Everything here is denominated in \textbf{burn value} $\burnval{i}$,
the imported frame
(\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame}), or in its residual ledger
reading $\burnbal{i}$
(\zcref{def:comparator:residual-balance}).  The only Layer~0
property used is the one the seam already demands: that $\burnval{i}$ is a
non-decreasing, irrevocable, per-actor scalar.  The appendix assumes no
Layer~0 price, redemption, or reserve-supply mechanism beyond the
interface properties already required at the seam: whether
burn value is costly to acquire, and how, is below the interface --- it is the
\emph{source cost}, which \zcref{sec:comparator} locates entirely in Layer~0
(\zcref{def:comparator:source-faithful}, S-actor).

\begin{remark}[Split Scope]
    \label{rem:gates:split-scope}
    For an unendorsed Actor maintaining reduced own-source rate~$c$, one
    further accepted action requires:
    \[
        c\numeraire+\safethresh
    \]
    of new burn value: $c\numeraire$ preserves the carried rate as the
    denominator rises, while $\safethresh$ pays the consummated action
    debit.

    Therefore:
    \begin{align*}
        \text{door-neutral sustaining rate}
            &=
            \partfloor\numeraire+\safethresh,\\
        \text{wall-neutral sustaining rate}
            &=
            \safefloor\numeraire+\safethresh
            =
            2\safethresh.
    \end{align*}

    At the chartered reference these are approximately $0.1528$ and
    $0.1056$ burn-value units per action.  Relational standing may
    reduce the burn needed to clear W2, but it never reduces the literal
    W1 debit~$\safethresh$.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Door and the Wall}
\label{subsec:gates:door-and-wall}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{theorem}[Own-Source Sustaining Rates]
    \label{thm:gates:sustaining}
    Suppose Actor~$i$ is unendorsed and begins an action with reduced
    own-source rate~$c$:
    \[
        \frac{\burnbal{i}}{\numeraire\actcount{i}}
        =
        c,
        \qquad
        \actcount{i}\ge1.
    \]
    Holding that rate constant across one accepted action requires
    exactly:
    \[
        c\numeraire+\safethresh
    \]
    of new burn value.

    Consequently:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item holding the individual stamp at the effective door
              $\partfloor$ requires
              $\partfloor\numeraire+\safethresh$
              per action;

        \item holding the individual stamp at the safety wall
              $\safefloor$ requires
              $\safefloor\numeraire+\safethresh=2\safethresh$
              per action.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    Let the current pair be
    $\burnbal{i}=c\numeraire\actcount{i}$.
    If new burn~$\Delta$ is supplied and one action executes, the new
    pair is:
    \[
        \left(
            \burnbal{i}+\Delta-\safethresh,\,
            \actcount{i}+1
        \right).
    \]
    Requiring the new reduced rate to remain~$c$ gives:
    \[
        \burnbal{i}+\Delta-\safethresh
        =
        c\numeraire
        \bigl(\actcount{i}+1\bigr),
    \]
    hence
    $\Delta=c\numeraire+\safethresh$.
    Substitute $c=\partfloor$ and
    $c=\safefloor=\safethresh/\numeraire$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Band-Floor Sustaining Cost]
    \label{cor:gates:band-floor}
    For an unendorsed Actor, the minimum burn value per action that
    holds the individual standing stamp exactly at the safety wall is:
    \[
        2\safethresh.
    \]
    At the chartered reference this is approximately $0.1056$.

    This is an own-source sustaining cost.  An Actor whose certified
    relational standing safely carries W2a may require less new burn to
    preserve the stamp, but still pays the full own-balance W1 debit
    $\safethresh$ for every accepted action.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[The Relationally Supported Actor]
    \label{rem:gates:propped}
    Final safe standing flow may raise an Actor's certified standing
    stamp above the Actor's own source rate.  Such relational support may:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item clear W2a when own source alone would lie below the safety
              wall;
        \item contribute to W2b's action-weighted epoch average;
        \item reduce the new burn needed to preserve the Actor's
              standing stamp.
    \end{itemize}

    It may not:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item pay the Actor's W1 debit;
        \item transfer another Actor's residual balance;
        \item reinstate target-side activation feedback while the Actor is below
              the safety wall (\zcref{prop:dynamics:safety-wall-clamp}) --- the
              clamp fixes the activation factor and zeroes self-feedback, though
              certified external source may still lift the Actor's standing;
        \item authorize an allocation not present in the certified
              conserved standing package.
    \end{itemize}

    Thus relational support can carry standing, not solvency: a
    relationally supported Actor can be band-writable through door
    headroom, but is never subsidy-solvent --- a record still debits the
    Actor's own $\burnbal{}$.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Sustaining Frontier and the Lazy-Burn Optimum}
\label{subsec:gates:frontier}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The Actor-facing question has two versions.

For an unendorsed Actor: what burn schedule minimizes burn value while
holding the Actor at the door or wall?

For a relationally supported Actor: how much own burn remains necessary
after the certified standing package supplies some of the stamp?

The first has an exact closed form.  The second is package-dependent,
because contributing rates, action masses, fold coefficients, the accepted rung,
and the declared standing box all affect the mediant.  No universal
relational ``discount rate'' exists.

\begin{theorem}[Unendorsed Sustaining Frontier]
    \label{thm:gates:frontier}
    For an unendorsed Actor:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item every schedule sustaining the effective door commits at
              least
              $\partfloor\numeraire+\safethresh$
              of burn value per accepted action in the long-run
              average;

        \item every schedule sustaining the safety wall commits at least
              $2\safethresh$
              per accepted action in the long-run average.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    \zcref{thm:gates:sustaining} gives the exact amount needed to keep
    the own-source rate unchanged across each action.  Front-loading may
    shift when burn occurs but cannot reduce the telescoping long-run
    average needed to replace the carried-rate increment and the
    consummated debit.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Two-Phase Transit]
    \label{prop:gates:two-phase-transit}
    For an unendorsed Actor taking actions without new burn, beginning at
    own reduced rate $(\hat r_0,N_0)$, the exact action counts to the policy
    membrane and safety wall are
    $m_1=N_0(\hat r_0-\partfloor)/(\partfloor+\safefloor)$ and
    $m_2=N_0(\hat r_0-\safefloor)/(2\safefloor)$ --- linear, exact, no
    continuum limit. Reference: $654.4$ / $1393.7$; band dwell $739.3$ actions,
    headroom-permitting. Re-entry from below either boundary is a burn lump ---
    a price, not a duration.

    Relational standing changes this transit because the Actor's stamp is no
    longer the own-source rate.  The formulas above remain exact for the
    unendorsed baseline and are not used to predict a certified relational
    row without replaying its standing package.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Front-Loading Changes Timing, Not the Own-Source Average]
    \label{rem:gates:frontload}
    Front-loading burn can delay the point at which an unendorsed
    Actor reaches the policy membrane or safety wall.  It does not
    reduce the long-run own-source sustaining average of
    \zcref{thm:gates:frontier}.

    A source-cost market may make earlier acquisition economically
    preferable, but acquisition timing and price belong below the
    Layer~1 interface.  Relational standing is another distinct input:
    it may change the certified stamp trajectory but does not change the
    W1 debit.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Relational Support and Own Solvency}
\label{subsec:gates:lever}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Initiator-owned safe standing flow is the only Layer~1 relational input
that can raise an Actor's stamp above the Actor's own source rate.
It is not a balance transfer and never discounts the Actor's own W1
price.

\begin{corollary}[Standing Flow Does Not Discount Solvency]
    \label{cor:gates:standing-transport-no-solvency-discount}
    Final safe standing flow may carry W2a and W2b by changing the
    certified standing mediant.  It cannot discount W1:
    \[
        \burnbal{i}\ge\safethresh
    \]
    remains an own-balance condition, and every accepted act debits
    exactly~$\safethresh$ from Actor~$i$.

    Therefore no source-relative path, complete person-vouch,
    lowered tilt rung, guild subsidy to another Actor, or high-standing
    neighbor lowers the per-action debit paid by the acting Actor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[A Lowered Tilt Rung Is Not a Price Discount]
    \label{rem:gates:tilt-is-not-price-discount}
    A lowered tilt rung $\tiltstrength{k}$ changes how sharply standing
    tilts the division of a source's conserved unit.  It does not:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item reduce $\safethresh$;
        \item credit residual balance;
        \item refund an action debit;
        \item change $\numeraire$;
        \item alter the Layer~0 source cost;
        \item change the policy floor.
    \end{itemize}

    Lowering the tilt rung may lower or remove relational stamp
    support.  The
    acting Actor must then supply whatever own source is needed to clear
    W1 and W2 under the recomputed certified package.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Equal-Rate Communities Do Not Self-Lift]
    \label{thm:gates:equal-rate-no-internal-lift}
    Suppose every source pair admitted into Actor~$i$'s standing row,
    including the own pair, has the same reduced rate~$c$:
    \[
        \frac{\burnbal{u}}
             {\numeraire\actcount{u}}
        =
        c
    \]
    for every contributing source~$u$, and:
    \[
        \frac{\burnbal{i}}
             {\numeraire\max(\actcount{i},1)}
        =
        c.
    \]
    Then:
    \[
        \frac{\standing{i}}{\numeraire}
        =
        c
    \]
    for every nonnegative certified source-target flow schedule.

    Thus mutual vouching, path multiplicity, action-mass variation,
    fold coefficients, and the tilt cannot lift a community
    whose admitted source rates are all equal.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    The standing formula is a weighted mediant of numerator/denominator
    pairs having the common ratio~$c\numeraire$.  A mediant of equal
    ratios has that ratio exactly.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Relational Support Is Package-Dependent]
    \label{rem:gates:external}
    By \zcref{thm:gates:equal-rate-no-internal-lift}, internal
    equal-rate delegation cannot raise a common standing rate.  By the
    rate-hull property
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}), no target exceeds the
    highest contributing source rate.

    Relational support from higher-rate Actors may lift a target, but
    its magnitude is package-dependent: source rates, source action
    masses, fold coefficients, transported shares, and the accepted rung
    all enter the mediant or its certified flow.

    An Actor may cultivate such support but cannot manufacture it
    through passive artifacts, unmatched legs, or path stacking (cf.\
    \zcref{rem:epoch:griefing-resistance,prop:epoch:dilution-cost}).
    Because later package recompilation may change the base matrix and the rung,
    relational support is not a fixed budgetable discount against W1.
    The $\safethresh$ debit itself remains own-anchored.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Funding Is a Layer-2 Freedom, Not a Layer-1 Assumption}
\label{subsec:gates:funding}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{remark}[A Guild May Bear an Actor's Source Cost]
    \label{rem:gates:guild-funding}
    Nothing above assumes \emph{who} commits an Actor's burn value. A Layer~0
    burn is funder-unconstrained and requires no recipient consent
    (\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame}): the resulting $\burnval{i}$ accrues
    to the Actor's address whoever paid for it. A guild may therefore choose, by
    its own Layer-2 measure, to supply an Actor's sustaining burn --- holding the
    Actor at the floor of \zcref{thm:gates:frontier}, or deliberately above it
    for richer discovery --- exactly as \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}
    permits, and Layer~1 neither prescribes nor prices that choice.

    Crucially, this relocates \emph{who bears the source cost} without faking it.
    The frame is non-transferable across addresses
    (\zcref{def:comparator:frame-binding}), and by \zcref{thm:gates:equal-rate-no-internal-lift}
    funding an Actor's own burns raises only that Actor's own rate; it confers
    no standing the Actor's endorsers have not independently earned. The
    comparator sees a funded Actor exactly as it sees a self-funded one --- the
    burn is real either way --- so guild subsidy is faithfulness-preserving by
    construction (\zcref{cor:comparator:sybil-resistance-is-faithfulness}).

    A guild funding Actor~$i$'s Layer~0 source raises the source pair bound
    to Actor~$i$; it does not purchase or redirect another Actor's standing
    allocation, and it does not control the rung certified by the Layer~1
    certificate.

    Thus guild funding and relational support are distinct:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item source funding changes Actor~$i$'s own residual source;
        \item person-vouches and safe paths change relational source mass;
        \item neither bypasses W1;
        \item both remain publicly attributable through their own records.
    \end{itemize}
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Scope of Standing Safety]
    \label{rem:gates:standing-safety-scope}
    The gate and standing certificates prove different properties.

    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{W1 solvency}
              proves the acting Actor can pay the next
              $\safethresh$ debit.

        \item \textbf{W2a/W2b}
              prove that the certified individual and epoch stamps clear
              the safety wall and policy membrane.

        \item \textbf{Conserved-map contraction}
              proves the standing map is contractive on the rate hull box at
              the accepted tilt rung:
              \[
                  \marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}\le1.
              \]
              The box needs no separate invariance certificate: the hull is
              invariant by construction, because every coordinate of the map is
              a weighted average of contributing rates
              (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).

        \item \textbf{Transition magnitude}
              is a separate quantity:
              contraction does not imply that the
              one-boundary standing movement
              $\left|\standing{i}^{(k)}-\standing{i}^{(k-1)}\right|$
              is small.

        \item \textbf{Rivalry and target consent}
              are separate protocol properties.  The standing package
              prevents source-target path stacking but does not conserve
              delegated view across different targets and provides no
              target veto
              (\zcref{rem:comparator:conserved-allocation-scope}).
    \end{enumerate}

    The host contract publishes standing movement, admitted incoming
    action mass, backoff rung, and certificate margin as distinct
    monitoring quantities.  None may be inferred from another merely
    because all are called ``safe.''
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Sustaining Denomination and Dial Separation]
    \label{rem:gates:sustaining-denomination}
    The exact own-source sustaining denomination is:
    \[
        c\numeraire+\safethresh
    \]
    for reduced own rate~$c$.  At the effective door:
    $\partfloor\numeraire+\safethresh$;
    at the safety wall:
    $2\safethresh$.

    The num\'eraire term and debit term have different roles:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item $\numeraire$ converts a reduced rate into carried
              burn-value per additional action count;
        \item $\safethresh$ is the literal consummated action price;
        \item $\polfloor$ changes the policy membrane
              (guarded by \zcref{rem:epoch:operator-authority-floor});
        \item $\safefloor=\safethresh/\numeraire$ changes the safety
              wall;
        \item a lowered rung changes how sharply standing tilts the division, and nothing else.
    \end{itemize}

    Consequently a num\'eraire migration, a policy-floor move, a
    safety-threshold move, and a standing-flow reallocation are four
    distinct events.  None should be described as a generic
    ``cheaper action'' without naming which term moved.
\end{remark}
