\section{Compositional Attribution Calculus}
\label{app:can}

The CAN governs how credit flows through compositional dependencies.
It is a terminal Layer~2 computation over the \CompGraph{}
(\zcref{subsec:introduction:the-graph}) and the
raw \AttrView{} of public records
(\zcref{def:graph:dual-view-architecture}): the Frobenius norm of the
full $3 \times 3$ sentiment slice, without temporal maturity and without
entropy damping.  It does not consume the
relation multigraph, source envelopes, causal standing
hop matrices, emission fractions, transport matrix, or
certificate.

A leaf's canonical default value is the Frobenius norm of its raw
$3\times3$ sentiment slice.  A composition's value is its transmission
coefficient times its redundancy correction times the weighted mean of
its children.

The same accepted records may have different declared readings:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item a complete Reference or Invitation is one semantic hop in
          standing;
    \item its A-leg and T-leg remain two raw CAN leaves and one depth-1
          CAN composition;
    \item feed may traverse the raw legs;
    \item payload policy may render the controlled bytes.
\end{itemize}
No consumer may substitute one reading for another.

The CAN is terminal and guild-reimplementable under
\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}: guilds publish their own CAN
recursion and all guild-specific parameters, and the canonical
recursion below is the reference default.  Three structural
invariants are mandatory for all guild CAN specifications and are
the preconditions for guild attribution claims to be independently
verifiable (\zcref{subsec:transport:guild-model,%
subsec:deployment:completeness}).

\begin{definition}[Mandatory Guild CAN Invariants]
    \label{def:can:mandatory-guild-invariants}
    Every guild CAN specification must satisfy all three:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Depth decay} (\zcref{thm:can:depth-decay}):
              credit cannot flow upward through composition.
        \item \textbf{Transmission strictly less than one}
              (\zcref{prop:can:transmission-bound}): every composition
              step attenuates.
        \item \textbf{Context independence}
              (\zcref{thm:can:context-independence}): adding a consumer
              to an existing node does not change its value.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

All other CAN parameters --- aggregation function, attribution
threshold, denomination of the enrichment factor --- are guild
choices within these constraints.

\begin{remark}[Standing Projection and CAN Are Separate Consumers]
    \label{rem:can:standing-allocation-separation}
    Complete-act standing atomicity does not collapse CAN structure.

    For a complete hyper-edge act
    $q=(e_A,e_T)$:
    \begin{description}[nosep]
        \item[\textnormal{standing}]
            may compile one Actor-to-Actor projected vouch edge from
            the complete semantic act;
        \item[\textnormal{CAN}]
            retains raw leaves $e_A,e_T$ and a depth-1 composition node
            under \zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}.
    \end{description}

    The relation coefficient
    $\foldcoef{\xi}$, the base matrix, the accepted rung,
    the conserved transport entries,
    causal standing path identities, and projected
    target activation enter no CAN formula.

    CAN may read the published standing scalar only through a raw
    Declaration leaf when that leaf is actually present in the guild's
    composition dependency closure
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}).  That limited
    path is explicit and does not import the internal standing package.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Final Standing Scope]
    \label{rem:can:final-standing-scope}
    A CAN value may depend on final standing only through a raw
    Declaration leaf included in its declared dependency closure.  Holding
    final standing and all raw record tensors fixed, changing an internal
    standing stage representation, solver initialization, standing
    certificate transcript, or cache changes no CAN value.  If no
    Declaration leaf of Actor~$i$ lies in the relevant dependency closure,
    then $\partial\canval{n}/\partial\epochstanding{k}{i}=0$.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Structure}
\label{subsec:can:structure}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Compositional Attribution Network]
    \label{def:can:compositional-attribution-network}
    A tuple $(N, E, \symbf{\Psi}, \symbf{\Lambda})$ where: $N$ is a
    finite set of contribution nodes; $E \subseteq N \times N$ is a
    set of directed composition edges (acyclic); $\symbf{\Psi}$
    assigns a $3 \times 3$ sentiment slice to every node and edge;
    $\symbf{\Lambda}: \strset \to N$ is a global append-only
    registry.

    This tuple is a terminal guild object derived from public records.  It
    contains no projected standing edge unless a guild explicitly represents
    the corresponding raw record as a contribution under the dependency
    rules below; even then it reads the raw record/leg, not the binding
    standing projection.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Compositional Depth]
    \label{def:can:compositional-depth}
    \begin{equation}
        \candepth{n} =
        \begin{cases}
            0, & n \text{ is a leaf,} \\
            1 + \max\set{\candepth{c} \mid (n,c) \in E},
                & \text{otherwise.}
        \end{cases}
        \label{eq:can:compositional-depth}
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Dependency Induction]
    \label{def:can:dependency-induction}
    The canonical mapping from raw \ActionGraph{} records to
    \CompGraph{} structure proceeds by four terminal Layer~2 rules
    applied in order.
    It operates on raw records and raw hyper-edge legs after the standing
    package has already been computed.  The mapping never consumes
    the base matrix, hop matrices, emission fractions, or
    the conserved transport entries.

    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{$V_u$-sourced edges.} Every canonical-default
              contribution record sourced from~$V_u$ maps
              to a CAN leaf with
              $\baseval{e} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F$, except the
              control families excluded by Rule~4. Rule~1 keys on
              source class, not authorship: the derived Declaration
              component may enter as one raw CAN leaf when a guild's
              dependency structure references it.  Its raw parameter is
              a published function of standing, so the insulation
              condition of
              \zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}
              remains necessary.  It does not expose source-relative
              hop matrices, or emission fractions.

        \item \textbf{Hyper-edge legs.} Every hyper-edge
              $\mathcal{H}$ with legs $e_1, e_2$ induces a depth-1 CAN
              composition node whose children are leaves $e_1$ and
              $e_2$, with $\redundancy{} = 1$, regardless of whether
              each leg is sourced from $V_u$ or $V_c$. Current
              families: Tag/A·T, Review/A·T, Send/A·T,
              Bid/A·T, Invitation/A·T, Reference/A·T,
              Participant/A·T.  A Participant act whose legs coincide
              contributes a composition whose T-leaf is a self-loop; the
              guild recursion reads it like any other leaf, and raw
              traversal prunes it (\zcref{lem:nodes:self-loop-neutral}).
              This raw two-leaf CAN reading coexists with the one-hop
              complete-act standing reading
              (\zcref{rem:can:standing-allocation-separation}); neither
              consumer changes the other's representation.

        \item \textbf{Exclusion of standalone $V_c$-sourced edges.}
              Any raw \ActionGraph{} edge sourced from $V_c$ and not
              designated as a hyper-edge leg in Rule~2 is excluded
              from the \CompGraph{}. The Reputation component
              ($\mathrm{Profile}_j \to \mathrm{Actor}_j$) is the
              unique current instance. Verification cost: $O(1)$ ---
              check the source node class and the \textbf{CG} column
              of \zcref{tbl:nodes:archetype-fingerprints}.

          \item \textbf{Exclusion of control edges.} Control edges ---
              settlement (Withdraw, Rescind) and conversational (Leave,
              De-invite/A·T) --- are excluded from the \CompGraph{}
              regardless of source class \emph{and regardless of
              hyper-edge membership}: Rule~4 takes precedence over
              Rule~2 for the De-invite legs.  They are structural
              state-declaration signals, not contributions; assigning
              them a CAN base value would credit cancellation or
              expulsion.  Verification cost: $O(1)$ --- check the edge
              type against the control-edge set (Withdraw, Rescind, Leave,
              De-invite).
    \end{enumerate}

    Higher-depth CAN compositions arise only from explicit
    registration in $\symbf{\Lambda}$. The parity sign
    $\detsign{\mathcal{H}} = \detsign{e_1}\cdot\detsign{e_2}$
    (\zcref{thm:graph:hyper-edge-reduction}) passes through the
    hyper-edge structure but does not alter \AttrView{} Frobenius base
    values.
\end{definition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Base Values and Transmission}
\label{subsec:can:base-values-and-transmission}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Base Value]
    \label{def:can:base-value}
    For a leaf $\ell$:
    \begin{equation}
        \baseval{\ell} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_\ell}_F.
        \label{eq:can:base-value}
    \end{equation}
    No temporal factor. No entropy damping. Temporal dynamics enter
    path scoring (\PathView{}) only.  This is the canonical terminal
    guild default, independently computable
    from the public raw record via the published parameters and the
    master formula (\zcref{def:graph:sentiment-slice}).  A
    host-published cached value is a non-authoritative by-product.  A
    guild may publish another CAN base-value
    rule under \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}, provided its complete
    CAN still satisfies the mandatory invariants and remains fully
    reproducible.

    No projected standing quantity enters this formula.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Transmission Coefficient]
    \label{def:can:transmission-coefficient}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:strict-transmission-decay}%
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}%
    For an internal node $n$ with children $c_1, \ldots, c_m$:
    \begin{equation}
        \meanedgenorm{n}
        = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{j=1}^{m}
          \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{(n,c_j)}}_F,
        \qquad
        \trans{n} = \sat{\meanedgenorm{n}},
        \qquad
        \sat{x} = \frac{x}{1+x}.
        \label{eq:can:transmission-coefficient}
    \end{equation}
    This is the canonical terminal guild default (arithmetic
    mean). Guilds may substitute another published aggregation function
    --- geometric mean, harmonic mean, or
    maximum (\zcref{frontier:can-aggregation-function}) --- provided
    $\trans{n}<1$, depth decay, and context independence remain valid.

    The mean uses raw \AttrView{} edge norms.  Source-relative standing
    views, path admission, relation coefficients, and standing-flow
    certificates enter neither $\meanedgenorm{n}$ nor $\trans{n}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Transmission Bound]
    \label{prop:can:transmission-bound}
    $\trans{n} < 1$ for all internal nodes.
    \proofsketch{$\sat{x} < 1$ for all finite $x > 0$.
    $\meanedgenorm{} \leq 3$ by \zcref{lem:graph:frobenius-bound}.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Implicit Diversity Bonus]
    \label{rem:can:implicit-diversity-bonus}
    The scalar CAN computes $\sat{\meanedgenorm{}}$ where
    $\meanedgenorm{}$ is the arithmetic mean of individual norms.
    A matrix CAN (\zcref{subsec:can:matrix-extension}) would use
    $\sat{\svdone{\overline{\mathbf{W}}}}$ where
    $\overline{\mathbf{W}}$ is the matrix mean. By the triangle
    inequality, the scalar CAN overestimates transmission by
    $\sim\!1.8\%$ at depth~1, functioning as a mild implicit
    diversity bonus (\zcref{frontier:svd-corrected-transmission}).
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Weights and Redundancy}
\label{subsec:can:weights-and-redundancy}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Dependency Weights]
    \label{def:can:dependency-weights}
    \begin{equation}
        \depweight{n}{c_i}
        = \frac{\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{(n,c_i)}}_F}
               {\sum_{j=1}^{m}
               \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{(n,c_j)}}_F}.
        \label{eq:can:dependency-weights}
    \end{equation}
    Proportional to $3 \times 3$ Frobenius norms (\AttrView{}).
    $\sum_i \depweight{n}{c_i} = 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Frobenius as Safe Schatten Norm]
    \label{rem:can:frobenius-as-safe-schatten-norm}
    Among Schatten $p$-norms, the Frobenius norm ($p = 2$) is
    preferred for attribution magnitude for one a priori and two
    empirical reasons:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
        \item \emph{Inner-product structure.} Only $p = 2$ is induced
              by an inner product, making $\norm{\cdot}_F$ the natural
              choice for the tensor-aggregation arithmetic in
              \zcref{def:graph:aggregated-sentiment} and the
              depth-additive structure of CAN values.
        \item \emph{Mask robustness.} Restricted-domain masks
              redistribute spectral mass into $\svdtwo{}, \svdthree{}$.
              The Opinion edge $e_2$ has
              $(\svdone{},\svdtwo{},\svdthree{}) = (\numval{result.e2.psi_svd1.num},\, \numval{result.e2.psi_svd2.num},\, \numval{result.e2.psi_svd3.num})$ (nearly rank-1)
              while Tag $e_5$ has
              $(\svdone{},\svdtwo{},\svdthree{}) = (\numval{result.e5.psi_svd1.num},\, \numval{result.e5.psi_svd2.num},\, \numval{result.e5.psi_svd3.num})$ --- a $\numval{result.tier.svd2_inflation.num}\times$
              inflation of $\svdtwo{}$. Frobenius squares the singulars
              before summing, damping $\svdtwo{}, \svdthree{}$
              quadratically relative to the nuclear norm ($p = 1$).
        \item \emph{Opinion-vs-Tag crossover.} On the reference graph
              (\zcref{subsec:verification:reference-graph}), the
              Opinion-vs-Tag pair has F-norms $\numval{result.e2.frobenius.num} > \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num}$ at
              $p = 2$ but inverts at $p^* \approx 1.65$. Frobenius
              sits $\sim\!0.35$ above this crossover, keeping
              Opinion-family Tribal edges above their Epistemic
              counterparts in attribution magnitude as intended.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Redundancy Ratio]
    \label{def:can:redundancy-ratio}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:redundancy-correction}%
    For children $c_1, \ldots, c_m$ with reachable leaf sets
    $L(c_i)$:
    \begin{equation}
        \redundancy{n}
        = \frac{|\bigcup_i L(c_i)|}
               {\sum_i |L(c_i)|}.
        \label{eq:can:redundancy-ratio}
    \end{equation}
    Disjoint children: $\redundancy{} = 1$.
    Overlapping: $\redundancy{} < 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[CAN Overlap Discount]
    \label{def:can:overlap-discount}
    For children $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ with reachable leaf sets $L(c_i)$, the
    canonical CAN overlap discount is
    \[
        \redundancy{n}
        \coloneqq
        \frac{
            \abs{
                \bigcup_iL(c_i)
            }
        }{
            \displaystyle\sum_i
            \abs{L(c_i)}
        }.
    \]
    It lies in $(0,1]$, equals one for disjoint child closures, and
    decreases as upstream dependency overlap increases.

    The factor expresses the canonical guild preference for non-overlapping
    upstream work.  It is not required to prevent literal numeric
    duplication under normalized dependency weights.  A guild may replace
    it under the terminal CAN grant, provided the mandatory depth-decay,
    strict-transmission, and context-independence invariants continue to
    hold.
\end{definition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Intrinsic Value}
\label{subsec:can:intrinsic-value}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Intrinsic Value]
    \label{def:can:intrinsic-value}
    \deploymentref{subsec:deployment:completeness}%
    \begin{equation}
        \canval{n} =
        \begin{cases}
            \baseval{n} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_n}_F,
            & \candepth{n} = 0, \\[6pt]
            \trans{n} \cdot \redundancy{n}
            \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{m}
            \depweight{n}{c_i} \canval{c_i},
            & \candepth{n} \geq 1.
        \end{cases}
        \label{eq:can:intrinsic-value}
    \end{equation}
    Equivalently, unrolling:
    \begin{equation}
        \canval{n}
        = \sum_{p: n \to \ell}
                    \biggl(
            \prod_{k \in p_{\mathrm{int}}}
            \trans{k}\,\redundancy{k}
                    \biggr)
                    \biggl(
            \prod_{(a,b) \in p}
            \depweight{a}{b}
                    \biggr)
          \baseval{\ell}.
        \label{eq:can:intrinsic-value-unrolled}
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Void Node]
    \label{def:can:void-node}
    The void $\bot$ is a distinguished leaf with base value:
    \begin{equation}
        \baseval{\bot}
        = \epsilon_\bot
        = e^{-\invtemp \ln 2}
        \numrel{const.can.void_base.num}.
        \label{eq:can:void-base-value}
    \end{equation}
    Maximum diversity, minimum information. The void base value uses
    the Layer~1 published constant $\invtemp = 2\ln 2$
    (\zcref{ax:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary}); it is $\invtemp$-dependent
    and should be republished if $\invtemp$ is updated
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas}).
\end{definition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Core Properties}
\label{subsec:can:core-properties}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{theorem}[Well-Definedness]
    \label{thm:can:well-defined}
    $\canval{n}$ is uniquely defined for all $n \in N$.
    \proofsketch{DAG prevents cycles. Depth decreases at each
    recursive step. All quantities are deterministic functions of
    $(N, E, \symbf{\Psi}, \symbf{\Lambda})$. No temporal dynamics
    enter (\AttrView{} only). No internal standing-package object
    enters.  Published standing enters
    only through a raw Declaration leaf when that leaf belongs to the
    CAN dependency closure
    (\zcref{prop:can:standing-package-independence}).}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Depth-Layered DAG]
    \label{thm:can:depth-layered-dag}
    Every edge points from a higher depth layer to a strictly lower
    one.
    \proofsketch{$\candepth{a} \geq 1 + \candepth{b}$ for all
    $(a,b) \in E$.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Depth Decay]
    \label{thm:can:depth-decay}
    For any internal node: $\canval{n} < \max_i \canval{c_i}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    $\canval{n}
    = \trans{n}\,\redundancy{n}
      \sum_i \depweight{n}{c_i}\canval{c_i}
    \leq \trans{n}\,\redundancy{n}
      \max_i\canval{c_i}
      \cdot \underbrace{\sum_i \depweight{n}{c_i}}_{=1}$.
    Since $\trans{n} < 1$ (\zcref{prop:can:transmission-bound})
    and $\redundancy{n} \leq 1$:
    $\canval{n} < \max_i \canval{c_i}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exponential Path Decay]
    \label{cor:can:exponential-path-decay}
    A leaf's contribution along a path of length $d$ is bounded
    by $(\bar{t}\,\bar{\mu})^d \baseval{\ell}$ where $\bar{t}$
    and $\bar{\mu}$ are the mean transmission coefficient and
    mean redundancy ratio along the path.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Credit Conservation]
    \label{thm:can:credit-conservation}
    Composition cannot inflate credit beyond the most valuable
    child.
    \proofsketch{Identical to \zcref{thm:can:depth-decay}; strict
    inequality at every internal node.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Context Independence]
    \label{thm:can:context-independence}
    Adding a consumer to an existing node does not change
    $\canval{n}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    $\canval{n}$ depends only on the outgoing composition subgraph rooted
    at~$n$.  A new incoming consumer changes no raw leaf, outgoing
    dependency, transmission coefficient, redundancy set, or child value.

    The source-relative standing projection is a separate consumer and
    cannot alter the CAN dependency graph.  A raw Declaration leaf, if
    already present in the outgoing closure, continues to read the
    published standing scalar exactly as before; adding another consumer
    of~$n$ changes neither that scalar nor the leaf's raw tensor.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Standing-Package Independence]
    \label{prop:can:standing-package-independence}
    Fix the raw records and a guild's CAN dependency graph.  Changing
    the base matrix, emission fractions,
    transport entries, certificates, or proof transcripts
    while leaving the published standing scalar and raw record tensors
    unchanged leaves every canonical CAN value unchanged.

    More generally, the only canonical formula path from standing into
    CAN is through a raw Declaration component that lies in the relevant
    composition dependency closure.  If no such Declaration leaf is
    present, then:
    \[
        \frac{
            \partial\canval{n}
        }{
            \partial\standing{i}
        }
        =
        0
    \]
    for the affected Actor~$i$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    The canonical recursion consumes only raw Frobenius base values,
    raw dependency-edge norms, redundancy sets, and child CAN values.
    None of the internal standing-package objects is an argument of
    those formulas.  The stated Declaration exception is exactly the
    raw tensor dependence already isolated by
    \zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Void Robustness]
    \label{thm:can:void-robustness}
    A void reference reduces $\canval{n}$ but does not collapse
    it to zero.
    \proofsketch{$\canval{\bot} = \epsilon_\bot > 0$; the void
    term $\depweight{n}{\bot}\epsilon_\bot > 0$.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parasitic Wrapper Elimination]
    \label{thm:can:parasitic-wrapper-elimination}
    A wrapper with edge norm $\delta \approx 0$ extracts
    $\canval{w} \approx \delta\,\canval{c}$.
    \proofsketch{$\trans{w} = \sat{\delta}
    = \delta/(1+\delta) \approx \delta$.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Redundancy Fairness]
    \label{thm:can:redundancy-fairness}
    Compositions with overlapping upstream dependencies receive
    lower value than those spanning disjoint work.
    \proofsketch{$\canval{n}$ is linear in $\redundancy{n}$.
    Disjoint: $\redundancy{} = 1$; overlapping: $\redundancy{}
    < 1$.}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity]
    \label{thm:can:monotonicity}
    $\canval{}$ is monotone in leaf base values. It is monotone in
    the outgoing edge norm $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{(n,b)}}_F$ to child
    $b$ precisely when $\canval{b} \geq \trans{n} \cdot \bar{V}_n$,
    where $\bar{V}_n = \sum_i \depweight{n}{c_i}\canval{c_i}$;
    strengthening a connection to an above-average child always
    raises $\canval{n}$, while strengthening a connection to a
    sufficiently weak child can lower it.
    \proofsketch{Leaf values enter linearly with non-negative
    coefficients (\zcref{eq:can:intrinsic-value-unrolled}). For edge
    norms, the sign of $\partial\canval{n}/\partial
    \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{(n,b)}}_F$ is
    $\operatorname{sgn}(\canval{b} - \trans{n}\bar{V}_n)$: the
    rising transmission coefficient competes against the dependency
    weight tilting toward $b$.}

    This theorem is internal to the guild CAN.  It makes no statement about
    monotonicity of the binding standing package, whose base matrix and accepted rung may
    change at an epoch boundary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Monotonicity Interpretation]
    \label{rem:can:monotonicity-conditional}
    Conditional monotonicity is a feature: the CAN penalises
    over-attribution to weak sources, so strengthening a connection
    to an outlier-weak child reduces the parent's value. This makes
    the CAN sensitive to curation quality, not just curation volume.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Operational Interface}
\label{subsec:can:operational-interface}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The canonical guild CAN reads raw accepted records through
\zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}.  A person-vouch act that becomes
one projected standing edge may still contribute one binary CAN leaf or
two hyper-edge leg leaves and one depth-1 composition node.  This is not
double counting: standing measures source-relative Actor delegation;
CAN attributes raw compositional contribution structure.

All values below use raw \AttrView{} Frobenius norms, no raw maturity,
no temporal damping, no source-relative standing view, and no standing
clip.  Every contribution edge maps to a CAN leaf with
base value $\baseval{e} = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F$; hyper-edges become
depth-1 compositions with $\redundancy{}
= 1$. For a Review $r$ with legs $e_1, e_2$:
\begin{align}
    \depweight{r}{e_i}
    &= \frac{\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_i}}_F}
            {\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}}_F
             + \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}}_F},
    \label{eq:can:review-weights} \\
    \canval{r}
    &= \sat{\tfrac{1}{2}
       (\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}}_F
        + \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}}_F)}
       \bigl(
         \depweight{r}{e_1}\baseval{e_1}
         + \depweight{r}{e_2}\baseval{e_2}
       \bigr).
    \label{eq:can:review-value}
\end{align}

For a Tag hyper-edge $g$ with legs of equal Frobenius norm
$\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}}_F = \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}}_F = w$
(which holds for the reference graph Tag at $w \numrel{result.e5.frobenius.num}$ by parameter
symmetry):
\begin{equation}
    \canval{g} = \frac{w^2}{1+w}.
    \label{eq:can:tag-equal-norm}
\end{equation}
For $w \numrel{result.e5.frobenius.num}$:
$\canval{g} = \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num}^2/2.762 \numrel{result.can.carol.num}$, consistent with
\zcref{subsec:verification:can-attribution}.
In the general case:
\[
    \canval{g}
    = \sat{\bar{w}} \cdot
    \frac{\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}}_F^2
          + \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}}_F^2}
         {\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}}_F
          + \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}}_F},
    \qquad
    \bar{w} = \tfrac{1}{2}
    (\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_1}}_F
     + \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}}_F).
\]

The guild reward formula (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}) uses
the CAN enrichment factor
$S_C^{\mathrm{CAN}} = S_C \cdot \canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$
(\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-vmax}), which is the
\AttrView{} layer of the reward formula. By
\zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}, this factor uses
exclusively \AttrView{} Frobenius norms: no $\tau$, no $\invtemp$,
no $\detscore{}$. It provides attribution equity
across interaction domains, with $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F$ varying only
$\sim\!21\%$ across the full range of edge types in the reference
graph (\zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}).
The enrichment factor remains terminal and insulated from the internal
standing package.  It may read the published standing scalar only
through a raw Declaration leaf in the declared dependency closure; it
never consumes projected vouch edges, source envelopes, selected
hop matrices, emission fractions, or certificates.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Worked Example}
\label{subsec:can:worked-example}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Alice creates photograph $C_1$. Bob reviews it (Comment $Co_1$).
Carol tags the Comment with Type ``StreetArt.'' All CAN values use the
\AttrView{}: $3 \times 3$ Frobenius norms, no $\tau$. The composition
structure follows the dependency-induction rule
(\zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}): each user-authored
$V_u$-sourced edge becomes a CAN leaf; the Review hyper-edge induces a
depth-1 composition with
$\redundancy{} = 1$.

For this CAN-only worked example, take the published standing input
$\standing{\text{Alice}}=0.300$ as a declared fixture.  The raw
Declaration component therefore has the corresponding raw bond
parameter $p_i=0.75$ under the raw Self-edge rule
(\zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}).  This example does
not rederive Alice's standing package; it tests only the canonical
CAN recursion and its insulation.

The Declaration component does not lie in the dependency closure of
Alice's Opinion leaf in this fixture, so every CAN value computed below
is independent of the standing input:
$\partial\canval{e_2}/\partial\standing{\text{Alice}} = 0$.

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Leaf values (\AttrView{}).}
    \label{tbl:can:leaf-values}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l c c@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Edge} & \textbf{Domain}
        & $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F$
        & $\baseval{}$ \\
        \midrule
        Alice creates $C_1$ (Opinion)
            & Tribal   & \numval{result.e2.frobenius.num} & \numval{result.e2.frobenius.num} \\
        Bob Review/A (Actor $\to C_1$)
            & Tribal   & \numval{result.e3.frobenius.num} & \numval{result.e3.frobenius.num} \\
        Bob Review/T ($C_1 \to Co_1$)
            & Epistemic & \numval{result.e4.frobenius.num} & \numval{result.e4.frobenius.num} \\
        Carol Tag/A (Actor $\to Co_1$)
            & Epistemic & \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num} & \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num} \\
        Carol Tag/T ($Co_1 \to$ StreetArt)
            & Epistemic & \numval{result.e6.frobenius.num} & \numval{result.e6.frobenius.num} \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Bob's Review ($r_B$, depth~1).}
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \meanedgenorm{r_B}
    &= \tfrac{1}{2}(\numval{result.e3.frobenius.num} + \numval{result.e4.frobenius.num}) \numrel{result.can.bob_mean.num}, \qquad
    \trans{r_B} = \numval{result.can.bob_mean.num}/2.698 \numrel{result.can.bob_trans.num} \\
    \depweight{r_B}{e_1} &= \numval{result.e3.frobenius.num}/\numval{result.can.bob_norm_sum.num} \numrel{result.can.bob_depweight_a.num}, \quad
    \depweight{r_B}{e_2} \numrel{result.can.bob_depweight_b.num} \\
    \canval{r_B}
    &= \numval{result.can.bob_trans.num} \times 1.0
       \times (\numval{result.can.bob_depweight_a.num} \times \numval{result.e3.frobenius.num} + \numval{result.can.bob_depweight_b.num} \times \numval{result.e4.frobenius.num}) \numrel{result.can.bob.num}
\end{aligned}
\]

\paragraph{Carol's Tag ($g_C$, depth~1).}
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \meanedgenorm{g_C}
    &= \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num}, \qquad
    \trans{g_C} = \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num}/2.762 \numrel{result.can.carol_trans.num} \\
    \canval{g_C}
    &= \numval{result.can.carol_trans.num} \times 1.0 \times \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num} \numrel{result.can.carol.num}
\end{aligned}
\]

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Attribution summary.}
    \label{tbl:can:attribution-summary}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l c c@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Participant} & \textbf{Role}
        & $\canval{}$ & $\canval{}/V_{\max}$ \\
        \midrule
        Alice & Creator  & \numval{result.e2.frobenius.num} & 1.000 \\
        Bob   & Reviewer & \numval{result.can.bob.num} & \numval{result.can.bob_share.num} \\
        Carol & Tagger   & \numval{result.can.carol.num} & \numval{result.can.carol_share.num} \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Key observations.}
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item Attribution ratios are compressed: Bob retains 59\%, Carol
          63\%. The \AttrView{}'s equalization across edge types means
          Tribal vs.\ Epistemic edges differ by only $\sim\!4\%$ in
          $3 \times 3$ norms for this example. The $\numval{result.tier.gap_lo.num}\times$
          Tribal/Epistemic gap in $\detscore{}$ that governs sorting
          (\zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}) does not
          propagate into attribution: the dual-view split ensures
          discrimination lives in sorting and equity lives in
          attribution.
    \item Transmission strictly less than 1 confirmed:
          $\trans{r_B} \numrel{result.can.bob_trans.num} < 1$ gives
          $\canval{r_B} = \numval{result.can.bob.num} < \max(\numval{result.e3.frobenius.num}, \numval{result.e4.frobenius.num}) = \numval{result.e3.frobenius.num}$
          (\zcref{thm:can:depth-decay}); $\trans{g_C} \numrel{result.can.carol_trans.num} < 1$
          gives $\canval{g_C} = \numval{result.can.carol.num} < \numval{result.e5.frobenius.num}$. Both mandatory guild
          invariants verified numerically.
    \item Standing-package independence confirmed: no source-relative
          view, hop share, emission fraction, transport value, or
          certificate enters the worked CAN graph.  The raw Declaration
          leaf ($p_i = \numval{fixture.e1.indirect.exact}$) is absent from the relevant dependency
          closure of the Opinion edge $e_2$, so varying the published
          standing scalar would change the Self-edge bond tensor but not
          $\symbf{\Psi}_{e_2}$, leaving every displayed CAN value
          unchanged
          (\zcref{prop:can:standing-package-independence,%
subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}).
\end{itemize}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Matrix CAN (Phase 3 Note)}
\label{subsec:can:matrix-extension}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

For deeper integration, the CAN can assign a $3 \times 3$ matrix to
each node and transmit via SVD-based attenuation. This is documented
for forward compatibility and as the reference for the
$\sim\!1.8\%$ scalar-vs-matrix correction cited in
\zcref{rem:can:implicit-diversity-bonus}. It is not the primary system
and is not required for compliance with the mandatory guild structural
invariants.

The matrix extension changes the terminal guild attribution
representation only.  It imports no allocation input and alters the standing of no record.

\begin{definition}[Matrix Leaf]
    \label{def:can:matrix-leaf}
    $\matcanval{\ell} = \symbf{\Psi}_\ell \in \R^{3 \times 3}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[SVD Transmission Matrix]
    \label{def:can:svd-transmission-matrix}
    Compute the mean outgoing edge matrix
    $\overline{\mathbf{W}}(n)
    = m^{-1}\sum_j \symbf{\Psi}_{(n,c_j)}$.
    SVD: $\overline{\mathbf{W}} = U\Sigma V^T$. The transmission
    matrix is:
    \begin{equation}
        \svdtrans{n}
        = U \cdot \operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(
          \sat{\svdone{}},\;
          \sat{\svdtwo{}},\;
          \sat{\svdthree{}}
        \bigr) \cdot V^T.
        \label{eq:can:svd-transmission-matrix}
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matrix Recursion]
    \label{def:can:matrix-recursion}
    Leaves: $\matcanval{\ell} = \symbf{\Psi}_\ell$. Internal:
    $\matcanval{n} = \redundancy{n} \cdot \svdtrans{n} \cdot
    \sum_i \depweight{n}{c_i} \matcanval{c_i}$. Weights remain
    scalar. Enrichment extracts a scalar:
    $\norm{\matcanval{n_C}}_F / V_{\max}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matrix Void]
    \label{def:can:matrix-void}
    $\matcanval{\bot} = \epsilon_\bot \cdot I_{3 \times 3}$.
    Isotropic: maximum diversity, minimum information.
\end{definition}

All scalar CAN theorems generalize via spectral norm substitution:
transmission bound ($\norm{\svdtrans{}}_2 = \sat{\svdone{}} < 1$),
depth decay, context independence, void robustness, and parasitic
wrapper elimination. The three mandatory guild structural invariants
(\zcref{def:can:mandatory-guild-invariants}) hold for the matrix CAN by the same
arguments applied to $\norm{\cdot}_2$ in place of the scalar
transmission coefficient. The matrix CAN is $\sim\!1.8\%$ stricter
than the scalar CAN at depth~1 (triangle inequality gap $\sim\!1.1\%$
plus asymmetry coupling $\sim\!0.7\%$). The advantage --- directional
filtering by the composition node's character --- becomes significant
at depth $3+$. Since most PeerNetwork compositions terminate at depth
1--2, the scalar CAN captures ${>}98\%$ of the matrix CAN's
information (\zcref{frontier:deep-composition}).
