\section{Bilateral Bridge Advertiser Transport}
\label{app:bridge}

The advertiser purchases an \emph{endorsed bridge circuit}: a terminal
guild reading of raw graph proximity, bridge-authored stance, advertiser
consent, and the already-published binding standing field.  It does not
compute or modify standing.  Structural
proximity alone is economically inert --- an advertiser may be one hop from a
target while every intermediary is oriented against it, connecting with no
one. The campaign scalar $\campaignscalar{A}$ prices the quality of the best
such circuit per target in the gate slot of the reward
formula (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}).

The canonical transport rests on three terminal channels, all
reproducible from public records:
\begin{description}[nosep]
    \item[Channel 1 --- raw affinity.]
        $\affinity{T, B}$: coherent positive-edge reach from target~$T$
        to bridge~$B$ on the raw positive subgraph.
    \item[Channel 2 --- raw endorsement stance.]
        $\endorsement{B, A}$: the bridge's authored directional stance
        toward advertiser~$A$, with magnitude carried by the raw
        Opinion/Reputation geometry.
    \item[Channel 3 --- raw consent.]
        $\consent{A, B}$: the advertiser's raw signed graph view of the
        bridge, clipped non-negative and vetoed by the advertiser's
        direct negative stance.
\end{description}
The raw per-edge default is $\dampedweight{e}$
(\zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}).  These channels are
terminal Layer~2 defaults under
\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}.  Their raw paths may contain passive
artifacts; that is valid for advertising discovery and consent because
no source balance, standing pair, or admission decision is transported.
The relation multigraph remains separate.
The product $\circqual{T, B, A} = \affinity{T, B} \cdot \endorsement{B, A}
\cdot \consent{A, B}$ rewards only complete circuits. The composition of
per-target circuits into a campaign scalar --- the outer
$\max_B$ over bridges --- is the \emph{canonical default} composition rule; it
is a Layer~2 guild choice, exactly as the CAN aggregation function is
(\zcref{subsec:transport:guild-model}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Overview and the \texorpdfstring{\zcref{sec:transport} $\leftrightarrow$ B}{7-B} Contract}
\label{subsec:bridge:overview}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This appendix and \zcref{sec:transport} divide the transport as follows.

\paragraph{\zcref{sec:transport} carries.}
The reward slot, guild model, target declaration, the statement
that bridge transport is terminal and guild-reimplementable, and the two
reward properties that hold verbatim (Zero-Reward,
\zcref{cor:transport:zero-reward}; Standing-Input Monotonicity,
\zcref{pty:transport:final-standing-input-monotonicity}).

\paragraph{This appendix carries.}
Every canonical raw channel definition, raw parity rule, campaign
composition, realizing-path structure, cancellation result
(\zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation}), and distributional surface.

\paragraph{The contract.}
No quantity in \zcref{sec:transport} is load-bearing without this appendix.
Conversely, this appendix consumes:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item public raw edge records and their canonical raw path-view
          quantities;
    \item the raw damped edge default
          (\zcref{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight});
    \item the raw determinant sign
          (\zcref{def:graph:determinant-sign});
    \item the raw signed double-cover service and its registers
          $\posreg{B}, \negreg{B}$
          (\zcref{subsec:epoch:raw-signed-service,%
alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs});
    \item raw Opinion and raw Reputation edge geometry;
    \item the binding standing field $\standing{i}$
          (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}) as a fixed scalar where a terminal
          channel specifies it.
\end{itemize}
All three channels are
computed from these without a new edge type, a new protocol constant, or a
new per-epoch batch computation.  It consumes no causal standing path,
emission fraction, transport matrix, or standing certificate.
Similar raw geometry does not make a bridge path a standing path.

The appendix proceeds from the parity discipline
(\zcref{subsec:bridge:parity-discipline}) and the positive
subgraph (\zcref{subsec:bridge:positive-subgraph}) to the three channels
(\zcref{subsec:bridge:channels}), the campaign scalar
(\zcref{subsec:bridge:campaign-scalar}), the cancellation result
(\zcref{subsec:bridge:cancellation}) and the distributional surface it
forces (\zcref{subsec:bridge:distributional-surface}), the re-scoped
monotonicity (\zcref{subsec:bridge:monotonicity}), structural properties
(\zcref{subsec:bridge:structural-properties}), and the
magnitude-attribution boundary that unifies every deferred refinement
(\zcref{subsec:bridge:magnitude-attribution-boundary}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Parity Discipline}
\label{subsec:bridge:parity-discipline}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The Layer~1 employs three traversal regimes with different parity
disciplines. All three follow one design principle.

\begin{remark}[Consumer-Set Heuristic]
    \label{rem:bridge:consumer-set-heuristic}
    The parity rule of a graph traversal is set by which nodes consume the
    transported orientation. If no consumer reads orientation, use magnitude
    only. If only the endpoints consume orientation, use per-path parity. If
    every node on the path consumes orientation, use per-edge parity.
\end{remark}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Terminal raw traversal}
        & \textbf{Consumer set}
        & \textbf{Raw parity rule} \\
    \midrule
    Feed-ranking BFS
        & querying user; no orientation verdict
        & magnitude only ($|\det|^{1/2}$) \\
    Raw signed consent service (Channel 3)
        & source and queried endpoint
        & total path parity $\detsign{p} = +1$ \\
    Bridge affinity (Channel 1)
        & every surfacing hop
        & per-edge $\forall e\!:\,\detsign{e} = +1$ \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Standing is omitted because it is not a raw traversal.  Its complete
person-vouch compiler checks semantic positivity and author ownership
before constructing Actor-only paths
(\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,%
prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}).

\zcref{rem:bridge:consumer-set-heuristic} is a \emph{design principle}, not a
theorem, and it is a \emph{sibling} of the positive-parity necessity argument
(\zcref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}), not a generalization that
subsumes it. That argument establishes that trust inference requires per-path
parity because routing influence through an inverted path treats inversion as
endorsement at the endpoints. Channel 1 applies the identical correctness
principle to the per-hop surfacing consumer set rather than the endpoint
consumer set.

\paragraph{Surfacing semantics.}
A Channel 1 path $T \xrightarrow{e_1} v_1 \cdots \xrightarrow{e_d} B$ is a
chain of surfacing relations: a positive edge means the next node surfaces in
the prior node's context as something the prior node approves of; a negative
edge means it surfaces under inversion. For the chain to be an
\emph{endorsement funnel} --- every hop an approval surface --- each hop must
individually be non-inverting. A compensating later negative edge restores
net parity but does not repair the interior hops already surfaced under
inversion. Per-path parity, correct for the endpoint-consuming endorsement inference,
is too weak for a per-hop-consuming funnel.

\begin{lemma}[Interior Coherence]
    \label{lem:bridge:interior-coherence}
    Let $p = (e_1, \ldots, e_d)$ be a path
    $v_0 \xrightarrow{e_1} v_1 \cdots \xrightarrow{e_d} v_d$. The orientation
    transported along $p$ arrives at interior node $v_k$ with cumulative sign
    $\pi_k = \prod_{j=1}^{k} \detsign{e_j}$, $\pi_0 = +1$. The transport is
    coherent at every node ($\pi_k = +1$ for all $k$) if and only if
    $\detsign{e_j} = +1$ for every $e_j$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    ($\Leftarrow$) A product of $+1$s. ($\Rightarrow$)
    $\detsign{e_k} = \pi_k / \pi_{k-1} = (+1)/(+1) = +1$.
\end{proof}

\zcref{lem:bridge:interior-coherence} is an arithmetic identity, not an
interpretive claim. Its role is to confirm that per-edge positivity is exactly
the set-theoretic characterization of coherent-at-every-node transport,
regardless of the semantic reading given to ``coherent.'' The decision that a
funnel \emph{must} be coherent at every node is the design choice; the lemma
records its unique structural consequence.

\begin{remark}[Disapproving-User Resolution]
    \label{rem:bridge:disapproving-user}
    A user who strongly disapproves of content ($\detsign{} = -1$, high
    $|\det|^{1/2}$) is excluded from Channel 1 despite genuine attention. This
    is correct under \zcref{rem:bridge:consumer-set-heuristic}:
    \emph{attention} is feed-ranking's domain (magnitude only, no parity
    filter --- the disapproving user is reachable for feed purposes);
    \emph{coherent endorsement funnelling} is Channel 1's domain (the
    disapproving user is an inverting hop, excluded from $\posgraph$). Two
    functions, two consumer sets, two derived rules.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\begin{remark}[Final Standing and Raw Bridge Paths]
    \label{rem:bridge:final-standing-and-raw-paths}
    Bridge transport reads the final standing field only through the
    formulas that explicitly contain it.  Raw target-to-bridge affinity
    may traverse a bridge Actor's raw Reputation edge, whose parameter is
    derived from final standing; bridge-to-advertiser endorsement may
    traverse the advertiser's raw Reputation edge; advertiser consent is
    read at the bridge Profile and does not traverse the bridge's raw
    Reputation edge.  These are terminal raw graph calculations: they do
    not alter final standing and do not reuse standing-stage paths or
    clips.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Positive Subgraph}
\label{subsec:bridge:positive-subgraph}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Positive Subgraph]
    \label{def:bridge:positive-subgraph}
    $\posgraph = (V, \posedgeset)$, where
    $\posedgeset = \set{e \in E : \detsign{e} = +1}$.
\end{definition}

$\posgraph$ is a terminal raw-graph projection used by the canonical
bridge affinity channel, reproducible by any participant from the
self-sufficient edge record: $\detsign{e}$ is published per edge
(\zcref{subsec:deployment:sufficiency}).  It is unrelated to the
relation multigraph: a raw positive edge may allocate to no person at all,
and a complete standing vouch is one semantic Actor
edge rather than a retained raw leg.
A guild may materialize $\posgraph$ by one pass over the public epoch
edge set filtering by $\detsign{e}$, or compute it lazily; a
host-published cache is a by-product and is not authoritative.
$\posgraph$ is used only by Channel 1; Channel 3 operates on the full
raw snapshot through the raw signed double-cover service (which tracks
both parities internally),
and Channel 2 is a fixed two-edge lookup. The feed-ranking BFS is unaffected.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Channel Definitions}
\label{subsec:bridge:channels}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Throughout, all channels use the shared damped weight $\dampedweight{e}$
(\zcref{rem:epoch:shared-raw-edge-primitive}). Targets and bridges are actors:
$T \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$, $B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$; the case $B = T$
is permitted.

% ─── Channel 1 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{definition}[Channel 1 --- Target--Bridge Affinity]
    \label{def:bridge:affinity}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:bridge-per-edge-positivity}%
    For target $T \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$ and candidate bridge
    $B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$:
    \begin{equation}
        \affinity{T, B}
        = \max_{p \,\in\, \mathrm{Paths}_3(T \to B,\; \posgraph)}
          \prod_{e \in p} \dampedweight{e},
        \label{eq:bridge:affinity}
    \end{equation}
    with $\affinity{T, B} = 0$ if no viable positive-only path of length
    $\leq 3$ exists. Convention: $\affinity{T, T} = 1$ (source
    initialization).
\end{definition}

This is the canonical terminal max-product BFS
(\zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs})
seeded at $T$, through raw depth at most three, executed on the raw
positive subgraph $\posgraph$ --- a pre-filter on the
edge set, not a modification of the relaxation rule.  It uses raw
$\dampedweight{e}$, including raw maturity and temporal damping.
Predecessor pointers are
retained for the realizing forest (\zcref{subsec:bridge:distributional-surface}).

It is not source-relative standing flow.  Passive vertices are allowed,
no balance/count pair is transported, and no W2 quantity reads the
result.

\begin{remark}[Depth-3 Rationale]
    \label{rem:bridge:depth-three}
    Channel 1 uses depth $\leq 3$, not $\leq 4$, to reserve one hop for
    Channel 2's authored endorsement edge: the full circuit
    $T \to \cdots \to B \to \mathrm{Profile}_A \to A$ has length $\leq 5$
    while no individual computation exceeds the protocol bound $L = 4$.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Affinity Properties]
    \label{prop:bridge:affinity-properties}
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item $\affinity{T, B} \in [0, 1]$.
        \item Every traversed edge has $\detsign{e} = +1$ by construction
              (no $\detsign{} = -1$ shortcuts in $\posgraph$).
        \item Dijkstra-compatible: $-\ln\dampedweight{e} > 0$ on $\posgraph$
              (\zcref{thm:sorting:log-transform-equivalence}).
        \item Bounded depth ($\leq 3$); one BFS per target; targets are
              advertiser-specified and few.
        \item Carries the raw Reputation weight of bridge~$B$,
              $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}}$, as the terminal factor
              of the raw affinity segment
              (the segment lands on $\mathrm{Actor}_B$); this is
              the sole appearance of $B$'s reputation in $\circqual{}$
              (\zcref{rem:bridge:reputation-single-traversal}).
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Reputation Enters the Circuit Exactly Once]
    \label{rem:bridge:reputation-single-traversal}
    By construction the Channel-1 affinity segment reaches the \emph{actor} $B$
    only through $\mathrm{Profile}_B$ followed by $B$'s single Reputation transfer
    $e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}$ ($\mathrm{Profile}_B\to B$), whose weight is a function
    of $\standing{B}$: a direct Actor$\to$Actor settlement edge (Accept or Ratify)
    is not a Channel-1 affinity terminus, so no affinity path reaches $B$ while
    bypassing that transfer.  This hop lies on the delivery circuit: it is the
    affinity segment's last edge, and the endorsement segment begins at
    $\mathrm{Actor}_B$.  The realizing path $\realizingpath{i}$
    (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-path}) therefore traverses it, and by the
    value/attribution invariant $\affinity{T, B}$ --- which must equal the
    weight of that segment --- carries $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}}$
    as its terminal factor (\zcref{prop:bridge:affinity-properties}).
    Consent (\zcref{def:bridge:consent}) is a gate, off the delivery circuit,
    and reads the double cover registers at $\mathrm{Profile}_B$ so it does not
    re-traverse $e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}$. Thus $B$'s reputation enters
    $\circqual{T, B, A}$ exactly once, linearly, on the segment the advertiser
    pays for. The necessity argument is
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference}: affinity keeps the hop
    because it is on the priced structure; consent sheds it because it is not.

    The Reputation quantity here is the raw derived edge weight used by
    the terminal bridge circuit.  It is distinct from the projected
    standing target activation $g_{\mathrm{vch}}$.  The two are both
    functions of the published standing state but have different
    formulas, consumers, and certificate status.
\end{remark}

% ─── Channel 2 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{definition}[Channel 2 --- Bridge--Advertiser Endorsement]
    \label{def:bridge:endorsement}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion}%
    For bridge $B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$ and advertiser $A \in V_u$, the
    endorsement traverses $B \xrightarrow{e_{\mathrm{Op}}} \mathrm{Profile}_A
    \xrightarrow{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} A$:
    \begin{equation}
        \endorsement{B, A}
                = \operatorname{sgn}\!\bigl(p_d(e_{\mathrm{Op}})\bigr)
          \cdot \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Op}}}
          \cdot \dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}},
        \label{eq:bridge:endorsement}
    \end{equation}
    where $e_{\mathrm{Op}}$ is the effective edge of $B$'s Opinion bundle on
    $\mathrm{Profile}_A$ under net stance (\zcref{def:epoch:net-stance}) ---
    netted, but \emph{not} restricted to positive stance: Channel~2 is a
    signed stance reader by
    design --- and
    $e_{\mathrm{Rep}}$ is the derived Reputation component of $A$'s
    Self-edge bond. If no such Opinion edge exists, or if
    $p_d(e_{\mathrm{Op}})=0$, then $\endorsement{B,A}=0$.  Channel~2 is a
    stance consumer: its sign is the bridge's authored directional verdict,
    not the determinant parity of the Opinion leg.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Endorsement Properties]
    \label{prop:bridge:endorsement-properties}
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item $\endorsement{B, A} \in (-1, 1)$, continuous through zero at the
              sign change (since $|\det|^{1/2} \to 0$ as parameters cross
              zero --- no discontinuity, no lump payment at the stance
              boundary).
          \item $\operatorname{sgn}(\endorsement{B, A})
              = \operatorname{sgn}(p_d(e_{\mathrm{Op}}))$. The sign is the
              bridge's own authored directional stance: positive vouches,
              negative is hostile.  This differs deliberately from
              determinant parity, which reads $\operatorname{sgn}(p_d p_i)$:
              Channel~2 reads stance, not coherence.
        \item The path uses the same raw Actor$\to$Profile Opinion and
              Profile$\to$Actor Reputation geometry as the profile-bridged
              feed path.  That raw two-edge geometry is not a standing
              path: standing compiles the complete Opinion act directly to
              an Actor-to-Actor projected vouch and uses the projected
              target activation.  The raw edge pair is public and
              independently reproducible; its terminal bridge role is
              distinct from the binding direct profile-vouch compilation
              of standing.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Guild Clip Option]
    \label{rem:bridge:clip-option}
    A guild may clip Channel 2 to $\max(0, \endorsement{B, A})$, restricting
    payment to bridges with realized positive stance endorsement. This is a
    Layer~2 policy choice, published per
    \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}. Under the clip the campaign scalar
    is non-negative and the \zcref[range]{sec:sorting,sec:transport} guarantees are inherited; under the signed
    form they require re-derivation (\zcref{rem:bridge:guild-fork}).
\end{remark}

% ─── Channel 3 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{definition}[Channel 3 --- Advertiser--Bridge Consent]
    \label{def:bridge:consent}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference}%
    For advertiser $A \in V_u$ and bridge $B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$, let
    $(\posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B}, \negreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B})$ be the
    positive and negative parity registers at $B$'s \emph{Profile} node from
    the raw signed double-cover service
    (\zcref{subsec:epoch:raw-signed-service,alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs})
    seeded at~$A$ and
    run on the \textbf{raw snapshot} $E_k$.  Consent is a \textbf{Layer-2
    canonical
    default} (\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}): its read-sites are terminal,
    and the raw-snapshot traversal is a guild-borne computation
    (\zcref{rem:bridge:consent-cost}).  The service is terminal and
    guild-borne; its raw registers are not the conserved transport
    $\transportentry{A}{B}$ and its output never enters the standing
    mediant. Let $\netpd{A\to\mathrm{Profile}_B}$ be the net direct directional
    stance of $A$'s authored bundle on $\mathrm{Profile}_B$, with value $0$
    when no such direct bundle exists. Define:
    \begin{equation}
        \consent{A, B}
        =
        \begin{cases}
            0,
                & \netpd{A\to\mathrm{Profile}_B} < 0, \\[4pt]
            \max\!\bigl(0,\;
              \posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B} - \negreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B}\bigr),
                & \netpd{A\to\mathrm{Profile}_B} \ge 0 .
        \end{cases}
        \label{eq:bridge:consent}
    \end{equation}
    The registers are read at $\mathrm{Profile}_B$, not at $\mathrm{Actor}_B$:
    consent is $A$'s authored regard for $B$ and must not re-traverse $B$'s
    Reputation component
    (\zcref{rem:bridge:reputation-single-traversal,subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference}).
    The first clause is the direct-stance veto: the advertiser's own direct
    negative stance toward the bridge defeats consent before multi-hop register
    evidence is considered.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Consent Range and Monotonicity]
    \label{prop:bridge:consent-properties}
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Range.} $\posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B},
              \negreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B} \in [0, 1)$ (each
              max-product path has length $\geq 1$ and
              $\dampedweight{e} < 1$,
              \zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-bound}), so
              $\posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B} - \negreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B}
              \in (-1, 1)$ and
              $\consent{A, B} \in [0, 1)$.
          \item \textbf{Monotonicity below the veto.} When
              $\netpd{A\to\mathrm{Profile}_B}\ge0$, $\consent{}$ is
              non-decreasing in the quality of positive-parity paths from $A$
              to $\mathrm{Profile}_B$ and non-increasing in the quality of
              negative-parity paths. A direct negative stance from $A$ to
              $\mathrm{Profile}_B$ is stronger than a register contribution:
              it triggers the veto clause and sets $\consent{A,B}=0$.
        \item \textbf{Subadditivity.} Under max-product,
              $\posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B}$ is the
              envelope of single-path products: a second positive-parity path
              of equal quality adds nothing.
              $\consent{}$ responds sublinearly to parallel positive paths,
              preventing redundancy amplification (the invariant of
              \zcref{subsec:necessity:max-product-path-scoring}).
        \item \textbf{Default-closed.} $\consent{A, B} = 0$ for a bridge with
              no positive-parity path from $A$.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Why the Difference]
    \label{rem:bridge:consent-difference-rationale}
    Two alternatives fail.  \emph{Over $\posreg{}$ alone:} hostile structure in
    the negative register is invisible, so multi-hop inverted dislike can fail to
    suppress consent.  The register difference retains the endpoint-parity
    discipline of the double cover.  \emph{Over registers alone:} the advertiser's
    own coherent condemnation $(-,-)$ of the bridge is a positive-parity path by
    the Quadrant Law and would raise $\posreg{}$ rather than suppress consent.
    The direct-stance veto supplies the missing verdict read: if the advertiser
    itself says no, by negative direct stance, consent is zero regardless of the
    coherence register.  A ratio $\posreg{}/\negreg{}$ fails differently ---
    undefined when $\negreg{}=0$, the common case.  The definition is
    therefore the minimal always-defined combination: registers for structural
    regard, direct stance for the advertiser's own veto. Both arguments
    presuppose the raw snapshot: the relation multigraph
    retains only complete positive person-vouches, so on it the negative
    register is empty by construction, which is precisely why
    \zcref{def:bridge:consent} mandates the raw run.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Consent Is Not Free, and Why Raw]
    \label{rem:bridge:consent-cost}
    The binding standing package supplies no double-cover run.  Canonical
    bridge consent therefore requires its own raw-snapshot signed
    traversal per advertiser: a genuine terminal guild computation, not a
    reuse of the binding standing package.

    The raw run is necessary because consent intentionally reads both
    positive and negative raw structural evidence --- including the
    coherent-hostile paths whose presence in $\negreg{}$ is the register
    difference's entire information content.  The initiator-owned
    standing projection retains only complete positive person-vouches
    and cannot substitute for that signed terminal question.

    The cost is priced to the guild that computes it.  Layer~1 \emph{may}
    publish the canonical-default consent values as an optional public
    service in the centralized phase, clearly labeled non-normative
    by-products.  Derivability
    is unaffected: the raw snapshot is public, so any participant
    recomputes both registers from $E_k$ --- a cost statement, not a
    trust statement.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Campaign Scalar}
\label{subsec:bridge:campaign-scalar}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{definition}[Circuit Quality and Campaign Scalar]
    \label{def:bridge:campaign-scalar}
    For advertiser $A$ with weighted targets $\set{(T_i, w_i)}$,
    $T_i \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$, $\sum_i w_i = 1$, the per-target
    \emph{circuit quality} is
    \begin{equation}
        \circqual{T, B, A}
        = \affinity{T, B} \cdot \endorsement{B, A} \cdot \consent{A, B},
        \label{eq:bridge:circuit-quality}
    \end{equation}
    and the \emph{bridge campaign scalar} is
    \begin{equation}
        \boxed{\;
        \campaignscalar{A}
        = \sum_{i:\, T_i \neq A} w_i
          \max_{B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}} \circqual{T_i, B, A}.
        \;}
        \label{eq:bridge:campaign-scalar}
    \end{equation}
\end{definition}

\paragraph{Composition semantics.}
The three factors trace a bilateral circuit:
\[
    T \;\xrightarrow[\text{affinity}]{\;\affinity{}\;}\; B
      \;\xrightarrow[\text{endorsement}]{\;\endorsement{}\;}\; A,
    \qquad
    B \;\xleftarrow[\text{consent}]{\;\consent{}\;}\; A.
\]
Channel 1 delivers coherent positive-parity affinity from target to bridge;
Channel 2 transmits the bridge's stance to the advertiser; Channel 3 confirms
the advertiser's structural regard for the bridge. The product rewards only
complete circuits where all three hold simultaneously.

\paragraph{Circuit length.}
The total edges traversed is at most $5$: up to $3$ (Channel 1) plus $2$
(Channel 2). No individual computation exceeds $L = 4$: Channel 1 is depth
$\leq 3$; Channel 3 is the double cover BFS at depth $\leq L$; Channel 2 is a
fixed two-edge lookup.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l c c c@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Configuration} & \textbf{C1 edges} & \textbf{C2 edges}
        & \textbf{Total} \\
    \midrule
    Direct ($B = T$)      & 0 & 2 & 2 \\
    One-hop bridge        & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
    Two-hop bridge        & 2 & 2 & 4 \\
    Three-hop bridge      & 3 & 2 & 5 \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\paragraph{Gating.}
The reward formula distributes for $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} > 0$, where
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A} = \campaignscalar{A}^{(k)}
- \campaignscalar{A}^{(k-1)}$; $R_C = 0$ when
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A} \leq 0$ (\zcref{cor:transport:zero-reward}).
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ is the campaign-viability gate slot,
serving as both gate and scalar magnitude; the level-based $S_C$ (\zcref{subsec:bridge:distributional-surface})
carries attribution.

\begin{remark}[Self-Target Exclusion]
    \label{rem:bridge:self-target}
    \necessityref{subsec:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion}%
    If $A$ targets itself, the domain restriction $T_i \in V_u \setminus
    \set{A}$ empties the target set, giving $\campaignscalar{A} = 0$, hence
    $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} \leq 0$ and $R_C = 0$ for all creators. This
    excludes the self-targeting degenerate case intrinsically; it requires
    no special-casing and simultaneously blocks the self-bridge case
    $B = A$.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Cancellation Lemma}
\label{subsec:bridge:cancellation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{lemma}[Campaign-Scalar Cancellation]
    \label{lem:bridge:cancellation}
    Write the reward formula (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula} with
    $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ in the gate slot) as
    \[
        R_C = \guildpool \cdot
        \frac{\Delta\campaignscalar{A} \cdot X_C}
             {\sum_{C'} \Delta\campaignscalar{A} \cdot X_{C'}},
        \qquad
          X_C = S_C \cdot \frac{\canval{n_C}}{V_{\max}} \cdot I_C
              \cdot \ampfactor{C} \cdot \boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}.
    \]
    Whenever $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} > 0$,
    \begin{equation}
        \boxed{\;
        R_C = \guildpool \cdot \frac{X_C}{\sum_{C'} X_{C'}}
        \;}
        \label{eq:bridge:cancellation}
    \end{equation}
    independently of the magnitude of $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$. Whenever
    $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} \leq 0$, $R_C = 0$ for all creators.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ is common to the numerator and to every
    summand of the denominator; for $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} > 0$ it cancels.
    For $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} \leq 0$ the gate of
    \zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula} sets every share to zero.
\end{proof}

The campaign increment $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ is creator-global and cancels
identically. The magnitude of
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ survives in exactly two places --- the binary gate
$\Delta\campaignscalar{A} > 0$ and, behaviorally and off-formula, the
advertiser's choice of pool $\guildpool$.

\begin{corollary}[Campaign-Global Factors Are Distributionally Inert]
    \label{cor:bridge:global-factors-inert}
    Any factor of the reward numerator constant across creators cancels from
    the normalized share. The campaign-global factors are
    $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ and $V_{\max}$; the creator-varying factors are
    $S_C$, $\canval{n_C}$, $I_C$, $\standing{C}$, and $\epochentropy{C}$.
\end{corollary}

In particular $V_{\max}$ --- a single campaign-wide scalar --- cancels exactly
as $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ does. The normalization point $V_{\max}$
(\zcref{subsec:bridge:distributional-surface}) is therefore
\emph{distributionally moot}: it alters the displayed enrichment
factor $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max} \in [0,1]$ (an interpretability and completeness
obligation, \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}) but changes no creator's
share.

\paragraph{Residual roles.}
The three-channel machinery reaches distribution through three channels, none
of which is ``magnitude as weight'':
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Gate} (magnitude, binary). $\Delta\campaignscalar{A} > 0$ is
          a threshold; above it, $10^{-7}$ and $0.5$ produce identical shares.
    \item \textbf{Structure selection} (argmax and path, not magnitude). The
          optimal bridge $\optbridge{i}
          = \arg\max_B \circqual{T_i, B, A}$ and the optimal affinity path fix
          the realizing forest, hence the support and topology of $S_C$
          and the improvement edge set behind $I_C$ (\zcref{subsec:bridge:distributional-surface}).
          This does not cancel: it determines \emph{which} creators are
          creditable.
    \item \textbf{Signal} (magnitude, to the advertiser). $\campaignscalar{A}$
          is information the advertiser consumes to set $\guildpool$ and decide
          whether to continue funding --- a market signal, not a formula
          weight.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{remark}
    \label{rem:bridge:one-line}
    $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ gates;
    $\arg\max_B \circqual{}$ selects; $\guildpool$ scales. Circuit magnitude
    enters distribution only through the binary gate and the advertiser's
    pool-funding decision, never as a per-creator weight.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Scale Inertness]
    \label{rem:bridge:scale-inertness}
    No positive lower bound on $\circqual{}$ exists (consent is a register
    difference, arbitrarily small near cancellation), and none is needed: by
    \zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation} magnitude never weights a share, and
    floating-point underflow of $\campaignscalar{A}$ to zero \emph{closes} the gate
    --- a conservative failure. The residual obligation is one verification row ---
    normalized $R_C$ denominators representable at realistic campaign sizes ---
    discharged at \zcref{ver:bridge:denominator-representability}.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Distributional Surface}
\label{subsec:bridge:distributional-surface}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The bridge model maintains a structural invariant: campaign value and per-creator
attribution are computed on the same paths. The value scalar $\campaignscalar{A}$
is realized on the bridge circuit, and $S_C$ is betweenness on that same realizing
structure. The creator-varying weights therefore sit on the structure that
realizes $\campaignscalar{A}$.

% ─── Realizing objects ───────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{definition}[Maximizing Bridge Class]
    \label{def:bridge:maximizing-bridge-class}
    For target~$T_i$ and advertiser~$A$, the maximizing bridge class is
    \[
        \bridgeclass{k}{i}
        \coloneqq
        \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{B\in V_u^{(k)}\setminus\set{A}}
        \circqual{T_i,B,A}.
    \]
    The campaign scalar consumes the common maximum value and therefore
    requires no bridge tie-break.

    Attribution retains every maximizing bridge and every maximizing
    realizing path.  Target weight is divided by ordinary optimal-path
    counting over the complete maximizing bridge/path class.  Actor
    identifiers and bridge identifiers do not select one semantic winner
    from an exact tie.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Realizing Path and Optimal Bridge]
    \label{def:bridge:realizing-path}
    For each target $T_i$ with $w_i > 0$ and $\max_B \circqual{} > 0$:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item the \emph{optimal bridge} is $\optbridge{i}
              = \arg\max_{B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}} \circqual{T_i, B, A}$;
          \item the \emph{optimal affinity path} $p^*_i : T_i \to \optbridge{i}$
              on $\posgraph$ is recovered from Channel 1's BFS predecessor
              pointers --- a free byproduct, exactly as feed-ranking does
              post-ranking for diagnostics (\zcref{rem:sorting:diagnostic-cost});
        \item the \emph{extended realizing path} appends the fixed Channel 2
              last hop:
              \[
                  \realizingpath{i} = p^*_i \cdot
                  \bigl(\optbridge{i}
                  \xrightarrow{e_{\mathrm{Op}}} \mathrm{Profile}_A
                  \xrightarrow{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} A\bigr).
              \]
    \end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Creditable Set]
    \label{def:bridge:creditable-set}
    $\creditset{\realizingpath{i}}
    = \set{\optbridge{i}} \cup \operatorname{int}_{V_u}(p^*_i)$, where
    $\operatorname{int}_{V_u}(p^*_i)$ is the set of $V_u$-nodes interior to the
    affinity segment (excluding its endpoints $T_i$ and $\optbridge{i}$), and
    $\optbridge{i}$ is added back as the bridge.
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Bridged} ($B \neq T$): the bridge plus intermediaries;
              the source $T_i$ is not credited (it is the affinity source, the
              analogue of the reached-content sink); $A$ and
              $\mathrm{Profile}_A$ never appear.
        \item \textbf{Direct} ($B = T$): $p^*_i$ is trivial,
              $\operatorname{int}_{V_u} = \void$, so
              $\creditset{} = \set{T_i}$ --- the target is credited as the
              endorser (it authored the Channel 2 edge).
        \item The buyer $A$ is structurally excluded; self-credit is
              impossible.
    \end{itemize}
\end{definition}

% ─── Realizing-Forest S_C ────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{definition}[Realizing-Forest Betweenness Centrality]
    \label{def:bridge:realizing-centrality}
    \begin{equation}
        \boxed{\;
        S_C = \sum_{i:\, T_i \neq A} w_i \cdot
              \frac{\sigma_C(\realizingpath{i})}{\sigma(\realizingpath{i})}
        \;}
        \label{eq:bridge:realizing-centrality}
    \end{equation}
    where $\sigma(\realizingpath{i})$ counts the max-product-optimal extended
    realizing paths for target $T_i$ and $\sigma_C(\realizingpath{i})$ counts
    those with $C \in \creditset{\realizingpath{i}}$. Here $\sigma$ and
    $\sigma_C$ are local path-count functions for this definition. This is betweenness
    centrality on the realized circuit structure
    ``$T_i \to \optbridge{i} \to \mathrm{Profile}_A \to A$ on $\posgraph$.''
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Exact Computation and Inheritance]
    \label{prop:bridge:sc-inheritance}
    With at most $k$ targets, each realizing path of depth $\leq 5$ and total
    creditable population $\lesssim 4k$, betweenness is computed \emph{exactly}
    in $O(kL)$ from the Channel 1 predecessor structure (Brandes-style
    dependency accumulation handles optimal-path ties). Consequently:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{$(\epsilon, \delta)$-approximation}
              (\zcref{thm:scalability:efficient-approximation}): holds with
              $\epsilon = 0$ (exact); there is nothing to sample.
        \item \textbf{Nash preservation}
              (\zcref{thm:scalability:nash-preservation}): depends only on
              $|\hat{S}_C - S_C| \leq \epsilon R_{\max}$ and the slack
              $\gamma$ --- satisfied a fortiori.
        \item \textbf{Reward Proportionality / Shapley}
              (\zcref{thm:transport:reward-proportionality}): efficiency, dummy,
              and symmetry on the realizing structure hold by construction (a
              creator on no realizing path is a dummy and earns zero). Holds
              under clipped Channel 2 ($\campaignscalar{A} \geq 0$); under
              signed Channel 2 the guild re-derives
              (\zcref{rem:bridge:guild-fork}).
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

The advertising $S_C$ is exact in $O(kL)$; no sampling pass is required.

% ─── Circuit-Improvement I_C ─────────────────────────────────────────

The active influence term $I_C$ is
defined over the circuit-improvement edge set: the $V_u$-authored edges on the
realizing forest that are new or strengthened this epoch. Unlike $V_{\max}$, $I_C$ is creator-varying
and \emph{survives normalization} (\zcref{cor:bridge:global-factors-inert}):
its definition is distribution-relevant.

\begin{definition}[Improvement Edge Set]
    \label{def:bridge:improvement-edge-set}
    For epoch $k$,
    \begin{equation}
        \improveset{A}
        = \Bigl\{\, e \in \textstyle\bigcup_i \realizingpath{i}^{(k)}
          \;\Big|\;
          e \in (E_k \setminus E_{k-1}),\ e\ \text{authored, non-derived}
          \,\Bigr\},
        \label{eq:bridge:improvement-edge-set}
    \end{equation}
    the $V_u$-authored edges on the epoch-$k$ extended realizing forest that are
    \emph{newly accepted} this epoch.  Ordinary authored edges fix their
    parameters and maturity at creation, so their damped weight does not change
    across epochs; the only weights that move are derived Self-edges (bond
    derivation from standing), which are excluded here as in $\creditset{}$ and
    tracked separately as non-reward diagnostics.  $A$-authored edges are
    likewise excluded.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circuit-Improvement Influence]
    \label{def:bridge:realizing-active-influence}
    Let $\improveset{A}^{\,C}$ be the subset of $\improveset{A}$ authored by
    $C$. If $\improveset{A} \neq \void$,
    \begin{equation}
        I_C = \frac{|\improveset{A}^{\,C}|}{|\improveset{A}|}
              \cdot (1 + \tau_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\,C})^{0.5};
        \label{eq:bridge:realizing-active-influence}
    \end{equation}
    otherwise --- the creditable change-set is empty, the gate having been
    opened solely by $A$-authored consent (the cold-start case,
    \zcref{rem:bridge:cold-start}) --- $I_C$ falls back to the
    \emph{winning-path support}: $C$'s authored fraction of the $V_u$-authored
    edges of the current realizing forest $\bigcup_i \realizingpath{i}^{(k)}$,
    maturity-weighted identically.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Flow, Not Stock; Orthogonal to $S_C$]
    \label{rem:bridge:flow-not-stock}
    $S_C$ rewards occupying the realizing forest (a level quantity, full
    $w_i$ per interior node); $I_C$ rewards having moved it this epoch (a flow
    quantity, authorship share over the improvement set). Among the surviving
    reward weights, only $I_C$ is defined over a $\Delta$-set: $S_C$ is stock,
    $I_C$ is flow.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Cold-Start Coherence]
    \label{rem:bridge:cold-start-coherence}
    The fallback is exact, not a patch. When the advertiser opens a closed
    gate by its own positive Opinion (\zcref{rem:bridge:cold-start}), the
    responsible edge is $A$-authored and excluded; reward must flow to the
    standing circuit the advertiser activated, and the fallback credits
    exactly that circuit's authors. Without it, the headline cold-start
    mechanism would clear the gate yet pay no creator (a $0/0$ collapse) ---
    a degeneracy latent in any $\Delta$-set influence definition and made prominent
    by the consent channel.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Churn Resistance]
    \label{rem:bridge:churn-resistance}
    Harvesting $I_C$ by adding edges is self-limiting: every new action
    irrevocably increments $\actcount{i}$, diluting $\commitrate{i}$ and
    $\standing{i}$ (\zcref{sec:comparator}), and an edge enters
    $\improveset{A}$ only if it genuinely lies on the improved realizing
    circuit. The only way to gain $I_C$ is to improve the campaign --- the
    aligned behavior. Append-only structure does for $I_C$ what max-product
    does for $S_C$ (\zcref{subsec:necessity:max-product-path-scoring}).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Computation and State]
    \label{rem:bridge:ic-state}
    $\improveset{A}$ requires the epoch-$(k-1)$ realizing forest in addition
    to the scalar $\campaignscalar{A}^{(k-1)}$ the gate already consumes.
    Under \zcref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility} the previous forest is
    recomputable from the published $E_{k-1}$; the marginal cost is a second
    Channel 1 pass per boundary, $O(k\bar{d}^3)$, derivable by any
    participant. This is the only part of the bridge transport that adds a
    genuine second pass.
\end{remark}

% ─── Realizing-Path V_max ────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{definition}[Realizing-Path CAN Enrichment Normalization]
    \label{def:bridge:realizing-vmax}
    \[
        V_{\max} = \max\set*{\canval{n} \mid n \text{ lies on some extended
        realizing path } \realizingpath{i} \text{ with } w_i > 0}.
    \]
    The enriched centrality $S_C^{\mathrm{CAN}}
    = S_C \cdot \canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ is otherwise unchanged. All properties
    of the enrichment factor --- pure \AttrView{} quantities,
    $\partial(\canval{n_C}/V_{\max})/\partial\standing{C} = 0$ for actors
    outside their dependency closure, attribution equity across edge types
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}) --- are preserved
    because $V_{\max}$ is a maximum of the same CAN values over a different
    node set.
\end{definition}

By \zcref{cor:bridge:global-factors-inert}, $V_{\max}$ is distributionally
inert: \zcref{def:bridge:realizing-vmax} affects the displayed enrichment
factor and interpretive consistency with the realizing structure, not any
creator's share.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Monotonicity (Re-Scoped Under Cancellation)}
\label{subsec:bridge:monotonicity}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Because the magnitude of $\campaignscalar{A}$ cancels
(\zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation}), the monotonicity properties govern
\emph{gate-clearing, bridge selection, and advertiser signal} --- not the
magnitude of any creator's share. Properties that move creator shares do so by
\emph{restructuring} the realizing forest, not by scaling a weight.

\begin{theorem}[Campaign-Scalar Monotonicity --- Gate and Selection]
    \label{thm:bridge:monotonicity}
    Let $\optbridge{i}$ be the optimal bridge for target $T_i$. Then
    $\campaignscalar{A}$ is:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item \textbf{Affinity-monotone (gate/signal):}
              $\partial\campaignscalar{A}/\partial\affinity{T_i, \optbridge{i}}
              \geq 0$. Improving coherent delivery to the optimal bridge raises
              circuit value, increasing the likelihood the gate clears and
              raising the signal to the advertiser; it does not by itself
              raise any creator's share.
        \item \textbf{Endorsement-magnitude-monotone (gate/signal;
              $\endorsement{} > 0$):}
              $\partial\campaignscalar{A}/\partial|\endorsement{\optbridge{i},
              A}| \geq 0$.
        \item \textbf{Endorsement-sign-monotone (gate; under clip):} flipping
              $\operatorname{sgn}(p_d(e_{\mathrm{Op}}))$ from $-1$ to $+1$ raises
              $\endorsement{}$ through zero; under the clip a clipped-out
              circuit can cross the gate.
        \item \textbf{Consent-monotone (gate/signal):}
              $\partial\campaignscalar{A}/\partial\consent{A, \optbridge{i}}
              \geq 0$.
          \item \label{itm:bridge:monotonicity-standing}%
              \textbf{standing-monotone (gate/signal, via Channel 2
              only):}
              $\partial\campaignscalar{A}/\partial\standing{A} \geq 0$, through
              $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep},A}}$ in the endorsement path
              $B \to \mathrm{Profile}_A \to A$
              (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}).
    \end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    Each factor of $\circqual{}$ is non-negative under the clip, and
    $\campaignscalar{A}$ is the weighted sum over targets of the outer
    envelope $\max_B \circqual{}$; the envelope of increasing functions is
    increasing. \zcref{itm:bridge:monotonicity-standing}: $\standing{A}$ enters
    only through Channel 2's
    Reputation component $e_{\mathrm{Rep},A}$, strictly increasing in
    $\standing{A}$ (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}). It does
    \emph{not} enter Channel 3: the double cover BFS from $A$ reaches
    $\mathrm{Profile}_B$ through $A$'s authored Opinion edges, never through
    $A$'s own Declaration component, so $\consent{A, B}$ is independent of
    $\standing{A}$. The named consumers
    (gate, signal, selection) follow from \zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation},
    where magnitude is shown not to enter share computation.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Discrete Structure Sensitivity of $S_C$]
    \label{prop:bridge:discrete-structure-sensitivity}
    Improving a single edge weight on the affinity segment of
    $\realizingpath{i}$ does not, in general, change any creator's share. The
    realizing-forest $S_C$ (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-centrality}) counts optimal
    realizing paths, not their weights; with a unique optimal realizing path,
    every interior $V_u$ node already receives the full $w_i$, and a
    within-path weight improvement changes $S_C$ for no one. $S_C$ changes only
    at discrete restructuring events:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item a weight change that flips $\arg\max_B \circqual{}$ to a
              different bridge;
          \item a weight change that promotes a suboptimal affinity
              path to optimal (or demotes the optimal one);
        \item the creation or destruction of an optimal-path tie,
              redistributing fractional Brandes credit.
    \end{enumerate}
    \proofsketch{$S_C$ depends on the realizing forest only through which
    paths are optimal and which $V_u$-nodes are interior to them. A
    perturbation preserving the argmax and the optimal-path set leaves both
    counts fixed.}
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[Selection-Tournament Incentive Alignment]
    \label{cor:bridge:selection-tournament}
    A relay maximizes its expected share by being \emph{selected} as an
    interior node of the optimal realizing path to the winning bridge ---
    equivalently, by holding the strongest positive-parity affinity edge among
    competitors for that target's delivery. Generically the optimal path's
    interior $V_u$-nodes take the full $w_i$ and competing relays take zero;
    fractional shares arise only at exact ties. The alignment between relay
    incentive and campaign value is real but operates through selection, not
    magnitude: a relay competes to improve $\circqual{}$ at the winning bridge
    in order to be chosen, and having been chosen, earns the structural share
    $w_i\,\sigma_C/\sigma$ regardless of by how much it won.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[The Eligibility Cliff Is the Primary Distribution Mechanism]
    \label{rem:bridge:eligibility-cliff-primary}
    The selection discontinuity --- a single edge toggling
    $\arg\max_B \circqual{}$ --- is not a peripheral monitoring item. Under
    \zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation} it is the principal mechanism by which the
    three-channel structure reaches per-creator distribution: the argmax flip
    \emph{is} the redistribution event. Graceful degradation (a runner-up
    bridge usually exists, so $\campaignscalar{A}$ degrades rather than
    collapses) bounds the impact on the gate and signal, but the impact on
    \emph{shares} is genuinely discontinuous at the flip
    (\zcref{prop:bridge:discrete-structure-sensitivity}). Deployment monitoring
    (\zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model}) should track argmax-flip
    frequency as a distribution-stability metric, not merely a
    campaign-value-stability metric.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Structural Properties}
\label{subsec:bridge:structural-properties}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{proposition}[Guard Structure]
    \label{prop:bridge:guard}
    Channel 3 ($\consent{} \geq 0$) guards Channel 2 ($\endorsement{}$
    signed): for any bridge to move $\campaignscalar{A}$ in either direction,
    the advertiser must hold $\consent{A, B} > 0$. This blocks:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item \emph{Griefing:} a competitor induces a hostile high-reach hub
              to post $\detsign{} = -1$ toward $A$; $A$ dislikes the hub
              ($\negreg{} > \posreg{}$, $\consent{} = 0$); the negative drag
              vanishes.
        \item \emph{Flip-flop ratchet:} a bridge oscillates its sign to
              harvest up-swings; $A$ dislikes the oscillator; $\consent{} = 0$.
    \end{itemize}
    The guard now has two layers.  The direct-stance veto is an absolute veto
    by the advertiser's own record: if
    $\netpd{A\to\mathrm{Profile}_B}<0$, then $\consent{A,B}=0$ even when the
    edge is coherent $(-,-)$ and would otherwise land in the positive register
    by the Quadrant Law.  Below that veto, the register difference is structural
    dominance: broader positive-parity regard may outweigh broader
    negative-parity regard, but it cannot override the advertiser's own direct
    no.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Griefing Immunity Under the Default Policy]
    \label{rem:bridge:griefing-clip}
    Under the default clipped Channel 2 (\zcref{rem:bridge:clip-option}), a
    hostile hub gives $\endorsement{} \leq 0 \Rightarrow \circqual{} = 0$
    regardless of $\consent{}$, so the clip is the primary griefing defense.
    The consent guard does independent work only in the signed variant, and
    only when $A$ has authored positive regard for the hub.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Sybil Resistance]
    \label{cor:bridge:sybil}
    A puppet bridge earns reward only at the intersection of two fields it does
    not control: $\affinity{T, B} \approx 0$ (no genuine positive-path
    standing in the target's community --- $\posgraph$ admits no
    $\detsign{} = -1$ shortcuts) and $\consent{A, B} \approx 0$ (no genuine
    positive-parity regard from the advertiser's neighborhood). The only factor
    the puppet controls is its own endorsement edge $\endorsement{}$;
    multiplied by two near-zero factors, the reward is near-zero. Resistance is
    anchored in audience-authored edges (Channel 1) and advertiser-graph-derived
    consent (Channel 3), not in the bridge's own actions.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Cold Start]
    \label{rem:bridge:cold-start}
    $\consent{A, B} = 0$ for a bridge with no positive-parity path from $A$ ---
    an unknown bridge earns nothing and costs nothing. The natural resolution
    is the advertiser's ordinary social activity: a positive Opinion on
    $\mathrm{Profile}_B$ creates a direct positive-parity path, opening
    $\posreg{B} > 0$ at the next epoch. No new edge type is required. Cold
    start and griefing immunity are the same mechanism: the default-closed gate
    excludes both the unknown and the griefer, and the same action --- a
    genuine positive edge from $A$'s neighborhood --- opens both.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Guild Fork: Signed vs.\ Clipped Channel 2]
    \label{rem:bridge:guild-fork}
    Non-negativity of the campaign scalar is not a mandatory guild invariant
    (those are the three CAN invariants
    (\zcref{def:can:mandatory-guild-invariants}) plus completeness). A guild may run
    signed Channel 2, but Shapley proportionality, Zero-Reward, and Nash
    preservation are proven only for non-negative formulas.
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l c c@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Policy} & \textbf{$\campaignscalar{A}$ sign}
            & \textbf{\zcref[range]{sec:sorting,sec:transport} guarantees} \\
        \midrule
        Clip ($\endorsement{} \leftarrow \max(0, \endorsement{})$)
            & $\geq 0$ & inherited \\
        Signed (unclipped)
            & may be $< 0$ & guild re-derives or accepts loss \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{center}
    A guild wanting signed Channel 2 with a safe denominator may floor the
    scalar ($\campaignscalar{A} \leftarrow \max(0, \campaignscalar{A})$),
    which re-clips in the underwater regime --- collapsing to gated behavior
    exactly when signing was supposed to matter. The guild genuinely chooses
    one of: clip Channel 2; signed-with-floor (effectively clipped when
    underwater); signed-unfloored (own your invariants). Under signed
    Channel 2 the realizing forest (built over targets with
    $\max_B \circqual{} > 0$) and the campaign sum (over all targets, including
    those whose best circuit is negative) range over different target subsets:
    a creator can earn positive $S_C$ on a circuit that reduced campaign value.
    The guild's re-derivation must address this. The chosen policy is published
    per \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Degenerate Cases]
    \label{rem:bridge:degenerate}
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l c c c l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Case} & $\affinity{}$ & $\endorsement{}$ & $\consent{}$
            & \textbf{Who is paid} \\
        \midrule
        Self-target $A = T$ & --- & --- & --- & $\campaignscalar{A} = 0$;
            $R_C = 0$ \\
        Direct $B = T$ & 1 & $\endorsement{T, A}$ & $\consent{A, T}$
            & $T$ as sole interior node \\
        Bridged $B \neq T$ & $< 1$ & $\endorsement{B, A}$ & $\consent{A, B}$
            & relays between $T$ and $B$, plus $B$ \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{center}
    No special-casing: the self-target row is the empty target set
    (\zcref{rem:bridge:self-target}); the direct row is the
    $\affinity{T, T} = 1$ convention with $\creditset{} = \set{T}$.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Magnitude-Attribution Boundary}
\label{subsec:bridge:magnitude-attribution-boundary}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This appendix specifies a \emph{magnitude-insensitive core} and defers every
\emph{magnitude-sensitive refinement} to Layer~2. That division is not three
separate deferrals; it is one boundary, encountered three times.

\paragraph{The core is magnitude-insensitive by construction.}
The Cancellation Lemma (\zcref{lem:bridge:cancellation}) establishes that the
magnitude of $\campaignscalar{A}$ does not survive normalization: it gates,
selects a bridge, and signals the advertiser, but never weights a creator's
share. Distribution is driven by \emph{which} structure realizes the circuit
--- $\arg\max_B \circqual{}$ and the realizing forest --- not by \emph{how
much} circuit value that structure carries. The realizing-forest $S_C$ counts paths,
not weights (\zcref{prop:bridge:discrete-structure-sensitivity}); the
circuit-improvement $I_C$ counts authored edges, not their contributions
(\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-active-influence}); $V_{\max}$ cancels outright
(\zcref{cor:bridge:global-factors-inert}). The single-bridge canonical default
is exactly this magnitude-insensitive object: it asks who is on the winning
circuit, never by how much.

\paragraph{Three refinements ask the magnitude-sensitive question, and it is
one question.}
Each wants to convert a circuit \emph{magnitude} into a per-participant
\emph{share} --- to decompose $\campaignscalar{A}$ over the actors and edges
that produce it, crediting each by marginal contribution.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{4.4cm} p{5.2cm} p{4.0cm}@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Where it arises} & \textbf{Object wanted} & \textbf{Reduces to} \\
    \midrule
    Magnitude-sensitive distribution (this appendix)
        & circuit magnitude flowing to creators proportionally
        & Shapley decomposition of $\campaignscalar{A}$ over participants \\
    \addlinespace
    Multi-bridge composition (\zcref{frontier:bridge-multi-bridge})
        & credit a chain $T \to B_1 \to B_2 \to A$ where neither bridge alone
          completes the circuit
        & Shapley value of a game over complementary intermediaries \\
    \addlinespace
    Exact $I_C$ responsibility
        (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-active-influence})
        & credit each realizing-forest edge by how much it moved
          $\campaignscalar{A}$, not whether it is newly accepted
        & marginal contribution of each edge to $\campaignscalar{A}^{(k)}$ \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{insight}[Three Deferrals, One Boundary]
    \label{ins:bridge:magnitude-boundary}
    Magnitude-sensitive reward distribution, multi-bridge attribution, and
    exact change-set responsibility are the same problem: a
    marginal-contribution decomposition of the campaign scalar over the actors
    and edges that realize it. The Layer~1 protocol supplies the
    magnitude-insensitive primitives --- the three channel values, the
    single-bridge envelope, the path-counting $S_C$, and the change-set $I_C$
    with its cold-start fallback --- together with the mandatory invariant that
    a guild claiming the \zcref[range]{sec:sorting,sec:transport} guarantees must inherit or re-derive them. The
    decomposition itself is a Layer~2 research direction, identical in kind to
    the guild's freedom over the CAN aggregation function
    (\zcref{frontier:can-aggregation-function}) and the composition rule. A guild
    that solves it once solves all three: a single Shapley construction
    delivers magnitude-sensitive shares, multi-bridge credit, and exact $I_C$
    responsibility, because they were never three problems.
\end{insight}

The boundary is principled, not pragmatic. A marginal-contribution
decomposition is genuinely a Layer~2 object, for the same reason the CAN
aggregation function is (\zcref{subsec:transport:guild-model}): there is no
canonical counterfactual for ``the circuit without this actor.'' Removing a
bridge may reroute through a runner-up (small marginal value) or collapse the
target's circuit entirely (large marginal value); the answer depends on
off-equilibrium structure that different guilds may legitimately model
differently. The protocol cannot pick one without imposing an economic theory
it has no standing to impose. It supplies the primitives and the verifiability
obligation, and lets guilds compete on the decomposition --- the same
Layer~1 / Layer~2 contract the Layer~1 draws everywhere else.
