\section{Staged Standing Equilibria and Certified Dynamics}
\label{app:dynamics}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Overview and Contracts}
\label{subsec:dynamics:overview}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

For one proposed completed epoch state, standing is computed through three
current-epoch stages.  The depth-two stage is a continuous max-envelope map
whose strongest source-target path may switch while the fixed point is solved.
The depth-three and depth-four stages are different: each selects paths at the
completed epoch set, freezes the base matrix and the emission diagonal, and
solves one fixed stage map
(\zcref{def:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium,%
def:epoch:conserved-standing-equilibrium}).

The epoch index, stage index, and solver-iteration index are distinct:
\[
    k=\text{epoch},\qquad
    h\in\{2,3,4\}=\text{projected-depth stage},\qquad
    n=\text{inner fixed-point iteration}.
\]
The solver orbit
$\boldsymbol x_{k,n+1}^{[h]}=\boldsymbol F_k^{[h]}(\boldsymbol x_{k,n}^{[h]})$
is an internal calculation for one completed epoch state; it is not the
protocol's epoch-to-epoch standing evolution.  Only the highest certified
stage is published as final standing (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}).

The deployed target dependence of every projected vouch edge is the
safety-wall-clamped activation
$\wallactivation{x}=\vouchactivation{\max(x,\safefloor)}$
(\zcref{def:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation}), built from the responsive
base
\begin{equation}
    \boxed{\;
    \vouchactivation{x}
    =
    \left[
        \vouchcore{p(x)}
    \right]^{\actexponent},
    \qquad
    \vouchcore{p}
    =
    \frac{
        \sigmoid{\invtemp p}
        \sqrt{\tanh p\,(1-\bleedparam^2\tanh p)}
    }{
        \sigmoid{\invtemp}
        \sqrt{\tanh 1\,(1-\bleedparam^2\tanh 1)}
    },
    \qquad
    p(x)=\frac{x}{1+x}.
    \;}
    \label{eq:dynamics:activation}
\end{equation}
Here $x=\standing{}/\numeraire$ is reduced standing.  The activation contains
no raw maturity or temporal-entropy factor; those remain raw feed and bridge
quantities.

Two gains must remain distinct:
\begin{align}
    \vouchgain{x}
    &\coloneqq
      \frac{d}{dx}\log\vouchactivation{x},
      \label{eq:dynamics:vouch-gain}\\
    \loggain{x}
    &\coloneqq
      \frac{d}{dx}\log Q_0(p(x)),
      \label{eq:dynamics:clean-budget-gain}
\end{align}
where $Q_0$ is the clean $\bleedparam=0$ core, with
\begin{equation}
    0\le
    \vouchgain{x}/\actexponent
    \le
    \loggain{x}
    \label{eq:dynamics:gain-domination}
\end{equation}
(\zcref{prop:dynamics:clean-gain-domination}).  The exact deployed per-hop gain
is the responsive $\vouchgain{}$; the effective gain $\wallvouchgain{x}$ is zero
below the wall, interval-valued at the wall, and equal to $\vouchgain{x}$ above
it; and $\loggain{}$ is the clean full-depth screening envelope used by the
width fence and safety-threshold calibration.

\paragraph{What is settled, and where.}
This appendix proves the responsive activation properties and the
projected-depth gain budget, promotes the conserved equilibrium to a
max-envelope contraction, gives the fixed depth-three and depth-four stage
derivatives and their propagation, and establishes uniqueness of the
within-epoch equilibrium by certified contraction.  The graph-dependent stage
certificate (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), not a global
criticality sign, is the normative deployment safety gate; the full-depth clean
gain envelope yields the prior width fence (\zcref{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}).

\paragraph{Scope of criticality.}
Smooth-branch statements --- monotonicity, concavity, log-concavity,
Schwarzian, and margin --- apply to the responsive base activation
$\vouchactivation{}$ on the branch $x>\safefloor$, never across the kink of the
wall-clamped activation
(\zcref{rem:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-scope}).  The prior oscillator,
onset, and drift analyses are quarantined pending rederivation on fixed
responsive stage cells.

\paragraph{Contracts.}
\zcref{sec:epoch} owns epoch construction, complete-act compilation, and stage
selection; Appendix~D proves activation, contraction, and convergence.  The
verification suite certifies concrete stage boxes (Vcert), graph-independent
gain screens (Fcert), and activation behaviour (Bcert).  \zcref{sec:nodes} owns
the closed standing-role census; Appendix~D consumes only the resulting
Actor-only projected paths.  Raw feed Self-edge dynamics
(\zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}) are not standing dynamics.
\textbf{Status is the environment:} a
\emph{theorem}/\emph{lemma}/\emph{corollary} is proved unconditionally; a
\emph{proposition} stated under a named \emph{conjecture} is proved modulo that
conjecture; a \emph{conjecture} is open.  Where a single \emph{clause} of an
otherwise unconditional statement hangs on an open conjecture, the environment
name carries a dagger ($\dagger$) hyperlinked to the open item, so the
dependence is visible on the page.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Within-Epoch Indices and the Scalar Self-Map}
\label{subsec:dynamics:within-epoch-indices}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{postulate}[Direct-Allocation-Dominated Row]
    \label{post:dynamics:direct-allocation-dominated}
    For Actor~$i$, the transported mass entering the standing row arrives at
    hop one: $\transportentry{u}{i}>0$ only for sources that allocate to~$i$
    directly.

    This is a special case of the general transport, obtained when the depth
    mass is concentrated at hop one or when the base matrix has no length-two
    support into~$i$.  It does not assert that the Action Graph lacks longer
    chains; it states that this row's transport does not use them, which is a
    property of the base matrix and so is checkable in advance
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:support-state-independence}).
\end{postulate}

Let
\[
    n_i\coloneqq\max(\actcount{i},1),
    \qquad
    \refrate{i}
    \coloneqq
    \frac{\burnbal{i}}{\numeraire n_i}.
\]
Every contributing source~$u$ has $\actcount{u}\ge1$.  Let
$c_{ui}\in(0,1]$ be the hop-one allocation share $\hopalloc{1}{u}{i}{}$ of the
source's conserved unit, excluding the recipient activation.
Define the action-mass-adjusted direct coefficient
\begin{equation}
    \gamma_{ui}
    \coloneqq
    \frac{\actcount{u}}{n_i}\,c_{ui}.
    \label{eq:dynamics:hop-one-mass-coefficient}
\end{equation}

The direct incoming structural mass and its source-rate mean are
\begin{align}
    \endorsermass{i}
    &\coloneqq
      \sum_{u\neq i}\gamma_{ui},
      \label{eq:dynamics:allocation-aggregates-mass}\\
    \endorsemean{i}
    &\coloneqq
      \frac{
          \sum_{u\neq i}\gamma_{ui}\refrate{u}
      }{
          \endorsermass{i}
      },
      \qquad
      \endorsermass{i}>0.
      \label{eq:dynamics:allocation-aggregates-rate}
\end{align}

Under \zcref{post:dynamics:direct-allocation-dominated}, every direct projected
edge into~$i$ carries the common deployed target activation
$\wallactivation{x}$.  The exact reduced standing map is therefore
\begin{equation}
    \boxed{\;
    f_i(x)
    =
    \frac{
        \refrate{i}
        +
        \wallactivation{x}\,
        \endorsermass{i}\,
        \endorsemean{i}
    }{
        1+
        \wallactivation{x}\,
        \endorsermass{i}
    }.
    \;}
    \label{eq:dynamics:scalar-row-map}
\end{equation}

This has the same fractional-linear shape as the uniform-activity
rate-DeGroot reduction, but its coefficients are exact
action-mass-adjusted quantities derived from the normative mediant
(\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing}).  The unadjusted reading
$\endorsermass{i}=\sum_u W_{ui}$ is valid only under uniform contributing
action counts.

\begin{remark}[Isolated Actor]
    \label{rem:dynamics:isolated-actor}
    If $\endorsermass{i}=0$, then
    \[
        f_i\equiv\refrate{i},
    \]
    so the row reaches its own neutral source in one update.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Responsive and Wall-Clamped Activation}
\label{subsec:dynamics:responsive-activation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Write
\[
    h(x)
    \coloneqq
    \vouchcore{p(x)}
    =
    \frac{Q_\eta(p(x))}{Q_\eta(1)},
    \qquad
    r\coloneqq\actexponent,
    \qquad
    \vouchactivation{x}=h(x)^r.
\]
The normalization is positive and constant, so it affects activation
magnitude but no log derivative.  Every statement in this subsection concerns
the responsive base $\vouchactivation{}$ on the smooth branch; the deployed
activation is its safety-wall clamp
(\zcref{prop:dynamics:safety-wall-clamp}).

\begin{proposition}[Responsive Vouch-Activation Monotonicity]
    \label{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}
    $\vouchactivation{}'(x)>0$ for every $x>0$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    The deployed core $Q_\eta(p)$ is strictly increasing on
    $p\in(0,1)$ and $p'(x)=(1+x)^{-2}>0$.  Hence $h'(x)>0$.
    Since $r>0$ and $h>0$,
    $\vouchactivation{}'(x)=r\,h(x)^{r-1}h'(x)>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Responsive Vouch-Activation Bound]
    \label{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-bound}
    \[
        0<\vouchactivation{x}<1
        \qquad
        \text{for every finite }x>0,
    \]
    with $\vouchactivation{x}\to1$ as $x\to\infty$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    For finite $x$, $p(x)<1$ and strict monotonicity gives
    $0<Q_\eta(p(x))<Q_\eta(1)$.  Thus $0<h(x)<1$, and raising to
    $r\in(0,1)$ preserves the interval.  The limit follows from
    $p(x)\to1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Responsive Vouch-Activation Log-Concavity]
    \label{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-log-concavity}
    \[
        \frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log\vouchactivation{x}<0
        \qquad(x>0).
    \]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    $\log\vouchactivation{x}=r\log h(x)$.
    The deployed core is strictly log-concave after Möbius reduction on
    the operating domain, and multiplication by the positive constant
    $r$ preserves the sign of the second derivative.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Responsive Vouch-Activation Concavity]
    \label{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-concavity}
    $\vouchactivation{}''(x)<0$ for every $x>0$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    The normalized core $h$ is positive, increasing, and concave.
    Differentiating $h^r$:
    \[
        \vouchactivation{}''
        =
        r h^{r-2}
        \left(
            h h''
            +(r-1)(h')^2
        \right).
    \]
    Here $r>0$, $h>0$, $h''<0$, and $r-1<0$, so both terms inside
    the parentheses are negative.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Responsive Vouch-Activation Scope]
    \label{rem:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-scope}
    Monotonicity, concavity, log-concavity, Schwarzian, and smooth
    criticality statements in this appendix apply to the responsive base
    function $\vouchactivation{}$ on the branch $x>\safefloor$, not across
    the kink of the effective wall-clamped activation
    $\wallactivation{}$.  The analytic core and interval certificates
    (\texttt{peer\_Bcert}, \texttt{peer\_Fcert}) separately verify
    positivity, monotonicity, clean-gain domination, and the required
    concavity/log-concavity on the published live domain; the fourth-root
    transformation preserves these properties as shown above.  Higher-order
    Schwarzian sign does not survive globally and is re-scoped to the
    responsive branch below.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Clean Full-Depth Gain Domination]
    \label{prop:dynamics:clean-gain-domination}
    For every positive reduced standing~$x$:
    \[
        0
        \le
        \vouchgain{x}/\actexponent
        \le
        \loggain{x}.
    \]
    Equality in the first comparison holds only at zero gain; the
    clean envelope strictly exceeds the deployed full-depth gain for
    positive finite~$x$ when $\bleedparam>0$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    The projected activation is the $\actexponent$ power of the
    normalized deployed core, so:
    \[
        \vouchgain{x}/\actexponent
        =
        \frac{d}{dx}\log Q_\eta(p(x)).
    \]
    The exact correction from the clean kernel to the deployed kernel is
    negative:
    \[
        K_0(p)-K_\eta(p)
        =
        \frac{\bleedparam^2}{2}
        \frac{\operatorname{sech}^2p}
             {1-\bleedparam^2\tanh p}
        >0.
    \]
    Multiplication by $p'(x)=(1-p)^2>0$ gives the result.  The interval
    certificate \texttt{peer\_Fcert2} verifies the inequality over the
    published domain.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Safety-Wall Clamp Properties]
    \label{prop:dynamics:safety-wall-clamp}
    Let $\wallactivation{x}=\vouchactivation{\max(x,\safefloor)}$
    (\zcref{def:epoch:safety-wall-clamped-activation}).  Then:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item $\wallactivation{}$ is continuous and nondecreasing;
        \item it is constant on $[0,\safefloor]$, with zero derivative on
              $(0,\safefloor)$;
        \item it equals the responsive activation $\vouchactivation{}$ on
              $(\safefloor,\infty)$;
        \item its Clarke generalized reduced-standing log-derivative at the
              wall lies in $[0,\vouchgain{\safefloor}]$;
        \item for every $x\ge0$,
              $0\le\wallvouchgain{x}\le\vouchgain{\safefloor}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Consequently a below-wall Actor contributes a fixed path factor with zero
    state derivative --- breaking any feedback cycle at that channel --- while
    raw maturity of its Reputation edge changes no projected activation.  There
    is no previous-standing memory and no last-valid branch: the clamp reads
    only the current standing state.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    Continuity follows from continuity of $\vouchactivation{}$ and
    $x\mapsto\max(x,\safefloor)$; below-wall constancy is direct; the responsive
    branch is the base activation
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}); the
    generalized derivative at the one-dimensional max kink is the convex hull of
    the one-sided derivatives; and $\vouchgain{}$ is decreasing
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-log-concavity}), so the
    wall value is the supremum.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\begin{remark}[Standing--Feed Separation]
    \label{rem:dynamics:standing-feed-separation}
    Standing and feed do not share one activation or one traversal.
    The profile-bridged discovery path
    (\zcref{def:nodes:profile-bridged-discovery-path}) consumes the raw
    damped Reputation weight; the standing map consumes the projected
    fourth-root activation $\wallactivation{}$.  Both are functions of the
    published standing state, so the converged fixed point $x_i^\ast$
    still fixes one stable published scalar, and the commitment
    amplification product
    (\zcref{def:nodes:raw-profile-bridge-amplification}) remains a
    stable monotone signal of that published input --- as a terminal
    reader, not as a second run of the standing machinery.
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Fixed-Point Residual Enclosure}
\label{subsec:dynamics:fixed-point-enclosure}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{lemma}[Fixed-Point Residual Enclosure]
    \label{lem:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure}
    Let $F$ be a $c$-contraction ($c<1$) in the $\infty$-norm on a complete
    invariant box, with unique fixed point $\boldsymbol x^\star$.  For any
    approximate point $\tilde{\boldsymbol x}$ in the box,
    \begin{equation}
        \|\tilde{\boldsymbol x}-\boldsymbol x^\star\|_\infty
        \le
        \frac{\|F(\tilde{\boldsymbol x})-\tilde{\boldsymbol x}\|_\infty}{1-c}.
        \label{eq:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure}
    \end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    With $r=\|F(\tilde{\boldsymbol x})-\tilde{\boldsymbol x}\|_\infty$,
    \[
        \|\tilde{\boldsymbol x}-\boldsymbol x^\star\|_\infty
        \le
        \|\tilde{\boldsymbol x}-F(\tilde{\boldsymbol x})\|_\infty
        +
        \|F(\tilde{\boldsymbol x})-F(\boldsymbol x^\star)\|_\infty
        \le
        r+c\,\|\tilde{\boldsymbol x}-\boldsymbol x^\star\|_\infty,
    \]
    and rearranging gives the bound.
\end{proof}

The enclosure lets a high-precision point solve certify a rigorous box around
the exact stage equilibrium, so the W2a and W2b threshold comparisons are
decided without ambiguity and independent fixtures agree.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Within-Epoch Fixed-Point Convergence}
\label{subsec:dynamics:within-epoch-convergence}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{theorem}[Within-Epoch Fixed-Point Convergence]
    \label{thm:dynamics:within-epoch-fixed-point-convergence}
    Fix a completed epoch state at the accepted rung, with the rate-hull box
    $\hullbox{k}$ and a valid certificate $\marginfactor\standingcert{k}\le1$
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}).  The inner
    solver orbit
    \[
        \standingvector_{k,n+1}
        =
        \standingmapvector{k}{\standingvector_{k,n}}
    \]
    converges geometrically to the unique equilibrium $\standingeq$ from every
    start in the box:
    \begin{equation}
        \norm{\standingvector_{k,n}-\standingeq}_\infty
        \le
        \bigl(\standingcert{k}\bigr)^{n}
        \operatorname{diam}_\infty\!\bigl(\hullbox{k}\bigr),
        \label{eq:dynamics:within-epoch-convergence}
    \end{equation}
    and the fixed point is independent of the initialization
    $\standingvector_{k,0}$
    (\zcref{cor:dynamics:standing-initialization-independence}).

    There is one such statement per epoch, not one per depth.  Edition~4 needed
    a convergence theorem for each certified stage because each stage had its
    own map, its own box and its own certificate; the conserved map has one of
    each, and the guaranteed factor is whatever the accepted rung certifies.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    The certified map is a contraction of factor $\standingcert{k}<1$ on the
    complete invariant box $\hullbox{k}$
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}), so Banach's
    fixed-point theorem gives a unique equilibrium; applying the contraction
    estimate $n$ times to $\operatorname{diam}_\infty(\hullbox{k})$ gives the
    geometric bound.
\end{proof}

The iteration index~$n$ is an inner solver step for one completed epoch state,
not an epoch: the whole orbit lives inside the single boundary computation of
\zcref{subsec:epoch:within-epoch-standing-solver} and is discarded once the
equilibrium is certified.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Standing Map-Shock Bound}
\label{subsec:dynamics:standing-map-shock-bound}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{proposition}[Standing Map-Shock Bound]
    \label{prop:dynamics:standing-map-shock-bound}
    Let $\boldsymbol F_{k-1}$ and $\boldsymbol F_k$ be consecutive
    certified final-stage standing maps on a common invariant box
    $\mathcal B$, with fixed points $\boldsymbol x_{k-1}^{\star}$ and
    $\boldsymbol x_k^{\star}$.  Suppose the current map has certified
    contraction enclosure $\mathcal K_k<1$.  Define the map shock
    \[
        \mapshock{k}
        \coloneqq
        \sup_{\boldsymbol x\in\mathcal B}
        \norm{
            \boldsymbol F_k(\boldsymbol x)
            -
            \boldsymbol F_{k-1}(\boldsymbol x)
        }_{\infty}.
    \]
    Then
    \[
        \norm{
            \boldsymbol x_k^{\star}
            -
            \boldsymbol x_{k-1}^{\star}
        }_{\infty}
        \le
        \frac{
            \mapshock{k}
        }{
            1-\mathcal K_k
        }.
    \]

    The bound separates change in the standing map from amplification by
    the current contraction margin.  It is a verification and monitoring
    quantity, not a W1/W2 admission gate.
    \proofsketch{Both points are fixed:
    $\boldsymbol x_k^{\star}=\boldsymbol F_k(\boldsymbol x_k^{\star})$ and
    $\boldsymbol x_{k-1}^{\star}=\boldsymbol F_{k-1}(\boldsymbol
    x_{k-1}^{\star})$.  Insert $\boldsymbol F_k(\boldsymbol
    x_{k-1}^{\star})$ and use the triangle inequality:
    $\norm{\boldsymbol x_k^{\star}-\boldsymbol x_{k-1}^{\star}}_\infty
    \le\norm{\boldsymbol F_k(\boldsymbol x_k^{\star})-\boldsymbol
    F_k(\boldsymbol x_{k-1}^{\star})}_\infty+\norm{\boldsymbol
    F_k(\boldsymbol x_{k-1}^{\star})-\boldsymbol F_{k-1}(\boldsymbol
    x_{k-1}^{\star})}_\infty$.  The first term is at most
    $\mathcal K_k\norm{\boldsymbol x_k^{\star}-\boldsymbol
    x_{k-1}^{\star}}_\infty$ by the certified contraction enclosure of
    $\boldsymbol F_k$ on $\mathcal B$; the second is at most
    $\mapshock{k}$.  Rearranging
    $(1-\mathcal K_k)\norm{\boldsymbol x_k^{\star}-\boldsymbol
    x_{k-1}^{\star}}_\infty\le\mapshock{k}$ gives the bound, using
    $\mathcal K_k<1$.}
\end{proposition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Solver Decomposition and Warm Starts}
\label{subsec:dynamics:solver-decomposition}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{remark}[Warm-Start Independence]
    \label{rem:dynamics:warm-start-independence}
    Previous final standing may initialize the depth-two solve, the depth-two
    equilibrium the depth-three solve, and the depth-three equilibrium the
    depth-four solve; cached path products and dependency-component solutions
    may reduce work.  None of this changes the result: each certified stage map
    is a contraction with a unique fixed point
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}), so caches are
    implementation state, not standing inputs.  An implementation may compute
    the strongly connected components of the stage dependency graph, solve the
    condensation DAG in topological order --- isolated zero-flow rows directly,
    independent components in parallel, and only cyclic components by coupled
    iteration --- without changing the mathematical map.
\end{remark}


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Responsive-Branch Criticality}
\label{subsec:dynamics:responsive-criticality}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The criticality analysis separates the unpowered deployed core
$Q_\eta$ from the projected standing activation
$g_{\mathrm{vch}}$.

Define:
\[
    Q_\eta(p)
    =
    \sigmoid{\invtemp p}
    \sqrt{\tanh p\,(1-\bleedparam^2\tanh p)},
    \qquad
    \widetilde Q_\eta(p)
    =
    \frac{Q_\eta(p)}{Q_\eta(1)},
\]
and:
\[
    g_{\mathrm{vch}}(x)
    =
    \widetilde Q_\eta(p(x))^{\actexponent},
    \qquad
    p(x)=\frac{x}{1+x}.
\]

Three derivative coordinates must remain distinct:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item the core p-gain
          \[
              K_\eta(p)
              =
              \frac{d}{dp}\log Q_\eta(p);
          \]
    \item the projected p-gain
          \[
              \vouchpgain{p}
              =
              \frac{d}{dp}\log
              \widetilde Q_\eta(p)^{\actexponent}
              =
              \actexponent K_\eta(p);
          \]
    \item the reduced-standing gain
          \[
              \vouchgain{x}
              =
              \frac{d}{dx}\log g_{\mathrm{vch}}(x)
              =
              (1-p(x))^2\vouchpgain{p(x)}.
          \]
\end{enumerate}

\begin{definition}[Tilt Gain Coordinates]
    \label{def:dynamics:tilt-gain-coordinates}
    The notation $\vouchpgain{p}$ is reserved for the projected
    p-coordinate gain, $\vouchgain{x}$ for the exact reduced-standing gain,
    and $\wallvouchgain{x}$ for its wall-clamped form --- the one the
    allocation derivative carries
    (\zcref{eq:epoch:rival-allocation-response}).  The clean screening gain
    remains $\loggain{x}$, and its value at the wall is $\wallgaincap$.

    The chain of certified inequalities is:
    \[
        0
        \le
        \wallvouchgain{x}
        \le
        \wallgaincap
        \le
        \tfrac14\loggain{\safefloor} ,
    \]
    the last step being clean-gain domination
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:clean-gain-domination}).  Each hop of the transport
    spends its own factor of the gain, weighted by that hop's tilt exponent;
    the profile's cumulative sum is what the fence prices, never a single
    depth constant.
\end{definition}

The Möbius kernel $p(x)=x/(1+x)$ has zero Schwarzian.  Positive
normalization by $Q_\eta(1)$ also contributes no Schwarzian, but the
$\actexponent$ power does.  Thus the negative-Schwarzian result for
$Q_\eta$ does not transfer unchanged to $g_{\mathrm{vch}}$.

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Schwarzian budget of the projected standing activation.}
    \label{tbl:dynamics:mobius-budget}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Stage} & \textbf{Form} & \textbf{Contribution} \\
        \midrule
        kernel $p(x)=x/(1+x)$
            & Möbius
            & zero Schwarzian \\
        normalization $Q_\eta/Q_\eta(1)$
            & positive affine scaling
            & zero Schwarzian \\
        depth distribution $z\mapsto z^{1/4}$
            & power map
            & adds $\numval{const.dynamics.schwarz_coeff.exact}K_\eta^2$ in p-coordinates \\
        deployed core $Q_\eta$
            & transcendental
            & core Schwarzian $S_pQ_\eta$ \\
        projected activation $g_{\mathrm{vch}}$
            & composite
            & certified sign partition \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{lemma}[Möbius Descent]
    \label{lem:dynamics:mobius-descent}
    Let:
    \[
        G(p)
        =
        \widetilde Q_\eta(p)^{\actexponent},
        \qquad
        g_{\mathrm{vch}}(x)
        =
        G(p(x)).
    \]
    Since $\Schwarz{}p\equiv0$:
    \begin{equation}
        \Schwarz{g_{\mathrm{vch}}(x)}
        =
        \bigl(p'(x)\bigr)^2
        \Schwarz[p]{G(p(x))}
        =
        \frac{
            \Schwarz[p]{G(p(x))}
        }{
            (1+x)^4
        }.
        \label{eq:dynamics:mobius-descent}
    \end{equation}
    Therefore the sign of the reduced-standing Schwarzian is exactly the
    sign of the projected p-Schwarzian.

    Writing
    $K_\eta=(\log Q_\eta)'$ and
    $r=\actexponent$:
    \begin{equation}
        \boxed{\;
        \Schwarz[p]{G}
        =
        \Schwarz[p]{Q_\eta}
        +
        \frac{1-r^2}{2}K_\eta^2
        =
        \Schwarz[p]{Q_\eta}
        +
        \frac{15}{32}K_\eta^2.
        \;}
        \label{eq:dynamics:projected-schwarzian}
    \end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Schwarzian freedom]
    \label{thm:dynamics:responsive-schwarzian-freedom}
    Let $\mathcal C$ be the $C^3$ projected activation family satisfying
    the monotonicity, boundedness, concavity, and log-concavity properties
    of \zcref[range]{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity,%
  prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-log-concavity} on a named live interval.
    Those properties constrain the 2-jet but do not determine the
    Schwarzian sign or the criticality of an activation outside the
    certified contraction region:
    $G\mapsto\Schwarz[p]{G(p^\ast)}$ is surjective onto $\mathbb R$ on
    every $C^2$-neighborhood in $\mathcal C$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    By \zcref{eq:dynamics:mobius-descent}, it suffices to sweep the
    projected p-coordinate Schwarzian.  Add the perturbation
    \begin{equation}
        G\ \mapsto\ G+A\delta^3\phi\!\big((p-p^\ast)/\delta\big),\qquad
        \phi\in C_c^\infty,\ \phi(0)=\phi'(0)=\phi''(0)=0,\ \phi'''(0)=1;
        \label{eq:dynamics:schwarzian-freedom-pert}
    \end{equation}
    the 2-jet is untouched, $G'''$ shifts by $A$, and $\delta=|A|^{-2}$ makes the
    $C^2$-perturbation $O(|A|^{-1})\to0$, so the four properties survive while
    $\Schwarz[p]{G(p^\ast)}$ sweeps $\mathbb R$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Deployment Consequence]
    \label{rem:dynamics:schwarzian-freedom-deployment}
    Dynamic safety is not inferred from the activation axioms or a
    global criticality sign.  It is carried by the graph-dependent
    conserved standing certificate
    (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate,%
thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}).

    The projected criticality partition remains relevant only if a
    schedule enters the contraction-free residual.  Any future change to
    the projected activation requires a new activation certificate and
    formula edition under the staged-standing reproducibility discipline
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}).
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate realization]
    \label{thm:dynamics:coordinate-realization}
    In deployed coordinates
    \begin{equation}
        \lyapone=Q(\text{2-jet})+c\,g'''(\alpha^\ast),\qquad c\neq0
        \label{eq:dynamics:coordinate-realization}
    \end{equation}
    throughout the bifurcation regime, with two first-power sources — diagonal terminal
    and interior relay — projecting to
    \begin{equation}
        c_{g'''}=\tfrac1{2D}\big[B(\hat r_b-\alpha^\ast)-\omega\,\gamma \vouchactivation{}^\ast(\refrate{s}-\alpha^\ast)\big],
        \label{eq:dynamics:c-gppp}
    \end{equation}
    generically nonzero by the opposite signs of the two rate gaps. A constructive
    witness for \zcref{thm:dynamics:responsive-schwarzian-freedom}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Monotone gain]
    \label{lem:dynamics:monotone-gain}
    \begin{equation}
        \loggain{\alpha}=(1-p)^2\gainkernel{p},\qquad
        \gainkernel{p}=\invtemp(1-\clampsigmoid{p})+1/\sinh2p,
        \label{eq:dynamics:monotone-gain}
    \end{equation}
    is strictly decreasing on $\alpha>0$.
    \proofsketch{As $\alpha\!\uparrow$, $p\!\uparrow$: $(1-p)^2\!\downarrow$,
    $\invtemp(1-\clampsigmoid{p})\!\downarrow$, $1/\sinh2p\!\downarrow$; product of positive
    decreasing factors.}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gain elasticity]
    \label{lem:dynamics:elasticity}
    On $[1,\infty)$ the elasticity $\elast{\alpha}:=\alpha\,\loggain{\alpha}$ is
    non-increasing.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    In the kernel variable, $\alpha=p/(1-p)$ and $\loggain{\alpha}=(1-p)^2\gainkernel{p}$
    (\zcref{lem:dynamics:monotone-gain}), so $\elast{}=p(1-p)\,\gainkernel{p}$. On
    $[\tfrac12,1)$ the prefactor $q(p)=p(1-p)$ has $q'=1-2p\le0$, and both kernel terms
    decrease ($\partial_p[\invtemp(1-\clampsigmoid{p})]<0$, $\partial_p[1/\sinh2p]<0$),
    so $\gainkernel{}'<0$. Hence $\elast{}'=q'\gainkernel{}+q\gainkernel{}'\le0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Analytic Elasticity Cap]
    \label{lem:dynamics:elasticity-cap}
    For all $p\in(0,1)$:
    $\elast{} < \elastcap
    \coloneqq \tfrac12+\tfrac{(\invtemp-1)^{2}}{8\invtemp} \numrel{const.dynamics.elastcap.num}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    $\operatorname{csch}x<1/x$ and $\clampsigmoid{p}>\tfrac12$ give
    $\gainkernel{p}<\tfrac{1}{2p}+\tfrac{\invtemp}{2}$, so
    $\elast{}=p(1-p)\gainkernel{}<(1-p)(\tfrac12+\tfrac{\invtemp p}{2})$, a
    downward parabola with maximum $\tfrac12+(\invtemp-1)^{2}/(8\invtemp)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Elasticity profile below the gate]
    \label{rem:dynamics:elasticity-profile}
    Certified (certificate \texttt{peer\_Fcert},
    \zcref{subsec:verification:graph-dependent-certificate}): $\elast{0^{+}}=\tfrac12$
    with $\elast{}'(0^{+})=\ln2-\tfrac12>0$; $\elast{}$ is strictly concave on
    $(0,\tfrac12]$ (analytic on $(0,0.29]$, interval-certified on
    $[0.02,0.50]$), strictly increasing on $[0.01,0.05]$ and strictly
    decreasing on $[0.10,1)$.  The \emph{ridge} is therefore unique and
    bracketed: $p^{\ast}\in(\numval{fixture.ridge.p_lo.exact},\numval{fixture.ridge.p_hi.exact})$, i.e.\
    $\hat\alpha^{\ast}\in(\numval{bound.dynamics.ridge_alpha_lo.num},\numval{bound.dynamics.ridge_alpha_hi.num})$, with
    $\elastmax\in[\numval{bound.dynamics.elastmax_lo.num},\,\numval{bound.dynamics.elastmax_hi.num}]$ (grid lower bound; analytic cap
    $\elastcap$, \zcref{lem:dynamics:elasticity-cap}).  The
    profile is a plateau near the ridge (total variation $<10^{-4}$ across
    $p\in[0.060,0.075]$), which is why the certified object is a bracket,
    never a point; tails below the certified intervals close by the
    expansion constants of \zcref{thm:dynamics:core-margin-limit}.  The
    profile is read by the width fence and its wall rule
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence,cor:dynamics:minimal-safe-wall})
    --- the fence floor is the requirement that the safety wall stay
    above the ridge bracket with margin.  This profile is a clean
    screening object; exact motif sensitivities use the projected
    per-hop gain (\zcref{def:dynamics:tilt-gain-coordinates}).
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Core Schwarzian Profile]
    \label{prop:dynamics:core-schwarzian-profile}
    Throughout this ladder $\sigma$ abbreviates $\sigmoid{\invtemp p}$ and
    $w=\coth 2p$ (locals shared with
    \zcref{lem:dynamics:core-schwarzian-factorization,thm:dynamics:core-interaction-negativity}).
    Let $K_\eta=(\log Q_\eta)'$ (rendered $K$ below, with the clean
    kernel form $\gainkernel{p}$).  With
    \begin{align}
        K'&=-\invtemp^2\sigma(1-\sigma)-2\cosh2p/\sinh^2 2p,
        \label{eq:dynamics:Kprime}\\
        K''&=-\invtemp^3\sigma(1-\sigma)(1-2\sigma)+4(\sinh^2 2p+2)/\sinh^3 2p,
        \label{eq:dynamics:Kdprime}
    \end{align}
    the unpowered deployed core has
    \begin{equation}
        \Schwarz[p]{Q_\eta}
        =\frac{K''}{\gainkernel{p}}
        -\tfrac32\Big(\frac{K'}{\gainkernel{p}}\Big)^2
        -\tfrac12\gainkernel{p}^2.
        \label{eq:dynamics:schwarzian-profile}
    \end{equation}
    At every sampled $p\in[\tfrac12,1)$ this is strictly negative and monotone
    (\zcref{tbl:dynamics:core-schwarzian-profile}), sign-set by the logistic anchor
    $\Schwarz{}\sigma\equiv-\tfrac12$.  The interval certificate
    \texttt{peer\_Bcert2} retains this core negativity as compatibility
    evidence on its certified core domain.  This proposition does not
    state the sign of $\Schwarz[p]{G}$ for the projected activation.
\end{proposition}

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Unpowered core Schwarzian profile
    (\zcref{eq:dynamics:schwarzian-profile}); core p-gain
    $K_\eta(p)$ column.}
    \label{tbl:dynamics:core-schwarzian-profile}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}c c c c@{}}
        \toprule
        $x$ & $p$ & $\Schwarz[p]{Q_\eta}$ & core p-gain $K_\eta(p)$ \\
        \midrule
        $1$ & $\numval{fixture.kernel.p1.num}$ & $\numval{result.schwarz.s_half.num}$ & $\numval{result.schwarz.k_half.num}$ \\
        $2$ & $\numval{fixture.kernel.p2.num}$ & $\numval{result.schwarz.s_p23.num}$ & $\numval{result.schwarz.k_p23.num}$ \\
        $3$ & $\numval{fixture.kernel.p3.num}$ & $\numval{result.schwarz.s_p34.num}$ & $\numval{result.schwarz.k_p34.num}$ \\
        $\to\infty$ & $\to1$ & $\numval{result.schwarz.s_p1.num}$ & $\to\numval{result.schwarz.k_p1.num}$ \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{lemma}[Core Schwarzian Factorization]
    \label{lem:dynamics:core-schwarzian-factorization}
    This factorization belongs to the unpowered clean/deployed core~$Q$.
    It is retained as analytic compatibility evidence and as an input to
    the projected transformation formula
    \zcref{eq:dynamics:projected-schwarzian}, not as a deployed
    standing-safety theorem.

    Write the $\bleedparam=0$ core log-gain $\gainkernel{p}=a+b$ with
    $a=\invtemp\,(1-\sigma(\invtemp p))$ and $b=\operatorname{csch}2p$, and set
    $w=\coth2p$ (so $b^2=w^2-1$), $\sigma=\sigma(\invtemp p)$. The Schwarzian
    numerator $\Psi:=\gainkernel{p}^2\,\Schwarz[p]{Q_0}=KK''-\tfrac32(K')^2-\tfrac12K^4$
    (with $K=\gainkernel{p}$) splits exactly:
    \begin{equation}
        \Psi=\Psi_1+\Psi_2+ab\,B,\qquad
        \Psi_1=-\tfrac12\invtemp^2 a^2,\qquad
        \Psi_2=b^2\!\left(\tfrac32 b^2-2\right),
        \label{eq:dynamics:schwarzian-factorization}
    \end{equation}
    \begin{equation}
        B=6w^2-2+\invtemp^2(3\sigma-2)-6\invtemp\sigma w-3ab.
        \label{eq:dynamics:schwarzian-B}
    \end{equation}
    Both stand-alone factors are negative: $\Psi_1<0$ (the exact logistic anchor
    $\Schwarz{}\sigma\equiv-\tfrac12\invtemp^2$, \zcref{prop:dynamics:core-schwarzian-profile}),
    and $\Psi_2<0$ since $\tfrac32 b^2\le\tfrac32\operatorname{csch}^2 1 \numrel{const.dynamics.psi2_bound.num} <2$ on
    $[\tfrac12,1)$. The entire $\sqrt{\tanh}$/$\operatorname{csch}$ interaction the
    profile of \zcref{prop:dynamics:core-schwarzian-profile} leaves implicit is therefore
    confined to the single scalar $B$.
    \proofsketch{The exact identity holds for any $Q=\exp\!\int\!K$; expanding $K=a+b$
    with $a''=-\invtemp^2\sigma(1-2\sigma)a$ and $b''=4b(w^2+b^2)$ (each proportional
    to its own factor) collects all mixed terms into $ab\,B$, after the absorption
    $-\invtemp^2\sigma(1-2\sigma)-2a^2=\invtemp^2(3\sigma-2)$.}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Core Interaction Negativity]
    \label{thm:dynamics:core-interaction-negativity}
    For the unpowered core, $B<0$ on $[\tfrac12,1)$, attaining its maximum
    at $p=\tfrac12$ with $B(\tfrac12)=-0.1163$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    On the rectangle $(\sigma,w)\in[\tfrac23,\tfrac45]\times(\coth2,\coth1]$ enclosing
    the parametrised curve: $\partial_\sigma B=3\invtemp(\invtemp-2w+\sqrt{w^2-1})$,
    whose bracket has interior maximum $\invtemp-\sqrt3<0$, so $B$ decreases in
    $\sigma$ and is maximal at the gate value $\sigma=\tfrac23$ (where $3\sigma-2=0$).
    There $\partial_w B>0$ (a sum of increasing terms, positive at the left endpoint
    $w=\coth2$), so $B$ is maximal at $w=\coth1$. The corner value
    $B(\tfrac23,\coth1)=-0.1163<0$; the binding corner coincides with $p=\tfrac12$, so
    the relaxation is tight.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Core Schwarzian Negativity]
    \label{prop:dynamics:core-schwarzian-negativity}
    For the unpowered deployed core~$Q_\eta$ at
    $\invtemp\numrel{const.activation.beta_2ln2.exact}$ and $\bleedparam\numrel{const.graph.bleed.num}$:
    \[
        \Schwarz[p]{Q_\eta}<0
    \]
    on the core domain certified by \texttt{peer\_Bcert2}.  The proof is
    the verified interval branch-and-bound compatibility gate of that
    artifact, whose analytic route is
    \zcref{lem:dynamics:core-schwarzian-factorization,thm:dynamics:core-interaction-negativity}:
    at $\bleedparam=0$, $\Psi=\Psi_1+\Psi_2+ab\,B<0$ (all three summands
    negative, $a,b>0$), and the deployed factor
    $\sqrt{1-\bleedparam^2\tanh p}$ perturbs the sign nowhere on the
    certified domain.

    This is a result about~$Q_\eta$, not about the projected standing
    activation
    $g_{\mathrm{vch}}=(Q_\eta/Q_\eta(1))^{1/4}$.
    By \zcref{eq:dynamics:projected-schwarzian}, the fourth-root power
    adds a positive term and creates the sign partition of
    \zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-criticality-partition}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Core Margin Limit]
    \label{thm:dynamics:core-margin-limit}
    Define the unpowered core synchronized margin:
    \[
        M_Q(p)
        \coloneqq
        \Schwarz[p]{Q_\eta}
        -
        \frac32K_\eta(p)^2.
    \]
    Writing $\gainkernel{}=\tfrac{1}{2p}+a_0+a_1p+O(p^{3})$ with $a_0=\ln2$,
    $a_1=-(\ln^{2}2+\tfrac13)$ (the $p^{2}$ coefficient vanishes
    identically), the $p^{-2}$ and $p^{-1}$ singularities of the three terms
    of $M_Q$ cancel identically --- the $p^{-2}$ cancellation holds \emph{iff}
    the leading csch coefficient is $\tfrac12$ (the score-exponent lock,
    \zcref{rem:graph:score-exponent-uniqueness}); the $p^{-1}$ cancellation
    is structural, independent of $a_0$ --- and the clean-kernel limit is
    \[
        M_Q(0^{+})=-12a_0^{2}+6a_1=-(18\ln^{2}2+2) \numrel{const.dynamics.mq_clean_limit.num},\qquad
        M_Q'(0^{+})=80\ln^{3}2+16\ln2 \numrel{const.dynamics.mq_clean_slope.num}
    \]
    The deployed kernel shifts $a_0\to\ln2-\bleedparam^{2}/2$ (limit
    $\numval{const.dynamics.mq_deployed_limit.num}$).  This margin belongs to the unpowered core; the
    projected synchronized margin is a separate object
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-criticality-partition}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Core Margin Negativity]
    \label{prop:dynamics:core-margin-negativity}
    The unpowered core margin satisfies
    \[
        M_Q(p)<0
    \]
    on the certified core domain, in clean and deployed modes, under the
    former \texttt{peer\_Fcert} / compatibility gates preserved by
    \texttt{peer\_Bcert2} and \texttt{peer\_Fcert2}.

    The statement is retained for core analysis only.  It does not imply
    negativity of the projected margin
    \[
        M_{\mathrm{vch}}(p)
        =
        \Schwarz[p]{G}
        -
        \frac32\vouchpgain{p}^2.
    \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Core Criticality Scope]
    \label{rem:dynamics:core-criticality-scope}
    The old global negative-margin result belongs to the unpowered core
    and supplies no deployment gate for the projected standing map.

    For the projected activation, the activation certificate publishes a
    live-domain sign partition
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-criticality-partition}).  Moving the
    safety wall changes which portion of that partition is reachable and
    therefore changes the residual criticality classification.  It does
    not alter the primary deployment rule:
    \[
        \marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}\le1.
    \]

    Any floor, activation, coefficient, or depth change must update the
    pinned formula edition and re-run the staged standing certificate
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Core Mode Split]
    \label{rem:dynamics:core-mode-split}
    The old \condPfour{} and \condPfourNS{} conditions were derived for
    the unpowered core and its former oscillator reduction.  They remain
    useful as core normal-form diagnostics but are not standing
    conditions for the projected map.

    For the projected activation, the synchronized one-dimensional
    criterion is the sign of:
    \[
        M_{\mathrm{vch}}(p)
        =
        \Schwarz[p]{G}
        -
        \frac32\vouchpgain{p}^2.
    \]
    The transverse pitchfork and Neimark--Sacker coefficients still
    require their center-manifold 2-jet offsets and are not determined by
    the synchronized margin alone
    (\zcref{subsec:dynamics:quarantined-residuals}).

    The global core mode verdict is therefore replaced by:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item the certified projected synchronized sign partition
              (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-criticality-partition});
        \item motif-specific exact onset formulas using
              $\vouchgain{x^\ast}$;
        \item the binding clipped-row contraction certificate
              (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}).
    \end{itemize}
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Responsive Vouch Criticality Partition]
    \label{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-criticality-partition}
    Let
    \[
        G(p)
        =
        \left(
            \frac{Q_\eta(p)}{Q_\eta(1)}
        \right)^{1/4},
        \qquad
        \vouchpgain{p}
        =
        \frac{d}{dp}\log G(p).
    \]
    Define:
    \[
        S_{\mathrm{vch}}(p)
        \coloneqq
        \Schwarz[p]{G},
        \qquad
        M_{\mathrm{vch}}(p)
        \coloneqq
        S_{\mathrm{vch}}(p)
        -
        \frac32\vouchpgain{p}^2.
    \]

    On the published dynamically live domain beginning at the certified
    safety wall, \texttt{peer\_Bcert2} proves:
    \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
        \item a certified positive region for
              $S_{\mathrm{vch}}$ below a narrow zero-containing bracket
              $I_S$;
        \item a certified negative region for
              $S_{\mathrm{vch}}$ above~$I_S$;
        \item a certified positive region for
              $M_{\mathrm{vch}}$ below a narrow zero-containing bracket
              $I_M$;
        \item a certified negative region for
              $M_{\mathrm{vch}}$ above~$I_M$;
        \item no possible zero outside the published unresolved
              brackets.
    \end{enumerate}

    The high-precision scouts place the brackets near:
    \[
        p_S\approx0.53825,
        \qquad
        p_M\approx0.51637,
    \]
    corresponding approximately to:
    \[
        x_S\approx1.166,
        \qquad
        x_M\approx1.068.
    \]
    The exact certified unresolved intervals and proof-tree hashes are
    published in the \texttt{peer\_Bcert2} artifact.

    Certified positive and negative regions flanking each unresolved
    bracket imply at least one zero in that bracket by continuity.  The
    present certificate does not prove uniqueness inside either bracket.

    Wherever the one-dimensional synchronized normal-form criterion
    applies, $M_{\mathrm{vch}}<0$ supplies the former supercriticality
    verdict.  No such global verdict holds in the positive-margin region.
    Deployment safety on either side remains the conserved standing certificate.
\end{proposition}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Existence and the Rate Hull}
\label{subsec:dynamics:conserved-standing-safety}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The exact row data are the allocation derivatives of
\zcref{eq:epoch:rival-allocation-response}, propagated through the transport
by \zcref{lem:dynamics:transport-derivative-propagation}; the transported mass
of row~$i$ is $\transcount{i}$
(\zcref{def:epoch:conserved-standing-map}).

\begin{proposition}[Support Is State-Independent]
    \label{prop:dynamics:support-state-independence}
    The support of $\transport{\standingvector}$ does not depend on
    $\standingvector$ or on the accepted rung $\tiltstrength{k}$: it is fixed
    by the base allocation matrix together with the epoch-final ledger
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}).  Consequently the
    contributing sets, the widths $W_i$, the hull box $\hullbox{k}$, and any
    cluster-closure question are all decided \emph{before} the solve, on
    published data.

    This is what makes the safety analysis non-circular.  Every bound in this
    appendix is stated over a box whose definition would otherwise depend on
    the fixed point being bounded; because support is state-independent, the
    box is a datum and the certificate is a check on it, not a
    self-referential claim.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Conserved Standing Existence]
    \label{thm:dynamics:conserved-standing-existence}
    The rate-hull box
    \[
        \hullbox{k}
        \subseteq
        [\refrate{\min},\refrate{\max}]^n
    \]
    is forward-invariant under $\standingmapvector{k}{}$: every row is a
    weighted average of the reduced rates of its contributing sources
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}), and the weights are transported
    masses summing to the row's denominator.  The map is continuous on the box,
    so Brouwer's theorem gives a fixed point.

    Invariance requires \textbf{no certificate}.  It is a property of the
    mediant's shape rather than of any bound on its derivative, which is the
    one structural simplification Edition~5 buys over the staged construction:
    there is a box before there is a contraction, and the certificate has only
    one job.
\end{theorem}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Conserved Standing Certificate}
\label{subsec:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificates}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{theorem}[Certified Conserved Standing Uniqueness]
    \label{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}
    Let $\hullbox{k}$ be the rate-hull box of
    \zcref{thm:dynamics:conserved-standing-existence}.  If the certificate is
    valid,
    \[
        \marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}\le1,
        \qquad
        \marginfactor>1,
    \]
    then
    \begin{equation}
        \sup_{\standingvector\in\hullbox{k}}
            \norm{D\standingmapvector{k}{\standingvector}}_\infty
        \le
        \frac1{\marginfactor}
        <1 .
        \label{eq:dynamics:certified-contraction-norm}
    \end{equation}

    Consequently $\standingmapvector{k}{}$ has exactly one fixed point in
    $\hullbox{k}$, every orbit in the box converges geometrically to it, and no
    single-step non-normal amplification occurs in the infinity norm.  The
    memorylessness postulate is therefore a \emph{theorem} of the certified
    epoch, not an assumption about solver hygiene: the epoch has one standing
    answer, and no history can select among several
    (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-memorylessness}).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    $\standingcert{k}$ is a verified upper bound on the maximum absolute row
    sum of $D\standingmapvector{k}{}$ over $\hullbox{k}$
    (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}).  The margin
    inequality gives a global Lipschitz constant at most
    $1/\marginfactor<1$.  Banach's fixed-point theorem gives uniqueness and
    geometric convergence; the induced infinity norm gives the single-step
    amplification bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Initialization Independence]
    \label{cor:dynamics:standing-initialization-independence}
    Under a valid certificate the fixed point is unique in $\hullbox{k}$, so
    the solver's starting vector cannot change the result.  A previous epoch's
    solution, a cache, or any other warm start is a work-saving device and
    never a semantic input: it may change how long the solve takes and may not
    change what it returns.  This is the operational content of
    \zcref{post:epoch:standing-memorylessness}, and it is why a host may
    optimize freely without acquiring discretion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{definition}[Local Contributing Width]
    \label{def:dynamics:local-width}
    For target row~$i$, the \emph{contributing set} is
    $\set{u:\transportentry{u}{i}>0}$ --- the sources with positive
    transported mass into~$i$, which always contains~$i$ itself
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).  Let $R_i$ be the set of their
    reduced source rates $\refrate{u}$, and define
    \[
        W_i
        \coloneqq
        \max R_i-\min R_i,
        \qquad
        \locwidth{}
        \coloneqq
        \max_{i\ \mathrm{live}}W_i.
    \]

    Width is allocation-mass-blind but support-aware: the transported masses
    affect the exact certificate, while width records only the largest
    source-rate gap the row can see.  It is additive, never a hull ratio.

    Because support is fixed by the base matrix and the ledger
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation}), $\locwidth{}$ is
    computable \emph{before} the solve and is not a function of
    $\standingvector$ or of the accepted rung.  It is published per epoch
    beside $\standingcert{k}$, and the safety threshold's requirement~R2b ---
    that the published value dominate the realized one --- is checkable against
    that publication (\zcref{def:epoch:safety-threshold}).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Entrywise Allocation Derivative]
    \label{lem:dynamics:allocation-entrywise-derivative}
    For every hop~$r$, row~$u$, and entry~$v$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:dynamics:allocation-entrywise-derivative}
        \sum_j
        \left\lvert
            \frac{\partial\hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{\standingvector}}
                 {\partial \standingstate{j}}
        \right\rvert
        \;\le\;
        2\,\tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}\,\wallgaincap\,
        \hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{\standingvector} ,
    \end{equation}
    the derivative of an entry being bounded \emph{proportionally to that
    entry}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    By \zcref{eq:epoch:rival-allocation-response} and
    $\wallvouchgain{\standingstate{j}}\le\wallgaincap$,
    \[
        \sum_j\lvert\partial_j\hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{}\rvert
        \le
        \tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}\wallgaincap\,
        \hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{}
        \Bigl[
            \bigl(1-\hopalloc{r}{u}{v}{}\bigr)
            + \sum_{j\ne v}\hopalloc{r}{u}{j}{}
        \Bigr] .
    \]
    Each bracketed term is a sum of allocation shares of one row and so is at
    most one; their sum is at most two.  Both terms are present because
    allocation is rival and normalized: the first is what the entry gains when
    it is the rising recipient, the second is what it loses to every other
    recipient's rise.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Transport Derivative Propagation]
    \label{lem:dynamics:transport-derivative-propagation}
    Entrywise proportionality survives both the hop product and the depth
    mixture:
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:dynamics:transport-derivative-propagation}
        \sum_j
        \left\lvert
            \frac{\partial\transportentry{u}{i}}{\partial \standingstate{j}}
        \right\rvert
        \;\le\;
        2\,\wallgaincap\,\tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\,
        \transportentry{u}{i} .
    \end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    Apply the product rule to
    $\transportm{m}{\standingvector}=\hopmatrix{1}{}\cdots\hopmatrix{m}{}$.
    Each factor contributes its own
    \zcref{eq:dynamics:allocation-entrywise-derivative} bound, and because each
    bound is proportional to the factor entry, the products telescope: the
    $m$-hop entry inherits the same coefficient with the per-hop exponents
    summed, $\sum_{r\le m}\tiltexp{r}{\tiltstrength{k}}
    =\tiltcum{m}{\tiltstrength{k}}$.  Mixing over depths with the
    published depth mass is a convex combination, so the mixture inherits the
    largest coefficient present, at the deepest supported depth $\suppdepth$.
    Emission multiplies each row by the constant $\emission{u}$ and adds a
    constant to the diagonal, which scales both sides of the bound identically
    and leaves the diagonal only larger
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:emission-certificate-transfer}).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Hop-Profile Width Fence]
    \label{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}
    At any state of the solve, with $\locwidth{}$ the published contributing
    width,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}
        \norm{D\standingmapvector{k}{\standingvector}}_\infty
        \;\le\;
        2\,\wallgaincap\,\tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\,
        \locwidth{} .
    \end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    Differentiating the mediant
    \zcref{eq:epoch:conserved-standing-map}, the denominator terms cancel
    against the numerator's and leave
    \[
        \frac{\partial\standingmap{k}{i}{\standingvector}}
             {\partial \standingstate{j}}
        =
        \frac{\sum_u \partial_j\transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u}
              \bigl(\refrate{u}-\standingmap{k}{i}{\standingvector}\bigr)}
             {\sum_u \transportentry{u}{i}\,\actcount{u}} .
    \]
    The mediant lies in the row's contributing-rate hull
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}), so each
    $\lvert\refrate{u}-\standingmap{k}{i}{}\rvert\le W_i$.  Summing over~$j$
    and applying \zcref{eq:dynamics:transport-derivative-propagation} to each
    row entry gives the propagation coefficient times~$W_i$, the transported
    masses cancelling exactly against the denominator.  Take the maximum
    over live rows.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The Factor Two Is Intrinsic to Rival Allocation]
    \label{rem:dynamics:rival-factor-two}
    The fence constant is not an artifact of the profile shape, the depth mass,
    or the estimate: it is the price of \emph{normalized rival} allocation.
    When a recipient's standing rises, that recipient gains share \emph{and}
    every sibling and the self-share lose exactly what it gains
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:rival-allocation-response}); the $\infty$-norm row sum
    counts both movements, which is precisely the two bracketed terms of
    \zcref{lem:dynamics:allocation-entrywise-derivative}.

    The temptation to remove it comes from comparing against a \emph{one-sided}
    path-gain budget, which is not a contraction argument for any
    row-stochastic system.  A flat profile makes the difference visible: its
    one-sided budget clears the clean-gain bound while its two-sided volume is
    twice the prior screen's cap, and it fails --- correctly.  The honest pair
    of statements is: one-sided path gain budget
    $\tiltnorm{\tiltstrength{k}}\wallgaincap$; two-sided contraction screen
    $2\wallgaincap\tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\locwidth{}$.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Tilt-Profile Prior Screen]
    \label{cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}
    Assume the chartered safety-threshold rule
    $\loggain{\safefloor}=1/(\marginfactor\,\locwidth{})$, clean-gain
    domination (\zcref{prop:dynamics:clean-gain-domination}), and the width
    dominance premise R2b of \zcref{def:epoch:safety-threshold}.  Then the
    margined fence
    $\marginfactor\sup_{\hullbox{k}}
    \norm{D\standingmapvector{k}{}}_\infty\le1$ holds \emph{a priori} whenever
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}
        \tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\;\le\;2 ,
    \end{equation}
    independently of the graph.

    The screen is keyed to the cumulative profile at the \emph{deepest
    supported depth} $\suppdepth=\max\set{m:\depthmass{m}>0}$: any positive
    depth mass at the deepest hop, however small, prices the full profile
    volume.  Since $\tiltcum{m}{t}\le\tiltnorm{t}$, the cruder condition
    $\tiltnorm{t}\le\numval{const.standing.prior_screen_cap.num}$ is sufficient
    in every depth configuration, and the chartered profile satisfies it at
    full strength with slack
    $\numval{const.standing.profile_slack.exact}$, a factor
    $\numval{const.standing.screen_margin.num}$.

    The screen is \textbf{sufficient, never necessary}.  It certifies the
    chartered margin without inspecting the graph at all, and
    its failure at some rung establishes nothing whatever about that rung:
    the operative per-epoch gate is the certificate $\standingcert{k}$
    (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), which reads the
    graph --- through the contributing width, and through nothing else
    (\zcref{rem:dynamics:certificate-is-the-fence}).  The depth-mass weighted
    refinement $\sum_m\depthmass{m}\tiltcum{m}{t}$ is legitimate in neither:
    the per-depth transported masses it averages over are graph-dependent
    weights, and the certificate does not read them.  It belongs to the
    tighter object of \zcref{frontier:certificate-enclosure} and is available
    only if that is ever built.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
    Chain the three hypotheses.  The width fence
    (\zcref{eq:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}) bounds the supremum over the
    box by
    $\numval{const.standing.rival_factor_2.exact}\,\wallgaincap\,
    \tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\locwidth{}$; clean-gain domination
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:clean-gain-domination}) bounds the wall gain cap by
    $\actexponent\loggain{\safefloor}$; and the chartered rule replaces
    $\loggain{\safefloor}$ by $1/(\marginfactor\,\locwidth{})$.  Composing the
    three,
    \[
        \marginfactor\sup_{\hullbox{k}}
        \norm{D\standingmapvector{k}{}}_\infty
        \;\le\;
        \marginfactor\cdot
        \numval{const.standing.rival_factor_2.exact}\,\actexponent\,
        \frac{\tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\,\locwidth{}}
             {\marginfactor\,\locwidth{}}
        \;=\;
        \numval{const.standing.rival_factor_2.exact}\,\actexponent\,
        \tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}} ,
    \]
    the contributing width and the published margin both cancelling.  The right
    side is at most one exactly when the cumulative profile is at most
    $1/(\numval{const.standing.rival_factor_2.exact}\,\actexponent)$, which is
    \zcref{eq:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Where the Cap Comes From]
    \label{rem:dynamics:screen-cap-is-derived}
    The cap $\numval{const.standing.prior_screen_cap.exact}$ is not a chosen
    round number.  The proof leaves exactly two constants standing, and the cap
    is the reciprocal of their product: the two-sidedness of rival allocation
    (\zcref{rem:dynamics:rival-factor-two}) and the activation exponent
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:clean-gain-domination}).  Both are structural, so the
    cap moves only if one of them does.

    What is \emph{absent} is the point.  The contributing width cancels, which
    is what makes the screen graph-free; and the published margin cancels, so
    the screen does not tighten when the margin does.  A reader who expected a
    depth or a margin in the cap is looking for the retired per-stage screens,
    which were functions of both.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The Chartered Decay Is Determined, Not Calibrated]
    \label{rem:dynamics:chartered-decay-determined}
    The chartered shape is geometric: each hop's weight is half its
    predecessor's.  That halving is not one admissible choice among many, and
    saying so is the difference between a calibration item and a structural
    coupling.

    Read the screen as a condition on the decay of a geometric shape.  At a
    fixed supported depth the cumulative volume falls as the decay steepens, so
    the screen admits every shape decaying at least as fast as one critical
    value --- at the chartered depth that value is
    $\numval{const.standing.critical_decay.num}$, and the chartered halving
    sits just inside it.  But the critical value itself \emph{falls} as the
    supported depth grows: a shape admissible to one depth need not survive a
    single hop more.  Halving is the infimum of the whole family --- the unique
    geometric decay whose cumulative volume clears the cap at every depth at
    once, and it reaches the cap only in the unbounded limit.

    Two consequences are worth stating plainly.  The slack is not a remainder
    that happened to come out positive: at every depth it equals the deepest
    hop's own weight exactly, so the chartered profile clears the cap by
    precisely what one more hop would cost, and the chartered slack
    $\numval{const.standing.profile_slack.exact}$ is the deepest chartered
    weight for that reason and no other.  And a louder geometric shape does not
    merely lose the screen at the chartered depth: it loses it at every depth
    past a finite one, so it buys a reach ceiling along with its volume
    (\zcref{frontier:tilt-profile-charter}).
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Conserved Standing Certificate]
    \label{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}
    For epoch~$k$ at rung $\tiltstrength{k}$, the certificate is the evaluated
    fence
    \[
        \standingcert{k}
        \;=\;
        \numval{const.standing.rival_factor_2.exact}\,\wallgaincap\,
        \tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}\,\locwidth{} ,
        \qquad
        \text{valid iff } \marginfactor\,\standingcert{k}\le1 ,
    \]
    which bounds
    $\sup_{\standingvector\in\hullbox{k}}
    \norm{D\standingmapvector{k}{\standingvector}}_\infty$ over the free
    invariant rate-hull box $\hullbox{k}$
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}).  Box invariance requires no
    certificate of its own: every coordinate of the map is a weighted average
    of contributing rates (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).  The scalar
    and its verdict are \tagclosure{}.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[What the Certificate Can and Cannot See]
    \label{rem:dynamics:certificate-is-the-fence}
    The certificate is the fence \emph{evaluated}, not an enclosure of the
    supremum obtained by interval evaluation over the box.  Those are two
    different objects and the design commits to the first; a reader who finds
    the second described anywhere is reading a proposal, not the gate.

    It is sound, which is what a gate must be: the fence bounds the supremum,
    so a valid verdict is a true one.  It is cheap: entrywise proportionality
    collapses the supremum to a closed form whose only graph-dependent factor
    is the contributing width, so the certificate is one sweep of the base
    matrix's support and needs no fixed point --- a rung can be screened
    \emph{before} it is solved
    (\zcref{prop:scalability:standing-certificate-cost}).

    And it is coarse, which is worth naming rather than leaving to be
    discovered.  It reads the graph \emph{only} through the contributing
    width.  It cannot see how balanced a row's allocation is, how dense a
    mutual-allocation clique is, or where within the hull the rates sit: two
    epochs of identical width receive identical certificates however
    differently they are shaped.  So no fixture can be binding \emph{for this
    object} by virtue of its shape, and tooling guidance naming a shape would
    be describing a sensitivity the gate does not have.  The tighter object
    that would have it, and what would oblige the design to build it, is
    \zcref{frontier:certificate-enclosure}.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Emission Certificate Transfer]
    \label{prop:dynamics:emission-certificate-transfer}
    The emission diagonal $\emissionmat$ is constant throughout the standing
    solve, with entries in $[0,1]$, because $\emission{u}$ reads only the
    epoch-final ledger (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism}).
    Hence
    $\partial_j\transportentry{u}{i}
    =\emission{u}\,\partial_j\transportraw{ui}$ and, entrywise,
    $\emission{u}\transportraw{ui}\le\transportentry{u}{i}$ --- with equality
    off the diagonal, the diagonal only gaining.  The entrywise-proportionality
    bound, the hop-profile width fence, and the prior screen therefore transfer
    \textbf{verbatim, with identical constants}
    (\zcref{lem:dynamics:transport-derivative-propagation,%
    thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence,%
    cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}).  The contributing width can only
    shrink, since exactly the zero-balance sources leave other rows'
    contributing sets.

    The transfer consumes only that $\emissionmat$ is a \emph{constant diagonal
    with entries in $[0,1]$}: every ledger-measurable emission rule inherits it
    equally, and it is not evidence for the chartered rule over any other.
    Linearity in the rate is selected by the capacity semantics --- one act of
    history exported per $\safethresh$ of present balance --- and by minting no
    new constant, \emph{not} by certificate transfer.  What certificate
    transfer does exclude is a state-dependent coupling, an $\emissionmat$
    varying with $\transport{\standingvector}$, which would re-create exactly
    the certified obligation this design retired.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[Minimal Safe Safety Wall]
    \label{cor:dynamics:minimal-safe-wall}
    Since the clean full-depth gain $\loggain{x}$ is strictly
    decreasing (\zcref{lem:dynamics:monotone-gain}), the un-margined
    minimum safety wall at contributing width~$W$ is
    \[
        \minsafewall{W}
        =
        \loggaininv{1/W}.
    \]

    Under the chartered margin factor, the interim safety-threshold rule
    uses:
    \[
        \safefloor
        \ge
        \loggaininv{1/(\marginfactor W)}.
    \]

    Both forms carry no $\tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\cdot}$, and that is a
    \emph{choice of rung}, not an omission: they are the wall at the prior
    screen's cap, where
    $\numval{const.standing.rival_factor_2.exact}\actexponent
    \tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}=1$
    (\zcref{cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}).  At the chartered
    profile the cumulative tilt sits strictly below that cap, so the wall
    these give is conservative by the same
    $\numval{const.standing.screen_margin.num}$ the screen clears by.  Read
    as a wall for the \emph{accepted} rung it would be a silent pinning of
    the profile to a volume it does not have.

    The clean table certified by \texttt{peer\_Fcert2} is conservative
    for the exact deployed path gain
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:clean-gain-domination}).
\end{corollary}



\begin{theorem}[Finite Max-Envelope Lipschitz Bound]
    \label{thm:dynamics:finite-max-envelope-lipschitz}
    Let $\{F_\sigma\}$ be a finite family of maps with common Lipschitz
    constant at most~$c$ on a common box.  Then their pointwise scalar max
    envelopes are also $c$-Lipschitz wherever the same nonnegative output
    coordinate is selected.

    The standing map does not differentiate any such envelope: conserved
    allocation apportions rather than selects, so no maximum is taken inside
    it.  The result is retained for compiler robustness, raw max diagnostics,
    and any future implementation that does evaluate maxima --- none of which
    is on the certified path.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
    From $|\max(u,v)-\max(u',v')|\le\max(|u-u'|,|v-v'|)$, the pointwise
    $\max$ of $c$-Lipschitz scalar maps is $c$-Lipschitz; the bound is
    coordinate-wise and requires the same output coordinate to be
    compared on both sides.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Quarantined Residual Questions}
\label{subsec:dynamics:quarantined-residuals}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The Edition-3 oscillator, onset, and drift apparatus is not retained as
normative Edition-4 dynamics.  Each result assumed a prior standing
family or a single monolithic selected-path map and must be rederived,
with explicit scope, before it can return.  The open questions are:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item the circulant oscillator and its flip / pitchfork /
          Neimark--Sacker onset classifications require rederivation on a
          \emph{fixed responsive} depth-three or depth-four stage cell;
          wall-crossing cells are nonsmooth and are not covered by the
          Schwarzian normal forms of
          \zcref{subsec:dynamics:responsive-criticality};
    \item the conserved map apportions over a whole row rather than
          selecting one path, so any circulant extremal transfer is an outer
          bound rather than an attained deployed threshold;
    \item constant-step ledger drift and its compensation algebra belong
          to approximate and incremental solvers
          (\zcref{subsec:dynamics:solver-decomposition}), not to the
          exact per-epoch equilibrium definition;
    \item non-normal transfer amplification is closed at every epoch
          whose conserved standing certificate clears the wall in the
          infinity norm (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate});
    \item contraction-free responsive cells --- where no stage certificate
          verifies yet no divergence is proved --- remain the sole
          residual research territory.
\end{itemize}

These questions are recorded for Appendix~G; no normative theorem in this
appendix depends on their resolution.

\section{Symbol Index}
\label{app:symbols}

This index distinguishes the current epoch's internal standing stages
from the one standing field published by the protocol.

Standing is calculated only at epoch closure.  The completed final epoch
state determines an certified conserved equilibrium, followed by
certified depth-three and depth-four delegated stages.  Only the highest
certified stage is published as epoch standing.  A stage map is
determined by the completed epoch state; any solver initialization within
the certified standing box converges to its unique fixed point.

The notation therefore separates:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item final published standing
          $\epochstanding{k}{i}$ and $\epochrefstanding{k}{i}$;
    \item internal stage standing $\standingstate{i}$,
          $h\in\{2,3,4\}$;
    \item the smooth responsive activation $\vouchactivation{x}$ and the
          deployed wall-clamped activation $\wallactivation{x}$;
    \item the conserved transport $\transport{\standingvector}$ and its
          entry form $\transportentry{u}{i}$;
    \item exact mathematical contraction factors and published verified
          row-certificate bounds.
\end{enumerate}

The raw Action Graph is available to feed, raw bridge, CAN, title,
payload, and signed diagnostic consumers.  Its raw path-view,
determinant, maturity, temporal damping, and raw double-cover state are
terminal defaults, not standing inputs.

A quantity that closes receives a glyph; a question that remains
semantic, architectural, or only bounded receives a label and no
protocol glyph.  Source-root eligibility, cross-target rivalry, target
consent, and delegated co-maximizer policy remain labelled frontiers
rather than scalars (\zcref{rem:comparator:structural-ceiling}).  The
shared ordered codomain $\R_{\geq0}$ --- the comparator's neutral frame,
the single line onto which all addresses are forced
(\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame}) --- likewise carries no glyph: it
is inhabited, never typeset.

Displayed decimals follow \zcref{rem:verification:numerical-rounding}:
formulas and verified enclosures are normative, while decimal examples
are shown only to the precision relevant to the claim.

One further rule governs the seam. A glyph imported across a layer seam must
re-pass the falsifiability test against its Layer~1 meaning.

binding standing-package values and validity verdicts are
