% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Stance Aggregation}
\label{subsec:verification:stance-aggregation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The Carol$\to$Profile$_A$ example has raw stance $(p_d,p_i)=(0.8,0.9)$.  Under
\zcref{def:epoch:net-stance}, subsequent same-author Opinion records alter only the
endorsement-flow projection; raw records remain visible to feed-ranking, CAN, and
settlement recognition.

\paragraph{Counter-edge to withdrawal.}
Carol appends a counter-edge $(-0.8,-0.9)$ to the same Profile. Net stance:
\[
    \netpd{\text{Carol}\to\mathrm{Profile}_A}=0,
    \qquad
    \netpi{\text{Carol}\to\mathrm{Profile}_A}=0.
\]
The effective edge has $\tilde w=0$, so
$\transportentry{\text{Carol}}{\text{Alice}}=0$ and Alice's standing returns to the
self-only value $\numval{fixture.seed.alice_rate.num}$. The revision is priced: Carol's
$\actcount{}$ increases from $12$ to $13$, so
$\commitrate{\text{Carol}}$ falls from $\numval{fixture.seed.carol_rate.exact} \numrel{fixture.seed.carol_rate.num}$ to $\numval{fixture.seed.carol_rate_revised.exact} \numrel{fixture.seed.carol_rate_revised.num}$. \okmark

\paragraph{Mixed overshoot.}
A further bundle with net stance $(-0.3,+0.4)$ has
$\detsign{}=-1$, so the double cover sends the canonical path to the
$\negreg{}$ register. The positive register at Alice is zero and
$\transportentry{\text{Carol}}{\text{Alice}}=0$: mixed-hostile overshoot is
parity-blocked exactly as an ordinary negative Opinion path is. \okmark

\paragraph{Symmetric overshoot.}
A bundle netted negative in both parameters, $(-0.3,-0.4)$, has
$\detsign{}=+1$ by the Quadrant Law
(\zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law}).  Under the vouch-gated projection it fails
\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution} and is omitted before the double cover BFS
runs.  Therefore
\[
    \transportentry{\text{Carol}}{\text{Alice}} = 0 .
\]
The edge remains a coherent record for terminal consumers, but it is not a
vouch and does not carry Carol's rate into Alice's standing. \okmark

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Proposal Edges and Payload-State Invariance}
\label{subsec:verification:proposals-and-payload}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\paragraph{Join Request.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:proposals:join-request}
Alice requests to join Chat $C$: $u = \numval{fixture.join.direct.exact}$, $f = \numval{fixture.join.indirect.exact}$, $\tau = \numval{fixture.join.maturity.exact}$.
Half-tier path-view: $\det \numrel{result.join.pv_det.num}$, $\detscore{} \numrel{result.join.detscore.num}$,
$\detsign{} = +1$. No Participant edge exists; Alice is not a member.

\paragraph{Invitation.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:proposals:invitation}
Bob invites Carol ($u = 0.8$, $f = 0.7$, $r = 0.8$, $\tau = 0$):
A-leg $\detscore{} \numrel{result.accept.detscore.num}$ (\tierhalf{}); T-leg $\det = \numval{const.graph.bleed.num} \times \numval{result.invite.core_pm.num}
\times (\numval{result.invite.core_pl.num} - \numval{result.invite.core_pm.num}) \numrel{result.invite.pv_det.num}$, $\detscore{} \numrel{result.invite.detscore.num}$,
$\detsign{} = +1$ (\tiermarginal{}). Conduit weight to Carol at
$\standing{\text{Carol}} = \numval{fixture.seed.carol_rate.num}$: $\numval{result.accept.detscore.num} \times \numval{result.invite.detscore.num} \times
\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} \numrel{result.invite.conduit.num}$ --- ${\sim}20\times$
weaker than the canonical 2-hop endorsement (\okmark,
\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}). At $\standing{} = 0$ the terminal
Reputation factor is $0$ and the conduit transmits nothing (\okmark).

\paragraph{Payload-state invariance.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:proposals:payload-invariance}
Take Opinion $e_2$ with a non-empty payload; compute all Layer~1
quantities; move the payload to the reduced state; recompute. Every value
--- $\symbf{\Psi}$, $\detsign{}$, $\dampedweight{}$, CAN values,
$\standing{}$, $\titlecert{}$ --- is bit-identical
(\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}). \okmark

\paragraph{Review of Type and Message.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:proposals:review-universality}
Leg tensors depend only on parameters and domain/mask, never on the
middle-node type (\zcref{post:nodes:canonical-tensor-pipeline}), so the
reference Review values carry over verbatim to Type and Message targets:
A-leg $\detscore{} \numrel{result.e3.detscore.num}$ (\tierfull{}), T-leg $\detscore{} \numrel{result.e4.detscore.num}$
(\tiermarginal{}), norms $\numval{result.e3.frobenius.num}/\numval{result.e4.frobenius.num}$
(\zcref{tbl:verification:reference-edges}). No standing quantity moves
(\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}). \okmark

\paragraph{Reference transposition.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:proposals:reference}
Reference is Review with legs transposed
(\zcref{edge:nodes:hyper-reference}), so at the reference parameters
$(e,f) = (0.7, 0.8)$ its leg values carry over from
\zcref{tbl:verification:reference-edges} verbatim, swapped: the A-leg
(roles $(f,e) = (0.8,0.7)$, Epistemic) reproduces $e_4$'s values ---
$\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \numrel{result.e4.frobenius.num}$, $\detscore{} \numrel{result.e4.detscore.num}$, \tiermarginal{}
--- and the T-leg (roles $(e,f) = (0.7,0.8)$, Tribal full) reproduces
$e_3$'s --- $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \numrel{result.e3.frobenius.num}$, $\detscore{} \numrel{result.e3.detscore.num}$,
\tierfull{}. Nothing is minted; no genesis row exists to check. Vouch
switch: with a Profile target and positive stance the T-leg vouches
(\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}); at $(e,f) = (-0.7,-0.8)$ the T-leg
carries $\detsign{} = +1$ by the Quadrant Law yet is projection-excluded
--- coherent condemnation cites, but never vouches
(\zcref{rem:nodes:reference-author-allocation}). \okmark

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Authored-Act Ownership}
\label{subsec:verification:act-ownership}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

These fixtures verify that the authored act owns payload, dependencies, causal
references, approval, debit, count, stamp, and time, and that an edge projection
owns only its incidence and role
(\zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology,rem:graph:act-ownership-invariant}).

\paragraph{Binary projection.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:binary-projection}
A binary act $q$ (Opinion $e_2$) projects to exactly one edge:
$\abs{\actedges{q}} = 1$ (\okmark).

\paragraph{Hyper-edge projection.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:hyper-projection}
The Invitation act $q$ projects to exactly two edges with distinct roles:
$\abs{\actedges{q}} = 2$ and $\set{\edgerole{e} : e\in\actedges{q}} = \set{A,T}$
(\okmark, \zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection}).

\paragraph{One act time.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:one-time}
Both projections of the Invitation inherit one act time:
$\acttime{\actof{e_A}} = \acttime{\actof{e_T}} = \acttime{q}$. This is
inheritance from the parent act, not two equal edge-owned clocks (\okmark,
\zcref{def:graph:act-incidence-causality}).

\paragraph{One payload lifecycle.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:one-payload}
Tombstoning $\actpayload{q}$ of a hyper-edge act leaves both edge projections ---
their identifiers, incidence, roles, parameter renderings, and act time ---
invariant (\okmark, \zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}).

\paragraph{One dependency projection.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:one-dependency}
Neither the A- nor the T-projection can carry a dependency commitment divergent
from the act's single $\actdepscommit{q}$: there is one act-owned
$\actdeps{q}$ (\okmark, \zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection}).

\paragraph{No projection-level dependency.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:no-leg-dependency}
A declared dependency naming an edge-projection identifier $\edgeid{e_A}$ rather
than the act identifier $\actid{q}$ is formation-invalid: dependencies name acts
(\okmark, \zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection}).

\paragraph{One approval witness.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:one-approval}
Altering either edge projection makes it fail verification against the approved
act's witness $\approvewitness{q}$: there is one approval per act (\okmark,
\zcref{def:graph:approval-witness}).

\paragraph{One debit and one count.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:one-debit}
A hyper-edge act contributes two edge projections to $\edgeincrement{k}$ but one
increment to its author's count and one $\safethresh$-debit:
$\Delta N_{\operatorname{author}(q)} = 1$ and
$\Delta b_{\operatorname{author}(q)} = -\safethresh$ (\okmark,
\zcref{cor:graph:hyper-act-indivisibility}).

\paragraph{One stamp.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:one-stamp}
If an implementation serializes the act stamp beside both edge projections, both
resolve to the single $\actstamp{q}$, and W2b counts it once (\okmark,
\zcref{def:epoch:final-act-stamps}).

\paragraph{Settlement act reference.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:settlement-reference}
The Accept and Ratify resolve the Bid \emph{act} identifier
$\actid{q_{\mathrm{Bid}}}$, not the Bid/T edge-projection key; Ratify also
resolves the exact Accept act id (\okmark,
\zcref{def:graph:settlement-act-reference}).

\paragraph{Derived-edge exception.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:ownership:derived-edge}
A derived Reputation Self-edge has no parent authored act, no payload, no
dependency projection, and no act time; it resolves only to its epoch boundary
slot $\boundaryslot{k}$ (\okmark, \zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Departure Lifecycle and Control Inertness}
\label{subsec:verification:membership-lifecycle}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\paragraph{Control tensor.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:membership:control-tensor}
Leave and both De-invite legs share the fixed-parameter Minimal slice
($p_d = p_i = 1$): $\fpm{1} \numrel{result.control.core_pm.num}$, $\fpl{1} \numrel{result.control.core_pl.num}$,
$\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \numrel{result.control.frobenius.num}$; path view
$\det = \bleedparam(\numval{result.control.core_pm.num} \times \numval{result.control.core_pl.num} - \bleedparam \times \numval{result.control.core_pm.num}^2)
\numrel{result.control.pv_det.num}$, $\detscore{} \numrel{result.control.detscore.num}$, $\detsign{} = +1$
(forced).  At $\tau = 0$: $\dampedweight{} \numrel{result.control.weight.num}$ --- the strongest
\tiermarginal{} record, still ${\sim}2.2\times$ below the weakest
\tierfull{} reference edge. \okmark

\paragraph{Membership fold.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:membership:fold}
Alice authors Participant $\to$ Chat~$C$ ($T = 10$), Leave ($T = 12$),
Participant ($T = 15$).  $M(\text{Alice}, C)$ is a $\prec$-chain;
$\prec$-maximal is the $T = 15$ Participant:
$\operatorname{member} = \text{true}$.  Truncating at $T = 12$:
$\operatorname{member} = \text{false}$.  Latest-record-wins, order-free.
\okmark

\paragraph{Vacuous records are inert.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:membership:vacuous}
Dave (never a member) authors Leave $\to$ $C$: the record appends
(both gates pass), $M(\text{Dave},C)$'s maximal element is a Leave,
$\operatorname{member} = \text{false}$ --- unchanged.  Dave then
De-invites Carol from a Chat neither has touched: the record appends;
the canonical fold ignores it (Dave is in no authority set); every
$\transportentry{}{}$ and $\standing{}$ value is bit-identical (control class
excluded from the projection,
\zcref{rem:epoch:control-acts-resolve-to-self}). \okmark

\paragraph{Expulsion never endorses.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:control-self-retention}
Bob De-invites Carol from Chat~$C$.  The candidate 3-hop path
Bob $\to C \to \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Carol}} \to$ Carol has feed
weight $\numval{result.control.weight.num} \times \numval{result.control.weight.num} \times
\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}(0.333) \approx 0.006$ --- attention
only.  In the endorsement-flow projection both De-invite legs are
absent, so $\transportentry{\text{Bob}}{\text{Carol}}$ is computed without
them: no standing transfer, in either quadrant reading. \okmark

\paragraph{Inviter revocation.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:membership:inviter-revocation}
Bob's Invitation of Carol into $C$ carries the conduit weight
$\numrel{result.invite.conduit.num}$ (\zcref{ver:proposals:invitation}).  Bob authors a
$\prec$-later De-invite toward $(C, \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Carol}})$:
$R(\text{Bob}, C, \text{Carol})$'s maximal element is the De-invite,
the Invitation bundle is suppressed, conduit contribution $= 0$.  A
still-later Invitation re-establishes it.  Each toggle costs an action:
$\actcount{\text{Bob}}$ rises, $\commitrate{\text{Bob}}$ falls
irrevocably.  Alice's independent Invitation of Carol into the same
Chat is untouched (per-author suppression only). \okmark

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Two-Gate Verification}
\label{subsec:verification:two-gate}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Fix the chartered reference
$(\numeraire,\polfloor,\marginfactor)=(0.10,1,1.25)$, so
$\safethresh \numrel{const.epoch.safethresh.num}$, $\safefloor \numrel{const.epoch.safefloor.num}$, and $\partfloor=1$.

\paragraph{W1 debit.}
Alice with $\burnbal{\text{Alice}}=2.47193$ writes one action. The ledger
updates
\[
    \burnbal{\text{Alice}}\gets 2.47193-\numval{const.epoch.safethresh.num},
    \qquad \actcount{\text{Alice}}\gets \actcount{\text{Alice}}+1.
\]
No stamp, door, or average moves a balance. \okmark

\paragraph{W2a individual safety.}
A record with $\actstamp{}=0.56$ clears at the reference safety floor but
fails after the compensated future value $\safefloor'=0.297147$ in the
exhibit's scaled coordinates; W2a is per-record and never averaged. \okmark

\paragraph{W2b average door.}
Band actors with $\safefloor\le\actstamp{}<\partfloor$ are writable only
when the epoch stamp clears the door. The reference door headroom is
$\doorheadroom{k}=4.72107$, and band packing is headroom-limited. \okmark

\paragraph{Translation law.}
The post-debit joint standing rows satisfy exact translation by
$\safefloor$ at fixed weights; residuals are below $6\times10^{-42}$ in the
Edition-4 run. \okmark

\subsection{Reference Constants}
\label{subsec:verification:reference-constants}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{table}[h!]
    \centering
    \caption{Reference constants.  Decimal values are rounded
    under \zcref{rem:verification:numerical-rounding}; defining formulas
    are normative.}
    \label{tbl:verification:reference-constants}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}l c l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Quantity} & \textbf{Reference value} & \textbf{Role} \\
        \midrule
        $L_{\mathrm{feed}}$ & $4$ & raw Action-Graph depth \\
        $\hopmax$ & $4$ & standing transport depth \\
        $\invtemp$ & $\approx1.386$ & inverse temperature \\
        $\bleedparam$ & $0.05$ & bleed \\
        $Q(1)$ & $\numrel{const.activation.qcore_cap.num}$ & activation normalization \\
        $\numeraire$ & $0.1$ & reserve/action num\'eraire \\
        $\marginfactor$ & $5/4$ & chartered safety margin \\
        $\safethresh$ & $\numrel{const.epoch.safethresh.num}$ & per-act debit \\
        $\safefloor$ & $\numrel{const.epoch.safefloor.num}$ & safety wall \\
        $\polfloor$ & $1$ & policy door \\
        $\partfloor$ & $1$ & effective door \\
        \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

The debit is defined by the width-fence inversion at the reference
$\locwidth{}\numrel{fixture.wall.width.num}$,
\[
    \safethresh
    =
    \numeraire\,\loggaininv{1/(\marginfactor\locwidth{})},
    \qquad
    \safefloor=\safethresh/\numeraire,
\]
so the printed decimals are rounded images of this formula, not independent
data.  The prior screen is exact and profile-only:
\[
    \tiltcum{\suppdepth}{\tiltstrength{k}}
    \le\numval{const.standing.prior_screen_cap.num},
    \qquad
    \tiltnorm{1}\numrel{const.standing.profile_l1.num},
\]
so the chartered profile clears the cap at full strength with margin.  Neither
number is a function of depth or of the margin factor, which is the content of
the screen being graph-free: Edition~4 published one screen per stage, each
scaled by $h/(4\marginfactor)$, because each stage had its own map to screen.

\subsection{Conserved Standing Fixtures}
\label{subsec:verification:conserved-standing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Edition~4 verified three stages here: an exact depth-two envelope, then a
delegated depth-three stage, then depth-four, each with its own selection,
schedule, equilibrium and certificate.  There is one solve now, so there is one
equilibrium to verify --- and a much larger obligation to verify the properties
that make it the \emph{right} one.

The fixtures below are stated as obligations on the verification suite rather
than as reported values: the reference-graph numbers they consume are
regenerated with the values pipeline
(\zcref{subsec:verification:reference-constants}), and no result identifier is
minted from a number inherited across the edition boundary.

\paragraph{The operator is what it claims to be.}
Row sums are one at random trial states, not merely at the fixed point
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:conservation}); the transported-mass
weighted mean of a closed cluster equals its ledger ratio, with an
$\varepsilon$-leakage case for the near-closed regime
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-cluster-rate}); a community at one
common rate stands exactly there under every profile, depth mass and rung
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:equal-rate-invariance}); and the support of
the transport is the one the base matrix predicts before the solve
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:support-preservation}).

\paragraph{The inputs are read once, and read right.}
Every accepted act is weighed exactly once, a hyper-edge as one act
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:universal-act-accounting}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:hyper-act-single-accounting}); domain
profiles sum to one so no act counts twice across its projections
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:domain-proportionality}); a settled
transfer stays settled when a later epoch resells
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:settlement-event-persistence}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:title-coupling}); control acts resolve to
their author and still cost what any act costs
(\zcref{ver:standing:control-self-retention}); an
artifact-heavy author and a vouch-only author at equal ledgers differ exactly
as retention predicts
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:artifact-heavy-author}); and every
transporting source carries $\actcount{u}\ge1$ in a fresh-registration epoch
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:anchored-count-invariant}).

\paragraph{Order and history are invisible.}
Standing is invariant under every dependency-compliant permutation of the act
sequence (\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:epoch-permutation-invariance}), and
identical from every start in the box, so a warm start changes duration and
never result (\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:warm-start-independence}).

\paragraph{Measuring does not spend.}
Every ledger entry the solve reads is bit-identical after it: the largest
change to any balance or action count across a complete solve is
$\numval{result.standing.ledger_defect.num}$
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:ledger-invariance}).  The fixture snapshots
the ledger, solves, and compares entry by entry, and its value is
\emph{exactly} zero rather than zero to working precision --- there is no
arithmetic here to be imprecise about, which is the whole content of
\zcref{post:epoch:standing-is-measurement}.  An implementation that debited,
credited or renormalized a count while solving would move this number and no
other check in this suite would notice.

\paragraph{Self-resolved activity crowds out export.}
One author with a single endorsement allocates
$\numval{result.crowding.bare.num}$ of its conserved unit outward with no
self-resolved activity, and $\numval{result.crowding.loaded.num}$ once three
units of artifact coefficient land on its own diagonal --- a
$\numval{result.crowding.drop.num}$ fraction of the outward share consumed
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:artifact-crowding}).  The reference epoch
contains no self-resolved cell, so this is its own two-Actor fixture; without
it \zcref{rem:epoch:artifact-activity-crowds-out-export} would rest on the
definition alone.

\paragraph{The tilt is the only voice, and it fades.}
Relative allocation odds between two recipients depend only on their base
scores and activations
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:relative-odds}); the rival-share
derivatives sum to zero across a row and vanish below the wall
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:rival-share-derivatives}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:wall-flatness}); hop one is
source-adjacent, so the same authored row renders at different exponents for
different transported mass
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:hop-order-convention}); and no source
improves its own standing by re-apportioning its own retention
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:self-retention-manipulation}).

\paragraph{Nothing binds beyond proof.}
The anchor rung is a bit-exact constant map
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:no-tilt-anchor}); the backoff accepts the
greatest certifying rung and each rung is certified on its own, never inherited
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:tilt-backoff}); the chartered profile
clears the prior screen with margin
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:prior-screen}); and the certificate binds
where \zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate} says it does --- a
dense mutual-allocation clique just above the wall, balanced rows, wide rate
spread, two-cycles at hop one
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:near-wall-clique}).

\paragraph{Emission relocates and never deletes.}
The emitted operator's rows still sum to one
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-conservation}); a zero-balance
source has an identity row and inbound flow to it is unaffected
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-zero-anchor}); a depleted
intermediary relays a solvent source at full strength
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-relay}); the emission fraction is
one exactly at the wall and linear below it, with the kink in ledger space
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-wall-symmetry}); the certified
norm matches the unmodified screen on every fixture
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-certificate-transfer}); and at
$\tiltstrength{k}=0$ the emitted map is bit-exact constant
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-no-tilt}).

Three emission fixtures carry corrections that must land with them.  The export
bound is checked on the depleted giant, and the ballast witness is
\emph{recomputed} under the chartered operator rather than inherited from the
frontier-era probe, which was written against a description the no-op argument
later refuted (\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-export-bound}).
Rate preservation is stated in aggregate form --- the exported pair equals
$\emission{u}(\burnbal{u},\actcount{u})$ summed over non-self columns ---
because the per-entry ratio is the source rate under \emph{any} scalar scaling
and so tests nothing
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-rate-preservation}).  And
self-inertia is fixtured directly: a depleted actor under strong inbound
regard, emitted against full-pair, so the behavioural change is measured rather
than asserted (\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-self-inertia}).

\paragraph{Splitting, which is not closed.}
Whale-split and giant-split cases confirm no export is gained by fragmenting an
address (\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:emission-split}).  These are
\emph{witnesses, not a theorem}: Actor-splitting invariance remains a nonclaim
(\zcref{frontier:allocation-split-invariance}), and a passing fixture must not
be cited as if it discharged it
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:actor-splitting}).

\paragraph{Downstream.}
Terminal consumers regress against the published standing only
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:terminal-regression}), and the canonical
encoding round-trips
(\phantomsection\label{ver:standing:canonical-encoding}).\okmark

\subsection{Pathological Graph Fixtures}
\label{subsec:verification:pathological-graphs}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\emph{Zero-source multiplicity.} The unclamped activation admits a zero branch
and a supported branch; under the wall clamp with positive external source the
supported branch is unique in the fixture, and the certificate covers the kink
by Clarke interval rather than by choosing a branch.
\phantomsection\label{ver:pathology:clamped-zero-source-branch}

\emph{Zero-rate cohort.} A mutually vouching zero-rate cohort has
$\max_i x_i=0$.
\phantomsection\label{ver:pathology:zero-rate-cohort}

\emph{Wall kink.} The generalized reduced-standing log-derivative at the wall
is enclosed by $\partial\log\wallactivation{\safefloor}\subseteq[0,\numval{result.wall.gain.num}]$.
\phantomsection\label{ver:pathology:wall-kink}

\emph{Symmetric diamond.} Two symmetric routes carry equal transported mass;
the relevant claim is exact symmetry of the resulting shares, which under
apportionment is an identity rather than a tie between selectable witnesses.
\phantomsection\label{ver:pathology:symmetric-apportionment}

\emph{Equal-rate field.} On a common source rate, standing equals that rate
exactly, the Jacobian vanishes, and the numerical residual is zero at working
precision.
\phantomsection\label{ver:pathology:equal-rate-field}

\emph{Depleted-source ballast.} This fixture is a \emph{certified result}
rather than a probe: source emission is chartered
(\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}) and its safety transfers
(\zcref{prop:dynamics:emission-certificate-transfer}).

The reference graph has no faded source, so the witness carries its own
two-Actor fixture: a solvent target at $(\burnbal{},\actcount{})=(1.4,10)$ and
a depleted giant at $(0.2,5000)$ --- huge history, no backing --- each retaining
$\selfretention$ and allocating one unit-coefficient act to the other.  The
giant's emission fraction is
$\numval{result.ballast.giant_emission.num}$.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Target's reduced standing} & \\
    \midrule
    full pair, no emission & $\numval{result.ballast.full_pair.num}$ \\
    emitted                & $\numval{result.ballast.emitted.num}$ \\
    ratio                  & $\numval{result.ballast.lift.num}$ \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The inherited $0.05\to0.099$ pair is deliberately \textbf{not} carried across
and is not reproduced.  It was computed against the frontier-era description of
the candidate rule --- the pre-normalization row scaling the no-op argument
later refuted --- and against an unspecified fixture, so it states a number
about an operator nobody chartered on a graph nobody published.  Both halves
had to be replaced, and the recomputed ratio is far larger because this
fixture's giant is far heavier relative to its target.  The claim the witness
supports is the qualitative one and always was: unbacked history crushes a
target under full-pair transport, and emission removes almost all of it.

What remains is not removed, and that residual is the export bound being
\emph{tight}.  The giant still contributes
$\numrel{result.ballast.export_slack.num}$ of denominator mass --- exactly
half its ceiling $\min(\actcount{u},\burnbal{u}/\safethresh)$, since half its
row points outward --- so \zcref{thm:epoch:emission-export-bound} holds with
the slack a published number rather than an asserted inequality.  A depleted
Actor is not silenced; it is charged, and what it can still pay for still
speaks.
\phantomsection\label{ver:pathology:depleted-source-ballast}\okmark

\subsection{Bridge Campaign Walkthrough}
\label{subsec:verification:bridge-campaign-walkthrough}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This section exercises the bridge campaign scalar
(\zcref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar}) on the reference graph
(\zcref{subsec:verification:reference-graph}) extended with three
hypothetical Opinion edges.  All channel values use the damped weight
$\dampedweight{e}$ (\zcref{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight}); consent is read
at the Profile node (\zcref{def:bridge:consent}).

\paragraph{Setup.}
Actors: Alice ($r = 0.300$), Bob ($r = 0.250$), Carol ($r = 0.333$),
Dave ($r = 0.200$); $\standing{} = r_i$ for all (no inter-actor edges in the
base graph).  All reference-graph edges have $\detsign{e} = +1$
(\zcref{tbl:verification:tensor-summary}), so $\posgraph = G$.
\textbf{Campaign:} Dave ($A = a_4$) targets Carol ($T = a_3$),
$w_1 = 1$.

\paragraph{Hypothetical edges} (all $\tau = 0$, $\detsign{} = +1$):
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l c c c@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Edge} & $p_d$ & $p_i$ & $\dampedweight{}$ \\
    \midrule
    Carol $\to \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}$ (Opinion)
        & $\numval{fixture.bridge_ca.direct.exact}$ & $\numval{fixture.bridge_ca.indirect.exact}$ & $\numval{result.bridge_ca.weight.num}$ \\
    Alice $\to \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Dave}}$ (Opinion)
        & $\numval{fixture.bridge_ad.direct.exact}$ & $\numval{fixture.bridge_ad.indirect.exact}$ & $\numval{result.bridge_ad.weight.num}$ \\
    Dave $\to \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}$ (Opinion)
        & $\numval{fixture.bridge_da.direct.exact}$ & $\numval{fixture.bridge_da.indirect.exact}$ & $\numval{result.bridge_da.weight.num}$ \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The Reputation-component weights are the raw \zcref{app:verification}
reference values:
$\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep},\text{Alice}}} \numrel{result.e1r.weight.num}$ (at
$\standing{} = \numval{fixture.seed.alice_rate.num}$, i.e.\ $\hat\alpha = 3$, $\tau = 0.50$),
$\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep},\text{Dave}}} \numrel{result.rep_dave.weight.num}$ (at
$\standing{} = \numval{fixture.seed.dave_rate.num}$, i.e.\ $\hat\alpha = 2$, $\tau = 0.50$; the $\tau = 0$ value $\numval{result.rep_dave.detscore.num}$ from
the raw temporal factor is
$\sqrt{1+\tau^2}\,\boltzfactor{\tentropy{}} = \numval{result.rep_dave.coherence.num} \times \numval{result.rep_dave.boltz.num}$).

\paragraph{Channel 1 --- affinity $\affinity{\text{Carol}, B}$.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:bridge:affinity}
Max-product BFS seeded at Carol on $\posgraph$, depth $\leq 3$, read at
the actor node.
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item $B = \text{Alice}$:
          Carol $\to \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}
          \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Rep}} \text{Alice}$, weight
          $\numval{result.bridge_ca.weight.num} \times \numval{result.e1r.weight.num} \numrel{result.bridge.affinity.num}$.  The terminal Reputation hop is
          on the delivery circuit (\zcref{rem:bridge:reputation-single-traversal}).
    \item $B = \text{Bob}$: no positive path Carol\,$\to$\,Bob;
          $\affinity{} = 0$.
\end{itemize}
Optimal bridge: $\optbridge{1} = \text{Alice}$,
$\affinity{\text{Carol}, \text{Alice}} \numrel{result.bridge.affinity.num}$.

\paragraph{Channel 2 --- endorsement $\endorsement{\text{Alice}, \text{Dave}}$.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:bridge:endorsement}
Path Alice $\xrightarrow{e_{\mathrm{Op}}} \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Dave}}
\xrightarrow{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} \text{Dave}$:
\[
    \endorsement{\text{Alice}, \text{Dave}}
    = (+1) \cdot \numval{result.bridge_ad.weight.num} \cdot \numval{result.rep_dave.weight.num} \numrel{result.bridge.endorsement.num}.
\]
Sign $=\operatorname{sgn}(p_d(e_{\mathrm{Op}}))=+1$ (Alice vouches for Dave).

\paragraph{Channel 3 --- consent $\consent{\text{Dave}, \text{Alice}}$,
read at $\mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}$.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:bridge:consent}
Double-cover BFS seeded at Dave \textbf{on the raw snapshot}
(\zcref{def:bridge:consent}; a Layer-2 canonical-default computation),
registers read at $\mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}$ (\emph{not} at the
actor --- the Reputation hop is excluded, \zcref{def:bridge:consent}).
On this reference graph the raw and vouch-gated registers coincide; they
diverge exactly when coherent-hostile actor-directed records exist
(\zcref{rem:bridge:consent-cost}). Dave's Opinion reaches
$\mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}$ directly:
\[
    \posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}} = \numval{result.bridge_da.weight.num},
    \qquad
    \negreg{\mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}} = 0,
    \qquad
    \consent{\text{Dave}, \text{Alice}} = \max(0,\, \numval{result.bridge_da.weight.num}) = \numval{result.bridge_da.weight.num}.
\]
If Dave instead has a direct net stance
$\netpd{\text{Dave}\to\mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}}<0$, the direct-stance
veto of \zcref{def:bridge:consent} sets
$\consent{\text{Dave},\text{Alice}}=0$ regardless of the register
difference.  A coherent condemnation $(-,-)$ therefore no longer counts as
consent; it is vetoed by stance. \okmark

\paragraph{Circuit quality and campaign scalar.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:bridge:circuit}
\[
    \circqual{\text{Carol}, \text{Alice}, \text{Dave}}
    = \numval{result.bridge.affinity.num} \times \numval{result.bridge.endorsement.num} \times \numval{result.bridge_da.weight.num}
    \numrel{result.bridge.circqual.num},
    \qquad
    \campaignscalar{\text{Dave}} = 1.0 \times \numval{result.bridge.circqual.num}
    = \numval{result.bridge.circqual.num}.
\]
The gate $\Delta\campaignscalar{} > 0$ clears.

\paragraph{Attribution.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:bridge:attribution}
Realizing path
$\realizingpath{1} = (\text{Carol} \to \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}
\to \text{Alice} \to \mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Dave}} \to \text{Dave})$.
Creditable set $\creditset{\realizingpath{1}} = \set{\text{Alice}}$:
Carol is the excluded source endpoint, the Profile nodes are passive, Dave
is the buyer.  Alice (the bridge) receives $S_{\text{Alice}} = 1.0$ as the
sole interior $V_u$ node on the sole target's realizing path
(\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-centrality}).

\paragraph{Reputation single-traversal check.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:bridge:reputation-check}
Alice's reputation weight ($\numval{result.e1r.weight.num}$) appears in $\affinity{}$ (terminal
hop of the affinity segment) but \emph{not} in $\consent{}$ (read at
$\mathrm{Profile}_{\text{Alice}}$, before the Reputation hop).  It enters
$\circqual{}$ exactly once, linearly, on the delivery circuit, as required
by \zcref{rem:bridge:reputation-single-traversal}.  Had consent been read at
the actor, it would have carried a second factor of $\numval{result.e1r.weight.num}$, giving
$\consent{} = \numval{result.bridge_da.weight.num} \times \numval{result.e1r.weight.num} \numrel{result.bridge.consent_double.num}$ and
$\circqual{} \numrel{result.bridge.circqual_double.num}$ --- the quadratic-reputation
double-count the Profile read eliminates. \okmark

\paragraph{Denominator representability.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:bridge:denominator-representability}
The normalized share (\zcref{eq:bridge:cancellation}) divides by
$\sum_{C'} X_{C'}$ after the campaign scalar cancels. Here the sole
creator term is $X_{\text{Alice}} \approx 1.0 \times 1.0 \times 1.0
\times 1.3 \times 1.0 = 1.3$; scaling to $10^6$ creators with worst-case
small factors bounded below by the clip floor keeps the denominator
within $[10^{-8}, 10^{6}]$ --- far inside IEEE-754 double range, and
underflow of $\campaignscalar{A}$ itself closes the gate conservatively
(\zcref{rem:bridge:scale-inertness}). \okmark

The derived constant $\wmax \numrel{bound.raw.wmax.num}$ is the supremum of the
Reputation component weight as $\standing{j} \to \infty$ and
$\tau \to 1^-$. It is therefore the valid upper bound for prospective
clipping: the ceiling must bound all per-edge weights, including the
standing-dependent Reputation component. Spam chains decay geometrically
because their accumulated state products are small regardless
of the ceiling value. The four rows marked $\star$ verify the numerical consequences
of the Self-edge bond analytic results: $\tilde{w} < 1$ guarantees
self-loop neutrality; the profile-bridged ceiling confirms the
discovery-path hierarchy; the rate bound $< 1$ guarantees geometric
convergence of the epoch recursion; and the $\tau$-ceiling bounds the
amplification available to blocked actors.

\subsection{Bootstrapping-Era Discovery Attenuation}
\label{subsec:verification:bootstrapping-attenuation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

During the bootstrapping phase, aggregate burn capacity is bounded
by $\burncap \approx 105$ reserve units (illustrative Layer~0 surface value)
(\zcref{def:comparator:bootstrap-capacity}). Commitment rates
cluster near $\numeraire$, producing weak Self-edge bonds. The
table below computes key routing quantities at
$\standing{} = \partfloor\numeraire = 0.10$ (the gate value) and
compares to the reference value $\standing{} = 0.300$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l c c c@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Quantity}
    & $\standing{} = 0.10$
    & $\standing{} = 0.30$
    & \textbf{Ratio} \\
    \midrule
    Self-edge bond $p_i$
        & $\numval{fixture.rep_half.indirect.num}$ & $\numval{fixture.e1.indirect.exact}$ & $0.67$ \\
    $\detscore{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}$
        & $\numval{result.rep_half.detscore.num}$ & $\numval{result.e1r.detscore.num}$ & $\numval{result.scaling.rep_ratio.num}$ \\
    $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}}$ at $\tau = 0.50$
        & $\numval{result.rep_half.weight.num}$ & $\numval{result.e1r.weight.num}$ & $\numval{result.scaling.rep_ratio.num}$ \\
    Profile-bridged ceiling
        & $\numval{result.scaling.bridged_low.num}$ & $\numval{result.scaling.bridged_high.num}$ & $\numval{result.scaling.rep_ratio.num}$ \\
    Canonical endorsement flow weight (unit Opinion)
        & $\numval{result.scaling.flow_low.num}$ & $\numval{result.scaling.flow_high.num}$ & $\numval{result.scaling.rep_ratio.num}$ \\
    Commitment amplification $A(\refstanding{})$
        & $0.388$ & $1.008$ & $0.385$ \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

With the saturating bond intensity
$p_i = \standing{}/(\numeraire + \standing{})$, the routing quantities remain
$67$--$77\%$ of the reference values because both the floor
($p_i = 0.5$) and the reference ($p_i = 0.75$) sit in the saturated
region of $\psi_+$. The terminal readout is different: the universal amplifier
uses $\refstanding{}$, so the gate-level actor reads as $0.385$ of the
reference, distinguishing gate-level from $3\times$ actors more sharply rather
than mildly attenuating them.
The Polarization Floor (\zcref{prop:graph:polarization-floor})
guarantees $\Psi^{11} \geq 0.5$; the always-active baseline
guarantees $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \geq 0.800$
(\zcref{lem:graph:non-vanishing-norm}). Feed ranking functions; the changed row
is a terminal readout, not a traversal change. All other App~F quantities ---
weights, flows, bonds, title, and certificates --- are untouched.
Post-bootstrapping (as external deposits raise $\standing{}$ toward
reference values), all routing quantities recover monotonically
(\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Boundary Admission}
\label{subsec:verification:boundary-admission}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\paragraph{Dependent-set pricing and subsidy.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:boundary:dependent-set-pricing}
Author $a$ (rate $0.12$) has record $e_1$; sponsor $b$ (rate $0.30$)
authors $e_2$ asserting $e_1$. Minimal dependent set $\set{e_1,e_2}$:
price $=(0.12+0.30)/2 = 0.21 \ge$ door $0.10$ \okmark; both members clear
$\safethresh \numrel{const.epoch.safethresh_m1.num}$ \okmark. Under the retired min rule the set priced
at $0.12$; under averaging the child carries the parent. Conversely a
sponsor at $0.30$ carrying records at exactly $\safethresh$: the subsidy
bound gives $n \le (0.30-0.10)/(0.10-\numval{const.epoch.safethresh_m1.num}) = 3.58$, so at most three
such records per sponsor record --- and none below $\safethresh$ at any
$n$. \okmark

\paragraph{Safety is not averaged.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:boundary:safety-not-averaged}
Set $\set{e_1,e_2}$ with author rates $0.30$ and
$0.03 < \safethresh$: price $0.165$ clears the door, the set is nonetheless
invalid --- clause~(ii) fails on the poor member. No valid write set contains
$e_2$ at any sponsor wealth. \okmark

\paragraph{Regime and door-headroom replay.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:boundary:regime-replay}
$\epochlen = 4$; certificate partition: stamps
$\set{0.30,0.21,0.15,0.12}$, $|\actsequence{k}| = 4$: regime binding, headroom
$\doorheadroom{k}=\sum(\actstamp{}-\partfloor)$. A second certificate,
three sets, $|\actsequence{k}| = 3 < \epochlen$: slack, positive headroom. Both replayed
from the certificate alone; no submission data exists or is needed.  The
count is of \emph{acts}, not projections
(\zcref{def:epoch:epoch-act-budget}): a fixture containing one hyper-edge act
distinguishes the two, and this one must count it once. \okmark

\paragraph{Invalid policy floor.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:boundary:invalid-polfloor}
Certificate $k$ publishes $\safethresh^{(k+1)} = 0.12$ (interim rule at an
elevated $\locwidth{}$). The host announces $\polfloor = 1$, i.e.\ door
price $0.10 < 0.12$: the announcement is invalid at publication
(\zcref{eq:epoch:floor-validity}). Had a faulty pipeline applied it anyway,
the effective floor reads $\partfloor = \max(1, 0.12/0.10) = 1.2$ --- the
defensive $\max$ over-floors, never under-floors. \okmark

\paragraph{Safety-threshold replay.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:boundary:safety-replay}
At the certified table value $\locwidth{} = 1.0$
(\zcref{cor:dynamics:minimal-safe-wall}: $\minsafewall{1.0} \numrel{const.epoch.safefloor_m1.num}$) with
margin $\marginfactor = 1$, the interim rule gives
$\safethresh = \numval{const.epoch.safefloor_m1.num}\,\numeraire \numrel{const.epoch.safethresh_m1.num}$ --- replayable by any
participant from the certificate width and the published constants (R1),
and comfortably below the canonical door price $0.10$: the reference
regime satisfies \zcref{eq:epoch:floor-validity} with margin
$\numval{result.epoch.floor_margin.num}\times$. \okmark

\paragraph{Canonical-time replay.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:boundary:canonical-time-replay}
Take the same written record set and replay it under two presentation orders:
$e_1,e_2,e_3$ and $e_3,e_1,e_2$. The endpoint-incidence relation, asserted-parent
fields, and identity keys are identical, so \zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}
assigns identical $\acttime{}$ values. Because maturity reads
$\prec_{\mathrm{inc}}$ and not submission order, $\tau$ and every
$\dampedweight{}$ value are bit-identical. \okmark

\paragraph{Write-policy invariance measurement.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:boundary:write-policy-invariance}
Fix the written edge set. Since non-written actors remain dynamically live
(\zcref{rem:epoch:non-written-dynamic-live}), $W_i$, $\locwidth{}$, and
$\standingcert{k}$ are functions of the written state only. A measurement obligation
for deployment instrumentation; it blocks no theorem. \okmark

\subsection{Boundary Admission Lint}
\label{subsec:verification:boundary-admission-lint}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}l X@{}}
    \toprule
    \textbf{Pattern} & \textbf{Verdict} \\
    \midrule
    selection position in recognition, tie-break, or scoring
        & prohibited by \zcref{rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance} \\
    door headroom or regime statistic in a $\numeraire$-side formula
        & prohibited by \zcref{rem:epoch:admission-statistics-quarantine} \\
    gate- or write-exempt record class
        & prohibited by \zcref{subsec:necessity:no-privileged-cancel-class} \\
        $\safethresh$ compared to a dimensionless quantity without explicit $\numeraire$
                & prohibited; sanctioned forms $\polfloor\ge\safefloor$ and
                    $\loggain{\safefloor}$ \\
    host-set congestion price
                & none exists; door headroom is descriptive
                    (\zcref{def:network:door-headroom}) \\
    asserted parent in $\tau$ or path viability
        & prohibited by \zcref{rem:graph:act-ordering-relations} \\
    raw full-coordinate amplifier at a terminal readout
        & prohibited; use $\ampfactor{}$. The standing recursion's self-weight
          denominator is a count weight and exempt \\
    invocation of atomic inclusion
        & retired; cite \zcref{post:graph:boundary-accountability} \\
    $N_i$ increment on non-write
        & prohibited by \zcref{rem:epoch:admission-statistics-quarantine} \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}

\subsection{Settlement Lifecycle}
\label{subsec:verification:settlement-walkthrough}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Extend the reference graph: Bob owns Sneakers ($i_1$) via the Owner edge
$e_8$ (the genesis Owner edge, \zcref{def:graph:item-genesis-act}). Carol buys.

\paragraph{Bid full-mask verification.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:settlement:bid-promotion-verification}
Carol's Bid on Sneakers: $g = \numval{fixture.bid.direct.exact}$, $u = \numval{fixture.bid.indirect.exact}$, $\tau = \numval{fixture.bid.maturity.exact}$. Signed
generosity, full stored block routed at \tierhalf{}. Bid/A path-view:
$\pathview{} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
\numval{result.bid.pv_a.num} & \numval{result.bid.pv_a.num} \\ \numval{result.bid.pv_a.num} & \numval{result.bid.core_pl.num} \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
(using $\halffloor\,\fpm{\numval{result.e7.inner.num}} = \numval{const.graph.halffloor.num} \times \numval{result.bid.core_pm.num} \numrel{result.bid.pv_a.num}$ at the
off-corner entries and $\fpl{\numval{result.e7.inner.num}} \numrel{result.bid.core_pl.num}$ at the polarization entry).
$\det \numrel{result.bid.pv_det.num}$, $\detscore{} \numrel{result.bid.detscore.num}$, $\detsign{} = +1$.
\tierhalf{} confirmed: the $\halffloor$ path-view floor attenuates the
Bid below the \tierfull{} band ($\numrel{result.bid_full.detscore.num}$ at full routing) by a
factor $\numrel{result.bid.tier_ratio.num}$ while preserving $\detsign{} = +1$
(\zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}). \okmark

\paragraph{Three-step settlement (happy path).}
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Bid} (Carol $\to$ Sneakers): creates Offer $o_1$.
          $\detsign{} = +1$ (generous).
    \item \textbf{Accept} (Bob $\to$ Carol, $c = \numval{fixture.accept.direct.exact}$, $e = \numval{fixture.accept.indirect.exact}$,
          \texttt{settles}$\to$Bid): $\det(\pathview{}) \numrel{result.accept.pv_det.num}$
          (\tierhalf{} floor),
          $\detsign{} = +1$ (comfortable). Authorization clause~(iii): Bob
          is the genesis owner of Sneakers. \okmark
    \item \textbf{Ratify} (Carol $\to$ Bob, $c = 0.9$, $e = 0.8$,
          \texttt{settles}$\to$Bid): $\detsign{} = +1$ (satisfied).
\end{enumerate}
Recognition: clauses (i)--(vi) hold; no cancel in any epoch
$\le \operatorname{ep}(\mathrm{Ratify})$; sole candidate at its boundary
($|C_k| = 1$, \zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}): title transfers Bob
$\to$ Carol at the certificate. $\titlecert{k+1}(i_1) = \text{Carol}$.
\okmark

Stance conjunction (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation}):
$\operatorname{sgn}(g)\wedge\operatorname{sgn}(c_{\mathrm{Acc}})\wedge
\operatorname{sgn}(c_{\mathrm{Rat}}) = (+)\wedge(+)\wedge(+)$: positive
commercial reputation. (Here the bilinear parities agree; they diverge
at \zcref{ver:settlement:coerced-unfair}.) \okmark

\paragraph{Same-epoch cancel.}\phantomsection\label{ver:settlement:same-epoch-cancel}
After Bob's Accept, Bob submits Rescind and Carol submits Ratify; both
finalize in epoch $k$ --- in either arrival order, with any Lamport times.
Clause~(v): $\operatorname{ep}(R) \le \operatorname{ep}(Ra)$, so the commit
is defeated. Not recognized; Bob retains title; escrow refunds Carol. No
time arithmetic is consulted. \okmark

\paragraph{Suppressed cancel.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:settlement:suppressed-cancel}
Bob forms Rescind before the boundary, but the certificate writes Carol's
Ratify on the same Offer and writes no defeating cancel. Recognition sees no
defeating cancel, so title may transfer; Layer~1 does not restore title after
the fact, and there is no Layer-1 evidence of the suppressed record. An escrow
keyed to the certificate releases correctly against what was written. The
exposure is \zcref{frontier:boundary-censorship}'s: a mechanism problem, not an
audit artifact. \okmark

\paragraph{Conflicting commits (mutual consumption).}\phantomsection\label{ver:settlement:mutual-consumption}
Bob Accepts both Carol and Dave; both Ratifys finalize in epoch~$k$. Both
candidates are recognized and authorized by $\titlecert{k-1} = \mathrm{Bob}$:
$|C_k| = 2$, so \textbf{both are consumed} --- no transfer, Bob retains,
both escrows refund, and the consumed records found nothing later
(\zcref{def:graph:settlement-consumption}). The Item remains transferable:
Carol re-bids in epoch $k{+}1$ and completes normally. If instead Dave's
Ratify finalizes at $k{+}1$: Carol transfers at $k$; Dave's candidate fails
clause~(iii) at $k{+}1$ (owner changed) and his escrow refunds ---
\emph{first epoch wins; ties consume}. \okmark

\paragraph{No death-by-inaction.}
A Bid left in Open indefinitely: no transition, no value locked, harmless.
An Accept left in Accepted: Bob may Rescind to clean up, or Carol may
Withdraw; neither party is forced to wait on the other
(\zcref{thm:graph:no-death-by-inaction}). No $T_{\mathrm{bid}}$ constant
appears anywhere in this walkthrough. \okmark

\paragraph{Coerced-unfair Accept: stance vs.\ parity.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:settlement:coerced-unfair}
Accept with $c = -0.7$, $e = -0.8$ (the honest worst case: coerced into
an unfair deal). Bilinear parity: $\detsign{} = \operatorname{sgn}(ce)
= +1$ (\zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law}) --- the edge routes coherently
through the double cover BFS. Stance marginal:
$\operatorname{sgn}(c) = -1$ --- the stance conjunction fails and
commercial reputation is negative
(\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation}). Title recognition is
unaffected in both readings (sentiment-blind,
\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}). The record also fails the Vouch Predicate
(\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}), so it is omitted from the
endorsement-flow projection and injects no standing endorsement. The worst-case
experience does not produce the best-case signal. \okmark

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Authored-Act Handshake, Ordering, and Accountability Fixtures}
\label{subsec:verification:authored-act-fixtures}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Behavioral fixtures for the Guide-15 admission handshake
(\zcref{def:graph:proposal-pre-commitment,def:graph:verified-act,%
def:graph:approval-witness}), atomicity, the authoritative order
(\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}), dependency tombstoning, and the
ordering fraud proof (\zcref{def:graph:ordering-fraud-proof}).  Each asserts a
pass (\okmark) or a required rejection.

\paragraph{Pre-commitment binding.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:pre-commitment}
Over $\precommit{q}$ (\zcref{def:graph:proposal-pre-commitment}):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*)]
    \item the correct proposal recomputes its pre-commitment;
    \item a modified endpoint, \item modified family,
    \item modified semantic coordinate, \item modified content,
    \item modified dependency list, or \item modified requested tombstone policy
          each fails the recomputation;
    \item a pre-commitment transplanted to another act identifier fails.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

\paragraph{Host salting.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:salting}
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*), start=9]
    \item Correct host salts reproduce the returned commitments;
    \item the content salt $\payloadsalt{q}$ and dependency salt $\actdepsalt{q}$
          are distinct; \item a salt reused across acts is rejected by
          conformance; the Actor rejects a returned commitment to a
    \item modified dependency list, \item modified content, or
    \item modified public protocol reference.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

\paragraph{Actor approval.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:approval}
Over $\approvewitness{q}$ (\zcref{def:graph:approval-witness}):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*), start=15]
    \item a valid approval witness verifies;
    \item an approval witness transplanted to another verified act fails,
    \item as does one over an altered host seal;
    \item an unapproved verified act cannot enter $\actsequence{k}$;
    \item one altered hyper-edge leg invalidates approval.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

\paragraph{Act atomicity.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:atomicity}
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*), start=20]
    \item A binary act has one record and one time;
    \item a hyper-edge act has two matched records and one time;
          reject on \item a missing leg, \item different act identifiers,
    \item different dependency commitments, \item different logical times, or
    \item a dependency naming one leg instead of the act.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

\paragraph{Authoritative ordering.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:ordering}
Under $\depok{k}{q}$ (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*), start=27]
    \item A prior-epoch dependency passes; \item a same-epoch earlier dependency
          passes; \item a same-epoch later dependency is non-compliant;
    \item a missing dependency is a non-compliant inclusion;
    \item a self-dependency is rejected at proposal;
    \item a dependency cycle rejects the cyclic candidate set;
    \item two unconstrained acts may be ordered either way;
    \item different permissible orders yield correspondingly different
          order-sensitive results.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

\paragraph{Dependency tombstoning.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:tombstoning}
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*), start=35]
    \item A full-empty projection commits and opens; \item so does a full
          projection; \item full$\to$tombstoned retains the same commitment;
          tombstoning changes no \item final standing, \item title, or
    \item authoritative time; \item a tombstoned projection cannot be restored as
          Layer-1 carriage; \item an external opening after tombstone verifies
          without restoring it.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

\paragraph{Ordering fraud proof.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:fraud}
Over $\fraudproof{q}$ (\zcref{def:graph:ordering-fraud-proof}):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*), start=43]
    \item A correct opening with a satisfied order shows no fraud;
    \item a correct opening with a later dependency, or \item a missing
          dependency, succeeds; \item a modified list, \item a modified salt, or
    \item an opening transplanted to another act fails; a valid fraud proof
          leaves \item finalized replay and \item title unchanged.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

\paragraph{Title order.}%
\phantomsection\label{ver:handshake:title}
\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=(\arabic*), start=51]
    \item $\mathrm{Bid}\prec\mathrm{Accept}\prec\mathrm{Ratify}$ in the
          authoritative order is well formed; \item Ratify before Accept or
    \item Ratify naming the wrong Accept is malformed;
    \item a same-epoch Rescind and Ratify let the cancel win in either order;
    \item same-epoch conflicting commits mutually consume in either order;
    \item the first finalized epoch wins across epochs;
    \item an optional dependency opened later proves host fault without reversing
          title.
\end{enumerate}
\okmark

% frontier apparatus (macros_network.tex): a flat label namespace frontier:<name>
% with the SPECIES carried by the reference type, so reclassification never breaks an
% inbound \zcref.  Every numbered entry self-adds to the ToC; App F is now navigable.
%
% SPECIES (narrow definition enacted): only `core' is an "Open Problem" — an
% unresolved question bearing on admission (gate / capacity / recognition / title)
% or comparator faithfulness/convergence.  Everything else is a calibration
% obligation, an architectural extension, a Layer-2 guild design choice, a
% ceiling-witness (a bounded instance of the PROVED §2 accountability-cost ceiling),
% a Layer-0 pointer, or a proposed numerical investigation.
%
% CHANGELOG:

%   (pre-0.22 history squashed; see the v0.21.1-dev edition for the full changelog)

\section{Research Frontiers}
\label{app:frontiers}

Edition~4 separates closed standing mathematics from the questions that
remain genuinely open.  For every finite completed epoch state, the exact
depth-two standing anchor is a continuous contractive max-envelope
equilibrium; deeper delegation enters only through certified depth-three
and depth-four stages, each with a safe fallback to the preceding stage.
Max switching, fixed-point existence, uniqueness inside accepted
certificates, below-wall gain, and non-normal one-step amplification are
therefore no longer open standing problems.

This appendix collects the questions that do remain, on the admission and
faithfulness axes; content-governance deferrals
(\zcref{subsec:content:provenance,subsec:content:metadata}) and the
carriage-entropy obligation (\zcref{rem:graph:erasure-floor}) are recorded
at their home sections and not duplicated here.  It is organized by
\emph{species}, because the questions are not all of one kind; a solved
theorem is not retained as a ``discharged frontier'' merely to preserve
its old number, and a no-longer-applicable question is deleted with its
callers repointed.

\begin{definition}[Layer-1 Open Problem]
    \label{def:frontiers:open-problem}
    A \emph{Layer-1 Open Problem} is an unresolved question whose resolution could
    change what Layer~1 guarantees \emph{in its role as comparator} --- i.e.\ a
    question bearing on \textbf{admission} (the participation gate, the capacity
    rule, the formation rule, or settlement recognition / title;
    \zcref{def:network:admission-closure}) or on \textbf{comparator
    faithfulness and convergence} (clauses (S)--(Q) of
    \zcref{post:comparator:faithfulness}). Only these are ``open problems.''
    A question whose only open content is the \emph{magnitude} of a bound
    witnessing an already-proved structural limit is a ceiling witness
    (\zcref{subsec:frontiers:witness}), not an open problem.
\end{definition}

Six species follow, each in its own subsection. \textbf{Open Problems}
(\zcref{subsec:frontiers:core}) is the narrow core of
\zcref{def:frontiers:open-problem}. \textbf{Calibration Obligations}
(\zcref{subsec:frontiers:calibration}) are not unsolved --- they are constants
awaiting empirical lock during the centralized phase
(\zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model}). \textbf{Architectural
Extensions} (\zcref{subsec:frontiers:architectural}) are expansions of Layer-1
structure, not defects. \textbf{Guild Design Choices}
(\zcref{subsec:frontiers:guild}) are Layer-2 degrees of freedom the protocol
deliberately delegates (\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}); their open content is
``which choice is good,'' owned by guilds. \textbf{Ceiling Witnesses}
(\zcref{subsec:frontiers:witness}) are bounded instances of a \emph{proved}
\S1--\S2 structural limit (accountability cost,
\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost} and
\zcref{rem:comparator:structural-ceiling}; or privacy of departure,
\zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}) --- the limit itself is not in this
appendix, it is established in \S1--\S2; these entries are its witnesses, and
their open content is a \emph{quantity} (a bound), not a question of whether
something breaks. \textbf{Proposed Investigations}
(\zcref{subsec:frontiers:investigations}) are structured numerical exercises with
deterministic targets.

\begin{remark}[Priority]
    \label{rem:frontiers:priority}
    Earlier editions closed the former standing fixed-point, max-switching,
    sub-gate-gain, and certified non-normality questions
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness,%
    thm:dynamics:finite-max-envelope-lipschitz}).

    Conserved allocation closed one more, and closed it by \emph{dissolution}
    rather than by answering it.  Delegated-stage co-maximizers needed a
    permutation-equivariant tie rule, because a selected witness decided which
    paths entered the next stage.  Apportionment selects nothing
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:finite-max-envelope-lipschitz}), so there are no
    witnesses to tie, no rule to choose, and no way for an Actor identifier to
    privilege one path over an automorphic twin --- the map is built from the
    base matrix by operations that commute with relabeling.  A question can
    stop existing as well as be answered, and this one did.

    The remaining core is smaller.  First, source-root eligibility
    (\zcref{frontier:source-root-eligibility}) decides whether a depleted
    source may continue exporting historical denominator mass.  Second, the
    cross-layer burn snapshot (\zcref{frontier:leverage-timing}) remains a
    temporal seam.

    The principal architectural obligations are standing evaluation
    at scale (\zcref{frontier:exact-conserved-evaluation}) and a
    decentralized final-set boundary mechanism
    (\zcref{frontier:boundary-mechanism}).  Their empirical companions are
    stage-certificate and standing-work calibration
    (\zcref{frontier:conserved-standing-certificate-monitoring,%
    frontier:conserved-standing-work-calibration}).
\end{remark}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Open Problems (Layer-1 Core)}
\label{subsec:frontiers:core}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{frontier}[Safety-Threshold and Burn-Snapshot Timing]{core}{leverage-timing}{Safety-Threshold and Burn-Snapshot Timing}
    \frontierstatus{Cross-layer temporal seam; substantially narrowed
    under epoch-final standing.}

    Standing is computed only from the completed epoch state
    (\zcref{def:epoch:proposed-final-act-state,%
    post:epoch:standing-quantization}).  The remaining timing question
    is whether an Actor can condition proposed acts on a Layer-0 burn
    that is visible to one side of the final-set boundary but not the
    other, or exploit advance knowledge of the action price in force.

    The weld samples once per epoch
    (\zcref{lem:comparator:frame-stability}); the debit price is
    announced with one-boundary lead and consummated per write
    (\zcref{post:epoch:act-debit}).  The Layer-0 half remains
    \attestationcref*{open:leverage-timing}; the network half is the
    exact relation among the settled burn snapshot, the accepted write
    set, and the debit price used by
    \zcref{eq:epoch:final-residual-balance}.

    Source emission adds a consumer of that same snapshot
    (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}): a late burn now moves the
    source's rate and its export capacity together, in the epoch it
    lands.  The substance of the seam is unchanged --- both are read
    once, from the completed state --- but a boundary rule must cover
    the emission fraction as well as the rate.

    \frontieropen{Specify and prove one cross-layer boundary rule under
    which every accepted act and every burn increment read into its
    final source pair belong to one unambiguous settlement view.}

    \frontierxref{def:epoch:proposed-final-act-state,%
    post:epoch:final-edge-set,lem:comparator:frame-stability,%
    post:epoch:act-debit,subsec:comparator:limitations,%
    post:comparator:faithfulness}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{core}{source-root-eligibility}{Source-Root Eligibility}
    \frontierstatus{\textbf{Resolved by charter.}  Retained for its
    derivation, which is the argument the resolution rests on.}

    The wall clamp controls the activation a recipient carries
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:safety-wall-clamp}).  It does not control whether a
    source Actor's own pair $(\burnbal{u},\actcount{u})$ may originate
    standing at all, and under a full-pair rule a source with zero residual
    balance and large historical action count contributes pure denominator
    mass --- certifiable, but in tension with the claim that standing pressure
    is continuously backed by current source cost.

    Five requirements were imposed on any remedy: preserve the source rate,
    prevent count fabrication, commute with the num\'eraire, survive address
    splitting, and integrate with the certificates.  The last deferred the
    question, because every earlier candidate implied a new certificate
    programme.  It is discharged by transfer rather than by new work: the
    emission diagonal is constant during the solve, so the fence and the screen
    carry over with identical constants
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:emission-certificate-transfer}).  The admissible
    class is fixed independently by cluster rate invariance --- relocation in,
    deletion out (\zcref{cor:epoch:conserving-source-root-criterion}) --- and
    the chartered member is
    $\emission{u}=\min(1,\refrate{u}/\safefloor)$
    (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}), which mints no new constant because
    the export cap and the activation wall key to the same coordinate.

    \frontierremedy{The resolution is normative.  What remains is
    calibration, not choice: the community-sag profile and the fading-actor
    experience are owned by
    \zcref{frontier:emission-sag-calibration}, and demurrage variants are
    parked as charter amendments rather than parameters
    (\zcref{frontier:influence-demurrage}).}

    \frontierxref{def:epoch:source-emission,%
    frontier:depleted-source-ballast,%
    frontier:allocation-split-invariance}
\end{frontier}

\paragraph{Retired boundary-pricing note.}
Layer~1 no longer prices or audits the unwritten: nothing occurs on a
non-write, and demand estimation is outside the ontology. The old temptation to
increment $N_i$ on rejection remains prohibited as historical rationale because
it would hand the host a censorship-to-dilution lever
(\zcref{post:epoch:act-debit,rem:epoch:admission-statistics-quarantine}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Calibration Obligations}
\label{subsec:frontiers:calibration}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

These items do not question whether Edition~5 standing is mathematically
defined.  They determine constants, monitoring thresholds, and work
envelopes before lock (\zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model}).

\begin{frontier}{calib}{tilt-profile-charter}{Tilt Profile and Depth Mass Charter}
    \frontierpriority{High --- the profile is chartered, its extension is
    not.}
    The chartered shape and depth mass satisfy the prior screen at full
    strength (\zcref{cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}), so nothing here
    blocks deployment.  What is open is the region \emph{above} the screen: a
    louder profile is not forbidden, it is merely unscreened, and would have to
    be certified per epoch on the graph rather than in advance.

    The chartered \emph{shape} is not part of what is open, and this entry
    should not be read as leaving it to calibration.  Its decay is determined:
    halving is the unique geometric decay the screen admits at every depth
    (\zcref{rem:dynamics:chartered-decay-determined}), so the open question is
    not which shape to pick but whether to leave the admissible region at all.
    That sharpens the trade below rather than softening it --- a louder shape
    forfeits the screen past a finite depth, so it costs a reach ceiling and
    not only a certification discipline.

    \frontieropen{Determine whether a profile exceeding the prior screen is
    worth the loss of graph-free certification \emph{and} of unbounded
    admissible reach, and if so publish the monitoring that makes per-epoch
    certification of it safe.  Any answer must respect that the screen's
    failure proves nothing --- a louder profile is a change in operating
    discipline, not a change in what is true.}

    \frontierxref{cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen,%
    rem:dynamics:chartered-decay-determined,%
    def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{depth-mass-calibration}{Depth Mass Calibration}
    \frontierpriority{Medium --- reference values are chartered and safe.}
    The published depth mass decides how far regard reaches: it is the only
    place the design says how much a distant source should count.  The
    chartered reference is front-loaded, and any admissible alternative is
    screened by the same prior condition, since the screen is keyed to the
    deepest \emph{supported} depth
    (\zcref{cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}).

    \frontieropen{Determine the depth mass from observed community structure
    rather than from the reference.  Note the discontinuity the screen makes
    explicit: giving the deepest hop any positive mass at all, however small,
    prices the full profile volume.  A calibration that shaves the deepest
    weight toward zero buys nothing until it reaches zero.}

    \frontierxref{def:epoch:standing-depth-mass,%
    cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{emission-sag-calibration}{Emission Sag and the Fading Actor}
    \frontierpriority{Medium --- an experience obligation, not a safety one.}
    Source emission is chartered and its safety transfers
    (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission}).  What is not settled is how it
    \emph{feels} across a community: the aggregate sag as many sources fade
    together, and the experience of a single depleted Actor whose relational
    rehabilitation is slowed by self-inertia
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:emission-self-inertia}).

    \frontieropen{Measure the community-level sag profile under realistic
    balance distributions, and determine whether the fading-actor path needs a
    published signal --- a warning before emission falls, say --- distinct from
    the standing value itself.  Also fix the $\safethresh$ vintage emission
    reads, which the burn-snapshot seam constrains
    (\zcref{frontier:leverage-timing}).}

    \frontierxref{def:epoch:source-emission,%
    rem:epoch:emission-self-inertia,frontier:depleted-source-ballast}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{arch}{influence-demurrage}{Influence Demurrage}
    \frontierstatus{Parked deliberately.  A charter amendment, not a
    parameter.}
    A recurring proposal is that unexercised standing should decay with time
    rather than only with dilution.  Under conserved allocation this is not a
    tuning knob: demurrage would either delete pair mass, which cluster rate
    invariance forbids
    (\zcref{cor:epoch:conserving-source-root-criterion}), or relocate it
    somewhere other than its owner's row, which requires a lawful sink the
    charter does not have.

    \frontieropen{If demurrage is ever wanted, it must arrive as an amendment
    naming its sink and re-proving the cluster identity against it.  It is
    recorded here so that the absence is a decision rather than an oversight.}

    \frontierxref{post:epoch:cluster-rate-invariance,%
    def:epoch:source-emission}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Floor and Numéraire Calibration]{calib}{floor-calibration}%
    {Floor and Numéraire Calibration}
    \frontierpriority{Top --- $(\numeraire,\partfloor)$ split pricing from
    admission.}
    Determine the operating dials $(\numeraire,\theta,\polfloor,\marginfactor)$
    as a function of observed network statistics.  The Edition-4 calibration
    quantities are the safety wall $\safefloor=\theta/\numeraire$, the
    full-depth width fence
    $\marginfactor\,\loggain{\safefloor}\locwidth{}\le1$
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}), the certified stage factors
    $\standingcert{k},\standingcert{k},\standingcert{k}$
    (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), and the effective door
    $\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}=\max(\rho_{\mathrm{pol}},\safefloor)$.

    \frontieropen{Calibrate $(\numeraire,\theta,\polfloor,\marginfactor)$
    against final-set admission rates, source-rate widths, exact stage
    certificates, and standing-work measurements.  The wall must preserve
    the full-depth margin (per-act source cost, W2a accessibility, W2b
    backpressure, stage-contraction clearance, admission rate, and the exact
    conserved-standing workload of \zcref{frontier:conserved-standing-work-calibration}) while
    the policy door remains economically and socially usable.}

    \frontierxref{rem:epoch:dial-scope,post:epoch:act-debit,%
    def:epoch:safety-threshold,thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence,%
    cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen,%
    frontier:conserved-standing-certificate-monitoring}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{conserved-standing-certificate-monitoring}%
    {Stage-Certificate Monitoring}
    \frontierstatus{Centralized-phase calibration obligation.}
    Publish separately for stages~$2,3,4$ the conserved standing certificate
    $\standingcert{k}$, the certified contraction factor
    $\standingcert{k}$, and the local width $\locwidth{}$, together
    with fixed-point enclosure radius, stage movement, candidate count,
    selected-pair count, positive clip count, total clip mass, and fallback
    frequency.  All inputs are certificate-derivable; the monitor is a
    replay.

    \frontieropen{Set alert, persistence, and review thresholds for
    certificate clearance, unresolved threshold comparisons, fallback
    frequency, and divergence between the universal stage screen
    (\zcref{cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}) and the exact
    graph-dependent certificate.}

    \frontierxref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate,%
    def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate,%
    frontier:tilt-backoff-monitoring}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{conserved-standing-work-calibration}%
    {Standing Work Calibration}
    \frontierstatus{Required before scale and constant lock.}
    Measure per accepted epoch and per trial set: direct projected edge
    count, base-matrix support size, contributing width, certificate
    clearance below its cap, SCC sizes, map passes to the accepted residual,
    cache invalidations, and wall-clock validation time.

    \frontieropen{Publish percentile envelopes and choose operational alert
    levels.  The data decide whether the sparse conserved solve meets the
    boundary duration at deployment scale, which is what
    \zcref{frontier:exact-conserved-evaluation} asks.}

    \frontierxref{def:scalability:conserved-standing-work-measures,%
    prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost,%
    rem:scalability:dense-projection-cost}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{cadence-maturity-coupling}{Cadence--Maturity Coupling}
    \frontierstatus{Calibration obligation; opened by external review of the
    calibration architecture.  Re-scoped: raw feed/bridge only ---
    maturity does not enter projected standing.}
    The tenure schedule advances per epoch boundary
    (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}), while governance procedures,
    persistence windows, and adversaries live in wall time.  Any change to the
    published boundary triple (target size, minimum duration, maximum duration;
    \zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-closure}) therefore moves the whole population
    along the raw maturity-amplification curve per unit wall time,
    changing raw feed ranking and raw bridge traversal weights.  Projected
    standing is unaffected: raw maturity is not a standing-drift input, and
    exact standing is recomputed at closure --- a cadence change alters only
    how often, in wall time, final-set standing and backpressure are
    recomputed and how large the candidate-set search budget is per
    interval.  The coupling is invisible in epoch-indexed time and decisive
    in the wall-clock frame governance is audited in.  Monitor: the
    wall-clock $\tau$-sheet drift rate of the raw consumers under any cadence
    change, alongside \zcref{frontier:conserved-standing-certificate-monitoring}.
    Procedural rule: freeze cadence retargeting during the declared
    adaptation window of any constant change
    (\zcref{frontier:incremental-equilibrium-solver}), so the cadence
    controller cannot chase the echo of the move it is measuring.
    \frontierxref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges,post:epoch:final-act-sequence-closure,%
    frontier:boundary-mechanism,frontier:conserved-standing-certificate-monitoring}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{boundary-policy-charter}{Boundary-Policy Charter}
    \frontierstatus{Calibration charter for the boundary mechanism.}
    The boundary-policy dial set is the epoch target size, the published
    minimum and maximum durations, the $\polfloor$ schedule, the $\theta$
    publication lead, the candidate-set search policy and trial budget, the
    final-set validation timeout, and the fallback when no proposed set
    verifies in time.  There is no special record class and no endogenous
    clearing price.  The cadence-freeze rule of
    \zcref{frontier:cadence-maturity-coupling} is retained: do not retune the
    boundary triple during the declared adaptation window of a constant move.
    \frontierxref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-closure,def:epoch:policy-floor,%
    def:epoch:safety-threshold,%
    frontier:cadence-maturity-coupling,frontier:boundary-mechanism}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[eta Calibration]{calib}{eta-calibration}{$\bleedparam$ Calibration}
    \frontierpriority{Standard --- locked in the centralized phase.}
    The bleed parameter $\bleedparam\numrel{const.graph.bleed.num}$
    (\zcref{def:graph:path-view-extraction}) controls the \tierfull{}/\tiermarginal{}
    gap. Since $\detscore{}$ scales as $\sqrt{\bleedparam}$ for restricted-mask
    edges while full-mask $\detscore{}$ is $\bleedparam$-independent
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:eta-softening}), the gap scales as
    $1/\sqrt{\bleedparam}$: at $\bleedparam=0.01$ the gap is $\sim 10\times$
    (strong domain identity); at $\bleedparam=0.15$ it is $\sim 2.6\times$ (easy
    cross-domain discovery). The choice $\bleedparam=\numval{const.graph.bleed.num}$
    ($\sim \numval{const.graph.softening_gap.num}\times$, i.e.\ $\sqrt{20}$) is a balance point. Empirical targets:
    cross-domain discovery rates, spam-resistance margins ($\wspam$ is a function
    of $\bleedparam$), tier reward distribution, and content-diversity
    satisfaction. Note the synchronized-sector Schwarzian negativity
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:core-schwarzian-negativity}) is certified robust across
    the band $\bleedparam\le0.39$ (certificate \texttt{peer\_Bcert}, gate C3,
    $\sim7.8\times$ headroom over the deployed $0.05$), so recalibration of
    $\bleedparam$ within any realistic range does not reopen that closure.
    One coupling is by construction and must be monitored, not discovered:
    the \tierhalf{} floor is $\halffloor=\sqrt{\bleedparam}$, so settlement
    and proposal attenuation move as $\bleedparam^{1/2}$ under any
    recalibration --- the one-knob ladder
