    $\set{1,\sqrt{\bleedparam},\bleedparam}$
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:eta-softening}) is a deliberate calibration
    commitment, and the sweep of \zcref{frontier:eta-sweep} should log the
    \tierhalf{} band alongside the \tierfull{}/\tiermarginal{} gap.
    \frontierxref{def:graph:path-view-extraction,%
    prop:graph:path-view-determinant-bound}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{tilt-backoff-monitoring}{Tilt-Backoff Monitoring}
    \frontierstatus{Calibration obligation for the centralized phase.}
    Publish per accepted epoch the standing-stage metrics: depth-two direct
    per-hop transported mass by depth; backoff rung fallback rates; the
    fraction of contributing coordinates pinned below the wall; the accepted
    rung $\tiltstrength{k}$ distribution; one-boundary standing movement;
    and the same-epoch Registration-plus-vouch cases.

    \frontieropen{Set alert thresholds on fallback frequency, co-maximizer
    incidence, and below-wall path fraction, and confirm the shares against
    the spam-resistance margins of \zcref{cor:scalability:spam-resistance}
    before constants lock.  Raw Review/Type/Comment conduit magnitudes are a
    separate terminal raw-service question, not a standing metric.}

    \frontierxref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate,%
    cor:scalability:spam-resistance,frontier:notoriety-field}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{bundle-audit}{Singleton-Bundle Assumption Audit and Chronicle Growth}
    \frontierstatus{Editing-pass obligation opened by \zcref{ax:graph:parallel-authored-acts}.}
    (1)~Worked examples and several lemmas quietly assume singleton bundles
    (``Carol's Opinion on Profile$_A$''); each must either tolerate bundles
    through the projection's netting (usually automatic) or state which
    fold it reads.  Mostly \zcref{app:verification}.
    (2)~Chronicle growth is unbounded by design; the sole brake is action
    pricing --- confirmed intended (the spam answer), recorded here so the
    payload/cache calibration (\zcref{frontier:payload-worst-case-calibration})
    sizes against parallel-bundle growth too.
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Inverse Temperature Optimisation]{calib}%
    {inverse-temperature-optimisation}{Inverse Temperature $\invtemp$ Optimisation}
    \frontierpriority{Standard.}
    Optimise $\invtemp$ via gradients $\partial\mathcal{U}/\partial\invtemp$ over
    graph evolutions. Adaptive $\invtemp$ could improve spam resistance in
    high-entropy epochs and relax the serendipity threshold in low-entropy epochs.
    Impact is confined to boundary-observed quantities: the \AttrView{} is
    $\invtemp$-invariant except through the void constant
    $\epsilon_\bot=e^{-\invtemp\ln2}$, and endorsement flow uses the identical
    $\dampedweight{e}$ formula as feed-ranking, so any change affects both systems
    simultaneously --- which makes the calibration tractable from a single
    observable (serendipity rate).
    \frontierxref{ax:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary,def:can:void-node}
\end{frontier}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\begin{frontier}{calib}{allocation-weight-calibration}{Domain Weight Calibration}
    \frontierpriority{High --- the weights decide what the network rewards.}
    The domain weights $\domweight{D}$ are published, nonnegative and uniform
    at the chartered reference.  Uniform is a starting point, not a result: it
    says every kind of accepted act counts the same, which is defensible only
    while nobody has measured whether it should.

    \frontieropen{Determine the weights from observed act semantics rather than
    from the reference.  The constraint is narrow and worth stating: the
    weights may not be act-class privileged in a way that is unpublished, and
    each act's domain profile must still sum to one, so calibration
    redistributes emphasis across domains and can never create weight
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:domain-weighted-allocation}).}

    \frontierxref{post:epoch:domain-weighted-act-sum,%
    eq:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{self-retention-base-calibration}{Self-Retention Base}
    \frontierpriority{Medium --- reference value chartered and safe.}
    The self-retention base $\selfretention$ decides how much of a source's
    conserved unit stays home before any act directs it outward.  At the
    chartered reference it equals one, which makes an Actor's own pair weigh as
    much as one authored act.

    \frontieropen{Determine $\selfretention$ from observed authoring rates.
    The trade-off is legible: a larger base makes standing more own-rate and
    less relational, a smaller one makes a lightly-active Actor's standing
    almost entirely a report on its neighbourhood.  Neither is unsafe --- the
    certificate does not care --- so this is a question about what the number
    should mean, not about whether it settles.}

    \frontierxref{def:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation,%
    subsec:necessity:self-retention-base}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{witness}{self-retention-manipulation}{Self-Retention Manipulation}
    \frontierstatus{Witness; no known exploit, and the search is not
    exhaustive.}
    The self entry is never standing-modulated, so standing cannot directly
    defend its own retention
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:rival-allocation-response}, clause~3).  What is not
    proved is that no \emph{indirect} route exists: an Actor shapes its own
    diagonal by choosing how much to author, and authoring is priced but not
    forbidden.

    \frontieropen{Exhibit a strategy that improves an Actor's own standing by
    re-shaping its own row, or bound the gain.  Note the two known
    counter-pressures: authoring more self-resolved acts concentrates the unit
    but does not raise the own rate
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:artifact-activity-crowds-out-export}), and every act
    pays its debit.}

    \frontierxref{prop:epoch:rival-allocation-response,%
    rem:epoch:artifact-activity-crowds-out-export}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{witness}{settlement-standing-accumulation}{Settlement Standing Accumulation}
    \frontierstatus{Witness; the per-act bound is known, the long-run
    accumulation is not.}
    A settled transfer is event-persistent, so its standing effect does not
    decay when a later epoch resells
    (\zcref{post:epoch:settlement-standing-title-coupling}).  Each settlement
    is one act, weighed once and priced once; what is open is whether a
    high-frequency legitimate trading relationship accumulates directed
    allocation faster than the dilution its own action counts impose.

    \frontieropen{Bound the steady-state standing of a mutually trading pair
    relative to a non-trading pair at the same ledger, or exhibit a rate at
    which trade dominates.  The distinguishing question is whether this is
    ordinary earned regard or a structural advantage of transacting over
    vouching.}

    \frontierxref{post:epoch:settlement-standing-title-coupling,%
    ver:standing:settlement-event-persistence}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{arch}{tilt-strictness}{Strict Tilt Modes}
    \frontierstatus{Open; deliberately absent.}
    The backoff grid is safely degradable: a failing rung falls to a lower one
    and the anchor cannot fail
    (\zcref{def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid}).  A recurring proposal is a strict
    mode --- refuse the epoch rather than lower the rung --- on the grounds that
    a quiet epoch misreports the network.

    \frontieropen{If strictness is ever wanted, it must arrive with an argument
    that liveness is not thereby hostage to the verifier: under a strict mode a
    numerically indecisive enclosure, which proves nothing
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:certificate-failure-versus-indecisive-enclosure}), would
    stop the network.  That is the failure this frontier exists to name.}

    \frontierxref{def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid,%
    rem:epoch:certificate-failure-versus-indecisive-enclosure}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{arch}{tilt-versus-export}{Tilt Strength versus Export Capacity}
    \frontierstatus{Open; the two dials are independent by construction and
    their interaction is unmeasured.}
    Tilt strength decides how sharply standing divides a source's unit;
    emission decides how much of that source's history travels at all.  They
    are orthogonal --- emission scales carriage without touching apportionment
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:emission-certificate-transfer}) --- and at $t=0$ they
    do not interact at all.

    \frontieropen{Measure whether the two dials should be calibrated jointly.
    A network of many faded sources is quiet for a reason emission explains;
    the same network at a low rung is quiet for a different reason, and a
    reader seeing only the standing field cannot tell which.}

    \frontierxref{def:epoch:source-emission,def:epoch:tilt-backoff-grid,%
    frontier:emission-sag-calibration}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{terminal-standing-regression}{Terminal Standing Regression}
    \frontierpriority{Medium --- a deployment obligation, not a Layer-1 gap.}
    Terminal consumers --- feed, reward, CAN, bridge --- read the published
    standing and nothing else.  Edition 5 changes the values that field takes
    without changing its type, so every terminal formula still compiles and
    every terminal output moves.

    \frontieropen{Regress each terminal consumer against the published standing
    across the edition boundary, and publish the deltas.  The specific hazard
    is a consumer whose calibration was implicitly fitted to Edition-4 standing
    distributions and which is now mis-tuned without failing anything.}

    \frontierxref{ver:standing:terminal-regression,%
    post:transport:guild-grant}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{canonical-standing-encoding}{Canonical Standing Encoding}
    \frontierpriority{High --- replay is only as good as the encoding.}
    Any participant reproduces the epoch's standing from the package
    (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package}), which requires that
    everyone agree bit-for-bit on how the inputs are encoded.

    \frontieropen{Fix the canonical encoding of the base allocation matrix, the
    depth mass, the emission fractions and the certificate, including
    ordering, rational representation and rounding disclosure.  Until it is
    fixed, replay agreement is a convention rather than a guarantee.}

    \frontierxref{subsec:deployment:canonical-standing-encoding,%
    ver:standing:canonical-encoding}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{calib}{canonical-standing-replay}{Canonical Standing Replay}
    \frontierpriority{High --- paired with the encoding.}
    Replay must be decidable, not merely possible: two honest participants
    reproducing the same package must agree on whether a certificate passed,
    including in the indecisive case.

    \frontieropen{Specify the replay procedure and its tolerance, and state
    which disagreements are protocol faults and which are permitted numerical
    slack.  A replay that can disagree about an indecisive enclosure without
    either side being wrong is a governance question, not an arithmetic one
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:certificate-failure-versus-indecisive-enclosure}).}

    \frontierxref{frontier:canonical-standing-encoding,%
    prop:scalability:conserved-standing-verifiability}
\end{frontier}

\subsection{Architectural Extensions}
\label{subsec:frontiers:architectural}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

These items strengthen or scale Layer-1 without changing the correctness of
the present finite exact definition.

\begin{frontier}{arch}{boundary-mechanism}{Boundary Set-Consensus and Final-Set Search}
    \frontierstatus{Design obligation; elevated by epoch-quantized title.}
    Title, gate, and standing read epoch membership, so the boundary
    mechanism is the single trust concentration point.  It must agree the
    accepted write set~$\actsequence{k}$ and edge set~$E_k$, the final ledger, and the
    final standing package, with no order consensus beyond causal validity
    (\zcref{rem:introduction:mechanism-agnostic} is load-bearing), the
    edge-blind accountability contract of
    \zcref{post:graph:boundary-accountability}, and attested boundary
    timestamps.  It also owns the final-set \emph{search}: validity of a
    proposed set is reproducible, but which valid set is selected is a
    separate problem, the candidate-set search is not part of the public
    ontology, and the mechanism must state a final-set solver availability
    target and its behavior if no valid set is found before the maximum
    duration.  Centralized phase: certificate accountability plus duration
    liveness only; the decentralized mechanism is where non-censorship
    becomes a property instead of a posture.
    \frontierxref{post:graph:boundary-accountability,%
    def:graph:dependent-act-set,post:epoch:final-edge-set,%
    rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance,post:introduction:epoch-edge-set,%
    rem:scalability:boundary-search-cost}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{arch}{high-dimensional-sentiment}{High-Dimensional Sentiment
    Tensors}
    With $k\geq3$ free parameters (e.g.\ valence / arousal / dominance), the
    intrinsic rank lifts to~3, potentially producing a non-degenerate
    $3\times3$ determinant and eliminating the dual-view split. Path composition
    generalizes to $3\times3$ multiplication ($O(27)$ per edge); the determinant
    sign generalizes to $\operatorname{sgn}(\det M)$ for the full $3\times3$
    path-view matrix, and the double cover BFS parity construction remains valid.
    Generalized boundary damping would require a multivariate temporal entropy ---
    whether the joint Shannon entropy of a $k$-dimensional maturity vector, the
    sum of marginal binary entropies, or a coupling-aware functional preserving the
    single-observable calibration of
    \zcref{frontier:inverse-temperature-optimisation} --- is itself part of this
    extension.
    \frontierxref{prop:graph:rank-two-constraint,%
    lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{arch}{typed-sign-transport}{Typed Sign Transport Beyond
    \texorpdfstring{$\mathbb{Z}_2$}{Z2} Parity}
    v0.18.3 separates the two sign consumers already present in the
    $2\times2$ path view: coherence $\operatorname{sgn}(p_dp_i)$ composes,
    while stance gates locally (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}).  A richer
    extension would transport more than the determinant bit --- for example,
    the signed-SVD rotation phase or a cone in mode-angle space --- and use
    that phase to distinguish irony, shared aversion, and person-directed
    condemnation at path level.  This is intentionally outside the Layer-1
    core: rotation data is order-sensitive and not Dijkstra-factorized at
    $\divpref=\tfrac12$, so any such extension must either be terminal/guild
    owned or re-prove the ordered-replay determinism properties.
    \frontierxref{def:graph:signed-svd,lem:graph:quadrant-law,%
    def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Standing Evaluation at Scale]{arch}{exact-conserved-evaluation}%
    {Standing Evaluation at Scale}
    \frontierpriority{Medium --- an engineering question with a proved
    bound, not an unbounded one.}
    The solve is linear in $\nnz_k$ per pass at a published pass count
    (\zcref{thm:scalability:conserved-equilibrium-cost}), so a dense
    projection costs its own density and no more
    (\zcref{rem:scalability:dense-projection-cost}).  What is open is
    engineering, not asymptotics: whether that bound is \emph{achievable}
    at deployment scale in the boundary duration available, on real
    hardware, with real memory locality.

    \frontieropen{Build and benchmark the sparse conserved solve at scale:
    layout of the base matrix, blocking of the hop products, cache
    behaviour of the mediant, and distribution of the pass across workers.
    Publish the size at which one epoch's solve stops fitting the boundary
    duration, and what fails first.}

    \frontierremedy{No sparsification of the base matrix is permitted.
    Dropping a relation because it is small changes standing, and would
    require a new standing definition rather than an implementation note ---
    the same prohibition the retired candidate-cap question carried, for the
    same reason.}

    \frontierxref{thm:scalability:conserved-equilibrium-cost,%
    prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost,%
    rem:scalability:dense-projection-cost}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Exact Incremental Equilibrium Solver]{arch}{incremental-equilibrium-solver}%
    {Exact Incremental Equilibrium Solver}
    \frontierstatus{Exact implementation extension; replaces the retired
    constant-step and drift-ledger questions.}
    A deployment recomputes standing per epoch, but may reuse exact
    projection maintenance, SCC invalidation, trial-set deltas, the previous
    final point as a warm start, previous interval boxes as candidate
    subdivisions, and exact component reuse --- with no semantic dependence
    on prior standing (\zcref{prop:scalability:exact-component-reuse,%
    rem:scalability:warm-start-neutrality}).

    \frontieropen{Prove deterministic equality between the incremental and
    from-scratch results, then benchmark the work reduction across epoch and
    trial-set deltas.}

    \frontierxref{prop:scalability:exact-component-reuse,%
    prop:scalability:transport-scc-decomposition,%
    rem:scalability:warm-start-neutrality}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{arch}{allocation-split-invariance}{Allocation Invariance Under Actor Splitting}
    \frontierstatus{Open; a nonclaim, not a gap in a proof.}
    Conservation closes cross-target cloning: a source disposes of one unit
    over self and all recipients, so multiplying recipients divides regard
    (\zcref{thm:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation}).  Edition~4 left this
    axis explicitly open, and Edition~5 closes it by construction.

    What remains open is the \emph{other} axis.  Whether an Actor fragmenting
    its ledger and its acts across several addresses can change any standing
    outcome is a property of the fold, resolution and tilt layers jointly, and
    conservation alone does not settle it: row-stochasticity constrains each
    row, not the number of rows.

    \frontieropen{Determine whether the allocation construction is invariant
    under Actor splitting, and under which hypotheses.  A positive answer needs
    an explicit theorem plus split fixtures; a negative answer needs the
    quantified advantage.  Until one exists, conservation must not be cited as
    splitting invariance.}

    \frontierremedy{The collision register carries the word row
    \emph{conservation vs Sybil-invariance}, and the claim is policed there.}

    \frontierxref{thm:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation,%
    rem:comparator:conserved-allocation-scope,%
    frontier:source-root-eligibility}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{arch}{tilted-monotonicity}{Monotonicity Under Tilted Feedback}
    \frontierstatus{Open at $\tiltstrength{k}>0$; proved at the anchor.}
    At the anchor rung the transport is state-independent and a burn provably
    raises the standing of everyone the burner's allocation reaches
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:no-tilt-commitment-monotonicity}).  At any positive
    rung the transport depends on the state it computes, and a burn
    re-apportions every row its mass passes through.

    Edition~4 asserted monotonicity without examining coupled feedback.  This
    frontier records the honest replacement: an open problem where there was an
    unexamined theorem.

    \frontieropen{Determine whether final standing is monotone in an underlying
    burn or accepted act at positive tilt strength, or exhibit a certified
    configuration where it is not.  Note that a counterexample would not
    threaten safety --- the certificate bounds the derivative's magnitude
    either way --- but it would bear on whether the mechanism can be described
    as rewarding commitment without qualification.}

    \frontierxref{prop:epoch:no-tilt-commitment-monotonicity,%
    pty:transport:final-standing-input-monotonicity,%
    frontier:tilt-profile-charter}
\end{frontier}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Guild Design Choices}
\label{subsec:frontiers:guild}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

These are Layer-2 degrees of freedom the protocol deliberately delegates
(\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}); their read-sites are terminal, so a guild may
reimplement them freely. The open content is ``which choice is good,'' owned by the
guild, not a Layer-1 defect.

\begin{frontier}{guild}{membership-policy}{Chat Membership and Expulsion Policy}
    Layer~1 records departure and de-invitation unconditionally; force is
    a published Layer-2 policy over the canonical fold
    (\zcref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold}).  Open content, all
    guild-owned: the authority set (inviter-only, genesis-participant,
    moderator quorum, standing-weighted vote over members' \standing{}
    read terminally); ban semantics (does a recognized De-invite defeat
    only current membership, or also $\prec$-later Participant edges);
    contested-expulsion display (De-invite density is a natural input to
    the terminal notoriety field, \zcref{frontier:notoriety-field}); and
    whether policy-recognized De-invites should discount the Chat's own
    conduits in the guild's sorting.  All read-sites are terminal;
    every choice must be published per
    \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}.
    \frontierxref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold,%
    rem:nodes:membership-is-terminal,post:transport:guild-grant,%
    frontier:notoriety-field}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{guild}{deep-composition}{Deep Composition Profiles}
    At what depth does the matrix CAN's correction
    (\zcref{subsec:can:matrix-extension}) exceed 5\%? At depth~1: $\sim 1.8\%$. At
    depth~2: $\sim 3$--$5\%$. Most compositions terminate at depth 1--2: if fewer
    than 5\% exceed depth~2 in a guild, the scalar CAN suffices indefinitely for
    that guild. This also subsumes the cross-shard context-independence
    question. Empirical target: depth distribution
    in deployed guild graphs. Guilds with deep compositions must still satisfy the
    three mandatory structural invariants
    (\zcref{def:can:mandatory-guild-invariants}).
    \frontierxref{subsec:can:matrix-extension}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{guild}{svd-corrected-transmission}{SVD-Corrected Scalar
    Transmission}
    The intermediate option $\trans{n}=\sat{\svdone{\overline{\mathbf{W}}(n)}}$
    yields $\sim 1\%$ correction at depth~1 relative to the arithmetic-mean
    baseline (\zcref{rem:can:implicit-diversity-bonus}), at the cost of one
    $3\times3$ SVD per composition node. Whether 1\% precision justifies the SVD at
    every composition node is a guild cost--benefit question.
    \frontierxref{rem:can:implicit-diversity-bonus}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{guild}{can-aggregation-function}{CAN Aggregation Function}
    The aggregation function for $\meanedgenorm{n}$ is a guild choice: arithmetic
    mean (canonical default), geometric (penalizes weak links), harmonic, or
    maximum (dominant dependency). All four preserve $\trans{n}<1$ and satisfy the
    mandatory depth-decay invariant (\zcref{thm:can:depth-decay}). The choice tunes
    what a guild considers high-quality curation; it must be published in full
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}).
    \frontierxref{def:can:transmission-coefficient}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{guild}{bridge-multi-bridge}{Multi-Bridge Circuit Composition}
    The campaign scalar (\zcref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar}) prices a single bridge
    per target via the outer $\max_B$. Navigational delivery physically supports
    multi-bridge chains $T\to B_1\to B_2\to A$ where neither bridge alone completes
    the circuit. Single-bridge is the canonical default composition rule, a Layer-2
    choice in the sense of \zcref{frontier:can-aggregation-function}: the three
    channel values are Layer-1 primitives, and a guild may publish a multi-bridge
    rule consuming them (\zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}). The open content is
    the attribution theory --- a cooperative game over complementary intermediaries
    whose credit split is a Shapley value with no canonical counterfactual. By
    \zcref{ins:bridge:magnitude-boundary} this is the same marginal-contribution
    decomposition required by magnitude-sensitive distribution and exact $I_C$
    responsibility: a guild that constructs the multi-bridge Shapley value solves
    all three at once. Open: characterise the game; determine whether a
    guild-publishable decomposition preserves the
    \zcref[range]{sec:sorting,sec:transport} guarantees that the single-bridge default
    inherits (\zcref{prop:bridge:sc-inheritance}); bound the circuit length at which
    device-local tractability (\zcref{subsec:deployment:device-local}) fails.
    \frontierxref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar,ins:bridge:magnitude-boundary,%
    def:bridge:realizing-active-influence,frontier:can-aggregation-function}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{guild}{bridge-eligibility-cliff}{Consent Near-Cancellation
    Eligibility Cliff}
    When $\posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B}\approx\negreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B}$ for the
    optimal bridge, $\consent{A,B}$ is near zero and a single edge can toggle the
    inner $\arg\max_B$ (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-path}). By
    \zcref{prop:bridge:discrete-structure-sensitivity} this flip is the
    \emph{primary} mechanism by which the three-channel structure reaches
    per-creator distribution. Graceful degradation
    (\zcref{rem:bridge:eligibility-cliff-primary}) bounds the impact on the gate and
    signal, but the impact on creator \emph{shares} is genuinely discontinuous.
    Open: characterise argmax-flip frequency under realistic graph growth;
    determine whether a smoothing rule (e.g.\ top-$k$ bridge ensembling, a Layer-2
    composition choice) reduces share volatility without reintroducing the
    redundancy amplification the single-bridge $\max$ prevents
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:max-product-path-scoring}). A monitoring and calibration
    target for the centralized phase.
    The decision procedure is pre-stated: the phase publishes an
    argmax-flip-rate threshold together with a share-volatility companion
    (the $\ell_1$ distance between consecutive normalized share vectors,
    both computable from epoch-certificate data). If exceeded, the
    operator publishes a \emph{reference} top-$k$ ensemble composition
    rule --- still terminal, still optional under
    \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant} --- and only then weighs
    commissioning the marginal-contribution decomposition of
    \zcref{ins:bridge:magnitude-boundary}. The protocol thereby commits
    its reaction function, never the research program.
    \frontierxref{prop:bridge:discrete-structure-sensitivity,%
    rem:bridge:eligibility-cliff-primary,def:bridge:realizing-path}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{guild}{bridge-delivery-semantics}{Bridge Delivery Semantics}
    The campaign scalar prices endorsement-circuit \emph{quality}, not traversal.
    Whether a community member actually navigates through the bridge, and what value
    that yields, is not a protocol quantity --- the advertiser observes
    $\campaignscalar{A}$, funds $\guildpool$, and the market is the feedback loop.
    The trivial reading is settled by definition: an \emph{observed} traversal is a
    private measurement, not a graph quantity, so it cannot enter a self-sufficient
    edge record (\zcref{subsec:deployment:sufficiency}). The non-trivial question is
    \emph{encoding}: whether traversal can be promoted to a published, reproducible
    graph quantity (e.g.\ a new edge type recording navigation, under the same
    parity and sufficiency discipline) that a guild may consume in a Layer-2 rule
    without reintroducing a private behavioral signal. Open: exhibit such an
    encoding and its sufficiency record, or prove none can satisfy the
    self-sufficient-record requirement without collapsing into a click-through
    proxy.
    \frontierxref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar,%
    subsec:introduction:verification-model,subsec:deployment:sufficiency}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{guild}{notoriety-field}{Terminal Notoriety / Condemnation Field}
    The Vouch Predicate removes coherent condemnation $(-,-)$ from standing
    endorsement while preserving the record as a public structural fact
    (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}).  A guild may therefore publish a
    terminal \emph{notoriety} or condemnation field that aggregates stance-negative
    actor-directed records for display, dispute routing, moderation policy, or
    advertiser avoidance, without feeding it back into admission.  Open content:
    which terminal aggregation is fair --- max-product, sum-of-paths, signed
    DeGroot, or a separate negative-register readout --- and how to prevent
    redundancy amplification while preserving the accountability value of public
    criticism.
    \frontierxref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,rem:graph:sign-semantics,%
    post:transport:guild-grant,tbl:symbols:boundary}
\end{frontier}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Ceiling Witnesses}
\label{subsec:frontiers:witness}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

These are bounded instances of a \emph{proved} \S1--\S2 structural limit
(accountability cost, \zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}; or privacy of
departure, \zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}): accountability cost is
endogenous, respects the relabeling gauge, and therefore deters but never
anchors. The limitation itself is established in \zcref{sec:comparator}
(\zcref{rem:comparator:structural-ceiling}) and is \emph{not} an open problem ---
it is closed as a limitation. What is open here is a \emph{quantity}: how large the
residual exposure is, and whether a Layer-2 remedy is warranted. Neither witness
blocks any Layer-1 deployment guarantee.

\begin{frontier}{witness}{boundary-censorship}{Boundary Censorship}
    \frontierstatus{Boundary-accountability witness.}
    A centralized host can silently decline to write cancels, competitors, or
    any other valid dependent set while accepting a conflicting one.  The
    validity of the accepted~$\actsequence{k}$ is reproducible, but rejected candidate
    sets are not Layer-1 objects and Layer~1 has no audit of the full demand
    set.  The mitigations are duration bounds, the safety clamp plus
    announcement lead, door-headroom/regime visibility, and the decentralized
    boundary mechanism, which is the structural remedy.  They make the
    exposure bounded and named, not impossible.
    \frontierxref{def:network:door-headroom,rem:epoch:consent-exposure,%
    post:graph:boundary-accountability,def:epoch:policy-floor,%
    rem:gates:guild-funding}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{witness}{depleted-source-ballast}{Depleted-Source Ballast}
    \frontierstatus{Concrete witness for
    \zcref{frontier:source-root-eligibility}; dynamically certifiable,
    economically unresolved.}
    Under the current full-pair source rule, an Actor with $\burnbal{u}=0$
    and large $\actcount{u}$ may still originate a path whose mediant
    contribution is pure denominator mass:
    \[
        \bigl(0,\; W_{\mathrm{end}}^{(k)}(u\to i)\,\actcount{u}\bigr).
    \]
    The target may be diluted substantially even though the source has no
    current residual balance.  This does not violate the standing hull or the
    stage contraction theorem
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull,%
    thm:dynamics:certified-conserved-standing-uniqueness}); it witnesses a different
    question --- whether historical action mass should remain fully
    exportable without current residual backing.

    \frontieropen{Measure prevalence and worst-case target movement under the
    current full-pair rule; compare the candidate source-root policies of
    \zcref{frontier:source-root-eligibility}.}

    \frontierxref{frontier:source-root-eligibility,%
    prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{witness}{settlement-tie-fabrication}{Collusive Settlement-Tie
    Fabrication}
    \frontierpriority{Low. Standing-channel impact filtered and dominated to negligibility;
    surviving exposure terminal/Layer-2.}
    \frontierstatus{Bounded ceiling-witness; the open content is a cohort-size
    bound, not a deployment hazard.}

    The exploit is an \emph{inflation} of a colluding cohort, not a gate quirk
    favouring third parties: a colluding pair authors Accept/Ratify edges that look
    recognized but back no consummated sale, and the recognition-blind double cover
    BFS flows the resulting commercial \emph{tie} as endorsement
    (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation}). The beneficiaries are the colluders;
    the harmed parties are honest creators they out-compete in the normalized reward
    pool, advertisers who pay for a fabricated bridge tie, and users shown a false
    commercial-reputation conjunction.

    \textbf{The standing channel is now filtered before it is dominated.}
    After \zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}, settlement edges inject standing
    endorsement only if the relevant Accept/Ratify records are stance-positive.
    Coerced, reluctant, or unfair records remain public and may affect terminal
    guild policy, but they do not carry source rate into standing.  The residual
    standing-channel exploit is limited to stance-positive fabricated ties:
    the colluders must publicly author records that look like genuine praise or
    satisfaction.

    Conditional on passing that vouch gate, endorsement flow is source$\to$target,
    so an edge $j$ authors lifts
    \emph{another} actor and never $j$ itself
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:author-directed-allocation,prop:nodes:self-loop-neutral}): solo
    Accept-and-Rescind self-inflation is void. What survives requires collusion and
    is then dominated by (1)~irrevocable action-count dilution
    (\zcref{cor:scalability:spam-resistance}, mechanism~4); (2)~the hull bound
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}), which permits gifting standing but
    not manufacturing it; (3)~the \tierhalf{} routing of settlement
    edges ($\detscore{}\approx0.20$) versus \tierfull{} honest endorsement
    ($\approx0.35$), making fabricated settlement a strictly \emph{worse} standing
    vector than honest endorsement at equal cost. Title is unaffected: recognition
    gates transfer on epoch-quantized consent (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition},
    clauses (iii)--(v)), so the same edges move no owner
    (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}).

    \textbf{The surviving exposure is terminal/Layer-2, with a narrower
    standing residual.} After the stance-negative cases are projection-excluded
    and the remaining stance-positive standing channel is dominated, what remains
    is the fabricated commercial tie read \emph{directly}
    --- not through $\standing{}$ --- by terminal consumers: the
    commercial-reputation conjunction read for display, and the bridge transport's
    endorsement/consent channels (\zcref{app:bridge}). The injection nonetheless
    rides a \emph{Layer-1} traversal (the recognition-blind double cover BFS), and
    that traversal \emph{cannot} be gated at Layer~1: doing so would couple a local,
    order-free traversal to global settlement state and break
    \zcref{lem:epoch:double-cover-bfs-correctness}. This is precisely why the
    boundary ledger flags it as the single ``feedback-but-terminally-consumed cell''
    (\zcref{rem:transport:guild-grant-preconditions}): Layer-1 locus, Layer-2 remedy.

    \frontieropen{(1)~Bound the fabricated commercial tie a colluding cohort can
    stamp through unrecognized settlements, as a function of cohort size and the
    vouch gate, \tierhalf{}/conjunction/dilution defenses. (2)~Determine whether those defenses
    suffice under coordination, or whether a Layer-2 cancel-heavy discount is
    warranted --- the natural home, since the surviving consumers are terminal.}
    \frontierremedy{If warranted, a Layer-2 guild-side cancel-heavy discount per
    \zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}; Offer reviews
    (\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}) supply its natural terminal evidence
    channel. Gating the BFS is \emph{not} a candidate
    (it would break \zcref{lem:epoch:double-cover-bfs-correctness}).}
    \frontierxref{rem:epoch:author-directed-allocation,rem:graph:settlement-reputation,%
    prop:epoch:final-standing-hull,cor:scalability:spam-resistance,%
    subsec:necessity:settlement-half-routing,alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs,%
    post:comparator:accountability-cost,def:comparator:source-faithful,%
    subsec:necessity:handshake-actor-incidence}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{witness}{item-genesis}{Referent Binding of Registered Items}
    \frontierpriority{Low--moderate. Identity is resolved; the open
    content is a deterrence bound.}
    \frontierstatus{Witness of the proved S-edge ceiling: Item identity
    is declarative (\zcref{def:graph:item-genesis-act}), so contested genesis
    is structurally impossible; only the referent question remains.}
    Two actors may register ``the same'' physical referent as two
    Items; no internal mechanism can decide which listing is real,
    because any in-graph referent test is a node the adversary writes
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:the-cut-no-mechanism-can-make}). Duplicate
    listing is deterred by accountability cost
    (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}) and resolved out-of-band by the same human look
    that makes every S-edge cut (\zcref{rem:graph:item-identity-limit}).
    \frontieropen{Bound the fabricated-listing surface: the rate at
    which duplicate or referent-free Items can accumulate title and
    settlement history as a function of cohort size, under the
    \tierhalf{}/dilution defenses shared with
    \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}.}
    \frontierremedy{Guild-side contested-listing discount, sharing the
    cancel-heavy channel of \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication};
    Reviews of the Item and its Offers
    (\zcref{rem:graph:reviews-commentary}) supply the terminal evidence.
    Gating recognition on referent proofs is \emph{not} a candidate ---
    it would import an identity authority
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:the-detector}).}
    \frontierxref{def:graph:item-genesis-act,rem:graph:item-identity-limit,%
    thm:graph:epoch-title-fold,frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{witness}{structural-residue-reidentification}%
    {Structural-Residue Re-Identification of a Departed Husk}
    \frontierpriority{Low--moderate. Privacy-only; the exposed quantity is, by
    construction, the same quantity that forbids the remedy.}
    \frontierstatus{Bounded ceiling-witness of the privacy-of-departure floor
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}). The open content is a quantity --- how
    identifiable, below what connectivity --- not a question of whether something
    breaks; and the bound is \emph{self-aligning}, which makes this a structural
    feature in the register of \zcref{ins:introduction:the-cut-no-mechanism-can-make},
    not a defect to engineer away.}

    \emph{Setting.} \zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}. The exposure and
    the duty-to-retain are one monotone quantity in connectivity: the same
    structural reliance that preserves a husk also supplies its re-identification
    surface. The open content is the bound.

    \frontieropen{(1)~Characterize a husk's re-identifiability as a function of its
    degree, standing $\standing{}$, and rate-hull, under a stated adversary
    side-information model. (2)~Locate the connectivity threshold below which a husk
    is $k$-anonymous among near-automorphic peers (the regime where
    \zcref{rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge} confers cover), giving a quantitative
    boundary between the two regimes above. (3)~Determine whether a Layer-2 custody
    service can add structural obfuscation for the departing actor without touching
    the immutable structural record others depend on.}
    \frontierremedy{Layer-2 only, and partial by construction. Identity-severance and
    content-erasure are already discharged (\zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave});
    further obfuscation is a Layer-2 service choice. Gating or perturbing the
    structural record at Layer~1 is \emph{not} a candidate: it would dissolve the
    dependency the residue exists to honour, and couple a local order-free record to
    global structure, exactly the move forbidden at
    \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}.}
    \frontierxref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave,ins:introduction:the-floor-we-name,%
    def:graph:act-payload-projection,rem:graph:act-payload-removal-neutrality,%
    rem:comparator:topology-is-gauge,prop:epoch:final-standing-hull,%
    def:comparator:frame-binding}
\end{frontier}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Layer-0 Reserve-Economy Pointers}
\label{subsec:frontiers:pointers}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\frontierpointer{Layer-0 Reserve-Economy Open Problems}
Three open problems are reserve-economy questions owned by \emph{Peer Attestation}
(Layer~0), not the network: optimal maturity-announcement timing, bootstrap-class
confidence-signal fidelity (a question about the secondary-market price
$\confprice{d}$, a Layer-0 surface quantity), and operator deposit disambiguation.
The network has no count content to add to any of them; they are recorded here only
as pointers. See \attestationcref{open:operator-disambiguation} and the maturity
material of \attestationcref{rem:maturity:announcement-timing},
\attestationcref{rem:maturity:confidence-signal}. The network's only stake in this
cluster is the frozen-factor timing half
(\zcref{frontier:leverage-timing}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Proposed Investigations}
\label{subsec:frontiers:investigations}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Each states a graph configuration, a target computation, and --- where it is a
continuous parameter sweep --- an explicit acceptance criterion that would trigger a
design decision. These are structured numerical exercises with deterministic
targets, distinct from the open mathematical questions above; numerical derivations
are deferred to empirical study.

\begin{frontier}{invest}{can-depth-decay}{CAN Depth Decay at Depth~2}
    \emph{Setup.} Compose the Review ($r_B$, $\canval{} \numrel{result.can.bob.num}$) and Tag ($g_C$,
    $\canval{} \numrel{result.can.carol.num}$) nodes from the reference graph
    (\zcref{subsec:verification:reference-graph}) under a hypothetical depth-2 node
    $n_{\mathrm{eval}}$, with outgoing edge norms $1.5$ and $1.6$ (both at or above
    the always-active floor of \zcref{lem:graph:non-vanishing-norm}).
    \emph{Target.} (1)~Compute $\meanedgenorm{n_{\mathrm{eval}}}$ and
    $\trans{n_{\mathrm{eval}}}$. (2)~Determine $\redundancy{n_{\mathrm{eval}}}$:
    under dependency induction (\zcref{def:can:dependency-induction}) the leaf sets
    $\set{e_3,e_4}$ and $\set{e_5,e_6}$ are \emph{disjoint edge-legs}, so
    $\redundancy{}=1$; add a variant registering $e_3$ under both children to
    exhibit $\redundancy{}<1$. (3)~Verify
    $\canval{n_{\mathrm{eval}}}<\max(\numval{result.can.bob.num},\numval{result.can.carol.num})$
    (\zcref{thm:can:depth-decay}).
    \frontierxref{def:can:intrinsic-value,thm:can:depth-decay,%
    subsec:verification:can-attribution}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[M-payload Worst-Case Calibration]{invest}{payload-worst-case-calibration}%
    {$\maxpayload$ Worst-Case Calibration}
    \emph{Setup.} Every edge may carry $\maxpayload$ bytes
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-projection}); one edge costs one action
    (\zcref{rem:graph:payload-size-not-act-cost}).
    \emph{Target.} Size $\maxpayload$ so the depth-$L$ ego-network remains
    device-local-cacheable (\zcref{subsec:deployment:device-local}) at
    realistic degree distributions under worst-case act payload use.
    \emph{Acceptance criterion.} Reject any $\maxpayload$ whose worst-case
    depth-4 cache exceeds a published device budget.
\end{frontier}


\begin{frontier}[Polarization x Maturity Interaction]{invest}{polarization-maturity}%
    {Polarization $\times$ Maturity Interaction}
    \emph{Setup.} New actor Dave posts an opposing Opinion on $\mathrm{Profile}_A$:
    $p_d=-0.8$, $p_i=0.6$, $\tau=0.7$. Tribal, full mask; first leg of a canonical
    2-hop endorsement path (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-fold-cell}).
    \emph{Target.} (1)~Confirm $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F$ is identical for $p_d=\pm0.8$
    (sign invariance under \AttrView{}). (2)~Confirm $|\det(\pathview{})|$ identical.
    (3)~Confirm $\detsign{e}=-1$ (\zcref{rem:graph:sign-semantics}).
    (4)~Verify the Polarization Floor in both views
    (\zcref{prop:graph:polarization-floor}). (5)~Confirm the canonical path has
    parity $(-1)(+1)=-1$, so it is \emph{not} an admissible endorsement path and
    the double cover BFS returns
    $\transportentry{\text{Dave}}{\text{Alice}}=\posreg{\text{Alice}}=0$ --- blocked by
    \emph{parity}, contrast \zcref{ver:parity:two-hop-example}.
    \frontierxref{def:graph:determinant-sign,cor:graph:path-parity-sign,%
    prop:graph:polarization-floor}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Licensing x Guild Interaction]{invest}{licensing-guild}%
    {Licensing $\times$ Guild Interaction}
    \emph{Setup.} Alice's Photo has $l_{ij}=1$. Assume $\numeraire=0.1$ and a network admitting
    $\standing{}=0.400$ ($\ampfactor{}=5.0$, so values lie inside the hull,
    \zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}; not the reference graph, max rate
    $0.333$). Compare $R_C$ across: (i)~$l_{ij}=0$, $\standing{}=0.400$;
    (ii)~$l_{ij}=1$, $\standing{}=0.400$; (iii)~$l_{ij}=1$, $\standing{}=0.050$
    ($\ampfactor{}=1.5$).
    \emph{Target.} Show $\standing{C}$ provides continuously graded amplification
    partially offsetting licensing penalties, magnitude set by burn history
    independently of guild topology; confirm (ii) retains a meaningfully higher
    reward than (iii)
    (\zcref{pty:transport:final-standing-input-monotonicity}).
    \frontierxref{rem:content:license-guild-interaction,%
    eq:transport:reward-formula}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Boundary x Auction Interaction]{invest}{boundary-auction}%
    {Boundary $\times$ Auction Interaction}
    \emph{Setup.} Carol bids on Sneakers: $g=0.8$, $u=0.6$. Compare $\tau=0.6$ vs.\
    $\tau=0.2$.
    \emph{Target.} (1)~Confirm CAN base values identical (atemporal \AttrView{}).
    (2)~Compute boundary-observed $\dampedweight{e}$ (differ via $\tentropy{}$).
    (3)~Verify epoch-entropy damping
    (\zcref{thm:transport:epoch-entropy-damping}): mid-career bids at
    $\tau\approx0.5$ raise $\epochentropy{C}$ and lower
    $\boltzfactor{\epochentropy{C}}$.
    \frontierxref{thm:transport:epoch-entropy-damping,eq:transport:epoch-entropy}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[beta Sensitivity Sweep]{invest}{beta-sweep}{$\invtemp$
    Sensitivity Sweep}
    \emph{Setup.} Reference graph, $\invtemp\in\set{0.5,1.0,1.386,2.0,3.0}$.
    \emph{Target.} (1)~Confirm CAN values $\invtemp$-invariant. (2)~Confirm
    $\tau=0$ edges unaffected. (3)~Show reward concentration on near-zero-entropy
    contributors as $\invtemp$ rises. (4)~Confirm $\dampedweight{e}$ is identical
    across feed-ranking and endorsement-flow BFS. (5)~\emph{Acceptance criterion.}
    Cross-cluster discovery failure at high $\invtemp$ is confirmed if the fraction
    of length-4 cross-tier paths surviving above $\wspam$ falls below a published
    target (e.g.\ below $1\%$ of the $\invtemp=2\ln2$ baseline) at $\invtemp=3.0$;
    absent such a threshold the sweep documents a trend but triggers no
    recalibration. Complements \zcref{frontier:inverse-temperature-optimisation}.
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Effective Door-Price Sensitivity Sweep]{invest}{floor-sweep}%
    {$\partfloor\numeraire$ Sensitivity Sweep}
    \emph{Setup.} Reference graph,
    $\numeraire\in\set{0.01,0.05,0.10,0.20,0.50}$.
    \emph{Target.} (1)~Compute $\safefloor$ and stamps per actor; confirm the
    gate-axis co-scaling law. (2)~Identify the $\numeraire$ at which Dave
    ($\standing{}=0.200$) is frozen below the safety wall. (3)~Compute door
    headroom $\doorheadroom{k}$. (4)~Confirm the entire Path and Attribution Views are
    $\numeraire$-invariant. (5)~\emph{Acceptance criterion.} Reject on
    barrier-to-entry grounds if it blocks more than a published fraction of
    reference actors (e.g.\ any $\partfloor\numeraire>\max_j\commitrate{j}$); reject on
    resource grounds if packed band actions exceed a published per-epoch
    headroom ceiling. Content update to the split-dial calibration architecture
    deferred to the calibration commit. Complements \zcref{frontier:floor-calibration}.
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[eta Sensitivity Sweep]{invest}{eta-sweep}{$\bleedparam$
    Sensitivity Sweep}
    \emph{Setup.} \tiermarginal{} Epistemic edge $e_7$,
    $\bleedparam\in\set{0.01,0.05,0.10,0.15}$. \AttrView{} is
    $\bleedparam$-invariant.
    \emph{Target.} Compute $\det(\pathview{e_7})$ and $\detscore{e_7}$; the
    determinant is linear in $\bleedparam$, so $\detscore{}\sim\sqrt{\bleedparam}$
    and the tier gap $\sim 1/\sqrt{\bleedparam}$ ($\sim 10\times$ at $0.01$;
    $\sim 4.5\times$ at $0.05$; $\sim 2.6\times$ at $0.15$).
    \emph{Acceptance criterion.} Reject if the tier gap falls below the
    spam-resistance margin (weakest legitimate \tiermarginal{} weight ceasing to
    exceed $\wspam$ by the published factor, reference $\approx3\times$) or rises so
    high that cross-domain discovery collapses below the serendipity target of
    \zcref{cor:sorting:serendipity-conditions}. Complements
    \zcref{frontier:eta-calibration}.
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}{invest}{can-aggregation-sensitivity}{CAN Aggregation Function
    Sensitivity}
    \emph{Setup.} Bob's Review node $r_B$, leg norms $1.733$ and $1.662$. Recompute
    $\trans{r_B}$, $\canval{r_B}$ under arithmetic mean (default, $\trans{} \numrel{result.can.bob_trans.num}$),
    geometric ($0.629$), harmonic ($0.629$), and maximum ($0.634$).
    \emph{Target.} (1)~Verify all four preserve $\trans{}<1$ and depth decay for
    $r_B$. (2)~Quantify the spread in $\canval{r_B}$. (3)~Determine which most
    closely matches the matrix CAN at depth~1, giving an empirical argument for
    guild selection (\zcref{frontier:can-aggregation-function}). (4)~Confirm all four
    comply with the mandatory CAN invariants
    (\zcref{subsec:transport:guild-model}). Complements
    \zcref{frontier:can-aggregation-function}.
\end{frontier}


\begin{frontier}[Shared Standing Fixture Agreement]{invest}{shared-standing-fixture}%
    {Shared Standing Fixture Agreement}
    \emph{Setup.} Run \texttt{peer\_rederive4.py} and \texttt{peer\_Vcert2.py}
    on the same exact JSON fixture using independent mathematical
    implementations.
    \emph{Target.} The high-precision rederived equilibrium agrees with the
    independently computed one to within the certified residual bound
    (\zcref{lem:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure}), and likewise for
    the emission diagonal, the certificate value and verdict, the epoch
    stamp, headroom, and W1/W2 verdicts.  This is the strongest integration
    test for the paper suite.
    \frontierxref{lem:dynamics:fixed-point-residual-enclosure,%
    def:epoch:final-standing,frontier:transport-fixtures}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Nontrivial Depth-Stage Coverage]{invest}{depth-coverage}%
    {Nontrivial Depth-Stage Coverage}
    \emph{Setup.} Ensure the depth-three and depth-four fixtures are
    nontrivial.
    \emph{Target.} Record the exact-depth candidate count, selected-pair
    count, transported-mass totals, the accepted rung, standing movement, and
    the row attaining the certificate.  Require at least one fixture with
    $\norm{\standingvector-\standingvector}_\infty>0$
    and
    $\norm{\standingvector-\standingvector}_\infty>0$;
    do not infer stage coverage from a passing stage certificate alone
    (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}).
    \frontierxref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate,%
    def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Allocation Work Sweep]{invest}{allocation-work-sweep}%
    {Allocation Work Sweep}
    \emph{Setup.} Synthetic and empirical projected graphs across $n$, average
    projected degree, degree skew, hub concentration, reciprocity, and
    complete-act family mix.
    \emph{Target.} Measure $\nnz_k$, map-pass time, memory, certificate sweep
    time, and passes to the accepted residual
    (\zcref{def:scalability:conserved-standing-work-measures,%
    prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost}).  Publish percentile scaling
    and identify the point at which the sparse conserved solve misses the
    boundary duration target
    (\zcref{rem:scalability:dense-projection-cost}).
    \frontierxref{def:scalability:conserved-standing-work-measures,%
    prop:scalability:conserved-map-pass-cost,%
    rem:scalability:dense-projection-cost}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Tighter Certificate by Enclosure]{arch}{certificate-enclosure}%
    {Tighter Certificate by Enclosure}
    \frontierpriority{None at the chartered charter; see the trigger.}
    The operative certificate is the fence evaluated
    (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), which is sound and
    costs one sweep, and reads the graph only through the contributing width
    (\zcref{rem:dynamics:certificate-is-the-fence}).  A genuine enclosure of
    the supremum --- interval evaluation over the invariant box, with Clarke
    intervals at the wall kinks --- would be strictly tighter, because it can
    see row balance, clique density and the placement of rates within the
    hull, none of which the fence distinguishes.  What it buys is headroom on
    graphs that are in fact benign; it buys no correctness, because the fence
    already proves what a gate must prove.

    This entry is therefore \textbf{not} a debt.  Nothing is missing at the
    chartered charter, and the enclosure is an optimization the design has
    declined, not a piece it has failed to build.

    \frontieropen{Build the enclosure only against a stated trigger, and state
    which.  The natural one is charter pressure: the chartered profile clears
    the prior screen with slack
    $\numval{const.standing.profile_slack.exact}$, and the slack falls with
    each hop of added reach
    (\zcref{rem:dynamics:chartered-decay-determined}), so a design wanting a
    louder profile or deeper reach loses graph-free certification and needs
    this object to certify per epoch at all.  Absent that pressure, the
    tightness is unspent.}

    \frontierremedy{An enclosure may only \emph{replace} the fence, never sit
    beside it as a second gate.  Two admissible certificates for one rung is
    the shape of a design that certifies whichever one passes.}

    \frontierxref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate,%
    rem:dynamics:certificate-is-the-fence,%
    frontier:tilt-profile-charter}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Source-Root Policy Sweep]{invest}{source-root-policy-sweep}%
    {Source-Root Policy Sweep}
    \emph{Setup.} Compare full current pair, W1-solvent source, hard
    source-rate wall, continuous emission factor, and final-standing-based
    source root, over fixtures: depleted high-count source, low-rate source,
    source splitting, same-epoch Registration, depleted intermediary relaying
    another source, and multi-target source.
    \emph{Target.} Report standing movement, source mass, split resistance,
    num\'eraire behavior, certificate clearance, and economic continuity.
    This informs the core policy of \zcref{frontier:source-root-eligibility}
    but does not resolve it by itself.
    \frontierxref{frontier:source-root-eligibility,%
    frontier:depleted-source-ballast}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Transport Symmetry Fixtures]{invest}{transport-fixtures}%
    {Transport Symmetry Fixtures}
    \emph{Setup.} Construct symmetric graphs: a two-path diamond, a
    three-way symmetric fan, an equal direct/two-hop pair, structurally
    identical neighbourhoods with different deeper continuations, and a graph
    automorphism swapping two Actors.
    \emph{Target.} Confirm that standing is equivariant under the
    automorphism --- swapping two structurally identical Actors swaps their
    standing and moves nothing else --- with no dependence on Actor
    identifier, record key or lexical order anywhere in the solve.  The
    property should hold by construction rather than by rule
    (\zcref{thm:dynamics:finite-max-envelope-lipschitz}), which is exactly
    why it is worth a fixture: a rule that has to be obeyed can be checked in
    review, while a property that falls out of the algebra fails silently if
    an implementation reintroduces a tie-break it does not need.
    \frontierxref{prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation,%
    post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism}
\end{frontier}

\begin{frontier}[Boundary-Search Benchmark]{invest}{boundary-search-benchmark}%
    {Boundary-Search Benchmark}
    \emph{Setup.} Measure candidate-set search under dependency packing, W1
    failures, W2a failures, W2b headroom, Registration plus same-epoch
    vouches, title conflicts, and candidate-set deltas.
    \emph{Target.} Compare from-scratch validation, exact incremental
    projection, warm-started stage solves, SCC invalidation, and interval-box
    reuse.  Publish trial count and total wall-clock envelope under target
    load, without claiming optimal selection
    (\zcref{rem:scalability:boundary-search-cost}).
    \frontierxref{rem:scalability:boundary-search-cost,%
    frontier:boundary-mechanism}
\end{frontier}

\section{Structural Irreducibility of Protocol Design Choices}
\label{app:necessity}

Every protocol-level design choice below has been tested against its
most natural simplification. In each case, the simplification violates
a structural invariant required for scaling, verification, or
manipulation resistance. The format is uniform: \emph{locked form},
\emph{obvious simplification}, \emph{failure mode},
\emph{proof sketch}, \emph{reference}.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Directed Edges}
\label{subsec:necessity:directed-edges}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Every edge $e = (u, v)$ is directed; $u \in V_u$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Undirected edges. Symmetric influence.
    \item[Failure]
        Unilateral influence fabrication.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Let clique $C$ of $k$ actors create Opinion edges to external
    content node $c^*$. Under undirected edges, the path
    $\text{ExternalUser}\text{---}c^*\text{---}\text{CliqueMember}$
    exists for every external user $u$ with an edge to $c^*$. Any
    external user whose shortest path to a target crosses $c^*$ now
    also reaches every clique member, manufacturing path existence
    without any outward action by the clique. Betweenness centrality:
    $S_{\text{clique}} \geq k / |N(c^*)| > 0$.

    Under directed edges, the Opinion arrow points
    $\text{CliqueMember} \to c^*$. No directed path leads
    $\text{ExternalUser} \to \text{CliqueMember}$.
    $S_{\text{clique}} = 0$. The same argument applies to endorsement flow:
    under undirected edges, clique members would receive spurious
    endorsement flow via paths that do not reflect genuine positive-parity
    endorsement, since the path direction is undefined.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:graph:partition}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Passive Authorship Control}
\label{subsec:necessity:passivity}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Every edge from a passive node is authored by an active node
        (or Layer~1) and is immutable after creation; no passive node
        autonomously initiates or redirects any edge
        (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Allow passive nodes to autonomously emit edges (e.g.\ content
        recommends related content; items advertise themselves).
    \item[Failure]
        Routing bypasses actor consent via autonomous passive-node
        edge injection.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under autonomous passive emission, a clique creates $k$ Opinion
    edges to content node $c^*$. If $c^*$ can autonomously emit edges
    to related content $c_1, \ldots, c_m$, then paths
    $\mathrm{ExternalUser} \to c^* \to c_j$ arise in the BFS without
    any actor endorsing the $c^* \to c_j$ connection, lifting
    $S_{\text{clique}}$ through connections no external actor authored.

    Under passive authorship control, passive nodes \emph{do} emit
    edges --- hyper-edge terminal legs and the Profile Reputation
    component --- but never autonomously: every outgoing edge from a
    passive node is authored by a specific active node (or Layer~1) who
    created the originating hyper-edge, with the target fixed at
    creation and immutable thereafter
    (\zcref{ax:graph:passivity,lem:graph:passive-out-degree}). A clique
    cannot cause $c^*$ to emit edges to chosen targets without an actor
    authoring a hyper-edge with $c^*$ as the middle node, and that
    hyper-edge is a public, author-attributed, immutable append-log
    record. The guarantee is reinforced by target structure: a
    passive-sourced leg can only point at the hyper-edge terminal
    designated by its author (Tag/T $\to$ Type, Review/T $\to$
    Comment, Bid/T $\to$ Offer, Send/T $\to$ Message,
    Invitation/T $\to$ Profile), so a clique
    cannot aim a passive node's outgoing edge at an arbitrary existing
    node of its choosing. Authorship and target constraint
    independently close the consent gap.

    The endorsement flow mechanism is protected identically: the double cover
    BFS extracts $\posreg{i}$ only for $i \in V_u$. Autonomous passive
    edges could manufacture positive-parity paths between actors via
    passive intermediaries no actor endorsed; the authorship invariant
    ensures every intermediate leg traces to a specific author. The
    directed 2-cycle
    $\mathrm{Actor}_j \to \mathrm{Profile}_j \to \mathrm{Actor}_j$ is
    computationally neutral: causal ordering blocks any continuation in
    the snapshot subgraph, and the max-product update rule ensures no
    BFS register inflation (\zcref{prop:nodes:self-loop-neutral}).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{ax:graph:passivity}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{$3 \times 3$}{3×3} Tensor Format}
\label{subsec:necessity:tensor-format}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        The edge's scoring objects are the $3 \times 3$ slice
        $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ and the $2 \times 2$ path-view $\pathview{e}$
        extracted from it. Routing, parity, and attribution read this
        matrix structure, never a single derived scalar.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Route on one scalar $w = f(p_d, p_i)$. (The parameters may still
        be stored and $w$ recomputed from them --- so this variant is
        \emph{fully auditable}; the objection is not verifiability.)
    \item[Failure]
        A scalar is expressively insufficient: it carries no orientation,
        does not compose along paths, and cannot separate routing
        discrimination from attribution equity.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The deficiency is structural, on three independent axes, each
    discharged in full elsewhere; this entry collects them.

    \emph{Orientation.} A scalar has no sign bit recording whether the
    sentiment map preserves or reverses orientation. The determinant sign
    $\detsign{e} = \operatorname{sgn}(\det(\pathview{e}))$ exists only
    because the path-view is a matrix; without it the positive-parity
    routing that protects endorsement flow from inverted paths
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}) cannot be expressed
    at all.

    \emph{Composition.} Influence along a path is the product
    $\pathmatrix{p} = \prod_e \pathview{e}$ of $2 \times 2$ matrices
    (\zcref{def:graph:path-matrix}); the determinant multiplies
    (\zcref{thm:graph:determinant-product}) and the parity bit accumulates
    (\zcref{cor:graph:path-parity-sign}). A scalar product discards the
    cross-coupling between sentiment modes
    (\zcref{subsec:graph:path-composition}) and cannot carry parity.

    \emph{Dual-view separation.} Routing must discriminate by directional
    coherence (the path-view determinant) while attribution must be
    equitable across edge types (the $3 \times 3$ Frobenius norm); the two
    differ by $\sim\!\numval{result.tier.edge_gap.num}\times$ versus $\sim\!16\%$ across tiers. A single
    scalar collapses these into one quantity, forcing either unfair
    attribution or directionless routing
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture}).

    Auditability does \emph{not} enter here: it is satisfied by storing the
    non-lossy parameter declaration and recomputing
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:sufficiency,subsec:deployment:feed-reproducibility}),
    and holds equally for the scalar-routing variant above. The lossy
    variant --- storing only $w$ and discarding the parameters --- does
    break auditability, but the remedy it forces is ``store the
    parameters,'' a sufficiency requirement, not the tensor format.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:path-matrix,%
    cor:graph:path-parity-sign,%
    subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing,%
    subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Over-Determination Is a Convenience, Not a Guard]
    \label{rem:necessity:tensor-overdetermination-convenience}
    The nine slice entries are functions of two continuous parameters and
    a discrete label, hence over-determined: a cached $\symbf{\Psi}_e$
    must satisfy seven internal relations to be a master-formula image.
    This is a \textbf{checksum on a derived cache}, not an adversarial
    guarantee. In the operative model a verifier recomputes
    $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ from the immutable parameters
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:sufficiency}) and never relies on a served
    slice, so there is nothing for over-determination to defend; and even
    a consumer that trusted a served slice would learn only that it is
    \emph{some} valid image, never that it is the \emph{declared} one ---
    consistency, not provenance. Provenance is carried entirely by
    immutability of the parameter record
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:immutability}); faithful scoring, by
    recomputation. The over-determination usefully detects corrupted
    caches and implementation bugs, and that is its whole role.
\end{remark}


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Average-Based Aggregation}
\label{subsec:necessity:average-based-aggregation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        $\bar{w}_c = |N(c)|^{-1} \sum_{u} w_{uc}$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        $\bar{w}_c = \sum_{u} w_{uc}$ (summation).
    \item[Failure]
        Resolution collapse: under summation, $N$ identical edges
        saturate the master formula's clamp and erase per-actor
        sentiment magnitude.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under summation, a clique of $N$ members each posting Opinion
    $(p\!=\!0.9,\; r\!=\!0.9)$ to content $c$ yields aggregated
    roles $\bar{p} = \bar{r} = 0.9N$. The master formula
    $\fpm{\bar{p}\bar{r}} = \sigmoid{\invtemp \cdot 0.81N^2}
    \cdot\tanh(0.81N^2)$ saturates to $1$ for $N \geq 2$ (at $N=5$,
    $\tanh(20.25) \approx 1$ to machine precision), so
    $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F$ plateaus at $\sim\!2.10$ rather
    than growing without bound. The genuine failure is therefore
    \emph{resolution collapse}: summation maps any non-trivial
    sentiment cluster to the saturation ceiling, destroying the
    distinction between a single $(0.9,0.9)$ opinion and a clique of
    them, and reducing the signal to a binary ``any vs.\ none''
    indicator. Averaging preserves parameter fidelity: a sentiment of
    $0.9$ averaged with further $0.9$ sentiments remains $0.9$, and
    $\norm{\symbf{\symcal{T}}_c}_F \in [0.800,\; 3\sqrt{2}]$
    regardless of $N$
    (\zcref{lem:graph:non-vanishing-norm,lem:graph:frobenius-bound}).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:graph:aggregated-sentiment}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Per-Author Netting}
\label{subsec:necessity:per-author-netting}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Full-incidence parallel bundles (\zcref{def:graph:authored-act-bundle}) net
        at the parameter level, sum-then-clip to $[-1,1]$, and only for
        endorsement-flow projection. Derived edges, settlement edges, and
        control edges are excluded
        (\zcref{def:epoch:net-stance}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Net edge weights directly, net across authors, or allow netting of Self-edge,
        settlement, or control records.
    \item[Failure]
        Ceiling escape through weight sums; crowd contention over shared passive
        sources; category error on non-record derived components, breaking
        responsive-activation monotonicity and settlement recognition.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Weight-level netting sums after the nonlinear master formula and can accumulate
    beyond the published path ceilings $\wmax$ and $\wmaxop$. Cross-author netting
    turns a passive target into a shared contention surface: one author's revision
    cancels another author's live consent, violating the directed authorship invariant
    of \zcref{subsec:necessity:directed-edges}. Netting derived Self-edge bonds
    would be a category error: they are not records and have no bundle.  The
    responsive activation is recomputed from final standing, not accumulated as a
    record quantity, so its monotone channel
    (\zcref{prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}) has nothing to
    net; netting
    settlement or control edges would hide the individual records read by
    \zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}. Parameter-level, per-author,
    endorsement-only netting preserves the range guard while making revision priced
    by \zcref{prop:epoch:net-stance-properties}.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:epoch:net-stance,prop:epoch:net-stance-properties,%
    prop:dynamics:responsive-vouch-activation-monotonicity}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Max-Product Path Scoring}
\label{subsec:necessity:max-product-path-scoring}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        $S(u,c)$ uses $\max_p \prod_{e \in p} \dampedweight{e}$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        $S(u,c) = \sum_p \prod_{e \in p} \dampedweight{e}$ (sum
        over all paths).
    \item[Failure]
        Redundancy amplification: $k$ parallel paths yield
        $k\times$ score.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Clique creates $k$ internal paths from boundary node $b$ to
    target content $c$, each via a distinct intermediate. Under
    sum-of-paths:
    $S \geq k \cdot \dampedweight{b \to m_i} \cdot
    \dampedweight{m_i \to c}$.
    Score scales linearly in $k$. Even $k = 2$ parallel paths
    (requiring only 2 cooperating actors or Sybil accounts) double
    the score. Clique manufactures visibility proportional to
    internal density. Under max-product, all $k$ paths yield
    products in the same range; the maximum selects one. Score is
    independent of $k$.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:sorting:relevance-score}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Conserved Rival Allocation}
\label{subsec:necessity:conserved-rival-allocation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Each Actor disposes of one conserved unit over self and all authored
        recipients; rows of $\transport{\standingvector}$ sum to one.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Independent per-pair weights, each in $[0,1)$, with no row constraint.
    \item[Failure]
        Regard becomes free.  A source may back every recipient at full
        strength, so backing carries no information about preference and a
        community's mean standing detaches from its ledger.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under independent weights, take a cohort of $n$ mutually endorsing Actors
    and raise every internal weight to its ceiling.  Each member's mediant is
    then a near-uniform average over the cohort, so a cohort of low-rate Actors
    that agrees to endorse maximally lifts every member toward the cohort's
    best rate at no cost to anyone --- there is nothing anyone gave up.  Under
    conservation the same act is self-limiting: the row sums to one, so
    endorsing everyone is indistinguishable from endorsing no one, and the
    cohort's transported-mass-weighted mean is exactly its ledger ratio
    whatever its members arrange.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{post:epoch:standing-pair-mass-conservation,%
    thm:epoch:closed-cluster-rate-identity}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Self-Retention as the Allocation Residual}
\label{subsec:necessity:self-retention-base}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        What a source does not allocate outward it retains; $\selfretention>0$
        and the self entry is never standing-modulated.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Unallocated mass is dropped, or the self share is tilted like any
        other.
    \item[Failure]
        Dropping detaches the cluster identity; tilting self lets standing
        defend its own retention, which is feedback with no source behind it.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    If unallocated mass is dropped, a cluster's row sums fall below one and its
    weighted mean no longer equals its ledger ratio --- the deletion case that
    \zcref{cor:epoch:conserving-source-root-criterion} rules inadmissible.  If
    the self entry is modulated by the source's own standing, then row $u$
    depends on $x_u$ and a high-standing Actor mechanically retains more,
    compounding its position without any act; the certificate would then have
    to price a self-loop that no accepted act created.  Leaving self
    unmodulated removes the direct channel while leaving the indirect diagonal
    terms, which the certificate does price.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{prop:epoch:rival-allocation-response},
    clause~3.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Domain-Weighted Allocation}
\label{subsec:necessity:domain-weighted-allocation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Folded coefficients are summed under published domain weights, and each
        act's domain profile sums to one.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Sum an act's contribution once per domain it projects into.
    \item[Failure]
        Cross-domain double counting: an act that projects into three domains
        counts three times, so act \emph{shape} buys standing.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Universal weighing guarantees each act is weighed once
    (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}); the domain profile is what
    makes ``once'' well defined when an act has several raw projections.
    Without $\sum_D\domprofile{D}{\foldcell}=1$, an author choosing a form that
    projects widely gains a multiple of the same authored intent for the same
    debit --- a fabrication surface in the act taxonomy rather than the ledger.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{post:epoch:domain-weighted-act-sum}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Finite-Depth Conserved Transport}
\label{subsec:necessity:finite-depth-conserved-transport}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        A published depth mass over finitely many hops, mixed into one
        operator.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Unbounded transitive closure, or a single hop.
    \item[Failure]
        Unbounded closure has no certificate and no bounded width; a single hop
        makes standing purely local and the whole comparator redundant.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The fence prices the profile's cumulative sum at the deepest
    \emph{supported} depth (\zcref{cor:dynamics:tilt-profile-prior-screen}), so
    an unbounded mixture has no finite screen to satisfy and its contributing
    width is the whole graph's rate range.  At one hop the transport is the
    base matrix itself: standing then reports who allocated to you and nothing
    about whether those sources were themselves backed, which is the property
    a comparator exists to supply.  Finiteness is what makes the certificate a
    closed-form pass rather than a limit.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:epoch:finite-depth-conserved-transport,%
    prop:scalability:standing-certificate-cost}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Hop-Faded Responsive Tilt}
\label{subsec:necessity:hop-faded-responsive-tilt}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        The tilt exponent decays with hop index and belongs to the transported
        mass.
    \item[Simpl.]
        A flat profile, or an exponent owned by the row.
    \item[Failure]
        Flat fails the prior screen at twice the cap; row-owned makes the fence
        unprovable, because one row would carry two exponents at once.
\end{description}
