\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    A flat profile's two-sided volume is the number of hops, not its
    front-loaded sum, so it fails the screen exactly as
    \zcref{rem:dynamics:rival-factor-two} exhibits.  For the ownership half:
    the same authored row relays its own pair at hop one and a distant
    source's at hop $r$, so an exponent attached to the row would have to take
    two values in one product.  Attaching it to the transported mass is what
    makes the propagation lemma's telescoping valid.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{rem:epoch:mass-owner-relative-hop-order,%
    lem:dynamics:transport-derivative-propagation}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Epoch-Set Standing}
\label{subsec:necessity:epoch-set-standing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Standing reads the completed epoch set and no clock the record does not
        contain.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Let standing read intra-epoch order, or the previous epoch's answer.
    \item[Failure]
        Order-reading hands the host a lever it can pull without leaving a
        trace; memory-reading makes the answer path-dependent, so two holders
        of the same record disagree.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Formation and admission may read order, and do
    (\zcref{post:epoch:standing-epoch-set-determinism}); the point is that
    standing may not.  If it did, a boundary operator could reorder two
    concurrent acts and move a gate verdict with no record of having chosen,
    which is unfalsifiable by construction.  If previous standing were a
    semantic input, the fixed point would depend on the initialization and
    replay would not be a check --- and the certified uniqueness that makes
    replay meaningful would say nothing.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{post:epoch:standing-memorylessness,%
    cor:dynamics:standing-initialization-independence}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Title-Coupled Settlement Standing}
\label{subsec:necessity:title-coupled-settlement-standing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        A settlement act allocates toward its counterparty only when the
        settlement settled; otherwise it resolves to its author.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Weigh the settlement act at its asserted face.
    \item[Failure]
        Free praise by assertion: an unauthorized or losing Accept costs its
        author one debit and delivers counterparty-directed standing anyway.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under face-value weighing, a colluding pair alternates unauthorized
    settlement acts and harvests directed allocation without either party ever
    completing a transfer; nothing in the ledger distinguishes the pattern from
    trade.  Coupling to the title fold makes the act's standing meaning the
    same object the graph already adjudicates, so fabricating the standing
    effect requires fabricating the settlement.  This is the settlement
    instance of the general rule that acts are weighed at their settled public
    meaning, alongside netting and revocation.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{post:epoch:settlement-standing-title-coupling}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Clamped Entry Bounds}
\label{subsec:necessity:clamped-entry-bounds}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        $\fpm{x} \in (-1,1)$, \quad $\fpl{x} \in (0.5, 1)$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Use raw products $p_i \cdot p_d$ without clamping.
    \item[Failure]
        Rank-1 degeneracy at weak parameters; loss of the
        Polarization Floor.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Parameters satisfy $p_d, p_i \in [-1, 1]$. Without clamping, the
    $(1,1)$ entry becomes $|p_i| \cdot |p_d|$, which is exactly $0$
    whenever either parameter vanishes. This makes the path-view
    matrix rank-1 with $\det(\pathview{e}) = 0$ and routing cost
    $c(e) = \infty$: any edge with a weak parameter becomes
    impassable. Products of entries in $[-1,1]$ shrink toward zero
    along paths; they do not overflow, but the rank-1 degeneracy
    disconnects the graph.

    With clamping, $\fpl{x} \geq 0.5$ guarantees $\Psi^{11} \geq
    0.5$ for all edges regardless of parameters, preserving the
    Polarization Floor (\zcref{prop:graph:polarization-floor}) and
    the self-reinforcement property
    (\zcref{prop:graph:polarization-self-reinforcement}). Entry
    magnitudes satisfy $|\Psi^{gh}| < 1$, so
    $\norm{\pathview{e}}_F \leq 2$ per edge: Dijkstra costs stay in
    representable range at all path lengths. The determinant sign
    $\detsign{e}$ is well-defined for all edges with nonzero
    parameters (\zcref{def:graph:determinant-sign}): rank-1
    degeneracy ($\det = 0$) would make the sign undefined,
    breaking the parity-product rule underlying endorsement flow
    (\zcref{cor:graph:path-parity-sign}).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:sentiment-slice,%
    prop:graph:polarization-floor}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Always-Active Baseline}
\label{subsec:necessity:always-active-baseline}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        $\Psi^{22} = \fpl{1} \numrel{const.graph.fpl_baseline.num}$, always active.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Drop the baseline entry, leaving the master formula's output for
        minimally-engaged interactions.
    \item[Failure]
        Edges with $p_d = p_i = 0$ lose the \emph{mask-independent} norm floor.
        Under the full mask the master formula still populates $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$,
        $(2,1)$ with $\fpl{0} \numrel{const.graph.sigmoid_floor.num}$, so the norm is $\numrel{const.graph.corner_norm.num}$ there ---
        deletion alone does not zero it. But those three entries are dropped by
        restricted masks (Identity's $(1,0,0,1)$ zeros the off-corners), so
        without the always-active $\Psi^{22} = \fpl{1} \numrel{const.graph.fpl_baseline.num}$ the
        guaranteed floor becomes mask-dependent and can fall away for a
        bare-activity edge under a restricted mask.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    With the baseline removed, $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, and $(2,1)$ remain populated by
    $\fpl{0} \numrel{const.graph.sigmoid_floor.num}$ under the full mask, giving $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F \geq
    \sqrt{3} \cdot \numval{const.graph.sigmoid_floor.num} \numrel{const.graph.corner_norm.num}$ at $p_d = p_i = 0$: deletion does not by
    itself collapse the norm, and the earlier ``drops to $0.5$'' reading was an
    arithmetic slip.  The baseline's necessity is narrower and exact ---
    $\Psi^{22}$ is the one entry present under \emph{every} interaction mask (that
    is what ``always active'' means), so it is the unique guaranteed, formula-
    and mask-independent anchor.  Restricted masks zero the off-corner entries a
    bare-activity edge would otherwise rely on, so without the baseline the
    non-vanishing-norm floor (\zcref{lem:graph:non-vanishing-norm}) becomes
    mask-dependent and can vanish, giving $\det(\pathview{e}) = 0$ and
    $c(e) = \infty$ for nodes reachable only through such edges.  The baseline
    therefore supplies a single invariant floor that lets the norm lemma and
    cache validation hold without a per-mask case analysis --- structurally
    distinct from $\bleedparam$-softening
    (\zcref{subsec:necessity:eta-softening}), which prevents the
    \PathView{}-determinant from vanishing under domain masks.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{lem:graph:non-vanishing-norm,%
    def:graph:path-distance}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{$\bleedparam$}{bleed}-Softening of Masked
Entries}
\label{subsec:necessity:eta-softening}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Masked path-view entries softened to $\bleedparam \numrel{const.graph.bleed.num}$,
        not zeroed.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Set masked entries to exactly $0$.
    \item[Failure]
        $\det(\pathview{e}) = 0$ for all restricted-mask edges;
        \tiermarginal{} edges become impassable.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The preceding entry (\zcref{subsec:necessity:always-active-baseline}) ensures $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F > 0$
    via the always-active baseline. This entry addresses a distinct
    failure: the path-view determinant can vanish even when the full
    tensor norm is nonzero, because the domain mask zeroes structural
    entries in the $2 \times 2$ extraction.

    Epistemic mask $(0,1,0,1)$ under hard zeroing:
    $\pathview{e}
    = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & * \\ 0 & * \end{smallmatrix}
    \bigr)$.
    $\det = 0$ identically, regardless of parameters. All Epistemic
    edges (Tag, Affinity, Review/T, Invitation/T) produce infinite
    routing cost. Similarly, Economic mask $(0,0,1,1)$ zeroes
    column~0: $\det = 0$. Minimal mask $(0,0,0,1)$ zeroes three of
    four entries: $\det = 0$.

    With $\bleedparam \numrel{const.graph.bleed.num}$: writing the softening factor as
    $\bleedparam$, the Epistemic softened path-view is
    $\Psi^{[P]}_e
    = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\bleedparam a & b \\
    \bleedparam c & d\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
    giving $\det(\Psi^{[P]}_e) = \bleedparam(ad - bc)$ --- linear in $\bleedparam$.
    Therefore $\detscore{} = \sqrt{|\det|} \sim \sqrt{\bleedparam}$, and
    the \tierfull{}/\tiermarginal{} gap is
    $\approx 1/\sqrt{\bleedparam} = 1/\sqrt{\numval{const.graph.bleed.num}} \numrel{const.graph.softening_gap.num}\,\times$,
    matching the promotion impact tabulated in
    \zcref{subsec:verification:mask-promotion-impact}.

    The floor ladder $\set{1, \halffloor, \bleedparam}
    = \set{\bleedparam^0, \bleedparam^{1/2}, \bleedparam^1}$ gives three
    routing tiers (\tierfull{}, \tierhalf{}, \tiermarginal{}); the
    \tierhalf{} floor is the half-power of the masking floor, the
    geometric mean of the \tierfull{} and \tiermarginal{} floors, and
    the path-view-only attenuation that demotes secondary directional
    signals (\zcref{subsec:necessity:settlement-half-routing}).

    Additionally, $\detsign{e}$ is well-defined for all softened
    edges: $\det \neq 0$ whenever $ad \neq bc$ (generically true for
    nonzero parameters), so the parity sign underlying endorsement flow
    (\zcref{def:graph:determinant-sign}) is defined for all \tiermarginal{}
    edges without exception.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:path-view-extraction,%
    prop:graph:path-view-determinant-bound}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Dual-View Architecture}
\label{subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        \PathView{} ($2 \times 2$ determinant) for routing and endorsement
        flow direction. \AttrView{} ($3 \times 3$ Frobenius norm)
        for CAN attribution.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Use the same norm for routing, endorsement flow, and attribution.
    \item[Failure]
        Either attribution discriminates unfairly across edge types,
        or routing loses directional sensitivity.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    \tierfull{} vs.\ \tiermarginal{} gap at representative parameters:
    $\detscore{\text{T1}} / \detscore{\text{T2}} \numrel{result.tier.edge_gap.num}$
    (\PathView{}); \quad
    $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{\text{T1}}}_F /
    \norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{\text{T2}}}_F \approx 1.2$
    (\AttrView{}).

    \emph{Single-view option~A (Frobenius for routing, endorsement flow, and
    attribution):} Tag and Opinion edges route nearly equally.
    Directional judgments lose their structural advantage in both
    feed-ranking and endorsement flow. The parity sign $\detsign{e}$ would
    need to be extracted from the Frobenius norm, which does not
    carry sign information: orientation-preserving and
    orientation-reversing interactions would be indistinguishable.

    \emph{Single-view option~B (determinant for routing, endorsement flow, and
    attribution):} Tag-based CAN compositions receive
    $\sim\!\numval{result.tier.edge_gap.num}\times$ less credit than Opinion-based compositions
    of comparable information content. Attribution penalizes edge
    type rather than contribution quality. The CAN enrichment factor
    $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ would discriminate by tier
    (${\approx}\,\numval{result.tier.edge_gap.num}\times$ gap) rather than by contribution quality
    (${\approx}\,21\%$ Frobenius variation), violating the invariant
    of \zcref{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}.

    The dual-view architecture is the minimum providing routing
    discrimination, endorsement flow parity information, and attribution
    equity simultaneously.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:dual-view-architecture,%
    ins:graph:rank-two-structural-consequence,%
    subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Positive-Parity Endorsement Routing}
\label{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Endorsement flow requires positive path parity
        ($\detsign{p} = +1$) as the routing component of admissible endorsement
        paths. The determinant sign $\detsign{e}$ is
        retained per edge and tracked through composition by the double
        cover BFS (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Discard $\detsign{e}$; route endorsement flow by the magnitude
        $|\det(\pathview{e})|^{1/2}$ alone, exactly as the feed-ranking
        BFS does.
    \item[Failure]
        A high-magnitude negative-parity path transmits influence as
        though it were a coherent endorsement: trust flows through a
        sentiment inversion.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:clamped-entry-bounds,%
    subsec:necessity:eta-softening} establish that $\detsign{e}$ is
    well-defined for every edge. This entry establishes why it must be
    \emph{used}.

    Take actors $j, i$ joined by a viable path $p$ with $\detsign{p} =
    -1$ and large $|\det(\pathmatrix{p})|^{1/2}$ --- strong directional
    coherence, inverted an odd number of times
    (\zcref{cor:graph:path-parity-sign,%
    rem:graph:sign-semantics}). Under magnitude-only routing,
    the positive register $\posreg{i}$ is large, so the raw endorsement service
    reads $j$ as coherently endorsing~$i$: $j$ \emph{endorses}~$i$.
    But $\detsign{p} = -1$ means the sentiment map from $j$ to $i$ is
    orientation-reversed --- a single negative edge has popularity and
    buzz dominant with the bilinear structure inverted. Magnitude-only
    routing reads the \emph{strength} of an inversion as the
    \emph{strength} of an endorsement, propagating commitment-rate trust
    through antagonism. This is not a loss of precision; it is a
    corruption of the influence signal.

    Under positive-parity routing, the double cover BFS places this
    contribution in the negative register $\negreg{i}$, not $\posreg{i}$
    (\zcref{def:epoch:double-cover-bfs-state}); the output filter
    returns $\posreg{i}$ only, which this inverted path leaves at~$0$. The parity gate
    blocks the inverted path by construction.  This proves necessity, not
    sufficiency: a coherent hostile actor-directed record $(-,-)$ has
    positive parity and must still be rejected as a non-vouch.  That local
    stance gate is the independent necessity of
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:universal-act-weighing}. The two-hop parity example
    of \zcref{ver:parity:two-hop-example} verifies
    $\posreg{i} = 0$ on a negative-parity path numerically.

    The same sign is correctly \emph{discarded} by feed-ranking: a user
    may be shown strong content regardless of its lean, so ranking needs
    only magnitude. Influence routing needs orientation. One determinant
    carries both; the two consumers take different subsets
    (\zcref{tbl:graph:consumer-map}). The cheapness of retaining the sign
    (one test per edge, \zcref{rem:graph:one-bit-extraction-cost}) is a
    performance property; the necessity of using it is this correctness
    property.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{cor:graph:path-parity-sign,%
    prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation,%
    alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs};
    \zcref{post:comparator:faithfulness}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Strict Transmission Decay}
\label{subsec:necessity:strict-transmission-decay}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        $\trans{n} = \sat{\meanedgenorm{n}}
        = \meanedgenorm{n}/(1+\meanedgenorm{n}) < 1$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        $\trans{n} = 1$ (lossless transmission).
    \item[Failure]
        Parasitic wrappers extract full child credit regardless of
        connection strength.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    With $\trans{} = 1$:
    $\canval{n}
    = \redundancy{n} \sum_i \depweight{n}{c_i} \canval{c_i}
    \leq \max_i \canval{c_i}$.
    Credit is conserved per step but does not decay. A wrapper $w$
    with one child $c$ connected by an edge of norm $\delta \approx
    0$: $\depweight{w}{c} = 1$, $\redundancy{w} = 1$, so $\canval{w}
    = \canval{c}$. Parasitic wrapper extracts 100\% of child's
    credit.

    With $\trans{} < 1$:
    $\canval{w} = \sat{\delta} \cdot \canval{c}
    = (\delta/(1+\delta)) \cdot \canval{c} \to 0$ as $\delta \to 0$.
    This also satisfies the mandatory guild structural invariant:
    depth decay (\zcref{thm:can:depth-decay}) requires
    $\canval{w} < \canval{c}$, which holds iff $\trans{w} < 1$.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:can:transmission-coefficient,%
    thm:can:parasitic-wrapper-elimination}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Inverse Temperature \texorpdfstring{$\invtemp = 2\ln 2$}%
{inverse temperature = 2ln2}}
\label{subsec:necessity:inverse-temperature}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        $\invtemp \numrel{const.activation.beta_2ln2.exact} \numrel{const.activation.beta_2ln2.num}$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Treat $\invtemp$ as a free parameter; tune post-deployment.
    \item[Failure]
        Crossover point $\tau^*$ shifts; either noise passes
        ($\invtemp$ too low) or cross-cluster discovery dies
        ($\invtemp$ too high).
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Net maturity factor $g(\tau) = \sqrt{1+\tau^2} \cdot
    e^{-\invtemp \tentropy{}}$. Net amplification iff $g(\tau) > 1$,
    i.e.\ $\tau > \tau^*(\invtemp)$.

    $\invtemp = 1.0$: $\tau^* \numrel{result.activation.tau_star_beta1.num}$. Edges with prior degree
    $\gtrsim 10$ receive net amplification. Moderate-maturity noise
    passes the boundary.

    $\invtemp = 2.0$: $\tau^* \numrel{result.activation.tau_star_beta2.num}$. Requires very high
    prior degree for amplification. Cross-cluster discovery is
    effectively impossible.

    The viable range $\invtemp \in (1.0,\; 2.0)$, giving $\tau^*
    \in (\numval{result.activation.tau_star_beta1.num},\; \numval{result.activation.tau_star_beta2.num})$, is bounded above by spam resistance and
    below by discovery viability. Within this range, $\invtemp =
    2\ln 2$ is the closed-form anchor closest to the midpoint,
    yielding $\tau^* \numrel{const.activation.tau_star.num}$ and maximum-entropy damping
    $e^{-2(\ln 2)^2} \numrel{const.can.void_base.num}$. The same $\invtemp$ applies
    identically to the feed-ranking BFS and the double cover endorsement-flow
    BFS: changing $\invtemp$ affects both systems simultaneously,
    which makes the calibration tractable from a single observable
    (serendipity rate in the deployed graph) during the centralized
    deployment phase
    (\zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model}).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{ax:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary,%
    prop:epoch:crossover-location}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Redundancy Correction}
\label{subsec:necessity:redundancy-correction}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        $\redundancy{n}
        = |\bigcup_i L(c_i)| / \sum_i |L(c_i)| \leq 1$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        $\redundancy{n} = 1$ always (ignore shared dependencies).
    \item[Failure]
        Credit duplication through overlapping fan-in.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Node $n$ depends on children $c_1, c_2$, both depending on the
    same leaf $\ell$. Assume equal edge norms so that
    $\depweight{n}{c_1} = \depweight{n}{c_2} = 0.5$.
    With $\redundancy{} = 1$:
    $\canval{n}
    = \trans{n}(0.5\,\canval{c_1} + 0.5\,\canval{c_2})$.
    Leaf $\ell$'s contribution appears in both $\canval{c_1}$ and
    $\canval{c_2}$. Effective credit attributed to $\ell$ within
    $\canval{n}$ is doubled. For $k$ children sharing the same leaf
    with equal weights: $k\times$ credit for one contribution.

    Under unequal weights the duplication is weighted but still
    present: $\ell$'s effective attribution is
    $\sum_i \depweight{n}{c_i} \cdot [\ell\text{'s share in }
    \canval{c_i}]$, which exceeds $\ell$'s single-contribution
    credit whenever multiple children share $\ell$.

    With $\redundancy{n} < 1$: $|\bigcup L(c_i)| = 1$,
    $\sum|L(c_i)| = k$, $\redundancy{} = 1/k$. Total attribution
    to $\ell$ is corrected to reflect a single unique contribution.
    This is also the third mandatory guild structural invariant:
    without redundancy correction, the CAN enrichment factor
    $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ would overstate attribution for
    compositions with shared upstream dependencies, violating the
    guild completeness requirement of
    \zcref{subsec:deployment:completeness}.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:can:redundancy-ratio,%
    thm:can:redundancy-fairness}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Participation Floor as a Distinct Dial}
\label{subsec:necessity:participation-floor}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Three objects: $\numeraire$ is the reserve/action join; $\polfloor$ is
        the dimensionless policy dial; $\safethresh$ is the algorithmic safety
        clamp, with $\partfloor$ derived.
    \item[Simpl. A]
        One coupled constant, the retired threshold.
    \item[Failure A]
        Admission and pricing tune jointly; congestion policy must reprice
        survivors.  \zcref{prop:epoch:compensation} shows the door and the curve
        are separable, so coupling them is gratuitous.
    \item[Simpl. B]
        Eliminate $\partfloor$ by forcing the participation gate to coincide
        with capacity.
    \item[Failure B]
        The two-gate architecture collapses exactly as the old $\numeraire=1$
        corner showed: the participation barrier becomes a hard monetary scale
        rather than a dimensionless policy bar.
    \item[Simpl. C]
        One host dial with no algorithmic clamp (fold $\safethresh$ into
        $\polfloor$).
    \item[Failure C]
        Safety becomes hostage to policy in both directions: the host can
        publish an unsafe floor, and every safety adjustment becomes a
        governance event. The clamp separates the replayable obligation
        (R1--R7) from the discretionary dial, with the meeting point a
        single published inequality (\zcref{eq:epoch:floor-validity}).
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The numéraire changes the exchange-rate curve and capacity scale; the
    policy floor changes the gate image. Collapsing them forces every
    admission decision to carry a pricing change, and every pricing migration to
    change who may act.
    Separating the dials makes the host-published floor extensive --- it
    excludes without repricing survivors --- while leaving numéraire changes as
    structural migrations and safety adjustments as replayable clamps.
    The certified fence (\zcref{thm:dynamics:hop-profile-width-fence}) is evidence
    \emph{about} this choice, not a new necessity argument: the gate would be
    required for admission economics under unconditionally tame dynamics; what
    the fence adds is a price list for the stability work the canonical gate
    had been doing unpriced.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{post:epoch:act-debit,%
    subsec:epoch:participation-gates,%
    rem:epoch:dial-scope,def:epoch:policy-floor,%
    def:epoch:safety-threshold,def:epoch:participation-floor};
    \zcref{ax:comparator:inter-cluster}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Floor as Num\'eraire}
\label{subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Reserve balances debit by $\safethresh$; reduced rates debit by
        $\safefloor$. Every reserve-denominated input is converted to
        action-equivalents (divided by $\numeraire$) before it meets a count,
        and the Self-edge bond intensity is
        $p_i = \hat\alpha/(1+\hat\alpha)$ with
        $\hat\alpha = \standing{i}/\numeraire$
        (\zcref{subsec:dynamics:within-epoch-indices}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Use reserve-denominated $\safethresh$ directly on reduced pairs, e.g.\
        write a reduced-pair update as $b-N\safethresh$, or use
        $\burnval{i}$ and $\standing{i}$ directly against $\actcount{i}$ / the
        literal $1$.
    \item[Failure]
        Adds $[\text{reserve}]$ to $[\text{action}]$; the hidden
        ``$1$'' is a hidden ``$1\,\text{reserve unit/action}$'', so the
        reduced ledger and the bond both detonate as
        $1\,\text{reserve unit} \to \infty$ (gate, debit, and bond all
        collapse at large reserve value). The single join between the
        reserve economy and the action economy is $\numeraire$; any
        other reserve/count adjacency is a units error.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The two economies have incommensurable units: reserve value is a transferable
    monetary quantity, while actions and counts $\actcount{i}$ are
    dimensionless event tallies. A well-formed expression may not add or
    compare the two without the explicit join $1/\numeraire$, so the
    only legitimate bridge is division by $\numeraire$.

    Suppose instead a reduced-pair debit writes $b-N\safethresh$. It subtracts
    reserve units from a dimensionless rate ledger: the floor-as-numeraire
    violation in debit clothing. Holding the reserve-denominated burn
    $\burnval{i}$ fixed in purchasing power while the reserve's market value
    scales by a factor $c$ rescales the numeric burn by $c$, so the
    reduced ledger moves without additional real commitment. The same hidden unit in the
    un-reduced bond kernel --- where the denominator's literal ``$1$'' silently
    means ``$1$~reserve unit per action'' --- makes $p_i \to 1$ under reserve
    repricing, saturating every Self-edge bond regardless of genuine
    commitment. Dividing by $\numeraire$ first, as in
    $\hat\alpha = \standing{i}/\numeraire$ and
    $\floorburn{i} = \burnval{i}/\numeraire$, removes the scale
    dependence: both are pure numbers invariant under repricing
    (\zcref{subsec:dynamics:within-epoch-indices}).

    The minimum deposit
    $\delta_{\min} = \partfloor\numeraire/\netliveshare$
    (\zcref{eq:comparator:admission-benchmark-deposits}) is the \emph{sole}
    legitimately reserve-dimensioned user-facing quantity, precisely because
    it is a deposit --- an input to the monetary side before conversion.
    This yields a checkable lint invariant: \emph{no term may add
    $[\text{reserve}]$ to $[\text{action}]$}, with $\numeraire$ the unique
    sanctioned conversion. \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{post:epoch:act-debit,%
    def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading,%
    subsec:necessity:participation-floor};
    \zcref{post:comparator:faithfulness}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{The Kernel Is Numéraire-Reduced}
\label{subsec:necessity:nu-reduced-kernel}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        The bond kernel reduces by $\numeraire$; $\partfloor$ is confined to
        the gate, freeze condition, and entry cost.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Reduce by the gate value $\partfloor\numeraire$.
    \item[Failure]
        Admission policy becomes monetary policy: every floor move reshapes
        every bond weight, reconstructing the retired coupled constant.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The kernel is the standing-dependent activation channel. It reads the
    reduced coordinate $\standing{i}/\numeraire$ because that is the unique
    reserve-to-action conversion.  Putting $\partfloor$ inside the denominator
    makes a gate move alter routing weights and coupled dynamics for actors who
    remain admitted, contradicting \zcref{post:epoch:reduction-convention} and the
    compensation structure of \zcref{prop:epoch:compensation}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Time-Locked Class Non-Burnability (Layer~0; Donated)}
\label{subsec:necessity:time-locked-non-burnable}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The irreducibility of the non-burnable time-locked class --- that collapsing
it into the live class ($\livesplit = 1$) restores unbounded zero-cost commitment
at genesis, and that a strict split ($\livesplit < 1$) is what bounds the bootstrap
capacity, the rate ceiling, and operator seigniorage --- is a \emph{Layer~0}
design choice, proven against Layer~0's own conservation and containment core
(\attestationcref{def:model:classes}, \attestationcref{thm:costliness:conservation-identity},
\attestationcref{prop:containment:floor-ceiling},
\attestationcref{prop:containment:seigniorage-suppression}). The network reads
only the resulting bootstrap capacity bound $\burncap$
(\zcref{def:comparator:bootstrap-capacity}); it does not re-derive the class structure.
This necessity argument is therefore donated upward: it belongs to a Layer~0
necessity treatment, not to the network's.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Time-Locked Class Non-Redeemability (Layer~0; Donated)}
\label{subsec:necessity:time-locked-non-redeemable}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The companion choice --- that the time-locked class is also non-redeemable, so
that its supply floor cannot be dissolved by redemption and the confidence
signal carried by its secondary-market price remains informative --- is
likewise a Layer~0 design choice
(\attestationcref{def:model:classes}, \attestationcref{rem:maturity:confidence-signal}).
The network consumes neither the reserve pool nor the redemption mechanism;
the irreducibility proof is donated upward with its companion above.

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Three-Step Settlement}
\label{subsec:necessity:three-step-settlement}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Commit at Ratify (buyer), after Accept (seller).
    \item[Simpl.] Commit at Accept (two-step Bid/Accept).
    \item[Failure] Funding and commit decouple; stale Accepts bind without
        the buyer's current consent.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    On a public append-log, two messages already achieve common knowledge
    of agreement, so the third step is never paying for the medium ---
    it pays for negotiation and for coupling funding to commit.  Under
    two-step, the commit is the seller's Accept, while the buyer's escrow
    must be funded earlier: a decoupling window in which buyer value is
    captive against a seller decision.  Worse, a seller may Accept a Bid
    the buyer rejects, binding the buyer to stale terms.  Three-step
    places the last authored act with the payer (Ratify), finalized at the
    boundary: the buyer funds and proposes commitment in one act, and nothing
    binds either party before the certificate, no pre-commit value is locked
    (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-cross-layer}), and a stale Accept binds
    nothing because the buyer simply never Ratifies.  This is the SYN/
    SYN-ACK/ACK structure with the payer committing last.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{subsec:graph:settlement-lifecycle,%
    rem:graph:settlement-cross-layer}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Explicit Settlement Cancellation}
\label{subsec:necessity:explicit-cancels}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Withdraw and Rescind are authored, immutable edges; no
        per-object timeout.
    \item[Simpl.] Per-Bid expiry: Bid non-recognizable after
        $T_{\mathrm{bid}}$ epochs.
    \item[Failure] Per-object state transition triggered by global
        throughput accumulation --- violating causal locality.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under per-object timeout a Bid dies because $\epochlen \cdot
    T_{\mathrm{bid}}$ edges accumulated \emph{elsewhere} in the log: its
    death is caused by unrelated throughput, a negative-evidence transition
    no edge represents.  Three failures follow: throughput coupling (busy
    networks expire Bids faster); an off-record state change (the first
    transition not represented by an authored record); and a calibration
    burden ($T_{\mathrm{bid}}$ with no semantic anchor, unlike $\invtemp$).
    Explicit cancels keep every death incident to the dying Offer
    (Withdraw, Rescind) --- authored, immutable, $\prec$-ordered,
    attributed --- with no counting and no constant.  Cancellation history
    is legible, yielding a reliability signal silent expiry discards
    (\zcref{rem:graph:causal-locality-principle,%
    thm:graph:no-death-by-inaction}).
    Boundary consumption (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}) is not a
    timeout: it is caused by authored records, evaluated at the uniform
    global progress point.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{thm:graph:no-death-by-inaction,%
    rem:graph:causal-locality-principle}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Mutual Consumption of Co-Epochal Commits}
\label{subsec:necessity:mutual-consumption}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Conflicting co-epochal commits are all consumed without
        transfer; the Item remains transferable.
    \item[Simpl. A] Canonical-order tiebreak.
    \item[Simpl. B] Permanent void: tied claims block the thread forever.
    \item[Failure] A re-imports the ordering authority. B is
        disproportionate: recognition is append-only and epoch indices never
        change, so a tied pair stays tied at the head of any minimal fold.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Any sub-epoch tiebreak re-imports the ordering authority rejected by
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent}. Permanent void would let
    one honest double-Accept plus a buyer race permanently brick the Item,
    stranding the thread's accumulated history. Consumption preserves the
    conservative core --- incumbent holds through the tie; ambiguity favors the
    owner --- while restoring liveness. Deterrence remains because consumption
    wastes every participant's priced records and leaves a public race on the
    seller's record.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold,%
    def:graph:settlement-consumption,thm:graph:settlement-order-freeness}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Epoch-Quantized Consent Rule}
\label{subsec:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Consent is live through the boundary: a cancel with
        $\operatorname{ep}(\mathrm{Cancel}) \le
        \operatorname{ep}(\mathrm{Ratify})$ defeats the commit.
    \item[Simpl.] Commit at the Ratify record instant, resolving
        cancel/commit races by sub-epoch order.
    \item[Failure] Sub-epoch order requires an ordering authority, and both
        available authorities corrupt title: operator-assigned order decides
        ownership by arrival accident, while author-asserted times admit
        time-stuffing.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Epoch membership is the unique granularity at which the ordering
    authority disappears: within the window there is nothing to decide, and
    membership itself is certificate-visible with validity replayable from the
    dependent-set partition
    (\zcref{rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance,%
    post:graph:boundary-accountability}). Any sub-epoch tiebreak is a
    choice function over co-epochal records; both realizable choice functions
    (arrival, assertion) corrupt title. The empty choice function is exactly
    quantization.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition,%
    rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance,%
    post:graph:boundary-accountability}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{No Privileged Cancel Class}
\label{subsec:necessity:no-privileged-cancel-class}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Cancels are admitted under the universal gates and the ordinary
        closure rule.
    \item[Simpl.] Gate- or write-exempt cancellation: control records bypass
        boundary selection.
    \item[Failure] An unpriced append channel breaks the spam-resistance rule
        that every act must dilute the author's rate, and creates an
        inexhaustible control-record graffiti primitive.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The consent problem is not solved by class privilege. A privileged cancel
    class would give any gate-cleared actor a record stream whose marginal
    congestion cost is detached from action pricing, directly contradicting the
    spam mechanism of \zcref{cor:scalability:spam-resistance}. The protocol instead
    keeps cancels ordinary priced acts and gives equal-epoch races to the
    cancel by recognition clauses~(iv)--(v)
    (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition}). No record class carries an
    write right; a suppressed cancel is the boundary exposure named in
    \zcref{rem:epoch:consent-exposure}, not a reason to exempt the class.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-closure,%
    post:graph:boundary-accountability,rem:graph:cancellation-best-effort}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Endogenous Clearing}
\label{subsec:necessity:endogenous-clearing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Published constraints, replayable dependent-set partition
        validity, and discretionary selection; the host holds no normative
        selection algorithm
        (\zcref{post:epoch:final-act-sequence-closure,def:network:door-headroom}).
    \item[Simpl.] A normative price-order or packing algorithm, audited against
        all non-written demand.
    \item[Failure] Unverifiable against an unobservable demand set: audit
        theater rather than protocol accountability.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    A normative selection algorithm would be a choice function over
    non-written candidates: whoever defines it decides, epoch by epoch, which
    invisible records should have existed. Every argument that disqualified
    sub-epoch ordering authority applies, with less evidence: the demand set is
    not a Layer-1 object, so abuse is unverifiable against a counterfactual.
    The protocol therefore fixes the constraints and publishes the chosen
    dependent-set partition; validity is replayable from the certificate, while
    selection remains discretion. The decentralized phase replaces discretion
    with mechanism, not with pre-write audit artifacts
    (\zcref{post:graph:boundary-accountability,frontier:boundary-mechanism}).
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Conflict Is Not Causality}
\label{subsec:necessity:conflict-not-causal}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Conflict protection is the written-side tie-favoring
        recognition rule plus the named boundary-censorship exposure; the
        dependent set is already its causal closure.
    \item[Simpl.] Widen the dependent set to co-transport conflicting
        commits and cancels.
    \item[Failure] Cancels and commits are concurrent by construction; grouping
        them requires mandatory cross-references or a serialization choice
        function, and both destroy the regret window.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    A Rescind that must cite the Ratify is a Rescind the buyer can outrun; a
    Withdraw that must cite a seller's later Accept has the same defect. Mandatory
    cross-references therefore erase the early-regret channel
    (\zcref{rem:graph:cancellation-best-effort}). A serialization choice function is
    worse: it re-imports the sub-epoch ordering authority rejected by
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent}. The dependent set is
    therefore limited to asserted parents and hyper-edge co-legs
    (\zcref{def:graph:dependent-act-set}); conflict accountability is the
    certificate plus the written-side tie rule, not prevention.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{rem:graph:dependency-closure-excludes-conflicts,%
    def:graph:settlement-recognition,post:graph:boundary-accountability}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Stance-Marginal Reputation Conjunction}
\label{subsec:necessity:stance-marginal-reputation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Commercial reputation reads the stance marginal
        $\operatorname{sgn}(p_d)$ of each settlement edge; routing reads
        the bilinear parity $\detsign{e}$
        (\zcref{rem:graph:settlement-reputation}).
    \item[Simpl.] Use $\detsign{e}$ for both.
    \item[Failure] The coerced-unfair Accept ($c<0$, $e<0$) has
        $\detsign{} = +1$: the honest worst-case experience produces the
        best-case reputation signal.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    By the Quadrant Law (\zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law}),
    $\detsign{e} = \operatorname{sgn}(p_dp_i)$, and the joint sign flip
    is an exact gauge of the path view: $(-,-)$ and $(+,+)$ are
    indistinguishable to every routing quantity. That identification is
    \emph{correct} for coherence --- shared aversion bonds --- and
    \emph{wrong} for any quantity whose meaning is the stance itself.
    Reputation is such a quantity: the verdict sought is ``was the
    seller comfortable,'' which is the $D$-odd component the gauge
    kills. The stance marginal $\fpm{p_d}$ survives in the stored
    slice's always-active row, is published, and is $O(1)$-verifiable;
    reading it restores injectivity exactly where the gauge must not
    apply. For the Bid, $u \geq 0$ collapses the two readings
    ($\detsign{} = \operatorname{sgn}(g)$,
    \zcref{cor:nodes:bid-leg-parity}), so only Accept and Ratify move.
    The conjunction is terminally consumed
    (\zcref{tbl:symbols:boundary}), so the redefinition touches no
    admission quantity and no traversal.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law,%
    rem:graph:settlement-reputation,ver:settlement:coerced-unfair}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Vouch-Gated Endorsement}
\label{subsec:necessity:universal-act-weighing}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        A person-directed act allocates \emph{outward} only on strictly
        positive mandatory coordinates $p_d>0,\ p_i>0$; every other act is
        weighed too, and resolves home
        (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,%
        def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Parity-only endorsement: every positive-parity path contributes,
        including actor-directed coherent hostility $(-,-)$.
    \item[Failure]
        Coherent condemnation becomes structurally indistinguishable from praise
        for standing: a high-rate critic lifts the target, and a colluder can
        publicly condemn while privately vouching through the formula.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The path-view sign space contains two different readings.  The determinant
    sign $\detsign{}=\operatorname{sgn}(p_dp_i)$ is the \emph{coherence}
    character: it composes along paths and is the correct bit for detecting
    orientation inversion (\zcref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}).
    The stance marginal $\operatorname{sgn}(p_d)$ is the author's verdict on
    the target.  By the Quadrant Law
    (\zcref{lem:graph:quadrant-law}), the joint sign flip
    $(p_d,p_i)\mapsto(-p_d,-p_i)$ is invisible to all coherence quantities:
    $(-,-)$ and $(+,+)$ route and rank identically.

    That identification is correct for object-mediated resonance: shared
    aversion can be a coherent content signal.  It is wrong for standing.
    Standing is the commitment-consensus of those who vouch for an actor
    (\zcref{def:epoch:final-standing,rem:epoch:author-directed-allocation}); a coherent
    condemnation is not a vouch.  Under parity-only endorsement, a Profile
    Opinion with $p_d<0,p_i<0$ enters the canonical endorsement path with the
    same magnitude as its positive counterpart and carries the critic's source
    rate into the target.  If the critic has a higher rate, the target's
    standing rises
    (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}).  The formula therefore rewards the
    target for being condemned by high-standing actors and permits deniable
    standing transfer by public hostility.

    A signed negative-weight remedy is impossible without destroying the
    convex-combination hull of \zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}; composing
    stance along paths is equally wrong because verdicts are local authored
    acts, not orientation transport.  The minimal repair is therefore local,
    and it is a repair to the \emph{destination} rather than to membership:
    keep parity as the compositional coherence test, and let the stance
    marginal decide where an act's weight lands.  A $(-,-)$ person-directed
    act stays coherent, stays weighed, and resolves to its author
    (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}).

    Resolution is the stronger instrument, and the difference is not
    presentational.  A gate would have \emph{excluded} the act, leaving the
    condemner free to condemn at no cost; resolution charges them the act's
    full magnitude against their own conserved unit
    (\zcref{rem:epoch:hostility-is-priced}), so public hostility is neither a
    transfer to the target nor a discount for the author.  The deniable
    standing transfer is closed at the target, and the free attack is closed
    at the source, by one rule.

    Nor does the repair perturb anything proved elsewhere.  It changes
    destinations, never totals: each row of the base matrix remains one unit
    however its cells resolve, so the hull bound and every App~D certificate
    hold verbatim rather than by a subgraph argument.  At the boundary
    $p_d=0$ or $p_i=0$ the act resolves home at coefficient zero
    (\zcref{rem:graph:zero-parameter-degeneracy}), so there is no
    discontinuity to introduce.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,prop:epoch:standing-support-preservation,%
    rem:graph:sign-semantics,prop:epoch:act-folding-properties}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Declarative Item Identity}
\label{subsec:necessity:declarative-item-identity}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] An Item's identity is its genesis record's structural
        identity key (\zcref{def:graph:item-genesis-act}).
    \item[Simpl.] Content-addressed identity (Item $=$ hash of its
        description); or an external registry binding Items to
        real-world referents.
    \item[Failure] Content-addressing welds title to erasable bytes;
        registry binding imports an identity authority.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    \emph{Content-addressing.} The description lives in a removable
    payload, and edge identity is required to be payload-free precisely
    so that erasure never breaks resolution
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-projection}): a content-addressed Item makes
    the right-to-leave (\zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}) and
    title stability (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}) mutually
    exclusive --- removing the description would orphan or re-key the
    thread. It dies by an axiom adopted for independent reasons.
    \emph{External registry.} A privileged sameness-verdict is the
    identity-authority branch of Douceur's fork re-imported at the Item
    layer --- owned, tiltable, endless
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:the-detector}). \emph{Declarative identity}
    is what the specification already practices: threads are per-node,
    \texttt{settles}-pointers are identity keys, and recognition never
    compares Items across genesis records. Uniqueness is record
    integrity's, not title logic's; the referent question is out-of-band
    by the gauge argument and witnessed at
    \zcref{frontier:item-genesis}.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:graph:item-genesis-act,%
    rem:graph:item-identity-limit,def:graph:act-payload-projection}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Actor-Incidence of the Settlement Handshake}
\label{subsec:necessity:handshake-actor-incidence}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Accept and Ratify are direct Actor $\to$ Actor edges ---
        the census's only such family; every other actor-directed gesture
        routes through the target's Profile and standing-dependent bond.
    \item[Simpl.] Route the handshake through Profiles, like Opinion.
    \item[Failure] A counterparty's zero-standing bond can sever a live
        settlement.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    One forcing (a second, Lamport race arithmetic, retired with
    epoch-quantized title): \emph{bond independence.} A Profile-routed handshake traverses the
    counterparty's Reputation component --- zero at zero standing, frozen
    below the gate (\zcref{prop:nodes:raw-self-edge-properties},
    \zcref{def:epoch:raw-self-edge-reading}) --- coupling title
    mechanics to a sentiment field title is required to ignore
    (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold}).

    The exception's cost is priced and named: direct actor edges bypass
    the standing-dependent funnel, and the recognition-blind endorsement
    they inject is exactly the ceiling witness
    \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}, attenuated by \tierhalf{}
    routing (\zcref{subsec:necessity:settlement-half-routing}). The
    exception is bought where load-bearing (certificate commit semantics) and
    paid where bounded (a dominated endorsement channel).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition,%
    subsec:necessity:settlement-half-routing}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Half-Tier Routing of Settlement Edges}
\label{subsec:necessity:settlement-half-routing}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] The settlement-handshake edges (Bid, Accept, Ratify)
        carry a full stored block but route at the \tierhalf{} tier
        (path-view floor $\halffloor$).
    \item[Simpl.] Route them at \tierfull{}, identical to Opinion/Owner.
    \item[Failure] A sentiment side-channel acquires primary routing
        authority: auction gravity and endorsement over-injection.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Title recognition and transfer are sentiment-independent
    (\zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold,rem:graph:settlement-reputation}):
    a sign-blind structural predicate decides the outcome, and the signed
    sentiment on Bid/Accept/Ratify feeds only the downstream reputation
    conjunction.  An edge whose primary effect is sentiment-independent
    must not exert primary (\tierfull{}) routing force, or its secondary
    signal dominates the quantities that \emph{are} sentiment-driven.

    Two failures follow \tierfull{} routing.  (1)~Auction gravity: the
    full Bid determinant concentrates routing weight around Items under
    active bidding, shortening paths toward them and distorting the feed
    from the serendipity target
    (\zcref{cor:sorting:serendipity-conditions}).  (2)~endorsement over-injection:
    the recognition-blind double cover BFS traverses Accept/Ratify
    regardless of recognition (\zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication}); at full
    strength these inject commercial-tie endorsement at the magnitude of a
    primary endorsement.

    \tierhalf{} routing attenuates both by $\halffloor$ per leg
    ($\approx 0.40$ on a two-leg product) without removing the signal,
    and is safe: by \zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance} the
    $AD$ term dominates $f\,AD - f^2 BC$ at both floors, so the demotion
    preserves every settlement determinant sign exactly --- the
    reputation conjunction and title transfer are untouched, and a
    predatory Bid ($g < 0$) keeps $\detsign{} = -1$, so it is feed-mass
    symmetric to a generous Bid of equal magnitude yet parity-gated out
    of positive endorsement flow.  Failure~(1) is thereby \emph{eliminated}, not
    merely reduced: a \tierhalf{} Bid ($\detscore{} \approx 0.20$) is
    strictly weaker than an ordinary \tierfull{} Opinion
    ($\detscore{} \approx 0.35$) on the same Item, so bidding confers no
    routing privilege beyond the generic content-cluster amplification
    already characterised by
    \zcref{cor:sorting:polarized-cluster-amplification} and calibrated in
    the deployment phase via \zcref{cor:sorting:serendipity-conditions}.
    Failure~(2) is reduced but structurally survives, as the residual
    injection question \zcref{frontier:settlement-tie-fabrication} records.
    \tiermarginal{} routing (floor $\bleedparam$) would crush a genuine
    signed stance to near-control-edge strength; \tierfull{}
    over-empowers it.  \tierhalf{} is the unique floor that is both
    attenuating and sign-preserving for a secondary directional signal.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{thm:graph:epoch-title-fold,%
    rem:graph:settlement-reputation,%
    lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance,%
    def:graph:proposal-half-tier}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Binary Join Request}
\label{subsec:necessity:binary-join-request}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Join Request is a binary Actor $\to$ Chat edge
        (\zcref{edge:nodes:join-request}).
    \item[Simpl.] A ternary hyper-edge routing the request through the
        recipient (an actor-middle structure).
    \item[Failure] An apparent recipient-sourced leg exists before the
        recipient has authored anything: authorship and source diverge on a
        leg readable as the recipient's stance.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    A join request has exactly two essential structural participants ---
    requester and Chat. Any third leg must be sourced somewhere, and every
    candidate source other than the requester creates a record attributable
    to a party who has not acted, violating the authorship gloss of
    \zcref{ax:graph:passivity}(a). The binary form leaves acceptance where
    consent lives: the Participant edge the joining actor authors
    (\zcref{rem:nodes:chat-proposals-do-not-participate}).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{ax:graph:passivity,edge:nodes:join-request}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Invitation Terminates at the Profile}
\label{subsec:necessity:invitation-profile-terminus}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] The Invitation/T-leg targets $\mathrm{Profile}_{\mathrm{invitee}}$
        (\zcref{edge:nodes:hyper-invitation}).
    \item[Simpl.] Target $\mathrm{Actor}_{\mathrm{invitee}}$ directly.
    \item[Failure] A second passive-sourced in-edge family on Actors breaks
        the unique-Reputation-funnel premise of the coupled dynamics and
        opens an undamped endorsement conduit to zero-standing accounts.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    \zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution} rests on the Reputation
    component being the sole passive-sourced in-edge of any Actor. A
    Chat $\to$ Actor terminal leg would falsify that premise and would
    transmit endorsement to an invitee independently of the invitee's own
    standing --- a Sybil surface, since fresh accounts could be mass-invited
    into endorsed Chats. Terminating at the Profile funnels all influence
    through the invitee's standing-dependent bond, which is zero at zero
    standing (\zcref{prop:nodes:raw-self-edge-properties}), and joins the
    address pattern of every actor-directed gesture (Opinion, Review).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Proposal Half-Tier Routing}
\label{subsec:necessity:proposal-half-tier}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Join Request and Invitation/A route at \tierhalf{}
        (\zcref{def:graph:proposal-half-tier}).
    \item[Simpl.] Route them at \tierfull{}, identical to Participant and
        Send/A.
    \item[Failure] Proposal spam acquires enacted-relation routing force;
        invitations into popular Chats out-route actual participation.
\end{description}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    A proposal's primary effect awaits the counterparty's Participant edge,
    so its sentiment is a stance about a relation that does not yet exist.
    At \tierfull{} force, unanswered proposals would concentrate routing
    weight indistinguishably from membership, and mass invitation would
    manufacture Chat-adjacent visibility at proposal cost. The \tierhalf{}
    floor attenuates without erasing the stance, preserves every sign
    (\zcref{lem:graph:tier-floor-sign-invariance}), and mirrors the
    settlement rationale of \zcref{subsec:necessity:settlement-half-routing}.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:graph:proposal-half-tier}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Unrestricted Departure and De-Invitation}
\label{subsec:necessity:unrestricted-departure}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Leave and De-invite append under the universal
        write rule only; Layer~1 imposes no
        membership, authority, or incidence precondition, and derives no
        membership state (\zcref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold}).
    \item[Simpl.] Validity checks: reject a Leave unless its author is a
        member; reject a De-invite unless its author is authorized and
        its target is a member or invitee.
    \item[Failure] A membership-recognition predicate enters the
        admission closure; membership becomes binding; authority becomes
        a Layer-1 verdict.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Append-time rejection is a feedback read-site by definition: the
    predicate ``is $a$ a member of $C$'' would decide what may append
    to~$E$, placing membership inside $\overline{\mathcal{A}}$
    (\zcref{def:network:admission-closure}) and enlarging the binding
    surface the reimplementation grant explicitly closes at
    $\set{\text{kernel}, \text{rules}, \standing{}\text{-as-gate},
    \titlecert{}}$ (\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}).  Two guilds
    wanting different membership semantics --- inviter-revocable,
    moderator-quorum, self-sovereign --- would then disagree on record
    validity and fork~$E$, where under the locked form they diverge
    terminally and harmlessly.  Title is the instructive contrast:
    settlement recognition sits in the closure \emph{because} clause~(iii)
    reads title back into validity; membership has no such read-back, so
    binding it is gratuitous.  The De-invite authority check is worse
    still: ``who may expel'' is an authority verdict --- the
    identity-authority branch of Douceur's fork
    (\zcref{ins:introduction:the-detector}) re-imported at the Chat layer,
    owned, tiltable, and endless.  Finally, the ``vacuous'' records the
    simplification would reject are not noise: a never-member's Leave is
    a public dissociation, a stranger's De-invite a public objection ---
    authored, attributed, immutable, priced per action
    (\zcref{cor:scalability:spam-resistance}, mechanism~4), and exactly
    the class of record accountability cost exists to govern
    (\zcref{post:comparator:accountability-cost}).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:nodes:canonical-membership-fold,%
    rem:nodes:membership-is-terminal,post:transport:guild-grant}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Control-Edge Endorsement Inertness}
\label{subsec:necessity:control-self-retention}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] Type-fixed control records (Withdraw, Rescind, Leave,
        De-invite/A·T) resolve to their author in every quadrant --- weighed
        like any other act, and never outward
        (\zcref{rem:epoch:control-acts-resolve-to-self}).
    \item[Simpl.] Let them through: they are forced $+1$ and Minimal
        tier, so their weight is small.
    \item[Failure] The De-invite/T-leg is actor-directed with fixed parameters
        $(1,1)$, which vacuously pass the open-positive-quadrant test:
        every expulsion becomes a vouch for the expellee.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Outward resolution reads \emph{authored stance}
    (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}); a control record's parameters are
    constants of its type, not choices of its author, so the record
    carries no stance to read.  Resolving it outward on its parameter values
    inverts the semantics maximally: the census's least sentiment-bearing
    record would allocate at the strength of its most positive one.  The
    exploit is then mechanical --- mass de-invitation of a target from
    high-weight Chats manufactures admissible 3-hop paths
    (endorser $\to$ Chat $\to$ Profile $\to$ Actor) carrying the
    de-inviters' rates into the target's standing, at control-record
    cost and with hostile intent: a standing pump indistinguishable in
    form from the critic-bump home resolution closed.  Smallness is no
    defense; the failure is semantic, not quantitative.  Home resolution is
    also cost-free to everything else proved: the row still sums to one unit,
    so the hull bound (\zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}) and every
    App~D contraction certificate hold unchanged rather than being preserved
    by shrinkage (\zcref{prop:epoch:act-folding-properties}).  The
    de-inviter still pays for the act --- it lands on their own retention and
    dilutes their outward shares --- so mass de-invitation is not merely
    ineffective as a pump, it is expensive.  Feed-ranking, an
    attention consumer, correctly still traverses control edges at
    Minimal magnitude.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{rem:epoch:control-acts-resolve-to-self,%
    def:epoch:effective-act-contribution,subsec:necessity:universal-act-weighing}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{De-Invite Terminates at the Profile}
\label{subsec:necessity:deinvite-profile-terminus}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked] The De-invite/T-leg targets
        $\mathrm{Profile}_{\mathrm{de\text{-}invitee}}$
        (\zcref{edge:nodes:hyper-deinvite}).
    \item[Simpl.] Target $\mathrm{Actor}_{\mathrm{de\text{-}invitee}}$
        directly.
    \item[Failure] A second passive-sourced in-edge family on Actors
        breaks the unique-Reputation-funnel premise of the coupled
        dynamics and opens an undamped attention conduit to arbitrary
        accounts.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Identical forcings to
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:invitation-profile-terminus}:
    \zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution} requires the Reputation
    component to be the sole passive-sourced in-edge of any Actor, and
    the Profile terminus funnels even the (feed-only) conduit through
    the target's standing-dependent bond, zero at zero standing
    (\zcref{prop:nodes:raw-self-edge-properties}) --- mass de-inviting
    fresh accounts transmits nothing.  The one argument that licenses
    actor-incidence elsewhere --- the settlement handshake's Lamport
    commit race (\zcref{subsec:necessity:handshake-actor-incidence}) ---
    has no analogue here: a De-invite binds nothing, so there is no
    concurrency to resolve and no exception to buy.  The default rule
    for actor-directed gestures therefore governs.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:invitation-profile-terminus,%
    def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Per-Edge Positivity on the Affinity Channel}
\label{subsec:necessity:bridge-per-edge-positivity}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Channel~1 affinity (\zcref{def:bridge:affinity}) operates on the
        positive subgraph $\posgraph$ with per-edge $\detsign{e} = +1$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Use per-path parity $\detsign{p} = +1$ --- the endorsement-flow rule
        (\zcref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}) --- for
        Channel~1.
    \item[Failure]
        Per-path parity admits paths with inverting interior hops, pricing
        a coherent endorsement delivered to a relay who disapproves of it.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Take an affinity path $T \to v_1 \to v_2 \to B$ with
    $\detsign{} = (-1, -1, +1)$ and net parity $\detsign{p} = +1$.  By
    the Interior Coherence Lemma (\zcref{lem:bridge:interior-coherence}),
    node $v_1$ receives the transported orientation with cumulative sign
    $\pi_1 = -1$: the funnel surfaces $v_1$ as something $T$ is oriented
    \emph{against}.  Per-path filtering admits this path and
    $\affinity{T, B}$ prices the delivery, but the chain's first hop has
    already surfaced under inversion --- the advertiser's endorsement,
    transported to $v_1$, arrives inverted.  This is the endpoint-consuming
    correctness argument of
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing} applied per hop rather
    than per path: where endorsement flow consumes orientation only at the endpoints
    (and so tolerates an even number of interior inversions), the affinity
    funnel is consumed at every interior node, and each interior consumer
    must receive a coherent signal.  Per-edge positivity excludes exactly
    the paths containing a mis-surfaced interior hop; by
    \zcref{lem:bridge:interior-coherence} it is the unique edge set on which
    every interior consumer is coherent.  This is a sibling derivation of
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}, not a new axiom.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:bridge:affinity,%
    lem:bridge:interior-coherence,%
    subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Consent as a Profile-Read Register Difference}
\label{subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Consent (\zcref{def:bridge:consent}) is
        $\consent{A, B} = \max(0,\, \posreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B} -
        \negreg{\mathrm{Profile}_B})$: the clipped difference of the
        double-cover registers read at $B$'s \emph{Profile} node.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Two natural simplifications: (a)~use $\posreg{}$ alone; (b)~read
        the registers at the \emph{actor} $\mathrm{Actor}_B$ rather than
        at $\mathrm{Profile}_B$.
    \item[Failure]
        (a)~makes the advertiser's authored dislike invisible to the
        consent gate; (b)~double-counts the bridge's reputation, biasing
        bridge selection by an irrelevant factor.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    \emph{Difference over $\posreg{}$ alone.}  The advertiser's negative
    edges toward $B$ enter $\negreg{}$, which $\posreg{}$-alone never
    consults: a bridge $A$ actively dislikes receives the same consent as
    one $A$ has never encountered.  The subtraction transmits a direct
    negative Opinion ($A \to \mathrm{Profile}_B$, raising $\negreg{}$ past
    $\posreg{}$) into $\consent{} = 0$.  The difference is the minimal
    operation making both positive and negative advertiser-authored edges
    actionable in the consent gate.  A ratio $\posreg{}/\negreg{}$ fails
    differently --- undefined at $\negreg{} = 0$, the common no-hostility
    case --- so the difference is also the minimal \emph{always-defined}
    such operation.

    \emph{Read at Profile, not at Actor.}  A path reaching the actor
    $\mathrm{Actor}_B$ terminates through $B$'s Reputation component
    $e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}$, whose weight is a function of $\standing{B}$.  That
    hop lies on the \emph{delivery circuit}: the affinity segment of the
    realizing path $\realizingpath{i}$ ends at $\mathrm{Actor}_B$, and by
    the value/attribution invariant $\affinity{T, B}$ must carry
    $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}}$
    (\zcref{rem:bridge:reputation-single-traversal}).  Reading consent at
    $\mathrm{Actor}_B$ would re-traverse $e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}$, making
    $\circqual{} = \affinity{}\cdot\endorsement{}\cdot\consent{}$ quadratic
    in $B$'s reputation: a $\sim 3\times$ spread in
    $\dampedweight{e_{\mathrm{Rep},B}}$ would become a $\sim 9\times$ spread
    in circuit quality, biasing $\arg\max_B$ toward high-reputation bridges
    beyond the merit either relationship confers.  Reading at
    $\mathrm{Profile}_B$ excludes the always-positive
    ($\detsign{e_{\mathrm{Rep}}} = +1$) Reputation hop --- which could only
    attenuate the parity difference, never inform it --- so $B$'s reputation
    enters $\circqual{}$ exactly once, linearly, on the segment the
    advertiser pays for.  The advertiser's authored regard for $B$ is itself
    an Opinion on $\mathrm{Profile}_B$, so the Profile register captures
    consent exactly.  The redundancy argument and the semantic argument
    agree, and the split direction is forced: affinity keeps the hop because
    it is on the priced structure, consent sheds it because it is not.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:bridge:consent,%
    rem:bridge:reputation-single-traversal,%
    def:bridge:realizing-centrality}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Domain Exclusion of Self-Target and Self-Bridge}
\label{subsec:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Targets and bridges exclude the advertiser:
        $T_i \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$, $B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$
        (\zcref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Permit $T_i = A$ (self-target) or $B = A$ (self-bridge).
    \item[Failure]
        Self-bridge yields an advertiser-controlled self-endorsement loop;
        self-target yields a feedback circuit disconnected from any
        external audience value.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    \emph{Self-bridge} ($B = A$): $\endorsement{A, A}$ requires $A$'s
    Opinion on its own Profile, a value $A$ authors unilaterally; the
    circuit $\circqual{T, A, A}$ would then let an advertiser manufacture
    its own endorsement factor with no counterparty.  \emph{Self-target}
    ($T_i = A$): the circuit runs $A \to B \to A$, pricing proximity of the
    advertiser to itself --- structurally disconnected from the audience
    value advertising is meant to purchase.  The single domain restriction
    $T_i, B \in V_u \setminus \set{A}$ closes both: under $T_i = A$ the
    weighted target set is empty, giving $\campaignscalar{A} = 0$ and
    $R_C = 0$ for all creators (\zcref{rem:bridge:self-target}); the same
    restriction blocks $B = A$ at the inner maximum.  This excludes the
    self-targeting degenerate case intrinsically and
    requires no categorical special case --- the zero-reward outcome
    (\zcref{cor:transport:zero-reward}) follows from the empty target
    set alone.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:bridge:campaign-scalar,%
    rem:bridge:self-target,%
    cor:transport:zero-reward}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Edge Ontology}
\label{subsec:necessity:edge-ontology}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Records are edges; nodes are implicit folds; Layer~1 appends nothing
        (\zcref{ax:graph:authored-act-ontology,def:graph:derived-raw-edges}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        First-class node records with attributes, plus Layer-1-appended bond
        records.
    \item[Failure]
        Node attributes create a second data plane with its own mutability,
        custody, and erasure semantics, so payload-state invariance and the
        right-to-leave analysis must be re-proved against it. Node-creation
        operations reopen genesis authorization and admission. Layer-1-appended
        bonds re-enter the admission set, reopening the append carve-out and the
        epoch cascade. The ontology is the fixed point where genesis, erasure,
        admission, and replay close simultaneously.
\end{description}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Universal Parallelism}
\label{subsec:necessity:universal-parallelism}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        All families are parallelizable; Layer~1 performs no merge or
        supersession; fold-freedom holds with the two bundle consumers of
        \zcref{rem:graph:authored-act-bundle-consumers}.
    \item[Simpl. A]
        Uniqueness constraints such as one Opinion per author per target or one
        Registration per actor.
    \item[Failure A]
        The append layer must reject records based on prior state, admission
        absorbs per-family state machines, and update semantics must be defined
        at Layer~1 to say which record survives. Priced walk-back also fails:
        conviction inertia (\zcref{rem:epoch:conviction-inertia}) requires
        parallel accumulation.
    \item[Simpl. B]
        Layer-1-defined update semantics, latest-wins everywhere.
    \item[Failure B]
        Latest-wins silently repeals sum-then-clip, making stance free to flip,
        and forces one fold onto consumers with different needs. The protected
        rule is exactly \zcref{rem:graph:authored-act-bundle-consumers}: standing projection
        and title ordering are binding; every other bundle reading is terminal.
\end{description}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Payload Isolation in the Edge Commitment}
\label{subsec:necessity:payload-isolation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Every edge's payload occupies a separable, concealing, removable part
        of its commitment, bounded by $\maxpayload$
        (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-projection,post:graph:separable-act-projections}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Commit the edge over the structural record and the payload \emph{jointly}.
    \item[Failure]
