        Removal and integrity become mutually exclusive: erasing the payload
        alters the joint commitment, so the edge fails to authenticate against
        its own record. The operator must choose between honoring a removal and
        preserving verifiable history --- either choice corrupts an invariant
        (\zcref{post:introduction:record-integrity,post:introduction:irrevocability}).
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under a joint commitment the verifier recomputes the edge commitment from the
    structural record and the payload together; absent the payload the
    recomputation cannot complete and the edge fails despite an intact structural
    record. Under separability the structural part verifies independently
    (\zcref{post:graph:separable-act-projections}, reduced projection), so removal
    leaves edge authentication untouched. Binding blocks re-binding the freed
    content part to a substituted payload; concealment, via the co-removed private
    value, blocks recovering a short or guessable payload from the residue by
    enumeration. Both are required: binding alone leaves a recoverable residue,
    concealment alone permits rewriting.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{post:graph:separable-act-projections}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Pre-Commitment Before Host Salting}
\label{subsec:necessity:pre-commitment-before-salting}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        The Actor signs a proposal pre-commitment $\precommit{q}$ over the
        \emph{unsalted} proposal before the host adds projection salts
        (\zcref{def:graph:proposal-pre-commitment}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Let the host construct the salted commitments first, then have the Actor
        sign only the finished verified act.
    \item[Failure]
        Nothing binds what the Actor originally proposed before host enrichment;
        a host that alters endpoints, content, or dependencies before salting
        leaves no cryptographic trace of the original.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The salts are host-chosen, so an evidence chain that begins only after the
    host's contribution cannot attribute a pre-salting substitution.  The
    pre-commitment binds the exact proposal --- body, content, dependency list,
    and requested publication states --- and cannot be transplanted to another
    act identifier, so a later full opening exposes any host alteration against
    a signature the Actor made first.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:proposal-pre-commitment,def:graph:verified-act}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Approval After Host Salting}
\label{subsec:necessity:approval-after-salting}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Only an approved verified act may be admitted: the Actor signs an
        approval witness $\approvewitness{q}$ over the host-salted verified act
        $\verifiedact{q}$ (\zcref{def:graph:approval-witness}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Admit any verified act the host constructs, with no second Actor
        signature.
    \item[Failure]
        The host contributes the salts and could bind a content or dependency
        list the Actor never opened; without a post-salting approval the Actor is
        bound to a realization it never checked.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The Actor verifies both salted commitments open to the original content and
    dependencies and that no structural field changed, then signs the approval
    witness; an unapproved verified act is off-record submission state and cannot
    enter the order.  Pre-commitment binds the Actor's proposal; the approval
    witness binds the exact host-salted realization --- both signatures are
    necessary to close the substitution gap the salts open.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:} \zcref{def:graph:approval-witness}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Act-Level, Not Leg-Level, Dependencies}
\label{subsec:necessity:act-level-dependencies}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Dependencies name authored acts, and a hyper-edge carries one dependency
        projection for the whole act
        (\zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection}); the two edge projections
        share one parent act, $\actof{e_A}=\actof{e_T}$.
    \item[Simpl.]
        Let each leg carry its own dependency list and be ordered independently.
    \item[Failure]
        Leg-level ordering could place one leg of an act before, and the other
        after, a third act --- splitting an atomic act across the order --- or
        attach a fraud-provable list to one leg only.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The co-leg relation is symmetric atomicity, not a directed parent
    (\zcref{def:graph:dependent-act-set}); both legs share one act identifier and,
    once accepted, one authoritative time, so a single act-level dependency
    projection is the only carrier consistent with admitting the pair whole.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection,cor:graph:act-projection-atomicity}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Authoritative Total Order}
\label{subsec:necessity:authoritative-order}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        The host publishes one total authoritative order $\actsequence{k}$; agreement
        on it, not merely on the edge set, is required
        (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Publish only the accepted edge set and let each participant linearize it.
    \item[Failure]
        Order-sensitive quantities --- maturity, projected act times, path
        eligibility --- then differ between participants who linearize
        concurrently appended acts differently: a fork with no single answer.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under the deployed model these quantities are functions of the ordered
    history, not of the set alone
    (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}); two dependency-free acts
    placed in different positions yield different standing.  Only a published
    total order makes replay deterministic, which is why agreement on $\actsequence{k}$
    is required.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order,lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Retained Commitment After Tombstoning}
\label{subsec:necessity:retained-commitment}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        A dependency tombstone removes the list and its opening but retains the
        binding commitment residue (\zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-tombstone}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Remove the commitment residue too when tombstoning.
    \item[Failure]
        With no retained commitment a later ordering fraud proof has nothing to
        open against; the Actor could present a fabricated list, or the host deny
        the committed one.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The residue binds one canonical dependency list to the act
    (\zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-projection}), and the fraud proof
    $\fraudproof{q}$ opens against it
    (\zcref{def:graph:ordering-fraud-proof}).  Privacy while unopened and public
    accountability when opened both require the residue to survive the tombstone.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:graph:act-dependency-tombstone,def:graph:ordering-fraud-proof}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Title Conflict Separated From Host Order}
\label{subsec:necessity:title-order-separation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.8cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Locked]
        Handshake well-formedness follows the authoritative order
        ($\mathrm{Bid}\prec\mathrm{Accept}\prec\mathrm{Ratify}$, forced by the
        public settlement references), but title conflict resolution is
        epoch-quantized (\zcref{rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance}).
    \item[Simpl.]
        Let sub-epoch host order also decide conflicts --- which commit wins.
    \item[Failure]
        The host's residual ordering of unconstrained acts would then decide
        title outcomes, handing the operator a title-fabrication lever.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The settlement references are public causal parents
    (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-act-reference}), so any authoritative order
    places the handshake in sequence and well-formedness is reproducible; the
    conflict rules read only membership and $\operatorname{ep}(\cdot)$, never the
    residual sub-epoch order, so no host discretion enters title.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{rem:graph:title-order-irrelevance,thm:graph:settlement-order-freeness}.
\end{proof}

\section{Structural Necessity of Deployment Architecture}
\label{app:deployment}

Every deployment-level property below has been tested against its
simplest alternative. Unlike the protocol-level choices in
\zcref{app:necessity} --- where removing a mechanism breaks a formal
mathematical invariant --- deployment choices typically admit multiple
valid realizations. Each entry locks an abstract property the
deployment must satisfy, identifies the space of implementations that
satisfy it, and demonstrates what breaks when the property is abandoned
entirely. Where the selection among valid implementations is principled,
the criterion is stated; where it is pragmatic, it is acknowledged as
such.

The transition between deployment phases --- centralized verification as
audit, decentralized verification as gate --- is documented in
\zcref{subsec:introduction:verification-model}. The deployment invariants
below apply in both phases. What the transition changes is the protocol
consequence of a failed verification: in the centralized phase a failed
verification flags a result already in effect; in the decentralized
phase it prevents the result from taking effect at all. The mathematical
specification being verified is unchanged; path-level checks use the
same retrieved edge records in both cases
(\zcref{prop:scalability:raw-path-verifiability}).

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Continuous Public Availability of Graph State}
\label{subsec:deployment:public-availability}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        The published state is the accepted authored-act history: every accepted
        act envelope --- act identifier, author, family, structural body, public
        protocol references and causal parents, the payload and dependency
        commitments, the admission handshake and approval witness, and the
        finalization epoch and act time $\acttime{q}$ --- together with its
        deterministic edge projection $\actedges{q}$ and a deterministic
        parent-act resolution $\actof{\cdot}$. Each edge projection carries
        parameters $(p_d, p_i, \text{domain})$, precomputed scalars
        $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F$, $\detscore{e}$, and $\detsign{e}$, and the
        inherited pair $(\acttime{\actof{e}}, \tau_e)$. An edge projection alone
        is sufficient for raw graph geometry; authorship, payload- and
        dependency-commitment verification, causal references, approval, act
        time, and hyper-edge atomicity require the parent act envelope. All of it
        is available to any participant at any time without access control, with
        new material available as acts are accepted. Availability applies
        unconditionally to the structural act record and the retained payload
        residue (the witness, \zcref{rem:graph:act-payload-custody-phases}); full
        payload bytes are available only while the payload is in a full
        projection (\zcref{def:graph:act-payload-state}), and no Layer~1
        verification requires them.
        Availability also covers every conserved standing package commitment
        and the data required to resolve it: complete-act witnesses,
        projection, the base matrix, emission fractions, the standing box,
        the accepted rung, the certificate value and verdict, and the declared
        inputs and formula editions.
    \item[Design space]
        Streaming append-log (pub/sub); open API polling with
        pagination; periodic snapshot with delta-encoding; P2P
        gossip replication. All four satisfy the invariant.
    \item[Selection]
        Pragmatic preference. Streaming minimises ego-network
        staleness between edge creation and client cache update;
        periodic snapshots and polling introduce bounded staleness
        without breaking the invariant. The selection is an
        engineering choice among equivalent options.
    \item[Failure]
        Gated read access to act envelopes or their edge projections.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under gated access, a participant whose readable subgraph is
    an arbitrary subset of the global edge log attempts to compute
    $S_C$ --- betweenness centrality over advertiser-to-target
    shortest paths (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-centrality}). Whether a
    path absent from the gated view would have passed through $C$'s
    node or routed around it is indistinguishable: both cases produce
    identical observable symptoms (the path is not visible). Under
    continuous public availability, a participant's BFS over the full
    published edge set with costs
    $1/(\detscore{e} \cdot \sqrt{1+\tau_e^2})$
    (\zcref{def:graph:path-distance}) produces the identical path set
    as the server, yielding a verifiable $\hat{S}_C$ satisfying the
    $(\epsilon,\delta)$-approximation guarantee of
    \zcref{thm:scalability:efficient-approximation}.
    Similarly, the raw signed double-cover service
    (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}) requires all edge
    records including $\detsign{e}$ for its raw parity registers.
    For standing, edge availability alone is insufficient: the verifier
    must also determine that no accepted act was omitted and that the
    base matrix and emission diagonal being certified are the ones
    actually consumed.  Projection completeness
    (\zcref{prop:deployment:allocation-input-completeness}) and the public
    declared inputs and formula editions supply those bindings.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula,%
    def:bridge:realizing-centrality,%
    prop:scalability:raw-path-verifiability}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Final Epoch State Agreement}
\label{subsec:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        At each boundary the operator publishes the authoritative ordered
        authored-act sequence $Q_k$
        (\zcref{def:graph:authoritative-act-order}) and its record projection,
        the monotone edge set $E_k$
        (\zcref{post:introduction:epoch-edge-set}); any participant accepting
        $Q_k$ replays identical epoch results
        (\zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism,%
        prop:epoch:epoch-replay-determinism}). Agreement on the ordered
        sequence $Q_k$ is required --- agreement on the edge set $E_k$ alone is
        insufficient, since acts the host may place in either order yield
        order-dependent results.  Agreement on $Q_k$ extends deterministically to
        the complete-act projection and conserved standing package under the
        pinned compiler versions.
    \item[Design space]
        Strict append-log linearization; cluster-closure writes under the
        published closure rule; BFT/finality gadget committing the ordered
        frontier; gossip replication with a stability depth. All are compliant
        iff honest participants converge on the same authoritative order $Q_k$.
    \item[Selection]
        Principled. The load-bearing object is the authoritative order $Q_k$,
        not the unordered set; cluster closure writes the ordered membership,
        and $\snapbuf$ buffers the burn snapshot only. Among compliant
        mechanisms the choice is pragmatic.
    \item[Failure]
        Participants disagree on $Q_k$, or a host presents a
        projection/envelope and admission package not deterministically derived from
        the agreed $Q_k$.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    By \zcref{lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism,%
    prop:epoch:epoch-replay-determinism}, the same authoritative order $Q_k$
    yields identical epoch results. Conversely, two dependency-free acts placed
    in different positions by different participants produce
    different snapshots, hence different residual source, complete acts,
    projected vouches, the base matrix, emission fractions, safe flow, standing,
    activations, stamps, and certificate verdicts --- a fork
    in the write rule. The exposure is
    quantitatively bounded by \zcref{prop:epoch:final-standing-hull}: the fork
    magnitude is bounded by the rate-hull width times the perturbed
    frontier weight mass, which the stability depth drives to zero.
    The act identifier exposes equivocation rather than absorbing it:
    distinct records claiming one $\operatorname{actid}(q)$ fail formation and
    are rejected by record integrity instead of silently receiving arbitrary
    positions.
    Guaranteeing frontier and order agreement under adversarial concurrent
    appends is the out-of-scope mechanism, on the same footing as
    record integrity (\zcref{subsec:deployment:immutability}).
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{post:introduction:epoch-edge-set,%
    post:introduction:record-integrity,%
    lem:graph:ordered-replay-determinism,%
    prop:epoch:epoch-replay-determinism}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Immutability of Published Records}
\label{subsec:deployment:immutability}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        Once an edge record is published, its stored parameters are
        fixed. Subsequent changes create new edges; they do not
        modify existing ones.
    \item[Design space]
        Any mechanism satisfying \zcref{post:introduction:record-integrity}
        is compliant. The selection among compliant mechanisms is
        outside the scope of this document.
    \item[Selection]
        Principled in character: something must enforce
        non-alteration. Implementation-agnostic: the enforcement
        mechanism is deployment-phase-dependent and less important
        than the guarantee it provides.
    \item[Failure]
        Mutable edge records --- parameter updates, retroactive
        corrections, or soft deletions.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Independent path verification
    (\zcref{prop:scalability:raw-path-verifiability}) requires that a
    retrieved record for edge $e$ remain valid at all future replay
    times. Under mutability, a parameter update to $(p_d, p_i)$
    silently invalidates every cached path computation referencing
    $e$'s prior values without signaling clients holding stale
    proofs. The local time integer $\acttime{\actof{e}}$ is not incremented
    by a parameter mutation --- causal ordering is preserved --- but
    the sentiment slice $\symbf{\Psi}_e$ causally established at
    $\acttime{\actof{e}}$ can disagree with the stored parameters. The
    determinant sign $\detsign{e}$ would change without record:
    positive-parity paths could become negative-parity or vice versa,
    silently altering endorsement flow weights $\transportentry{j}{i}$ and Effective
    standing values $\standing{i}$ already published for the current epoch
    without triggering a recomputation. Under immutability, any
    participant replaying the committed edge records arrives at the
    identical graph state. All derived quantities ---
    $\pathview{e}$, $\detscore{e}$, $\detsign{e}$,
    $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_e}_F$ --- are permanently fixed at the time
    of publication.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{ax:graph:act-causality,%
    def:graph:raw-snapshot-path,%
    prop:scalability:raw-path-verifiability}
\end{proof}

\begin{postulate}[Public-Object Replay]
    \label{post:deployment:public-object-replay}
    Binding Layer~1 objects are identified by their public structural
    identities and verified by deterministic replay from:
    \[
        \text{accepted acts},
        \qquad
        \text{the final ledger},
        \qquad
        \text{published constants},
        \qquad
        \text{formula editions}.
    \]

    Layer~1 assigns no normative meaning to a hash, Merkle root, source
    digest, manifest digest, proof-tree root, or content-addressed
    locator.  An implementation may use such values for indexing,
    caching, transport, or storage integrity, but they do not alter the
    mathematical object, do not select among valid objects, and do not
    substitute for replay.
\end{postulate}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Client-Reproducible Feed Ranking}
\label{subsec:deployment:feed-reproducibility}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        Any two clients holding identical ego-network edge records
        and the seven published scoring constants
        ${\invtemp,\, \bleedparam,\, \divpref,\, \numeraire,\, \partfloor,\,
        \epochlen,\, \snapbuf}$, together with the depth bound $L$, produce
        identical ranked feeds.
        These are the scoring subset of the nine network protocol
        constants; the Layer~0 surface constants $\feerate$, $\livesplit$, and the
        maturity lead $\matlead$ are surfaced with the
        protocol constants but do not enter feed ranking.
    \item[Design space]
        Deterministic closed-form formula (chosen); ML model with
        publicly distributed locally-executable weights; consensus-
        computed ranking refreshed per epoch. All satisfy the
        invariant if and only if a client can execute the full
        computation without server state.
    \item[Selection]
        Principled among the valid options. A deterministic
        closed-form formula satisfies the invariant at zero
        model-weight overhead. Publicly distributed locally-executable
        ML weights could satisfy it in principle; at the scale of
        modern recommendation models they require gigabytes of weight
        data and hardware inference support, violating the device-local
        invariant of \zcref{subsec:deployment:device-local}. The
        closed-form formula is the unique realization jointly
        compatible with the invariants of this subsection and
        \zcref{subsec:deployment:device-local}.
    \item[Failure]
        Opaque server-held model weights, inaccessible to clients.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under opaque model weights, two clients with identical input
    edge records produce divergent feeds because neither holds the
    server's weights. A server can produce any ordering and claim it
    satisfies $\operatorname{argmax}_{c} S(u,c)$ without
    contradiction --- the claim is unfalsifiable.

    Under client reproducibility, a participant executes
    \zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs} with the seven published
    scoring constants and locally cached edge records, then compares their
    output list to the server's. The log-transform equivalence
    (\zcref{thm:sorting:log-transform-equivalence}) ensures the
    max-product path and shortest-path computations are
    interchangeable, and both are deterministic functions of the
    same inputs. Divergence between client and server output is
    immediately detectable and attributable to exactly one party.
    The same argument applies to the double cover BFS
    (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}): given the six
    published scoring constants and the snapshot subgraph edge records, any
    participant independently produces the same $\transportentry{j}{i}$
    and $\standing{i}$ values published by Layer~1 at the epoch
    boundary.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs,%
    thm:sorting:log-transform-equivalence,%
    lem:sorting:bfs-correctness}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Device-Local Computation Scope}
\label{subsec:deployment:device-local}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        Feed computation is executable from locally cached data on a
        standard personal device, with no per-request server
        dependency.
    \item[Design space]
        Depth-bounded ego-network at $L = 4$ (chosen); $L = 3$ or
        $L = 6$; server-assisted computation beyond local cache. The
        invariant requires a depth bound keeping the ego-network
        subgraph device-cacheable; the exact value is calibrated.
    \item[Selection]
        $L = 4$ is the greatest depth satisfying device-local
        tractability across realistic mean-degree regimes. At mean
        out-degree $\bar{d} = 10$: depth~4 yields up to
        $\bar{d}^4 = 10^4$ BFS nodes (tens of megabytes, cacheable
        on any current personal device); depth~6 yields up to $10^6$
        nodes (gigabytes, requiring server infrastructure for most
        devices). The value is empirically calibrated against real
        degree distributions; the invariant --- device-local scope
        --- is fixed. The double cover BFS
        (\zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs}) operates on the
        same depth-$L$ ego-network but runs at the epoch boundary on
        Layer~1 infrastructure, not per client request; the
        invariant applies specifically to the feed-ranking BFS.
    \item[Failure]
        Feed computation requiring graph data unavailable from the
        local cache.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Client-side verification of feed ranking requires the client
    to independently compute $S(u, c)$ for content nodes in the
    ranked list and compare results against the server's output
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:feed-reproducibility}). If the required
    subgraph exceeds the local cache, the client must request
    additional edge records from the server. In this configuration,
    both the claimed feed and the data required to dispute it
    originate from the identical server: the data for verifying
    the server's output is controlled by the party under audit.

    The depth bound $L = 4$ is the structural mechanism making
    client verification and server feed computation disjoint
    pipelines operating on the same locally cached data. A client
    that prefetches the depth-4 ego-network at initialization holds
    all data required to execute \zcref{alg:sorting:feed-ranking-bfs}
    independently of the server for the lifetime of the cache. Raw snapshot connectivity (\zcref{def:graph:raw-snapshot-path}) and BFS correctness
    (\zcref{lem:sorting:bfs-correctness}) are preserved without
    modification.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:sorting:relevance-score,%
    lem:sorting:bfs-correctness,%
    def:graph:raw-snapshot-path}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Transparency of Protocol Constants and Formulas}
\label{subsec:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        The network protocol constants ${\invtemp,\, \bleedparam,\,
        \divpref,\, \numeraire,\, \polfloor,\, \safethresh,\,
        \marginfactor,\, \epochlen,\, \snapbuf,\, L,\, \hopmax,\,
        \maxpayload}$,
        the derived effective floor $\partfloor$, and the published boundary
        triple (target size, minimum duration, maximum duration), plus the
        network derived constants
        ${\wspam,\, \wmax,\, \wmaxop}$;
        the standing-census, complete-act compiler, coefficient,
        projected-activation, path-selection, allocator, mediant,
        scalar-encoding, and certificate formula editions;
        together with the
        surfaced Layer~0 constants ($\feerate$, $\livesplit$, $\matlead$, and
        the derived $R_{\mathrm{ceil}}$;
        \attestationcref{subsec:model:constants}), are known to all clients
        and do not change without clients being able to detect the change
        and invalidate affected cached computations before the change
        applies.
    \item[Design space]
        Full post-launch immutability (chosen); governance-vote
        updates on a published schedule with sufficient advance
        notice; time-locked update windows with independent oracle
        attestation. All satisfy the invariant provided clients
        cannot be surprised by a silent change.
    \item[Selection]
        The key criterion is absence of silent change, not
        immutability per se. Full immutability is the strictest valid
        realization and eliminates all coordination overhead.
        Governance-vote updates satisfy the invariant if the schedule
        is published with sufficient lead time for clients to
        recompute affected cached values before the change applies.
        Pragmatic in mechanism; principled in the ordering
        constraint that changes must be announced before they occur.
    \item[Failure]
        Server-tunable constants updated without client notice.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    A silent change to $\invtemp$ shifts the maturity crossover
    $\tau^*$ (\zcref{prop:epoch:crossover-location}): for edges with
    $\tau \in (\numval{result.activation.tau_star_beta1.num}, \numval{const.activation.tau_star.num})$, the net maturity factor $g(\tau)$
    crosses from below~$1$ to above~$1$ or vice versa, reversing
    amplification/suppression. A client that cached $\dampedweight{e}$
    under the prior $\invtemp$ produces a feed that disagrees with
    the server's, but cannot determine whether the discrepancy arises
    from the parameter change, a client implementation error, or
    deliberate server manipulation: all three produce identical
    observable symptoms.

    A silent change to $\bleedparam$ collapses or widens the
    \tierfull{}/\tiermarginal{} gap ($\detscore{}$ scales as $\sqrt{\bleedparam}$
    for Epistemic-mask edges; \zcref{subsec:necessity:eta-softening}),
    reordering paths whose scores straddle the tier boundary. The
    derived constants $\wspam$, $\wmax$, and $\wmaxop$ are
    functions of $\bleedparam$ and $\invtemp$; a silent change to
    either primary constant invalidates all four derived constants
    simultaneously without client notice.

    A silent change to a Layer~0 surface constant propagates into the
    network's read values. Changing the live/time-locked split $\livesplit$
    alters the minting ratio for all future issuances, moving the burn
    capacity bound the network reads (\zcref{def:comparator:bootstrap-capacity}), the
    rate ceiling (\attestationcref{prop:containment:floor-ceiling}), the
    seigniorage suppression factor
    (\attestationcref{prop:containment:seigniorage-suppression}), and the
    entry cost (\zcref{eq:comparator:admission-benchmark-deposits}) simultaneously and without
    participant notice. Changing the maturity lead $\matlead$ alters
    the minimum lead time for maturity announcements
    (\attestationcref{post:maturity:announcement}): shortening it allows a
    conversion to be sprung with insufficient market preparation;
    lengthening it locks time-locked-class holders into illiquidity beyond
    the published commitment. These are Layer~0 surface constants
    (\attestationcref{subsec:model:constants}); the deployment obligation is
    that the network surfaces any such change under the same
    no-silent-change discipline.

    A silent change to $\polfloor$ alters the derived participation gate
    $\refstanding{i} \geq \partfloor$ enforced at the epoch boundary.
    A silent change to the structural numéraire $\numeraire$ reprices reduced
    quantities and is a migration event.
    Actors who were participation-permitted under the prior threshold
    may become blocked, or vice versa, without any record of the
    change accessible to participants attempting to verify their own
    gate status. A silent change to $\epochlen$ changes the write budget. A
    silent duration change is equally material: shrinking the minimum duration
    silently deflates back-pressure and door headroom, a stealth giveaway of
    write budget; stretching the maximum silently delays liveness. Both are
    certificate-auditable through closure cause plus attested timestamp
    (\zcref{post:graph:boundary-accountability,post:network:host-contract}). A
    silent change to $\snapbuf$ shifts the burn snapshot depth, altering
    $\commitrate{i}^{(k)}$ and downstream standing quantities without changing
    membership.

    A silent change to the Layer~0 minting fee $f$ alters the operator
    share in the Layer~0 cycle and therefore the auditable seigniorage bound
    during bootstrapping
    (\attestationcref{alg:operations:cycle-processing},
    \attestationcref{thm:seigniorage:bootstrapping-bound}). Participants cannot
    verify whether fee-derived reserve accrual stays within the published
    bound unless the fee rate is governed by the same transparency rule.
    The fee is a Layer~0 surface constant
    (\attestationcref{def:model:fee-and-split}).

    A silent change to $\hopmax$, the $\actexponent$ activation
    exponent, the relation coefficient, the source-envelope rule, or
    the stage-admission allocator changes standing while leaving the raw
    graph unchanged.  A silent change to the released formula edition --- which its
    published hash merely locates --- would let a different program attest the
    package.  Each is therefore as material as a silent change to $\numeraire$ or
    $\polfloor$.

    Under constant transparency, any change is either impossible or
    announced with sufficient lead time for clients to invalidate
    stale cached values before the change applies, making any
    subsequent discrepancy between client and server output
    attributable to a specific, timestamped cause.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{prop:epoch:crossover-location,%
    def:graph:path-view-extraction,%
    ax:epoch:thermodynamic-boundary,%
    post:epoch:final-edge-set},~%
    \attestationcref{alg:operations:cycle-processing},~%
    \attestationcref{thm:seigniorage:bootstrapping-bound}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Self-Sufficient Edge Record}
\label{subsec:deployment:sufficiency}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        The published record for each edge contains exactly the
        fields required to compute $\dampedweight{e}$,
        $\detsign{e}$, $\baseval{e}$, and the identity key used for
        canonical boundary placement. The server's scoring and boundary
        computations depend on no additional unpublished field. The record
        splits into a structural part --- sufficient for every Layer~1
        computation --- and a payload part (state and witness) sufficient to
        verify carriage; the structural part alone supports full replay
        (\zcref{prop:graph:removable-projection-invariance}). Derived edges add no
        record fields: they are recomputed from the certificate
        (\zcref{def:graph:derived-raw-edges}).
        For a hyper-edge leg, the record also contains its role and
        reciprocal co-leg identity, so complete-act identity is
        independently reconstructible.
    \item[Design space]
        Minimal sufficient record (chosen); extended record with
        precomputed derived quantities for client convenience
        (e.g.\ pre-cached $\tentropy{e}$ alongside $\tau_e$); extended
        record with additional verified-but-redundant fields.
        Proprietary enrichment fields that the server's computation
        depends on are not a valid implementation.
    \item[Selection]
        Pragmatic at the lower boundary: adding verified redundant
        fields satisfies the invariant, since clients can verify
        them by recomputing. Principled at the upper boundary:
        adding server-computation-load-bearing proprietary fields
        violates the invariant categorically. Minimality marks the
        boundary between these cases. The determinant sign
        $\detsign{e}$ is part of the minimal sufficient record: it is
        a derived quantity from the stored parameters and the published
        constants, but publishing it cached
        alongside the record reduces per-client verification cost
        from $O(4)$ (recompute determinant) to $O(1)$ (read cached
        sign).
    \item[Failure]
        Server's scoring computation depends on fields absent from
        the published record.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Suppose the server applies a proprietary
    \texttt{recency\_weight} field as a multiplicative factor in
    feed ranking alongside the published $\dampedweight{e}$.
    A client computing $\hat{S}(u,c)$ from the published record
    alone produces a divergent ranking. The client cannot determine
    whether the divergence is a client implementation error, a
    formula version mismatch, or deliberate protocol manipulation:
    all three produce identical symptoms --- the client's formula
    and the server's formula agree on all published inputs but
    produce different outputs.

    Self-sufficiency collapses this ambiguity. If every field the
    server uses is present in the published record, any divergence
    between client and server output is unambiguously a protocol
    violation by whichever party produced the incorrect result:
    identical published inputs under an identical deterministic
    formula must produce identical outputs. The canonical pipeline
    (\zcref{post:nodes:canonical-tensor-pipeline}) specifies the
    minimal sufficient record: parameters $(p_d, p_i,
    \text{domain})$ and temporal attributes $(\acttime{\actof{e}},
    \tau_e)$, together with the author and endpoints identifying the
    edge. All scoring quantities ---
    $\symbf{\Psi}_e$, $\pathview{e}$, $\detscore{e}$,
    $\detsign{e}$, $\dampedweight{e}$, $\baseval{e}$ --- are
    deterministic functions of these fields and the seven published
    scoring constants. The canonical identity key is likewise
    reproducible from public data alone. The raw signed double-cover
    service additionally reads
    $\detsign{e}$ at every edge --- a one-bit quantity derivable from
    the stored parameters at $O(1)$ cost
    (\zcref{rem:graph:one-bit-extraction-cost}) and useful to raw
    consumers, though standing authority is determined by the
    complete-act census and strictly positive semantic coordinates, not
    by parity.  The standing compiler additionally checks that a
    selected Reference or Invitation consists of one matched complete
    act (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection}); publishing both raw legs
    without their reciprocal act linkage would leave standing atomicity
    unverifiable even though each raw edge were individually sufficient
    for feed scoring.  The person-vouch predicate itself is the strict
    positive-coordinate test after the declared fold
    (\zcref{def:epoch:effective-act-contribution}).
    Settlement Accept and Ratify edges additionally carry a
    \texttt{settles}-pointer --- the identity key of the Bid they
    reference (\zcref{subsec:graph:settlement-lifecycle}); since the key is
    itself reproducible from public data, the pointer adds no
    non-public field to the minimal sufficient record.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:epoch:damped-edge-weight,%
    post:nodes:canonical-tensor-pipeline,%
    prop:scalability:raw-path-verifiability}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Concealment-Entropy Custody Across Phases}
\label{subsec:deployment:concealment-entropy}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        Every content commitment's private value
        (\zcref{post:graph:separable-act-projections}) is generated with
        entropy sufficient for the reduced projection to conceal, and
        custody of that obligation is explicitly assigned in each phase:
        the operator in the centralized phase; a published
        constrained-generation rule binding Layer~2 carriage once the
        append layer decentralizes
        (\zcref{rem:graph:act-payload-custody-phases}).
    \item[Design space]
        Operator-generated values under audit (centralized); client-side
        generation against a published entropy specification validated at
        append; deterministic derivation from a client secret under a
        published rule. All comply iff low-entropy generation is
        detectable or precluded before concealment is relied upon.
    \item[Selection]
        Principled in character, phase-split in mechanism: something must
        own the obligation in every phase, because the network cannot
        audit the value itself (private by construction,
        \zcref{rem:graph:erasure-floor}).
    \item[Failure]
        Unassigned custody in the decentralized phase.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Concealment rests entirely on the entropy of the co-removed private
    value: for a short or enumerable payload, an adversary holding the
    residue tests candidate (payload, value) pairs against the
    commitment, and a guessable value collapses removal into disclosure
    --- erasure would then \emph{weaken} privacy exactly where it
    promises to discharge it (\zcref{ins:introduction:right-to-leave}). In
    the centralized phase the operator both generates and removes, so the
    obligation is auditable as an implementation property. In the
    decentralized phase Layer~1 holds only the witness; absent a
    published generation rule binding the carriage layer, the guarantee
    degrades with no observable symptom until an adversary demonstrates
    recovery. Assigning custody per phase keeps the erasure floor
    (\zcref{rem:graph:erasure-floor}) an honest named limit rather than an
    unowned one.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{post:graph:separable-act-projections,%
    rem:graph:act-payload-custody-phases,rem:graph:erasure-floor}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Independent Reproduction of Conserved Standing}
\label{subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        Every binding input, intermediate value, validity verdict, and
        output of the conserved standing package
        (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package}) is independently
        derivable from:
        \[
            E_k,\quad
            \text{the completed final ledger},\quad
            \text{published constants and formula editions}.
        \]
        No server-maintained relation counter, unpublished emission
        fraction, private model weight, or unpublished certificate verdict
        may enter standing.

    \item[Design space]
        A deterministic reference compiler plus independently executable
        certificate tools; a machine-checked formal compiler; or another
        implementation producing the same outputs.  The implementation may
        vary only when the formula/compiler edition changes under the
        no-silent-change rule.

    \item[Selection]
        The published deterministic compiler and certificate program are
        chosen because act reconstruction, fold-cell resolution, base
        allocation, emission, certificate evaluation, and mediant
        convergence must all be replayable from public inputs.

    \item[Failure]
        A host publishes a safe-looking projection, base matrix, emission
        diagonal, or certificate verdict that is valid in isolation but
        omits accepted records, differs from the deterministic allocator,
        uses another standing point, or does not match the final standing
        output.
\end{description}

The replay sequence is:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item derive residual balances and action counts from the boundary
          source state and debit schedule;
    \item reconstruct all complete acts and their public identities
          (\zcref{def:graph:act-edge-projection});
    \item apply the standing census to \emph{every} accepted act, with its
          per-author folds, revocations, and recipient resolution --- an
          act whose target is not an Actor resolves home, and is weighed
          there (\zcref{def:epoch:standing-recipient-resolution,%
          def:epoch:effective-act-contribution});
    \item compute each fold cell's coefficient and domain profile, and
          compare the resulting cell census;
    \item assemble the base allocation matrix, self-retention included,
          and compare it entrywise
          (\zcref{def:epoch:domain-weighted-base-allocation});
    \item recompute every emission fraction from the completed ledger and
          compare the diagonal (\zcref{def:epoch:source-emission});
    \item evaluate the certificate at each rung the host attempted and
          compare its value and verdict.  This step needs no equilibrium:
          the certificate is closed form and decided before the solve
          (\zcref{def:dynamics:conserved-standing-certificate}), so a
          verifier can reject an inadmissible rung without reproducing any
          iteration;
    \item iterate the conserved map at the accepted rung to the published
          residual and compare the equilibrium; the residual bound, not the
          host's pass count, decides agreement
          (\zcref{prop:scalability:fixed-point-check-cost});
    \item derive final standing, projected activations, stamps,
          and W2 decisions.
\end{enumerate}

Two of these steps are cheaper than they look, and a verifier should know
which.  The certificate is one sweep and is independent of the solve, so
\emph{admissibility} can be checked in isolation; and checking a claimed
equilibrium is one map pass rather than a re-solve, because a certified
residual bounds the distance to the fixed point.  A verifier never needs to
reproduce the host's iteration history.

\begin{proposition}[Projection Completeness]
    \label{prop:deployment:allocation-input-completeness}
    Let $\operatorname{Compile}_{v}$ be the compiler version committed by
    the constants ledger.  For fixed $E_k$ and fixed published constants:
    \[
        \operatorname{Compile}_{v}(E_k)
        =
        \bigl(
            \text{complete acts},
            \text{fold cells},
            \text{base allocation matrix},
            \text{emission diagonal}
        \bigr)
    \]
    is deterministic.

    A standing package is projection-complete iff independent replay of
    $\operatorname{Compile}_{v}(E_k)$ produces the same complete-act
    witnesses, the same fold cells, and the same two matrices.  A
    certificate verdict over a selectively omitted projection does not
    establish projection completeness: the certificate reads the base
    matrix it is given and says nothing about which acts produced it.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
    Complete-act identity, family and target census, bundle folds,
    revocation state, recipient resolution, the coefficient formula, the
    domain profile, self-retention, and the emission fraction are all
    deterministic functions of public committed inputs.  Therefore any
    omitted, substituted, or reordered act changes the replay result or its
    root.

    There is no eligibility predicate to agree about.  Every accepted act
    is weighed (\zcref{post:epoch:universal-act-weighing}), so an omission
    cannot be defended as a filtering decision --- which removes the
    category of dispute the retired eligible-vouch census created, where a
    host and a verifier could each replay faithfully and still disagree
    about what belonged in the set.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Completeness and Safety Are Orthogonal]
    \label{rem:deployment:completeness-safety-orthogonal}
    Projection replay answers:
    \emph{did the standing package weigh exactly the accepted acts the
    protocol requires?}

    The certificate answers:
    \emph{is the resulting map contractive at the rung the host claimed?}

    Either may fail while the other passes, and the reason is that the
    certificate never sees the acts.  It reads the base matrix and the
    contributing width, so a package built from a selectively omitted act
    set can certify perfectly --- its matrix is simply a different, smaller,
    entirely admissible one.  Conversely a complete package may fail the
    certificate and be backed off to a lower rung, which is a valid
    outcome, not an invalid package.  A valid standing package requires
    both checks because neither is evidence for the other.
\end{remark}

Under independent derivability, any participant reproduces the binding
standing package and checks its certificate.  A discrepancy identifies
a protocol violation rather than an inaccessible server choice.


% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Canonical Standing Encoding}
\label{subsec:deployment:canonical-standing-encoding}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Replay is the whole audit right, and replay is only as strong as the agreement
about what was published.  Two honest participants reproducing the same
conserved standing package must arrive at the same bits, not merely at the same
mathematics, or a disagreement cannot be attributed.

\begin{postulate}[Canonical Standing Publication]
    \label{post:deployment:canonical-standing-publication}
    The host publishes the conserved standing package
    (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package}) in a canonical encoding:
    a declared ordering of Actors and of each row's support, a declared
    representation for every rational quantity, and a declared rounding
    disclosure for every value that is not exact.  The encoding is itself
    published and versioned under the no-silent-change discipline
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas}).

    Two consequences are the point of the postulate.  First, replay is
    \emph{decidable}: a participant who recomputes the package either matches
    the published bits or has found a discrepancy to attribute, with no third
    outcome in which both parties are arguably right.  Second, the certificate
    verdict is part of what is encoded --- including which rungs were attempted
    and failed --- so a reader can tell a quiet epoch from an uncertified one
    without trusting the host's summary of its own backoff.

    What the postulate does \emph{not} do is fix the encoding here.  The
    encoding is a deployment artifact with its own calibration obligation
    (\zcref{frontier:canonical-standing-encoding}), and the replay procedure
    and its tolerance are a second
    (\zcref{frontier:canonical-standing-replay}).  Publishing an encoding badly
    is a deployment defect; not declaring one at all is a protocol defect, and
    that is the line this postulate draws.
\end{postulate}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Auditable Terminal Centrality}
\label{subsec:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        Each epoch's centrality computation produces a certificate
        sufficient for any participant to independently verify
        $\hat{S}_C$ for any creator, to within the published
        $(\epsilon, \delta)$ bounds
        (\zcref{def:scalability:approximation}).
    \item[Design space]
        Published Dijkstra-tree samples (chosen); commitment scheme
        with per-creator selective reveal; third-party auditor
        attestation.
    \item[Selection]
        Principled among available options. Published Dijkstra-tree
        samples are transparent, require no trusted intermediary,
        and allow any participant to run the identical computation
        independently. Commitment
        with selective reveal allows a creator to verify their own
        certificate but not others', weakening the collective
        auditing surface. Third-party attestation reintroduces a
        trusted intermediary.
    \item[Failure]
        Publish only centrality scalars $\hat{S}_C$; suppress the
        supporting sampled Dijkstra-path trees.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Under scalar-only publication, a participant receives $\hat{S}_C$
    but not the $k$ sampled Dijkstra trees underlying it. The
    participant cannot determine whether $\hat{S}_C$ was computed
    over legitimate Dijkstra trees with costs
    $1/(\detscore{e} \cdot \sqrt{1+\tau_e^2})$
    (\zcref{eq:sorting:log-cost-decomposition}) or over fabricated path sets:
    both produce a scalar in $[0,1]$. Nash preservation
    (\zcref{thm:scalability:nash-preservation}) requires that the
    approximation error $\epsilon = |\hat{R}_C - R_C|/R_{\max}$
    be a participant-verifiable quantity, so that the bound
    $2\epsilon R_{\max} < \gamma$ can be independently checked.
    Under scalar-only publication, $\epsilon$ is a server claim
    about the server's own computation --- precisely the failure
    the bound was designed to prevent.

    Under published Dijkstra-tree samples, any participant runs
    Dijkstra on the identical published graph with costs
    \zcref{eq:sorting:log-cost-decomposition}, checks $C$'s node membership
    against each sampled path, and reproduces $\hat{S}_C$ to
    floating-point precision. The approximation bound from
    \zcref{thm:scalability:efficient-approximation} becomes a
    participant-computed quantity, and the Nash-preservation condition
    is independently checkable.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:bridge:realizing-centrality,%
    thm:scalability:efficient-approximation,%
    thm:scalability:nash-preservation}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Attribution-View Insulation of CAN Enrichment}
\label{subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        The CAN enrichment factor $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ entering
        the guild reward formula uses exclusively \AttrView{}
        quantities satisfying
        $\partial(\canval{n_C}/V_{\max})/\partial\standing{C} = 0$
        for all actors whose Declaration component does not lie within their own
        composition dependency closure, and no \PathView{} or
        $\standing{}$-derived quantity enters the CAN recursion.
    \item[Design space]
        CAN enrichment via pure \AttrView{} Frobenius norms
        (chosen); CAN enrichment with an $\standing{}$-scaled
        component; CAN enrichment blended with a \PathView{}
        correction on $\detscore{}$.
    \item[Selection]
        Principled. The condition
        $\partial(\canval{n_C}/V_{\max})/\partial\standing{C} = 0$
        is not a design preference: it is a consequence of the
        \AttrView{} CAN recursion containing no formula path through
        $\standing{C}$ unless $C$'s Declaration component lies in its own
        dependency closure (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-vmax}).
        Either alternative in the design space introduces
        $\standing{}$-dependence or \PathView{} tier-discrimination
        categorically.
    \item[Failure]
        Any $\standing{}$-dependent or \PathView{}-derived quantity
        entering the CAN enrichment factor.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Two failure paths are structurally distinct.

    \emph{$\standing{}$-dependent CAN factor.}
    The reward formula (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula})
    already contains $\ampfactor{C}$ as a multiplicative factor.
    This Layer~1 quantity fully captures the influence of the
    actor's commitment history on reward scaling. Introducing
    $\standing{}$-dependence into the CAN enrichment factor
    $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ would double-count the Layer~1 influence
    signal: an actor's commitment history would enter the reward
    formula via both $\ampfactor{C}$ and via the enrichment
    factor simultaneously. The double-counting amplification would
    grow with $\standing{C}$ without bound above the single-factor
    rate, creating an asymmetric compound advantage for high-rate
    actors in the attribution layer that is not present in the
    centrality layer ($S_C$ is $\standing{}$-independent by
    construction: it depends only on graph shortest-path topology).

    More concretely: the Declaration component carries
    $p_i = \standing{i}/(\numeraire+\standing{i})$, which enters
    $\norm{\symbf{\Psi}_{\mathrm{Self}}}_F$ and therefore propagates
    into $\canval{n_C}$ if the Declaration component lies in the dependency
    closure. For actors whose Declaration component is \emph{excluded} from
    their own composition dependency closure (the normal case),
    $\partial\canval{n_C}/\partial\standing{C} = 0$ exactly. Any
    enrichment formula that adds an explicit $\standing{C}$-dependent
    term would re-introduce this dependence for all actors regardless
    of dependency closure structure.

    \emph{\PathView{} correction.}
    Introducing a $\detscore{}$-based correction amplifies creators
    with \tierfull{}-dominated interaction histories
    ($\detscore{} \approx 0.27$--$0.36$) over creators with
    \tiermarginal{}-dominated histories ($\detscore{} \approx 0.07$--$0.08$),
    a ${\approx}\,\numval{result.promotion.ratio.num}\times$ per-edge gap
    (\zcref{subsec:verification:mask-promotion-impact}). Tag
    contributors --- whose epistemic interactions carry
    attribution-comparable \AttrView{} norms
    ($\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \numrel{result.e5.frobenius.num}$;
    \zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}) but low
    \PathView{} determinants --- would receive ${\approx}\,\numval{result.tier.edge_gap.num}\times$
    less cross-attribution credit than Opinion contributors of
    comparable information content. The CAN enrichment signal would
    discriminate by edge type rather than contribution quality:
    this is precisely the single-view failure documented in
    \zcref{subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture}, applied to
    attribution.

    Under \AttrView{} insulation, the CAN recursion
    (\zcref{def:can:intrinsic-value}) contains no formula path
    through $\standing{C}$ (for actors outside their own dependency
    closure) and no reference to $\detscore{}$. The enrichment
    factor $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ uses exclusively \AttrView{}
    Frobenius norms whose variation across all edge types is
    ${\approx}\,16\%$ ($\norm{\symbf{\Psi}}_F \in [\numval{result.e7.frobenius.num}, \numval{result.e8.frobenius.num}]$;
    \zcref{subsec:verification:tensor-computation}) rather than
    ${\approx}\,\numval{result.tier.edge_gap.num}\times$ (the \PathView{} tier gap). Attribution
    equity across interaction domains is preserved; discrimination
    by directional coherence remains confined to $\Delta\campaignscalar{A}$ and
    $S_C$ in the \PathView{} layer.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{def:bridge:realizing-vmax,%
    prop:epoch:final-standing-hull,%
    subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Formula Completeness}
\label{subsec:deployment:completeness}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        The published material --- all protocol constants, all mask
        promotion criteria, all edge-type specifications, the CAN
        recursion, the reserve economy, the settlement recognition
        predicate and title certificate
        (\zcref{def:graph:settlement-recognition,%
        def:graph:title-certificate}), and the epoch boundary computation sequence
        --- is jointly sufficient to reproduce the server's output
        from published edge records alone, without any unpublished
        component.
    \item[Design space]
        Normative written specification (chosen); open-source
        reference implementation; machine-checked formal
        specification with test vector suite. All satisfy the
        invariant. A test vector suite particularly disambiguates
        mask promotion criteria, $\bleedparam$-softening behavior
        at boundary parameter values, and the double cover BFS
        parity-swap relaxation rule. Partial publication ---
        structure without constants, constants without promotion
        criteria, or promotion criteria without the epoch
        architecture --- does not satisfy the invariant.
    \item[Selection]
        Pragmatic over publication format; principled over
        completeness. The selection among written specification,
        reference implementation, and test vector suite is an
        engineering preference. The requirement for completeness
        is not.
    \item[Failure]
        Any proprietary component in any path from edge parameters
        to reward fractions.
\end{description}

The completeness obligation is scoped by the boundary of
\zcref{def:network:admission-closure}: it is required for every binding
value, and for any terminal value a guild elects to publish under
\zcref{post:transport:guild-grant}; a guild that reimplements a terminal default
publishes its own complete specification in its place.

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    Nash preservation (\zcref{thm:scalability:nash-preservation})
    requires participants to verify the approximation error
    $\epsilon = |\hat{R}_C - R_C|/R_{\max}$. Computing $\hat{R}_C$
    requires the complete reward formula
    (\zcref{eq:transport:reward-formula}). Representative
    incompleteness failures each corrupt a distinct factor:

    \emph{Mask promotion criteria unpublished.}
    The eight promotion decisions recorded in the Edge Census
    (\zcref{tbl:nodes:archetype-fingerprints,rem:nodes:edge-census-normative})
    determine whether each affected edge type enters at \tierfull{}
    ($\detscore{} \approx 0.27$--$0.36$) or \tiermarginal{}
    ($\detscore{} \approx 0.07$--$0.08$). Without the criteria,
    $\detscore{e}$ for promoted edges is underspecified. A
    $4.5\times$ per-edge error propagates multiplicatively along
    every path containing a promoted edge.

    \emph{CAN recursion unpublished.}
    Without \zcref{def:can:intrinsic-value}, the enrichment factor
    $\canval{n_C}/V_{\max}$ is uncomputable. This factor is the
    unique CAN-to-reward bridge
    (\zcref{def:bridge:realizing-vmax}); its
    suppression renders the reward formula partially opaque at the
    \AttrView{} layer.

    \emph{Epoch architecture unpublished.}
    Without the boundary triple, the closure cause, and $\snapbuf$, the write
    budget, liveness window, and burn snapshot are undefined. Different
    participants apply different closure and burn-state assumptions, producing
    different $\commitrate{i}^{(k)}$ and thus different $\standing{i}^{(k)}$
    values. The participation gate $\refstanding{i} \geq \partfloor$ becomes
    unverifiable: two participants with the same published edge records but
    different boundary assumptions will disagree on which actors are
    participation-permitted in epoch $k$.

    \emph{Double cover BFS parity rule unpublished.}
    Without the relaxation rule of
    \zcref{alg:epoch:double-cover-bfs},
    a participant cannot independently verify which raw paths are
    positive-parity.  The parity rule remains required only for raw
    signed services that publish such results; standing reproducibility
    instead requires the initiator-owned standing package.

    \emph{Standing projection or certificate program unpublished.}
    Without the closed person-vouch census, complete-act linkage,
    coefficient formula, projected activation, selected-path rule, clip
    allocator, standing box, and path-incidence certificate, two
    participants holding the same $E_k$ may derive different standing
    fields while each claims to implement the public mediant.  Publishing
    only final $\standing{}$ values or only a certificate verdict is
    insufficient: the projection may be incomplete, the verdict may concern
    a different base matrix, or the final standing may have been solved at a
    different rung.  Formula completeness requires the entire
    conserved standing package
    (\zcref{def:network:conserved-standing-package}).

    In each case, $\epsilon$ becomes a server assertion rather
    than a participant measurement. Formula completeness is the
    technical precondition for any equilibrium claim to be auditable
    by the agents the claim is about.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \zcref{thm:scalability:nash-preservation,%
    def:scalability:incentive-slack,%
    eq:transport:reward-formula}
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Maturity-Announcement Irrevocability (Preserved)}
\label{subsec:deployment:maturity-announcement-irrevocability}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The irrevocability of the maturity announcement --- that once the operator
commits the conversion schedule it cannot be retracted, deferred, or silently
replaced --- is a Layer~0 surface property
(\attestationcref{post:maturity:announcement}). The network does not re-derive
it; the deployment obligation is that the network's record substrate
\emph{preserves} that irrevocability rather than reintroducing mutability at
the application layer.

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        The Layer~0 maturity announcement, once posted, is carried by the
        network as an immutable append-log record; deployment adds no
        channel by which it could be silently removed or replaced.
    \item[Design space]
        Append-log immutability (chosen, per
        \zcref{post:introduction:record-integrity}); governance-vote
        deferral with published schedule; operator discretion with
        audit trail. All satisfy the invariant provided the
        operative announcement cannot be silently removed.
    \item[Selection]
        Principled --- identical to record integrity for edge records.
        The maturity announcement is an append-log record subject to
        the same immutability guarantee as all other records
        (\zcref{subsec:deployment:immutability}).
    \item[Failure]
        Silent retraction or deferral of an announced maturity schedule.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The announcement's irrevocability and the confidence signal carried by
    the time-locked class's secondary-market price are Layer~0 properties
    (\attestationcref{post:maturity:announcement},
    \attestationcref{rem:maturity:confidence-signal}). A deployment that
    permitted silent retraction would let participants who positioned on the
    announced schedule suffer unrecoverable losses from reliance on a
    retracted commitment, and would destroy the signal's informativeness ---
    the mechanism equivalent of record mutability
    (\zcref{subsec:deployment:immutability}) applied to the maturity timeline.
    Carrying the announcement under the same append-log immutability as every
    other record preserves the Layer~0 guarantee without restating it.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \attestationcref{post:maturity:announcement},~%
    \attestationcref{rem:maturity:confidence-signal},~%
    \zcref{subsec:deployment:immutability}.
\end{proof}

% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\subsection{Time-Locked Class Supply Auditability (Preserved)}
\label{subsec:deployment:time-locked-class-supply-auditability}
% ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Public auditability of the Layer~0 surface supply --- the live- and
time-locked-class balances, the reserve pool, and the redemption-rate floor
derived from them --- is a Layer~0 property
(\attestationcref{def:model:supply}, \attestationcref{def:model:ratefloor},
\attestationcref{post:interface:auditability}). The network neither models the
reserve pool nor recomputes the floor; the deployment obligation is that the
network surfaces the Layer~0 state transparently rather than occluding it.

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.3cm, style=nextline, nosep]
    \item[Invariant]
        The Layer~0 surface supply state is exposed by the network without
        modification, so any participant can audit it against Layer~0 at all
        times.
    \item[Design space]
        Same as \zcref{subsec:deployment:public-availability}: any
        mechanism satisfying
        \zcref{post:introduction:public-accessibility} for the surfaced Layer~0
        state is compliant.
    \item[Selection]
        Identical to graph state availability. The surfaced supply state is
        a small fixed set of scalars and imposes no additional architectural
        burden.
    \item[Failure]
        Occluded surface state --- participants cannot audit the Layer~0
        supply denominator through the network.
\end{description}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    The redemption-rate floor that converts burns
    (\zcref{def:comparator:imported-frame}) and redemptions
    (\attestationcref{def:operations:redemption}) is a Layer~0 surface quantity
    whose auditability Layer~0 establishes
    (\attestationcref{post:interface:auditability}). If the network occludes
    the surfaced supply state, participants lose the ability to audit that
    denominator at the instant of any read; the floor invariants
    (\attestationcref{thm:invariants:floor-non-decrease}) and the containment
    bounds (\attestationcref{subsec:containment:bounds}) become unverifiable
    through the network even though Layer~0 guarantees them. Surfacing the
    Layer~0 state transparently --- the same public-availability obligation
    the network meets for graph state --- preserves the Layer~0 auditability
    without re-deriving it.
    \hfill\emph{Ref:}
    \attestationcref{def:model:supply},~%
    \attestationcref{def:model:ratefloor},~%
    \attestationcref{post:interface:auditability},~%
    \zcref{subsec:deployment:public-availability}.
\end{proof}
